Inspection programme supportNDT technique selection and procedure review for API 510, 570 and 653 style programmesTerminal, refinery, gas plant and tank owners and their contractors

See the Canada consulting overview and the main consulting page for the full offer.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own document for training, examining, certifying and recertifying NDT personnel, and under SNT-TC-1A it is what an auditor checks first. For BC contractors it usually has to sit beside a Canadian quality system and a CGSB-certified workforce, and satisfy project specifications that change from one EPC to the next.

The common BC failure is a written practice built for a bid rather than for the work. A contractor needs an SNT-TC-1A document to prequalify for a project, adapts one from elsewhere, and then discovers during the owner's audit that it lists methods the crew does not perform, requires records the company never kept, or does not mention the advanced techniques the project depends on. Other frequent findings are practical examinations without graded checklists, expired vision tests, missing experience records for technicians who moved between employers, and no clear statement of how CGSB certification relates to the SNT-TC-1A levels.

We start with the work: which methods and techniques, which codes, which projects and owners. We then set out levels, training and experience (linked to the training requirements matrix rather than invented numbers), examination content and grading, vision testing, records, recertification and Level III arrangements. Technique-specific requirements, such as additional qualification for PAUT or TOFD on project welds, are written in so the document matches the specification. The written practice development page shows the general structure; our notes on written practices for LNG, pulp and paper and mining and minerals cover sector points that matter in BC.

An audit tests the records against the document. You receive findings ranked by audit risk with suggested corrections, and we can help close them. For employers that train staff, Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A-based training online and onsite; see NDT training in Canada and corporate NDT training.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in British Columbia

Direct answer: BC NDT procedures follow the code that governs the item: CSA B51 and ASME for boilers, pressure vessels and piping under Technical Safety BC, CSA Z662 for oil and gas pipelines regulated by the BC Energy Regulator or the Canada Energy Regulator, API 620 and 625 for LNG tanks on many projects, CSA W59 and AWS D1.1 for structures, and classification-society or naval rules for ships.

  • Boilers, pressure vessels and refrigeration: Technical Safety BC oversees design, construction, installation and operation of boilers, pressure vessels and refrigeration plants under the Safety Standards Act and the Power Engineers, Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Safety Regulation, and contractors working on that equipment must be licensed. Design registration follows CSA B51 and the ASME codes it references. See Technical Safety BC compliance, CSA B51 and CRN registration.
  • Pipelines: the BC Energy Regulator, formerly the BC Oil and Gas Commission, regulates oil and gas pipelines within the province, while utility pipelines fall under the BC Utilities Commission and interprovincial lines such as Trans Mountain under the Canada Energy Regulator. Pipeline NDT is done to CSA Z662 and operator specifications. See CSA Z662.
  • LNG facilities: process piping to ASME B31.3, storage tanks frequently to API 620 or API 625 with project-specific requirements, and CSA Z276 for LNG production, storage and handling in Canada. Cryogenic stainless and nickel-steel welds often need specially qualified UT, PAUT or RT techniques.
  • Structures, bridges and ships: CSA W59 and CSA W47.1 for welded steel, CSA S6 for highway bridges, AWS D1.1 on US-specification work, and classification-society or Department of National Defence specifications for ships. CSA W178.1 covers certification of welding inspection organisations; see CSA W178.1.
  • Radiography: gamma radiography is licensed by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission and exposure devices must be operated by CNSC-certified exposure device operators or under their direct supervision. Radiation safety at BC workplaces, including X-ray equipment, is also covered by WorkSafeBC's Occupational Health and Safety Regulation. See CNSC compliance.

A sound procedure states the code requirement, shows how your equipment and people meet it, and is specific enough for two technicians to perform the examination the same way. Technique sheets turn it into settings for a given weld or component. For cryogenic LNG welds, that means calibration blocks in the right material, beam-path and coverage evidence, and acceptance criteria from the governing code. For ship hulls and naval structures, it means joint configurations, plate thicknesses and the classification-society's criteria. For pulp mill recovery boilers and digesters, it means thickness survey grids and weld inspection that can be repeated outage to outage. We write procedures and technique sheets, check them against the edition the contract names, demonstrate techniques where required, and review procedures that an owner or EPC has rejected.

Outsourced and interim Level III for British Columbia crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is a named Level III who carries your programme's Level III duties under a standing agreement; an interim Level III fills a gap. Atlantis provides both to BC employers, remotely for documents and technical questions and onsite for examinations, technique demonstrations and audits, including at remote northern and coastal sites when the work needs it.

  • Ongoing outsourced Level III (retainer): we act as your programme's Level III, approving procedures and technique sheets, maintaining the written practice, administering examinations and attending owner or EPC audits.
  • Project-based work: a defined deliverable, such as a project-specific written practice and procedure set for an LNG or pipeline contract, technique sheets for a ship class, or examinations for a cohort of new hires.
  • Audit-preparation sprint: a focused review before a pre-mobilisation, shipyard or accreditation audit.

Project timing is the BC pressure point. A contractor that wins a scope on an LNG or pipeline job has a short window to show a compliant programme, and a Level III who leaves mid-project can stall approvals of technique sheets or new technician certifications. Interim Level III cover keeps the programme moving while you recruit. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III. Companies operating in BC and Alberta, or in BC and Washington State, can use multi-site NDT programme harmonisation to align written practices.

Audit readiness: owner, EPC, shipyard and accreditation audits

Direct answer: BC NDT programmes are audited by LNG and pipeline owners and their EPCs, by shipyards and naval customers, by mills and mines that hire inspection contractors, by accreditation bodies for ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 17025 laboratories, by CWB Group for CSA W178.1, and by radiation-safety regulators. Atlantis prepares the NDT personnel and procedure side of each.

Pre-mobilisation audits on energy projects usually check the written practice, procedures and technique qualification, certification files, vision tests and equipment calibration, and they often happen before the contractor has a single technician on site. Shipyard and naval audits focus on traceability from procedure to report and on personnel qualification to the specification. ISO/IEC 17025 assessments look at method validation, traceability and competence. Radiography licensees are inspected by the CNSC for radiation safety. We review your documents and records against the auditor's checklist, run a mock audit and help close gaps. We do not grant owner approvals, accreditation or Technical Safety BC licences; we help you prepare for the organisations that do.

The LNG audit support, pipeline audit support, shipbuilding audit support, maritime audit support and mining audit support pages set out what each type of audit concentrates on. If an audit is scheduled, ask about an audit-preparation review for your BC programme.

Sector notes: what BC industries ask of a Level III

Direct answer: LNG and pipeline projects want specification-matched procedures and technique qualification; shipyards want traceable structural-weld inspection; pulp mills, mines and smelters want repeatable in-service inspection; hydro owners want reliable inspection of penstocks, turbines and gates. A Level III's priorities move with each sector.

LNG on the coast

Kitimat, Squamish and the Fraser River host liquefaction, storage and export facilities. Cryogenic weld inspection, tank inspection and process piping examination dominate construction, followed by in-service programmes once plants are running.

Pipelines and the north-east gas fields

Coastal GasLink, Trans Mountain and the gathering systems of the Montney make girth-weld AUT and RT, facility piping inspection and integrity digs routine. Gas plants around Fort St. John and Chetwynd add pressure-equipment inspection.

Shipbuilding and naval repair

North Vancouver, Esquimalt and Victoria yards build and refit vessels with heavy UT, MT and VT on structural welds.

Pulp and paper, mining, smelting and hydro

Mills in Prince George and elsewhere rely on recovery boiler and digester inspection. Mines need inspection of crushers, mills and mobile equipment; the Trail and Kitimat smelters need maintenance NDT on process equipment and structures; and BC Hydro's dams and generating stations need inspection of penstocks, turbine runners and gates.

Cities we support across British Columbia

Direct answer: Atlantis supports NDT employers anywhere in British Columbia, remotely and onsite at your facility, yard or site, including Metro Vancouver, the Fraser Valley, Vancouver Island, Kitimat and Prince Rupert, Prince George, Fort St. John and the north-east, and the Interior. There is no Atlantis office in the province.

Metro Vancouver. Port terminals, shipbuilding in North Vancouver, the Burnaby refinery and terminal, fabrication shops in Surrey, Delta and Richmond, and aerospace maintenance around the airport. See NDT consulting in Vancouver, NDT training in Vancouver, Practical NDT in Vancouver, NDT ERP in Vancouver, and method pages for ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle testing and radiographic testing in Vancouver.

Fraser Valley. Abbotsford and Chilliwack have fabrication, agricultural processing and aerospace maintenance, supported remotely and onsite.

Vancouver Island. Victoria and Esquimalt for naval refit and ship repair; Nanaimo and the island's mills and port facilities.

Kitimat, Terrace and Prince Rupert. LNG, aluminium smelting and port terminals on the north coast.

Prince George and the central Interior. Pulp mills, sawmills, pipelines and supply bases. See Practical NDT in Prince George.

Fort St. John, Dawson Creek and Chetwynd. Montney gas production, gas plants and pipeline construction.

Kamloops, Kelowna and the Kootenays. Mining near Logan Lake, the metallurgical complex at Trail, mills and fabrication.

Province-wide: the British Columbia Practical NDT hub for simulator practice before practical examinations, and the Vancouver digital twin page.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: You outline your methods, projects, owners and deadlines on a call; we agree scope, deliverables and the remote and onsite split; the work is drafted and reviewed with your team; and for ongoing cover we remain your named Level III. Quotes are given on request after scoping.

  1. Scoping call. Your operation, methods and techniques, the certifications your people hold, the codes and project specifications you work to, and mobilisation or audit dates.
  2. Document request. Your written practice, quality-manual sections, procedures, technique sheets and a sample of certification files, plus the project specification if one applies.
  3. Proposal. A written scope: deliverables, remote and onsite work and who does it. Quotes on request.
  4. Delivery. Drafting and review with your team; examinations under your written practice; site visits planned around project schedules, outages and travel to remote locations.
  5. Handover or ongoing cover. Final documents and records under your control, or continuing Level III approvals, support and audit attendance.

To start, book a Level III scoping call for British Columbia.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Owners and EPCs want to know whose name is on the written practice and procedures; with Atlantis that is clear from the first call. Anoop also leads Atlantis NDT's SNT-TC-1A-based training, which keeps documents and training consistent.

Frequently asked questions about NDT Level III consulting in British Columbia

Do BC inspection contractors need an ASNT Level III?

Only when they certify personnel to an ASNT scheme, which LNG, pipeline and terminal project specifications from US or international EPCs often require. Work that only requires CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification does not need an ASNT written practice.

Can our CGSB-certified technicians work under an SNT-TC-1A written practice?

Yes. The written practice can recognise CGSB certification as evidence of training and experience and set out the employer examinations needed for SNT-TC-1A certification. The CGSB certificate itself stays with the certification body.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in British Columbia?

Technical Safety BC, under the Safety Standards Act and the Power Engineers, Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Safety Regulation. Contractors working on that equipment must hold a Technical Safety BC licence.

Who regulates pipelines in BC?

The BC Energy Regulator regulates oil and gas pipelines within the province; utility pipelines fall under the BC Utilities Commission, and interprovincial pipelines under the Canada Energy Regulator. CSA Z662 is the core technical standard.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in BC?

Gamma radiography requires a CNSC licence and CNSC-certified exposure device operators. WorkSafeBC's Occupational Health and Safety Regulation also applies to radiation safety at BC workplaces.

What changed with CGSB in 2026?

The Canadian General Standards Board ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Notices from Natural Resources Canada and CWB Group say CAN/CGSB-48.9712 stays valid and certifications continue; confirm the current certification body for new certifications and renewals.

Can you write procedures for LNG cryogenic welds?

Yes, procedures and technique sheets for UT, PAUT, TOFD and RT written to the project's governing codes and specification, with demonstration on representative specimens where the specification requires it.

Can an outsourced Level III approve our procedures?

Yes, when your written practice designates that Level III and they are certified in the relevant methods. The review must be genuine and traceable.

How much does Level III consulting cost in BC?

It depends on scope: methods, project requirements, whether you need a new written practice or a review, how many people need examining and how much onsite time, including travel to remote sites. Quotes are given on request after scoping.

Do you provide Technical Safety BC inspections?

No. Atlantis is not a jurisdictional inspection body. We provide Level III support to NDT programmes and inspection programmes, such as technique selection and procedure review.

Can you train our technicians?

Yes, to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, online and onsite at your facility. Atlantis does not train toward CGSB certification. See NDT training and practise on the Practical NDT simulator before practical examinations.

Talk to a Level III about your British Columbia programme

Whether you are mobilising a PAUT crew to an LNG site at Kitimat, inspecting hull welds in North Vancouver, running thickness surveys in a Prince George pulp mill or radiographing girth welds in the north-east, the Level III questions are the same: does the written practice match the project, are the procedures right, and can you prove each technician is qualified under the scheme the owner requires? NDT Level III Consulting Services in Denmark

Short answer: Atlantis NDT gives Danish fabricators, inspection contractors and plant operators access to an ASNT NDT Level III for work governed by US codes and US customers: SNT-TC-1A written practices, ASME, API and AWS procedures and technique sheets, employer examinations, outside-agency and interim Level III cover, and audit preparation. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, leads every engagement, remotely or onsite at your facility. Atlantis has no Danish office and is not a Danish or Nordic certification body.

Denmark already has a mature NDT certification system. Personnel certification under EN ISO 9712 and the Nordic ISO 9712/Nordtest scheme is handled by accredited bodies; FORCE Certification A/S, accredited by DANAK, certifies NDT operators under both, and the Danish Society for NDT is the national technical society. Atlantis does not compete with that system, does not issue ISO 9712 certificates and does not train toward them. Our role is narrower and specific: a Danish yard building transition pieces for a US developer, a fabricator welding to AWS D1.1 for an American client, a defence supplier delivering to a US prime, or an inspection company asked by a US auditor to produce an SNT-TC-1A written practice and a named Level III. If you are in one of those positions, request a Denmark Level III consultation.

Why Danish NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: A Danish employer that certifies its own NDT personnel under ASNT SNT-TC-1A must have a written practice approved by a Level III, written procedures for every method and a Level III who examines and certifies Level I and II staff. Danish suppliers on US-code projects and to US primes are usually asked to name that Level III at audit.

Denmark's NDT market is shaped by three industries that sell heavily abroad. The first is wind. Vestas, headquartered in Aarhus, and Siemens Gamesa, with its onshore and offshore operations at Brande and a blade plant in Aalborg, sit at the centre of a supply chain of tower, flange, casting, nacelle and foundation suppliers. Ørsted, one of the world's largest offshore wind developers, has built and operated wind farms in Danish waters for decades and has developed projects off the US East Coast. Esbjerg on the west coast is the main base port for North Sea offshore wind installation and service. Monopiles, transition pieces and secondary steel from Danish and nearby yards are fabricated to EN 1090, ISO 5817 and DNV standards and examined with UT, MT and VT on a very large scale, and when the end client or developer is American, the specification can add AWS D1.1 or ASNT-based personnel requirements.

The second is North Sea oil and gas. Esbjerg has long been the hub for Danish offshore production, and the redeveloped Tyra gas field, operated by TotalEnergies, returned to production in 2024. Offshore platforms, risers, pipelines and process modules need in-service inspection, and contractors work from Esbjerg to Danish authority requirements and the operator's specifications. The Baltic Pipe, which carries Norwegian gas across Denmark to Poland, added a major onshore and offshore pipeline construction and inspection programme.

The third is refining, process and pharmaceuticals. Denmark has two refineries: the Kalundborg Refinery, acquired by the Klesch Group from Equinor in 2022 and processing around 107,000 barrels of crude per day, and the Fredericia refinery operated by Crossbridge Energy. Kalundborg is also home to one of Europe's largest pharmaceutical production sites and the Kalundborg Symbiosis industrial park, with Novo Nordisk and Novonesis among the large process operators. Large district-heating and combined heat-and-power plants around Copenhagen, Aarhus, Odense and Aalborg carry boilers, heat exchangers and high-energy piping. Maritime work runs through Lindø Industrial Park in Odense, repair yards in Frederikshavn and Skagen, and offshore service vessels out of Esbjerg. Defence and aerospace manufacturing includes Terma in Aarhus, a supplier of structural and composite parts to the F-35 programme.

Regulation sits on top of this. Pressure equipment placed on the market must meet the Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU; equipment in use falls under Danish working environment rules enforced by the Danish Working Environment Authority (Arbejdstilsynet), with periodic inspection carried out by accredited inspection bodies. Industrial radiography requires authorisation from the Danish Health Authority, Radiation Protection (often still referred to by its former initials, SIS), under the Radiation Protection Act. Offshore installations add their own Danish authority oversight. None of these regulators requires SNT-TC-1A. US customers and US codes do, and that is the gap an ASNT Level III consultant fills.

EN ISO 9712, Nordtest and SNT-TC-1A: which applies to your Danish work?

Direct answer: EN ISO 9712 (with the Nordic Nordtest variant) is the default in Denmark and covers most EU-code fabrication and in-service work. SNT-TC-1A applies when a US code, US owner or US customer specification requires employer-based certification. Danish contractors serving both markets often need technicians certified under both and a written practice that explains the split.

The two systems answer the same question in different ways. ISO 9712 places certification with an independent, accredited body; the certificate belongs to the individual. SNT-TC-1A makes the employer responsible; certification is granted under the employer's written practice, using examinations administered by a Level III, and lapses when the person leaves. ASME Section V generally refers to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 for personnel qualification, so a pressure vessel built in Denmark to ASME Section VIII, or piping built to ASME B31.3 for a US-designed plant, tends to bring SNT-TC-1A with it.

The practical answer for many Danish companies is a hybrid written practice. It recognises existing ISO 9712 or Nordtest training and experience, adds employer-specific and practical examinations where a US contract requires them, and names a responsible Level III. We write those documents so a Danish auditor and an American auditor can both read them and find what they expect.

Level III services for Danish employers

Direct answer: Atlantis provides the Level III functions a Danish company needs for SNT-TC-1A and US-code work: written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets, personnel examinations, outside-agency and interim Level III cover, and audit preparation. Scope, deliverables and the remote and onsite split are agreed on a scoping call.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: The written practice is the employer's own rulebook for training, examining, certifying and recertifying NDT personnel. Under SNT-TC-1A it is the document that auditors test. We write it around how your Danish company actually works, then check your certification records against it.

Danish companies starting their first SNT-TC-1A programme tend to make one of two mistakes. The first is copying an American template wholesale, which leaves in references to US-specific arrangements and methods the company does not use. The second is translating an ISO 9712 quality procedure into SNT-TC-1A vocabulary without changing the logic, so the document still assumes a third-party body certifies people and never says who administers the employer's examinations. Both fail the first serious audit.

A written practice we prepare covers:

  • Scope: methods, techniques, product forms and the codes or specifications that apply.
  • Levels and duties for trainees, Level I, Level II and Level III, including signature authority.
  • Training and experience requirements, cross-referenced to the training requirements matrix, with a clear rule for crediting prior ISO 9712 or Nordtest training and experience.
  • Examinations: general, specific and practical; grading; re-examination; and who administers each.
  • Vision examinations and their interval.
  • Records: content of each technician's file, retention and access.
  • Interrupted service, revocation, recertification and outside-agency arrangements.

An audit tests the document against the evidence. We sample certification files and check each one for training, experience, examination grades, vision results and the right signatures, then return a numbered findings list with clause references and fixes. See written practice development and SNT-TC-1A certification guidance for background.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Denmark

Direct answer: Every method needs a written procedure that satisfies the governing code, and many jobs need a technique sheet for the specific weld or component. In Denmark that code is EN, ISO or DNV for most wind and offshore steel, ASME for US-designed pressure equipment, AWS for structural steel on US contracts, and API-based owner practices for refinery maintenance.

  • Offshore wind foundations and towers. Thick-section longitudinal and circumferential welds in monopiles and transition pieces, flange welds and secondary steel are typically examined with UT, often PAUT, plus MT and VT. On European contracts the procedures follow EN ISO 17640 and related standards; where a US contract applies, AWS D1.1 or a customer specification may govern acceptance. A procedure has to make clear which acceptance standard applies to which weld.
  • Wind turbine components. Castings, forgings, bearings and bolted connections bring UT, MT and PT on components that are shipped worldwide. OEM specifications govern; procedures and technique sheets must reflect them exactly.
  • Offshore oil and gas. Corrosion mapping, weld inspection after modification and pipeline work around Esbjerg follow operator specifications. See pipeline Level III support.
  • Refining and process. At Kalundborg and Fredericia, piping, vessels, exchangers and tanks are inspected during turnarounds under owner practices that often echo API 510, 570 and 653. See petrochemical Level III support.
  • Pharmaceutical plants. Stainless process piping and vessels, sometimes designed to ASME B31.3, ASME BPE and ASME Section VIII, with VT, borescope and RT or UT as the code requires.
  • Power and district heating. Boilers, headers and high-energy piping in combined heat-and-power plants. See power generation Level III support.
  • Maritime. Repair and conversion work at Danish yards follows classification society rules. See maritime Level III support.

Our procedure development work produces procedures with defined essential variables, calibration and reference blocks, coverage and scan plans, recording and evaluation rules and the acceptance criteria. Where a PAUT or TOFD application needs a performance demonstration, we plan it with you. We review existing Danish procedures as well as writing new ones, which is often the faster route when a European procedure only needs a US-code annex.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Danish crews

Direct answer: An outside-agency Level III, the role UK and European buyers often call a responsible Level 3, is a Level III who is not your employee but formally holds the Level III duties in your written practice. For a Danish company with a modest SNT-TC-1A workload, it is usually the most efficient model.

The arrangement must be explicit. Your written practice names the outside agency, defines what the Level III approves, describes how examinations are administered and graded, and states who keeps the records. We draft that language as part of setting up the engagement.

Three engagement models cover most Danish needs:

  • Ongoing outside-agency Level III. A standing arrangement for written practice ownership, procedure approval, examinations, technical questions and customer audits.
  • Project-based work. A defined package, such as an SNT-TC-1A written practice for a new US contract, a UT and MT procedure set for a foundation campaign, or technique sheets for a vessel order.
  • Audit-preparation sprint. A focused review ahead of a known audit by a US developer, OEM or prime.

When a Level III leaves at a bad moment, interim Level III cover keeps approvals and examinations moving. Most document work runs remotely; practical examinations, demonstrations and audits are carried out onsite at your facility. Ask about outside-agency Level 3 support for your Danish team.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Danish NDT employers face customer and developer audits on export work, owner audits at refineries and offshore installations, and accreditation assessments by DANAK for inspection bodies and laboratories. Atlantis prepares the NDT programme evidence: written practice, procedures, certification files and Level III records.

A US developer or OEM audit samples a technician's file, the procedure used on a specific weld, the Level III approval of that procedure and the calibration of the equipment used. Owner audits at Kalundborg, Fredericia or offshore installations add owner-specific approvals and witness requirements. DANAK assessments of ISO/IEC 17020 inspection bodies and ISO/IEC 17025 laboratories are a separate process; Atlantis has no part in DANAK decisions, but we can make sure the NDT technical content the assessor samples is consistent and traceable.

Our readiness reviews check that:

  • The written practice matches current methods, staff and customer requirements.
  • Each certified technician's file is complete, current and correctly signed.
  • Each procedure in use is current, approved and cited on reports.
  • Equipment and reference standards are calibrated and traceable.
  • The Level III arrangement is documented.

Aerospace and defence suppliers can read our note on Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness and the aerospace Level III audit support page.

Where in Denmark we support NDT programmes

Direct answer: Atlantis works with Danish companies remotely and onsite at their facilities. The main clusters are Esbjerg and the west coast, Jutland's wind manufacturing belt, Funen and the Lindø area, Kalundborg and western Zealand, and Greater Copenhagen.

Esbjerg and the west coast. Offshore oil and gas operations, offshore wind installation and service, fabrication yards and the contractors that support North Sea work. Many of these companies already run ISO 9712 programmes and add SNT-TC-1A where a US contract requires it.

Aarhus, Brande, Herning and central Jutland. Wind turbine design and manufacturing, component suppliers and defence manufacturing. Procedure and technique work for castings, forgings and welded components is common here.

Aalborg and northern Jutland. Blade manufacturing, heavy steel fabrication for offshore foundations, the port, and repair yards in Frederikshavn and Skagen.

Odense, Funen and Fredericia. Lindø Industrial Park's heavy fabrication and offshore wind activity, the Fredericia refinery and port, and process industry in the Triangle Region.

Kalundborg and western Zealand. The Kalundborg Refinery, large pharmaceutical and biotech production and the Kalundborg Symbiosis industrial park.

Greater Copenhagen. Head offices of developers, engineering firms and inspection companies, combined heat-and-power plants and pharmaceutical sites. For neighbouring markets, see Norway, Germany and the Netherlands.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: A scoping call comes first, then a review of your documents and records, then delivery of the written practice, procedures, examinations or audit support you need. Most work is remote; onsite visits are planned for practical examinations, demonstrations and audits. You receive a quote after the call.

  1. Scoping call. Methods, staff, certification schemes in use (ISO 9712, Nordtest, SNT-TC-1A), customers, codes and deadlines.
  2. Document request. Your current written practice or quality procedure, NDT procedures, a sample of certification files and the customer requirements driving the work.
  3. Review and plan. Gaps, deliverables, sequence and any onsite needs agreed in writing.
  4. Delivery. Documents drafted, reviewed with your team and issued under revision control.
  5. Examinations. General and specific examinations administered remotely under controlled conditions where your written practice permits; practical examinations onsite on real specimens.
  6. Ongoing support. Outside-agency Level III service for approvals, questions, recertification and audits.

Pricing is quote on request: affordable, accessible and fully customisable. Request a quote for Level III support in Denmark.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who is the named Level III on documents Atlantis prepares and approves. Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training delivered online or onsite, the Practical NDT simulator for practice before practical exams, and an NDT ERP that records ISO 9712 and ASNT certifications side by side. These complement, and do not replace, ISO 9712 certification from an accredited Danish or European body.

Frequently asked questions about NDT Level III consulting in Denmark

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised in Denmark?

SNT-TC-1A is not a Danish national scheme; EN ISO 9712 and the Nordtest scheme are. SNT-TC-1A is recognised where a contract, code or customer requires it, which in practice means ASME and AWS work and supply to US developers, OEMs and primes.

Can an ASNT Level III be our responsible Level 3 in Denmark?

For an SNT-TC-1A programme, yes, as an outside agency named in your written practice. For ISO 9712 certification the certification body sets the rules, and for aerospace work under EN 4179 or NAS 410 your customer and national aerospace NDT board decide; confirm acceptance with them first.

Who certifies NDT personnel to ISO 9712 in Denmark?

Accredited certification bodies. FORCE Certification A/S, accredited by DANAK, certifies NDT operators under ISO 9712 and the ISO 9712/Nordtest scheme. Atlantis does not certify to ISO 9712.

Does Atlantis offer ISO 9712 or Nordtest training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. We can recognise your staff's existing ISO 9712 certificates and experience inside an SNT-TC-1A written practice where the rules allow.

Who licenses industrial radiography in Denmark?

The Danish Health Authority, Radiation Protection, under the Radiation Protection Act and its executive orders. Radiography sources, X-ray equipment and radiation protection arrangements must be authorised before work starts.

Do offshore wind contracts for US developers need SNT-TC-1A?

Some do and some do not. It depends on the contract's personnel qualification clause and the referenced codes. Check the specification; if it names SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 or AWS D1.1, an employer written practice and a named Level III are usually expected.

Can you write ASME Section V procedures for a Danish fabricator?

Yes. We write procedures for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET to ASME Section V and the construction code, plus technique sheets for specific components, and can add US-code annexes to existing European procedures.

Can examinations be held remotely for Danish staff?

General and specific written examinations can be administered remotely under controlled conditions defined in your written practice. Practical examinations require real specimens and equipment and take place onsite.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Denmark?

Quote on request. The quote depends on methods, the state of your documents, how many people need examination and how many onsite days are required.

Can you help with a DANAK assessment?

We can prepare the NDT technical content an assessor samples: procedures, competence records and method validation. DANAK conducts the assessment and makes the decision.

Do you provide inspection programme support at Danish refineries?

We support the NDT side of API 510, 570 and 653 style programmes: technique selection, procedure review and data quality. See API 510 support, API 570 support and API 653 support. We do not sell risk-based inspection or fitness-for-service assessments.

Does Atlantis have an office in Denmark?

No. Atlantis supports Danish clients remotely and travels to your facility for onsite work.

Talk to a Level III about your Danish NDT programme

If a US developer, OEM, prime or code is asking your Danish team for an SNT-TC-1A written practice, US-code procedures or a named Level III, start with a short call. Book a Level III consultation for Denmark or send us a procedure for review.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Indiana

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III services to Indiana employers: outsourced or interim Level III, SNT-TC-1A written practices, procedures and technique sheets, personnel qualification exams under your written practice, and audit readiness. The work is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, and delivered remotely and onsite at your mill, refinery, plant or shop. Atlantis has no office in Indiana. Scope and fees are set on a short call, and quotes are on request.

Indiana is a manufacturing state first and an energy state second, and its NDT programmes reflect that. The Calumet Region along Lake Michigan holds the largest concentration of integrated steelmaking left in the United States and one of the biggest inland refineries in the country. Central Indiana builds aero-engines, transmissions and diesel engines. The north-central counties around Elkhart build most of the recreational vehicles sold in North America. The Ohio River and Wabash valleys run coal and gas power stations, aluminium smelting and a small crude refinery. A steel mill's crane-hook MT programme, an aero-engine supplier's penetrant line and a refinery contractor's PAUT crew all need a Level III, but they need very different things from one. This page explains what each Indiana sector asks of its Level III, which state agencies matter, and how to request an Indiana Level III consultation.

Why Indiana NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A and CP-189, an NDT programme only works if a Level III is responsible for it: someone has to approve the written practice, approve procedures, write and grade qualification exams and sign certifications. Indiana's mix of steel, refining, aerospace, automotive and power work means most programmes are audited by demanding customers, so that Level III role cannot be an afterthought.

The Calumet Region: Whiting, East Chicago, Gary, Burns Harbor and Portage

The north-west corner of the state is heavy industry on a scale few places match. BP's Whiting refinery processes heavy crude through cokers, hydrotreaters and crude units that need thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD weld examination and large radiography scopes every turnaround. Next door, the integrated steel mills at Indiana Harbor in East Chicago, Gary Works and Burns Harbor run blast furnaces, basic oxygen furnaces, casters, hot and cold rolling mills and coke-related plant. Their maintenance and reliability groups use MT on crane hooks, ladles, trunnions and shafts, UT on rolls, rails and heavy weldments, and VT and MT on structural repairs. Northern Indiana Public Service Company's generating stations at Michigan City and Wheatfield, the Port of Indiana at Burns Harbor, and fabricators around Hammond, Portage, La Porte and Crown Point add boiler, structural and fabrication work. Contract inspection companies that serve this corridor are audited by refinery owners and steel producers, each with its own contractor qualification checklist.

Central Indiana: Indianapolis, Columbus and Lafayette

Indianapolis is an aero-engine town. Rolls-Royce builds and services gas-turbine engines there, and a ring of machine shops, forging houses and heat treaters supplies them. Allison Transmission and other drivetrain makers add production NDT. In Columbus, Cummins' engine and component plants and their suppliers use MT, PT, ET and UT on castings, forgings and machined parts. Lafayette has Subaru's assembly plant, aerospace and engine suppliers, and Purdue University's engineering programmes. Aerospace work here is driven by prime-contractor specifications and, for many suppliers, Nadcap NDT accreditation, which is where a strong written practice and a Level III who knows the audit criteria pay for themselves.

Northern and north-central Indiana: Elkhart, South Bend and Fort Wayne

Elkhart County and its neighbours build RVs, trailers, and aluminium and steel frames in volume. Most of that inspection is VT of welds, with some PT and MT, and many shops have never had a formal SNT-TC-1A programme until a customer or an insurer asked for one. South Bend and Mishawaka have aerospace, defence and automotive suppliers. Fort Wayne and the surrounding counties have General Motors' truck assembly, steel processing and electric-arc steelmaking nearby, plus wire, cable and defence-electronics manufacturers.

Southern Indiana and the Ohio River

Evansville, Mount Vernon and Newburgh combine power generation, aluminium, plastics and chemicals, and CountryMark's refinery at Mount Vernon. Toyota's assembly plant at Princeton draws a large supplier base. Coal and gas stations such as Gibson, Rockport and Edwardsport need boiler-tube, header and piping inspection during outages. Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane supports defence electronics and ordnance programmes, and its contractors work under defence quality requirements. Terre Haute adds manufacturing and chemicals. Interstate gas and liquids pipelines cross the whole state.

Indiana regulators that touch NDT

Radiography. Indiana signed an agreement with the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission in late September 2026 to become an Agreement State, with the Indiana Department of Homeland Security taking over licensing of radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, from the NRC. Because the change is so recent, confirm the current licensing authority with the state before you apply for, amend or transfer a radioactive materials licence. Radiation-producing X-ray equipment is registered with the state. Radiation-safety obligations sit beside, not inside, the SNT-TC-1A programme, and a Level III should make sure the two line up.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Indiana's boiler and pressure vessel safety programme sits within the Department of Homeland Security's Division of Fire and Building Safety, working within the National Board framework. Repairs and alterations to boilers and pressure vessels are done by authorised repair organisations, and the NDT in those repairs must follow the construction code and the organisation's quality manual.

Pipelines. The Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission's Pipeline Safety Division oversees intrastate gas pipeline operators. Interstate gas and hazardous-liquid pipelines crossing Indiana are regulated by the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA).

Level III services for Indiana employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT covers the full set of Level III functions an SNT-TC-1A programme requires: written practice, procedures, technique sheets, exams and certification records, programme audits and audit support, plus interim cover when your Level III leaves. Each service can be bought on its own or combined into a retained arrangement. The table maps them to typical Indiana clients.

ServiceWhat it coversTypical Indiana client type
Outsourced Level III of recordNamed Level III responsible for the written practice, procedure approval, exams and certification sign-offCalumet Region contract inspection companies; RV and trailer manufacturers starting a formal programme
Interim Level IIICover while you recruit, keeping certifications current and audits on trackSteel mill and refinery maintenance groups whose Level III has retired or left

For the full service description, see ASNT Level III consulting services. Sector pages that match Indiana's industry map include Level III audit support for steel and metals, refining, aerospace, power generation, pipeline and fabrication.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own document that sets how NDT personnel are trained, examined, certified and recertified. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, so the written practice is what an auditor actually holds you to. Atlantis writes new written practices for Indiana employers, rewrites outdated ones and audits programmes against them.

The most common Indiana problem is not a missing written practice but a stale one. A steel mill or a forge may have adopted a written practice ten owners and three Level IIIs ago. Since then, methods have been added, equipment has changed, phased array has replaced some conventional UT, and the training and experience records no longer match what the document says. When a customer audits, the gap is obvious. A Level III review fixes the document so it describes the programme you actually run, and then fixes the records so they support it.

A good written practice for an Indiana employer usually needs to settle these points clearly:

  • Which methods and techniques the company performs, and at which levels, including whether PAUT and TOFD are separate certifications or part of UT.
  • Training and experience requirements for each level and method. Atlantis links these to the training requirements matrix and to your clients' requirements rather than inventing new numbers.
  • How general, specific and practical exams are written, administered and graded, and who may administer them.
  • Vision examination requirements and how records are kept.
  • Recertification intervals, interrupted service and how a technician regains certification.
  • How outside agencies, including an outsourced Level III, fit into the programme.
  • How customer-specific requirements are handled, for example aerospace prime specifications or a refinery owner's contractor rules.

Production shops such as RV, trailer and automotive suppliers often need a lean written practice that covers VT and one or two surface methods. Contract inspection companies serving the Whiting refinery and the Calumet mills need a broader one covering UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and sometimes ET, with clear rules for technicians who move between clients. Aerospace suppliers in Indianapolis, Lafayette and South Bend usually need a written practice that also satisfies prime-contractor and Nadcap-style expectations. Read more on written practice development, the industry-specific written practice for steel and metals, written practice for refining and written practice for aerospace, and our SNT-TC-1A guidance.

Audits work the other way round. We start from your written practice, sample certification files, procedures, technique sheets, equipment calibration and exam records, and report gaps with a fix for each one. If an owner or customer audit is booked, we work back from that date. You can ask for a written practice audit for your Indiana programme.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Indiana

Direct answer: Indiana NDT procedures must be written to the code or specification that governs the work, and that varies sharply by sector: ASME and API for refining and boilers, AWS for structural steel and bridges, customer and aerospace specifications for engines, and API 1104 and federal pipeline rules for pipelines. A Level III writes the procedure to the right document and approves technique sheets beneath it.

The codes that come up most often in Indiana work include:

  • Refining and chemicals (Whiting, Mount Vernon, Terre Haute): ASME Section V for NDE methods, ASME Section VIII and B31.3 for vessels and process piping, API 510, 570 and 653 for in-service inspection of vessels, piping and tanks, API 577 for weld inspection, and the owner's own engineering standards.
  • Power generation (NIPSCO, Duke Energy and other stations): ASME Section I and B31.1 for boilers and power piping, Section V for methods, and the National Board Inspection Code for repairs.
  • Steel mills: AWS D1.1 for structural repairs, crane and lifting-equipment standards for hooks and lifting devices, ASTM methods for rolls, forgings and plate, and the mill's own reliability specifications.
  • Bridges and highways: AWS D1.5 for bridge welding and Indiana Department of Transportation requirements on state work.
  • Aerospace and engines (Indianapolis, Lafayette, South Bend): prime-contractor specifications, ASTM E1417 for penetrant, ASTM E1444 for magnetic particle, and the personnel qualification standard named in the purchase order.
  • Pipelines: API 1104 for welding and NDT of pipeline girth welds, plus the operator's own procedures under federal pipeline rules.
  • Automotive and heavy equipment (Columbus, Princeton, Fort Wayne, Elkhart): customer drawings and specifications, which frequently call up ASTM practices and set their own acceptance criteria.

A procedure is only as good as the technique sheet a technician carries to the job. For a refinery contractor, that means technique sheets for each common geometry, material and thickness range; for a mill, sheets for each critical component family; for an aerospace supplier, sheets tied to part numbers and customer approvals. Atlantis writes and approves both layers and, where a client or code requires it, supports procedure demonstration on representative specimens. See NDT technical procedure development and procedure qualification and demonstration.

For inspection-programme work around API 510, 570 and 653, Atlantis supports the NDT side: technique selection, procedure and technique-sheet approval, data quality and personnel qualification. Inspection decisions stay with the owner's certified inspectors. See API 510 pressure vessel inspector services, API 570 piping inspector services and API 653 tank inspector services.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Indiana crews

Direct answer: Most Indiana inspection companies and manufacturers do not need a full-time Level III on payroll; they need the Level III functions performed reliably and on time. An outsourced Level III of record provides those functions under contract. An interim Level III covers the gap when your own Level III leaves, retires or is out for a long period.

In practice, outsourced Level III support for an Indiana client usually includes approving and maintaining the written practice, approving procedures and technique sheets, preparing and grading general and specific exams, administering or overseeing practical exams on suitable specimens, reviewing certification files, and being available when a customer auditor wants to speak to the Level III. Remote work handles most document and exam-preparation tasks. Onsite visits handle practical exams, procedure demonstrations and audit days.

Interim cover is a common need in the Calumet Region and in central Indiana manufacturing, where many long-serving Level IIIs are retiring. When the Level III goes, certifications still expire, new hires still need exams, and turnarounds and customer audits do not move. An interim engagement keeps the programme legal while you recruit or develop a successor. It also gives you a documented hand-over, which matters if your next customer audit asks who approved the procedures in use. Read more on interim NDT Level III support, what to do when your Level III resigns, Level III succession planning and what an outside Level III can and cannot do.

If you are developing a Level III from within, the Indiana NDT training page covers ASNT SNT-TC-1A training for Indiana crews, including Level III exam preparation. Trainees can practise methods on the Practical NDT simulator for Indiana, which is practice only and does not replace practical exams on real specimens. To discuss cover for your crew, ask about interim Level III cover in Indiana.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Indiana NDT programmes are audited from several directions: refinery and steel owners auditing contractors, aerospace primes and Nadcap-style auditors auditing suppliers, ISO 9001 registrars auditing quality systems, and ISO/IEC 17025 assessors auditing laboratories. Atlantis prepares programmes for these audits and supports you on the day.

What auditors in Indiana tend to look at first:

  • Whether the written practice matches the methods and levels actually in use.
  • Whether every certified technician's file has training hours, experience records, exam results with the correct weighting, and a current vision examination.
  • Whether procedures are approved by a Level III, controlled, and at the current revision on the shop floor.
  • Whether technique sheets exist for the work being done, and whether they trace to an approved procedure.
  • Whether equipment, probes, wedges, blocks and reference standards have current calibration or verification records.
  • Whether you can show which procedure revision and which technician were used on a past inspection.

For aerospace suppliers in Indianapolis, Lafayette and South Bend, audit readiness usually means preparing for prime-contractor source audits and, where you hold or seek it, Nadcap NDT accreditation. See Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness and NAS 410 responsible Level 3 for context. For contract inspection companies serving refineries and mills, the owner's contractor audit is the one that decides whether you work. Laboratories that test samples for steel, castings and forgings may be working toward ISO/IEC 17025, where personnel competence and method validation records are central.

A typical audit-readiness engagement is a gap assessment against the written practice and the auditor's criteria, a list of corrections with owners and dates, and a final check before the audit. See NDT programme audit and gap assessment and multi-site programme harmonisation if you run crews in Indiana and neighbouring states. When an audit date is set, book an Indiana audit-readiness review.

Where can I find an NDT Level III consultant in Indiana?

Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to Indiana employers remotely and onsite at your facility, from the Calumet Region to Evansville. We have no Indiana office; we travel to your site when the work needs it.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Ireland

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to employers and contractors in Ireland: outside-agency (outsourced) and interim Level III cover, SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, NDT procedures and technique sheets to ASME, API and AWS codes, personnel examinations under your written practice, and audit preparation. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, and run remotely or onsite at your facility. Atlantis has no office in Ireland and holds no Irish or European certification-body accreditation.

That last sentence matters, so it comes first. In Ireland the normal route for NDT personnel certification is EN ISO 9712 (published here as I.S. EN ISO 9712), and many Irish technicians carry certificates issued under ISO 9712-based schemes such as PCN. Atlantis does not certify anyone to EN ISO 9712 and does not run ISO 9712 courses. What Atlantis does is help the large group of Irish sites and contractors whose customers, parent companies or project codes are American: the US-owned pharmaceutical, biotech and semiconductor plants in Cork Harbour, Dublin, Kildare and Limerick; contractors building or maintaining equipment to ASME Section VIII and ASME B31.3; fabricators shipping to US clients under AWS D1.1; and anyone asked by a US auditor for an SNT-TC-1A written practice and a named Level III. If that describes your situation, you can request an Ireland Level III consultation and we will scope it on a call.

Why Irish NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: Any Irish employer that certifies its own NDT staff under ASNT SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice approved by a Level III, written procedures for each method, and a Level III to examine and certify Level I and II personnel. Irish sites working to US codes and US customer quality clauses are also routinely asked to name that Level III during audits.

Ireland's NDT demand does not look like a typical heavy-industry country. There is one oil refinery, no shipbuilding industry of any size and no nuclear power. What Ireland has instead is one of the densest concentrations of US-owned advanced manufacturing in Europe, and that changes what an NDT programme has to prove. Cork Harbour, around Ringaskiddy, Little Island and Carrigtwohill, is lined with active pharmaceutical ingredient and biologics plants. Dublin's western edge at Grange Castle, the Kildare corridor around Leixlip, Limerick, Waterford, Sligo and Westport all host large pharmaceutical, biotech, semiconductor or medical-technology sites. These plants run clean steam, purified water, solvent recovery, reactors, fermenters and high-purity process piping, much of it designed to ASME Section VIII, ASME B31.3 and the ASME BPE bioprocessing standard because the engineering standards came from a US parent or a US engineering contractor.

Energy is the second anchor. The Whitegate refinery in Cork Harbour, owned by Irving Oil, is Ireland's only oil refinery, with a capacity of about 75,000 barrels per day. The Corrib gas terminal at Bellanaboy in County Mayo processes gas from the Atlantic, and Gas Networks Ireland runs the transmission system and the interconnectors to Scotland. ESB's power stations, including the large Moneypoint station on the Shannon Estuary, along with the gas-fired stations at Aghada, Whitegate, Huntstown and Poolbeg, carry boilers, heat-recovery steam generators, high-energy piping and storage tanks that need periodic inspection. Aughinish Alumina near Foynes runs digesters, heat exchangers and pressure piping in caustic service. Offshore wind is the growth sector: Arklow Bank has operated since the mid-2000s, east-coast projects are in development, and the Shannon Foynes port has positioned itself for floating wind. Each of these brings welding, fabrication and in-service inspection, and each has its own owner specification.

Then there is the long tail: food and dairy processors with stainless pressure vessels and evaporators, breweries and distilleries, data-centre construction with structural steel and standby-power fuel systems, the Shannon aviation and leasing cluster with its maintenance and component work, and bridge and rail structures maintained for Transport Infrastructure Ireland and Iarnród Éireann. Many of the contractors serving these sites are small. A fabrication shop with two or three welding inspectors or a mechanical contractor with a handful of UT and PT technicians cannot justify a full-time Level III, but the moment a US-owned client asks for an SNT-TC-1A written practice, someone has to own it. That is where ASNT Level III consulting services fit.

Regulation shapes the work too. Pressure equipment placed on the market must meet the Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU as transposed into Irish law, with the Health and Safety Authority (HSA) responsible for market surveillance and workplace enforcement. In use, Part 10 and Schedule 12 of the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work (General Application) Regulations require specified pressure vessels to be examined periodically by a competent person. Industrial radiography with sealed sources or X-ray sets needs an authorisation from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which is the national radiation regulator under the Radiological Protection Act 1991 and the Ionising Radiation Regulations 2019. Northern Ireland is a different jurisdiction, with HSENI and the Pressure Systems Safety Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2004; for UK work see our UK NDT consulting page.

Which certification scheme applies in Ireland: EN ISO 9712 or SNT-TC-1A?

Direct answer: Both are used. EN ISO 9712 is the European norm and the default for Irish and EU-code work, with third-party certificates issued by accredited bodies. ASNT SNT-TC-1A is an employer-based system used where US codes, US owners or US customer specifications apply. Many Irish contractors need both, and the written practice must say which governs which work.

The difference is structural, not cosmetic. Under EN ISO 9712, an independent certification body examines and certifies the individual, and the certificate travels with the technician. Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its own people against its own written practice, using examinations administered by a Level III; the certification is valid only while the technician works for that employer. ASME Section V refers to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 for personnel qualification in most cases, and ASME Section VIII and B31.3 rely on Section V, which is why US-designed pharmaceutical and process plants in Ireland often end up asking for SNT-TC-1A certification even when the inspection contractor's staff already hold ISO 9712 certificates.

A common Irish arrangement is the hybrid: technicians hold ISO 9712 certificates, and the employer adds an SNT-TC-1A written practice that recognises their existing training and experience, adds the employer-specific and practical examinations a US client expects, and names a responsible Level III. Done properly, this avoids duplicate training while satisfying the customer. Done badly, it produces a written practice that contradicts itself. We write these documents so the two schemes sit side by side without conflict, and we are explicit in the document about which jobs require which certification.

Direct answer: Atlantis covers the full set of Level III functions for Irish companies working to US codes: written practice authoring and review, procedures and technique sheets, examination and certification of Level I and II personnel, programme audits, audit-readiness support, and outside-agency or interim Level III cover. Every engagement is scoped on a call around your methods, codes and customers.
