The common thread is accountability. A US auditor or an owner's quality engineer wants to see that a qualified Level III approved the documents your technicians work to and examined the people who sign reports. We make that true and keep the records that prove it. The consulting overview lists every service line, and interim NDT Level 3 cover explains how short-notice support works.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own document describing how NDT personnel are trained, examined, certified and recertified. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, so the written practice is what an auditor actually checks. We write it to match how your Irish operation really works, then audit your records against it.

Most written practice problems are not technical. They are mismatches between the document and reality. A written practice copied from a previous employer may list methods the company no longer performs, require training hours nobody recorded, or name a Level III who left years ago. In Ireland a further problem is common: the document was written for EN ISO 9712 thinking and then relabelled as SNT-TC-1A, so it refers to a certification body that has no role under SNT-TC-1A, or it never explains who administers the employer's examinations. An auditor from a US-owned site will spot that quickly.

A written practice we prepare typically covers:

  • Scope: the methods, techniques and product forms the company actually inspects, and whether SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 or a customer specification governs.
  • Levels and responsibilities for trainee, Level I, Level II and Level III, including what each may sign.
  • Training and experience requirements, cross-referenced to the training requirements matrix, and how prior ISO 9712 training and experience is credited.
  • Examination structure: general, specific and practical examinations, pass criteria, re-examination and who administers each.
  • Vision examinations, near vision and colour contrast, with the testing interval stated.
  • Certification records: what goes in each file, who keeps it, and how long.
  • Interrupted service, revocation and recertification rules.
  • Outside-agency arrangements, if the Level III is not an employee.

An audit runs the other way. We take your current written practice and a sample of certification files and test one against the other: does each technician's file show the training, experience, examination grades and vision results the document requires? Findings come back as a numbered list with the clause, the evidence and the fix. More detail is on NDT written practice development and SNT-TC-1A certification guidance.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Ireland

Direct answer: Each NDT method needs a written procedure that meets the governing code, and many jobs need a technique sheet for the specific joint or component. In Ireland the code depends on the project's origin: ASME and API on US-designed plants, EN and ISO standards for EU-code fabrication under the PED, and AWS for structural steel shipped to US clients.

Ireland's sectors pull in different directions, which is why a procedure library has to be built per sector rather than copied:

  • Pharmaceutical and biotech. High-purity stainless piping and vessels to ASME B31.3 and ASME BPE, with ASME Section VIII for vessels. Visual and borescope examination of orbital welds dominates, with radiography or ultrasonic examination where the piping category requires it. Procedures need to reflect the acceptance criteria in the governing code, not a generic table.
  • Refining and gas processing. The Whitegate refinery and the Corrib terminal carry piping, vessels and tanks maintained to API-style in-service practices: thickness surveys, corrosion mapping with PAUT, weld examination after repair, and tank floor and shell inspection. See Level III audit support for refining.
  • Power generation. Boiler tubes, headers, high-energy piping and HRSG components at ESB and independent stations need UT, MT, PT and replication-style surface work during outages. See Level III support for power generation.
  • Offshore wind and structural steel. Towers, transition pieces and secondary steel are fabricated to EN 1090 and ISO 5817 quality levels with EN ISO 17640 ultrasonic testing, often under DNV standards. US-owned developers and US-code subcontracts may add AWS D1.1. See Level III support for offshore work.
  • Pipelines. Gas transmission and distribution work follows the operator's specifications, which in Ireland typically reference EN and ISO standards; contractors with international experience often also hold API 1104 procedures. See pipeline Level III support.
  • Aviation components. Maintenance and component work in the Shannon and Dublin clusters works to OEM manuals and EN 4179 or NAS 410 personnel requirements. Atlantis can help with procedures and technique review against OEM requirements; whether an ASNT Level III is acceptable as your responsible Level 3 is a question for your national aerospace NDT board and your customers, and we will say so plainly.

Our NDT procedure development work produces method procedures with clear essential variables, calibration and reference-block requirements, scanning coverage, recording and evaluation criteria, and the acceptance standard. Where a code requires demonstration, such as some PAUT and TOFD applications, we plan the demonstration and the specimens with you.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Irish crews

Direct answer: An outside-agency Level III, sometimes called a responsible Level 3, is a qualified Level III who is not your employee but formally carries the Level III functions in your written practice. For Irish companies working to SNT-TC-1A this is usually the most practical model: you get named technical accountability without a full-time salary.

The arrangement has to be written down properly. The written practice must name the outside agency, define what that Level III approves, set how examinations are administered and graded, and state how records are kept. We put that wording in place at the start, so an auditor sees a deliberate arrangement rather than a gap.

Three engagement models cover most Irish needs:

  • Ongoing outside-agency Level III. A standing arrangement: written practice ownership, procedure approval, examinations as needed, technical questions answered, and attendance at customer audits remotely or onsite.
  • Project-based work. A defined deliverable, such as a new written practice, a procedure set for a pharma shutdown, or a technique-sheet package for a fabrication contract.
  • Audit-preparation sprint. A focused review before a known customer or parent-company audit, closing gaps in documents and records.

Interim cover is the short-notice version. If your Level III leaves before a plant shutdown or a contract start, interim Level III support keeps approvals and examinations moving while you recruit. Most of this work is document- and record-based and runs remotely; practical examinations, procedure demonstrations and site audits can be done onsite at your facility.

If you are unsure which model fits, ask us about outside-agency Level 3 cover in Ireland and we will recommend one on the call.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Irish NDT employers face three kinds of audit: customer and parent-company audits from US-owned sites, owner audits on refinery and power contracts, and accreditation assessments for inspection bodies and laboratories by the Irish National Accreditation Board (INAB). Atlantis prepares the NDT programme side: written practice, procedures, certification files and Level III evidence.

Customer audits on US-owned sites follow the parent's supplier-quality model. They sample a technician's certification file, ask to see the procedure used on a specific job, check that the procedure was approved by a Level III and trace a report back to calibrated equipment. The common failure is not missing competence; it is missing evidence. Owner audits on energy contracts add site-specific requirements, such as the owner's own approval of procedures or a witness of a demonstration.

Accreditation is a separate track. Inspection bodies working to ISO/IEC 17020 and laboratories working to ISO/IEC 17025 in Ireland are assessed by INAB. Atlantis is not an accreditation body and does not grant anything; what we can do is make sure the NDT technical content an assessor will sample, including procedures, competence records and method validation, is coherent and traceable. Aerospace suppliers facing Nadcap-style audits can read our note on Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness, which explains why findings usually land on records rather than technique.

A typical audit-readiness review checks:

  • That the written practice matches current methods, staff and customer requirements.
  • That every certified technician's file is complete, in date and signed by the right person.
  • That each procedure in use is current, approved and referenced on reports.
  • That equipment calibration and reference standards are traceable.
  • That the Level III arrangement, employee or outside agency, is documented.

Where in Ireland we support NDT programmes

Direct answer: Atlantis supports employers across Ireland remotely, and onsite at your facility when the work needs it. Demand clusters in Cork Harbour, Greater Dublin and Kildare, the Shannon Estuary and Limerick, and the pharmaceutical and medtech towns of the south-east, west and north-west.

Cork and Cork Harbour. The busiest NDT market in the country: the Whitegate refinery, the Aghada and Whitegate power stations, and a long line of pharmaceutical and biologics plants at Ringaskiddy, Little Island and Carrigtwohill. Shutdowns at these sites bring in piping, vessel and tank work, and the contractors who carry it out often have to present SNT-TC-1A credentials to US-owned clients.

Dublin and Kildare. Grange Castle and the western business parks, the semiconductor campus at Leixlip, data-centre construction, Dublin Port fuel terminals, the Poolbeg and Huntstown power stations and the head offices of many contractors. Procedure and written-practice work for this region is mostly remote with onsite examinations.

Limerick, Shannon and the Shannon Estuary. Moneypoint and Tarbert power stations, Aughinish Alumina, the Foynes port, biologics and pharmaceutical manufacturing in Limerick, and the Shannon aviation cluster. This is a mixed market of energy, process and aerospace work.

Waterford, Wexford and the south-east. Pharmaceutical and medtech manufacturing, food processing and port activity.

Galway, Mayo and the west. Medical-device manufacturing in Galway, the Corrib gas terminal at Bellanaboy and pharmaceutical sites in Westport and the north-west.

Midlands and north-east. Fabrication shops, food and dairy processors, and contractors serving cross-border work. For Northern Ireland, see our UK consulting page; for comparable programmes on the continent, see Netherlands and Germany.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: Engagements start with a scoping call, move to a document and records review, then deliver written documents, examinations or audit support. Most work is remote; onsite visits are scheduled for practical examinations, demonstrations and audits. Scope and quote follow the call, with no fixed packages.

  1. Scoping call. We discuss your methods, staff, certification schemes in use (EN ISO 9712, SNT-TC-1A or both), customers, codes and deadlines.
  2. Document request. You send your current written practice, procedures, a sample of certification files and any customer requirements or audit findings.
  3. Review and plan. We identify gaps and agree deliverables, sequence and whether anything needs to happen onsite.
  4. Delivery. Written practice, procedures and technique sheets are drafted, reviewed with your team and issued under revision control.
  5. Examinations. General and specific examinations can be administered remotely under controlled conditions; practical examinations are arranged at your facility on real specimens.
  6. Ongoing support. For outside-agency arrangements, we stay on as named Level III for approvals, questions, recertification and audits.

Pricing is quote on request: affordable, accessible and fully customisable to the scope you need. Request a Level III quote for your Irish programme.

Your Level III

Atlantis consulting engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He is the named Level III on the documents Atlantis prepares and approves. Atlantis also offers SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training, including online NDT training and corporate programmes, the Practical NDT simulator for practice before practical examinations, and an NDT ERP that tracks certifications under ASNT and ISO 9712 schemes side by side. None of these replaces an EN ISO 9712 certificate from an accredited body.

Frequently asked questions about NDT Level III consulting in Ireland

Can an ASNT Level III act as our responsible Level 3 in Ireland?

For an SNT-TC-1A programme, yes: SNT-TC-1A allows the employer to use an outside agency Level III, as long as the written practice says so. For an EN ISO 9712 scheme or for aerospace work under EN 4179, the rules come from the certification body or the national aerospace NDT board, so confirm acceptance with them and with your customer before relying on an ASNT Level III.

Do Irish NDT technicians need EN ISO 9712 certification?

For most EU-code work, ISO 9712 certification is what clients and specifications expect. For work on US-designed plants or under US customer contracts, the client may instead require SNT-TC-1A certification by the employer. Many Irish technicians hold ISO 9712 certificates and are also certified by their employer under SNT-TC-1A.

Why does a US-owned pharma plant in Cork ask for SNT-TC-1A?

Because the plant's piping and vessels are often designed to ASME B31.3, ASME BPE and ASME Section VIII, which point to ASME Section V for NDT, and Section V generally references SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 for personnel qualification. The parent company's supplier-quality procedures usually follow the same logic.

Does Atlantis provide ISO 9712 or PCN training in Ireland?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. If you need ISO 9712 or PCN certification, use an accredited certification body and an approved training provider. We can help you map those certificates into an SNT-TC-1A written practice where a customer requires it.

Who licenses industrial radiography in Ireland?

The Environmental Protection Agency is the national radiation regulator. Radiography with sealed sources or X-ray equipment needs an EPA authorisation under the Ionising Radiation Regulations 2019 before work starts. Northern Ireland is regulated separately under UK law.

Who regulates pressure equipment in Ireland?

The Health and Safety Authority enforces the Pressure Equipment Directive regulations for equipment placed on the market and the General Application Regulations for equipment in use, which require periodic examination of specified pressure vessels by a competent person. Atlantis does not act as a statutory competent person; we support the NDT behind the inspection.

Can you write NDT procedures to ASME Section V for an Irish project?

Yes. We write method procedures for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET to ASME Section V and the governing construction code, and technique sheets for specific joints or components. We can also align procedures with EN ISO standards where a project mixes US and European codes.

Can examinations be done remotely from Ireland?

General and specific written examinations can be administered remotely under controlled conditions defined in your written practice. Practical examinations need real specimens and equipment, so they are arranged onsite at your facility.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Ireland?

It is quote on request. Cost depends on the number of methods, the state of your current documents, how many technicians need examination and whether onsite days are needed. Tell us the scope on a call and we will send a quote.

Can you help us prepare for an INAB assessment?

We can prepare the NDT technical side, such as procedures, competence records and method validation, so it is coherent and traceable. INAB carries out the assessment and grants accreditation; Atlantis has no role in that decision.

Do you support API 510, 570 or 653 programmes at Irish sites?

We support the NDT side of those inspection programmes: technique selection, procedure review and data quality. We do not provide risk-based inspection or fitness-for-service assessments as services. See API 510 support, API 570 support and API 653 support.

Does Atlantis have an office in Ireland?

No. Atlantis works with Irish clients remotely and travels to your facility for onsite work such as practical examinations, demonstrations and audits.

Talk to a Level III about your Irish NDT programme

If your site or your customers work to US codes and you need an SNT-TC-1A written practice, procedures, examinations or a named outside-agency Level III, start with a short call. Book a Level III consultation for Ireland or send us your written practice for review.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Kentucky

Short answer: Kentucky employers can hire Atlantis NDT for ASNT NDT Level III work without adding a full-time Level III to payroll. We act as outsourced or interim Level III, write and audit SNT-TC-1A written practices, write and approve procedures and technique sheets, administer qualification exams under your written practice, and prepare your programme for customer and owner audits. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, leads every engagement, working remotely and onsite at your plant. Atlantis has no Kentucky office. Work is scoped on a call and quoted on request.

Kentucky's NDT work is unusually spread out. A single state holds a large Ohio River refinery at Catlettsburg, a stainless steel mill at Ghent, three major vehicle assembly operations, a battery manufacturing complex, two of the world's busiest air cargo hubs, a chemical cluster at Calvert City, coal and gas power stations along every major river, and pipelines crossing from the Appalachian Basin to the Gulf Coast markets. Those employers do not share a single code, customer or audit regime. A Level III serving Kentucky has to switch between API and ASME in the morning and automotive customer specifications or aerospace maintenance requirements in the afternoon. This page sets out how that works in practice and how to talk to a Level III about your Kentucky programme.

Why Kentucky NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A places responsibility for an NDT programme on a Level III, who approves the written practice and procedures and writes and grades the exams that certify Level I and II personnel. Kentucky's refining, steel, automotive, aviation, chemical and power employers are audited by owners and customers who check exactly those things, so a capable Level III, in-house or outsourced, is essential.

Eastern Kentucky and the Big Sandy: Ashland and Catlettsburg

Marathon Petroleum's Catlettsburg refinery sits where the Big Sandy meets the Ohio, and it anchors the most refinery-focused NDT work in the state. Its turnarounds bring contract crews for ultrasonic thickness, phased array and TOFD weld examination, radiography of piping and vessel welds, and surface methods on repairs. Around it are river terminals, fabrication shops, rail facilities and the gas gathering and transmission systems of the Appalachian Basin. Contractors serving the refinery are audited against the owner's contractor qualification rules, which nearly always start with the written practice and certification files.

The Ohio River industrial corridor: Ghent, Carrollton and Northern Kentucky

North American Stainless at Ghent is one of the largest stainless steel producers in the country, and Nucor's steel operations in Gallatin County sit nearby. Mills use UT on plate, rolls and shafts, MT on crane and lifting components and structural repairs, and VT across maintenance welding. Kentucky Utilities' Ghent Generating Station adds boiler and piping outage work. Further upstream, Northern Kentucky has the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky airport's cargo operations, the Brent Spence Bridge corridor, and steel fabricators serving bridge and building projects on both sides of the river.

Louisville

Louisville combines auto assembly at Ford's Louisville Assembly Plant and Kentucky Truck Plant, GE Appliances' Appliance Park, a chemical district along the river in the west end, UPS Worldport's aircraft maintenance, Louisville Gas and Electric's power stations, and a dense base of fabricators and machine shops. That mix produces three very different Level III needs: production NDT in auto and appliance plants, field NDT in chemical plants and power stations, and aviation maintenance NDT governed by the operator's maintenance programme.

Central Kentucky: Lexington, Georgetown, Frankfort and Richmond

Toyota's Georgetown plant is one of the company's largest vehicle factories anywhere, and its supplier base spreads across the Bluegrass. Suppliers use MT, PT, ET and UT on castings, forgings, welded assemblies and machined parts, usually under the customer's own specifications and acceptance criteria. Frankfort and the surrounding counties add metals and manufacturing, and the Blue Grass Army Depot near Richmond adds defence work.

South-central and Western Kentucky: Bowling Green, Owensboro, Paducah and Calvert City

General Motors builds the Corvette at Bowling Green, and the BlueOval SK battery complex at Glendale has brought large-scale construction and production work to Hardin County. Owensboro and Henderson have aluminium, power generation, river fabrication and pipeline compressor stations. Paducah has the Department of Energy's former gaseous diffusion plant site, now in clean-up, and TVA's Shawnee Fossil Plant. Calvert City's chemical complex on the Tennessee River runs pressure vessels, process piping and storage tanks that need in-service inspection. Fort Campbell and Fort Knox add military maintenance and construction.

Kentucky regulators that touch NDT

Radiography. Kentucky is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the Radiation Health Branch of the Cabinet for Health and Family Services, Department for Public Health, under 902 KAR Chapter 100. The branch also registers X-ray equipment. Contractors bringing sources in from other states need to sort out reciprocity before the job. Radiation safety is a separate obligation from SNT-TC-1A RT certification, and a Level III should make sure your RT procedures and your radiation safety programme do not contradict each other.

Boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping. The Boiler Inspection Section, part of the Division of Plumbing in the Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction (Public Protection Cabinet), administers Kentucky's boiler and pressure vessel law under KRS Chapter 236 and 815 KAR Chapter 15. Kentucky's rules reach pressure piping as well as boilers and vessels, which matters for fabricators and plant contractors.

Pipelines. The Kentucky Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety, and the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines.

Level III services for Kentucky employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers each Level III function as a separate service or as a retained package: Level III of record, interim cover, written practices, procedures and technique sheets, exams, programme audits and inspection-programme technique support. The right mix depends on whether you are a refinery contractor, a mill, an automotive supplier, a chemical plant or a small fabricator.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: The written practice is your company's rulebook for training, examining, certifying and recertifying NDT personnel. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, so auditors judge you against your own written practice. Atlantis drafts new written practices for Kentucky employers, revises outdated ones and audits programmes against them.

Kentucky's manufacturing growth has created many first-time NDT programmes. A supplier that used to rely on its customer's inspectors now has to inspect its own castings or welds; a battery or appliance plant brings in ultrasonic or eddy current inspection for the first time; a fabrication shop wins pressure-piping work and suddenly needs certified RT and UT. In each case the customer's first question is "show me your written practice." A lean written practice that fits the methods actually used is far better than a long template copied from another company that nobody follows.

Established programmes have the opposite problem. Refinery contractors and mills often have written practices that grew by patchwork. Phased array was added by memo, a new method was introduced without updating exam requirements, or the recertification rules no longer match the client's. A Level III review brings the document and the records back together.

Elements we settle in a Kentucky written practice:

  • Scope: methods, techniques and levels, including how PAUT and TOFD are certified.
  • Training and experience requirements, cross-checked against the training requirements matrix and your customers' rules.
  • Exam content, weighting, administration and grading, and who is authorised to give practical exams.
  • Vision examination and records.
  • Recertification, expiry, interrupted service and revocation.
  • Use of outside agencies and an outsourced Level III.
  • Customer-specific add-ons for automotive, aviation maintenance or owner contractor rules.

Learn more on written practice development, written practices for chemical manufacturing, written practices for fabrication shops and SNT-TC-1A certification. For an existing programme, ask for a Kentucky written practice review.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Kentucky

Direct answer: A Kentucky NDT procedure has to be written to the document that governs the work: ASME and API for refineries, chemical plants and boilers; AWS for structural steel and bridges; customer specifications for automotive and appliance production; the operator's maintenance programme for aircraft; and API 1104 for pipelines. The Level III approves the procedure and every technique sheet that sits under it.

  • Refining and chemicals (Catlettsburg, Calvert City, Louisville's west end): ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3; API 510, 570 and 653 for in-service inspection; API 577 for weld inspection; owner engineering standards.
  • Power stations (LG&E, KU, TVA, rural cooperatives): ASME Section I and B31.1, Section V methods, and the National Board Inspection Code for repairs, alongside Kentucky's boiler and pressure piping rules.
  • Steel mills (Ghent and Gallatin County): AWS D1.1 for structural repairs, ASTM practices for plate, rolls and forgings, crane and lifting-device requirements, and mill reliability specifications.
  • Bridges: AWS D1.5 and Kentucky Transportation Cabinet requirements for fabrication and repair of bridge steel, relevant to the Ohio River crossings.
  • Automotive, appliance and battery production (Georgetown, Louisville, Bowling Green, Glendale): customer drawings and specifications, often calling up ASTM methods with customer acceptance criteria and process-control requirements.
  • Aviation maintenance (Louisville and Northern Kentucky cargo hubs): the operator's maintenance programme and manufacturer's NDT manuals, with personnel qualification to the standard the operator specifies.
  • Pipelines: API 1104 for girth welds and operator procedures under federal pipeline rules.

We write method procedures, then technique sheets for the real geometries: nozzle welds and small-bore piping at Catlettsburg, crane hooks and roll necks at Ghent, cast suspension parts in the Bluegrass, battery and enclosure welds at Glendale. Where a client asks for it, we support a procedure demonstration on representative samples. See NDT technical procedure development and UT procedure development for refining.

For in-service inspection programmes at refineries, terminals and chemical plants, Atlantis supports the NDT side only, while inspection decisions stay with the owner's certified inspectors. See API 510 pressure vessel inspector services, API 570 piping inspector services and API 653 tank inspector services.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Kentucky crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III gives a Kentucky employer the Level III functions under contract: approvals, exams, record reviews and audit support. An interim Level III does the same for a defined period while you replace a departing Level III. Both work remotely for documents and onsite for practical exams and audits.

Smaller Kentucky employers, such as a fabrication shop in Owensboro, a machine shop supplying Georgetown or a two-crew inspection company in Ashland, rarely have enough Level III work to justify a full-time hire. They still need someone qualified to sign the written practice, approve procedures and certify technicians. A retained outsourced Level III fits that pattern: regular document and exam work remotely, onsite visits when practical exams or audits require them.

Larger employers more often need interim cover. Mills, power-station service groups and refinery contractors usually have their own Level III, and when that person leaves, the programme is exposed straight away. Certifications approach expiry, new hires cannot be examined, and procedure changes stall. Interim Level III support keeps certifications current, reviews pending procedure changes and prepares a clean hand-over to the permanent replacement. See interim NDT Level III, Level III exam oversight and setting up an NDT programme for a start-up inspection company.

To grow your own Level III, the Kentucky NDT training page covers ASNT SNT-TC-1A courses and Level III preparation online or onsite. Technicians in Lexington and Louisville can practise on the Practical NDT simulator for Lexington and Louisville; the simulator is practice only and does not replace a practical exam on real specimens. To discuss cover, ask about an outsourced Level III for your Kentucky crew.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Kentucky NDT programmes face refinery and chemical-plant contractor audits, automotive customer audits, aviation operator audits, ISO 9001 surveillance and, for laboratories, ISO/IEC 17025 assessments. Atlantis runs a gap assessment against the right criteria, fixes the findings with you and supports you on audit day.

Findings we see repeatedly in programmes like those in Kentucky:

  • Written practices that list methods the company stopped performing, or omit techniques it now uses.
  • Certification files missing documented experience hours or a current vision exam.
  • Exams that do not match the weighting or question counts the written practice promises.
  • Procedures without a Level III approval, or several uncontrolled versions on the floor.
  • Reference blocks, probes and wedges without traceable calibration or verification records.
  • No easy way to show which procedure revision applied to a past report.

Automotive suppliers in Georgetown, Louisville and Bowling Green often face customer process audits that include NDT where NDT is a special process. Aviation maintenance NDT at the cargo hubs is audited under the operator's programme. Aerospace parts suppliers may face Nadcap-style audits; see Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness. Refinery and chemical contractors face owner audits; see NDT programme audit and gap assessment. If you operate across Kentucky, Ohio, Indiana and West Virginia, multi-site programme harmonisation keeps one written practice workable in every location. When an audit is booked, book a Kentucky audit-readiness review.

Cities we support across Kentucky

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT supports Kentucky employers statewide, remotely and onsite. Dedicated consulting pages exist for Catlettsburg, Calvert City, Owensboro and Frankfort, with training and simulator pages for Lexington and Louisville. Every other Kentucky city is covered by this hub.

River fabricators building barges and towboats need weld inspection procedures and VT programmes.

The Bluegrass and Louisville. Automotive, appliance and battery suppliers need lean, customer-specific programmes with strong process control. Chemical and power work in Louisville follows the refinery pattern at smaller scale. Aviation maintenance NDT follows the operator's programme.

Ghent and Northern Kentucky. Mill reliability teams need component-specific UT and MT technique sheets and exam banks built from their own parts. Bridge and building fabricators need AWS-based VT, UT and MT procedures.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: A Kentucky engagement runs in five or six steps: scoping call, document review, written proposal, remote document and exam work, onsite days for practical exams and audits, and sign-off. Fees and timelines are set during scoping and quoted on request, because they depend on your methods, headcount and deadlines.

  1. Scoping call on methods, levels, crew size, customers, codes and any fixed audit or turnaround dates. Request a Kentucky scoping call.
  2. Confidential document review of your written practice, procedures, technique sheets and sample certification files.
  3. Written proposal listing deliverables, remote work and onsite days. Quote on request.
  4. Remote work on documents, exam banks and record reviews.
  5. Onsite days at your facility for practical exams, demonstrations, crew briefings and audit support, planned around production schedules, outages and turnarounds.
  6. Sign-off of approved documents and certification records, with an open-items list, and optional retained support afterwards.

The Level III is Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Companies that track certifications, calibrations and reports in spreadsheets can also look at the Atlantis NDT ERP, a separate product.

Frequently asked questions

How do I find an NDT Level III consultant in Kentucky?

Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to Kentucky employers remotely and onsite at your facility, from Ashland to Paducah. Start with a short scoping call.

Can an outside Level III certify my technicians in Kentucky?

An outside Level III can prepare, administer and grade exams under your written practice and recommend certification. Under SNT-TC-1A, certification itself is issued by the employer.

Is Kentucky an Agreement State for industrial radiography?

Yes. Kentucky is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the Radiation Health Branch of the Cabinet for Health and Family Services.

Who inspects boilers and pressure vessels in Kentucky?

The Boiler Inspection Section of the Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction administers Kentucky's boiler and pressure vessel law, which also covers pressure piping.

We are a new inspection company in Kentucky. Where do we start?

Start with a written practice that fits the methods you will offer, then procedures, then qualified personnel. See NDT programme for a start-up inspection company.

Do you support refinery turnaround contractors at Catlettsburg?

Yes. We prepare procedures, technique sheets, exams and audit files for contractors serving the refinery and other Ohio River plants, and we can work onsite before or during a turnaround.

Can you help an automotive supplier set up NDT for the first time?

Yes. We write a lean written practice and customer-specific procedures for the methods you need, and prepare your inspectors' exams and records.

What codes do Kentucky NDT procedures follow?

It depends on the work: ASME and API for refineries, chemical plants and boilers; AWS for structures and bridges; customer specifications for production parts; API 1104 for pipelines.

Do you provide interim Level III cover?

Yes. Interim cover keeps your programme running after a Level III leaves. See interim NDT Level III.

It depends on scope, methods, headcount and onsite time. We quote on request after a scoping call and do not publish a price list.

Do you offer NDT training in Kentucky as well?

contentHtml:

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Manitoba

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III services to Manitoba employers, remotely and onsite at the employer's own facility: an outsourced or interim Level III for SNT-TC-1A programmes, written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets, qualification exams under the employer's written practice, and preparation for customer, prime and owner audits. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, and every scope is quoted on request.

Manitoba's NDT market looks different from the oil provinces to the west. Winnipeg is one of Canada's main aerospace centres, with engine overhaul, composite structures and component manufacturing for North American and global primes. The province generates most of its electricity from hydro stations on the Nelson, Winnipeg and Saskatchewan rivers, with long transmission lines south to Winnipeg. Nickel mining and processing at Thompson, copper and zinc mining around Snow Lake and Flin Flon, a scrap-based steel mill at Selkirk, bus and coach manufacturing, agricultural equipment makers, a nitrogen fertiliser plant at Brandon, oil production in the southwest corner around Virden and Waskada, and interprovincial oil and gas pipelines that cross the province toward the United States all need inspection. A large share of that work is for US customers, US primes or equipment going south, which is where an ASNT Level III fits. If you are ready, ask for a Manitoba Level III quote.

Why Manitoba NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: A Manitoba employer that certifies NDT personnel under ASNT SNT-TC-1A must have a Level III who owns the written practice, approves procedures and examines staff. Aerospace primes, utilities, mine operators and pipeline companies audit their NDT suppliers, and most Manitoba shops are too small to employ a full-time Level III, so an outsourced Level III is the practical answer.

Aerospace comes first in Winnipeg. Engine maintenance, repair and overhaul, composite aerostructures and precision machining and fabrication shops perform fluorescent penetrant, magnetic particle, eddy current, ultrasonic and radiographic inspection on flight hardware. Their customers are engine manufacturers, airframers, airlines and defence programmes, and those customers impose detailed NDT requirements, flow-down specifications and audits. Many smaller machine shops in the city do special-process work for the larger aerospace firms and must meet the same requirements without the same resources.

Hydro power is the second pillar. Manitoba Hydro's generating stations on the Nelson River in the north, including the recently completed Keeyask station, and older stations closer to Winnipeg, contain turbines, runners, penstocks, gates, hoists, draft tube liners and large structural steel that need weld and material inspection during construction and outages. Converter stations and transmission towers add structural and bolting work. Utility work brings strict documentation and safety expectations, and contractors are audited on both.

Mining and metals follow. The Thompson nickel operations, mines around Snow Lake and the Flin Flon district run hoists, headframes, crushers, mills, conveyors and heavy mobile equipment that depend on MT and UT for crack detection. The Selkirk steel mill makes products from recycled scrap, and its own equipment and products need inspection. Bus and coach builders and agricultural equipment manufacturers in Winnipeg and rural Manitoba weld structures and frames that their customers, many of them American, expect to be inspected by qualified personnel to recognised codes.

Energy infrastructure rounds out the picture. Major oil pipelines enter the United States from Manitoba near Gretna, natural gas mainlines cross the province, and southwest Manitoba has active light-oil production with batteries, tanks and gathering lines. Brandon's fertiliser plant runs high-pressure equipment. The Whiteshell Laboratories site near Pinawa is in decommissioning, which keeps nuclear-industry document control in the provincial mix.

The regulatory picture: boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping are regulated under The Steam and Pressure Plants Act by Inspection and Technical Services (ITS), part of the Office of the Fire Commissioner, which handles design registration, quality assurance plans, welding procedure registration, inspections and inspection certificates. Industrial gamma radiography is licensed federally by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC), and exposure devices must be operated by CNSC-certified exposure device operators or under their direct supervision. Interprovincial and international pipelines are regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator; provincially regulated lines answer to the province under CSA Z662-based requirements. Aviation maintenance organisations answer to Transport Canada and to their approved maintenance manuals. Confirm the current authority for X-ray equipment and any provincial changes before you mobilise.

Which NDT certification scheme applies in Manitoba?

Direct answer: Manitoba employers meet several schemes. Canada's national scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712). Aerospace suppliers usually work to NAS 410 or EN 4179 through their primes. US customers and US-code work commonly use ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A Level III services plus procedure, technique and audit support around the others; we are not a CGSB, ISO 9712 or NAS 410 certification body.

A note on the national scheme, because it changed this year. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published the standard, closed on 1 April 2026; the standard remains valid, and both Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body and CWB Group, as an accredited certification body, have said they continue to certify. Confirm the current certification body for your method and sector before you rely on it.

The practical rule: the contract, the prime's specification or the referenced code decides. Where a national or aerospace certification is mandatory, our role is drafting, technical review and audit readiness that your properly certified Level 3 signs. Where the customer accepts employer-based SNT-TC-1A certification, Atlantis can serve as your Level III of record. Shops that serve aerospace, utilities and US buyers at the same time often need help keeping three sets of requirements from contradicting each other, and that reconciliation is often the most valuable thing we do.

Atlantis provides Level III expertise rather than field crews, certifications or regulatory approvals; our work stands behind your own technicians. See ASNT Level III consulting services, the consulting overview and NDT consulting in Canada.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's document that defines how NDT personnel are trained, examined, certified and recertified under SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis writes new written practices for Manitoba employers and audits existing ones so the document fits the methods you perform, the customers who audit you and the other schemes your people hold.

Manitoba shops often run two or three personnel systems at once, and the written practice is where they collide. Problems we see include a practice that claims SNT-TC-1A but borrows aerospace wording that the company does not actually follow; aerospace and industrial technicians mixed in one document without clear method and sector boundaries; national-scheme certificates treated as automatic employer certification; a named Level III who has left; methods such as eddy current or phased array performed but not listed; and practical exams with no specimens on file. Seasonal manufacturing and outage-driven hiring also leave vision exams and recertification dates lapsed.

A written-practice engagement defines scope, training and experience requirements referenced to the current SNT-TC-1A edition, examination content and grading, vision exams, certification and recertification, interrupted service, transfer of certification and the Level III's authority. Where your customers impose ANSI/ASNT CP-189 or aerospace requirements, we show exactly where the practice must differ, or recommend a separate document. Training-hour figures come from the training requirements matrix. More: written practice development and the SNT-TC-1A guide. To start, request a written-practice review for your Manitoba company.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Manitoba

Direct answer: Manitoba procedures follow the governing code or customer specification: the prime's NDT specifications and ASTM methods for aerospace; CSA B51 with the ASME Code for ITS-regulated pressure equipment; CSA W59 or AWS D1.1 for structures; CSA Z662 or API 1104 for pipelines; and utility and manufacturer requirements for hydro and mining equipment.

  • Aerospace. Fluorescent penetrant, magnetic particle, eddy current and ultrasonic procedures and part-specific technique sheets that trace to the prime's specification and the referenced ASTM practices, with process-control checks a Nadcap auditor expects to see.
  • Hydro generation. Weld inspection on penstocks, gates, runners and hoists; UT and MT on shafts, bolting and structural members; procedures that work in wet, confined and cold environments during outages.
  • Mining and metals. MT and UT on hoist components, crushers, mill parts and mobile equipment frames at Thompson, Snow Lake and Flin Flon, and inspection of mill equipment and products at Selkirk.
  • Bus, coach and agricultural equipment. Weld inspection on frames and structures to AWS D1.1, CSA W59 or the customer's specification, often for US buyers who audit the supplier.
  • Pipelines and oil production. Girth-weld radiography or automated UT on construction, integrity digs and facility inspection in southwest Manitoba, under the operator's specification and the radiography company's CNSC licence conditions.
  • Pressure equipment. Vessels and piping built or repaired under ITS registration, where NDT forms part of the registered quality programme.
  • Cold weather. Winter conditions affect penetrant and particle product limits, couplant, equipment and safe access; the procedure should address them explicitly.

Sector notes: aerospace, power generation, mining, steel and metals, fabrication and pipeline. For hydro and thermal utilities, see written practices for power generation.

Aerospace NDT in Winnipeg: prime audits and Nadcap context

Direct answer: Winnipeg aerospace suppliers are audited by their primes and, for many, through Nadcap. Atlantis helps them prepare: mock audits against the prime's specification, procedure and technique-sheet review, process-control records, personnel files and corrective actions. The audit and accreditation decisions belong to the prime and the accreditation body, and personnel certification follows NAS 410 or EN 4179 under the supplier's own programme.

Aerospace NDT audits focus on detail: penetrant system checks and their records, magnetic particle field verification, eddy current reference standards, ultrasonic calibration blocks and their certification, technique sheets that match the drawing and the specification revision, and personnel whose certification and eye exams are current on the day the part was inspected. The usual problems are not dramatic; they are missing signatures, superseded revisions and records that cannot be traced. A Level III review finds them before the auditor does.

We are candid about scope. NAS 410 has its own requirements for who may act as the Responsible Level 3, and primes set their own approvals. We support the technical content and the audit preparation; confirm with your prime whether an outside Level III can hold a formal role in your NAS 410 programme. See NAS 410 and Nadcap audit support, or book an aerospace audit-readiness call for your Manitoba shop.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Manitoba crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is a named ASNT Level III who serves as your SNT-TC-1A programme's Level III under a standing agreement; an interim Level III fills a gap. For Manitoba employers the work is mainly remote, with onsite visits for practical exams, procedure demonstrations and audits at the employer's facility.

  1. Ongoing outsourced (retained) Level III. Atlantis is named in your written practice, approves procedures, administers exams, answers technical questions, reviews the programme each year and supports you in customer audits.
  2. Project-based work. A new written practice, a procedure set for a new hydro, mining or manufacturing contract, PAUT technique sheets, or an exam campaign before an outage.
  3. Audit-preparation sprint. A focused review before a known audit date with a prioritised corrective-action list and support while you close it.

Practical exams need the candidate, real specimens and the examiner together, so they are held onsite at your facility in Winnipeg, Brandon, Thompson, Selkirk or wherever you operate. Atlantis has no office or training centre in Manitoba. See interim NDT Level III, or discuss outsourced Level III coverage for your Manitoba programme.

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, so you know exactly who approves your procedures and examines your people.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Manitoba NDT suppliers are audited by aerospace primes, utilities, mine operators, pipeline companies and US customers, and some by ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 17025 or CSA W178.1 assessors. A Level III review before the audit finds gaps in the written practice, certifications, procedures and reports while there is time to fix them.

Common findings: certifications issued under a superseded written practice; aerospace and industrial records mixed together; expired vision exams; practical exams with no specimen or grading record; procedures not approved by a Level III or tied to an outdated specification revision; reference standards without certificates; and technicians working outside their certified methods. Utility and nuclear-related decommissioning work adds traceability expectations that general fabrication shops may not be used to.

An audit-readiness engagement samples personnel files, procedures and reports, maps them to the written practice and the customer's specification, and delivers a prioritised corrective-action list with follow-up support. For laboratories pursuing ISO/IEC 17025, we help with the NDT technical content; the accreditation decision belongs to the accreditation body. See also nuclear audit support and infrastructure audit support. Audit coming up? Book a Manitoba audit-readiness call.

Cities we support across Manitoba

Direct answer: Atlantis supports Manitoba employers province-wide, remotely and onsite at the client's facility. Most requests come from Winnipeg, Selkirk, Brandon, Thompson, the Snow Lake and Flin Flon mining district, southwest oil country around Virden, and the hydro corridor in the north.

  • Winnipeg. Aerospace overhaul and manufacturing, bus and coach building, agricultural equipment, fabrication, utility head offices and engineering firms. Related pages: NDT training in Winnipeg and the Practical NDT simulator for Winnipeg.
  • Selkirk. The steel mill and related fabrication and services.
  • Brandon. Fertiliser production, food processing, agricultural equipment and services for southwest oil production.
  • Virden and Waskada. Light-oil production with batteries, tanks and gathering systems.
  • Thompson. Nickel mining and processing and the service hub for northern Manitoba.
  • Snow Lake and Flin Flon. Base-metal mining and processing.
  • The Nelson River corridor. Manitoba Hydro generating and converter stations, served by contractors based in Winnipeg and Thompson.
  • Gretna and the southern border. Pipeline facilities where major lines cross into the United States.
  • Churchill. The northern port and rail line, with periodic structural and marine-related inspection work.

For the national picture see NDT consulting in Canada and NDT training in Canada.

Training alongside the Level III service

Direct answer: Manitoba clients can combine Level III consulting with ASNT SNT-TC-1A training for their own technicians, live online or onsite at their facility. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only: it does not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712, NAS 410 or EN 4179 certification, and we say so up front.

Training covers Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for employers whose customers expect SNT-TC-1A certification, such as fabricators and manufacturers shipping to US buyers. The Practical NDT simulator lets trainees practise twelve methods in five virtual environments, including an aircraft hangar and an NDT lab, before practical exams; it is a practice tool and does not replace a practical exam on real specimens. See training, online NDT training, corporate NDT training and ASNT Level III training.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: A Manitoba engagement begins with a call about your methods, customers, codes, certification schemes and staffing, followed by a written scope and quote. Document work runs remotely; practical exams and site visits happen at your facility. Timing is agreed in the scope, not assumed.

  1. Discovery call. Methods, customers and primes, codes and specifications, schemes your people hold, and the trigger: an audit, a new contract, a departing Level III or a move into US work.
  2. Document review. You share your written practice, procedures and a sample of certification files and reports; we identify gaps.
  3. Scope and quote. Deliverables, remote and onsite elements and responsibilities in writing. Pricing is quote on request.
  4. Delivery. Drafting, approval and issue of documents; exams under your written practice; corrective actions; ongoing Level III duties if retained.
  5. Onsite visits. Practical exams, procedure demonstrations and audit support at your Manitoba site, planned around outages, production schedules and winter travel to the north.
  6. Review. Annual programme review for retained clients and updates when specifications, codes or customers change.

Ready to scope it? Request a scoped Level III proposal for Manitoba.

Frequently asked questions

How do I find an NDT Level III consultant in Manitoba?

Independent Level IIIs are scarce in Manitoba, so many shops use an outside Level III who works remotely and visits onsite. Atlantis provides that service for SNT-TC-1A programmes, led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in Manitoba?

Inspection and Technical Services, part of the Office of the Fire Commissioner, administers The Steam and Pressure Plants Act, including design registration, quality assurance plans, welding procedure registration, inspections and inspection certificates.

Is ASNT certification accepted in Manitoba?

It depends on the customer. US customers and US-code work commonly accept SNT-TC-1A. Aerospace primes usually require NAS 410 or EN 4179, and many Canadian owners specify national certification to CAN/CGSB-48.9712. Read the contract first.

Can Atlantis act as our NAS 410 Responsible Level 3?

We help aerospace suppliers prepare for prime and Nadcap audits and review procedures and technique sheets. Whether an outside Level III can hold a formal NAS 410 role depends on the standard and your prime's requirements, so confirm with the prime.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Manitoba?

Gamma radiography requires a CNSC licence for the company and CNSC-certified exposure device operators, or work under their direct supervision. Confirm current provincial requirements for X-ray equipment before work starts.

What does an outsourced Level III do for a Manitoba shop?

They act as the Level III named in your SNT-TC-1A written practice: approving procedures, administering exams, reviewing certifications, answering technical questions and supporting customer audits, without a full-time hire.

Can you write NDT procedures for hydro generating stations?

Yes. We write UT, MT, PT and VT procedures and technique sheets for penstocks, gates, runners, shafts and structural welds to the utility's specification and the applicable code.

Do you write SNT-TC-1A written practices for manufacturers shipping to the US?

Yes. We write new written practices and audit existing ones for bus, coach, agricultural-equipment and fabrication companies whose US customers expect SNT-TC-1A personnel.

Can practical exams be done remotely?

No. Practical exams need the candidate, real specimens and the examiner together, so they are held onsite at your facility.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Manitoba?

Quote on request. Cost depends on methods, retained versus project work, exam volume and onsite visits. Atlantis keeps its services affordable, accessible and fully customisable.

Does Atlantis have an office in Winnipeg?

No. Atlantis has no physical office or training centre in Manitoba; work is delivered remotely and onsite at the client's facility.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Maryland

Short answer: Maryland employers use Atlantis NDT for ASNT NDT Level III work: outsourced Level III of record, interim cover, SNT-TC-1A written practices, procedures and technique sheets, qualification exams under your written practice, and preparation for customer, owner and accreditation audits. The Level III is Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, working remotely and onsite at your yard, plant, terminal or shop. Atlantis has no Maryland office. Engagements are scoped on a call and quoted on request.

Maryland packs a lot of demanding NDT into a small state. Southern Maryland has a nuclear power station and an LNG export terminal within a few miles of each other on the Chesapeake. Baltimore has one of the East Coast's major ports, a Coast Guard shipyard, the redeveloped Sparrows Point industrial site and the rebuild of the Francis Scott Key Bridge. The I-95 corridor and the Patuxent River region are dense with defence, aerospace and test sites, and Western Maryland builds truck powertrains. Each of those sectors brings its own codes, auditors and customer rules, and a Level III serving Maryland has to know which one applies to which job. This page sets out how we support Maryland programmes and how to talk to a Level III about your Maryland programme.

Why Maryland NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 put a Level III in charge of the written practice, procedure approval and qualification exams. Maryland employers in nuclear, LNG, shipbuilding and repair, bridges, defence and aerospace face some of the toughest customer and owner audits in the country, and each audit starts with the Level III's work. Whether in-house or outsourced, that Level III has to be capable and available.

Southern Maryland: Calvert Cliffs, Cove Point and the Patuxent

Constellation's Calvert Cliffs Nuclear Power Plant in Lusby runs refuelling outages that bring ASME Section XI in-service inspection, and its suppliers and service contractors work under nuclear quality assurance programmes. A few miles south, the Cove Point LNG terminal liquefies and exports natural gas, with cryogenic stainless and nickel-steel piping, large storage tanks and gas-turbine-driven compression that need careful weld inspection and in-service monitoring. Naval Air Station Patuxent River, the Navy's flight test centre, and the contractors around it add aircraft structural inspection: eddy current, ultrasonic testing of composites and bonded structures, and penetrant inspection of components. Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head adds energetics and ordnance work.

Baltimore and the port

The Port of Baltimore handles autos, roll-on/roll-off cargo, containers and bulk coal through terminals that need crane, structural and marine inspection. The U.S. Coast Guard Yard at Curtis Bay builds and repairs Coast Guard cutters, and private yards and marine contractors around the harbour repair tugs, barges and workboats. At Sparrows Point, the former Bethlehem Steel site is now Tradepoint Atlantic, a logistics and industrial campus with marine terminals, and it is being positioned to support offshore wind. The rebuild of the Francis Scott Key Bridge, after its 2024 collapse, is the largest bridge project in the region and a heavy user of structural welding inspection. Constellation, BGE and other power and gas utilities, chemical and pharmaceutical plants, and fuel terminals at Curtis Bay and Fairfield add plant inspection work.

The I-95 and BWI corridor: defence and aerospace

Lockheed Martin's Middle River site builds naval launching systems. Northrop Grumman's sensor and mission-systems operations sit near BWI. Aberdeen Proving Ground in Harford County tests Army vehicles and equipment, Fort Meade and Joint Base Andrews add defence construction and maintenance, and a large supplier base of machine shops, welders and metal finishers serves them. Defence and aerospace work here runs to prime-contractor specifications, military standards and, for many parts suppliers, Nadcap-style audits.

Western Maryland and the Eastern Shore

Hagerstown is home to the Volvo Group's powertrain plant, which builds heavy-truck engines and transmissions and draws a casting, forging and machining supply base. Frederick and the US-15 corridor have life-sciences and manufacturing plants with stainless process piping and pressure equipment. Conowingo Dam on the Susquehanna generates hydropower. On the Eastern Shore, food processing, poultry, agriculture and natural gas distribution generate pressure-vessel, refrigeration and pipeline work, and proposed offshore wind projects off Ocean City may add more.

Maryland regulators that touch NDT

Radiography. Maryland is an NRC Agreement State. The Maryland Department of the Environment's Radiological Health Program, in its Air and Radiation Administration, licenses and inspects users of radioactive materials, including industrial radiographers, under COMAR 26.12, and registers radiation machine facilities. Out-of-state radiography companies need reciprocal recognition before working in Maryland. Radiation safety is a separate obligation from SNT-TC-1A RT certification, and a Level III should check that RT procedures and the radiation safety programme agree.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Inspection Unit in the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Labor and Industry enforces the state Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act, with periodic inspection of regulated equipment and construction to the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code with National Board registration.

Pipelines. The Maryland Public Service Commission's pipeline safety staff oversee intrastate gas pipeline operators, and the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines and LNG facilities.

Level III services for Maryland employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT provides each Level III function on its own or as a retained service: Level III of record, interim cover, written practices, procedures and technique sheets, qualification exams, programme audits and inspection-programme technique support. In Maryland the mix is usually shaped by nuclear, LNG, marine, bridge and defence customers.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: The written practice is the employer's document governing how NDT personnel are trained, examined, certified and recertified. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, so your written practice is what auditors enforce. Atlantis writes new written practices for Maryland employers, revises outdated ones and audits programmes against them.

Maryland written practices often have to serve more than one master. A marine inspection contractor in Baltimore may work for the Coast Guard Yard, a commercial ship-repair customer and a bridge contractor in the same quarter. A machine shop on the I-95 corridor may supply a defence prime that names one personnel standard and a commercial aerospace customer that names another. A service contractor at Calvert Cliffs or Cove Point works within the owner's quality programme and may need CP-189 alignment. The written practice has to hold the common core and show clearly how each customer's extra requirements are met.

What we settle in a Maryland written practice:

  • Methods, techniques and levels, including PAUT, TOFD and digital radiography where used.
  • Training and experience requirements, cross-referenced to the training requirements matrix and your customers' rules.
  • Exam preparation, administration and grading, and who may give practical exams.
  • Vision examinations and records.
  • Recertification, interrupted service and revocation.
  • Use of outside agencies and an outsourced Level III.
  • Customer-specific requirements for nuclear, naval and Coast Guard, defence and aerospace work.

Read more on written practice development, written practices for nuclear power, written practices for LNG, written practices for fabrication shops and SNT-TC-1A certification. To have an existing programme checked, ask for a Maryland written practice audit.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Maryland

Direct answer: Maryland NDT procedures must be written to whatever governs each job: ASME Section XI and nuclear quality requirements at Calvert Cliffs, ASME and API codes at the LNG terminal and fuel terminals, AWS D1.5 and state requirements on bridges, naval and Coast Guard requirements in ship work, and prime-contractor specifications in defence and aerospace. The Level III approves each procedure and its technique sheets.

  • Nuclear (Calvert Cliffs and suppliers): ASME Section XI for in-service inspection, Section III for new components, Section V methods and the owner's quality programme. See NQA-1 nuclear supplier NDT programmes.
  • LNG and fuel terminals (Cove Point, Curtis Bay, Fairfield): ASME B31.3 process piping, API 620 and 625 context for low-temperature storage tanks, API 653 for atmospheric tanks, and federal LNG facility rules, with procedures suited to austenitic stainless and nickel steels. See UT procedure development for LNG.
  • Bridges and transport infrastructure: AWS D1.5 for bridge welding and Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration and Maryland Transportation Authority requirements, relevant to the Key Bridge rebuild, Chesapeake crossings and transit projects.
  • Shipbuilding and repair (Curtis Bay, Baltimore harbour, Sparrows Point): Coast Guard and naval technical requirements, classification society rules and owner specifications. See NAVSEA NDT requirements for shipyards and ship-repair yard NDT programmes.
  • Power (gas, coal and hydro stations): ASME Section I and B31.1, the National Board Inspection Code for repairs, and utility standards.
  • Defence and aerospace (Middle River, BWI, Patuxent River, Aberdeen): prime-contractor specifications, military standards named on drawings, and ASTM penetrant and magnetic particle practices with tight process control.
  • Heavy truck powertrain (Hagerstown): customer specifications for castings, forgings and machined parts, often calling up ASTM methods with customer acceptance criteria.

Technique sheets turn procedures into repeatable work: weld-specific sheets for bridge girders and cross-frames, sheets for cryogenic piping at the LNG terminal, component sheets for Section XI examinations, and part-number sheets for defence suppliers. Atlantis writes and approves both layers and supports procedure demonstration on representative specimens where customers ask for it. See NDT technical procedure development and procedure qualification and demonstration.

For in-service inspection programmes at terminals and plants, Atlantis supports the NDT side only; the owner's certified inspectors make inspection decisions. See API 510, API 570 and API 653 inspector services.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Maryland crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III provides a Maryland employer with Level III functions under contract: written practice, approvals, exams, record review and audit support. An interim Level III covers a defined period after a Level III leaves. Document work is remote; practical exams, demonstrations and audits are onsite at your facility.

Many Maryland inspection companies are small specialist firms serving marine, bridge and structural customers around Baltimore, or defence suppliers with a few inspectors on one or two methods. They need a Level III who understands Coast Guard, naval, bridge and prime-contractor requirements, but not on payroll full-time. A retained outsourced Level III handles approvals and exam work remotely and comes onsite when practical exams or audits need it.

Larger employers, such as outage service contractors, LNG and terminal maintenance groups and fabricators on major bridge or port projects, tend to need interim cover when their own Level III leaves in the middle of a project or before an outage. Interim support keeps certifications and procedure approvals current, closes open audit items and leaves a clean hand-over file. See interim NDT Level III, what to do when your Level III resigns, Level III exam oversight and what an outside Level III can and cannot do.

To train technicians or prepare a future Level III, see the Maryland NDT training page and NDT training in Baltimore. Trainees can practise on the Practical NDT simulator for Baltimore; it is practice only and does not replace a practical exam on real specimens. To talk about cover, ask about an outsourced Level III for your Maryland crew.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Maryland NDT programmes are audited by nuclear and LNG owners, defence primes, Nadcap-style auditors, government shipyard and bridge owners, ISO 9001 registrars and, for laboratories, ISO/IEC 17025 assessors. Atlantis carries out a gap assessment against the right criteria, works through the findings with you and supports you during the audit.

Findings we commonly see in programmes like Maryland's:

  • A written practice that does not explain how nuclear, naval or prime-contractor requirements are met on top of SNT-TC-1A.
  • Certification files missing experience hours, method-specific training records or current vision exams.
  • Procedures that call up superseded code editions, or technique sheets that do not trace to an approved procedure.
  • Calibration blocks, probes and wedges without traceable records, a frequent ISO/IEC 17025 finding.
  • Radiography paperwork that does not distinguish Maryland radiation-safety requirements from SNT-TC-1A RT certification, or out-of-state crews without reciprocal recognition.
  • No reliable way to show which procedure revision and which technician applied to a past report.

Aerospace and defence suppliers can see Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness. For any sector, see NDT programme audit and gap assessment; contractors with crews in Maryland, Delaware, Virginia and Pennsylvania can see multi-site programme harmonisation. Once an audit is on the calendar, book a Maryland audit-readiness review.

Cities we support across Maryland

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT supports Maryland employers across the state, remotely and onsite. Baltimore and Sparrows Point have dedicated consulting pages, and Baltimore also has training and Practical NDT simulator pages. Southern Maryland, the I-95 corridor, Western Maryland and the Eastern Shore are covered by this hub.

Southern Maryland. Nuclear and LNG service contractors need CP-189-aware written practices, Section XI and cryogenic-material procedures, and records that survive owner audits.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: A Maryland engagement starts with a scoping call and moves through document review, a written proposal, remote work, onsite days at your facility and sign-off. Fees and timelines are set during scoping and quoted on request.

  2. Confidential document review: written practice, procedures, technique sheets and sample certification files.
  3. Written proposal: deliverables, remote work and onsite days; quote on request.
  4. Remote work: drafting and revisions, exam banks and record reviews.
  5. Onsite at your facility: practical exams, demonstrations, briefings and audit support, planned around outages, ship schedules and production.
  6. Sign-off: approved documents, certification records and an open-items list, with optional retained Level III support afterwards.

The Level III is Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. If your certifications, calibrations and reports live in spreadsheets, the Atlantis NDT ERP is a separate product that brings them together.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I find an NDT Level III consultant in Maryland?

Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to Maryland employers remotely and onsite at your facility, from Baltimore to Southern Maryland and Hagerstown.

Is Maryland an Agreement State for industrial radiography?

Yes. Maryland is an NRC Agreement State. The Maryland Department of the Environment's Radiological Health Program licenses industrial radiography, and out-of-state companies need reciprocal recognition.

The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Inspection Unit in the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Labor and Industry enforces the state's boiler and pressure vessel law.

Yes. We support written practices, procedures and audits for marine contractors working for government and commercial customers around the harbour.

Yes. We review your written practice, procedures, process-control records and certification files and support you during the audit. Accreditation decisions stay with the accrediting body.

Do you offer NDT training in Maryland too?

Massachusetts is not a refinery state, and that changes what a Level III spends time on here. The work that drives NDT in the Commonwealth is aero-engine and defence manufacturing on the North Shore and along Route 128 and I-495, precision forging and machining in Worcester County, offshore wind staging in New Bedford, an LNG import terminal in Everett, gas transmission and distribution pipe that has been under intense scrutiny since 2018, a nuclear plant in decommissioning at Plymouth, and a large stock of ageing bridges, transit structures and institutional boiler plant. Each of those sectors asks for different things from an NDT programme. This page explains what a Massachusetts NDT company or in-house inspection department actually needs from a Level III, which agencies and codes apply, and how to request a Massachusetts Level III consultation.

Why Massachusetts NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, an employer that certifies its own NDT personnel needs a written practice approved by a responsible Level III, procedures for each method, and a Level III to examine and certify Level I and II staff. Massachusetts aerospace suppliers, fabricators, inspection contractors and plant owners also face prime-contractor audits and state oversight that expect a named Level III.

The Commonwealth's industrial map explains why the demand looks the way it does. On the North Shore, GE Aerospace's Lynn plant has built and serviced military and commercial jet engines and their components for generations, and its supply chain reaches into machine shops, heat treaters, coaters and special-process houses across Essex and Middlesex counties. Along Route 128 and I-495, defence electronics and systems integrators, including Raytheon's sites in Andover and Tewksbury, buy machined housings, castings, brazed assemblies and welded structures from local suppliers that must satisfy prime-contractor quality clauses. In Worcester County, Wyman-Gordon's forging operation in North Grafton supplies large aerospace and energy forgings, and dozens of smaller forge, foundry and precision shops make parts for aerospace, defence, medical and industrial customers. Those shops run penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic and sometimes eddy current or radiographic inspection, and most of them answer to a written practice that someone has to own.

The energy side is different from most states. Massachusetts imports liquefied natural gas through the Everett Marine Terminal, and its gas supply arrives through the Tennessee Gas, Algonquin and Maritimes and Northeast transmission systems. The September 2018 Merrimack Valley gas explosions in Lawrence, Andover and North Andover led to tighter state oversight of gas distribution work and a heavy programme of main and service replacement, which keeps welding, coating and inspection contractors busy. Offshore wind has added a new industry: the New Bedford Marine Commerce Terminal was built to stage offshore wind components, and fabrication, transition-piece and structural-steel inspection follow that work. Pilgrim Nuclear Power Station in Plymouth stopped generating in 2019 and is being decommissioned, which brings its own inspection and waste-handling requirements.

Underneath all of that sits public infrastructure. MassDOT and the MBTA maintain thousands of bridges, viaducts and transit structures, many of them steel, many of them old, and steel-bridge fabrication and rehabilitation work to AASHTO/AWS D1.5 depends on qualified NDT personnel. Hospitals, universities, laboratories and campuses run large steam and hot-water plants that the Commonwealth registers and inspects. Each of these buyers, from a GE Aerospace supplier to a bridge fabricator, eventually asks the same question: who is your Level III, and can we see the written practice?

That is the gap an outside Level III fills. Many Massachusetts NDT employers are small. A precision shop with three penetrant inspectors, a fabricator with two ultrasonic technicians, or a regional inspection contractor with a dozen field staff cannot justify a full-time Level III, but they still need the functions a Level III performs. ASNT Level III consulting services let them keep a compliant programme without carrying the salary of a full-time specialist.

Each engagement is scoped on a call around your methods, codes and customers.
