NDT Level III Consulting Services in Ontario

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to Ontario employers: outsourced and interim Level III cover, SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 written practices and audits, NDT procedures and technique sheets, personnel examinations under your written practice, and preparation for owner, prime-contractor and accreditation audits. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, delivered remotely or onsite at your facility. Atlantis has no office in Ontario; the Level III works with you online and comes to your plant or shop when the work requires it.

Ontario's NDT market looks nothing like Alberta's. It is shaped by nuclear power, steel, manufacturing and a dense cross-border supply chain. Refurbishment work at the Bruce and Darlington nuclear generating stations and the small modular reactor build at the Darlington site keep a specialised nuclear supply chain busy from Cambridge and Peterborough to Kincardine and Durham Region. Hamilton and Sault Ste. Marie make steel. Sarnia's Chemical Valley and the Nanticoke refinery process crude and make chemicals. The Greater Toronto Area holds aerospace engine, landing-gear and component manufacturing, and southern Ontario builds cars and the parts that go into them. A large share of that output ships to US customers who expect suppliers to run an employer-based ASNT programme with a named Level III. This page explains what Ontario NDT employers need from a Level III, which regulators and codes apply, and how to request an Ontario Level III consultation.

Why Ontario NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: An Ontario employer that certifies its own NDT personnel to ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 needs a written practice, method procedures and a responsible Level III who examines and certifies Level I and II staff. Ontario's nuclear, aerospace and export-manufacturing customers audit those programmes closely, so the Level III must be named, qualified in the methods used and able to defend every document.

Nuclear sets the tone. Ontario's CANDU fleet, operated by Ontario Power Generation and Bruce Power, has been through some of the largest refurbishment programmes in the world, replacing pressure tubes, feeders and steam generator components and inspecting thousands of welds and components to CSA N285 requirements. Suppliers that fabricate, machine or inspect parts for that work must meet nuclear quality-assurance requirements, typically from the CSA N299 series, and their NDT programmes are audited by the utilities and their prime contractors. Many of those suppliers also serve US nuclear plants and have to show NDT personnel qualification under SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 to US utility auditors. The BWRX-300 small modular reactor project at the Darlington site adds a new generation of nuclear fabrication and inspection work.

Steel is the second anchor. Hamilton's integrated mills, Algoma Steel in Sault Ste. Marie and steel processing around Nanticoke produce plate, coil and pipe that need ultrasonic and surface inspection, and the mills themselves run heavy maintenance programmes on cranes, rolls, ladles and pressure equipment. Fabricators across the Golden Horseshoe turn that steel into bridges, buildings, pressure vessels and machinery.

Refining and chemicals cluster in Sarnia, where several refineries and chemical plants form Chemical Valley along the St. Clair River, and at Nanticoke on Lake Erie. Their turnarounds bring the familiar pattern of PAUT, TOFD, RT and surface-method scopes, with inspection contractors working to owner specifications and TSSA-registered equipment. The TC Energy mainline, Enbridge's systems and the Dawn gas storage hub near Sarnia make pipeline and station work steady.

Aerospace and manufacturing complete the picture. The GTA hosts aero-engine, landing-gear, actuation and structural component makers serving global OEMs, and southern Ontario's automotive plants and parts suppliers in Windsor, Oakville, Alliston, Cambridge, Woodstock and Ingersoll rely on penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic and eddy current inspection. Customers in aerospace often specify NAS 410 or their own rules rather than SNT-TC-1A, which is one more reason Ontario employers want a Level III who can read the flow-down requirements correctly. ASNT Level III consulting services give small and mid-sized Ontario employers that capability without a full-time hire.

Which certification scheme applies in Ontario?

Direct answer: Canada's national NDT certification scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712), and Canadian owners and codes generally expect it. Ontario suppliers serving US nuclear utilities, US aerospace primes or US-code projects are often also asked for ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 programmes, and aerospace customers may require NAS 410. Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 Level III expertise, not CGSB certification.

Ontario has more dual-scheme employers than any other province because so much of its industrial output crosses the border. A nuclear component shop near Cambridge can have welders and inspectors qualified for CANDU work under Canadian requirements and, in the same building, a US utility order that calls for CP-189 personnel qualification. An aerospace machine shop in Mississauga may answer to a Canadian engine maker and a US airframer with different NDT rules. The written practice has to make those overlapping requirements explicit. On the national scheme: the Canadian General Standards Board, which published CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Notices from Natural Resources Canada and CWB Group say the standard remains valid and certifications continue; confirm the current certification body and transition arrangements before relying on any single source.

Every service comes down to evidence: that a qualified Level III approved the documents your technicians use and examined the people who sign reports. The Canada consulting overview and the main consulting page describe the full offer.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own procedure for training, examining, certifying and recertifying NDT personnel. In Ontario it often has to serve two or three customer regimes at once, so it must state clearly which scheme applies to which work, how CGSB certificates are treated and how the Level III function is provided. We write it to match how your operation actually works, then audit records against it.

The typical Ontario problem is accumulation. Over the years a supplier adds a nuclear customer, then an aerospace one, then a US fabrication order, and each brings a new clause. The written practice gets patched, the certification files follow whichever version was current when someone was hired, and nobody is sure which rules govern a given technician. Auditors find the seams: a technician certified under the general programme signing reports on a nuclear order that requires CP-189, a practical examination graded without a checklist, an expired vision test, a Level III named in the document who left two years ago.

We untangle that by starting from the work: which methods and techniques, which customers, which codes. The written practice then sets out levels, training and experience (linked to the training requirements matrix rather than invented numbers), examination content and grading, vision testing, records, recertification and Level III arrangements, with a clear section for each customer regime. Our written practice development page shows the structure, and our sector notes on written practices for nuclear power, steel and metals, aerospace and refining cover the details that differ.

An audit tests the files against the document. You receive findings ranked by audit risk and suggested corrections, and where you want it we help close them. For employers that train in-house, the written practice and the training content should agree; Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A-based training online and onsite, described on NDT training in Canada and corporate NDT training.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Ontario

Direct answer: Ontario NDT procedures follow the code governing the item: ASME and CSA B51 for boilers and pressure vessels registered with TSSA, CSA N285 requirements for CANDU pressure-retaining systems, CSA Z662 for pipelines, CSA W59 and AWS D1.1 for structural steel, CSA S6 for highway bridges, and customer specifications for aerospace and automotive parts.

  • Boilers and pressure vessels: the Technical Standards and Safety Authority administers Ontario Regulation 220/01 (Boilers and Pressure Vessels) under the Technical Standards and Safety Act, 2000. Design registration follows CSA B51 and the ASME codes it references, with ASME Section V for examination methods. See TSSA Ontario compliance and CSA B51.
  • Oil and gas pipelines: TSSA's Fuels Safety programme administers Ontario Regulation 210/01 (Oil and Gas Pipeline Systems), which adopts CSA Z662. Interprovincial transmission lines are regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator. See CSA Z662.
  • Nuclear: the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission licenses nuclear power plants, and CSA N285.0 and N285.4 set requirements for CANDU pressure-retaining systems and their periodic inspection. Nuclear suppliers commonly work under CSA N299 quality-assurance requirements set by the utilities.
  • Structural steel and bridges: CSA W59 with fabricators certified to CSA W47.1, CSA S6 for highway bridges, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 on US-specification work. CSA W178.1 covers certification of welding inspection organisations; see CSA W178.1.

Industrial X-ray machines in Ontario workplaces fall under Regulation 861 (X-Ray Safety) under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, including registration with the Ministry of Labour. See CNSC compliance.

A procedure that passes an audit states the code requirement, shows how your equipment and people meet it, and is specific enough that two technicians would get the same result. Technique sheets turn it into settings for a particular weld, casting, forging or component. In nuclear work that often means detailed scan plans, qualification on representative mock-ups and tight documentation of equipment and calibration. In steel and fabrication it means joint geometry, thickness ranges and acceptance criteria from the right code. In aerospace it means part-number technique sheets, system performance checks and process control records. We write procedures and technique sheets, check them against the code edition your contract calls for, demonstrate techniques where required, and review procedures that a customer or auditor has rejected.

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is a named Level III who carries your programme's Level III responsibilities under a standing agreement; an interim Level III covers a gap. Atlantis provides both to Ontario employers, remotely for documents and technical questions and onsite for examinations, technique demonstrations and audits.

  • Ongoing outsourced Level III (retainer): we act as your programme's Level III, approving procedures and technique sheets, maintaining the written practice, administering examinations and attending audits. This suits Ontario inspection contractors, fabricators and component suppliers who need year-round cover without a full-time ASNT Level III.

Frequently asked questions about NDT Level III consulting in Ontario

Do Ontario employers need an ASNT Level III?

Only when they certify personnel to an ASNT scheme such as SNT-TC-1A or CP-189, which is common for suppliers to US utilities, US-code fabrication and US-owned plants. Work that only requires CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification does not need an ASNT written practice.

Can a nuclear supplier use SNT-TC-1A?

It depends on the customer. US nuclear utilities often specify CP-189 or a particular edition of SNT-TC-1A; Canadian utilities set their own requirements, typically alongside CSA N299 quality assurance. The purchase order and quality clauses decide.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in Ontario?

The Technical Standards and Safety Authority administers Ontario Regulation 220/01, Boilers and Pressure Vessels, under the Technical Standards and Safety Act, 2000.

Who regulates pipelines in Ontario?

TSSA administers Ontario Regulation 210/01, Oil and Gas Pipeline Systems, which adopts CSA Z662. Interprovincial pipelines are regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Ontario?

Gamma radiography requires a CNSC licence and CNSC-certified exposure device operators. X-ray equipment used at Ontario workplaces is covered by Regulation 861 under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, including registration.

What happened to CGSB certification in 2026?

The Canadian General Standards Board ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Guidance from Natural Resources Canada and CWB Group says CAN/CGSB-48.9712 remains valid and existing certifications continue. Confirm the current certification body for new certifications and renewals.

Can an outsourced Level III approve our procedures?

Yes, when your written practice designates that Level III and they hold certification in the relevant methods. Review must be genuine and traceable.

Can you prepare us for an aerospace customer or Nadcap-style audit?

Yes. We review your written practice, technique sheets, certification files and process control records, run a mock audit and help close findings. We do not grant accreditation or customer approval.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Ontario?

It depends on the number of methods, the customer regimes involved, whether you need a new written practice or a review, how many people need examining and how much onsite time is needed. Quotes are given on request after scoping.

Can you examine our technicians at our plant?

Yes. General and specific examinations can be administered under controlled conditions, and practical examinations are performed onsite on suitable specimens under your written practice.

Do you train technicians in Ontario?

Yes, to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, online and onsite at your facility. Atlantis does not train toward CGSB certification. See NDT training and practise on the Practical NDT simulator before practical examinations.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Oregon

Short answer: Oregon NDT employers can bring in an ASNT NDT Level III from Atlantis NDT for outsourced or interim Level III cover, SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets, Level I and II examinations under the employer's written practice, and readiness for customer, owner and accreditation audits. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, leads each engagement. Work is done remotely and onsite at your plant, shipyard or site anywhere in Oregon; Atlantis has no office in the state.

Oregon is a metals-and-water state as far as NDT is concerned. It has no oil refinery and no operating nuclear plant. What it does have is a dense industrial riverfront in Portland, where ships are repaired, barges and railcars are built, aerospace castings are poured and trucks are assembled; the bulk fuel tank farms that hold most of the state's liquid fuel supply on the banks of the Willamette; specialty-metals producers in the Willamette Valley; a steel minimill and plate production; federal hydroelectric dams on the Columbia; semiconductor manufacturing in Hillsboro; data centres in The Dalles and Prineville; gas transmission pipelines that run the length of the state; and coastal ports and bridges exposed to salt air. This page sets out what Oregon NDT programmes need from a Level III, the agencies and codes that apply, and how to request an Oregon Level III consultation.

Why Oregon NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: Oregon employers certifying NDT personnel to SNT-TC-1A need a Level III-approved written practice, method procedures and Level III-administered examinations. Aerospace casting customers, Navy and commercial ship owners, fuel terminal operators, utilities and semiconductor owners also audit their NDT suppliers and expect a named Level III behind the programme.

Portland's working riverfront. Swan Island on the Willamette is home to a large ship repair yard with dry docks that handle Navy, government and commercial vessels. At Rivergate, Gunderson builds barges and railcars for its parent Greenbrier, and a steel plate and pipe mill rolls heavy plate. Daimler Truck North America has its headquarters in Portland and builds trucks there. Precision Castparts, whose PCC Structurals operation in southeast Portland makes large titanium, nickel and steel structural castings for aircraft engines and airframes, anchors an aerospace supply chain of machine shops and special-process houses. Boeing has a parts plant in Gresham. Every one of these operations depends on weld, casting and forging inspection: radiography of castings, ultrasonic testing of plate and welds, penetrant and magnetic particle testing of machined parts, and visual inspection of ship and barge structures.

Fuel terminals. Most of Oregon's petroleum products arrive by pipeline from Washington refineries and by marine vessel, and are stored at bulk terminals along the Willamette in northwest Portland, an area known as the Critical Energy Infrastructure hub. The 2022 Oregon law SB 1567 lets the Department of Environmental Quality require large bulk fuel terminals in Columbia, Lane and Multnomah counties to assess their seismic vulnerability and carry out mitigation plans. Tank, piping and foundation work at these terminals relies on API 653 tank inspection and associated NDT.

Metals, power and technology. ATI's operations in Albany and Millersburg produce zirconium, titanium and other specialty alloys. Cascade Steel Rolling Mills runs a minimill in McMinnville. The US Army Corps of Engineers operates Bonneville, The Dalles, John Day and McNary dams on the Columbia, and utilities run hydro, gas-fired and wind generation across the state; penstocks, turbines, gates and cranes all need inspection. Intel's largest research and manufacturing campus is in Hillsboro, and data-centre construction continues in Hillsboro, The Dalles and Prineville. Williams' Northwest Pipeline and TC Energy's Gas Transmission Northwest carry natural gas through the state, and the Ruby pipeline ends at Malin near Klamath Falls. The Oregon Air National Guard flies from Portland and from Kingsley Field in Klamath Falls.

Most Oregon NDT companies are not big enough to employ a Level III in every method they perform. A Willamette Valley foundry with a small radiography and penetrant crew, a marine inspection contractor at Swan Island or a fabricator in Eugene still has to show a customer who approved its written practice and examined its technicians. ASNT Level III consulting services supply that function without a full-time hire.

Direct answer: Atlantis provides the full range of Level III functions to Oregon companies: written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets, examinations, outsourced and interim Level III, programme set-up, audit readiness and NDT support to API 510, 570 and 653 inspection programmes. Every engagement is scoped on a call.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own procedure for qualifying, examining and certifying NDT personnel. SNT-TC-1A recommends what it should cover, but an auditor checks your document against your records. We write written practices that fit your Oregon operation and audit existing ones so problems surface before a customer finds them.

Oregon's industry mix produces some recognisable written practice issues. Casting and forging suppliers to aerospace customers may need a programme that satisfies SNT-TC-1A for some work and NAS 410 or customer-specific rules for others, and the written practice must make clear which applies where. Marine contractors moving between Navy repair work and commercial vessels face different qualification expectations under different specifications. Fabricators that grew with the data-centre and semiconductor build-outs may have certified technicians under a borrowed template that never matched their methods. Companies that lost their Level III may have files nobody has reviewed in years.

Our written practices define methods, techniques and levels; training and experience requirements, referenced to the training requirements matrix; examination content and grading; practical specimens and checklists; vision testing; records; recertification; and how the Level III function is provided. Background is on our written practice development page and our SNT-TC-1A guidance.

Audits compare a sample of certification files with the written practice. Typical findings include radiographers certified without documented film or digital interpretation training, practical examinations without graded checklists, lapsed vision tests, technicians signing in methods outside their certification, and procedures that still reference superseded code editions. You receive a ranked list and, if you want it, help closing every item.

Where your written practice calls for formal training, Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A-based courses online and onsite; see NDT training in Oregon and corporate NDT training.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Oregon

Direct answer: Oregon procedures follow the governing code for each job: customer and ASTM specifications for aerospace castings and forgings, Navy and classification-society requirements for ships, AWS D1.1, D1.5 and D1.6 for structural, bridge and stainless work, API 653 and 570 for fuel terminals, ASME codes for boilers and pressure vessels, and API 1104 for pipelines.

  • Aerospace castings and forgings: customer specifications commonly reference ASTM E1417 for penetrant, E1444 for magnetic particle, E1742 for radiography and E2375 for ultrasonic testing of wrought products. Radiographic technique sheets for complex castings are part-specific and often customer-approved.
  • Ship repair and barge building: Navy technical publications for naval work, and classification-society and owner specifications for commercial vessels. Hull, piping and machinery welds need VT, MT, UT and RT procedures matched to the specification named in the contract. See shipbuilding audit support.
  • Fuel terminals: API 653 for aboveground storage tanks and API 570 for terminal piping, with ASME Section V methods. Floor scanning, shell thickness surveys and weld examinations need clear procedures and calibration control. See tank terminal audit support.
  • Boilers and pressure vessels: Oregon's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Program sits in the Building Codes Division of the Department of Consumer and Business Services. NDT for repairs and alterations follows the ASME and National Board requirements that apply.
  • Bridges and structures: AWS D1.5 for steel bridges and D1.1 for structural steel, with ODOT and project specifications. Oregon's coastal and Columbia River bridges add corrosion and fatigue inspection.
  • Pipelines: API 1104 under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Intrastate gas pipeline safety in Oregon is overseen by the Public Utility Commission of Oregon working with PHMSA; interstate lines such as Northwest Pipeline and GTN fall under PHMSA.
  • Radiography: Oregon is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is licensed and inspected by the Oregon Health Authority's Radiation Protection Services. Radiography procedures must work alongside the licensee's radiation safety programme, especially for field shooting in shipyards and on terminal sites.

Oregon's damp climate is a practical factor. Rain, condensation and cold steel on the coast and the lower Columbia affect penetrant and magnetic particle surface preparation, couplant performance and drying times. Procedures should state minimum surface conditions, temperature ranges and how calibration temperature differences are controlled under ASME Section V. We write those requirements in, and we review procedures written by others when a customer or auditor raises a concern. For questions about what a Level III can approve, see Level III method scope limitations.

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is named in your written practice and carries the Level III responsibilities under a standing agreement; an interim Level III covers a temporary gap. Atlantis provides both for Oregon employers, with document work done remotely and examinations, demonstrations and audits onsite at your facility when required.

  • Ongoing outsourced Level III: procedure and technique-sheet approvals, written practice maintenance, examinations, technical support for technicians and audit attendance. Suited to Portland-area inspection contractors, foundries and fabricators needing year-round Level III cover.
  • Project work: defined deliverables such as a written practice, a radiography technique set for a new casting family, PAUT scan plans for thick-plate welds, or examinations for a group of new hires.
  • Audit-preparation sprint: a focused review in the run-up to a customer, owner or accreditation audit.

Oregon's specialised employers, particularly aerospace casting and semiconductor operations, compete hard for experienced Level IIIs, and a smaller supplier can lose its Level III with little warning. Interim Level III cover keeps certifications and approvals moving while you recruit. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III. Contractors that work on both sides of the Columbia, in Oregon and Washington, can harmonise programmes across sites; see multi-site programme harmonisation.

Direct answer: Oregon NDT programmes face aerospace prime and Nadcap-style audits, ship-owner and Navy contractor audits, fuel terminal and utility owner audits, ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 17025 assessments and radiation safety inspections by the Oregon Health Authority. Aerospace casting customers check that every radiographic and penetrant technique is approved, every technician's certification matches the work signed, and process controls are recorded; see Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness. Ship owners and Navy contractors check procedures against the governing specification and personnel qualifications against the contract. Terminal owners and utilities check certifications, procedures and calibration before contractors start. Accreditation assessors look at competence records, method validation and traceability.

We prepare the NDT portion of each audit; we do not grant approvals, accreditation or vendor status. NDT Level III Consulting Services in Poland

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting for Polish companies that work to US codes or supply US customers: SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets to ASME, API and AWS, examinations under your written practice, outside-agency and interim Level III cover, and audit preparation. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, leads each engagement, remotely or onsite at your facility. Atlantis has no office in Poland and holds no Polish accreditation or UDT authorisation.

Poland has a long-established national NDT certification system built on PN-EN ISO 9712. Personnel are certified by accredited bodies such as UDT-CERT, which grew out of work by the Polish Society for NDT and Technical Diagnostics (PTBN) and the Office of Technical Inspection, and the certification centre at the Łukasiewicz Research Network's welding institute in Gliwice. Atlantis does not certify anyone to PN-EN ISO 9712 and does not train toward it. Our work is the US-facing part of Polish industry, which is growing fast: aero-engine and helicopter plants owned by or supplying American OEMs in the Podkarpacie region, the first Polish nuclear power plant being prepared with US reactor technology, energy and petrochemical projects delivered by US engineering contractors, and fabricators exporting to US clients. If your programme needs SNT-TC-1A documents or a named ASNT Level III, request a Poland Level III consultation.

Why Polish NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: A Polish employer that certifies NDT staff under ASNT SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice approved by a Level III, a procedure for every method and a Level III to examine and certify Level I and II personnel. Polish suppliers to US OEMs and US-code projects are expected to name that Level III and produce the records behind each certification at audit.

Aerospace is the strongest US link. The Aviation Valley cluster around Rzeszów in south-eastern Poland is one of Europe's densest aerospace manufacturing regions. Pratt & Whitney has major engine-component operations in Rzeszów, PZL Mielec is owned by Lockheed Martin and builds Black Hawk helicopters and aerostructures, and Safran and many Polish-owned machine shops, foundries and special-process houses supply engine and airframe parts. These plants run penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic, eddy current and radiographic inspection to American and European OEM specifications, usually with NAS 410 or EN 4179 personnel requirements and Nadcap accreditation for special processes.

Nuclear is the newest. Poland selected the Westinghouse AP1000 design for its first nuclear power plant at Lubiatowo-Kopalino in Pomerania, with Westinghouse and Bechtel as the technology and construction partners. The state project company, Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe, submitted its construction licence application to the national nuclear regulator in March 2026, with preparatory works under way on site; first nuclear concrete is expected later in the decade. A US-designed reactor brings US codes into the supply chain, notably ASME Section III for components and ASME Section XI for in-service inspection, and Polish fabricators and inspection companies that want to take part will be asked how their NDT personnel are qualified. Most of that work is years away, but programmes take time to build.

Energy and process industry form the backbone. Orlen's refinery at Płock is the largest in Poland, and the Gdańsk refinery, now part of the Orlen group, has Saudi Aramco as a minority shareholder. Chemical complexes operate at Police, Puławy, Kędzierzyn-Koźle and Włocławek. Gas infrastructure includes the LNG terminal in Świnoujście, the planned floating LNG terminal in the Gulf of Gdańsk, the Gaz-System transmission network and the Baltic Pipe from Norway via Denmark. Large coal and gas-fired power stations at Bełchatów, Kozienice, Opole and elsewhere, many under conversion or modernisation, need boiler, piping and turbine inspection. Offshore wind is the new growth sector: projects such as Baltic Power, Baltica 2 and Bałtyk 2 and 3 are bringing foundation, cable and substation work to the Baltic coast, with port and fabrication activity in Gdańsk, Gdynia and Szczecin, where shipyards also build and repair vessels and offshore units. Steelmaking in Dąbrowa Górnicza and Częstochowa, copper mining and smelting around Lubin and Głogów, and a large fabrication industry exporting to Germany and Scandinavia complete the picture.

Regulation is distinctive. The Office of Technical Inspection (UDT) supervises pressure equipment and other technical devices in operation, including periodic inspection, while the Transport Technical Inspection (TDT) covers transport equipment, and pressure equipment placed on the market must meet the Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU. Industrial radiography requires authorisation from the President of the National Atomic Energy Agency (PAA) under the Atomic Law, and PAA is also the nuclear safety regulator. The Polish Centre for Accreditation (PCA) accredits certification bodies, inspection bodies and laboratories. None of these requires SNT-TC-1A. US customers, US codes and US contractors often do, and that is where an ASNT Level III consulting service fits.

PN-EN ISO 9712 or SNT-TC-1A: which applies to Polish work?

Direct answer: PN-EN ISO 9712, with UDT-CERT and the Gliwice certification centre as the main certification bodies, is the Polish default and covers most EU-code and domestic work. SNT-TC-1A applies when a US code, owner, contractor or customer requires employer-based certification. Aerospace runs on NAS 410 or EN 4179. Many Polish companies need two or three of these side by side.

ISO 9712 places certification with an accredited third party; the certificate belongs to the technician. SNT-TC-1A makes the employer responsible, certifying staff under its own written practice with examinations administered by a Level III; certification ends when employment ends. ASME Section V generally refers to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 for personnel qualification, so ASME Section VIII vessels, B31.3 piping and, in future, ASME Section III nuclear components built in Poland will tend to bring SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 with them, unless the contract states otherwise.

Each engagement is scoped on a call around your methods, codes and customers.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: The written practice is your company's own rulebook for training, examining, certifying and recertifying NDT staff. Under SNT-TC-1A it is the document an auditor checks first. We draft it to match how your Polish operation actually works, then audit your certification records against it.

Polish NDT technicians are generally well trained and hold ISO 9712 certificates, so the gap is rarely competence. The gap is that the quality system was built around third-party certification, and when a US customer asks for an employer-based written practice there is nothing to show. Translating an American template word for word causes its own problems: references to arrangements that do not exist in Poland, methods the company does not use, and examination rules nobody follows. A written practice has to be written for the company that will live with it, and it often needs to exist in both Polish and English so that technicians and auditors can both use it.

The written practices we prepare cover:

  • Scope: methods, techniques, products and the codes or specifications that apply.
  • Duties and signature authority for trainee, Level I, Level II and Level III.
  • Training and experience requirements, cross-referenced to the training requirements matrix, with explicit rules for crediting PN-EN ISO 9712 training and experience.
  • Examinations: general, specific and practical; grading; retests; who administers each.
  • Vision examinations and their interval.
  • Records, retention and access.
  • Interrupted service, revocation, recertification and outside-agency arrangements.

An audit samples certification files and checks each element the document requires, then returns numbered findings with clause references and fixes. Background is on written practice development, written practices for nuclear power and SNT-TC-1A certification guidance.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Poland

Direct answer: Each NDT method needs a procedure that satisfies the governing code, and production work usually needs technique sheets for specific parts or welds. In Poland that means PN-EN and ISO standards for domestic and EU work, ASME and AWS on US contracts, OEM specifications in aerospace, and owner practices in refining and power.

  • Aerospace. Penetrant and magnetic particle lines, immersion and contact UT of forgings and machined parts, eddy current on holes and surfaces, and radiography of castings and welds, all to OEM specifications. See Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness and written practices for aerospace.
  • Nuclear supply chain. ASME Section III components need NDT performed under Section V with personnel qualified as Section III and the contract require. Polish fabricators preparing for the AP1000 programme can start by aligning procedures and personnel documents now; we can help with that preparation, not with nuclear qualification or regulatory approvals.
  • Refining and chemicals. Turnaround inspection at Płock, Gdańsk and the chemical complexes: corrosion mapping with PAUT, weld inspection after repair, exchanger and tank inspection under owner practices that often follow API 510, 570 and 653. See refining Level III audit support and petrochemical Level III audit support.
  • Offshore wind and shipbuilding. Thick-section structural welds in foundations, towers and substations, and hull and outfitting work, to EN ISO 17640, ISO 5817, DNV and class rules, with AWS D1.1 added on some US-contract work. See offshore Level III audit support.
  • Gas and LNG. Pipeline girth welds, terminal piping and cryogenic tanks under operator specifications. See pipeline Level III audit support.
  • Power generation. Boiler tubes, headers, high-energy piping and turbine components at large coal and gas stations. See power generation Level III audit support.
  • Steel, metals and mining. Mill equipment, rolls, plate and heavy mining machinery. See mining Level III audit support.

Our procedure development service produces procedures with defined essential variables, calibration and reference standards, coverage, recording and evaluation rules and acceptance criteria, and plans performance demonstrations where PAUT or TOFD applications need them. An existing Polish procedure can often be kept and given a US-code annex rather than rewritten.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Polish crews

Direct answer: An outside-agency Level III, called a responsible Level 3 by many European buyers, is a qualified Level III who is not your employee but formally holds the Level III duties in your written practice. For Polish companies with a growing but part-time SNT-TC-1A workload, this is usually the most practical model.

The arrangement has to be documented: the written practice names the outside agency, defines what the Level III approves, sets how examinations are administered and graded, and states who keeps records. We write that language at the start.

  • Ongoing outside-agency Level III. Written practice ownership, procedure approvals, examinations, technical queries and customer audits on a standing basis.
  • Project-based work. A defined deliverable such as a written practice for a first US order, a procedure package for an offshore wind contract or technique sheets for a new aerospace part family.
  • Audit-preparation sprint. A focused review before a scheduled US customer, OEM or EPC audit.

For aerospace programmes under NAS 410 or EN 4179, whether an external ASNT Level III may act as your responsible Level 3 is decided by your customer and the relevant aerospace NDT board; confirm before you appoint anyone. When a Level III leaves at short notice, interim Level III cover keeps approvals and examinations moving. Ask about outside-agency Level 3 cover for your Polish team.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Polish NDT employers face US OEM and EPC audits, owner audits at refineries, power stations and energy projects, UDT oversight of equipment in service, and PCA accreditation assessments for inspection bodies and laboratories. Atlantis prepares the NDT programme evidence: written practice, procedures, certification files and Level III records.

A US customer audit follows a part or weld back through the report to the procedure, its Level III approval, the technician's certification file and the equipment calibration. Owner audits add site approvals and witness points. PCA assessments of ISO/IEC 17020 inspection bodies and ISO/IEC 17025 laboratories are a separate process in which Atlantis has no role, though we can make sure the NDT technical content an assessor samples is coherent and traceable. UDT's statutory role over equipment is likewise untouched; we support the NDT behind it.

A readiness review confirms that:

  • The written practice reflects current methods, staff and customers.
  • Every certified technician's file is complete, in date and correctly signed.
  • Each procedure in use is current, approved and cited on reports.
  • Equipment and reference standards are calibrated and traceable.
  • The Level III arrangement is documented, in both languages where needed.

Where in Poland we support NDT programmes

Direct answer: Atlantis works with Polish companies remotely and onsite at their facilities. The main clusters are Podkarpacie's Aviation Valley, the Pomeranian coast, Masovia and Płock, Upper Silesia and Lesser Poland, Lower Silesia, and West Pomerania.

Rzeszów, Mielec and Podkarpacie. Aero-engine and helicopter manufacturing for US and European OEMs and a deep supply chain of machine shops, foundries and special-process houses. The strongest demand for US-aligned NDT documentation in the country.

Gdańsk, Gdynia and Pomerania. The Gdańsk refinery, shipyards, offshore wind ports and fabrication, the planned FSRU, and the nuclear site at Lubiatowo-Kopalino. Existing Atlantis pages for this area include NDT training in Gdańsk, third-party inspection in Gdańsk, NDT ERP for Gdańsk and digital twins in Gdańsk.

Płock, Warsaw and Masovia. Orlen's Płock refinery and petrochemical complex, the Kozienice power station, and the head offices of energy companies, EPCs and inspection firms in Warsaw.

Katowice, Gliwice, Kraków and southern Poland. Steel, coke, power, heavy fabrication and engineering, plus the certification centre in Gliwice. See third-party inspection in Katowice.

Wrocław, Lubin and Lower Silesia. Copper mining and smelting, aerospace and automotive suppliers, and the Turów and Opole power stations in the wider south-west.

Szczecin, Police and Świnoujście. The LNG terminal, the Police chemical complex, shipyards and offshore wind logistics. For more on Atlantis in Poland see Atlantis NDT Poland; for neighbouring markets see Germany.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: Engagements start with a scoping call, continue with a review of your documents and records, and deliver written practices, procedures, examinations or audit support. Most work is remote; onsite visits are planned for practical examinations, demonstrations and audits. A quote follows the call.

  1. Scoping call. Methods, staff, schemes in use (PN-EN ISO 9712, NAS 410 or EN 4179, SNT-TC-1A), customers, codes and deadlines.
  2. Document request. Current written practice or quality procedure, NDT procedures, sample certification files and customer requirements, in Polish or English.
  3. Review and plan. Gaps, deliverables, sequence and onsite needs agreed in writing.
  4. Delivery. Documents drafted in English, reviewed with your team and issued under revision control; your team can maintain a Polish working translation.
  5. Examinations. General and specific examinations remotely under controlled conditions where your written practice allows; practical examinations onsite on real specimens.
  6. Ongoing support. Outside-agency Level III service for approvals, questions, recertification and audits.

Pricing is quote on request: affordable, accessible and fully customisable. Request a quote for Level III support in Poland.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, the named Level III on documents Atlantis prepares and approves. Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training, available online or onsite, the Practical NDT simulator for practice before practical examinations, and an NDT ERP that keeps PN-EN ISO 9712, NAS 410 and ASNT certifications in one register. None of these replaces ISO 9712 certification by an accredited Polish body.

Frequently asked questions about NDT Level III consulting in Poland

Is ASNT SNT-TC-1A recognised in Poland?

It is not the national scheme; PN-EN ISO 9712 is. SNT-TC-1A is recognised wherever a contract, code or customer requires it, most often ASME and AWS work, US-designed plants and supply to US OEMs.

Who certifies NDT personnel to ISO 9712 in Poland?

Accredited certification bodies, including UDT-CERT and the certification centre of the Łukasiewicz Research Network in Gliwice. Atlantis does not certify to ISO 9712.

Can an ASNT Level III be our responsible Level 3?

For an SNT-TC-1A programme, yes, as an outside agency named in your written practice. For aerospace work under NAS 410 or EN 4179, your customer and the relevant aerospace NDT board decide; confirm before appointing anyone.

Will the AP1000 project require SNT-TC-1A?

Each contract will set its own personnel qualification requirements. Because the plant is a US design built to ASME codes, suppliers should expect ASME Section V-based requirements, which generally reference SNT-TC-1A or CP-189; confirm against the actual contract documents when they arrive.

Who licenses industrial radiography in Poland?

The President of the National Atomic Energy Agency (PAA) authorises activities involving ionising radiation, including industrial radiography, under the Atomic Law.

What is UDT's role in NDT?

UDT, the Office of Technical Inspection, supervises pressure equipment and other technical devices in service, including periodic inspection, and its certification arm UDT-CERT certifies NDT personnel to ISO 9712. Atlantis has no UDT authorisation and does not perform statutory inspection.

Does Atlantis offer ISO 9712 training in Poland?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. We can recognise existing ISO 9712 certificates and experience inside an SNT-TC-1A written practice where the rules allow.

Can documents be prepared in Polish?

Atlantis prepares documents in English, the language US customers and auditors expect. Your team can maintain a controlled Polish working translation, and we can review that it matches the approved English version.

Can examinations be done remotely?

General and specific written examinations can be administered remotely under controlled conditions defined in your written practice. Practical examinations need real specimens and take place onsite.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Poland?

Quote on request. It depends on the methods, the state of your documents, how many staff need examination and whether onsite days are needed.

Do you support API-style inspection programmes at Polish refineries?

We support the NDT side of API 510, 570 and 653 style programmes: technique selection, procedure review and data quality. See API 510 support, API 570 support and API 653 support. We do not sell risk-based inspection or fitness-for-service assessments.

Does Atlantis have an office in Poland?

No. Atlantis supports Polish clients remotely and travels to your facility for onsite work.

Talk to a Level III about your Polish NDT programme

If a US OEM, EPC, code or customer is asking your Polish team for an SNT-TC-1A written practice, US-code procedures or a named Level III, start with a short call. Book a Level III consultation for Poland or ask about a written practice for your first US order.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Quebec

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to Quebec employers: outsourced and interim Level III cover, SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, NDT procedures and technique sheets, personnel examinations under your written practice, and preparation for aerospace, owner and accreditation audits. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, and are delivered remotely or onsite at your facility. Atlantis has no office in Quebec, and it works in English; French versions of documents are planned with you during scoping.

Quebec's NDT market is built around aerospace, aluminium, hydroelectricity and heavy manufacturing rather than oil and gas. Greater Montreal is one of the world's main aerospace clusters, with aircraft assembly, aero-engines, landing gear and hundreds of machining, special-process and component suppliers. The Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean region, the Côte-Nord and the Bécancour industrial park produce much of North America's primary aluminium. Hydro-Québec runs one of the largest hydroelectric systems anywhere. Lévis has a refinery and a federal-programme shipyard, Montréal-Est has refining and petrochemicals, and the province builds rail cars, buses, structural steel and bridges. A large part of that output is sold to US customers, which is why so many Quebec suppliers are asked to show an employer-based ASNT programme with a named Level III. This page explains what Quebec employers need from a Level III, which regulators and codes apply, and how to request a Quebec Level III consultation.

Why Quebec NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: A Quebec employer that certifies its own NDT personnel to ASNT SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice, method procedures and a responsible Level III who examines and certifies Level I and II staff. Aerospace primes, US customers and plant owners audit those programmes, so the Level III must be named, certified in the methods used and able to explain every document, whatever language it is kept in.

Aerospace defines Quebec's NDT profile. Around Montreal, Mirabel, Longueuil, Dorval and Saint-Laurent, business-jet and commercial-aircraft assembly, helicopter manufacturing, aero-engine production and landing-gear manufacturing sit at the top of a supply chain that includes machine shops, heat treaters, platers, composite fabricators and NDT laboratories across the Montérégie, Laval and the Laurentides. Those suppliers run penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic, eddy current and radiographic inspection under customer specifications. Some customers specify NAS 410 or their own rules; others, especially US customers outside the aerospace primes, accept an SNT-TC-1A programme. Either way, the supplier needs someone who can read the flow-down requirements and keep the NDT programme consistent with them.

Aluminium is the second pillar. Smelters in the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean region, at Sept-Îles, Baie-Comeau, Deschambault and Bécancour run potlines, anode plants, casting centres, cranes and large structural and electrical systems. Maintenance NDT there is heavy on magnetic particle, ultrasonic and visual inspection of cranes, structures, rotating equipment and pressure equipment, and the welding of aluminium busbars and structures has its own inspection challenges.

Hydro-Québec's generating stations, from the La Grande complex in the James Bay region to the Manicouagan-Outardes and Romaine rivers, need inspection of penstocks, spiral cases, turbine runners, gates and hoists, often during short planned outages. Refining at Lévis and Montréal-Est, the chemical industry in Montréal-Est and Bécancour, the Chantier Davie shipyard at Lévis, pulp and paper mills throughout the province, iron-ore operations on the Côte-Nord, gold mines in Abitibi and an enormous stock of steel and concrete bridges complete the picture.

Many of these employers are small. An aerospace special-process shop with four penetrant inspectors, a fabricator with two UT technicians or a maintenance contractor serving the smelters cannot justify a full-time ASNT Level III, but still needs the functions one performs. ASNT Level III consulting services fill that role.

Which certification scheme applies in Quebec?

Direct answer: Canada's national NDT certification scheme, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712), is what most Quebec owners and Canadian codes expect. Aerospace work is often governed by NAS 410 or customer rules. SNT-TC-1A applies when a US customer, US-owned plant or US-code contract specifies employer-based ASNT certification. Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A Level III expertise; it does not certify or train to CGSB.

Quebec has an unusually mixed landscape. In a single industrial park you can find an aerospace supplier certifying inspectors under NAS 410 for one customer, a structural fabricator whose technicians hold CGSB certificates for Canadian work, and a pressure-vessel shop that needs an SNT-TC-1A written practice because its biggest customer is in Ohio. Each scheme puts responsibility in a different place: CGSB certification belongs to the individual and is issued by an independent certification body, while SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 are employer-based and depend on a written practice and a responsible Level III. On the national scheme: the Canadian General Standards Board, which published CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Guidance from Natural Resources Canada and CWB Group says the standard remains valid and certifications continue; confirm the current certification body and transition arrangements before relying on any one source.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own document for training, examining, certifying and recertifying NDT personnel; under SNT-TC-1A it is what an auditor reviews first. In Quebec it must also fit a company quality system that is often kept in French, sit beside NAS 410 or CGSB arrangements, and match how the shop actually works. We write it to the work, then audit the records against it.

Quebec suppliers tend to run into two problems. The first is overlap: a company has an aerospace programme under NAS 410, a general programme copied from a US template, and staff with CGSB certificates, and no single document explains which rules apply to which job. Auditors then find technicians signing work under the wrong programme, practical examinations graded without checklists, expired vision tests and experience records that cannot be traced. The second is language. Under Quebec's Charter of the French Language, documents provided to workers, such as procedures, work instructions and training material, generally need to be available in French. A written practice that exists only in English, or a French version that has drifted from the English one, creates its own audit findings.

We start from the work: which methods and techniques, which customers and codes, which existing certifications. The written practice then sets out levels, training and experience (linked to the training requirements matrix rather than invented numbers), examination content and grading, vision testing, records, recertification and Level III arrangements, with clear clauses on how CGSB and NAS 410 certifications are treated. Atlantis prepares documents in English; if you need French versions, we plan the translation and review steps with you so the two stay aligned. The written practice development page shows the structure, and our notes on written practices for aerospace, steel and metals and pulp and paper cover sector details.

An audit tests the records against the document and returns findings ranked by risk with suggested corrections. For employers that train in-house, Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A-based training online and onsite; see NDT training in Canada and corporate NDT training.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Quebec

Direct answer: Quebec NDT procedures follow the code governing the item: CSA B51 and the ASME codes for boilers, pressure vessels and piping approved by the Régie du bâtiment du Québec, CSA W59 and AWS D1.1 for structural steel, CSA S6 for highway bridges, CSA Z662 for pipelines, and customer specifications for aerospace, rail and other manufactured parts.

  • Pressure installations: the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) regulates boilers, pressure vessels, fittings and piping under the Building Act and the Regulation respecting pressure installations. Designs are registered with a Canadian Registration Number and conform to CSA B51 and the codes it references, and equipment is inspected periodically by persons or bodies recognised by the RBQ. ASME Section V governs examination methods. See RBQ Quebec compliance, CSA B51 and CRN registration.
  • Pipelines: interprovincial transmission pipelines crossing Quebec fall under the Canada Energy Regulator, and CSA Z662 is the core technical standard; for pipelines and gas distribution regulated within the province, confirm the applicable provincial authority for the specific system. See CSA Z662.
  • Structural steel, bridges and rail: CSA W59 with fabricators certified to CSA W47.1, CSA S6 for highway bridges, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 on US-specification work, and customer specifications for rail cars and transit vehicles. CSA W178.1 covers certification of welding inspection organisations; see CSA W178.1.
  • Aerospace: customer specifications that frequently call up ASTM practices such as E1417 for penetrant and E1444 for magnetic particle testing, plus customer approvals for special processes.
  • Radiography: gamma radiography is licensed by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission, and exposure devices must be operated by CNSC-certified exposure device operators or under their direct supervision. Workplace health and safety rules administered by the CNESST also apply; confirm current provincial requirements for X-ray equipment. See CNSC compliance.

A procedure that holds up states the code requirement, shows how your equipment and people meet it, and is specific enough that two technicians perform the examination identically. Technique sheets turn it into settings for a specific part number, weld or component. For aerospace penetrant and magnetic particle lines, that means process control checks, system performance verification and part-specific parameters. For hydroelectric penstocks and turbine components, it means scan plans and acceptance criteria that work within outage windows. For smelter cranes and structures, it means inspection methods and frequencies that the maintenance team can repeat. For pressure vessels built for US customers, it means ASME Section V and VIII requirements applied exactly. We write procedures and technique sheets, check them against the edition your contract names, demonstrate techniques where required and review procedures a customer or auditor has rejected.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Quebec teams

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is a named Level III who carries your programme's Level III responsibilities under a standing agreement; an interim Level III covers a gap. Atlantis provides both to Quebec employers, remotely for documents and technical questions and onsite for examinations, technique demonstrations and audits, in Montreal, the regions and at remote sites when needed.

  • Ongoing outsourced Level III (retainer): we act as your programme's Level III, approving procedures and technique sheets, maintaining the written practice, administering examinations and attending customer audits.
  • Project-based work: a defined deliverable, such as an SNT-TC-1A written practice for a new US customer, procedures for adding PAUT or eddy current, technique sheets for a new part family, or examinations for new hires.
  • Audit-preparation sprint: a focused review before a customer source audit, owner audit or accreditation assessment.

Experienced Level IIIs in Quebec are concentrated in the aerospace primes, large inspection companies and Hydro-Québec, which makes them hard for a small supplier to hire. If your only Level III retires, you may be unable to certify a new inspector or close a customer's corrective-action request. Interim Level III cover keeps the programme compliant while you recruit. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III. Companies with plants in Quebec, Ontario and the US can use multi-site NDT programme harmonisation to align their written practices.

Audit readiness: aerospace, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Quebec NDT programmes are audited by aerospace primes and their customers, by US customers of fabricators and machine shops, by smelter, refinery and utility owners, by accreditation bodies for ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 17025 laboratories, by CWB Group for CSA W178.1, and by radiation-safety regulators. Atlantis prepares the NDT personnel and procedure side of each audit.

Aerospace audits are the most demanding: they trace each technician's certification, every procedure revision and every process-control record. Some customers require Nadcap-style special-process accreditation; our Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness page explains how those audits view an NDT programme. US customers of Quebec fabricators audit against SNT-TC-1A and their purchase-order clauses. Owners such as smelters, refineries and utilities review contractors' qualification records before outages and turnarounds. ISO/IEC 17025 assessments look at method validation, traceability and competence. Radiography licensees are inspected by the CNSC for radiation safety.

We review your written practice, procedures, technique sheets, certification files, vision tests and calibration records against the auditor's checklist, run a mock audit and help close gaps. We do not grant accreditation, customer approvals or RBQ recognition; we help you prepare for the organisations that do. The aerospace audit support, steel and metals audit support, power generation audit support, refining audit support, shipbuilding audit support and infrastructure audit support pages describe what each type of audit focuses on. If an audit is on the calendar, ask about an audit-preparation review for your Quebec programme.

Sector notes: what Quebec industries ask of a Level III

Direct answer: Aerospace suppliers need traceable certifications and part-specific technique sheets; aluminium smelters need dependable maintenance inspection of cranes, structures and equipment; Hydro-Québec contractors need outage-ready procedures for penstocks and turbines; refineries and shipyards need code-matched weld inspection. The Level III's priorities follow the sector.

Aerospace in Greater Montreal

Assembly, engine, landing-gear and component plants in Mirabel, Longueuil, Dorval and Saint-Laurent, and the supply chain around them, use PT, MT, ET, UT and RT under customer specifications. Process control and part-number technique sheets are what auditors check first.

Aluminium smelting

Smelters in Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, on the Côte-Nord and at Bécancour and Deschambault need maintenance NDT on overhead cranes, potroom structures, rotating equipment and pressure equipment. See Practical NDT in Saguenay.

Hydroelectric generation

Penstocks, spiral cases, runners, gates and hoists are inspected during planned outages, often at remote northern sites, which places a premium on procedures that crews can execute quickly and consistently.

Refining, chemicals and shipbuilding

The Lévis and Montréal-Est refineries and the chemical plants of Montréal-Est and Bécancour run turnaround inspection scopes; the Davie shipyard at Lévis builds and refits vessels with heavy structural-weld inspection. See refining NDT training in Montreal and refining NDT training in Quebec City.

Mining, pulp and paper, rail and bridges

Iron-ore operations on the Côte-Nord, gold mines in Abitibi, pulp and paper mills, rail-car builders and bridge fabricators all rely on UT, MT and VT under Canadian and, for export work, US codes.

Cities we support across Quebec

Direct answer: Atlantis supports NDT employers anywhere in Quebec, remotely and onsite at your facility, including Greater Montreal and Laval, the Montérégie, Mirabel and the Laurentides, Quebec City and Lévis, Trois-Rivières and Bécancour, Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, the Côte-Nord, Sherbrooke and Abitibi. There is no Atlantis office in the province.

Montreal, Laval and the Montérégie. Aerospace, refining and petrochemicals in Montréal-Est, rail and transit manufacturing, structural fabrication and many NDT laboratories. See NDT training in Montreal, Practical NDT in Montreal, NDT ERP in Montreal, NDT reporting software in Montreal and digital twins in Montreal.

Mirabel and the Laurentides. Aircraft and helicopter assembly and their suppliers, supported remotely and onsite.

Quebec City and Lévis. Refining, shipbuilding, manufacturing and public infrastructure. See Practical NDT in Quebec City.

Trois-Rivières and Bécancour. Aluminium, chemicals and the Bécancour industrial park.

Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean. Aluminium smelting, hydroelectric assets, pulp and paper. See Practical NDT in Saguenay.

Côte-Nord. Sept-Îles and Baie-Comeau aluminium, iron-ore handling and port facilities, and the Manicouagan hydroelectric system.

Sherbrooke, the Eastern Townships and Abitibi. Manufacturing, rail and mining, supported remotely with site visits for examinations and audits.

Province-wide: the Quebec Practical NDT hub for simulator practice before practical examinations on real specimens.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: You outline your methods, customers, codes, language requirements and deadlines on a call; we agree scope, deliverables and the remote and onsite split; the work is drafted and reviewed with your team; and for ongoing cover we remain your named Level III. Quotes are given on request after scoping.

  1. Scoping call. Your operation, methods and techniques, the certifications your people hold (ASNT, CGSB, NAS 410), customer and code requirements, audit dates and whether French versions of documents are needed.
  2. Document request. Your written practice, quality-manual sections, procedures and a sample of certification files, in English or French.
  3. Proposal. A written scope: deliverables, remote and onsite work, translation steps if needed, and who does what. Quotes on request.
  4. Delivery. Drafting and review with your team; examinations administered under your written practice; site visits planned around production, outages and travel to the regions.
  5. Handover or ongoing cover. Final documents and records under your control, or continuing Level III approvals, support and audit attendance.

To begin, book a Level III scoping call for Quebec.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Customers and auditors want to know whose name is on the written practice and procedures; with Atlantis that is clear from the start. Anoop also leads Atlantis NDT's SNT-TC-1A-based training, so programme documents and training content stay aligned.

Frequently asked questions about NDT Level III consulting in Quebec

Do Quebec companies need an ASNT Level III?

Only when they certify personnel to an ASNT scheme, which US customers, US-owned plants and US-code contracts often require. Work governed only by CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or by an aerospace customer's NAS 410 programme follows those rules instead.

Can one company run SNT-TC-1A, NAS 410 and CGSB together?

Yes, and many Quebec suppliers do. The written practice should state which scheme governs which work and how certifications under one are treated under another. CGSB certificates remain with the certification body.

Do our NDT procedures need to be in French?

Under the Charter of the French Language, documents provided to workers in Quebec generally need to be available in French. Confirm your obligations with your own adviser; Atlantis prepares documents in English and plans French versions with you during scoping.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in Quebec?

The Régie du bâtiment du Québec, under the Building Act and the Regulation respecting pressure installations. Designs carry a Canadian Registration Number and equipment is inspected by persons or bodies recognised by the RBQ.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Quebec?

Gamma radiography requires a CNSC licence and CNSC-certified exposure device operators. Provincial workplace health and safety rules also apply; confirm current requirements for X-ray equipment with the province.

What happened to CGSB certification in 2026?

The Canadian General Standards Board ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Notices from Natural Resources Canada and CWB Group say CAN/CGSB-48.9712 remains valid and certifications continue; confirm the current certification body for new certifications and renewals.

Can you prepare an aerospace supplier for a customer audit?

Yes. We review your written practice, technique sheets, certification files and process control records, run a mock audit and help close findings. We do not grant accreditation or customer approvals.

Can an outsourced Level III approve our procedures?

Yes, when your written practice designates that Level III and they are certified in the relevant methods. The review must be genuine and traceable.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Quebec?

It depends on scope: methods, customer regimes, whether you need a new written practice or a review, translation needs, how many people need examining and how much onsite time is required. Quotes are given on request after scoping.

Can you administer examinations at our plant?

Yes. General and specific examinations can be administered under controlled conditions, and practical examinations are performed onsite on suitable specimens under your written practice.

Can you train our technicians in Quebec?

Yes, to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, online and onsite at your facility, delivered in English. Atlantis does not train toward CGSB certification. See NDT training and practise on the Practical NDT simulator before practical examinations.

Talk to a Level III about your Quebec programme

Whether you run a penetrant line for an aero-engine customer in Longueuil, maintain cranes in a Saguenay smelter, inspect penstocks during a Hydro-Québec outage or build pressure vessels in the Beauce for a US buyer, the Level III questions are the same: does the written practice match the work and the customer, are the procedures right, and can you prove each inspector is qualified under the scheme the order requires? Ask about outsourced Level III cover in Quebec, or request a written practice review. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Quotes on request.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Queensland

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III services to Queensland employers, remotely and onsite at the employer's own facility. That includes acting as your outsourced or interim Level III under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, writing and auditing written practices, writing and approving procedures and technique sheets, administering qualification exams under your written practice, and preparing you for owner, customer and prime-contractor audits. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, leads every engagement, and scopes are quoted on request.

Queensland buyers deserve a straight account of where we fit. The local norm for NDT personnel is AINDT certification under ISO 9712. Pressure-equipment inspectors working to AS/NZS 3788 are commonly AICIP-certified, and laboratories and inspection bodies compete on NATA accreditation. Atlantis holds none of those local credentials and does not claim to. Our value is SNT-TC-1A and US-code expertise for the Queensland companies that need it: contractors to the Curtis Island LNG plants, suppliers to US aerospace and defence primes in South East Queensland, and fabricators building to ASME, API or AWS specifications. If that is your situation, request a Queensland Level III quote.

Why Queensland NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: A Queensland employer that certifies its NDT personnel under ASNT SNT-TC-1A must have a Level III who owns the written practice, approves procedures and administers exams. Most Queensland inspection companies are mid-sized and AINDT-based, so when an LNG operator, refinery, US OEM or defence prime asks for ASNT-based certification, an outsourced Level III is the practical answer.

Queensland's industrial map is spread along a long coastline and deep into the resources regions. Gladstone is the heavy-industry anchor: three LNG export plants on Curtis Island (QCLNG, APLNG and GLNG) process coal seam gas piped from the Surat and Bowen basins, and the APLNG downstream facility is operated by ConocoPhillips, a US-headquartered company. Gladstone also hosts alumina refineries, the Boyne Island aluminium smelter, a coal-fired power station and a busy bulk port. These assets generate construction, maintenance and turnaround inspection of piping, vessels, tanks, heat exchangers and structural steel.

Brisbane holds the Ampol Lytton refinery, one of only two fuel refineries still operating in Australia, along with the port, chemical and fuel terminals, and a large fabrication and maintenance supply base. Refinery turnarounds bring in UT thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD weld inspection, tube inspection and a heavy demand for documented procedures. See refining audit support.

The coal and minerals economy runs through Central and North Queensland. The Bowen Basin mines around Moranbah, Dysart and Emerald and the export terminals near Mackay and Gladstone rely on MT and UT of draglines, shovels, haul-truck components and conveyor drives. Townsville hosts zinc and copper refining and a growing defence presence, and the North West Minerals Province around Mount Isa adds processing plant and mobile equipment. Power stations at Callide, Stanwell, Tarong, Kogan Creek and Millmerran need boiler and high-energy piping inspection during outages.

Aerospace and defence are increasingly important. Boeing Defence Australia, part of the US Boeing group, is headquartered in Brisbane and is developing MQ-28 Ghost Bat production at the Wellcamp precinct near Toowoomba. RAAF Base Amberley near Ipswich supports heavy-lift and air-combat fleets, and the armoured-vehicle manufacturing centre at Redbank anchors a land-systems supply chain. Suppliers to US aerospace primes often find their customer's NDT requirements reference ASNT-based qualification and NAS 410 or equivalent standards, so check the purchase order flow-downs before choosing your scheme.

Queensland's regulators are distinct from the other states. Workplace Health and Safety Queensland administers plant design and item registration for boilers and pressure vessels under the Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011. Industrial radiography is licensed by Queensland Health under the Radiation Safety Act 1999, which requires a use licence for each radiographer and a possession licence with an approved radiation safety and protection plan for the company. Petroleum and gas pipelines are licensed under the Petroleum and Gas (Production and Safety) Act 2004, which requires compliance with AS 2885, and safety is overseen by the Petroleum and Gas Inspectorate of Resources Safety and Health Queensland, which also regulates mine safety. Confirm the current requirement with the regulator before mobilising.

Which NDT certification scheme applies in Queensland?

Direct answer: AINDT certification under ISO 9712 is standard for Queensland NDT technicians, AICIP certification applies to in-service pressure-equipment inspectors under AS/NZS 3788, and NATA accreditation applies to laboratories and inspection bodies. ASNT SNT-TC-1A is used when a client or specification calls for it, which is common on US-owned and US-code work.

The difference that matters for Queensland employers is who holds the certificate. Under AINDT, the technician holds a personal, portable certificate issued by a central body. Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies the technician against its own written practice, and the certification lapses when the technician leaves. That makes SNT-TC-1A flexible, because the employer can tailor training, experience and exams to its actual work, and demanding, because the employer must run the programme properly and a Level III must stand behind it.

QuestionAINDT / ISO 9712ASNT SNT-TC-1A
Who issues the certificate?Central certification bodyThe employer, under its written practice
Is it portable between employers?YesNo; a new employer must recertify
Who sets the exams?The certification bodyThe employer's Level III
Typical Queensland useMost contracts, NATA-accredited labs, state infrastructureUS-owned operators, US OEM and defence supply chains, US-code projects
Atlantis roleNone for certificationWritten practice, Level III, exams, procedures, audits

Many Queensland companies run both: an AINDT-certified workforce for most clients, plus an SNT-TC-1A written practice for the jobs that require it. Done well, the same training records, experience logs and vision tests support both, which keeps the administration manageable.

Level III services for Queensland employers

Direct answer: Atlantis provides every Level III function an SNT-TC-1A programme depends on, from writing the written practice to approving technique sheets, running exams, reviewing certifications and preparing for audits. Most work is remote; practical exams and some audits are done onsite at your Queensland facility.

Outsourced Level IIINamed ASNT Level III in your written practice; approvals, exams, technical questionsGladstone maintenance contractor supporting LNG and alumina shutdowns
Interim Level IIITemporary cover during recruitment or absenceBrisbane inspection firm mid-way through a refinery turnaround season
