Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: Atlantis writes SNT-TC-1A written practices for Queensland employers from a blank page or revises existing ones, and audits written practices against SNT-TC-1A and client requirements. The output is a document your Level III can stand behind and an auditor can trace from end to end.

When we review a Queensland written practice, we test it against the work the company actually does. A Gladstone contractor that performs PAUT weld inspection and corrosion mapping needs PAUT covered explicitly, with training and experience requirements that make sense. A Brisbane aerospace supplier may need to show how its programme meets its customer's flow-downs, which often go beyond SNT-TC-1A. A Bowen Basin mining contractor needs MT and UT for heavy components and probably nothing else. A written practice that tries to cover everything usually covers nothing well.

The audit side is equally practical. We sample technicians, trace their certification back through training records, experience logs, exam papers, grades and vision tests, and note every break in the chain. We also check how outside agencies, transfers from other employers and AINDT certificates are handled, because that is where Queensland programmes most often go wrong when staff move between contractors. See written practice development and the training requirements matrix.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Queensland

Direct answer: Queensland NDT procedures must meet the code governing the work: ASME V with B31.3 or Section VIII on many LNG and refinery packages, AS 2885 or API 1104 on pipelines, AS/NZS 1554 or AWS D1.1 on structural steel, AS/NZS 3788 for in-service pressure equipment, and customer specifications in aerospace. Atlantis writes and approves procedures for ASME, API, AWS and client-specified work.

  • LNG on Curtis Island: ASME and API codes are common on these plants alongside Australian standards; PAUT and TOFD often replace radiography for weld inspection, and tank inspections follow API 653 or the owner's equivalent. See LNG audit support.
  • Refining at Lytton: piping, vessels and heat exchangers inspected against API inspection codes and owner specifications, with thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD. Procedures must handle elevated-temperature scanning and coating removal limits.
  • Coal seam gas pipelines: AS 2885 governs design, construction, welding and operation; API 1104 appears on some packages. See pipeline audit support.
  • Mining and minerals: MT and UT of heavy structural welds, shafts and gears to OEM requirements. See mining audit support.
  • Aerospace and defence: customer specifications, NAS 410 or equivalent personnel requirements, and process-specific NDT standards. See aerospace audit support.
  • Power generation: boiler tube, header and high-energy piping inspection during outages. See power generation audit support.

Every procedure we write states its governing code, equipment, calibration, personnel level, scanning or exposure technique, recording and acceptance criteria, and each technique sheet applies it to a specific component. Radiography procedures must also align with the company's Queensland Health radiation safety and protection plan, which stays the responsibility of your licensed staff.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Queensland crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III gives a Queensland contractor a named ASNT Level III for its SNT-TC-1A programme without a full-time hire. It suits companies whose ASNT-specified work comes and goes with LNG shutdowns, refinery turnarounds and defence contracts.

The pattern in Queensland is seasonal. Turnarounds at Gladstone and Lytton, power station outages and mine shutdowns cluster at certain times of year, and contractors scale up fast. During those peaks, an outsourced Level III reviews certifications, approves technique sheets, answers acceptance and technique questions from site and keeps the paperwork in order, while your supervisors run the crews. Between peaks, the arrangement keeps the written practice current and recertifications on schedule.

An interim Level III is a narrower arrangement: cover while you recruit a permanent Level III, or while yours is on leave or committed to another project. It keeps your written practice valid and your approvals flowing. You can choose an ongoing outsourced arrangement, a single project such as a written practice or procedure set, or an audit-preparation sprint, each scoped on a call and quoted on request. Talk to us about outsourced Level III cover in Queensland.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Atlantis prepares Queensland NDT companies for owner audits of their SNT-TC-1A programmes, customer and prime-contractor supplier audits, and the NDT portion of quality-system audits. We run a mock audit, give you prioritised findings and help you close them. The auditor still makes the decision.

Owners such as LNG operators and refiners prequalify their NDT contractors and audit them periodically. Aerospace and defence primes audit suppliers' special processes, including NDT. Both kinds of audit sample personnel and reports and trace them back to the written practice, the approved procedure and the calibrated equipment used. Our mock audit does exactly that before the real one. Typical findings in Queensland programmes include technique sheets that were never formally approved, experience hours that cannot be evidenced, expired vision tests and procedures referencing superseded code editions.

Atlantis is not a NATA assessor and does not hold NATA accreditation. Where a laboratory or inspection body is preparing for NATA assessment, we can review NDT procedures and personnel records for consistency, but we do not represent that work as accreditation consulting. Schedule a mock NDT audit for your Queensland programme.

Cities and regions we support across Queensland

Direct answer: Atlantis supports employers across Queensland, from Brisbane and the Gold Coast to Gladstone, Mackay, Townsville and the inland resources regions, remotely and onsite at the client's facility. Atlantis has no office or training centre in Queensland.

  • Brisbane and Ipswich: Lytton refinery, port and terminals, Boeing Defence Australia, RAAF Base Amberley and the main fabrication base. See NDT consulting in Brisbane, NDT training in Brisbane, Practical NDT for Brisbane and third-party inspection in Brisbane.
  • Gladstone: Curtis Island LNG, alumina, aluminium smelting and power. See NDT training in Gladstone and third-party inspection in Gladstone.
  • Mackay and the Bowen Basin: coal mining, export terminals and mining-equipment maintenance.
  • Townsville: zinc and copper refining, port and defence.
  • Toowoomba and the Darling Downs: the Wellcamp aerospace precinct and coal seam gas support.
  • Surat Basin (Roma, Chinchilla, Miles): gas fields, compression and gathering pipelines.
  • Mount Isa and the North West: minerals processing and mobile equipment.

For the national picture, see NDT consulting in Australia.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: Every engagement follows the same sequence: a scoping call, a written scope and quote, a review of your documents, delivery of the agreed documents, onsite work only where needed and, for ongoing clients, continuing support. Timing is agreed on the scoping call because it depends on your records and deadlines.

  1. Scoping call: methods, clients, governing codes, certification schemes in use and the audit or project date driving the work.
  2. Scope and quote: deliverables, remote and onsite elements and responsibilities on both sides.
  3. Document review: written practice, certifications, procedures, technique sheets, calibration records and sample reports.
  4. Delivery: written practice, procedures, technique sheets, exam sets or audit findings, under revision control.
  5. Onsite work: practical exams on real specimens or audit support at your Queensland facility, when the scope calls for it.
  6. Ongoing support: approvals, queries, recertifications and updates when codes or client requirements change.

Technician training is separate: see ASNT SNT-TC-1A training, online NDT training and corporate NDT training. Technicians can practise on Practical NDT before practical exams; it is practice only and does not replace an exam on real specimens.

Your Level III

Queensland engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, founder of Atlantis NDT. The Level III you speak to on the scoping call is the Level III who signs your documents. Read more about Atlantis NDT.

Frequently asked questions

Who is an NDT Level III consultant in Queensland for SNT-TC-1A programmes?

Atlantis NDT provides ASNT Level III services to Queensland employers, led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, delivered remotely and onsite at your facility.

Do Queensland LNG operators accept ASNT-certified technicians?

Requirements vary by operator, contract and package. Some specifications accept or require ASNT-based certification, others require AINDT or ISO 9712. Read the contract's personnel-qualification clause and confirm with the owner.

Can Atlantis provide AINDT or ISO 9712 certification?

No. Atlantis does not certify or train to AINDT or ISO 9712. We support employer-based SNT-TC-1A programmes and can align them with AINDT-certified staff.

Is Atlantis NATA-accredited?

No. Atlantis does not hold NATA accreditation and does not issue NATA-endorsed reports. We support procedures and personnel records only.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Queensland?

Yes. Queensland Health requires an industrial radiography use licence for each radiographer and a possession licence for the company, with an approved radiation safety and protection plan, under the Radiation Safety Act 1999.

Who registers boilers and pressure vessels in Queensland?

Workplace Health and Safety Queensland registers plant designs and items of plant, including boilers and pressure vessels of the relevant hazard levels, under the Work Health and Safety Regulation 2011. In-service inspection follows AS/NZS 3788.

Can you write PAUT procedures for Gladstone LNG work?

Yes. We write PAUT and TOFD procedures and technique sheets to ASME V and the applicable construction code, aligned with the owner's specification and approved by our Level III.

Can a Brisbane aerospace supplier use your written practice?

We can write one, but aerospace customers often require NAS 410 or their own specification rather than SNT-TC-1A alone. Check your purchase order flow-downs first; we will design the programme around them.

Can practical exams be done remotely?

No. Practical exams need the candidate, real specimens and the examiner together, so they are held onsite at your facility. Most other Level III work is remote.

Does Atlantis have an office in Brisbane or Gladstone?

No. Atlantis has no physical office or training centre in Queensland; work is delivered remotely and onsite at the client's facility.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Queensland?

Quote on request. Cost depends on methods, ongoing versus project work, exam volume and onsite visits. Atlantis keeps its services affordable, accessible and fully customisable.

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III services to Saskatchewan employers, delivered remotely and onsite at the employer's own facility: an outsourced or interim Level III for SNT-TC-1A programmes, written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets, qualification exams under the employer's written practice, and audit preparation. Every engagement is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, and every scope is quoted on request.

Saskatchewan's inspection work follows its resources. Heavy oil around Lloydminster and Kindersley, light oil in the Bakken and Viewfield plays around Estevan and Weyburn, the Co-op refinery complex in Regina, asphalt refining in Moose Jaw, potash mines from Esterhazy to Rocanville, Belle Plaine, Lanigan, Allan, Cory and the new Jansen project, uranium mines and mills in the Athabasca Basin, coal and gas power stations near Estevan and Coronach, a steel and pipe mill in Regina, and a strong agricultural-equipment manufacturing base all depend on NDT. Interprovincial oil and gas pipelines cross the province and feed terminals and pump stations along the way. Most Saskatchewan inspection companies are regional and lean, and many of them work for US-owned operators, US customers or projects built to US codes. That is where a named ASNT Level III adds the most value, and this page explains how. If you already know what you need, ask for a Saskatchewan Level III quote.

Why Saskatchewan NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: Any Saskatchewan employer that certifies its own NDT personnel under ASNT SNT-TC-1A needs a Level III who owns the written practice, approves procedures and examines staff. Saskatchewan operators, refiners, potash miners and pipeline companies audit their NDT contractors, and most regional inspection firms are too small to keep a full-time Level III on staff, so an outsourced Level III fills that role.

Start with oil. The Lloydminster region straddles the Alberta border and processes heavy oil through an upgrader and an asphalt refinery, surrounded by thermal and cold heavy-oil production, batteries, tanks and gathering lines. West-central fields around Kindersley and Kerrobert and the southeast Bakken around Estevan, Weyburn and Carlyle add thousands of wells, batteries, gas plants and flowlines. The Weyburn area is also known for carbon dioxide injection for enhanced oil recovery, which brings its own corrosion and materials questions. Each of these assets needs weld inspection on construction, ultrasonic thickness surveys in service, tank inspection and repair inspection, and the producers who own them audit the contractors who perform it.

Refining and processing are concentrated. The Co-op refinery complex in Regina is one of the larger refineries in Western Canada, with turnarounds that pull in inspection crews from across the Prairies. Moose Jaw has an asphalt refinery. Fertiliser and chemical plants, ethanol and canola crushing plants and gas processing facilities add pressure equipment and piping that must be inspected under the provincial boiler and pressure vessel rules.

Potash is uniquely Saskatchewan. The province's underground and solution mines operate hoists, headframes, shafts, mills, dryers, compaction and loadout equipment, and large new construction at Jansen east of Saskatoon has added fabrication and erection work. Hoist and shaft components, crushers, conveyors and structural steel need MT, UT and visual inspection, often to the mine owner's specification and the manufacturer's requirements. In the north, the Athabasca Basin uranium mines and mills bring nuclear-industry document control and radiation-protection expectations.

Power and manufacturing complete the map. SaskPower operates coal and gas plants including Boundary Dam near Estevan, with its carbon capture unit, and Shand and Poplar River near Coronach; boiler tubes, headers and high-energy piping need outage inspection. SaskPower has selected a site near Estevan for further study for a potential first small modular reactor, which would bring nuclear-grade quality requirements to the region. The Regina steel and pipe mill, and shortline agricultural equipment makers across the province, need weld and material inspection in their own shops.

The regulatory picture is distinctly Canadian. Boilers and pressure vessels are regulated by the Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan (TSASK) under The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act, 1999 and its regulations; owners or insurers can apply to the Chief Inspector for approval of their own Quality Management System of inspection. Provincially licensed pipelines are regulated by the Ministry of Energy and Resources under The Pipelines Act, 1998 and Directive PNG034, the Saskatchewan Pipelines Code, with CSA Z662 as the minimum technical standard; interprovincial pipelines fall under the Canada Energy Regulator. Industrial gamma radiography is licensed federally by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC), and anyone operating an exposure device must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator or work under the direct supervision of one. X-ray equipment and workplace radiation protection fall under provincial occupational health and safety rules, so confirm the current requirement with the province before mobilising.

Which NDT certification scheme applies in Saskatchewan?

Direct answer: Canada's national NDT personnel certification scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, and many Canadian codes and owners call for it. ASNT SNT-TC-1A is the employer-based scheme used by US codes and US customers. Atlantis provides Level III expertise for SNT-TC-1A programmes and procedure, technique and audit support around both; we are not a CGSB or ISO 9712 certification body.

A note on the national scheme, because it changed this year. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published the standard, closed on 1 April 2026; the standard remains valid, and both Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body and CWB Group, as an accredited certification body, have said they continue to certify. Confirm the current certification body for your method and sector before you rely on it.

This question matters more in Saskatchewan than in most US states, because many local contractors hold technicians certified under both systems. A crew may do pipeline work for a Canadian operator that asks for national certification on Monday, and shop inspection for a US equipment buyer that asks for SNT-TC-1A certification and an ASME or AWS procedure on Tuesday. The two schemes work differently, and confusing them is one of the most common audit findings we see.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's document that defines how NDT personnel are trained, examined, certified and recertified under SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis writes new written practices for Saskatchewan employers and audits existing ones, so the document matches the methods you actually perform and the customers who will audit you.

The most common Saskatchewan problems are predictable. A written practice copied from a US company years ago names a Level III who is no longer involved. Methods listed in the practice do not match what the crew does, for example phased array on pipeline tie-ins or eddy current on exchanger tubing at a refinery turnaround. Technicians certified under the national scheme are treated as if that certificate automatically satisfies SNT-TC-1A, without the employer's own examinations or a documented review. Experience hours claimed for technicians hired from Alberta or from US contractors are undocumented. Vision exams have lapsed over the winter shutdown.

A written-practice engagement sets the scope, training and experience requirements referenced to the current SNT-TC-1A edition, examination content and grading, vision examinations, certification and recertification, interrupted service, transfer of certification between employers and the Level III's authority. If you also hold national certifications, we document how those certificates are recorded and how they relate to your employer-based programme, without claiming one replaces the other. Training-hour figures come from the training requirements matrix rather than from memory. See written practice development and the SNT-TC-1A guide, or go straight to it: request a written-practice review for your Saskatchewan company.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Saskatchewan

Direct answer: Saskatchewan procedures follow the governing code and the owner's specification: CSA Z662 and Directive PNG034 for provincially licensed pipelines; CSA B51 with the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code for TSASK-regulated equipment; API 510, 570 and 653 practice at refineries and terminals; CSA W59 or AWS D1.1 for structures; and manufacturers' requirements for mining equipment.

Procedure work in the province falls into recurring groups:

  • Pipelines and gathering systems. Girth-weld radiography or automated UT on construction, and integrity-dig inspection in service. Procedures must reflect CSA Z662 and the operator's specification, and gamma radiography procedures must fit the CNSC licence conditions of the radiography company.
  • Heavy oil and thermal facilities. Thickness monitoring, weld inspection and crack detection on high-temperature piping and vessels around Lloydminster, with technique sheets that state temperature limits for couplant and probes.
  • Refining and upgrading. Repair and alteration inspection, PAUT and TOFD on thick sections, corrosion mapping and exchanger tube inspection during turnarounds at Regina and Moose Jaw.
  • Potash and uranium mining. MT and UT on hoist components, shafts, crusher and mill parts and structural welds, to the mine's own requirements and the manufacturer's instructions, with clear acceptance criteria for maintenance planners.
  • Power generation. Boiler tube, header and high-energy piping inspection during SaskPower outages, and documentation suitable for TSASK-regulated equipment.
  • Shop fabrication for US customers. Pressure vessels, skids and agricultural equipment built to ASME or AWS for delivery south of the border, where the US buyer expects SNT-TC-1A personnel and ASME Section V-style procedures.
  • Cold weather. Prairie winters affect penetrant and magnetic particle product limits, couplant behaviour, battery life and safe access, and a good procedure addresses them rather than assuming a heated shop.

We write procedures and technique sheets, review procedures supplied by others, and resolve conflicts between owner specifications, codes and your written practice. Sector notes: pipeline, refining, mining, power generation, steel and metals and fabrication. For mine operators specifically, see the mining written practice page.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Saskatchewan NDT contractors are audited by producers, refiners, potash and uranium miners, utilities and pipeline operators, often through prequalification, and some by CSA W178.1, ISO 9001 or ISO/IEC 17025 assessors. A Level III review before the audit finds the gaps in written practice, certifications, procedures and reports while there is still time to fix them.

Typical findings in the province: certifications issued under a superseded written practice; national-scheme certificates filed as if they were employer certifications, with no record of the employer's own review; expired vision exams; practical exams with no specimen or grading record; procedures not approved by a Level III or tied to an outdated code edition; calibration records that do not match the instruments in reports; and technicians performing techniques outside their certification. Uranium and future nuclear-related work raise the bar further on document control and traceability.

An audit-readiness engagement samples personnel files, procedures and reports, maps them to the written practice and the owner specification, and produces a prioritised corrective-action list followed by support for the fixes. For aerospace or defence suppliers we help with Nadcap-style audit preparation as context, while the audit itself belongs to the accreditation body. For organisations seeking CSA W178.1 certification as an inspection organisation, we help with the NDT technical content of procedures and personnel records; the certification decision belongs to the certifying body. Audit date set? Book a Saskatchewan audit-readiness call.

Inspection programme support for refineries, terminals and pressure equipment

Direct answer: At Saskatchewan refineries, upgraders, terminals and plants, pressure equipment is regulated by TSASK and inspected under the owner's or insurer's programme, often using API 510, 570 and 653 practice. Atlantis supports that work from the NDT side, with method selection, procedures, technique qualification and data quality. We do not supply authorised inspectors or offer API certification training.

The value of thickness data, weld inspection and tank floor scans depends on consistent measurement locations, techniques matched to the damage mechanism and reports the inspector can use. A Level III can help a contractor or owner standardise practice across crews and choose between conventional UT, PAUT corrosion mapping and profile radiography for corrosion under insulation or high-temperature service. Where an owner operates an approved Quality Management System of inspection, NDT procedures and personnel records are part of what that system has to control. Frequently asked questions

How do I find an NDT Level III consultant in Saskatchewan?

Saskatchewan has few independent Level IIIs, so many contractors engage an outside Level III who works remotely and visits onsite. Atlantis offers that service for SNT-TC-1A programmes, led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III.

Is ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification accepted in Saskatchewan?

It depends on the owner and the code. Work to US codes or for US customers commonly accepts SNT-TC-1A. Many Canadian owner specifications and CSA-referenced work call for national certification to CAN/CGSB-48.9712. Check the contract before assigning a technician.

What is CAN/CGSB-48.9712 and does Atlantis certify to it?

It is Canada's national adoption of ISO 9712 for NDT personnel certification, issued by accredited certification bodies such as NRCan's NDT Certification Body and CWB Group. The Canadian General Standards Board closed on 1 April 2026, but the standard remains valid; confirm the current certification body. Atlantis does not certify or train to it. We provide SNT-TC-1A Level III services and procedure and audit support.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in Saskatchewan?

The Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan (TSASK) administers The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act, 1999 and its regulations, including periodic inspections and approval of owner or insurer Quality Management Systems of inspection.

Who regulates pipelines in Saskatchewan?

The Ministry of Energy and Resources licenses provincial pipelines under The Pipelines Act, 1998 and Directive PNG034, with CSA Z662 as the minimum standard. Interprovincial pipelines are regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Saskatchewan?

Gamma radiography requires a CNSC licence for the company, and operators must be CNSC-certified exposure device operators or work under the direct supervision of one. X-ray equipment falls under provincial occupational health and safety rules; confirm the current requirements before work starts.

What does an outsourced Level III do for a Saskatchewan contractor?

They act as the Level III named in your SNT-TC-1A written practice: approving procedures, administering exams, reviewing certifications, answering field questions and supporting owner audits, without a full-time hire.

Can you write NDT procedures for potash mine equipment?

Yes. We write MT, UT, PT and VT procedures and technique sheets for hoist components, shafts, crushers and structural welds to the mine's requirements and the applicable welding code.

Can practical exams be done remotely?

No. Most Level III work can be remote, but practical exams need the candidate, real specimens and the examiner together, so they are held onsite at your facility.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Saskatchewan?

Quote on request. Cost depends on the methods involved, retained versus project work, exam volume and onsite visits. Atlantis keeps its services affordable, accessible and fully customisable.

Does Atlantis have an office in Regina or Saskatoon?

No. Atlantis has no physical office or training centre in Saskatchewan; work is delivered remotely and onsite at the client's facility.

Can you help before an owner prequalification or CSA W178.1 audit?

Yes. An audit-readiness review samples your written practice, procedures, certifications and reports and gives you a prioritised list of fixes, with support while you close them. The certification or approval decision stays with the auditing body.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in South Australia

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to South Australian employers, fabricators and inspection contractors whose work is governed by US codes or US customers: SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, NDT procedures and technique sheets to ASME, API and AWS, personnel examinations under your written practice, outsourced or interim Level III cover, and audit preparation. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, and are delivered remotely, with onsite visits to your facility scoped when the work needs them. Atlantis has no office in South Australia and is not NATA-accredited or AINDT-recognised.

That last line is deliberate. In South Australia, as in the rest of the country, the normal personnel certification route is AINDT certification to AS/NZS ISO 9712, and the normal trust signal for an inspection business is NATA accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025 or ISO/IEC 17020. Atlantis does neither of those things, and this page will not pretend otherwise. What we do is fill a narrower gap that South Australian companies keep running into: the moment a US prime contractor, a US-headquartered owner, or a project specified to ASME Section VIII, ASME B31.3, API 1104 or AWS D1.1 asks for an SNT-TC-1A written practice, ASME Section V procedures and a named ASNT Level III, somebody has to own those documents. If that is your situation, request a South Australia Level III consultation and we will scope it on a call.

Why South Australian NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: South Australia combines naval shipbuilding, defence aerospace, a large mining and smelting sector, the Cooper Basin gas industry and a fast-growing renewable power grid. Several of these sectors buy from or sell to US organisations, and every SNT-TC-1A programme needs a Level III to approve the written practice, write or approve procedures, and examine and certify Level I and II personnel.

The state's industrial map is unusual for its size. On the Lefevre Peninsula at Osborne, the naval shipbuilding precinct is the centre of Australia's sovereign shipbuilding effort: ASC sustains the Collins class submarines there, BAE Systems Maritime Australia is building the Hunter class frigates, and the precinct has been named as the construction site for Australia's future nuclear-powered submarines under AUKUS. Shipbuilding at this scale runs on welding, and welding runs on NDT: ultrasonic and radiographic examination of hull and pressure-hull welds, magnetic particle and penetrant examination of structural joints, and visual inspection under defined procedures. A large share of the supply chain feeding Osborne is small and mid-sized fabricators in Port Adelaide, Wingfield, Lonsdale and the northern suburbs, many of them qualifying for defence work for the first time.

North of Adelaide, RAAF Base Edinburgh and the surrounding Edinburgh and Salisbury defence and aerospace cluster bring aircraft maintenance, component repair and electronics work. Aerospace NDT is procedure-driven and audit-heavy, and suppliers to US original equipment manufacturers are often asked to show a written practice and a responsible Level III even when their technicians already hold AINDT or other ISO 9712 certificates.

Further out, the resources sector dominates. BHP's Olympic Dam at Roxby Downs is one of the world's largest copper-uranium-gold-silver deposits, with a smelter, refinery and hydrometallurgical plant on site; BHP also operates Prominent Hill and Carrapateena. Nyrstar's Port Pirie smelter processes lead and other metals, and the Whyalla steelworks, which entered administration in 2025, has been the subject of a government-led sale process (confirm current ownership before relying on this). Each of these runs pressure equipment, tanks, process piping, kilns, conveyors and heavy structures that need in-service inspection. In the far north-east, Santos operates the Moomba gas processing plant in the Cooper Basin, gas and liquids flow south through pipelines to Adelaide and Port Bonython, and the SEA Gas pipeline links the state to Victoria. Gas-fired and thermal plant at Torrens Island and Pelican Point, plus a large fleet of wind farms and grid batteries, round out the energy picture.

Not every one of these organisations needs SNT-TC-1A. Many are perfectly served by AINDT-certified technicians and NATA-accredited inspection bodies. The ones that do need it are usually easy to recognise: a US parent or US joint-venture partner, a contract quality clause that cites ASNT, a code that sends you to ASME Section V for personnel qualification, or a customer auditor who asks "who is your Level III?" For those companies, an outsourced ASNT Level III consulting service is often quicker to set up than recruiting a full-time Level III into a small team.

South Australia's regulators and standards, in one place

Direct answer: In South Australia, industrial radiography is licensed by the Environment Protection Authority (EPA) under the Radiation Protection and Control Act 2021; plant such as boilers and pressure vessels falls under SafeWork SA and the state's work health and safety regulations; and petroleum pipelines are regulated by the Department for Energy and Mining. Australian Standards set the technical rules.

Radiography is the area where getting it wrong has the biggest consequences. South Australia replaced its old radiation regulations with the Radiation Protection and Control Act 2021 and the Radiation Protection and Control Regulations 2022, administered by the EPA. Under that framework, a business that possesses radiation apparatus or sealed sources needs a radiation management licence and a radiation management plan, apparatus must be registered, and people who operate industrial radiography equipment need an appropriate user licence. The EPA's published guidance links the industrial radiography user licence to certification in NDT radiography and radiation safety from a provider endorsed by the AINDT Certification Board, or an EPA radiation examination. Atlantis does not provide that radiation safety certification. Our role is to make sure the radiographic procedures, technique sheets and personnel qualification records in your NDT programme line up with your EPA licence conditions and your radiation management plan, rather than contradicting them.

For pressure equipment, South Australia follows the harmonised work health and safety model. The Work Health and Safety Regulations 2012 (SA) require registration of certain plant designs and certain items of plant, including many boilers and pressure vessels, and SafeWork SA is the regulator. Day-to-day technical practice rests on Australian Standards: AS 1210 for pressure vessel design, AS 4041 for pressure piping, AS 4037 for examination and testing of pressure equipment during manufacture, AS/NZS 3788 for in-service inspection, AS/NZS 1554 for structural steel welding and AS 2885 for gas and liquid petroleum pipelines. Petroleum activities, including Cooper Basin facilities and pipelines, are licensed under the Petroleum and Geothermal Energy Act 2000 through the Department for Energy and Mining.

Where this matters for a Level III is in the mapping. A US-owned plant in South Australia may need its NDT procedures to satisfy ASME Section V for an ASME-stamped vessel, AS 4037 for a locally designed one, and AS/NZS 3788 for in-service inspection, sometimes on the same site. Writing procedures that state clearly which code governs which work, and which acceptance criteria apply, avoids the most common audit finding we see: a procedure that cites three standards and satisfies none of them.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: An SNT-TC-1A written practice is the employer's own rulebook for qualifying and certifying NDT personnel. Atlantis writes new written practices for South Australian employers and audits existing ones against SNT-TC-1A, the customer's specification and the company's actual records, then fixes the gaps.

A written practice is not a template you download and sign. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer decides the methods and levels it certifies, the training and experience it requires for each, the examinations it gives, who administers them, how vision is tested, how long certification lasts, and what happens when a technician has a break in service or changes employer. A Level III approves that document, and the employer then has to follow it exactly. Most audit findings come from the gap between what the written practice says and what the records show.

South Australian employers bring a particular twist: many of their technicians already hold AINDT certificates under AS/NZS ISO 9712. A well-drafted written practice can recognise that prior training and experience, define what additional employer-specific and practical examination is required, and keep AINDT certification as the governing scheme for Australian-code work while SNT-TC-1A certification covers the US-specified contracts. A badly drafted one ends up demanding duplicate training or, worse, contradicting itself. We write the hybrid version deliberately, so that an auditor from either side can follow it.

A typical written practice engagement covers: scope and responsibilities, methods and levels, training and experience requirements (we point you to the training requirements matrix rather than inventing hour figures), examination content and grading, practical specimen requirements, vision examination, certification and recertification, interrupted service, records, and how outside agencies are used. For the audit service, we sample personnel files against the document and give you a written list of findings and corrective actions. More detail is on our written practice development page, and background on the standard itself is on our SNT-TC-1A guide. If you already have a written practice and an audit date, ask for a written practice review.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in South Australia

Direct answer: Procedures say how a method is applied; technique sheets apply that procedure to a specific component. Atlantis writes and approves NDT procedures to ASME Section V, AWS D1.1, API 1104 and customer specifications for South Australian companies, and cross-references Australian Standards where a project uses both.

The codes in play depend on the sector. Naval and defence fabrication in Adelaide is governed by the prime contractor's specifications and classification or naval standards, and suppliers should expect those documents to prevail; we help translate them into method procedures but do not claim any defence or class-society approval. Process and pressure equipment for US-owned or US-engineered projects is typically ASME Section VIII with ASME Section V for examination and ASME B31.3 for piping. Pipeline construction is AS 2885 locally, with API 1104 appearing on US-specified work. Structural steel is AS/NZS 1554, with AWS D1.1 on export or US-specified jobs. Mining and smelting plant mixes all of these with owner standards.

Method by method, the work we see most in South Australia is: ultrasonic procedures for butt welds and thickness surveys, including phased array and TOFD where the client wants encoded, recordable data; radiographic procedures for pipe and vessel welds, written to sit inside the operator's EPA licence conditions; magnetic particle and penetrant procedures for structural and machined components; visual procedures with clear acceptance references; and eddy current for tubing and aerospace components. Each procedure states its scope, personnel qualification, equipment and calibration, technique, scanning coverage, recording and evaluation, acceptance criteria by reference to the governing code, and reporting. Technique sheets then fix the variables for a specific joint or part so the result is repeatable from one technician to the next.

Approval matters as much as authorship. Many customers want to see a procedure signed by a Level III in the method. Where Atlantis is your outsourced Level III, Anoop Rayavarapu reviews and approves the procedure, and where your own Level III or your customer's Level III must approve it, we prepare the document for their review.

Outsourced and interim Level III for South Australian crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is a named ASNT Level III, outside your company, who fulfils the Level III responsibilities defined in your written practice. Interim cover does the same while you recruit. Atlantis provides both to South Australian employers, remotely with onsite visits when required.

The engagement models are simple. An ongoing outsourced Level III arrangement covers document control, procedure approvals, examination of new hires, answers to technical questions from the field, and support during audits. A project-based engagement delivers a defined set of documents, such as a written practice and five method procedures, and ends. An audit-preparation sprint focuses on one upcoming audit. Interim cover is useful in a state where experienced Level IIIs are scarce and often committed to large employers; it gives a small contractor a responsible Level III while a permanent hire is found, or indefinitely if that hire never makes sense.

Distance is a fair question. Much of a Level III's work is document review, examination preparation, records checking and technical advice, and all of that works remotely across time zones. Written and specific examinations can be administered under controlled, invigilated conditions defined in your written practice. Practical examinations on real specimens, procedure demonstrations and some audits need a person in the room, and those are scoped as onsite visits to your facility. We say clearly in the proposal which parts are remote and which are onsite, so there are no surprises. To discuss cover for your team, ask about outsourced Level III for South Australia, or read about interim NDT Level 3 cover.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Atlantis prepares South Australian NDT programmes for customer quality audits, owner and prime-contractor supplier audits, and the NDT elements of ISO 9001 audits. For NATA accreditation we can help tidy procedures and personnel records, but NATA assesses you independently and Atlantis holds no NATA accreditation.

Audits in South Australia come from several directions. Defence primes audit their supply chain, and suppliers often discover that their NDT records are the weakest part of their quality system. US-owned operators send corporate auditors who expect to see SNT-TC-1A documents in a familiar format. Mining and smelting owners audit inspection contractors before major shutdowns. Inspection bodies seeking or maintaining NATA accreditation to ISO/IEC 17020 or 17025 face technical assessment of their methods and staff competence.

Our audit preparation follows a consistent pattern: we read the requirement (the customer specification, contract clause or accreditation criteria), compare your written practice, procedures and records against it, sample personnel files and equipment calibration records, and deliver a findings list ranked by risk. Then we help you close the findings: revised documents, re-examinations where certification evidence is missing, and a short brief for the people who will face the auditor. We do not attend an audit as if we were your accreditation body, and we do not promise an outcome. We aim to make sure that nothing the auditor asks for is missing or contradictory.

Cities and regions we support across South Australia

Direct answer: Atlantis supports NDT programmes anywhere in South Australia, remotely and with onsite visits to your facility. The busiest areas are metropolitan Adelaide and Port Adelaide, the Osborne and Edinburgh defence precincts, the Upper Spencer Gulf industrial towns, the Far North mining province and the Cooper Basin.

Adelaide and Port Adelaide. The capital hosts most of the state's fabrication, engineering and inspection companies, plus the Osborne shipyards and the northern defence cluster. For Adelaide employers we also have ASNT NDT training for Adelaide technicians, an NDT ERP page for Adelaide inspection companies and a digital twin page for Adelaide asset owners.

Whyalla, Port Pirie and Port Augusta. The Upper Spencer Gulf carries the state's heavy industry: the Whyalla steelworks, the Port Pirie smelter, the Port Bonython liquids facility and a growing renewable energy footprint around Port Augusta. Related pages: digital twin for Whyalla and NDT ERP for Whyalla.

Roxby Downs and the Far North. Olympic Dam, Prominent Hill and Carrapateena are fly-in, fly-out operations where shutdown windows are short and contractor crews rotate. A clear written practice and procedures that every rotation follows the same way are worth a great deal here. See our overview of the Australian mining NDT market.

Cooper Basin and Moomba. Gas processing, compression and gathering systems, often with joint-venture partners and international engineering contractors, bring ASME and API documents into a remote desert operation. Context on why US-affiliated energy operators ask for SNT-TC-1A is in our article on SNT-TC-1A in Australia.

Mount Gambier, the Riverland and regional fabrication. Timber processing, food and wine processing, and agricultural equipment fabrication all use pressure equipment and welded structures, usually under Australian Standards; we help when a customer or export market asks for US-code documents.

For the national picture, see NDT consulting across Australia and ASNT NDT training in Australia.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: You describe your situation on a call, we agree a written scope and quote, Atlantis delivers documents and examinations remotely and onsite as agreed, and you receive signed, revision-controlled deliverables. Timelines depend on scope and are set during scoping, not promised in advance.

  1. Discovery call. We ask what triggered the need: a new contract, a customer audit, a departing Level III, a new method. We ask which codes and specifications govern your work and which certification schemes your staff already hold.
  2. Document review. You send your current written practice, procedures, a sample of personnel records and the customer requirement, if any.
  3. Written scope and quote. We list the deliverables, what is remote and what is onsite, and who approves what. Pricing is quote on request.
  4. Drafting. We write or revise the written practice, procedures and technique sheets, and send them for your review with comments explaining each choice.
  5. Examinations. Where the scope includes them, general and specific examinations are administered under the written practice, and practical examinations are arranged at your facility on real specimens.
  6. Approval and handover. Signed documents, revision history and an audit pack you can hand to the next auditor.
  7. Ongoing cover. If you choose an outsourced Level III arrangement, we stay on as your named Level III for approvals, new hires and audits.

Ready to start? Book a scoping call for your South Australian NDT programme.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Buyers of Level III services rightly want a named, credentialed person rather than an anonymous team, and that is who you will deal with: the same Level III who reviews your documents approves them. Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A training for employers who want to build their own Level I and II capability alongside the consulting work, and the Practical NDT simulator, which lets technicians practise methods in a 3D environment before their practical examination. The simulator is practice only; it does not replace a practical examination on real specimens.

Frequently asked questions

Can an ASNT Level III be our responsible Level III in South Australia?

Yes, for an SNT-TC-1A programme. SNT-TC-1A allows an employer to use an outside agency Level III, and the written practice names that person and defines the responsibilities. It does not make the Level III your AINDT or NATA authority; those are separate systems.

Do South Australian NDT technicians need AINDT certification?

For most Australian-code work, employers and owners expect AINDT certification to AS/NZS ISO 9712. SNT-TC-1A certification is an additional, employer-based certification used when a US code, US owner or US customer requires it. Check your contract and owner specification.

Is Atlantis NATA-accredited?

No. Atlantis holds no NATA accreditation and is not an inspection body for NATA purposes. We help with NDT procedures and personnel records, but accreditation is assessed independently by NATA.

Who licenses industrial radiography in South Australia?

The Environment Protection Authority under the Radiation Protection and Control Act 2021 and the 2022 Regulations. Businesses need a radiation management licence and plan, apparatus registration and appropriately licensed users. Confirm current requirements with the EPA.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in South Australia?

SafeWork SA, under the Work Health and Safety Regulations 2012 (SA), which require registration of certain plant designs and items. Technical inspection practice follows Australian Standards such as AS/NZS 3788 for in-service equipment.

Can you write NDT procedures to ASME Section V for an Adelaide fabricator?

Yes. We write and approve procedures to ASME Section V, AWS D1.1 and API 1104, and cross-reference Australian Standards where a project uses both.

Can examinations be done remotely from Australia?

General and specific written examinations can be administered remotely under invigilated conditions that your written practice defines. Practical examinations on real specimens need an onsite visit to your facility.

Does Atlantis provide AINDT or ISO 9712 training in South Australia?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. For AINDT certification, use an AINDT-recognised route.

How much does Level III consulting cost in South Australia?

It is quoted on request after a scoping call, because it depends on the number of methods, documents, examinations and onsite days. Affordable, accessible and fully customisable is how we aim to structure it.

Can you help a supplier to the Osborne shipyards?

We can prepare NDT procedures and personnel records that address the prime contractor's requirements. We do not hold defence, naval or class-society approvals, and the prime's specification always governs.

Do you support API 510, 570 or 653 programmes?

We support them with NDT technique selection, procedures and personnel qualification for the inspectors who run them. We do not provide risk-based inspection or fitness-for-service assessments.

Does Atlantis have an office in South Australia?

No. Work is delivered remotely, with onsite visits to your facility when the scope requires them.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Sweden

Short answer: Atlantis NDT supports Swedish manufacturers, inspection companies and plant operators that need an ASNT NDT Level III for US-code and US-customer work: SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets to ASME, API and AWS, employer examinations, responsible (outside-agency) and interim Level III cover, and audit preparation. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, and are delivered remotely or onsite at your facility. Atlantis has no Swedish office and holds no Swedac accreditation.

Sweden's own NDT system is well established and Atlantis does not replace any part of it. Personnel certification follows SS-EN ISO 9712, including the Nordic ISO 9712/Nordtest arrangement, through certification bodies accredited by Swedac. Nuclear in-service inspection has its own layer: NDT systems used on reactor components must be qualified, and the Swedish Qualification Centre (SQC) has carried out that qualification work since the 1990s. Atlantis does not certify to ISO 9712, does not train toward it and does not qualify NDT systems for nuclear plants. Where we help is the US-facing part of Swedish industry: aero-engine and airframe suppliers delivering to American OEMs, fabricators building pressure equipment to ASME, process plants with US-designed units, and inspection companies asked for an SNT-TC-1A written practice by an American client. If that is your situation, request a Sweden Level III consultation.

Why Swedish NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: A Swedish employer that certifies NDT staff under ASNT SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice approved by a Level III, method procedures and a Level III to examine and certify Level I and II personnel. Swedish suppliers to US OEMs and US-code projects are regularly asked to identify that Level III, and to show the records behind every certification.

Sweden's industrial map is broader than its population suggests. Aerospace is the clearest US link. GKN Aerospace's engine-component business in Trollhättan designs and manufactures parts for commercial and military aero engines, a supply chain dominated by American and European engine makers, and Saab in Linköping builds the Gripen fighter and supplies aerostructures. Their sub-tier suppliers, including machine shops, foundries, forging houses, heat treaters and coating shops across Västra Götaland and Östergötland, run penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic, eddy current and radiographic inspection to customer specifications that usually invoke NAS 410 or EN 4179 for personnel and Nadcap for special processes.

Nuclear power is the second anchor. Forsmark in Uppland, Ringhals in Halland and Oskarshamn in Småland operate Sweden's reactors. In-service inspection at these plants is governed by the Swedish Radiation Safety Authority (SSM) through regulations covering mechanical equipment, with NDT systems qualified before use and independent accredited inspection bodies reviewing compliance. This is a specialist world with its own qualification route; Atlantis can support the documentation and procedure discipline around it, but qualification itself sits with the accredited qualification body.

The process industry forms the third group. Preem operates refineries at Lysekil and Gothenburg, St1 runs a refinery in Gothenburg, and Stenungsund hosts Sweden's main petrochemical cluster. Pulp and paper mills along the Norrland coast and in Värmland run recovery boilers, digesters and large piping systems that need regular NDT. Steel and special metals are a fourth group: SSAB in Luleå, Oxelösund and Borlänge, the special-steel producers in Sandviken, Hofors and Hällefors, and the new hydrogen-based steel project in Boden. Add hydropower penstocks, district-heating and combined heat-and-power plants, the vehicle and heavy-equipment industry around Gothenburg and Södertälje, and naval shipbuilding in Karlskrona, and you have a country where NDT demand is wide and specification-driven.

Regulation: pressure equipment placed on the market must meet the Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU; in use, equipment falls under the rules of the Swedish Work Environment Authority (Arbetsmiljöverket), with periodic inspection by accredited inspection bodies. Industrial radiography requires a licence from SSM, which also regulates nuclear safety. Swedac accredits certification bodies, inspection bodies and laboratories. None of these requires SNT-TC-1A, but US customers and US codes often do, which is the gap an ASNT Level III consulting service addresses.

SS-EN ISO 9712, Nordtest and SNT-TC-1A: which applies to Swedish work?

Direct answer: SS-EN ISO 9712, including the Nordtest scheme, is the Swedish default and covers most European-code work. SNT-TC-1A applies where a US code, owner or customer requires employer-based certification. Aerospace work often runs on a third route, NAS 410 or EN 4179, set by the customer. A Swedish company serving several markets needs a written practice that states which route governs which job.

Under ISO 9712 an accredited certification body examines and certifies the individual. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies its people against its own written practice, with examinations administered by a Level III. NAS 410 and EN 4179 are employer-based schemes for aerospace with stricter, customer-audited requirements, including a responsible Level 3. ASME Section V generally references SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 for personnel qualification, so pressure equipment built in Sweden to ASME Section VIII, or piping to ASME B31.3, usually brings SNT-TC-1A with it.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own procedure for training, examining, certifying and recertifying NDT personnel, and under SNT-TC-1A it is the document an auditor tests. We draft it to fit how your Swedish company actually operates, then audit your certification files against it.

The usual Swedish problem is not a lack of competence; Swedish NDT technicians are typically well trained and well certified under ISO 9712. The problem is that the company's quality system was built around third-party certification, so when a US customer asks for an employer-based written practice there is nothing in the system that does that job. Writing one from scratch, rather than relabelling the ISO 9712 procedure, is the step that makes the first audit go smoothly.

The written practices we prepare cover:

  • Scope: the methods, techniques, products and codes that actually apply.
  • Duties and signature authority for trainee, Level I, Level II and Level III.
  • Training and experience requirements, cross-referenced to the training requirements matrix, with explicit rules for crediting ISO 9712 or Nordtest history.
  • Examinations: general, specific and practical; grading; retests; who administers each.
  • Vision examinations and their interval.
  • Records, retention and access.
  • Interrupted service, revocation, recertification and outside-agency arrangements.

An audit samples your certification files and checks every element the document requires, then returns a numbered list of findings with clause references and corrective actions. More detail is on written practice development, written practices for aerospace and SNT-TC-1A certification guidance.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Sweden

Direct answer: Each NDT method needs a procedure that satisfies the governing code, and most production work needs technique sheets for specific parts or welds. In Sweden the governing document is often a customer specification in aerospace, ASME or AWS on US contracts, EN and ISO standards for European fabrication, and owner practices in refining and pulp and paper.

  • Aero-engine and airframe parts. Penetrant and magnetic particle lines, immersion ultrasonic testing of forgings and rotating parts, eddy current on holes and surfaces, and radiography of castings and welds, all to OEM specifications. Procedures and technique sheets must reflect those specifications exactly; see Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness.
  • Pressure equipment. Vessels, heat exchangers and piping built to ASME VIII and B31.3 for export or for US-designed units at Swedish plants, with Section V procedures and code acceptance criteria.
  • Refining and petrochemicals. Turnaround inspection at Lysekil, Gothenburg and Stenungsund: corrosion mapping with PAUT, weld inspection after repair, exchanger tube testing and tank inspection under owner practices that often echo API 510, 570 and 653. See refining Level III audit support.
  • Pulp and paper. Recovery boiler tubes, digesters and process piping inspected during mill shutdowns. See written practices for pulp and paper.
  • Steel and metals. Plate, bar and tube inspection, rolls and heavy mill equipment. See written practices for steel and metals.
  • Power and hydropower. Boilers, high-energy piping, turbine components and penstocks. See power generation Level III support.

Our procedure development service produces procedures with defined essential variables, calibration and reference standards, coverage, recording and evaluation rules and acceptance criteria. Where a PAUT or TOFD application needs a performance demonstration, we plan the demonstration and specimens with you. Existing Swedish procedures can often be kept and given a US-code annex rather than rewritten.

Responsible and interim Level III for Swedish teams

Direct answer: A responsible or outside-agency Level 3 is a qualified Level III who is not your employee but formally holds the Level III duties in your written practice. For a Swedish company whose SNT-TC-1A workload does not justify a full-time hire, this is usually the right model.

It only works if it is written down. Your written practice must name the outside agency, define what the Level III approves, describe how examinations are administered and graded, and say who keeps records. We set up that language at the start of the engagement.

  • Ongoing responsible Level III. Written practice ownership, procedure approvals, examinations, technical queries and customer audits on a standing basis.
  • Project-based work. A defined deliverable such as a new written practice for a US order, a procedure set for a vessel contract or technique sheets for a new part family.
  • Audit-preparation sprint. A focused review before a scheduled US customer or prime-contractor audit.

For aerospace programmes under NAS 410 or EN 4179, the acceptability of an external ASNT Level III as your responsible Level 3 depends on your customer and on national aerospace NDT board requirements; check before you sign up for that role. When a Level III leaves suddenly, interim Level III cover keeps approvals and examinations moving. Ask about responsible Level 3 cover for your Swedish team.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Swedish NDT employers face customer audits from US OEMs and primes, owner audits at refineries, mills and power plants, and Swedac accreditation assessments for inspection bodies and laboratories. Atlantis prepares the NDT programme evidence: written practice, procedures, certification files and Level III records.

US customer audits trace a part or weld back through the inspection report to the procedure, the Level III approval, the technician's certification file and the equipment calibration. Owner audits add site-specific approval and witness requirements. Swedac assessments of ISO/IEC 17020 inspection bodies and ISO/IEC 17025 laboratories are separate; Atlantis plays no part in Swedac's decision, but we can make sure the NDT technical content an assessor samples is coherent and traceable.

A readiness review confirms that:

  • The written practice reflects current methods, staff and customers.
  • Every certified technician's file is complete, in date and correctly signed.
  • Each procedure in use is current, approved and referenced on reports.
  • Equipment and reference standards are calibrated and traceable.
  • The Level III arrangement is documented.

Where in Sweden we support NDT programmes

Direct answer: Atlantis works with Swedish companies remotely and onsite at their facilities. The main clusters are Västra Götaland and the west coast, Östergötland and Mälardalen, Stockholm and Uppland, southern Sweden, and the northern steel, mining and pulp belt.

Gothenburg, Trollhättan and the west coast. Aero-engine manufacturing in Trollhättan, refineries in Gothenburg and Lysekil, the Stenungsund petrochemical cluster, Ringhals nuclear plant and a large vehicle and engineering supply base. The densest mix of US-facing NDT work in the country.

Linköping, Norrköping and Östergötland. Military and civil aerospace, their sub-tier suppliers, and Oxelösund steel on the coast to the north-east.

Stockholm, Mälardalen and Uppland. Head offices of inspection and engineering companies, NDT certification and qualification organisations, Forsmark nuclear plant, Södertälje heavy-vehicle manufacturing and industrial clusters around Västerås and Eskilstuna.

Småland, Skåne and the south. Oskarshamn nuclear plant, Karlskrona naval shipbuilding, foundries and machine shops across Småland, and process industry in Skåne.

Bergslagen, Gävleborg and Dalarna. Special steel in Sandviken, Hofors and Hällefors, Borlänge steel and paper, and mills along the Bothnian coast.

Norrbotten and Västerbotten. Steel in Luleå, the Boden steel project, mining and hydropower. For neighbouring markets see Norway and Germany.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: Engagements begin with a scoping call, continue with a review of your documents and records, and deliver written practices, procedures, examinations or audit support. Most work is remote; onsite visits cover practical examinations, demonstrations and audits. A quote follows the call.

  1. Scoping call. Methods, staff, schemes in use (ISO 9712, Nordtest, NAS 410 or EN 4179, SNT-TC-1A), customers, codes and deadlines.
  2. Document request. Current written practice or quality procedure, NDT procedures, sample certification files and customer requirements.
  3. Review and plan. Gaps, deliverables, sequence and onsite needs agreed in writing.
  4. Delivery. Documents drafted, reviewed with your team and issued under revision control.
  5. Examinations. General and specific examinations remotely under controlled conditions where your written practice allows; practical examinations onsite on real specimens.
  6. Ongoing support. Responsible Level III service for approvals, questions, recertification and audits.

Pricing is quote on request: affordable, accessible and fully customisable. Request a quote for Level III support in Sweden.

Your Level III

Every engagement is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, the named Level III on documents Atlantis prepares and approves. Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training, available online or onsite, the Practical NDT simulator for practice, and an NDT ERP that tracks ISO 9712, NAS 410 and ASNT certifications in one register. Frequently asked questions about NDT Level III consulting in Sweden

Is ASNT SNT-TC-1A accepted in Sweden?

It is not the national scheme; SS-EN ISO 9712 and Nordtest are. SNT-TC-1A is accepted wherever a contract, code or customer calls for it, typically ASME and AWS work and supply to US customers.

Can an ASNT Level III act as our responsible Level 3?

For an SNT-TC-1A programme, yes, as an outside agency named in the written practice. For NAS 410 or EN 4179 aerospace programmes, your customer and the relevant aerospace NDT board decide; confirm before appointing anyone.

Who certifies NDT personnel to ISO 9712 in Sweden?

Certification bodies accredited by Swedac under ISO/IEC 17024. Several operate in Sweden. Atlantis is not one of them.

Does Atlantis qualify NDT systems for Swedish nuclear plants?

No. NDT systems for Swedish nuclear in-service inspection are qualified by an accredited qualification body under SSM regulations. Atlantis can support procedure writing and documentation discipline around that work, not the qualification itself.

Who licenses industrial radiography in Sweden?

The Swedish Radiation Safety Authority (SSM). Radiography with sources or X-ray equipment needs an SSM licence and the radiation protection arrangements it requires.

Does Atlantis offer ISO 9712 training in Sweden?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. We can credit ISO 9712 or Nordtest training and experience inside your SNT-TC-1A written practice where the rules allow.

Can you write procedures for a Swedish aerospace supplier?

Yes, procedures and technique sheets for PT, MT, UT, ET and RT written against the customer's specification. Whether those procedures also need approval by a customer-recognised Level 3 is set by your customer; we will check that with you at the start.

Can examinations be done remotely?

General and specific written examinations can be administered remotely under controlled conditions defined in your written practice. Practical examinations need real specimens and are held onsite at your facility.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Sweden?

Quote on request. It depends on the number of methods, the state of your documents, how many staff need examination and whether onsite days are needed.

Can you help prepare for a Swedac assessment?

We can prepare the NDT technical content an assessor samples, such as procedures, competence records and method validation. Swedac carries out the assessment and makes the decision.

Do you support API-style inspection programmes at Swedish refineries?

We support the NDT side of API 510, 570 and 653 style programmes: technique selection, procedure review and data quality. See API 510 support, API 570 support and API 653 support. Risk-based inspection and fitness-for-service assessments are not services we sell.

Does Atlantis have an office in Sweden?

No. Atlantis supports Swedish clients remotely and travels to your facility for onsite work.

Talk to a Level III about your Swedish NDT programme

If a US customer, US code or US-designed plant is asking your Swedish team for an SNT-TC-1A written practice, US-code procedures or a named responsible Level III, start with a short call. Book a Level III consultation for Sweden or ask for a written practice audit.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Tasmania

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to Tasmanian manufacturers, shipbuilders, energy businesses and inspection contractors that need US-code or SNT-TC-1A documents: written practices and audits, NDT procedures and technique sheets to ASME, API and AWS, examinations under your written practice, outsourced or interim Level III cover and audit preparation. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Because Tasmania's NDT community is small and spread across the island, most of the work is delivered remotely, with onsite visits to your facility scoped where the work needs them. Atlantis has no Tasmanian office and holds no NATA accreditation or AINDT recognition.

Tasmania is a different kind of NDT market from the mainland resource states. It has no refinery and no LNG plant. What it has is one of the largest hydro-electric systems in the country, a cluster of metal smelters and mineral processors, a world-known aluminium shipbuilder, an island gas pipeline, and a long tail of food, timber and engineering businesses. The inspection workforce is small, and a single Level III often supports several employers. When a Tasmanian business wins an export contract, ships to a US customer, works for a multinational parent, or is told by a client to provide an SNT-TC-1A written practice and a named Level III, there may be nobody on the island who has time to own that paperwork. That is the gap Atlantis fills. To talk it through, request a Tasmania Level III consultation.

Why Tasmanian NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: Tasmania's NDT demand comes from hydro power, metal smelting and mineral processing, aluminium shipbuilding, gas transmission and general fabrication. Employers whose customers or codes require SNT-TC-1A need a Level III to approve their written practice and procedures and to examine and certify Level I and II personnel; small island teams rarely have one in-house.

Hydro Tasmania's system is the backbone of the state's energy supply, with 30 hydropower stations and more than fifty major dams. Hydro infrastructure is an inspection-heavy asset class: steel penstocks, surge tanks, gates, valves, turbine runners, generator components and the welded structures that hold them together, much of it decades old. Ultrasonic thickness and weld examination of penstocks, magnetic particle and penetrant examination of runners and shafts, and visual inspection of gates and structures are routine. Refurbishment and redevelopment projects bring new welding, often designed or supplied by international contractors with their own code preferences. The Basslink interconnector to Victoria and the planned Marinus Link add converter stations and associated plant, and a growing wind fleet adds tower and foundation welds.

Heavy industry clusters in the north and around Hobart. At Bell Bay on the Tamar River, the Rio Tinto aluminium smelter runs potlines, carbon plants and supporting plant, alongside other processing and port facilities and the gas-fired Tamar Valley Power Station. At Risdon, on the Derwent just north of Hobart, the Nyrstar zinc works is one of the island's largest industrial sites. On the west coast, mines around Rosebery, Savage River and Henty feed concentrate and ore to ports at Burnie and Port Latta, where Grange Resources runs its pellet plant. Smelters and mineral processors depend on pressure vessels, process piping, tanks, kilns, cranes and heavy structural steel, all inspected under owner standards during short maintenance shutdowns.

Hobart is home to Incat, the builder of large high-speed aluminium catamarans for operators around the world. Aluminium welding brings its own NDT requirements, with penetrant, ultrasonic and radiographic examination procedures written for non-ferrous material, and export customers and classification societies set the rules. Hobart is also the base for Australia's Antarctic programme and its icebreaker, and for a marine services industry that maintains fishing, aquaculture and research vessels. In the north-west, Devonport and Burnie handle Bass Strait shipping. Across the state, food and beverage processors, paper and timber mills, cement production and a busy fabrication sector use boilers, pressure vessels and welded structures.

Most of this work is well served by AINDT-certified technicians under Australian Standards. The employers who need an ASNT Level III consulting service are the ones with a US connection: an export contract citing ASME or AWS, a US-owned customer, a multinational engineering contractor that writes specifications in American terms, or a client auditor who expects to see SNT-TC-1A documents.

Tasmanian regulators and standards that shape NDT work

Direct answer: In Tasmania, radiation sources used for industrial radiography are licensed by the Department of Health's Radiation Protection Unit under the Radiation Protection Act 2005; boilers and pressure vessels fall under WorkSafe Tasmania and the work health and safety laws; and gas transmission pipelines are licensed under the Gas Pipelines Act 2000.

For radiography, the Radiation Protection Act 2005 requires a licence to deal with a radiation source, and "dealing" is defined broadly: using, possessing, storing, acquiring, transporting, disposing of or servicing a prescribed source. The Radiation Protection Unit in the Department of Health is the regulator and issues licences, and it publishes the qualifications it recognises for licence holders. Atlantis is not a radiation safety training provider and does not hold or replace those licences. A Level III's job is to make sure radiographic procedures and technique sheets in your NDT programme fit the conditions of your licence and your safety arrangements, especially when exposures are done in the field at a smelter, power station or shipyard rather than in a shielded enclosure.

Pressure equipment follows the national work health and safety model. Tasmania's Work Health and Safety Act 2012 and the regulations under it require registration of certain plant designs and items of plant, including many boilers and pressure vessels, and WorkSafe Tasmania is the regulator. Technical inspection practice rests on Australian Standards: AS 1210 for pressure vessel design, AS 4041 for pressure piping, AS 4037 for examination and testing during manufacture, AS/NZS 3788 for in-service inspection, AS/NZS 1554 for structural steel welding and AS/NZS 1665 for aluminium structural welding. Gas transmission pipelines are licensed under the Gas Pipelines Act 2000, with the Director of Gas granting licences and the Director of Gas Safety certifying that a pipeline can convey gas safely; AS 2885 is the governing technical standard.
