Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own procedure for training, examining and certifying NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis writes written practices for Tasmanian employers and audits existing ones against SNT-TC-1A, customer specifications and your actual personnel records.

In a small market, a written practice has to do more with less. A Tasmanian employer may have two or three technicians covering several methods, part-time NDT duties combined with welding supervision or quality roles, and no in-house Level III at all. SNT-TC-1A allows for that: the employer defines what it needs, and an outside agency Level III can carry the Level III responsibilities. The document still has to be specific about methods and levels, training and experience, examinations, vision testing, certification periods, interrupted service and records, and the employer still has to follow it.

Many Tasmanian technicians already hold AINDT certificates to AS/NZS ISO 9712. A good written practice uses that, recognising prior training and experience, defining any additional employer-specific and practical examination for SNT-TC-1A purposes, and stating clearly that AINDT certification remains the basis for Australian-code work. The result is one coherent system rather than two competing ones. We reference training and experience requirements to the training requirements matrix rather than inventing figures. Read more on our written practice development page and our SNT-TC-1A guide, or ask for a written practice review for your Tasmanian business.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Tasmania

Direct answer: Atlantis writes and approves NDT procedures and component technique sheets to ASME Section V, AWS D1.1, AWS D1.2 (aluminium), API 1104 and customer specifications, and cross-references Australian Standards where projects use both. Tasmania's mix of hydro, smelting, aluminium shipbuilding and fabrication needs a broad method set.

Hydro assets call for ultrasonic thickness and weld procedures for penstocks and pressure conduits, often on large-diameter, thick-walled plate with access constraints, plus MT and PT procedures for runners, shafts and castings. Where a refurbishment contractor works to ASME or other international codes, procedures must state which code governs the new welds and which governs assessment of the existing structure. Smelters and mineral processors need procedures for pressure vessels, piping, tanks, cranes and structural steel, frequently under owner standards, and they need them written so that a contractor crew arriving for a short shutdown can apply them consistently.

Aluminium shipbuilding is a specialist area. Penetrant examination on aluminium welds, ultrasonic examination of thin aluminium plate, and radiography of aluminium all differ in technique from steel work. Export customers and classification societies define the acceptance rules; we write the procedures to meet those rules, and we do not claim any class-society approval for Atlantis. Gas pipeline work follows AS 2885, with API 1104 appearing if a US-specified project requires it. General fabrication typically uses AS/NZS 1554 and AS 1210, with ASME Section VIII and AWS D1.1 on export orders.

Every procedure we write states scope, personnel qualification, equipment and calibration, technique, coverage, evaluation, acceptance criteria by reference to the governing code, and reporting. Technique sheets fix the variables for a specific joint or component. Where Atlantis is your Level III, Anoop Rayavarapu approves them; where your customer's Level III must approve, we prepare the documents for that review.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Tasmanian crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is a named ASNT Level III outside your company who fulfils the Level III duties in your written practice. Atlantis provides ongoing, project-based and interim Level III cover for Tasmanian employers, mostly remotely, with onsite visits for practical examinations or audits.

For many Tasmanian businesses, outsourcing is simply the realistic option. A full-time Level III is hard to justify for a small team and hard to recruit to the island. An outside Level III gives you a named person for document approval, examination of new hires, technical questions and audit support. Three models cover most needs: an ongoing arrangement where we are named in your written practice; a project package, such as a written practice and a set of method procedures for an export contract; and a focused audit-preparation sprint. Interim cover bridges a gap if your Level III retires or moves on.

Distance from the mainland matters less than you might expect. Document review, written examinations under invigilated conditions defined in your written practice, records checks and technical advice all work remotely. Practical examinations on real specimens, procedure demonstrations and some audits need an onsite visit to your facility, and those are scoped and agreed in advance. To discuss cover, ask about outsourced Level III for your Tasmanian team, or read about interim NDT Level 3 cover.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Atlantis prepares Tasmanian NDT programmes for customer quality audits, owner and EPC supplier audits and the NDT elements of ISO 9001 audits. For NATA accreditation we can help get procedures and personnel records in order, but NATA assesses you independently and Atlantis is not NATA-accredited.

Export customers audit their suppliers' quality systems, sometimes remotely and sometimes with a visit. Owners of hydro, smelting and mineral processing assets audit contractor competence before shutdowns. Inspection bodies holding NATA accreditation to ISO/IEC 17020 or 17025 undergo periodic technical assessment. In each case the NDT section of the quality system is a common source of findings: missing examination records, expired vision tests, procedures that cite the wrong code edition, or a written practice nobody has read since it was issued.

Our preparation is practical. We read the requirement, compare your documents and records against it, sample personnel and calibration files, and give you a list of findings ranked by risk. Then we help you close them with revised documents, re-examinations where evidence is missing and a briefing for the people who will meet the auditor. We do not promise outcomes and we do not claim approvals we do not hold.

Where in Tasmania we support NDT programmes

Direct answer: Atlantis supports employers anywhere in Tasmania, remotely and with onsite visits to your facility. The main centres of NDT work are Hobart and the Derwent, Launceston and the Tamar Valley, the north-west coast around Burnie and Devonport, the west coast mining towns and the Central Highlands hydro system.

Hobart and the Derwent. Aluminium shipbuilding, the Risdon zinc works, marine services, the Antarctic and research fleet, and many of the state's engineering and fabrication firms. Bridges and civil structures across the Derwent add inspection work for asset owners.

Launceston, the Tamar Valley and Bell Bay. The aluminium smelter, gas-fired generation, port facilities and the terminus of the Tasmanian Gas Pipeline make Bell Bay the island's main heavy-industrial precinct. Launceston hosts engineering, food processing and fabrication businesses.

Burnie, Devonport and the north-west. Ports, mineral handling, the Port Latta pellet plant, paper and food processing, and Bass Strait shipping.

Queenstown, Rosebery and the west coast. Underground and open-cut mines with processing plant, inspected in short shutdowns by small crews.

Central Highlands. Hydro power stations, dams, penstocks and canals, where much of the island's long-term structural inspection work sits.

Atlantis does not yet have city pages for Tasmania. For national context, see NDT consulting across Australia, ASNT NDT training in Australia and our Australia region page.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: A scoping call, a review of your existing documents, a written scope and quote, delivery of documents and examinations remotely and onsite as agreed, then signed, revision-controlled deliverables. Timelines depend on scope and are agreed during scoping.

  1. Scoping call. What triggered the need, which codes and customer specifications apply, which certificates your staff hold, and the deadline you are working to.
  2. Document review. Existing written practice, procedures, sample personnel files and the customer's requirement.
  3. Written scope and quote. Deliverables, remote and onsite elements and approval responsibilities. Pricing is quote on request.
  4. Drafting. Written practice, procedures and technique sheets, sent for your review with explanations of each decision.
  5. Examinations. Written examinations under your written practice; practical examinations at your facility on real specimens.
  6. Approval and handover. Signed documents, revision history and an audit pack.
  7. Ongoing cover. Optional outsourced Level III arrangement for approvals, new hires and audits.

Book a scoping call for your Tasmanian NDT programme.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who reviews and approves the documents he scopes. Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A training online, live-virtual or onsite at your facility, and the Practical NDT simulator, where technicians can practise methods in 3D environments such as a welding workshop and a storage tank before their practical examination. The simulator is practice only and does not replace a practical examination on real specimens.

Frequently asked questions

Can an outside ASNT Level III be our Level III in Tasmania?

Yes, for an SNT-TC-1A programme. SNT-TC-1A allows an outside agency Level III, named in your written practice. It does not replace AINDT certification for Australian-code work.

Do Tasmanian NDT technicians need AINDT certification?

For most Australian work, employers and owners expect AINDT certification to AS/NZS ISO 9712. SNT-TC-1A certification is added when a US code, customer or owner requires it.

Who licenses industrial radiography in Tasmania?

The Radiation Protection Unit in the Department of Health, under the Radiation Protection Act 2005. Confirm current licence and qualification requirements with the unit.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in Tasmania?

WorkSafe Tasmania, under the Work Health and Safety Act 2012 and its regulations, which require registration of certain plant designs and items.

Who licenses gas pipelines in Tasmania?

Transmission pipelines are licensed under the Gas Pipelines Act 2000. The Director of Gas grants licences, and the Director of Gas Safety must certify that the pipeline can convey gas safely.

Can you write NDT procedures for aluminium welding?

Yes. We write PT, UT and RT procedures for aluminium welds to AWS D1.2 or customer and class requirements, cross-referenced to AS/NZS 1665 where relevant.

Can you support penstock and hydro plant inspection?

We write and approve UT, MT, PT and VT procedures and technique sheets for hydro components, and help with personnel qualification for the crews doing the work.

Can examinations be done remotely from Tasmania?

Written examinations can be administered remotely under invigilated conditions defined in your written practice. Practical examinations need an onsite visit.

Is Atlantis NATA-accredited?

No. Atlantis holds no NATA accreditation and is not AINDT-recognised.

Does Atlantis offer AINDT or ISO 9712 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Tasmania?

Quote on request after a scoping call; it depends on methods, documents, examinations and onsite days. Affordable, accessible and fully customisable.

Does Atlantis have an office in Tasmania?

No. Work is delivered remotely, with onsite visits to your facility when the scope needs them.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in the UAE

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III consulting to NDT service companies, fabricators and asset owners across the United Arab Emirates: SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, NDT procedures and technique sheets to ASME, API and AWS, procedure review and harmonisation across contractors, examinations under your written practice, outsourced or interim Level III cover, and preparation for operator, client and accreditation audits. Every engagement is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, and is delivered remotely with onsite visits to your facility or site when the work requires them. Atlantis has no UAE office and does not hold ADNOC, ENOC or other operator vendor approvals, an ICV certificate, FANR licences or UAE accreditation.

We put that list up front because the UAE is an approval-first market. Service companies here lead with their operator approvals, their accreditation to ISO/IEC 17020, their class-society recognitions and their In-Country Value score, and buyers check them before they read anything else. Atlantis is not competing for that position. What Atlantis offers is the Level III expertise underneath those approvals: the written practice that governs how your technicians are certified, the procedures your operator's inspection department reviews, and a named ASNT Level III who can answer for both. SNT-TC-1A is widely accepted in the UAE oil and gas sector alongside ISO 9712, and many UAE NDT companies run SNT-TC-1A programmes that need regular care. If yours does, request a UAE Level III consultation.

Why UAE NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: UAE NDT work is driven by oil and gas, refining and petrochemicals, storage terminals, shipbuilding and offshore fabrication, power and water, aviation and a nuclear power plant. Operators require approved procedures and qualified personnel, and under SNT-TC-1A a Level III approves the written practice and procedures and examines and certifies Level I and II technicians.

Abu Dhabi holds most of the country's hydrocarbon assets. The ADNOC group runs onshore fields and gas processing across the emirate, offshore fields and island facilities such as Das Island and Zirku, gas liquefaction, and one of the world's largest refining and petrochemical complexes at Ruwais, where ADNOC's refineries sit alongside the Borouge petrochemical plants. These assets generate a constant flow of new-construction, shutdown and in-service inspection work: weld examination on new piping and vessels, corrosion mapping and thickness surveys, inspection of heat exchangers and tank floors, and examination of offshore structures and pipelines. Much of it is performed by contracted NDT service companies working to ADNOC's group standards and the engineering contractor's project specifications, which in turn rely heavily on ASME, API and AWS codes.

Dubai and the northern emirates add a different mix. ENOC's refinery and terminals at Jebel Ali, the Jebel Ali Free Zone with its many fabrication and engineering businesses, Drydocks World's ship repair and conversion yard, and the large power and desalination complexes operated by DEWA all need inspection. Sharjah's Hamriyah Free Zone hosts fabrication yards that build modules and structures for regional and international projects. Fujairah, on the east coast, is one of the world's major bunkering hubs, with large oil storage terminals whose tanks, pipelines and jetties are inspected to API 653 and owner requirements.

Beyond energy, the UAE has a serious aviation sector, with airline engineering and maintenance organisations in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, engine and component repair businesses, and aerostructure manufacturing in Al Ain supplying international aircraft programmes. Aerospace NDT is procedure-driven and audit-heavy. In the far west of Abu Dhabi, the Barakah nuclear power plant, regulated by the Federal Authority for Nuclear Regulation, has four units and a supply chain with demanding quality expectations.

Across all of this, NDT service companies are expected to show a working personnel qualification system and approved procedures before they mobilise. A company with a strong Level III function wins pre-qualification more easily and handles operator audits with less disruption. Many UAE companies keep a Level III on staff; many others rely on outside Level III support for some methods, or need a second pair of eyes before a major audit. That is where ASNT Level III consulting services fit.

Approvals, regulators and standards in the UAE

Direct answer: In the UAE, operator approvals (ADNOC, ENOC and others), ISO/IEC 17020 accreditation and the national In-Country Value programme shape who gets work; FANR licenses radiation sources for industrial radiography; and ASME, API, AWS and operator standards govern the technical work. Both SNT-TC-1A and ISO 9712 personnel certification are common.

Supplier registration with ADNOC runs through its supplier portal and involves trade licence, financial and certification documents, with In-Country Value certification now aligned to the national ICV framework managed by the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology. ICV certificates are not always mandatory to bid, but they carry weight in commercial evaluation. Other operators and owners run their own vendor registration and approval processes. Atlantis holds none of these approvals and does not claim to. What we can do is help your company's NDT documentation stand up when an operator's inspection or quality team reviews it as part of your approval or re-approval.

Accreditation of inspection bodies to ISO/IEC 17020 and testing laboratories to ISO/IEC 17025 is provided in the UAE by national accreditation bodies, including the Emirates International Accreditation Centre (EIAC) in Dubai and the federal system under the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology. Many NDT companies hold such accreditation, and their accreditation assessments review method procedures and personnel competence. Atlantis is not an accreditation body and is not accredited, but procedure quality and personnel records are exactly what a Level III review improves.

Industrial radiography is regulated federally. The Federal Authority for Nuclear Regulation (FANR), established under Federal Law by Decree No. 6 of 2009, is the sole body that licenses regulated activities involving radioactive sources and X-ray generators, and it licenses industrial radiography companies. A Level III does not hold or replace a FANR licence. Our job is to make sure your RT procedures and technique sheets are consistent with your FANR licence conditions and radiation protection programme, and that field crews are not using procedures that assume different sources, collimation or controlled-area arrangements.

Technically, UAE oil and gas work leans on ASME Section V, VIII and B31.3, API 510, 570, 653 and 1104, AWS D1.1, and operator group standards. Shipyards add classification society rules. Workplace safety is governed at federal and emirate level, including Abu Dhabi's OSHAD framework, and free zones have their own authorities.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: An SNT-TC-1A written practice is the employer's own rulebook for training, examining and certifying NDT personnel. Atlantis writes written practices for UAE companies and audits existing ones against SNT-TC-1A, operator requirements and your actual records, then helps you close the gaps.

The UAE NDT workforce is international. A typical service company employs technicians trained and certified in India, Pakistan, the Philippines, Europe and elsewhere, some under SNT-TC-1A at previous employers, some under ISO 9712 schemes, some under both. SNT-TC-1A certification does not transfer between employers, so every new hire has to be qualified and certified under your written practice. The written practice needs a clear, defensible rule for recognising documented training and experience, deciding which examinations a new hire must take, and running practical examinations on your specimens. When that rule is vague, operators' auditors notice.

A UAE written practice we write covers scope and responsibilities, methods and levels, training and experience requirements (referenced to the training requirements matrix), examination content and grading, practical specimens, vision examinations, certification and recertification periods, interrupted service, outside agency use and records. Where an operator or client requires ISO 9712 certification for certain work, the document says so and explains how the two schemes coexist in your company. Where your clients accept SNT-TC-1A, it lets the employer control the timing of certifying an incoming technician, because the employer runs the process.

Written practice audits look at the document and at what actually happened: we sample personnel files for evidence of training, experience, examination results, vision tests and certification signatures, and list every gap. See our written practice development page and our SNT-TC-1A guide for more, or ask for a written practice audit for your UAE company.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in the UAE

Direct answer: Atlantis writes, reviews and approves NDT procedures and component technique sheets to ASME Section V, API 1104, AWS D1.1, API 653 and UAE operators' specifications. For asset owners we also review contractor procedures independently and harmonise them so that results from different contractors are comparable.

Selecting the right procedure is where many problems start. A corrosion survey on hot piping, a weld examination on thick-wall vessel nozzles, a tank-floor scan and an inspection of austenitic or dissimilar-metal welds each need different techniques, and operators increasingly expect encoded, recordable data from phased array, TOFD or automated corrosion mapping rather than manual readings. Our procedures state scope, applicable codes, personnel qualification, equipment and calibration, scan plans and coverage, evaluation, acceptance criteria by reference to the governing code, and reporting. Technique sheets then fix probes, wedges, focal laws, reference blocks and coverage for each component so results are repeatable.

The UAE climate is a real technical factor. High ambient and surface temperatures affect couplant behaviour, wedge velocity and calibration stability in ultrasonic testing, and sand and humidity affect magnetic particle and penetrant work. Procedures written for temperate climates often say nothing useful about this; ours address temperature ranges and verification checks explicitly.

For owners and EPCs, procedure harmonisation is a common need. When three NDT contractors inspect the same unit with three different procedures, thickness and indication data cannot be compared from one turnaround to the next. A Level III review sets a common baseline: the same reference standards, coverage rules, recording thresholds and reporting format, and a register of approved procedures with revision control. That register is often the simplest way to make NDT data trustworthy over the life of an asset. Where Atlantis is your Level III, Anoop Rayavarapu approves the procedures; where the operator's own Level III must approve them, we prepare them for that review and respond to comments.

Outsourced and interim Level III for UAE crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is a named ASNT Level III outside your company who carries the Level III duties defined in your written practice. Atlantis provides ongoing, project-based and interim Level III cover to UAE companies, mainly remotely, with onsite visits for practical examinations, procedure demonstrations and audits.

Many UAE NDT companies have a Level III in one or two methods but not in every method they offer. Others lose their Level III to a competitor or an operator and need cover while they recruit. Some simply want an independent Level III to examine new hires or approve procedures in methods their own Level III does not hold. All of these are standard outsourced arrangements under SNT-TC-1A, provided the written practice names the outside agency and defines its responsibilities.

Three models cover most needs. Ongoing outsourced Level III: named in your written practice for agreed methods, handling approvals, examinations, technical queries and audit support. Project-based: a defined package such as a written practice plus PAUT and TOFD procedures for a new contract. Audit-preparation sprint: a focused review before an operator audit or accreditation assessment. Interim cover fills the gap until your own Level III is in place.

Remote delivery covers document work, written examinations under invigilated conditions, records checks and technical advice. Practical examinations on real specimens, procedure demonstrations and some audits need someone onsite, and we scope those as visits to your facility or site. To discuss cover, ask about outsourced Level III for your UAE team, or read about interim NDT Level 3 cover.

Audit readiness: operator, client and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Atlantis prepares UAE NDT programmes for operator pre-qualification and re-approval reviews, EPC and client audits, ISO/IEC 17020 and 17025 accreditation assessments and the NDT parts of ISO 9001 audits. We improve the documents and records the auditor will see; we do not grant approvals or promise outcomes.

Audits are frequent in the UAE. Operators review contractors before approval and periodically after it. EPCs audit subcontractors before mobilisation. Accreditation bodies assess method procedures, validation evidence and personnel competence. Class societies review shipyard NDT. The questions are predictable: Is the written practice current and approved? Do personnel files show training, experience, examinations and vision tests for every certified technician? Are procedures approved by a Level III in the method, and do they cite the right code edition? Is equipment calibrated and traceable?

Our preparation reads the specific requirement, compares your documents and records against it, samples personnel and calibration files, and delivers a ranked findings list. We then help close findings with revised documents, re-examinations where evidence is missing, and a short briefing for your team. Read more on the API 510 pressure vessel inspection support and API 653 tank inspection support pages if your audit covers in-service inspection programmes.

Emirates and cities we support across the UAE

Direct answer: Atlantis supports NDT programmes across all seven emirates, remotely and with onsite visits to your facility or site. Most work comes from Abu Dhabi (including Ruwais and Musaffah), Dubai and Jebel Ali, Sharjah's free zones and Fujairah's terminals.

Abu Dhabi. ADNOC's onshore and offshore operations, the Musaffah industrial area with its fabrication yards and NDT companies, shipbuilding and port developments, and aviation businesses. City pages: NDT consulting in Abu Dhabi, ASNT NDT training for Abu Dhabi, Practical NDT simulator in Abu Dhabi and corrosion inspection in Abu Dhabi.

Ruwais. The refining and petrochemical complex in the Al Dhafra region generates large turnaround scopes. See NDT consulting in Ruwais and NDT training for Ruwais.

Dubai and Jebel Ali. Refining and terminals, free-zone fabrication, ship repair, power and desalination, and aviation maintenance. See NDT consulting in Dubai, NDT training in Dubai, Practical NDT in Dubai and third-party inspection in Dubai.

Sharjah. Fabrication yards and industrial businesses in Hamriyah and the Sharjah industrial areas. See NDT consulting in Sharjah and NDT training in Sharjah.

Fujairah. Oil storage terminals, bunkering and jetties, with heavy API 653 and pipeline inspection demand. See NDT consulting in Fujairah, third-party inspection in Fujairah and NDT training in Fujairah.

Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. Aerostructures in Al Ain; cement, ceramics, port and fabrication industries in the northern emirates.

National pages: ASNT NDT training in the UAE, NDT ERP for UAE inspection companies, asset integrity digital twins in the UAE and our UAE region page. Working across the Gulf? See NDT consulting in Saudi Arabia.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: A scoping call, a review of your documents and the operator's requirement, a written scope and quote, delivery of documents and examinations remotely and onsite as agreed, and signed, revision-controlled deliverables. Timelines depend on scope and are set during scoping around your audit or mobilisation dates.

  1. Scoping call. What triggered the need (new contract, re-approval, audit, departing Level III), which operator and codes apply, and which schemes your technicians hold.
  2. Document review. Your written practice, procedures, sample personnel files and the operator or client requirement.
  3. Written scope and quote. Deliverables, remote and onsite elements and approval responsibilities. Pricing is quote on request.
  4. Drafting and review. Written practice, procedures and technique sheets with explanations, revised against your comments and, where relevant, the operator's comments.
  5. Examinations and demonstrations. Written examinations under your written practice; practical examinations and procedure demonstrations onsite.
  6. Approval and handover. Signed documents, a procedure register, revision history and an audit pack.
  7. Ongoing cover. Optional outsourced Level III arrangement for new hires, approvals and future audits.

Book a scoping call for your UAE NDT programme.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who reviews and approves the documents he scopes. Atlantis also delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A training online, live-virtual or onsite at your facility, and the Practical NDT simulator lets technicians practise methods in 3D environments, including an oil and gas site, a storage tank and an aircraft hangar, before their practical examination. The simulator is practice only; it does not replace a practical examination on real specimens.

Frequently asked questions

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted in the UAE?

Yes, SNT-TC-1A is widely accepted in the UAE oil and gas sector alongside ISO 9712. Each operator and client sets its own requirement, so check the contract specification for which scheme applies to your work.

Can an outside ASNT Level III be our Level III in the UAE?

Yes, under SNT-TC-1A an employer may use an outside agency Level III named in its written practice. Operators may also have their own requirements for contractor Level III personnel; check them.

Is Atlantis ADNOC-approved?

No. Atlantis holds no ADNOC, ENOC or other operator approval and no ICV certificate. We help NDT companies prepare the documents operators review; the approval itself is between you and the operator.

Who licenses industrial radiography in the UAE?

The Federal Authority for Nuclear Regulation (FANR), which licenses regulated activities involving radioactive sources and X-ray generators, including industrial radiography.

Can you write PAUT and TOFD procedures for UAE operators?

Yes. We write and approve PAUT, TOFD, UT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET procedures and technique sheets to ASME Section V and operator specifications, and support procedure demonstrations.

Can you review procedures from several NDT contractors on one asset?

Yes. Independent Level III review and harmonisation of contractor procedures is a common service for owners and EPCs.

Do you help with ISO/IEC 17020 accreditation in the UAE?

We improve the NDT procedures, competence records and validation evidence that assessors review. Atlantis is not an accreditation body and is not accredited itself.

Can examinations be done remotely in the UAE?

Written examinations can be administered remotely under invigilated conditions set out in your written practice. Practical examinations need an onsite visit.

Does Atlantis provide ISO 9712 or PCN training in the UAE?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only.

How much does Level III consulting cost in the UAE?

Quote on request after a scoping call; it depends on methods, documents, examinations and onsite days. Affordable, accessible and fully customisable.

Do you support API 510, 570 and 653 programmes in the UAE?

We support them with NDT technique selection, procedures and personnel qualification for the crews that execute them. We do not offer risk-based inspection or fitness-for-service assessments.

Does Atlantis have an office in the UAE?

No. Work is delivered remotely, with onsite visits to your facility or site when the scope needs them.

If an operator, EPC or auditor is asking about your written practice, procedures or Level III, start with a short call. Get a quote for Level III consulting in the UAE, or browse our consulting services.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Utah

Short answer: Atlantis NDT gives Utah employers access to an ASNT NDT Level III without a full-time hire: outsourced or interim Level III cover, SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets, Level I and II examinations under your written practice, and audit preparation for refinery owners, aerospace primes, mining companies and accreditation bodies. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, leads every engagement. Delivery is remote, plus onsite visits to your Wasatch Front, Uinta Basin or rural Utah facility. Atlantis has no office in Utah.

Utah packs an unusual amount of NDT work into a narrow strip of the Wasatch Front. Within an hour's drive of Salt Lake City sit a cluster of five refineries in Salt Lake and Davis counties, an Air Force depot that overhauls fighter aircraft and supports the intercontinental ballistic missile fleet, solid rocket motor plants, aerostructure and defence electronics factories, one of the world's largest open-pit copper mines with its own smelter and refinery, steel mills and fabricators, and the transmission pipelines that move Wyoming and Uinta Basin gas and crude. East of the mountains, the Uinta Basin oilfield around Vernal and Roosevelt adds production, gathering and trucking work. This page explains what Utah NDT programmes need from a Level III, which state agencies and codes apply, and how to request a Utah Level III consultation.

Why Utah NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: Utah employers certifying NDT personnel to SNT-TC-1A need a written practice approved by a Level III, procedures for each method and Level III-administered examinations. Refinery owners, Hill Air Force Base contractors, rocket-motor and aerospace primes and mining companies all audit their NDT suppliers and expect a named Level III behind the programme.

Refining. The refineries in North Salt Lake, Woods Cross and Salt Lake City, operated by companies including Chevron, Marathon, HF Sinclair and Big West Oil, process Utah, Wyoming, Colorado and Canadian crude, including the waxy crude produced in the Uinta Basin. Turnarounds bring large inspection crews for pressure vessels, process piping, heaters and storage tanks, with work done to API 510, 570 and 653 inspection codes and ASME construction codes. Contractors serving these owners need procedures and certification records that survive owner audits.

Aerospace and defence. Hill Air Force Base near Ogden is home to the Ogden Air Logistics Complex, which performs depot maintenance on fighter aircraft and supports the ICBM fleet and its replacement programme. Northrop Grumman builds solid rocket motors and composite structures at Promontory and at the Bacchus works in Magna. Boeing makes composite and assembled aerostructures in Salt Lake City, and L3Harris has a large defence-communications operation there. Machine shops, composite fabricators and special-process houses along I-15 from Ogden to Provo supply these primes. Their NDT ranges from penetrant and magnetic particle testing of machined parts to ultrasonic testing of composites and bonded structures and radiography of assemblies.

Mining, metals and power. Rio Tinto Kennecott operates the Bingham Canyon copper mine, a concentrator, a smelter and a refinery west of Salt Lake City. Nucor makes steel bar in Plymouth and steel joists in Brigham City. The Intermountain Power Project near Delta is being repowered from coal to gas-fired generation. Mine haul trucks, shovels, crushers and smelter vessels need heavy-section UT and MT; steel mills need structural and equipment inspection; power plants need boiler and piping work.

Pipelines. The Kern River natural gas pipeline crosses Utah from Wyoming to Nevada, the Ruby pipeline crosses the north of the state, and local gas distribution is run by Enbridge Gas Utah (formerly Dominion Energy Utah). Crude and products lines serve the refineries. Construction and integrity work on these systems relies on API 1104 welding and inspection.

Many of the companies doing this work are small or mid-sized. A Clearfield composite shop, a Uinta Basin inspection contractor or a fabricator in Ogden rarely has its own Level III for every method, but customers still expect one. ASNT Level III consulting services close that gap.

Level III services for Utah employers

Direct answer: Atlantis covers all core Level III functions for Utah companies: written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets, Level I and II examinations, outsourced and interim Level III, audit readiness, programme set-up and technical support to API 510, 570 and 653 inspection programmes. Scope is set on a call.

ServiceWhat it coversTypical Utah client type
Written practice developmentA new or rewritten SNT-TC-1A written practice covering methods, levels, training and experience, examinations, vision tests, records and recertificationAerospace and composite suppliers along I-15 from Ogden to Provo
Written practice and certification auditGap review of an existing programme against SNT-TC-1A, customer clauses and actual certification filesRefinery turnaround contractors before an owner audit
Procedures and technique sheetsUT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET procedures to the governing code, with joint- or part-specific technique sheets and PAUT/TOFD scan plansFabricators, pipeline contractors, mining-equipment repair shops

Inspection programme supportNDT technique selection, procedure review and data quality for API 510 vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 tank programmesRefinery, terminal and plant owners and their contractors

The consulting overview lists the full range. Inspection programme support is limited to NDT technique and procedure work for inspection programmes; we do not offer API inspector training.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's own procedure for qualifying and certifying NDT personnel. SNT-TC-1A recommends its content, but your auditor tests your written practice against your records. Atlantis writes written practices that fit your Utah operation and audits existing ones so gaps are fixed before an owner, prime or accreditation body finds them.

Utah's industries create distinct written practice pressures. Turnaround contractors at the Woods Cross and North Salt Lake refineries hire seasonally and certify quickly, which tests whether experience records, vision tests and examination files keep up. Aerospace and defence suppliers near Hill Air Force Base and in the Salt Lake Valley may need a written practice that sits alongside NAS 410 or prime-specific requirements on some contracts. Uinta Basin inspection companies that started with one method may have added others without updating the document. A written practice has to describe what the company really does and must be kept up to date as the work changes.

When writing a written practice we define the methods, techniques and levels covered; training and experience requirements, referenced to the training requirements matrix; examination content, question banks and grading; practical examination specimens and checklists; vision testing; certification records; recertification and interrupted service; and how the Level III function is provided. See written practice development and SNT-TC-1A training and certification for background.

In audits we sample certification files and compare them with the written practice. Common findings: technicians certified in a method the written practice does not cover; experience hours with no supporting records; practical exams without a graded checklist; examinations given by someone not named as Level III; and procedures citing superseded editions of ASME, API or AWS documents. You receive a ranked finding list and help fixing it if you want it.

Where training is needed to meet the written practice, Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A-based courses online and onsite; see NDT training in Utah and corporate NDT training.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Utah

Direct answer: Utah procedures are written to the code that governs each job: API 510, 570 and 653 with ASME Section V for refinery in-service inspection; ASME Sections I and VIII and B31.1 and B31.3 for new construction; API 1104 for pipelines; AWS D1.1 for structural and mining work; and customer specifications for aerospace, rocket-motor and composite parts.

  • Refining and terminals: in-service inspection to API 510, 570 and 653, with examination methods per ASME Section V. Corrosion mapping, PAUT and TOFD weld examinations and thickness surveys need procedures that state coverage, calibration and recording clearly. See refining audit support.
  • Boilers and pressure vessels: the Utah Labor Commission's Division of Boiler, Elevator and Coal Mine Safety enforces the Utah Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act, inspecting boilers and pressure vessels across the state. Repairs and alterations need NDT to the ASME and National Board requirements that apply.
  • Pipelines: API 1104 under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Intrastate gas pipeline safety in Utah is overseen by the Division of Public Utilities under the Public Service Commission's rules, as a PHMSA-certified state programme. Interstate lines such as Kern River and Ruby fall under PHMSA directly.
  • Aerospace, defence and composites: customer specifications commonly referencing ASTM E1417 (penetrant), E1444 (magnetic particle), E2375 (ultrasonic, wrought products) and composite ultrasonic standards. Technique sheets are usually tied to part numbers and approved by the customer.
  • Mining and steel: AWS D1.1 for structural work and equipment makers' repair specifications for haul-truck frames, shovel booms and crusher components.
  • Radiography: Utah is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials licences for industrial radiography are issued and inspected by the Utah Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control. Radiography procedures must align with the licensee's radiation safety programme.

Utah's climate matters for field procedures too. Winter turnarounds and pipeline work at altitude bring sub-freezing temperatures that affect penetrant dwell times, couplant behaviour and battery-powered equipment, and the Uinta Basin's winter inversions and cold can stretch field schedules. Procedures should state temperature limits for consumables and how calibration temperature differences are controlled under ASME Section V. We write those controls in, and we review procedures written by others when a customer rejects them or an auditor raises a finding.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Utah crews

Direct answer: As your outsourced Level III, Atlantis is the named Level III in your written practice under a standing agreement. As interim Level III, we cover a gap until you have your own. Document work is done remotely; examinations, procedure demonstrations and audits are done onsite at your facility in Utah when needed.

  • Ongoing outsourced Level III: approvals of procedures and technique sheets, maintenance of the written practice, examinations, technical questions and audit attendance. This suits Wasatch Front and Uinta Basin NDT companies that need Level III accountability year-round.
  • Project work: a defined deliverable such as a new written practice, a procedure set for PAUT or TOFD, technique sheets for a new composite part family, or examinations for a cohort hired before a turnaround.
  • Audit-preparation sprint: a focused review before an owner, prime or accreditation audit.

Utah's large defence and aerospace employers recruit experienced Level IIIs heavily, and smaller suppliers can lose theirs with little notice. Interim Level III cover keeps certifications, procedure approvals and corrective-action responses moving while you recruit. Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III. Companies running crews in Utah and neighbouring Wyoming, Idaho, Nevada or Colorado can align their programmes across sites; see multi-site programme harmonisation.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Utah NDT programmes are audited by refinery owners before turnarounds, by aerospace and defence primes and Nadcap-style auditors, by mining companies before contractors mobilise, by ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 17025 assessors, and by the Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control for radiography licensees. Atlantis prepares the NDT evidence and runs mock audits.

Refinery owner audits focus on procedure approval, technician certifications against the work they will do, equipment calibration and how inspection data is recorded. Aerospace audits test traceability of certifications, procedure revisions and process controls on penetrant and magnetic particle lines; see Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness. Mining owners check certifications, procedures and safety documents. Accreditation assessors check competence records, method validation and traceability. Radiography licensees face separate radiation safety inspections.

We prepare the NDT portion of each audit and do not grant approvals, accreditation or vendor status. Related pages: refining audit support, aerospace audit support, mining audit support, pipeline audit support and steel and metals audit support. With an audit coming up, ask for a Utah audit-readiness review.

Sector notes: Utah industries and their Level III needs

Direct answer: Refinery contractors need code-matched in-service procedures and turnaround-ready certification files; aerospace and rocket-motor suppliers need part-specific techniques and traceable records; composite fabricators need ultrasonic procedures suited to laminates and bonds; mining and steel shops need heavy-section UT and MT; and pipeline crews need API 1104-ready documents.

Refineries of the Davis and Salt Lake county corridor

Turnarounds concentrate a year's inspection into weeks. Procedures, technique sheets and certification files need to be ready before mobilisation. See refining NDT consulting in Woods Cross and refining NDT consulting in Salt Lake City.

Hill Air Force Base and the defence supply chain

Depot maintenance on aircraft and support of missile systems flows NDT requirements to contractors around Ogden, Layton and Clearfield, with eddy current, ultrasonic, penetrant and magnetic particle testing all in use.

Rocket motors and composites

Solid rocket motors, composite cases and aerostructures need ultrasonic and radiographic inspection under strict customer specifications. Procedures for composites differ from metals and must be qualified on representative standards.

Copper, steel and heavy industry

Bingham Canyon's equipment, the smelter and refinery, and the state's steel mills create continuous structural and equipment inspection. See steel NDT consulting in Salt Lake City and steel and metals audit support.

Uinta Basin oil and gas

Production facilities, gathering lines and crude handling around Vernal and Roosevelt need pipeline, tank and vessel inspection. See NDT consulting in Roosevelt and pipeline audit support.

Cities we support across Utah

Direct answer: Atlantis supports Utah NDT employers statewide, remotely and onsite at your facility: Salt Lake City and the Salt Lake Valley, Davis and Weber counties, Utah County, the Uinta Basin, Tooele and the west desert, Delta and southern Utah. We have no office in Utah.

Salt Lake City and the Salt Lake Valley. Refineries, Kennecott, Boeing and L3Harris, fabrication, rail and utilities. Related pages: NDT consulting in Salt Lake City, refining NDT consulting in Salt Lake City, steel NDT consulting in Salt Lake City, NDT training in Salt Lake City, Practical NDT in Salt Lake City, and method pages for ultrasonic testing, radiographic testing, magnetic particle testing, penetrant testing, eddy current testing and visual testing in Salt Lake City.

Davis and Weber counties (Woods Cross, North Salt Lake, Bountiful, Layton, Clearfield, Ogden). The refinery corridor, Hill Air Force Base and its contractors, aerospace and composite shops and rail. See refining NDT consulting in Woods Cross.

Northern Utah (Brigham City, Promontory, Logan). Rocket motor manufacturing, steel joist fabrication and food and equipment manufacturing.

Utah County (Provo, Orem, Lehi, Spanish Fork). Technology manufacturing, metal fabrication, redevelopment of the former Geneva Steel site in Vineyard and growing data-centre construction.

Uinta Basin (Vernal, Roosevelt). Oil and gas production, gathering and crude handling. See NDT consulting in Roosevelt and Practical NDT in Vernal.

Tooele, the west desert, Delta and southern Utah. Military depots and test ranges, the Intermountain Power Project, and mining and pipeline work.

Technician training is covered on the Utah NDT training hub, and trainees can rehearse methods on the Practical NDT simulator, which is practice only and does not replace practical exams on real specimens.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: We start with a scoping call about your methods, codes, customers and deadlines; agree a written scope with the remote and onsite split; deliver documents and examinations with your team; and either hand over or stay on as your named Level III. Quotes are provided on request.

  1. Scoping call. What you inspect, which methods and codes apply, who your customers are, and what is driving the timing: a turnaround, a new contract or an audit.
  2. Document review. Your current written practice, procedures and a sample of certification files, or your scope of work if you are starting fresh.
  3. Scope and quote. Deliverables, responsibilities, remote and onsite work, and the Level III assigned. Quotes are on request.
  4. Delivery. Drafts reviewed with your quality team; examinations, demonstrations and mock audits scheduled at your facility around production, turnarounds and weather.
  5. Handover or continuing cover. Final documents and records under your control, or ongoing outsourced Level III support.

To begin, book a Utah Level III scoping call.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Refinery owners and aerospace primes want to know who the Level III is behind a contractor's programme; with Atlantis the name is stated at the start. Anoop also leads Atlantis NDT's SNT-TC-1A-based training, so your written practice and your technicians' training line up.

Frequently asked questions about NDT Level III consulting in Utah

Where can I find an NDT Level III consultant in Utah?

Atlantis provides Level III consulting across Utah, remotely and onsite at your facility, led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III. Look for a Level III certified in your methods who will be named in your written practice.

Does my Utah company need its own Level III?

You need Level III functions if you certify personnel to SNT-TC-1A, but they can be provided by an outside Level III when your written practice defines that arrangement.

Who issues industrial radiography licences in Utah?

Utah is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials licences, including for industrial radiography, are issued by the Utah Department of Environmental Quality's Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control.

Which agency inspects boilers and pressure vessels in Utah?

The Utah Labor Commission's Division of Boiler, Elevator and Coal Mine Safety, which enforces the Utah Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act.

Who regulates pipeline safety in Utah?

The Division of Public Utilities oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety under the Public Service Commission's rules as a PHMSA-certified state programme. Interstate pipelines are regulated by PHMSA.

Can you get our certification files ready before a refinery turnaround?

Yes. We review the written practice and files for the technicians you plan to mobilise, fix gaps, administer any needed examinations and confirm procedures match the owner's requirements.

Do you work with Hill Air Force Base contractors?

We support contractors' NDT programmes: written practices, procedures, technique sheets, examinations and audit preparation against the customer's requirements. We do not represent ourselves as approved by any military customer.

Can you write ultrasonic procedures for composites?

Yes. Composite UT procedures and technique sheets can be written to the customer's specification and qualified on representative reference standards.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Utah?

It depends on methods, volume of procedures and examinations, and onsite time. Quotes are provided on request after a scoping call.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted by Utah employers?

It is the common basis for employer certification in US refining, pipeline, power and fabrication work. Some aerospace and defence customers require NAS 410 or their own schemes, so check the contract.

Do you offer API 510 or 570 inspector training?

No. We provide Level III technical support to API 510, 570 and 653 inspection programmes. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based.

Can Atlantis train our Utah technicians too?

Yes. Level I, II and III training is available online and onsite; see NDT training in Utah.

A named Level III for your Utah programme

Whether you run a turnaround crew in Woods Cross, a composite inspection cell in Clearfield, a mining maintenance contractor near Bingham Canyon or a pipeline crew in the Uinta Basin, the questions are the same: is the written practice right, are the procedures right, and can you prove your people are qualified? Ask about outsourced Level III cover in Utah or request a Utah written practice review. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Quotes on request.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Victoria, Australia

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III services to employers in Victoria, Australia, remotely and onsite at the employer's own facility. We act as outsourced or interim Level III for ASNT SNT-TC-1A programmes, write and audit written practices, write and approve procedures and technique sheets, administer qualification exams under the employer's written practice and prepare companies for customer, owner and prime-contractor audits. Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, leads every engagement, and every scope is quoted on request.

This page is about the Australian state of Victoria, not Victoria in Texas or British Columbia. In Victoria, the usual credentials for NDT work are AINDT certification under ISO 9712 for technicians, AICIP certification for in-service pressure-equipment inspectors working to AS/NZS 3788, and NATA accreditation for laboratories and inspection bodies. Atlantis holds none of these and never claims them. Our role is narrower: SNT-TC-1A and US-code expertise for Victorian companies that supply US aerospace primes, work on US-owned assets, build to ASME, API or AWS codes, or support defence programmes with US-linked requirements. If that describes your business, request a Victoria Level III quote.

Why Victorian NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: A Victorian employer certifying NDT personnel under ASNT SNT-TC-1A needs a Level III who owns the written practice, approves procedures and administers exams. In Victoria that demand comes mostly from aerospace composites and defence manufacturing in Melbourne and Geelong, from contractors on the Geelong refinery and Gippsland gas assets, and from fabricators building to US codes.

Victoria's industrial base is concentrated around Port Phillip Bay and in Gippsland. Geelong hosts the Viva Energy refinery, one of only two fuel refineries still operating in Australia, which supplies a large share of Victoria's fuel. Its turnarounds and ongoing integrity programme generate demand for UT thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD weld inspection, heat-exchanger tube testing and documented procedures. Altona and Hastings add fuel and LPG terminals, and Melbourne's western suburbs have a long chemical and plastics history, although some plants have closed in recent years. See refining audit support and petrochemical audit support.

Gippsland is Victoria's energy region. Esso Australia, an ExxonMobil subsidiary, operates the Gippsland Basin joint venture, with offshore platforms in Bass Strait and onshore gas processing at Longford; platform decommissioning and plant maintenance both require inspection. The Latrobe Valley's brown-coal power stations, Loy Yang A, Loy Yang B and Yallourn, need boiler, header and high-energy piping inspection during outages, and Gippsland is also the focus of Australia's first offshore wind zone. Elsewhere, the Portland aluminium smelter in the south-west, underground gas storage near Port Campbell and gas transmission pipelines across the state add more pressure equipment and pipeline work. See power generation audit support and offshore audit support.

Aerospace and defence are where Victoria's link to US requirements is strongest. Boeing Aerostructures Australia at Fishermans Bend designs and builds composite structures for Boeing commercial aircraft and is the sole-source supplier of 787 moveable trailing edges; NDT is one of the site's core capabilities, and its local supply chain includes hundreds of businesses. Hanwha's Armoured Vehicle Centre of Excellence at Avalon, near Geelong, builds infantry fighting vehicles and self-propelled howitzers for the Australian Army. The Williamstown shipyard, Melbourne and Avalon airport maintenance, and a broad precision-manufacturing base complete the picture. Aerospace customers frequently flow down NAS 410 or their own NDT specifications rather than SNT-TC-1A alone, so check your purchase orders first. See aerospace audit support.

Victoria's regulatory framework differs from most other states because Victoria has not adopted the national model WHS laws. Workplace safety is administered by WorkSafe Victoria under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 and the OHS Regulations 2017, which require registration of designs for listed plant, including pressure equipment; Victoria's approach to registering individual items differs from the other states, so check WorkSafe's current guidance. Industrial radiography is regulated by the Victorian Department of Health under the Radiation Act 2005, which requires individual radiographers to hold a use licence and organisations to hold a management licence. High-pressure pipelines are licensed under the Pipelines Act 2005, must be designed, built and operated to AS 2885, and are overseen for safety by Energy Safe Victoria. Offshore Bass Strait facilities in Commonwealth waters fall under NOPSEMA. Confirm the current requirement with the regulator before mobilising.

Which NDT certification scheme applies in Victoria?

Direct answer: AINDT certification under ISO 9712 is the default for Victorian NDT technicians, AICIP certification applies to in-service pressure-equipment inspectors, and NATA accreditation applies to laboratories and inspection bodies. SNT-TC-1A is used where a customer requires it, typically US-linked aerospace, defence or US-code fabrication. Aerospace customers may require NAS 410 instead.

The schemes are not competitors so much as answers to different customers. An Australian refinery or utility will normally expect AINDT-certified technicians, AICIP-certified inspectors for pressure equipment and, for endorsed test reports, a NATA-accredited laboratory. A US aerospace prime expects its supplier to comply with its own NDT specification, which typically references NAS 410 and requires a Level III who stands behind procedures and techniques. A fabricator building ASME pressure vessels for a US-owned client may need technicians certified under the employer's own SNT-TC-1A written practice.

Direct answer: Atlantis provides the full Level III role for Victorian SNT-TC-1A programmes: written practice, procedure and technique-sheet approval, exams, certification records, audit readiness and day-to-day technical answers. Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: Atlantis writes SNT-TC-1A written practices for Victorian employers and audits existing ones against SNT-TC-1A and customer requirements. The goal is a written practice that matches the methods you perform and the customers you serve, and that an auditor can trace from document to technician to report.

Victorian written practices vary widely. A composites supplier needs UT methods suited to laminates and bonded structures, careful technique-sheet control by part number and a clear statement of how customer specifications override or add to SNT-TC-1A. A Geelong or Gippsland maintenance contractor needs UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT, PT and VT for pressure and piping work, with training and experience requirements a busy contractor can actually evidence. A small defence fabricator may need only MT, UT and VT for structural welds. Each is better served by a written practice built for it than by a borrowed template.

When we audit, we follow the evidence. We select technicians and trace each certification through training, experience, exams, grades and vision tests; we check that procedures and technique sheets carry valid Level III approval; and we look at how certificates from other employers and AINDT certifications are treated. The result is a prioritised list of findings and support while you close them. Background reading: written practice development, our SNT-TC-1A guide and the training requirements matrix.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Victoria

Direct answer: Victorian procedures must satisfy the governing code: ASME V with Section VIII or B31.3 on US-code pressure work, AS/NZS 3788 for in-service pressure equipment, AS 2885 or API 1104 on pipelines, AWS D1.1 or AS/NZS 1554 on structural steel, and customer specifications in aerospace and defence. Atlantis writes and approves procedures for ASME, API, AWS and customer-specified work.

  • Refining and terminals: thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD of piping and vessel welds, tank inspection to API 653 where the owner applies it, and procedures that handle hot surfaces and coatings.
  • Gas processing and offshore: corrosion mapping, weld inspection and decommissioning-related examinations under the operator's specifications. See pipeline audit support.
  • Power generation: boiler tubes, headers, high-energy piping and rotating plant during outages in the Latrobe Valley.
  • Aerospace composites: pulse-echo and through-transmission UT procedures, bond-line inspection, part-specific technique sheets and customer approval routes.
  • Defence land systems and shipbuilding: structural and armour weld inspection to Australian defence specifications and prime requirements. See shipbuilding audit support and fabrication audit support.
  • Infrastructure: bridges, tunnels and transport projects using structural steel welding standards. See infrastructure audit support.

Radiography procedures must remain consistent with the company's Radiation Act 2005 management licence and its radiographers' use licences; radiation safety stays with your licensed staff, while we cover technique, sensitivity and acceptance.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Victorian crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III gives a Victorian company a named ASNT Level III for its SNT-TC-1A programme without a full-time hire. It suits aerospace and defence suppliers needing continuous oversight of technique sheets, and maintenance contractors whose ASNT-specified work peaks with refinery turnarounds and power outages.

Two patterns dominate in Victoria. Manufacturers in the aerospace and defence supply chain need steady Level III involvement because technique sheets change with new parts, revisions and customer requests, and auditors expect evidence that the Level III reviews them. Maintenance contractors on the refinery, gas plants and power stations need intense support around shutdowns: certification checks before mobilisation, rapid technique-sheet approvals and answers to site questions. An outsourced Level III covers both patterns from one arrangement.

Interim Level III cover keeps your programme valid while you recruit, while your Level III is on leave, or when an audit arrives before a replacement does. You can choose an ongoing outsourced arrangement, a single project such as a written practice or procedure set, or an audit-preparation sprint, each scoped on a call and quoted on request. Discuss outsourced Level III cover for your Victorian team.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Atlantis prepares Victorian companies for customer and prime-contractor audits of their NDT special process, owner audits of SNT-TC-1A programmes and the NDT portion of quality-system audits, including Nadcap-style aerospace audits. We run a mock audit, prioritise the findings and support the fixes. The auditor makes the decision.

For aerospace and defence suppliers, auditors look at the written practice, each technician's file, current vision tests, Level III-approved procedures and part-specific technique sheets, equipment calibration and process control. For refinery and gas contractors, owners focus on certification validity, procedure compliance and report quality. In both cases the same few gaps recur: unsigned or outdated technique sheets, missing experience evidence, expired vision tests and procedures that cite superseded editions.

Atlantis is not a NATA assessor or a Nadcap auditor and does not hold NATA accreditation. We prepare documents and people; accreditation and approval remain with the accrediting body or customer. Arrange a pre-audit review for your Victorian programme.

Cities and regions we support across Victoria

Direct answer: Atlantis supports employers across Victoria, from Melbourne and Geelong to the Latrobe Valley, Gippsland and regional centres, remotely and onsite at the client's facility. Atlantis has no office or training centre in Victoria.

  • Melbourne: Boeing Aerostructures Australia at Fishermans Bend, the Williamstown shipyard, the Port of Melbourne, Altona terminals and a broad manufacturing base. See NDT consulting in Melbourne, NDT training in Melbourne, Practical NDT for Melbourne and third-party inspection in Melbourne.
  • Geelong and Avalon: Viva Energy's refinery, Hanwha's armoured vehicle centre, Avalon airport and advanced manufacturing.
  • Latrobe Valley: Loy Yang A and B, Yallourn and associated mining and maintenance.
  • Gippsland coast: Longford gas plants, Bass Strait support, and the offshore wind zone.
  • Hastings and Western Port: LPG and crude processing and port activity.
  • Portland and the south-west: aluminium smelting, port and gas storage.
  • Bendigo, Ballarat and regional Victoria: defence vehicle manufacturing, engineering and fabrication.

For the national picture, see NDT consulting in Australia.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: An engagement moves from a scoping call to a written scope and quote, a document review, delivery of documents, onsite work where needed and continuing Level III support for ongoing clients. Timing is agreed on the scoping call because it depends on scope, the state of your records and your deadlines.

  1. Scoping call: methods, customers and their flow-downs, codes, schemes in use and the date that matters.
  2. Written scope and quote: deliverables, remote and onsite elements and responsibilities.
  3. Document review: written practice, certification files, procedures, technique sheets, calibration and sample reports.
  4. Delivery: written practice, procedures, technique sheets, exams or audit findings, under revision control.
  5. Onsite work: practical exams on real specimens and audit support at your Victorian facility when required.
  6. Continuing support: approvals, questions, recertifications and updates as codes and customer requirements change.

Technician training is separate: ASNT SNT-TC-1A training, online NDT training and corporate NDT training. Practice before a practical exam is available on Practical NDT; it is practice only and does not replace an exam on real specimens.

Your Level III

Victorian engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, founder of Atlantis NDT. One named Level III handles your programme from the first call to the signed documents. More about Atlantis NDT.

Frequently asked questions

Who provides NDT Level III consulting in Victoria, Australia?

Atlantis NDT provides ASNT Level III services to Victorian employers, led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, delivered remotely and onsite at your facility.

Is this page about Victoria, Australia or Victoria, Texas?

This page covers the Australian state of Victoria. Atlantis serves other places called Victoria on separate pages.

Do Victorian aerospace suppliers need NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A?

It depends on the customer. Many aerospace primes flow down NAS 410 or their own NDT specification. Check your purchase orders; we design SNT-TC-1A programmes and prepare for customer audits, but we do not certify to NAS 410.

Can Atlantis certify technicians to AINDT or ISO 9712?

No. Atlantis does not certify or train to AINDT or ISO 9712. We support employer-based SNT-TC-1A programmes and help them work alongside AINDT-certified staff.

Is Atlantis NATA-accredited?

No. Atlantis does not hold NATA accreditation and does not issue NATA-endorsed reports. We support procedures and personnel records only.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Victoria?

Yes. Under the Radiation Act 2005, radiographers need a use licence and the organisation needs a management licence from the Victorian Department of Health. Confirm current licence conditions before work starts.

Does WorkSafe Victoria register pressure vessels?

WorkSafe Victoria requires registration of designs for listed plant, including pressure equipment, under the OHS Regulations 2017. Its approach to item registration differs from other states, so check current guidance. In-service inspection follows AS/NZS 3788.

Can you write procedures for the Geelong refinery or Gippsland gas plants?

Yes, for contractors working there. We write UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT and VT procedures and technique sheets to the governing code and the owner's specification, with Level III approval.

Can practical exams be done remotely?

No. Practical exams need the candidate, real specimens and the examiner together, so they are held onsite at your facility. Most other Level III work is remote.

Does Atlantis have an office in Melbourne or Geelong?

No. Atlantis has no physical office or training centre in Victoria; work is delivered remotely and onsite at the client's facility.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Victoria?

Quote on request. Cost depends on methods, ongoing versus project work, exam volume and onsite visits. Atlantis keeps its services affordable, accessible and fully customisable.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Western Australia

Short answer: Atlantis NDT gives Western Australian employers access to an ASNT NDT Level III, delivered remotely and onsite at the client's own facility. The work covers outsourced or interim Level III duties for ASNT SNT-TC-1A programmes, written practices and written-practice audits, procedures and technique sheets, qualification exams under the employer's written practice, and preparation for owner and customer audits. Every engagement is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, and every scope is quoted on request.

Let us be clear about the local picture first. In Western Australia, as in the rest of the country, most NDT technicians hold AINDT certification under the ISO 9712-based national scheme, and most inspection laboratories compete on NATA accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025 or ISO/IEC 17020. Atlantis does not certify personnel to AINDT or ISO 9712, does not hold NATA accreditation, and does not replace a NATA-accredited laboratory. What we do is narrower and, for a specific group of WA employers, very useful: we bring ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level III expertise and US-code experience (ASME, API, AWS) to companies that work for US-owned operators, US original equipment manufacturers, US defence programmes or projects specified to US codes. If that describes your work, ask for a Western Australia Level III quote.

Why Western Australian NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: Any WA employer that certifies its own NDT people under ASNT SNT-TC-1A needs a Level III who owns the written practice, approves procedures and examines staff. In Western Australia that usually means contractors serving LNG trains, Pilbara iron ore, Kwinana process plants, Henderson shipbuilding and the AUKUS submarine programme, where clients or specifications call for ASNT-based certification alongside, or instead of, AINDT.

Western Australia's inspection economy is shaped by distance and scale. The Pilbara iron ore system, run by BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue and Roy Hill, includes mines, rail, car dumpers, stackers, reclaimers, shiploaders and port infrastructure at Port Hedland and Dampier. Structural welds, crusher and conveyor components, rail wheels and axles, slew rings and wear plate all need MT, UT, PT and visual inspection, and the shutdown calendar drives demand for fly-in fly-out NDT crews.

The North West Shelf carries Australia's largest LNG concentration. The Karratha Gas Plant and Pluto LNG near Dampier, Chevron-operated Gorgon on Barrow Island and Wheatstone near Onslow, and Shell's Prelude floating LNG facility offshore each depend on weld inspection during construction and on corrosion monitoring, thickness surveys, tank inspection and pressure-equipment examination in service. Gorgon and Wheatstone are operated by a US-headquartered major, and many of their packages and vendors work to US codes such as ASME B31.3, ASME Section VIII and API 650/653 alongside Australian standards. That is where an SNT-TC-1A written practice and a Level III who knows US code requirements earns its keep.

South of Perth, the Kwinana industrial area hosts the former BP refinery site now operating as a fuel import terminal, chemical and fertiliser plants, nickel and lithium processing, and a cluster of fabrication and maintenance contractors. Alumina refining at Pinjarra and Wagerup, lithium hydroxide plants at Kwinana and Kemerton, the Collie power stations and the Greenbushes lithium operations add more pressure equipment, piping, tanks and rotating plant. In the Goldfields, Kalgoorlie's gold and nickel operations rely on mobile-equipment and structural inspection.

Defence is the fastest-moving piece. Henderson's Australian Marine Complex south of Fremantle hosts shipbuilders and fabricators, and HMAS Stirling on Garden Island is being prepared for Submarine Rotational Force-West, which is planned to rotate US Virginia-class and a UK Astute-class submarine through the base from 2027, with sustainment work at Henderson. Suppliers entering that supply chain can expect quality requirements set by the contracting authority, and some of them will reference US naval or ASNT-based personnel qualification. Confirm the exact requirement with the prime contractor before you build a programme around it.

Regulation in WA is state-based. Workplace safety, including registration of boiler and pressure-vessel designs and items of plant, sits with WorkSafe WA under the Work Health and Safety Act 2020 and the WHS (General Industry) Regulations 2022, with separate WHS regulations for mines and for petroleum and geothermal operations. Industrial radiography is licensed by the Radiological Council of Western Australia under the Radiation Safety Act 1975, which licenses radiographers and registers premises and equipment. Pipelines are designed and operated to AS 2885, onshore petroleum pipelines are licensed under the state Petroleum Pipelines Act 1969, and facilities in Commonwealth offshore waters fall under NOPSEMA. Confirm the current requirement with the relevant regulator before mobilising.

Which NDT certification scheme applies in Western Australia?

Direct answer: AINDT certification under ISO 9712 is the normal scheme for WA technicians, and AICIP certification is expected for in-service pressure-equipment inspectors working to AS/NZS 3788. ASNT SNT-TC-1A is an employer-based alternative that WA contractors use when a US-owned operator, US OEM or US-code specification asks for it. Many WA technicians hold both.

The three systems answer different questions. AINDT certification is central, third-party certification of an individual technician against ISO 9712: the technician sits examinations set by the certification body and holds a certificate in their own name. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice published by ASNT under which the employer certifies its own personnel according to its own written practice, with a Level III responsible for exams and procedures; the certification is valid only while the person works for that employer. AICIP certifies in-service inspectors and senior in-service inspectors who examine pressure equipment under AS/NZS 3788, and hazard level A and B equipment is generally expected to be examined by AICIP-certified inspectors.
