Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: An SNT-TC-1A written practice is the employer's own document describing how NDT personnel are trained, examined, certified and recertified. Atlantis writes new written practices for WA employers and audits existing ones against SNT-TC-1A and against what your clients' specifications actually require.

A good written practice is short enough to follow and specific enough to audit. It names the methods and levels the company certifies, the training and experience the employer requires for each, the exam structure, the eye examination, the role of the Level III, how outside agencies are used, how records are kept and when certification expires. It should also say how the company treats people who arrive with AINDT or other certificates, which matters in WA, where many technicians you hire will hold ISO 9712 credentials and a few will hold both.

We see three recurring problems in WA programmes. First, a written practice copied from another company, still naming methods the employer does not perform and missing the ones it does, such as PAUT corrosion mapping or TOFD. Second, training and experience requirements that do not match the reference tables in SNT-TC-1A or the client's specification, which is the first thing an auditor checks. Third, records spread across FIFO rosters, email and personal folders, so the company cannot prove who was certified for what on the date of a given shutdown. A written-practice audit catches all three and leaves you with a prioritised fix list. See written practice development and our SNT-TC-1A guide for more background.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Western Australia

Direct answer: A WA NDT procedure must satisfy the code the work is built to. On LNG and process plants that is often ASME V with ASME B31.3 or Section VIII acceptance criteria; on structural steel it is AS/NZS 1554 or AWS D1.1; on pipelines it is AS 2885 or API 1104; on in-service pressure equipment it is AS/NZS 3788. Atlantis writes and approves procedures for the US-code side of that list.

The useful distinction is between a procedure and a technique sheet. The procedure states the requirements of the governing code for a method: equipment, calibration, personnel, surface condition, scanning, sensitivity, recording and acceptance. A technique sheet applies the procedure to one component: probe, angle, wedge, focal law or film and source arrangement, reference block, scan plan and coverage. Auditors on US-code projects usually ask for both, and they ask to see Level III approval on each.

  • LNG and gas processing: ASME V and B31.3 for piping, Section VIII for vessels, API 650 and API 653 for tanks, client specifications for PAUT and TOFD in place of radiography, and Australian standards where the owner applies them.
  • Iron ore and mining: AS/NZS 1554 and AWS D1.1 structural welding, OEM requirements for mobile equipment, MT and UT of slew rings, pins, crusher shafts and conveyor pulleys. See Level III audit support for mining.
  • Pipelines: AS 2885 for gas and liquid petroleum pipelines in Australia, API 1104 on US-specified packages. See pipeline audit support.
  • Shipbuilding and defence: class-society rules, Australian defence specifications and, for US platforms, the requirements flowed down by the prime. See shipbuilding audit support.
  • Radiography: procedures must reflect the Radiological Council's licence conditions on the site; we cover the technique side, while radiation safety plans stay with your licensed radiation safety officer.

Outsourced and interim Level III for Western Australian crews

Direct answer: An outsourced Level III is a named, external ASNT Level III who carries the Level III responsibilities in your written practice without being on your payroll. For WA contractors with a mostly AINDT workforce and a handful of US-code clients, it is usually the most practical way to keep an SNT-TC-1A programme alive between projects.

WA shutdowns are intense and short. A contractor can go from a quiet month to forty technicians on a Karratha or Barrow Island turnaround in a week, and the client wants certification records, procedures and technique sheets before anyone is mobilised. An outsourced Level III works through that peak remotely: reviewing records, approving technique sheets, answering scanning and acceptance questions from site and signing what needs to be signed. When practical exams are needed, they are held onsite at the employer's facility in Perth or a regional base, with real specimens and the examiner present.

Engagement models are simple. An ongoing outsourced Level III arrangement keeps a named Level III attached to your programme. A project engagement covers a single deliverable, such as a written practice or a procedure set for one contract. An audit-preparation sprint focuses on the weeks before a known audit. Each is scoped on a call and quoted on request. Ask about an outsourced Level III for your WA crew.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Atlantis prepares WA NDT companies for owner and customer audits of their SNT-TC-1A programme, prime-contractor supplier audits and the NDT portion of quality-system audits. We check written practices, certifications, procedures, technique sheets, equipment calibration records and reports. The audit decision always stays with the auditor.

In practice, an owner's NDT audit samples a few technicians and a few reports and traces each one back: was this person certified in this method at this level on this date, against which written practice, using which approved procedure and technique sheet, with calibrated equipment? An audit-readiness review does the same sampling before the real audit, then gives you a list of findings in priority order. Typical fixes are missing Level III signatures, lapsed eye examinations, experience logs that do not add up, procedures without a revision history, and technique sheets that do not match the equipment used.

For laboratories and inspection bodies seeking or holding NATA accreditation, we can review NDT procedures and personnel records for consistency, but we are not a NATA assessor and do not offer accreditation consulting as a guarantee of outcome. For aerospace suppliers, we can prepare the NDT side of a customer or Nadcap-style audit. See LNG audit support and offshore audit support. Book an audit-readiness review for your WA programme.

Cities and regions we support across Western Australia

Direct answer: Atlantis supports employers across Western Australia, from Perth and Kwinana to the Pilbara and the Goldfields. Work is delivered remotely and onsite at the client's facility; Atlantis has no office or training centre in WA.

  • Perth and Fremantle: head offices of most WA inspection contractors, Henderson shipbuilding and fabrication. See NDT consulting in Perth, NDT training in Perth and the Practical NDT simulator for Perth.
  • Kwinana and Rockingham: process plants, fuel import terminal, lithium and nickel processing, and the HMAS Stirling and Henderson defence precinct nearby.
  • Port Hedland: iron ore export port, rail and processing infrastructure. See NDT consulting in Port Hedland.
  • Karratha and Dampier: the Karratha Gas Plant, Pluto LNG and iron ore port operations. See NDT training in Karratha and third-party inspection in Karratha.
  • Onslow and Barrow Island: Wheatstone and Gorgon LNG, served largely by FIFO crews.
  • Bunbury, Collie and the South West: alumina, lithium, power generation and port activity.
  • Kalgoorlie-Boulder and the Goldfields: gold and nickel mining and processing.

For the national picture, see NDT consulting in Australia.

How an engagement works

Direct answer: Engagements start with a short call, followed by a written scope and quote, a document review, the agreed deliverables, and onsite work only where it is needed. Timing depends on scope, the state of your records and your project dates, so we agree it on the call rather than promise a fixed turnaround.

  1. Scoping call: your methods, clients, codes, current certification scheme or schemes, and the deadline you are working to.
  2. Written scope and quote: deliverables, remote and onsite elements, and who in your team owns what.
  3. Document review: written practice, certifications, procedures, technique sheets and sample reports, shared securely.
  4. Deliverables: revised or new written practice, procedures, technique sheets, exam sets and an audit findings list, with revision control.
  5. Onsite work where needed: practical exams on real specimens, or audit support at your WA facility.
  6. Ongoing support: for outsourced Level III clients, continuing approvals, queries and recertification.

Training for your technicians is a separate service: see ASNT SNT-TC-1A training, online NDT training and corporate programmes. Practice before practical exams is available on Practical NDT, which is practice only and not a substitute for an exam on real specimens.

Your Level III

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. You deal with a named Level III, not a rotating call centre, and the same person signs the documents and answers the questions. Learn more about Atlantis NDT.

Frequently asked questions

Is ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification recognised in Western Australia?

It is recognised where a client or specification asks for it, which is common on US-owned LNG assets, US OEM supply chains and some defence packages. For most other Australian work, AINDT certification under ISO 9712 is the norm. Check your contract before deciding which scheme to use.

Can Atlantis certify my technicians to AINDT or ISO 9712?

No. Atlantis does not certify or train to AINDT or ISO 9712. We support SNT-TC-1A programmes, where the employer certifies its own personnel, and we can make your procedures and records work alongside AINDT certificates.

Is Atlantis NATA-accredited?

No. Atlantis does not hold NATA accreditation and does not issue NATA-endorsed reports. If your client requires a NATA-accredited laboratory or inspection body, you need one. We support procedures and personnel records only.

What does an outsourced Level III do for a WA contractor?

They act as the Level III named in your written practice: approving procedures and technique sheets, administering exams, reviewing certifications and supporting audits, without a full-time hire.

Can you write procedures for LNG plant inspections in Western Australia?

Yes. We write UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT and VT procedures and technique sheets to ASME V and the applicable construction code, aligned with the owner's specification.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Western Australia?

Yes. The Radiological Council of Western Australia licenses industrial radiographers and registers premises and equipment under the Radiation Safety Act 1975. Confirm current licence conditions with the Council before work starts.

Who registers pressure vessels in Western Australia?

WorkSafe WA registers plant designs and items of plant, including pressure vessels of hazard levels A, B and C under AS 4343, under the WHS (General Industry) Regulations 2022. In-service inspection follows AS/NZS 3788.

Can practical exams be done remotely?

No. Most Level III work can be remote, but practical exams need the candidate, real specimens and the examiner together, so they are held onsite at your facility.

Does Atlantis have an office in Perth?

No. Atlantis has no office or training centre in Western Australia; work is delivered remotely and onsite at the client's facility.

How much does Level III consulting cost in Western Australia?

Quote on request. Cost depends on the methods involved, ongoing versus project work, exam volume and any onsite visits. Atlantis keeps its services affordable, accessible and fully customisable.

Can you help a supplier preparing for AUKUS submarine work at Henderson?

We can prepare the NDT side of your quality system, including written practice, procedures and records, for a prime-contractor audit. The specific personnel-qualification requirement is set by the contracting authority, so confirm it with the prime first.

NDT Level III Consulting Services in Wyoming

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT NDT Level III services to Wyoming employers, delivered remotely and onsite at the employer's own facility: an outsourced or interim Level III of record, SNT-TC-1A written practices and audits, procedures and technique sheets, qualification exams under the employer's written practice, and audit preparation. Every engagement is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III, and every scope is quoted on request.

Wyoming is an energy state from one border to the other. The Powder River Basin around Gillette produces more coal than any other region of the country and also holds major oil and gas fields; Casper is the service centre for much of that activity. The southwest corner around Rock Springs, Green River, Kemmerer and LaBarge combines natural gas fields and processing plants with the world's largest known trona deposit and the soda-ash plants built on it. Refineries operate at Sinclair and Newcastle, and the Cheyenne refinery site has been converted to renewable diesel. Coal-fired power plants, uranium in-situ recovery operations, large wind farms, interstate gas pipelines and a new advanced reactor project near Kemmerer complete the picture. Wyoming's NDT contractors are typically small, mobile and spread thin across long distances, which is exactly where an outside Level III helps. This page sets out how. If you are ready, ask for a Wyoming Level III quote.

Why Wyoming NDT programmes need a Level III

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A requires every employer that certifies NDT personnel to have a Level III who owns the written practice, approves procedures and examines staff. Wyoming's operators, refiners, mines and pipeline companies audit their NDT contractors, yet most Wyoming inspection companies are too small to employ a full-time Level III, so an outsourced Level III is the practical answer.

Start in the northeast. The Powder River Basin's surface coal mines run fleets of haul trucks, draglines, shovels, conveyors, crushers and train loadout facilities, and maintaining them depends on magnetic particle and ultrasonic inspection of frames, booms, pins, shafts and weld repairs. The same basin produces oil and gas from horizontal wells, with gathering systems, compressor stations and processing plants that need weld inspection, ultrasonic thickness surveys and tank inspection. Power stations near Gillette and Glenrock add boiler tube inspection and high-energy piping work during outages. Casper is the base for many of the inspection and fabrication companies that serve all of this.

The southwest is gas and minerals. The Jonah and Pinedale fields, the Moxa Arch and the gas processing complex at LaBarge feed processing plants and the Opal hub, where interstate transmission pipelines begin. Sour gas, carbon dioxide and sulfur recovery make corrosion and cracking control a serious subject at these plants. Trona mines and soda-ash refineries west of Green River run heavy rotating equipment, kilns, calciners and pressure equipment that need MT, UT and visual inspection. Coal-fired plants near Point of Rocks and Kemmerer add utility work, and the TerraPower Natrium demonstration project near Kemmerer brings nuclear-grade construction quality requirements to the region.

Refining sits at Sinclair, in Carbon County, and at Newcastle, near the South Dakota line, with the Cheyenne site now producing renewable diesel. Uranium in-situ recovery operations in the Powder River and Great Divide basins, wind energy construction around Rawlins and Medicine Bow, F.E. Warren Air Force Base and the Union Pacific main line through Cheyenne, Laramie and Rock Springs round out the market.

Wyoming's regulatory picture differs from most states. Wyoming is an NRC Agreement State, but only for uranium and thorium milling and related source material, so industrial radiography using byproduct material such as iridium-192 remains licensed by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission; confirm X-ray equipment requirements and the current licensing authority before mobilising a radiography crew. Wyoming does not have the general state boiler and pressure vessel inspection rules found in most states and does not employ state boiler inspectors, so requirements come from locally adopted mechanical codes, insurers and owners' own programmes; confirm the requirement with the local authority and the owner. The Wyoming Public Service Commission is authorised by PHMSA for intrastate gas transmission, distribution, regulated gathering and LNG safety, while PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines directly. The Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission regulates wells, and mine operators answer to the Mine Safety and Health Administration. Where state rules are thin, owners' specifications and contracts carry more weight, and they are what NDT contractors are audited against.

Level III services for Wyoming employers

Direct answer: Wyoming employers most often need an outsourced or interim Level III, a written practice that fits a small mobile crew, procedures and technique sheets for oil and gas, mining and power work, qualification exams under their written practice, and preparation for owner audits. Most of the work is remote, with onsite visits for practical exams and audits.

Written practice development and audits

Direct answer: A written practice is the employer's document defining how NDT personnel are trained, examined, certified and recertified under SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis writes new written practices for Wyoming employers and audits existing ones so the document fits a small, mobile workforce and the owners it works for.

Small Wyoming contractors often run on a written practice that was written once and never revisited. Problems we look for include a practice that names a Level III who is no longer involved; methods listed that the company does not perform and techniques performed that the practice does not list, such as phased array on gas plant welds or eddy current on exchanger tubing; certification files without practical exam records; and experience claimed for technicians hired from other employers without documentation. Because Wyoming's state-level rules are lighter than many states', owners lean heavily on contractor documentation, and an outdated written practice is the first thing an owner auditor finds.

A written-practice engagement sets scope, training and experience requirements referenced to the current SNT-TC-1A edition, examinations and grading, vision examinations, certification and recertification, interrupted service, transfer of certification and the Level III's authority. For nuclear-related or other customer requirements such as ANSI/ASNT CP-189, we show where your practice changes. Training-hour figures come from the training requirements matrix. More: written practice development and the SNT-TC-1A guide. To start, request a written-practice review for your Wyoming company.

Procedures, technique sheets and code compliance in Wyoming

Direct answer: Wyoming procedures follow the governing code and the owner's specification: API 1104 with 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195 for pipelines; ASME B31.3 and Section VIII with API 510 and 570 at refineries and gas plants; API 650 and 653 for tanks; ASME Section I and B31.1 for power plants; AWS D1.1 for structures; manufacturers' requirements for mining equipment.

Procedure work in Wyoming falls into a few recurring groups:

  • Mining equipment. MT and UT on haul-truck frames and wheel motors, dragline and shovel booms, pins, shafts and conveyor components, with weld repair inspection to AWS D1.1. Procedures must deal with field conditions: coatings, grease, limited access and cold.
  • Gas processing and sour service. Weld inspection on plant piping and vessels, thickness monitoring, and techniques for detecting cracking in sour or carbon dioxide service. Technique sheets need clear acceptance criteria and reporting for integrity engineers.
  • Pipelines. Girth-weld radiography or automated UT to API 1104 and operator specifications, plus integrity dig inspection.
  • Refining and renewable fuels. Repair and alteration inspection, thickness monitoring and PAUT or TOFD on thick sections to support the authorised inspector.
  • Power generation. Boiler tube inspection, high-energy piping weld inspection and turbine component inspection during outages.
  • Wind energy. Weld and bolting inspection on towers and foundations, typically to the owner's or turbine manufacturer's requirements.
  • Cold and altitude. Winter temperatures and high-wind sites affect couplant, penetrant and magnetic particle product limits, calibration and safe access, and the procedure should address them.

We write procedures and technique sheets, review procedures supplied by others, and resolve conflicts between owner specifications, codes and your written practice. Sector notes: mining, pipeline, refining, petrochemical, power generation and nuclear.

We approve procedures, administer exams, answer field questions, review the programme annually and support you in owner audits. This suits contractors that need Level III authority through the ups and downs of coal, oil and gas activity.
  2. Project-based work. A defined deliverable: a new written practice, a procedure set for a new mine or gas plant contract, PAUT technique sheets, or an exam campaign before an outage.
  3. Audit-preparation sprint. A focused review before a known audit date, with a corrective-action list and support while you close it.

Wyoming's distances make remote work the default. Written practices, procedures, exam preparation and record reviews are all handled by video call and document exchange. Atlantis has no office or training centre in Wyoming. See interim NDT Level III, or discuss outsourced Level III coverage for your Wyoming programme.

Engagements are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, so you know exactly who approves your procedures and examines your people.

Audit readiness: customer, owner and accreditation audits

Direct answer: Wyoming NDT contractors are audited by mine operators, producers, gas processors, refiners, utilities and pipeline operators, often as part of prequalification, plus ISO 9001 or ISO/IEC 17025 assessors. Where state rules are light, owner audits are the main check, and a Level III review finds the gaps before the auditor does.

Typical findings: certifications issued under a superseded written practice; expired vision exams; practical exams with no specimen or grading record; procedures not approved by a Level III or tied to an outdated code edition; calibration records that do not match the instruments in reports; and technicians performing techniques outside their certification. Nuclear-related work near Kemmerer adds stricter document control and traceability expectations that a typical oilfield contractor may not be used to.

An audit-readiness engagement samples personnel files, procedures and reports, maps them to the written practice and the owner specification, and produces a prioritised corrective-action list, followed by support for the fixes. For aerospace or defence suppliers, we help with Nadcap-style audit preparation as context, while the audit itself belongs to the accreditation body; for laboratories pursuing ISO/IEC 17025, we help with the NDT technical content. See also fabrication and infrastructure audit support. Audit date set? Book a Wyoming audit-readiness call.

Inspection programme support for refineries, gas plants and tanks

Direct answer: At Wyoming refineries, gas plants and tank farms, API 510, 570 and 653 inspections are carried out and signed by the owner's authorised inspectors. Atlantis supports that work from the NDT side, with method selection, procedures, technique qualification and data quality. We do not provide authorised inspector certification training.

The quality of thickness data, weld inspection and tank floor scans depends on consistent measurement locations, techniques matched to the damage mechanism, and reports the authorised inspector can use. For sour gas plants in the southwest, technique choice for detecting cracking matters as much as thickness data. A Level III can help a contractor or owner standardise practice across crews and choose between conventional UT, PAUT corrosion mapping and profile radiography. See our API 510, API 570 and API 653 support pages.

Cities we support across Wyoming

Training covers Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. contentHtml:

NDT ERP Software for Inspection Companies in British Columbia

Short answer: The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies working in British Columbia. It holds technician certifications (CAN/CGSB-48.9712, SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 and others) with automatic expiry status, controls instrument calibration, dispatches crews to remote sites, captures reports offline and runs quoting through invoicing on one system. Implementation is remote and typically takes 2 to 4 weeks from kickoff, depending on how clean your existing records are. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Ask for a British Columbia demo.

British Columbia is an awkward province to run an inspection business in. The work is spread across a coastline, an interior plateau and a northeast gas field that are days apart by road, and much of it sits in places with no mobile signal. One week a crew is on a shipyard block in North Vancouver, the next it is at a gas plant north of Fort St. John, and the week after that a technician is on a pulp mill shutdown in the Interior. The paperwork follows them everywhere: certificates, calibration records, permits, timesheets and reports. This page explains what that means for the software you run the business on, what the Atlantis ERP actually does, and what you should ask any vendor before you sign.

The British Columbia inspection market: where the NDT work is

Direct answer: NDT demand in British Columbia comes from five clusters: the Lower Mainland (refining, pipeline terminals, ports and shipbuilding), Vancouver Island (naval and ship repair, pulp and paper), the North Coast (LNG and aluminium), the Northeast (Montney gas production and processing) and the Interior (mining, smelting, forestry and hydro). Each cluster has different clients, codes and paperwork.

Lower Mainland. The Burnaby refinery on Burrard Inlet is the province's main coastal refinery and a regular source of turnaround inspection work. The Trans Mountain pipeline ends at the Westridge Marine Terminal in Burnaby, and the expanded system that entered service in 2024 added tankage and loading infrastructure that will need in-service inspection for decades. The Port of Vancouver handles bulk, container and liquid cargo, and its terminals, cranes and storage tanks all need periodic NDT. Seaspan's Vancouver Shipyards in North Vancouver build federal vessels under the National Shipbuilding Strategy, which brings weld inspection to classification-society and government standards. Fabrication shops in Delta, Surrey and Richmond supply all of this, and they run their own MT, PT, UT and VT.

Vancouver Island. CFB Esquimalt is the home of the Royal Canadian Navy's Pacific fleet, and Seaspan Victoria Shipyards operates the Esquimalt Graving Dock for repair and refit work. Pulp mills on the island run digesters, recovery boilers and pressure vessels that need regular thickness surveys and weld inspection.

North Coast. LNG Canada's export terminal at Kitimat shipped its first cargo in 2025, fed by the Coastal GasLink pipeline from the Dawson Creek area. Rio Tinto's aluminium smelter in Kitimat and the Port of Prince Rupert add their own maintenance demand. Work here is often rotational, with crews flying in and staying in camps.

Northeast. The Montney formation around Fort St. John and Dawson Creek is the centre of BC natural gas production, with gas plants, compressor stations, gathering lines and pipelines that need construction and in-service NDT. Site C, BC Hydro's dam on the Peace River, added large steel and penstock fabrication work.

Interior. Prince George has a refinery, pulp mills and a rail and logistics hub. Highland Valley Copper near Logan Lake, the smelter at Trail and many smaller mines run crushers, mills, pressure equipment and structural steel that need inspection. Kamloops, Kelowna and the Okanagan have fabrication, light aerospace and maintenance shops.

For an inspection company, that map means long travel, mixed codes and clients who each want their own document pack. The software problem is not "can we write a report"; it is "can we prove, for any job on any date, that the right certified person used a calibrated instrument under an approved procedure, and can we bill for it correctly".

Who sets the rules for inspection work in British Columbia

Direct answer: Pressure equipment falls under Technical Safety BC and the Safety Standards Act, with CSA B51 as the construction code. Oil and gas pipelines and facilities are regulated by the BC Energy Regulator under the Energy Resource Activities Act, with CSA Z662 for pipelines. Interprovincial pipelines answer to the Canada Energy Regulator, and industrial radiography is licensed federally by the CNSC.

Technical Safety BC administers the Power Engineers, Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Safety Regulation, handles design registration (which leads to the Canadian Registration Number, or CRN) and oversees contractors who install, alter and repair regulated equipment. See our notes on Technical Safety BC compliance, CSA B51 and CRN registration. The boundary matters: equipment used in connection with a pipeline or facility as defined in the Energy Resource Activities Act is largely handled by the BC Energy Regulator rather than Technical Safety BC, so the same inspection company may answer to two provincial regulators in one week.

The BC Energy Regulator requires pipeline permit holders to follow the current edition of CSA Z662. Trans Mountain, as an interprovincial line, is regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator. Industrial radiography in every province is licensed by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission, and exposure device operators must hold CNSC certification; see CNSC compliance for inspection companies. WorkSafeBC enforces the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation on every site you send a crew to.

On the personnel side, the Canadian national scheme for NDT certification is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the national adoption of ISO 9712. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published the standard, closed on 1 April 2026; CAN/CGSB-48.9712 remains valid, but confirm the current certification body for your technicians' renewals. Many BC employers also run an ASNT SNT-TC-1A written practice for US-owned clients or US-code projects. Fabricators and inspection organisations that work under CSA W47.1 often need CSA W178.1 certification as an inspection organisation and W178.2 certified welding inspectors.

None of this is software certification. What it creates is an evidence trail. An auditor from a client, a regulator or a certification body will pick a job and ask who did the work, what their certification was on that date, which instrument they used, when it was last calibrated, and which procedure revision applied. Your ERP should answer that in minutes.

What operators and EPCs in British Columbia ask NDT vendors for

Direct answer: Before a BC operator or EPC lets your crew on site, expect a prequalification file (safety programme, insurance, often a contractor-management platform such as ISNetworld, Avetta or ComplyWorks), a personnel file showing current certifications, a calibration file for every instrument, and procedures approved by your Level III. During the job they expect daily reports, timesheets and a final report pack.

The pattern repeats across the province. A gas plant in the Montney wants radiography crews whose CNSC certification and dosimetry records are current, and wants to see the source container and vehicle paperwork. A shipyard wants UT and MT technicians certified to the scheme its class society and customer accept, with reports in its own format. A refinery turnaround wants dozens of technicians mobilised on a fixed date, all with valid site orientations, plus a daily record of what was inspected. A pulp mill wants thickness readings and weld inspection reports it can file against its own equipment records.

Each of those requests touches a different part of your business: HR, equipment, quality, operations and accounting. Most small and mid-sized BC inspection firms handle them with a mix of spreadsheets, shared folders, a reporting tool and accounting software. That works until the business grows past a handful of technicians or a client audit lands during a busy month. The Atlantis ERP puts those records in one place and connects them, so a certificate that lapses shows up at dispatch, on the timesheet and in the report, not just in a spreadsheet nobody opened.

What the Atlantis ERP does for British Columbia NDT companies

Direct answer: The Atlantis ERP covers technician certification tracking, NDT equipment and calibration control, crew dispatch, offline field reporting, procedures, quoting, timesheets and invoicing for inspection companies. The table maps typical BC needs to built-in features; anything not listed is configured during implementation.

Certification tracking for CGSB, ASNT and CNSC records

Direct answer: Each technician's certificates are stored as separate records with scheme, level, method, certifying body and dates. A CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certificate is recorded under the ISO 9712 scheme with the certifying body named; SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 certificates sit beside it. CNSC exposure device operator certificates can be recorded the same way so they get the same expiry warnings.

BC inspection firms often carry technicians with more than one certification. A UT technician may hold a CGSB Level 2 certificate for Canadian work and an employer certification under an SNT-TC-1A written practice for a US-owned client. A radiographer needs a CGSB or employer certification for the method and a CNSC certification to operate an exposure device. A welding inspector may also hold CSA W178.2. If those live in different spreadsheets, someone eventually misses a renewal.

In the Atlantis ERP, each certificate record holds the scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), the level (trainee, I, II or III), the method, the certifying body, the industry sector, issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT hours, training hours, whether the exam was passed, and attachments such as the scanned certificate. Status is computed automatically, so nobody has to remember to change it. Vision tests are recorded separately with near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic and expiry, because a lapsed eye exam can invalidate an otherwise current certification under many written practices.

The employee's NDT profile pulls this together: technician flag, highest level, methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry. Certificate templates per scheme let you set validity in months, whether a vision test or exam is required, and minimum OJT and training hours. Examination sheets record general, specific and practical scores against a passing score (70% by default, adjustable). Company-level certifications, such as your ISO 9001 certificate or CSA W178.1 certification, are tracked the same way with their own alert days, so the company's own paperwork does not lapse during a busy season.

Equipment, calibration and radiography logistics across the province

Direct answer: Every instrument, probe and accessory is tracked by serial number with its assigned person, condition, lifecycle stage and calibration status. Calibration records and certificates carry due dates and expiry alerts, and dispatch warns when someone assigns out-of-calibration equipment. Vehicles can be flagged as able to carry radioactive sources, with transport licence number and expiry.

Equipment in BC spends a lot of time in trucks and on aircraft. A flaw detector goes north on a crew truck, a probe gets damaged in a camp, a thickness gauge comes back from Kitimat missing its cable. The asset management app records each item's equipment type, asset tag, firmware, accessories and lifecycle stage (new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed). Issue and return go through supervisor and manager approval with condition recorded both ways, so you know when and where the cable went missing. Reservations stop two crews from booking the same phased array unit for overlapping jobs.

The maintenance log covers preventive and corrective work, repairs, cleaning, firmware updates and probe replacement, with condition before and after. Consumables such as couplant, penetrant, developer, magnetic particles and PPE are tracked with reorder levels and a low-stock flag, which matters when the nearest supplier is hundreds of kilometres from the job. Purchase orders can be linked to a specific equipment serial, and calibration labs can be recorded as vendors with an accredited-lab flag, accreditation number and expiry.

For radiography, the fleet app records vehicle purpose, whether the vehicle can carry radioactive sources, the transport licence number and expiry, and assignment to a project or driver with dates and mileage. Field operations: remote sites, rotations and offline reporting

Direct answer: Jobs are created as team assignments with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation dates, technicians and equipment are checked for clashes and validity at assignment, and reports are captured in an offline app that syncs when the crew is back in signal. Timesheets separate inspection, travel, standby and setup time for billing.

A typical Northeast BC job runs like this. The office creates a project with the client PO, site, methods, codes, scope and acceptance criteria. The dispatcher creates a team assignment, picks technicians from the availability calendar and assigns equipment by serial number. If a technician is on leave or already booked, the overlap is blocked; if a gauge is out of calibration, the dispatcher gets a warning. The job moves through planned, dispatched and in field. On site, the technician uses the offline field app to pick the method, fill the report, take photos and sign on screen. Drafts and photos stay on the device until it syncs at the hotel or camp.

The report then follows a draft, in progress, review, approved and sent workflow with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures, plus a third-party or authorized inspector name and signature where the client requires one. Seventeen report types are built in, including UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography, each with its own numbering sequence. Method-specific data is captured properly: probe calibration tables for UT, source, technique and IQI type and placement for RT, focal laws for PAUT, readings by direction for thickness surveys, and weld or job lines with defect type and orientation.

Timesheets record work type, method, site, client, equipment serial, billable flag and rate multiplier, and go through approval. Standby days at a gas plant waiting for a permit and travel days to Kitimat are recorded as what they are, which makes the invoice easier to defend. Field expenses and per diems go through the expenses app and can be re-billed to the job.

Compliance, reporting and data questions in British Columbia

Direct answer: The ERP holds the evidence auditors ask for: certificate status on the job date, calibration records, approved procedure revisions, signed reports and approved timesheets. It does not certify you to any standard. Hosting location, data residency and privacy questions for BC public-sector or Crown corporation clients are discussed during scoping.

Procedures live in a register with document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard (for example ASME Section V or a CSA standard), acceptance criteria and body text or an uploaded file. They go through draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published stages, with rejection reasons and approver reminders, and approved revisions are locked with a full revision history. An AI-assisted first draft is available, but your Level III still reviews and approves it. If you need outside Level III help with procedures or a written practice, see NDT consulting in Vancouver or NDT consulting across Canada.

Non-conformance and corrective action (NCR/CAPA) workflows can be set up during implementation to match your quality manual. Taxes, including GST and PST on BC invoices, are configured during implementation; the ERP is not presented as certified tax software, and your accountant should confirm the setup.

What the ERP does not do is also worth stating. It does not perform risk-based inspection or fitness-for-service assessments, it does not calculate API 510, 570 or 653 inspection intervals or corrosion rates, and it does not hold TML or CML databases for a client's plant. Those belong in the owner's inspection data management system. The Atlantis ERP runs the inspection company's side: people, equipment, jobs, reports and money. If you want inspection data shown on a 3D model, look at Digital Twin Reporting and Atlantis Digital Twins.

Implementation for a British Columbia inspection company

Direct answer: Implementation is remote and typically takes 2 to 4 weeks from kickoff; it depends on how clean your existing records are. The work is mainly loading technicians and certificates, equipment and calibration records, procedures, clients and report templates, then training your office and field staff.

The first step is a scoping call: how many technicians, which methods, which certification schemes, which clients need their own report formats, and what accounting system you run now. Then your data is collected. Certificates, calibration certificates and equipment lists are usually the slowest part, because they are spread across spreadsheets, email and paper files. A firm with one tidy spreadsheet per area moves quickly; a firm whose records live in several people's inboxes takes longer, and the timeline reflects that.

Configuration covers certificate templates per scheme, alert recipients and look-ahead days, report templates with your logo and each key client's format, invoice layout and taxes, and any NCR/CAPA workflow. Office staff are trained on dispatch, quoting and invoicing; technicians are trained on the offline field app, which is usually the quickest part because it follows the report forms they already know. Because everything is remote, the time difference does not matter and nobody has to fly to Vancouver or Fort St. John.

NDT ERP Software for Inspection Companies in Denmark

Short answer: The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies working in Denmark. It holds EN ISO 9712 certificates and ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 records for each technician with automatic expiry status, controls calibration on every instrument, plans crews for offshore wind, North Sea, refinery and power-plant work, captures reports offline and runs quotation, timesheet and invoice on one system. Implementation is remote and typically takes 2 to 4 weeks from kickoff, depending on how clean your existing records are. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Request a Denmark demo.

Danish inspection work swings between two very different worlds. On one side are the energy transition industries that Denmark is known for: offshore wind farms, turbine and blade factories, and the ports that service them. On the other side are the older energy assets that still need careful attention: North Sea gas and oil platforms, two refineries, combined heat and power plants and kilometres of district heating pipe. A Danish NDT company can easily send one crew to a monopile weld in a fabrication hall and another to a turnaround at a refinery in the same week, with different clients, different codes and different paperwork. This page looks at what that means for the system you run the company on.

Where NDT work comes from in Denmark

Direct answer: Danish NDT demand comes from offshore wind (Esbjerg and the west coast ports, turbine and blade manufacturing in Jutland), North Sea oil and gas, the Kalundborg and Fredericia refineries, combined heat and power and district heating, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and shipbuilding, ship repair and heavy fabrication.

Offshore wind and Esbjerg. The Port of Esbjerg is one of Europe's main bases for installing and servicing offshore wind farms, and Denmark has built offshore wind since the earliest projects in the 1990s. Vestas has its headquarters in Aarhus and Siemens Gamesa has major operations in Brande and a blade factory in Aalborg, so turbine components, towers and flanges are made and inspected in Jutland. Thor, a large wind farm off the west coast of Jutland, adds construction and later service work. Foundations, transition pieces and towers mean long seam and circumferential welds that need UT or PAUT, MT on attachments, and dimensional and visual checks, all with heavy documentation requirements from developers and certifying bodies.

North Sea oil and gas. Denmark's offshore fields are operated mainly out of Esbjerg, and the Tyra hub was rebuilt and brought back into production in 2024. Offshore platforms, risers, pipelines and topsides equipment generate in-service inspection campaigns that run on tight logistics: helicopter seats, bed space, permits and short weather windows.

Refining. Kalundborg Refinery, owned by Klesch, is Denmark's largest, and the Fredericia refinery is operated by Crossbridge Energy. Both run turnarounds and day-to-day inspection on vessels, exchangers, furnaces, piping and tankage.

Power, heat and industry. Large combined heat and power plants around Copenhagen, Aarhus and Kalundborg run boilers and steam systems, many converted from coal to biomass, and Danish cities are served by extensive district heating networks whose welded steel pipes need inspection when they are laid and when they are repaired. Kalundborg is also home to major pharmaceutical manufacturing, and pharma and food plants run stainless process piping and pressure equipment.

Maritime and fabrication. Denmark has a long shipping tradition and an active ship repair and conversion sector, including the yard at Lindø near Odense, which also serves offshore wind. Steel fabricators across Jutland and Funen build structures, pressure equipment and process skids for export.

What Danish clients and developers ask NDT vendors for

Direct answer: Expect requests for EN ISO 9712 certificates (and ASNT-based certification on US-owned or US-code projects), approved procedures, traceable calibration, method-specific reports in the client's format, offshore training and medical records, and often ISO/IEC 17020 or 17025 accreditation through DANAK.

Offshore wind developers and their EPC contractors run detailed quality plans. A weld inspection report on a transition piece is expected to name the procedure and revision, the technician and their certificate, the instrument and probe serial numbers with calibration status, the acceptance standard and the result, and it will be reviewed by the client and often by a third-party certifier. The same is true on North Sea platforms, where operators also want proof of offshore safety training and medical fitness before anyone gets a seat on a helicopter.

Pressure equipment work in Denmark sits under the Danish Working Environment Authority (Arbejdstilsynet), whose rules require periodic inspection of pressure equipment in use by an inspection body accredited by DANAK or another accreditation body in the European multilateral agreement. NDT companies often perform the testing that supports those inspections, which means the inspection body will look closely at your procedures, certificates and calibration evidence. New pressure equipment built for the European market falls under the Pressure Equipment Directive, which requires NDT personnel on category III and IV equipment to be approved by a recognised third-party organisation.

US-owned operators and suppliers, and projects built to ASME, API or AWS codes, often ask for ASNT-based certification under the employer's written practice. That is where Atlantis's background as an ASNT Level III-led consultancy helps; the ERP itself records whichever schemes your technicians hold.

What the Atlantis ERP does for NDT companies in Denmark

Direct answer: The Atlantis ERP handles technician certificates, vision tests, instrument calibration and issue, crew assignment, offline reports, procedures, quotations, timesheets and invoicing. Tracking EN ISO 9712 and ASNT certificates for Danish technicians

Direct answer: Every certificate is its own record, so an EN ISO 9712 Level 2 in UT and an SNT-TC-1A employer certification in UT for the same person are tracked separately with their own dates, attachments and alerts. Vision tests sit in their own records with their own expiry.

Danish NDT technicians usually hold EN ISO 9712 certificates from an accredited certification body, which may be in Denmark or elsewhere in Europe; PCN certificates are also common among technicians who have worked in the UK North Sea. Contractors working on US-code projects add employer-based certification under SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. Welding inspectors may hold international welding qualifications or CSWIP. The ERP holds all of them without pretending one is a substitute for another; which scheme a given client accepts is set in their contract.

Each certificate record holds scheme, level (trainee, I, II or III), method, certifying body, industry sector, issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT and training hours, exam result and attachments. Certificate templates per scheme set the validity in months, whether a vision test or exam is required, and minimum OJT and training hours. Vision tests record near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic and expiry, because a lapsed annual eye test can stop a technician from working even when the certificate itself is current.

The ERP's daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before a certificate or vision test expires, and timesheets warn when someone books time against a job while their certificate is not valid. That second check catches the case nobody plans for: a technician who was valid when the job was planned but whose certificate lapsed during a long offshore campaign. Menus for Expiring Soon and Expired give the quality manager a one-click list before every audit.

For companies that certify their own staff under an SNT-TC-1A written practice, the ERP stores exam sheets with general, specific and practical scores against a passing score. Writing the written practice itself is consulting work; see written practice development.

Radiography, pressure equipment and data rules in Denmark

Direct answer: Use of radioactive sources and X-ray equipment for industrial radiography is regulated by the Danish Health Authority's radiation protection function (often called SIS) under the Radiation Protection Act. Pressure equipment in use is regulated by Arbejdstilsynet with inspections by accredited bodies. GDPR and the Danish Data Protection Agency (Datatilsynet) govern personal data in technician records.

The ERP does not replace your radiation protection programme or your permits, but it holds the records that change daily. Employee profiles carry radiation safety training and dose badge numbers. Source-related equipment is tracked by serial number with issue, return and movement records. Fleet records show whether a vehicle may carry radioactive sources, its transport licence number and expiry, and which project and driver it is assigned to with dates and mileage.

For pressure equipment, Danish rules distinguish routine inspections and more thorough internal and external examinations at set periods, carried out by accredited inspection bodies. NDT companies supporting those examinations need fast retrieval: every report for a given client, site or item, with procedure and standard references, signed and approved. Reports in the ERP capture work order, request, drawing, WPS, contract, procedure and standard references, so they can be found by any of them.

Data residency and access rights are common questions from Danish clients and from employees' representatives. Where data is hosted, which roles can see medical and eye-test data, and how long records are kept are discussed during scoping and configured during implementation. If a public-sector client requires electronic invoices through NemHandel in the OIOUBL format, raise it during scoping; invoicing, Danish VAT and payment terms are configured during implementation.

A Danish-language interface for technicians or office staff is discussed during scoping. Most Danish NDT companies we would expect to speak to already work in English on offshore and export projects, but the question is worth asking early.

Offshore and wind logistics: equipment, crews and offline reports

Direct answer: Offshore and wind work punishes poor planning. The ERP blocks double-booking of people and instrument serial numbers, warns on out-of-calibration kit, tracks who has which instrument, and lets technicians report offline on a platform or in a turbine tower and sync later.

A campaign on an offshore wind farm or a North Sea platform usually means a fixed crew list, a fixed kit list and a narrow window. If a phased-array instrument is still booked to a fabrication job in Esbjerg, or one technician's medical fitness has lapsed, the campaign is in trouble before it starts. In the ERP, the technician availability calendar shows assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable days with overlaps blocked, and each technician shows utilisation, current assignment and next available date. Equipment reservations prevent clashes, and the issue workflow records who took which instrument, in what condition, with whose approval.

Calibration records carry provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, result and next due date. Consumables such as couplant, magnetic ink, penetrant and PPE are tracked with reorder levels so a crew does not reach the quay without them. The maintenance log records preventive and corrective work, cleaning, firmware updates and probe replacement with condition before and after.

Out at the asset, the installable offline field app works without signal: pick the method, record readings and indications, take photos, sign on screen and preview the PDF. Drafts and photos are stored on the device and synced when a connection returns. Reports then move through review and approval in the office, with reviewer and approver signatures, before they are sent to the client. For reporting in depth, see Digital Twin Reporting Software; to view inspection results on a 3D model of the asset, see Atlantis Digital Twins.

Implementation for a Danish NDT company

Direct answer: Implementation is remote and typically takes 2 to 4 weeks from kickoff. How long it really takes depends on how clean your records are: technician certificates, instrument and calibration lists, clients and sites, procedures and report templates.

We start with a scoping call that covers which apps you need, which certification schemes your staff hold, which clients dictate report formats, how you quote and invoice, and the data and language questions above. You send what you already have, even if it is messy: certificate spreadsheets, instrument registers, client lists and sample reports. Atlantis configures certificate templates per scheme, alert recipients and look-ahead days, report templates with your branding, quotation and invoice layouts, VAT and payment settings, and user access by role. Office staff, supervisors and technicians get short, role-based training, and the first live jobs run with support available.

The most common delay is certificate data: scanned certificates in email, expiry dates missing, two spreadsheets that disagree. Cleaning that up pays off immediately, because the alerts are only as good as the dates behind them. Larger groups with several business units or integrations agree a longer plan during scoping. See the implementation timeline for a step-by-step version.

Integrations: finance, client systems and field devices

Direct answer: The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections. Integrations are scoped per implementation, so you only build the links that save real work.

Danish inspection companies most often ask about two links. One is to an existing finance system, where approved invoices or timesheet totals are sent across so accounting can stay where it is. The other is to clients' maintenance systems: energy operators and large manufacturers often run SAP or Maximo, and receiving work-order numbers automatically, or returning report references, removes a lot of retyping. The REST API for field devices also exposes the jobs assigned to a technician, the equipment issued to them, report submission and sync. NDT ERP Software for Inspection Companies in Ireland

Short answer: The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies working in Ireland. It keeps PCN and other EN ISO 9712 certificates next to ASNT SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 records with automatic expiry status, controls instrument calibration, dispatches crews to pharma sites, the refinery, power stations and fabrication yards, captures reports offline and runs quoting through invoicing on one system. Implementation is remote and typically takes 2 to 4 weeks from kickoff, depending on how clean your existing records are. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Ask for an Ireland demo.

Inspection companies in Ireland have an unusual client mix. A large share of the work comes from US-owned pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device and semiconductor plants that bring American codes and American quality expectations with them, while the refinery, the power stations, the gas network and the fabrication shops work to European standards and Irish regulations. One technician may hold a PCN certificate for European work and an employer certification under an SNT-TC-1A written practice for a US client in the same month. The software you run the business on has to cope with both without anyone keeping a second spreadsheet. This page explains where the work is, what clients and regulators ask for, what the Atlantis ERP actually does, and what to check before you choose any system.

The Ireland inspection market: where NDT companies find work

Direct answer: NDT demand in Ireland clusters around Cork Harbour (refining, pharma, power), the Shannon Estuary (alumina, power, aviation), the greater Dublin area (pharma, data centres, semiconductors, power and gas), the Corrib gas terminal in Mayo, and fabrication and engineering shops spread across the midlands and the west. Each cluster brings its own codes, clients and document packs.

Cork Harbour. The Whitegate refinery, owned and operated by Irving Oil, is Ireland's only oil refinery, and it generates turnaround and in-service inspection work on vessels, exchangers, piping and storage tanks. Around the harbour, Ringaskiddy, Little Island and Carrigtwohill host one of Europe's densest clusters of pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturing. Those plants run stainless process piping, clean steam systems, reactors and pressure vessels, and their capital projects and shutdowns produce steady visual, borescope, penetrant, radiographic and ultrasonic work. Gas-fired power stations and the port add their own maintenance demand.

Shannon Estuary and the mid-west. The Aughinish alumina refinery near Askeaton is a large heavy-industry site with digesters, tanks, pressure equipment and structural steel. Moneypoint, ESB's large station on the Clare side of the estuary, and the Tarbert site across the water have long been sources of boiler and pipework inspection. Shannon Airport and the surrounding industrial zone support aircraft maintenance, component repair and engineering firms, and Ireland's role as a global aircraft-leasing centre means a steady flow of aircraft records and inspection work when aircraft move between lessees.

Greater Dublin and Leinster. Pharma and medical-device plants run from Dublin out to Kildare, Meath and Louth. The semiconductor campus at Leixlip and a long pipeline of data-centre projects need structural and piping weld inspection during construction. Dublin Bay has gas-fired generation at Poolbeg and Ringsend, and Dublin Port handles fuel and bulk cargo with tank farms that need periodic inspection.

West and offshore. The Corrib gas field feeds the Bellanaboy terminal in County Mayo. Gas Networks Ireland's transmission pipelines and the interconnectors to Scotland need integrity work. Offshore wind is at an early stage: Arklow Bank Phase 1 off Wicklow has operated for two decades, and larger east-coast and south-coast projects are moving through consenting and auctions, which should bring foundation, tower and port fabrication work over the coming decade.

For an inspection company, that map means mixed codes, travel between clusters and clients who each specify their own report format. The software problem is not writing one report. It is proving, for any job on any date, that a certified person used a calibrated instrument under an approved procedure, and then billing for it correctly.

What clients in Ireland ask NDT vendors for

Direct answer: Irish clients ask for current personnel certificates (usually PCN or another EN ISO 9712 certificate, and ASNT-based employer certification for US-owned sites), approved procedures, calibration certificates for every instrument, method-specific reports in their own format, safety documentation for site access, and often ISO/IEC 17020 or 17025 accreditation through INAB.

US-owned pharma and device manufacturers tend to run supplier qualification the way their US parent does. Expect requests for certification records with method, level, expiry and eye-test dates; procedure numbers and revisions on every report; equipment serial numbers matched to calibration certificates; and change control on anything that touches a validated system. Process piping on these sites is often built to ASME BPE and ASME B31.3, so ASME Section V references and ASNT-based certification come up regularly, even though the technician may also hold a PCN certificate.

The refinery, power stations and gas network tend to ask for EN ISO 9712 certification, procedures referencing EN and ISO standards, written schemes of examination for pressure systems, and permit-to-work and induction records before anyone is allowed through the gate. Fabricators building pressure equipment for the European market need NDT personnel who satisfy the Pressure Equipment Directive, which for category III and IV equipment requires NDT personnel to be approved by a recognised third-party organisation.

Accreditation matters too. Many Irish laboratories and inspection bodies hold ISO/IEC 17025 or ISO/IEC 17020 accreditation from the Irish National Accreditation Board (INAB), and some clients only buy from accredited providers. An ERP does not make you accredited, but it holds the evidence an assessor asks to see: competence records, calibration traceability, procedure control and report review. Atlantis itself runs an ISO 9001 quality system, so the document-control habits built into the ERP come from the same discipline.

What the Atlantis ERP does for NDT companies in Ireland

Direct answer: The Atlantis ERP covers technician certification tracking, NDT equipment and calibration control, crew dispatch, offline field reporting, procedure control, quoting, timesheets and invoicing. Certification tracking for PCN, EN ISO 9712 and ASNT side by side

Direct answer: Each certificate is a separate record with its own scheme, level, method, certifying body and dates, so a PCN UT Level 2 certificate and an SNT-TC-1A employer certification for the same technician sit side by side with separate expiry tracking. Vision tests are recorded separately with their own expiry.

Ireland does not run a national NDT certification body of its own in the way some countries do, so Irish technicians commonly hold PCN certificates issued through BINDT or certificates from other EN ISO 9712 certification bodies elsewhere in Europe. Technicians who work for US-owned clients, or who have worked in the United States, often also hold employer certification under an SNT-TC-1A written practice or a CP-189 programme. CSWIP welding inspection certificates are common on fabrication and construction work. The ERP records all of these; it does not certify anyone and it does not decide which scheme a client will accept.

Each certificate record holds the scheme, level (trainee, I, II or III), method, certifying body, industry sector, issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT hours, training hours, whether the exam was passed, and the scanned certificate as an attachment. Certificate templates per scheme hold the validity period in months, whether a vision test or exam is required, and the minimum OJT and training hours, so a new record follows the rules you set for that scheme. Vision tests are recorded with near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic, certificate file and expiry.

For employer-based certification under SNT-TC-1A, the ERP also stores examination sheets with general, specific and practical scores against a passing score, so your Level III can see the exam evidence behind each certification. The employee NDT profile shows the highest level held, the methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry. That last group matters in Ireland because radiography work is licensed by the EPA and clients want to see dose monitoring and training records before a source arrives on site.

If your company needs help writing or updating an SNT-TC-1A written practice for US-client work, that is a consulting service rather than an ERP feature; see employer certification programmes and written practice development. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A based only; we do not train toward PCN or other ISO 9712 certificates, but the ERP stores them.

Compliance, regulators and data questions in Ireland

Direct answer: Industrial radiography in Ireland is authorised by the Environmental Protection Agency under the Radiological Protection Act 1991 and the Ionising Radiation Regulations 2019. Pressure systems in use fall under the Health and Safety Authority's general application regulations, and new pressure equipment under the EU Pressure Equipment Directive. GDPR applies to every technician record you hold.

The EPA is the national regulator for ionising radiation and uses a graded system of registration and licensing; higher-risk practices such as industrial radiography need a licence, and transport of radioactive sources must also be authorised. An inspection company's radiation protection paperwork lives partly outside the ERP, but the ERP can hold the parts that change with people and equipment: radiation safety training and badge numbers on each employee profile, source-related equipment by serial number with movement records, and vehicles flagged as able to carry radioactive sources with transport licence numbers and expiry dates in the fleet app.

The Health and Safety Authority enforces the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work (General Application) Regulations, which include the pressure systems requirements for written schemes and examinations by a competent person. NDT companies usually support those examinations rather than act as the competent person, so the useful ERP features are the references captured on each report (work order, request, drawing, procedure and standard numbers) and the ability to pull every report for one asset or one client quickly when an examination is due. The Pressure Equipment Directive governs equipment placed on the market, and fabricators need NDT personnel approval records for higher-category equipment; the certificate register keeps those approvals with their certifying body and dates.

Data protection is a real question in Ireland, where the Data Protection Commission is the regulator and many clients have strict supplier rules. Technician records include personal data such as eye tests, medical fitness dates and dose badge numbers. Where your data is hosted, who can access it, and retention rules are discussed during scoping, and the access rights for each role are configured during implementation. We do not promise a particular hosting location on this page; ask the question on your demo call and get the answer in writing.

VAT invoicing is set up for your company during implementation. Taxes, payment terms and reminders are configured per country, so invoices carry the details your accountant and Revenue expect; confirm any specific e-invoicing format a public-sector client requires during scoping.

Equipment, calibration and field reporting across Irish sites

Direct answer: Every flaw detector, probe, yoke, thickness gauge and source-related item is tracked by serial number with its calibration status, the person it is issued to and its condition. The offline field app lets technicians write reports where there is no signal and sync later.

Irish NDT companies often run a modest pool of instruments across a lot of sites, which is exactly when kit goes missing or goes out on a job a week past its calibration date. In the asset management app, each item carries its equipment type, assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories, lifecycle stage (new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed), calibration frequency and status. Equipment is issued and returned through a workflow with supervisor and manager approval, and condition is recorded both ways. Reservations prevent two crews booking the same phased-array set for overlapping jobs, and inbound and outbound movements are recorded.

Calibration records hold the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, whether the lab is accredited, the result and the next due date, and the calibration certificate register holds the lab's accreditation number and the PDF with valid, expiring and expired status. When a supervisor assigns a gauge that is out of calibration to a job, the team assignment shows a warning. Consumables such as couplant, penetrant, developer, magnetic ink and PPE are tracked with reorder levels and a low-stock flag.

On site, technicians use the installable offline app: pick the method, enter readings, take photos, sign on screen and preview the PDF. Drafts and photos stay on the device until there is a connection. The ERP supports 17 report types, including UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography, each with its own numbering. Reports move from draft to in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures and a field for a third-party or authorised inspector. For more on report design, see Digital Twin Reporting Software and where Excel reporting breaks.

Implementation for an Irish inspection company

Direct answer: Implementation is remote and typically takes 2 to 4 weeks from kickoff. The main variable is how clean your existing records are: technician certificates, instrument lists with calibration dates, client lists and report templates. Atlantis configures the system to your process rather than asking you to change it.

A typical sequence looks like this. First, a scoping call to agree which apps you need, which certification schemes you hold, which report formats your top clients demand, and how you invoice. Second, data collection: a spreadsheet of technicians and certificates, an instrument register with serial numbers and calibration dates, a client and site list, your procedure index and sample reports. Third, configuration: certificate templates per scheme, alert recipients and look-ahead days, report templates with your logo, quotation and invoice layouts, and VAT and payment settings. Fourth, a short training session for office staff, supervisors and technicians, followed by a first live job with support on hand.

If your certificate records are scattered across email attachments and three different spreadsheets, cleaning them up is the slowest step, and it is worth doing anyway. If you already have tidy registers, the 2-week end of the range is realistic. Larger companies with several divisions or complex integrations take longer; that is agreed during scoping, not discovered later. See the implementation timeline page for a more detailed plan.

Local-language interface questions do not usually arise in Ireland because work is done in English, but if you run crews with other first languages, the options are discussed during scoping.

Integrations with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite and QuickBooks

Direct answer: The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections. Each integration is scoped per implementation, so you build only the connections you actually need.

The common integration requests from Irish inspection companies fall into three groups. The first is accounting: some companies keep their existing finance package and want approved invoices or timesheet totals pushed across. The second is client systems: large pharma and energy clients often run SAP or Maximo for work orders, and an inspection company may want to receive work-order numbers or return report references automatically rather than retyping them. The third is field devices: the ERP's REST API for field devices exposes the jobs assigned to a technician, the equipment issued to them, report submission and sync. Integrations are scoped, built and tested during implementation. See the integration matrix for what is typically exchanged with each system.
