Running an NDT company in Western Australia is a logistics business as much as an inspection business. Much of the work sits more than 1,500 km north of Perth by road, on LNG trains and iron ore plant, out in the Goldfields on processing plant and pipelines, offshore on platforms and floating facilities, and close to home in the Kwinana industrial strip and the Henderson shipyards. Technicians rotate on swings, flights and site inductions have to line up, and a single expired certificate or an instrument that slipped past its calibration date can stop a crew at the gate after the company has paid to fly them there. The software you run the business on has to know who is certified for what, which equipment is fit to go, where everyone is, and what each day on site should be billed at. This page covers where the work is in WA, what operators and principal contractors ask for, what the Atlantis ERP actually does, and what to check before you choose any system.

The Western Australia inspection market: where NDT companies find work

Direct answer: NDT demand in Western Australia clusters in the Pilbara (LNG, iron ore, ports), offshore in the Carnarvon and Browse basins, in the Goldfields and Wheatbelt (gold, nickel, lithium and processing plant), along the Kwinana and Rockingham industrial strip south of Perth, at the Australian Marine Complex in Henderson, and across the South West alumina and lithium belt. Each area brings different clients, codes and logistics.

The Pilbara and the North West Shelf. Karratha and Dampier sit beside the North West Shelf project's Karratha Gas Plant and the Pluto LNG facility. Further west, the Wheatstone plant near Onslow and the Gorgon plant on Barrow Island process gas from the Carnarvon Basin. Those plants carry large inventories of pressure vessels, heat exchangers, cryogenic and high-pressure piping and storage tanks, and their shutdowns pull in UT thickness, PAUT, TOFD, radiography, MT, PT and visual teams by the planeload. Port Hedland, the world's largest bulk export port by tonnage, and the iron ore rail and port networks around it generate structural, weld and lifting-equipment inspection work on stackers, reclaimers, ship loaders, conveyors and car dumpers, with mine-site processing plant inland at Newman, Tom Price and Paraburdoo.

Offshore. Platforms, subsea infrastructure and floating facilities in Commonwealth waters off the north-west coast are regulated by NOPSEMA and are supported from Perth, Karratha, Dampier and Broome. Offshore campaigns bring rope access NDT, coating and corrosion surveys, and tight requirements on who goes offshore with which tickets.

The Goldfields and the lithium belt. Kalgoorlie-Boulder anchors the gold industry, with processing plants, tanks, pipelines and mobile plant that need regular inspection. Nickel operations in the region were placed in care and maintenance in late 2024, and lithium processing at Kwinana and Kemerton has been through curtailments as prices fell. For an NDT company this means demand that swings from site to site, which is exactly where clean scheduling and quick re-quoting matter.

Kwinana, Rockingham and Henderson. The Kwinana Industrial Area south of Perth holds a fuel import terminal on the site of the former refinery, alumina, chemical and fertiliser plants, power generation and port facilities. Next door, the Australian Marine Complex at Henderson hosts shipbuilding, naval sustainment and heavy fabrication yards, where weld inspection to class-society rules and defence quality requirements is routine. Perth's own metropolitan workshops supply skids, pressure vessels, structural steel and modules for the north.

The South West. Alumina refineries around Pinjarra and Wagerup, power stations near Collie, and the port of Bunbury add another cluster of shutdown and in-service inspection work within driving distance of Perth.

The digital twin page for Australia covers how inspection results from these plants can be shown on a 3D model; this page is about running the inspection company itself.

What WA operators and principal contractors ask NDT vendors for

Direct answer: Western Australian clients expect proof of personnel certification (usually AINDT under ISO 9712, sometimes ASNT-based employer certification for US-owned or US-code projects), current radiation licences, NATA-traceable calibration certificates, approved procedures, site-specific inductions and medicals, and inspection reports in the client's format on time. A vendor who cannot produce these quickly loses the gate or the next tender.

The requirement lists look similar across the big LNG operators, the iron ore majors and the EPC and maintenance contractors who manage shutdowns for them:

  • Personnel competence. Certificates by method and level, usually AINDT certification under ISO 9712. Projects built or owned by US-linked operators, US OEM equipment packages and some offshore scopes may instead ask for qualification under an employer written practice based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. Many WA technicians hold both.
  • Radiation. Industrial radiographers in WA must be licensed by the Radiological Council under the Radiation Safety Act 1975, and the company needs registration of its sources and apparatus. Clients ask to see licences, dosimetry arrangements and transport documentation before a source comes on site.
  • Calibration. Certificates for flaw detectors, thickness gauges, yokes, light meters and reference blocks, typically from NATA-accredited laboratories, with a visible next-due date.
  • Procedures and techniques. Approved, revision-controlled procedures referencing the applicable Australian standards (for example AS 3978 for NDT of pressure equipment, AS/NZS 1554 for structural welding, AS 2885 for pipelines) or ASME Section V for US-code equipment.
  • Site readiness. Inductions, medicals, drug and alcohol testing and site access cards, plus the contractor management and prequalification systems each principal uses.
  • Reporting. Reports in the client's template, signed off by the right level, delivered fast enough for the shutdown schedule, with a clear acceptable or not-acceptable result.

Plant registration and in-service inspection of pressure equipment in WA is regulated by WorkSafe WA under the Work Health and Safety (General) Regulations 2022, with AS/NZS 3788 the normal reference for in-service inspection. Your NDT results feed those programmes; the inspection planning itself sits with the owner and its registered inspectors.

Direct answer: The Atlantis ERP brings technician certificates, equipment and calibration, procedures, crew dispatch, field reports, timesheets, quotations and invoices into one system, so an office in Perth can see who is certified, what equipment is fit to fly north, where every crew is and what every job should be billed. Direct answer: Each technician can hold any number of certificate records. An AINDT certificate is recorded under the ISO 9712 scheme with AINDT as certifying body; an employer certification under an SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 written practice is recorded under its own scheme. Each record carries method, level, sector, dates, hours and attachments, and its status is computed automatically.

That matters in WA because the same person often works under both systems. A Level 2 UT technician might hold AINDT certification for most of the year, then join a crew on an offshore or US-code package where the client wants qualification under the contractor's ASNT-based written practice. Without a single record per certificate, the office ends up checking two spreadsheets and a pile of scanned cards every time a crew list is sent.

In the Atlantis ERP each certificate record holds:

  • Scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level (trainee, I, II, III), method and industry sector.
  • Certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT hours, training hours, exam passed and attached copies.

Vision tests are tracked separately, with near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic, certificate file and expiry. Certificate templates per scheme set validity in months, whether a vision test or exam is required, and minimum OJT and training hours.

The employee NDT profile also records radiation safety training and the radiation badge number. A daily check creates warning tasks 90 days before any certificate or vision test expires, and configurable daily email alerts go to the people you choose. Timesheets warn when a technician's certificate is not valid, which catches problems before they reach an invoice. Radiographer licence copies issued by the Radiological Council can be attached to the technician record; a dedicated licence field with its own alert is configured during implementation if you want one.

If your company qualifies technicians under an ASNT-based written practice and needs help writing or auditing it, see written practice development. Atlantis training covers ASNT SNT-TC-1A methods only; it does not train toward AINDT certification.

Equipment, calibration and the long haul north

Direct answer: Every flaw detector, probe, gauge, yoke, source-related item and vehicle is tracked by serial number with lifecycle status, assigned person and calibration status. Calibration certificates from NATA-accredited laboratories are held with certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty and next due date, and expiry alerts go out before anything ships north.

In a WA company the expensive mistake is flying an instrument to the Pilbara and finding on site that its calibration expired last week. The ERP prevents that in three ways: calibration status sits on every equipment record, team assignments warn when assigned equipment is out of calibration, and the calibration certificate register shows valid, expiring and expired certificates with expiry alerts.

  • Equipment records: equipment type, assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories and lifecycle (new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired, disposed). Rental rates can be recorded when you hire kit to or from others.
  • Calibration records: provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, pass, fail or conditional result, next due date and the PDF certificate with the lab's accreditation number.
  • Maintenance log: preventive, corrective, repair, cleaning, firmware update and probe replacement entries with condition before and after.
  • Consumables: couplant, penetrant and magnetic particle chemicals, film or plates, PPE and stationery with reorder levels and low-stock flags, so a crew does not leave Perth short.
  • Purchasing: vendor types (OEM, dealer, calibration lab) with an accredited-lab flag, accreditation number and expiry, and order lines linked to a specific equipment serial.
  • Fleet: vehicles marked as able to carry radioactive sources, with transport licence number and expiry, and vehicle assignment to a project or driver with dates and mileage.

Company-level accreditations and licences, such as your NATA accreditation, ISO 9001 certificate or radiation registration, can be recorded as company certifications with their own alert days.

Crew dispatch for FIFO rosters, shutdowns and offshore campaigns

Direct answer: Jobs are team assignments with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates. The availability calendar blocks overlaps, so a technician on R&R, in training or already on another shutdown cannot be booked twice, and the same applies to equipment serial numbers.

FIFO work makes scheduling harder than in a city practice. Swings are often fixed, so days off are known weeks ahead, while shutdown dates move with the operator's plan. Entering rostered days off as leave or unavailable in the availability calendar means the dispatcher sees who is genuinely free, and the system will not let anyone build a crew list that relies on someone who is flying home that day. Each technician shows status, current assignment, utilisation percentage and next available date, with calendar, kanban and list views for the people who plan the work.

Project records carry the client PO, contract, methods, codes, scope, acceptance criteria, assigned equipment and technicians, plus safety induction and work permit fields. Tasks carry method, technician, component, result, indication and defect counts, and the procedure and WPS references. That gives a shutdown coordinator in Perth a live picture of what has been inspected, what is waiting for review, and what has been sent to the client.

Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), method, billable flag, rate multiplier, site, client and equipment serial, and they go through approval. Travel days and weather or permit standby are where WA companies quietly lose money; recording them properly and feeding them into invoicing is a simple fix.

Field reporting from sites with no signal

Direct answer: The offline field app is an installable web app that works without signal, stores drafts and photos on the device and syncs when a connection returns. Reports then move through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures.

Mine sites, remote pipeline corridors and offshore facilities often have no usable connection where the technician is working. The field app gives a method picker, photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview, so the report can be drafted at the component and finished at camp. Report types cover UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday and coating, and computed radiography, each with its own numbering sequence. Method-specific fields include the UT probe calibration table, RT source, technique and IQI details, MT technique and particle type, PT method and developer, PAUT focal laws and UT thickness readings by direction.

Marine mode helps the Henderson yards and offshore scopes: a vessel cover page and photo, inspection location and dates, and a PDF that merges the classification-society certificate, the inspector's Level II certificate and the calibration certificate. For the reporting product on its own, see Digital Twin Reporting Software.

Compliance, regulators and data questions in Western Australia

Direct answer: The ERP helps you keep the records WA regulators and clients ask about, but it does not make you compliant on its own. GST and BAS reporting, payroll and e-invoicing settings are configured during implementation. Where your data is hosted and data residency requirements are discussed during scoping.

The regulators an NDT company in WA deals with most:

  • Radiological Council of Western Australia: licensing of industrial radiographers and registration of sources and apparatus under the Radiation Safety Act 1975.
  • WorkSafe WA: work health and safety, plant and pressure equipment registration under the Work Health and Safety (General) Regulations 2022.
  • Mines safety: the Work Health and Safety (Mines) Regulations 2022 for work on mine sites, administered by the state's mines safety regulator.
  • NOPSEMA: offshore petroleum safety in Commonwealth waters.
  • NATA: accreditation of testing and inspection bodies to ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO/IEC 17020, which many clients require of the labs and companies they use.

Australian tax settings, GST on invoices, BAS-ready reporting and Peppol e-invoicing if your clients want it are configured during implementation. NDT Inspection Services in Alabama

In brief: Atlantis NDT provides non-destructive testing to refineries, chemical plants, steel mills, shipyards, paper mills, utilities, aerospace manufacturers and pipeline operators throughout Alabama. The service list covers UT thickness and corrosion surveys, PAUT and TOFD weld inspection, radiography performed by radiography crews licensed in Alabama, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual and eddy current testing, and the NDE behind API 510, API 570 and API 653 inspections. Technicians are ASNT-certified, procedures are approved by an ASNT NDT Level III, crews travel to your site, and every job closes with a code-referenced digital report.

Alabama packs an unusual range of inspection work into one state. Mobile Bay combines a deep-water port, Navy shipbuilding, commercial aircraft assembly, a refinery, a chemical corridor and a major steel complex. Birmingham still makes iron and steel products and cast pipe. The Tennessee Valley around Huntsville and Decatur builds rockets and engines, runs chemical and steel plants and hosts a three-unit nuclear station. In between are paper mills, coal mines, auto assembly plants and the fuel pipelines that carry Gulf Coast products to the eastern seaboard. Each of these sectors works to different codes and different customers. The sections below map that market, explain who regulates what in Alabama, and describe how Atlantis scopes and reports a job. If you are ready to price a job, send your Alabama inspection request.

Where inspection work is in Alabama

Direct answer: Alabama inspection demand concentrates in the Mobile Bay industrial area (port, shipyards, refinery, chemical plants, steel and aircraft assembly), the Birmingham iron, steel and pipe district, the Tennessee Valley around Huntsville, Decatur and the Shoals, the Tuscaloosa and Black Warrior Basin area, central Alabama's auto and paper belt, and the Wiregrass in the southeast.

Mobile Bay: port, shipyards, refinery and chemicals

The Port of Mobile handles coal, steel, containers and liquid bulk, and the land around it is the densest inspection market in the state. Austal USA builds naval vessels on the Mobile River, where weld inspection follows Navy requirements such as NAVSEA Technical Publication 271 for NDT and MIL-STD-2035 for acceptance rather than commercial codes. Airbus assembles commercial aircraft at Brookley, with aerospace NDT flowed down from the manufacturer. A refinery at Saraland north of Mobile, chemical plants along the river corridor at Axis, Bucks and McIntosh and in the Theodore industrial area south of the city, terminals and tank farms, and Alabama Power's Plant Barry generate classic mechanical-integrity work: CML thickness surveys, weld examination on repairs and tie-ins, tank inspections and exchanger work. AM/NS Calvert's large steel processing complex north of Mobile adds crane, rolling-line and structural inspection. Salt air, heat and humidity make atmospheric corrosion and CUI the default damage mechanisms on the coast, and hurricane season puts a premium on post-storm structural and tank checks.

Birmingham: iron, steel and pipe

Birmingham was built on iron and steel, and the district still has electric-arc steelmaking and tubular operations at Fairfield, bar and rebar mills, and cast iron and ductile iron pipe foundries such as American Cast Iron Pipe Company and McWane. Inspection there means UT and MT on crane runways, ladles, rolling-mill and pipe-mill components, foundry casting inspection, and weld inspection on structural steel and equipment repairs to AWS D1.1. Coal-fired and gas-fired generating stations west and south of the city, including Plant Miller and Plant Gaston, need boiler tube, header and high-energy piping NDE during outages.

Tennessee Valley: Huntsville, Decatur and the Shoals

Huntsville is the state's aerospace and defence capital, with NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center and the Army at Redstone Arsenal, rocket-engine and launch-vehicle production nearby (including Blue Origin's engine plant in Huntsville and United Launch Alliance's factory in Decatur), and a large vehicle assembly plant at Mazda Toyota Manufacturing. Aerospace and space hardware is inspected to customer and agency requirements such as NASA-STD-5009 and NAS 410-based personnel certification, which is specialist work controlled by the prime. Decatur's riverfront is industrial: chemical and fibre plants, a Nucor steel mill and barge terminals on the Tennessee River, all generating vessel, piping, tank and structural scopes. The Browns Ferry nuclear plant near Athens, operated by TVA, runs its NDE under ASME Section XI and owner programmes, and TVA's dams and hydro plants along the river need structural and mechanical inspection. The Shoals area around Florence and Muscle Shoals adds metals, manufacturing and power generation.

Tuscaloosa and the Black Warrior Basin

Tuscaloosa County has a refinery, Mercedes-Benz's Vance assembly plant and its supplier base, and metallurgical coal mining in the Black Warrior Basin, where coalbed methane gathering lines and compression also operate. The refinery generates standard API 510/570/653 scopes; mining and preparation plants need structural, conveyor and heavy-equipment inspection; and suppliers need weld and component NDT.

Central Alabama and the Black Belt: auto, paper and power

Montgomery hosts Hyundai's assembly plant and Maxwell Air Force Base, and the region from the Black Belt to the Coosa and Alabama rivers is home to many of the state's pulp and paper mills. Mills are a distinct inspection specialty: digesters, recovery boilers, power boilers, black liquor and chemical recovery piping, and bleach plant equipment all need thickness surveys, weld inspection and crack detection during annual outages. Hydroelectric dams on the Coosa and Tallapoosa add penstock and gate inspection.

The Wiregrass and pipelines statewide

Southeast Alabama has Southern Nuclear's Farley plant near Dothan and the Army aviation training centre in Dale County, with associated helicopter maintenance and manufacturing. Statewide, major refined-products lines such as the Colonial and Plantation systems cross Alabama on their way from the Gulf Coast to the Southeast and East Coast, and interstate natural gas transmission lines, compressor stations and storage sites cross the state as well. New construction, relocations and integrity digs all call for API 1104 weld inspection and UT.

NDT methods we deliver in Alabama

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers UT thickness and corrosion mapping, conventional UT, PAUT, TOFD, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Alabama, MT, PT, VT and eddy current. The table links each method to typical Alabama applications and the code most often cited. The final technique is agreed with your inspector of record or engineer during scoping.

MethodTypical Alabama applicationCode / standard usually cited
UT thickness and corrosion mappingCML surveys at the Mobile and Tuscaloosa refineries and river-corridor chemical plants; paper-mill digesters and recovery-boiler tubes; tank shells at Mobile terminalsAPI 570, API 510, API 653; ASME Section V Article 23 (SE-797 practice)
Phased array UT (PAUT)Repair and tie-in welds during turnarounds; high-energy piping at utility plants; heavy fabrication and structural weldsASME Section V Article 4; ASME B31.1, B31.3 and Section VIII; AWS D1.1; API 1104
TOFDThick-wall vessel and header welds; flaw sizing to support engineering reviewASME Section V Article 4 and owner-specified code cases
Radiography (RT)Pipeline girth welds; small-bore and socket welds; shop fabrication; ship hull and piping welds where specifiedASME Section V Article 2; API 1104; NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 and MIL-STD-2035 on Navy work
Magnetic particle (MT)Crane runways and mill components in Birmingham and Calvert; nozzle and attachment welds; mining equipmentASME Section V Article 7; AWS D1.1; ASTM E709 practice
Penetrant (PT)Stainless and alloy welds in chemical and paper plants; aluminium ship structures; non-magnetic componentsASME Section V Article 6; ASTM E165 practice; Navy and customer requirements
Visual (VT)External inspections of vessels, piping and tanks; weld fit-up and final visual; post-hurricane checks of structures and tanksAPI 510/570/653 practices; AWS D1.1; ASME Section V Article 9
Eddy current (ET)Exchanger and condenser tubing where scoped; surface-crack screening through paint; aerospace componentsASME Section V Article 8; customer and owner procedures

Each technique runs to a written procedure approved by an ASNT NDT Level III and is performed by technicians certified under an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Navy, aerospace and nuclear customers often require their own qualifications, procedures or approvals before a contractor works on their hardware; we work to those requirements where the customer accepts us, and we say so plainly where a scope needs credentials we do not hold.

API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in Alabama

Direct answer: Atlantis performs the nondestructive examination that Alabama owners' API 510 vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 tank inspections depend on, such as thickness surveys, weld examination, tank floor follow-up and visual inspection, and hands the documented results to the owner's API-certified Authorized Inspector, who remains the inspector of record and signs the report.

API 510 pressure vessels. Refinery drums and columns at Saraland and Tuscaloosa, reactors and separators in the Mobile River and Decatur chemical plants, and pressure vessels at paper mills and gas plants follow the same basic pattern. We measure thickness at the vessel's CMLs, examine nozzle and attachment welds with MT or PT during entries, apply PAUT or TOFD where cracking or repair history justifies it, and record external condition. Alabama's state boiler and pressure vessel programme also has in-service inspection requirements, so we format data to support both the API 510 record and any state inspection your item needs. See API 510 pressure vessel inspection support.

API 570 piping. On the coast, the biggest threats are external: CUI on insulated lines and atmospheric corrosion on bare carbon steel, worst at supports, low points and soil-to-air interfaces. We survey CMLs to your isometrics, add scanning at injection points and deadlegs where your programme requires it, and run thickness and corrosion mapping when insulation is removed. Data is delivered per CML for loading into your inspection database. See API 570 piping inspection support.

API 653 storage tanks. Mobile's crude, product and chemical terminals, refinery tank farms and pipeline breakout stations along the Colonial and Plantation routes hold most of the state's large tanks. For out-of-service inspections we do floor scanning with UT prove-up, shell course thickness, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination, and nozzle work; for in-service externals we measure shell thickness, inspect the roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and record settlement for your inspector's API 653 Annex B evaluation. See API 653 tank inspection support and third-party inspection in Mobile.

Atlantis does not sell risk-based inspection (API 580/581) or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments. We supply the traceable inspection data; the integrity decisions stay with your engineers and programme.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: Most Alabama inspection volume is planned around refinery and chemical turnarounds, paper-mill annual outages, utility spring and autumn outages and shipyard build milestones. Atlantis joins the planning phase, agrees methods and procedures, and mobilises crews to your site on dates fixed during scoping so NDE stays off the critical path.

Each sector plans differently. Refineries and chemical plants on the Mobile River and in Decatur set turnaround dates years ahead and freeze NDE scopes months before, and they benefit most from moving thickness surveys and external visual into on-stream work before the outage. Paper mills take short, intense annual outages in which digesters, recovery boilers and power boilers are opened for a few days; NDE must be pre-planned to the hour, with crews ready to inspect as soon as vessels are cleaned and cooled. Utilities on the Southern Company and TVA systems schedule boiler and turbine work around shoulder-season demand, while nuclear refuelling outages carry long contractor processing lead times. Shipyards need inspection to follow the build schedule, block by block, rather than an outage window.

Weather matters too. Alabama summers bring heat stress on exposed tank shells and high humidity that affects surface preparation for MT and PT, and the Gulf hurricane season from June to November can move turnaround dates or create sudden post-storm inspection needs at coastal terminals. The earlier you share a plan, the easier it is to hold the crew and equipment you need. Plan an Alabama turnaround or outage inspection.

Alabama regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: Alabama's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act covers boilers and pressure vessels through the Inspections Division of the Alabama Department of Workforce; the Department of Public Health's Office of Radiation Control licenses radiography because Alabama is an NRC Agreement State; the Alabama Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipelines with PHMSA; and federal OSHA's PSM standard governs mechanical integrity.

Boilers and pressure vessels: a state programme covering both

Alabama adopted its Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act in 2000 (Code of Alabama Title 25, Chapter 12), one of the last states to do so, and regular state inspections began in 2004. The Act created a Board of Boilers and Pressure Vessels and requires permits to install regulated equipment and operating certificates kept current through periodic inspection, unless an item is exempt. The programme was administered by the Alabama Department of Labor, which became the Alabama Department of Workforce in 2025; it sits in that department's Inspections Division. Unlike states that regulate only boilers, Alabama's programme reaches unfired pressure vessels as well, so owners running API 510 programmes also need to keep state operating certificates in order. Confirm the exemption status and inspection interval for specific equipment with the division.

Radiography: ADPH Office of Radiation Control

Alabama has been an NRC Agreement State since 1966. The Alabama Department of Public Health, Office of Radiation Control, licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, registers X-ray equipment and enforces radiographer qualification rules. Atlantis does not claim to hold an Alabama radioactive material licence: radiography on Atlantis scopes is carried out by radiography crews licensed in Alabama, working to Atlantis procedures with Level III review. Where radiography's exclusion zone would stop work around a live unit or a busy shipyard, PAUT or TOFD may be an alternative if the code and owner accept it.

Pipelines: Alabama PSC and PHMSA

The Alabama Public Service Commission's gas pipeline safety programme inspects intrastate natural gas systems as PHMSA's state partner, while PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous liquid lines, including the large refined-products systems crossing the state, under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Girth welds on new pipelines generally follow API 1104. See pipeline inspection services.

Process safety, tanks and the coast

Alabama private-sector employers are covered by federal OSHA. The process safety management standard (29 CFR 1910.119) requires written mechanical integrity procedures, inspection and testing to recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, and a record of each inspection for covered equipment. EPA's SPCC rule (40 CFR Part 112) expects aboveground oil tanks to be integrity-tested to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001, and the Alabama Department of Environmental Management (ADEM) administers state environmental programmes that touch tank and pipeline facilities. Shipyards add OSHA's maritime standards and Navy quality requirements.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Every Alabama inspection produces a digital report from Atlantis's own reporting platform. Readings, indications and photos are tied to the asset, location, procedure, technician certification and instrument calibration, acceptance criteria are quoted from the governing code, and each report is reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight before release.

A good report lets the inspector of record, the state boiler inspector, a Navy or aerospace quality representative, an insurer or an OSHA compliance officer follow the evidence without phoning the technician. We make that possible by linking each reading to a named location, each indication to the procedure and acceptance criterion used, and each result to the technician's certification and the instrument's calibration record. Data is captured digitally in the field, offline where needed, and exported in formats inspection data systems can import. Learn more on the NDT inspection software page and in best NDT reporting software 2026; for marine customers, see NDT reporting software in Mobile.

The data can also go beyond a PDF. It can drive scheduling, certification tracking and invoicing in Atlantis ERP, or be shown on a 3D model in our digital twin platform; see digital twins in Mobile and digital twins in Huntsville. Level III-led inspection, digital reporting and an optional twin from one company is a combination few inspection contractors offer.

Cities we cover across Alabama

Direct answer: Atlantis mobilises inspection crews to sites anywhere in Alabama. There is no Atlantis office or laboratory in the state; crews travel to your plant, mill, shipyard, terminal or right-of-way, with dates agreed during scoping. The pages below go deeper on individual Alabama cities.

  • Mobile and the Gulf Coast: third-party inspection in Mobile, NDT consulting in Mobile, maritime and shipyard NDT consulting, steel NDT consulting, inspection software for Theodore and the chemical corridor at Axis (refining consulting in Axis).
  • Huntsville and the Tennessee Valley: third-party inspection in Huntsville, NDT consulting in Huntsville, aerospace NDT Level III in Huntsville, steel NDT consulting, Decatur, refining consulting in Decatur and Florence.
  • Birmingham: Practical NDT in Birmingham; steel, pipe and power sites across Jefferson County by arrangement.
  • Tuscaloosa: NDT consulting in Tuscaloosa.
  • Montgomery and central Alabama: NDT consulting in Montgomery, aerospace NDT consulting in Montgomery and paper mills across the Black Belt by arrangement.
  • Dothan and the Wiregrass: inspection software for Dothan; utility and manufacturing sites by arrangement.

Related Alabama hubs: NDT consulting in Alabama for Level III services, written practices and procedures, and NDT training in Alabama for ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based technician courses. City training pages cover Mobile, Huntsville and Montgomery, and trainees can practise on the Practical NDT simulator for Alabama.

How to request inspection

Direct answer: Send the asset, location, method, governing code, dates and deliverable. Atlantis replies with clarifying questions or a scope and quote, shares procedures and technician certifications for approval, mobilises the crew on the agreed date and issues a Level III-reviewed digital report.

  1. Describe the job. Asset type (vessel, piping, tank, boiler, pipeline, hull block, structure or component), site location in Alabama, method if known, governing code (API 510/570/653, ASME, API 1104, AWS D1.1, Navy or customer specification), quantities, dates and report format. Submit your Alabama RFQ.
  2. Scoping call. We confirm technique, access (scaffold, insulation removal, confined space, marine access), site safety and contractor prequalification, and whether radiography or an ultrasonic method suits the job.
  3. Scope and documents. You receive a written scope and quote, the procedures and the technician certifications your inspector of record or customer needs to approve.
  4. Mobilisation. The crew completes site orientation and starts on the agreed date.
  5. Inspection. Findings that need action are reported to your representative during the shift.
  6. Report. A digital report reviewed under Level III oversight, traceable to code, procedure, technician and instrument.

Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in Alabama

What NDT inspection services does Atlantis offer in Alabama?

UT thickness and corrosion mapping, conventional UT, PAUT, TOFD, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Alabama, MT, PT, VT and eddy current, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes and pipeline work, all under ASNT Level III oversight.

Do you have an office in Mobile or Birmingham?

No. Atlantis has no physical office or lab in Alabama. Crews are mobilised to your site anywhere in the state on dates agreed during scoping.

Does Alabama inspect pressure vessels as well as boilers?

Yes. Alabama's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act covers both, with installation permits and operating certificates maintained through periodic inspection unless an item is exempt. The programme sits in the Inspections Division of the Alabama Department of Workforce.

Who licenses industrial radiography in Alabama?

Alabama is an NRC Agreement State. The Alabama Department of Public Health's Office of Radiation Control licenses radioactive materials and regulates industrial radiography. Radiography on our scopes is performed by crews licensed in Alabama.

Can you perform API 653 tank inspection in Mobile?

We perform the NDE that API 653 inspections rely on: floor scanning with UT prove-up, shell thickness, weld examination and settlement measurement. Your API 653-certified Authorized Inspector remains the inspector of record and signs the report.

Do you inspect ships and shipyard welds?

We can perform UT, MT, PT, VT and radiography (through licensed crews) on marine fabrication where the shipyard or customer accepts our procedures and personnel. Navy work follows requirements such as NAVSEA Technical Publication 271 and MIL-STD-2035, and the yard or customer decides which contractors may work to them.

Do you inspect paper-mill digesters and recovery boilers?

Yes. Thickness surveys, weld examination with UT, MT or PT, and visual inspection of digesters, recovery and power boilers, and chemical recovery piping are typical outage scopes. Plan them early so the crew is ready the moment vessels are released.

How much does NDT inspection cost in Alabama?

Atlantis quotes on request. Cost depends on the method, number of locations or welds, access, travel to the site, crew size, schedule, shift pattern and report format. Send your scope and you will receive a written quote.

NDT Inspection Services in Alaska

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides non-destructive testing inspection in Alaska: ultrasonic thickness surveys and corrosion mapping, phased array (PAUT) and TOFD weld inspection, radiography through radiography crews licensed for work in Alaska, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual and eddy current testing, plus the NDE that API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank programmes rely on. Work is performed by ASNT-certified technicians under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, crews are mobilised to your site, from Anchorage and the Kenai Peninsula to Fairbanks, Valdez and the North Slope, and results arrive as a code-referenced digital report.

Inspection in Alaska is shaped by three things that do not apply in the lower 48 in the same way: distance, cold and a regulatory map that leans heavily on federal agencies. A crew bound for Prudhoe Bay flies through Deadhorse and works a rotation; a crew at a Cook Inlet platform depends on weather and marine logistics; a tank inspection at Valdez sits under some of the most closely watched oil-spill rules in the country. Alaska is also not an NRC Agreement State, and it has no state pipeline safety programme, so PHMSA and the NRC deal with operators directly. This page maps where inspection work is, what methods and codes apply, which agencies shape scope, and what Atlantis does and does not deliver. When you are ready, request an Alaska inspection quote with the asset, method, code, location and season.

Where inspection work is in Alaska

Direct answer: Alaska inspection demand concentrates on the North Slope oil fields around Prudhoe Bay, Kuparuk and Alpine, along the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System to the Valdez Marine Terminal, in Cook Inlet and on the Kenai Peninsula at Nikiski, in the Fairbanks and North Pole area, and in Anchorage with its port, airport and military bases. Mining, power and marine work add scopes across the state.

North Slope: Prudhoe Bay, Kuparuk, Alpine and new developments

The North Slope is the centre of Alaskan oil production. Prudhoe Bay, Kuparuk and the Alpine fields carry thousands of miles of well lines, flow lines and transit lines, plus gathering centres, flow stations, compressor plants, seawater treatment and power generation, and new developments such as Willow and Pikka are adding modules, piping and facilities. Inspection work is dominated by corrosion: produced water, CO2 and solids drive internal corrosion, and elevated, insulated lines are exposed to corrosion under insulation where moisture gets behind jacketing. After the 2006 Prudhoe Bay transit-line leaks, internal corrosion monitoring and inspection of low-flow lines received intense attention across the industry. The everyday scopes are UT thickness and corrosion mapping on piping and vessels, profile radiography and UT at CUI-prone locations where insulation can be opened, weld inspection on module tie-ins and repairs, and tank inspection at pads and plants. See practical NDT for North Slope work.

Trans-Alaska Pipeline System and Valdez

The Trans-Alaska Pipeline System runs roughly 800 miles from Prudhoe Bay to the Valdez Marine Terminal, operated by Alyeska Pipeline Service Company, with pump stations along the route and the terminal's crude storage tanks and berths at the head of Prince William Sound. Pipeline integrity there is driven by the operator's programme, in-line inspection and federal regulation; contractors supply NDE for repairs, station piping, tanks and terminal equipment. Valdez also hosts refining and fuel distribution. Tank floor scanning, shell thickness surveys, weld inspection on station and terminal piping, and structural inspection on marine and dock steel are typical. See our pipeline inspection services.

Cook Inlet, Kenai and Nikiski

Cook Inlet has produced oil and gas since the 1950s and 60s. Offshore platforms, subsea and onshore pipelines, gas fields that supply Southcentral Alaska, the Marathon Kenai refinery at Nikiski and associated terminals and gas facilities make the Kenai Peninsula a dense inspection market for its size. Older assets mean thickness surveys, corrosion mapping and repair-weld inspection on piping and vessels, API 653 work on refinery and terminal tanks, and structural inspection on platforms and docks in a strong-current, icy marine environment. See the refining Level III consulting page for Anchorage and Southcentral and practical NDT for refinery work.

Anchorage and the Mat-Su

Anchorage is the logistics hub of the state: the Port of Alaska, Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport with its large air-cargo operation, Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, utility power plants and fuel terminals. Industrial inspection here covers fuel tanks and transfer piping, power-plant pressure equipment, structural steel and cranes, and fabrication shops that build modules and skids for the North Slope. Aviation maintenance NDT follows FAA and manufacturer requirements and is normally done by certificated repair stations, so we focus on the industrial side. See third-party inspection in Anchorage.

Fairbanks, North Pole and the Interior

The Interior combines fuel refining and terminals at North Pole, power plants in Fairbanks and Healy, Eielson Air Force Base and Fort Wainwright, and large hard-rock mines such as Fort Knox and Pogo. Winter temperatures far below zero shape everything: equipment, couplants, PT materials and personnel all have limits. Scopes include tank inspection, boiler and pressure vessel NDE, mill and crusher structural welds, and piping thickness surveys.

Southeast and Western Alaska

Southeast Alaska has a shipyard at Ketchikan, mines such as Greens Creek and Kensington, seafood processing and hydro power, while Western and Northwest Alaska include the Red Dog mine and its port, and fuel tank farms in hub communities. These scopes are planned around barge and air logistics and short seasons, and usually bundle several assets into one mobilisation.

NDT methods we deliver in Alaska

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional shear-wave UT, radiography through crews licensed for Alaska work, MT, PT, VT, eddy current and MFL tank floor scanning. Cold-weather limits on couplants, penetrants and equipment are addressed in the procedure. Final method selection is agreed with your inspector of record during scoping.

Cold changes the physics. Ultrasonic velocity varies with temperature, so thickness readings on cold steel need calibration on a block at a similar temperature; couplants must be chosen so they do not freeze; batteries and screens lose performance; and liquid penetrant examination outside the standard temperature range in ASME Section V requires a procedure qualified for the actual temperature. Every Atlantis procedure is reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III with these limits in mind, and every technician is certified under an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Where your site requires its own procedures, we work to those.

API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in Alaska

Direct answer: Atlantis performs the NDE that API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank inspections rely on, including thickness surveys, weld examination, tank floor scanning and visual examination, and hands documented results to your API-certified Authorized Inspector, who remains the inspector of record and signs the inspection report.

API 510 pressure vessels. Separators, scrubbers, slug catchers, heaters, refinery drums and exchangers across the North Slope, Cook Inlet and the Interior run on API 510 programmes. We carry out external visual examination, UT thickness at the vessel's CMLs, corrosion mapping where localised loss is expected, PAUT or TOFD on welds with a cracking history or prior repairs, and MT or PT on nozzles and attachments during entries. Readings are reported against the previous survey so your inspector can calculate corrosion rates and set intervals. See API 510 pressure vessel inspection support.

API 570 piping. On the North Slope the piping population is enormous and largely insulated, so CML surveys, injection-point and deadleg scanning, and CUI screening where insulation is opened are the core of most programmes. At refineries and terminals the same work runs on process and transfer piping. Results are delivered per CML so they load into your inspection data system. See API 570 piping inspection support.

API 653 storage tanks. Alaska's tanks range from the crude tanks at Valdez to refinery tanks at Nikiski and North Pole, fuel terminals in Anchorage and tank farms in remote hub communities. For out-of-service inspections we perform MFL floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell course thickness surveys, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination and nozzle work; for external inspections we survey shell thickness, examine roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and take settlement measurements presented against API 653 Annex B, which matters on permafrost and frost-susceptible foundations. See API 653 tank inspection support.

What we do not do: Atlantis does not sell risk-based inspection (API 580/581) or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments, and it does not act as the Authorized Inspector. Our reports give your engineers clean, traceable data; the integrity decisions built on it stay with your programme.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: In Alaska, inspection timing is set by season and logistics as much as by turnaround schedules. Atlantis joins the planning stage, agrees methods and procedures, completes site prequalification and mobilises crews on dates fixed during scoping, often bundling several assets into one trip to make the most of each mobilisation.

Summer is the main window for tank out-of-service inspections, tank-farm work in remote communities, construction-season weld inspection and marine and dock work, because barges and roads are open and temperatures allow normal procedures. Winter brings ice roads and pads on the North Slope, which opens access to some locations but pushes NDE into heated enclosures and procedures qualified for low temperatures. Plant turnarounds at refineries and gas facilities follow their own calendar, and North Slope facility outages are planned well ahead.

A good scope still has three layers: on-stream work before the outage (thickness surveys, external visual, in-service weld examination), work that needs entry or isolation during the outage, and re-examination of repair welds before start-up. In Alaska we add a fourth: logistics. Crew travel through Anchorage, Fairbanks or Deadhorse, camp space, North Slope orientation such as the North Slope Training Cooperative programme required by many operators, equipment freight and weather contingency all have to be planned before the dates are fixed. Tell us early and we will build the plan around your season. Plan an Alaska inspection campaign.

Alaska regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: In Alaska, boilers and unfired pressure vessels are regulated by the Department of Labor and Workforce Development Mechanical Inspection Section; radioactive materials, including radiography sources, are licensed by the NRC because Alaska is not an Agreement State; PHMSA directly regulates both interstate and intrastate pipelines; AKOSH enforces process safety; and ADEC regulates oil discharge prevention.

Boilers and pressure vessels: Mechanical Inspection Section

The Mechanical Inspection Section of the Division of Labor Standards and Safety administers Alaska's boiler and pressure vessel programme under AS 18.60, covering both new construction and existing installations. A state certificate of operation is required for boilers and unfired pressure vessels, with exemptions set out in the regulations, and inspections may be made by state deputy inspectors or approved inspectors. NDE data from Atlantis supports those inspections and the owner's API 510 programme; it does not replace the commissioned inspector. Confirm the status of a specific vessel with the Mechanical Inspection Section.

Radiography: NRC licensing because Alaska is not an Agreement State

Alaska has not signed an agreement with the NRC, so licences for radioactive materials such as industrial radiography sources are issued and inspected by the NRC, through its Region IV office, rather than by the state. The state keeps jurisdiction over X-ray equipment and certain other sources. Atlantis does not claim to hold an NRC or Alaska radiography licence: radiography on Atlantis scopes is performed by radiography crews licensed for work in Alaska, working to reviewed procedures under our Level III. Where radiation exclusion zones are hard to manage on a crowded pad or in a module, PAUT or TOFD may be an alternative if your code and owner accept it.

Pipelines: PHMSA directly, plus state right-of-way oversight

Alaska is one of very few states that has not filed a state certification with PHMSA for gas or hazardous liquid pipelines, so PHMSA's Office of Pipeline Safety inspects and enforces the federal regulations (49 CFR Parts 192 and 195) for both interstate and intrastate operators in Alaska, with staff based in Anchorage. Separately, the state oversees pipeline right-of-way leases on state land, including the Trans-Alaska Pipeline System, through the Department of Natural Resources. Girth-weld inspection on new construction normally follows API 1104.

Process safety, tanks and oil discharge prevention

Alaska runs an OSHA-approved State Plan, Alaska Occupational Safety and Health (AKOSH), which enforces process safety management requirements equivalent to 29 CFR 1910.119: written inspection and testing procedures, inspection following recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, and documentation of each inspection. For oil storage and facility piping, the Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation administers oil discharge prevention and contingency plan rules under 18 AAC 75, which include tank and facility-piping integrity requirements, and EPA's SPCC rule (40 CFR Part 112) expects tank integrity testing to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001. The result is that Alaskan operators need well-documented tank and piping inspection records.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Every Atlantis inspection in Alaska produces a digital report built in our own reporting platform: each reading, indication and photo tied to the asset, location, procedure, technician certification and instrument calibration, with acceptance criteria quoted from the governing code. Reports are reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight before release.

Remote work makes good field data capture essential. Our reporting tools capture data offline, which matters on a pad, a platform or a remote tank farm with no reliable connection, and sync when a connection is available. Inspectors of record, ADEC, PHMSA and insurers reject reports for predictable reasons: readings that cannot be traced to a CML, indications without a procedure and acceptance criterion, technicians whose certification cannot be shown, and instruments without calibration records, including the calibration temperature for cold-weather UT. The platform is designed around those points and exports in formats your inspection data management system can import. Read more on our NDT inspection software page, or compare options in best NDT reporting software 2026.

The data can also go further than a PDF. Results can feed scheduling, certification tracking and invoicing in Atlantis ERP (see NDT ERP in Alaska), or be placed on a 3D model of a pad, module or tank farm in our digital twin platform (see digital twins in Alaska), which is especially useful when engineers in Anchorage or outside the state need to review findings on assets they cannot easily visit.

Cities and regions we cover across Alaska

Direct answer: Atlantis mobilises inspection crews to client sites anywhere in Alaska that the job's logistics allow. Atlantis has no physical office in Alaska, so crews travel to your pad, plant, terminal, mine or right-of-way, with the schedule agreed during scoping. The pages below cover Alaska locations in more depth.

  • North Slope: Prudhoe Bay, Kuparuk, Alpine and Deadhorse; see North Slope practical NDT.
  • Kenai Peninsula and Cook Inlet: Nikiski, Kenai and platforms by arrangement; see refining NDT consulting and refinery practical NDT.
  • Valdez: marine terminal, tanks and TAPS-related scopes by arrangement.
  • Fairbanks and North Pole: refinery, terminal, power plant and mine scopes by arrangement.
  • Southeast and Western Alaska: Juneau, Ketchikan, Kodiak and hub-community tank farms, planned around barge and air logistics.

Related Alaska hubs: NDT consulting in Alaska for Level III services, written practices and procedures, NDT training in Alaska for ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based technician training, and practical NDT in Alaska for simulator practice before field work.

How to request inspection

Direct answer: Send the asset, method, location, governing code, season or dates and the deliverable you need. Atlantis replies with clarifying questions or a scoped quote, confirms procedures, technician certifications and logistics, mobilises the crew on the agreed date and delivers a Level III-reviewed digital report.

  1. Tell us the job. Asset type (vessel, piping, tank, pipeline, structure), method if known, location in Alaska, governing code (API 510/570/653, ASME, API 1104, AWS D1.1), target season or dates, quantity and report format. Send your Alaska RFQ.
  2. Scoping call. We confirm method and technique, access (scaffold, insulation removal, entry, heated enclosures), temperature limits, site orientation requirements and whether radiography or an ultrasonic alternative suits the job.
  3. Quote, procedures and logistics plan. You receive a scope and quote, the procedures and technician certifications for your inspector's review, and the travel, freight and camp plan.
  4. Mobilisation. Crews complete prequalification and orientation and mobilise on the date agreed during scoping.
  5. Inspection and daily updates. Findings that need immediate attention are reported to your representative the same shift.
  6. Report. A Level III-reviewed digital report, traceable to code, procedure, technician and instrument.

Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in Alaska

Which NDT inspection services does Atlantis offer in Alaska?

UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional UT, radiography through crews licensed for Alaska work, MT, PT, VT, ET and MFL tank floor scanning, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes and pipeline inspection, under ASNT Level III oversight.

Do you have an office in Anchorage?

No. Atlantis does not operate a physical office or lab in Alaska. Crews are mobilised to your site, and travel, freight and schedule are agreed during scoping.

Can you work on the North Slope?

Yes, by arrangement with the operator. North Slope work requires operator prequalification, site orientation, camp space and travel through Deadhorse, all planned during scoping before dates are fixed.

Is Alaska an NRC Agreement State for radiography?

No. Alaska is not an Agreement State, so the NRC licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, through Region IV. Radiography on our scopes is done by crews licensed for work in Alaska.

Who regulates pipelines in Alaska?

PHMSA. Alaska has not filed a state pipeline safety certification, so PHMSA's Office of Pipeline Safety regulates both interstate and intrastate pipelines in the state. The Department of Natural Resources oversees right-of-way leases on state land.

Does Alaska inspect boilers and pressure vessels?

Yes. The Department of Labor and Workforce Development Mechanical Inspection Section regulates boilers and unfired pressure vessels and issues certificates of operation, with inspections by state or approved inspectors.

Can you perform API 653 tank inspections in Alaska?

We perform the NDE an API 653 inspection relies on: MFL floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell thickness, weld examination and settlement measurement. Your API 653-certified Authorized Inspector remains the inspector of record and signs the report.

Can NDT be done in sub-zero temperatures?

Yes, within limits. UT needs couplants that do not freeze and calibration at a similar temperature, PT outside the standard range needs a qualified procedure, and much winter work is done in heated enclosures. Our Level III reviews these limits in the procedure.

How much does NDT inspection cost in Alaska?

Atlantis quotes on request. Cost depends on method, number of locations or welds, access, travel, freight and camp logistics, season, crew size and the report format required. Send the scope and you will get a written quote.

When is the best time to schedule tank inspections?

Most out-of-service tank work and remote tank-farm inspection is scheduled in summer, when barges and roads are open and temperatures allow standard procedures. Book early, because the season is short.

Will our inspector or regulator accept your reports?

Reports quote the procedure, acceptance criteria and code, list technician certifications and instrument calibration, and are reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight. Agree the report format with us during scoping.

Do you offer RBI or fitness-for-service assessments?

California inspection is shaped by regulation more than in any other state. Refineries operate under Cal/OSHA's refinery-specific process safety rule, many pressure vessels need a state permit to operate, radiographers need California-recognised certification, and seismic design and environmental rules sit on top of everything. The industrial base is just as distinctive: refineries in the Los Angeles basin and the San Francisco Bay Area, oilfields in Kern County, the twin ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, aerospace and space launch from Palmdale to Vandenberg, naval shipbuilding in San Diego, and power generation including the Diablo Canyon nuclear plant. This page covers each of those, the rules that change inspection scope, and how Atlantis delivers. To start, request a California inspection quote.

Where inspection work is in California

Direct answer: California inspection demand concentrates in the Los Angeles basin refineries and ports, the San Francisco Bay Area refining and industrial belt from Richmond to Benicia, the Kern County oilfields around Bakersfield, the Southern California aerospace and space corridor, San Diego's naval and shipbuilding base, and statewide power, water and transport infrastructure.

Los Angeles basin: El Segundo, Carson, Wilmington, Torrance and Long Beach

The South Bay and harbour area holds most of Southern California's refining capacity, including Chevron's El Segundo refinery, the Marathon Los Angeles refinery spanning Carson and Wilmington, and the Torrance refinery, along with marine terminals, tank farms, pipelines and the Port of Los Angeles and Port of Long Beach, the busiest container port complex in the country. Typical scope is UT thickness on piping circuits and vessels, PAUT and RT on repair welds, CUI work on insulated lines, API 653 work on terminal tanks and inspection of marine-terminal piping and structures. Several California refineries have closed or converted to renewable fuels in recent years, so local scope keeps shifting from crude units to conversion projects and tank and terminal integrity. See Los Angeles third-party inspection, El Segundo, Carson, Wilmington and Torrance.

Bay Area: Richmond, Martinez, Benicia and the Carquinez Strait

Chevron's Richmond refinery and the refineries and terminals around Martinez and Benicia make the Carquinez Strait the second refining cluster in the state, alongside chemical plants, power stations and the Port of Oakland. Some Bay Area sites have converted to renewable diesel, which brings new-construction weld inspection on modified units as well as continued integrity work. Bay Area refineries were among the first to work under the refinery PSM rule's damage mechanism review requirements, which tend to generate targeted inspection scopes for specific mechanisms such as sulfidation and high-temperature hydrogen attack. See Richmond refining NDT consulting, Martinez, Benicia and San Francisco tank inspection.

Kern County and the San Joaquin Valley

Bakersfield sits among California's largest oilfields, including Kern River and Midway-Sunset, where steam-flood operations put steam generators, high-temperature piping, separators and produced-water tanks under constant thermal and corrosive load. Inspection here means UT thickness on steam and production lines, tank inspection at lease facilities, weld inspection on gathering lines and vessel surveys. Agriculture and food processing across the valley add pressure vessels, ammonia refrigeration piping and boilers. See Bakersfield third-party inspection, Bakersfield refining NDT consulting and Taft.

Aerospace and space: Palmdale, Edwards, Hawthorne and Vandenberg

Southern California designs and builds aircraft and spacecraft at Air Force Plant 42 in Palmdale, flight-tests at Edwards Air Force Base, builds rockets in Hawthorne and launches from Vandenberg Space Force Base. Aerospace NDE is governed by prime-contractor specifications and NAS 410 personnel rules, so Atlantis's role there is usually support to suppliers' own programmes and Level III consulting rather than field crews; see NDT consulting in California.

San Diego: shipbuilding and the Navy

San Diego hosts one of the largest naval concentrations in the country and the General Dynamics NASSCO shipyard, plus ship-repair yards around the bay. Weld inspection to NAVSEA and ABS requirements, UT and MT on structural and hull welds, and RT on piping are the core methods. See San Diego weld inspection, maritime NDT consulting in San Diego and radiographic testing in San Diego.

Power, water and infrastructure

The Diablo Canyon nuclear plant near San Luis Obispo, gas-fired plants and a growing fleet of battery storage and hydrogen projects drive power-sector NDE. API 653 storage tanks. Terminal and refinery tanks in California also face seismic anchorage and foundation questions. For out-of-service inspections we perform floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell thickness, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination and nozzle work; for externals, shell thickness, visual examination of roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and settlement measurement presented against API 653 Annex B. See API 653 tank inspection support, Los Angeles tank inspection and San Francisco tank inspection.

Atlantis does not sell risk-based inspection (API 580/581) or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments; our reports supply the data your engineers use for those decisions.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: California refinery turnarounds are planned long in advance and closely watched because they affect state fuel supply. Atlantis joins planning early, agrees methods and procedures with your inspector, and mobilises crews on dates fixed during scoping, so inspection and repair-weld re-examination do not extend the outage.

We split a turnaround scope into on-stream work before the outage (thickness surveys, external visual, in-service weld examination), outage work (entries, tank floors, exchanger bundles, welds under insulation) and post-repair re-examination. Moving scope on-stream wherever your inspector agrees is the single biggest lever on outage length.

California-specific planning points: refineries must account for the inspection actions coming out of damage mechanism reviews and hazard analyses, which can add mechanism-specific scope late in planning; work on the Los Angeles and Bay Area coasts must deal with marine-layer humidity that affects coatings and CUI; summer heat in Kern County and the desert limits working hours; and many sites have strict air-quality permits that affect blasting, coating removal and hot work. Contractor safety prequalification and site orientation are completed before mobilisation. Plan a California turnaround inspection.

California regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: In California, boilers and many unfired pressure vessels need permits from Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit, refineries work under Cal/OSHA's refinery PSM rule (Title 8 section 5189.1), radiography is regulated by the California Department of Public Health Radiologic Health Branch, hazardous liquid pipelines by the Office of the State Fire Marshal, gas pipelines by the CPUC, and tanks by APSA and EPA SPCC.

Boilers and pressure vessels: Cal/OSHA Pressure Vessel Unit

California is one of the states that regulates unfired pressure vessels as well as boilers. Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit issues permits to operate for boilers and for many unfired pressure vessels, such as air receivers and LPG tanks, under the Title 8 Boiler and Fired Pressure Vessel and Unfired Pressure Vessel Safety Orders, and permit inspections are performed by state inspectors or qualified insurance-company inspectors. Which process vessels need a permit depends on the scope and exemptions in the Safety Orders, so confirm specific items with Cal/OSHA. Atlantis is not a permit inspector; our NDE data supports yours.

Refinery process safety: Title 8 section 5189.1

California is a state-plan OSHA state. General industry follows the state PSM standard (Title 8 section 5189), and petroleum refineries follow the refinery-specific standard in section 5189.1, adopted in 2017, which adds requirements such as damage mechanism reviews, hierarchy-of-hazard-controls analyses and stronger mechanical integrity programmes. The parallel CalARP programme applies to many of the same facilities. For inspection contractors this means scopes are increasingly tied to specific damage mechanisms, and reports must show exactly which technique was used where.

Radiography: CDPH and Agreement State status

California is an NRC Agreement State. The California Department of Public Health's Radiologic Health Branch licenses radioactive material and regulates industrial radiography, including certification requirements for radiographers working in the state. Atlantis does not claim to hold a California radioactive material licence; radiography on our scopes is performed by radiography crews licensed in California, working to procedures reviewed under our Level III. In congested refineries and ports, PAUT or TOFD can be proposed instead of RT where the code and owner accept it.

Pipelines, oilfields and tanks

The Office of the State Fire Marshal's pipeline safety programme regulates intrastate hazardous liquid pipelines, the California Public Utilities Commission oversees gas pipeline safety, and PHMSA regulates interstate lines under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Oil and gas production facilities are overseen by the California Geologic Energy Management Division (CalGEM). Aboveground petroleum storage falls under the Aboveground Petroleum Storage Act, administered locally by Certified Unified Program Agencies, and EPA's SPCC rule (40 CFR Part 112) expects integrity testing to a standard such as API 653 or STI SP001. See pipeline inspection services and Los Angeles pipeline inspection.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Each California inspection is delivered as a digital report from Atlantis's own reporting platform, with every reading and indication tied to asset, location, procedure, acceptance criterion, technician certification and instrument calibration, and reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight before release.

California's refinery rule makes documentation more important than anywhere else in the country: inspection results feed damage mechanism reviews, mechanical integrity records and, after incidents, regulatory investigations. A report that cannot show which technique was used on which location, by whom, with what calibrated instrument, is a liability. Our platform captures data in the field, offline where needed, structures it per asset and CML, and exports to the formats your inspection data system imports. See NDT inspection software and best NDT reporting software 2026.

The same data can feed Atlantis ERP for scheduling, certifications and invoicing, or a 3D model of the unit on our digital twin platform; see digital twins in California. Level III-led inspection, a digital report and an optional twin from one company is something the large inspection firms do not offer as a single service.

Cities we cover across California

Direct answer: Atlantis mobilises inspection crews to client sites anywhere in California. Atlantis has no physical office in California, so crews travel to your refinery, terminal, yard or right-of-way, with dates agreed during scoping. These pages go deeper on individual California cities.

  • Los Angeles and the harbour: third-party inspection, weld inspection, corrosion inspection, Long Beach, Paramount and El Segundo refining.
  • Bay Area: San Francisco weld inspection, San Francisco pipeline inspection, piping inspection, Martinez refining and Fremont.
  • Central Valley: Bakersfield, Sacramento and Fresno.
  • San Diego: tank inspection, pressure vessel inspection and pipeline inspection.
  • North Coast: Eureka.

Related California hubs: NDT consulting in California for Level III services, procedures and written practices, and NDT training in California for ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based technician training.

How to request inspection

Direct answer: Send Atlantis the asset, method, site, governing code, dates and the report you need. We reply with questions or a scoped quote, share procedures and certifications for your inspector's review, mobilise on the agreed date and deliver a Level III-reviewed digital report.

  1. Describe the job. Asset, method if known, California site, governing code (API 510/570/653, ASME, API 1104, AWS D1.1/D1.5, NAVSEA or ABS), any damage mechanism the inspection targets, dates, quantities and report format. Send your California RFQ.
  2. Scoping call. Technique, access, site safety, air-permit constraints and whether RT or an ultrasonic alternative fits.
  3. Quote and procedures. Scope, quote, procedures and technician certifications for review.
  4. Mobilisation. Orientation and crew mobilisation on the date agreed during scoping.
  5. Inspection. Critical findings reported to your representative during the shift.
  6. Report. Digital, code-referenced, reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight.

Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in California

What NDT inspection services does Atlantis offer in California?

UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional UT, radiography through California-licensed crews, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes and pipeline inspection, under ASNT Level III oversight.

Do you have an office in Los Angeles or the Bay Area?

No. Atlantis has no physical office in California; crews mobilise to your site and dates are agreed during scoping.

Do pressure vessels need a state permit in California?

Many do. Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit issues permits to operate for boilers and many unfired pressure vessels such as air and LPG tanks. Scope and exemptions are set by the Title 8 Safety Orders, so confirm individual vessels with Cal/OSHA.

What is Cal/OSHA section 5189.1?

It is California's process safety management standard for petroleum refineries, adopted in 2017. It adds damage mechanism reviews and stronger mechanical integrity requirements, which shape what refineries ask inspection contractors to examine and document.

Who regulates industrial radiography in California?

California is an NRC Agreement State, and the CDPH Radiologic Health Branch licenses radioactive material and regulates industrial radiographers. Our radiography is done by crews licensed in California.

Can you support API 653 tank inspections at California terminals?

Yes: floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell thickness, weld examination and settlement measurement. Your API 653 Authorized Inspector remains the inspector of record.

How much does NDT inspection cost in California?

Atlantis quotes on request. Cost depends on method, quantity, access, travel, crew size, schedule, site requirements and report format. Send the scope for a written quote.

Can inspection be done while the unit is running?

Many thickness surveys, external visuals and some weld examinations can be done on-stream within temperature limits and site permits, which reduces turnaround scope.

Who regulates pipelines in California?

The Office of the State Fire Marshal regulates intrastate hazardous liquid pipelines, the CPUC regulates gas pipeline safety, and PHMSA regulates interstate lines.

Do you inspect in the Kern County oilfields?

Yes. Typical scopes are UT thickness on steam and production piping, tank inspection at lease facilities, vessel surveys and weld inspection on gathering lines.

Do you do aerospace NDT in California?

Aerospace NDE is governed by prime-contractor specifications and NAS 410. We support suppliers mainly through Level III consulting and procedures; talk to us about your programme.

Do you provide RBI or fitness-for-service assessments?

No. Atlantis does not offer API 580/581 RBI or API 579 FFS; we provide the inspection data those assessments use.

Get a California inspection scope

A reactor weld list in El Segundo, a terminal tank in Long Beach, steam lines near Bakersfield or ship piping in San Diego: send the asset, method, code and dates. Get a quote for NDT inspection in California, or book a call with our ASNT Level III to agree the technique first. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. See also all inspection services.
