NDT Inspection Services in Illinois

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers NDT inspection services throughout Illinois using ASNT-certified technicians under ASNT Level III oversight: UT thickness and flaw detection, PAUT, TOFD, corrosion mapping, MT, PT, VT and ET, radiography through crews licensed in Illinois and holding Illinois radiographer certification, and NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes. Crews are mobilised to your site, the schedule is set during scoping, and results are issued as Level III-reviewed digital reports.

Illinois packs an unusual amount of inspectable steel into one state. Four refineries ring the Chicago area and southern Illinois, the state runs the largest nuclear fleet in the country, the Patoka and Wood River areas form one of the busiest crude-oil crossroads in North America, and Chicago remains the rail, barge and manufacturing hub of the Midwest. That variety means an Illinois inspection provider has to switch comfortably between refinery CML surveys, nuclear-grade paperwork, pipeline welds and heavy-equipment fabrication. Below we map where that work sits, which methods and codes apply, which Illinois agencies matter, and how to get a job scoped. To skip ahead, request an Illinois inspection quote.

Where inspection work is in Illinois

Direct answer: Illinois inspection demand concentrates in five zones: the southwest Chicago refining and chemical corridor (Joliet, Lemont, Channahon, Morris), the Chicago metro and Lake Michigan shoreline, the Metro East and Wood River area across from St. Louis, the southern Illinois crude hub around Patoka and Robinson, and the central Illinois manufacturing and agri-processing cities of Peoria, Decatur, Rockford and the Quad Cities.

Joliet, Lemont and the Des Plaines and Illinois river corridor

Southwest of Chicago, a large refinery near Joliet and another at Lemont sit within a short drive of petrochemical and polymer plants around Channahon, Morris and Seneca. Pipelines, product terminals and river barge docks tie them together. This corridor produces the bulk of Illinois refinery inspection: UT thickness at piping CMLs, PAUT and TOFD on new and repaired welds, MT and PT on nozzle and attachment welds, internal VT of vessels and exchangers during turnarounds, and corrosion mapping where wall loss needs repeatable tracking. The procedure side is covered on our Joliet and Lemont Level III pages.

Chicago and the Lake Michigan shoreline

Chicago itself is a mix of food and chemical processing, metal fabrication, district energy plants, high-rise building systems, rail yards and port terminals on Lake Calumet. The southeast side and the neighbouring Indiana shoreline remain steel country. Typical inspection includes structural weld inspection to AWS D1.1, pressure vessel and boiler NDE for repair organisations, rail and transit component checks, and tank surveys at liquid terminals. Chicago already has its own Atlantis service pages for weld inspection, pressure vessels, piping, tanks and third-party inspection, plus a rail NDT consulting page.

Metro East: Wood River, Hartford, Granite City and Madison

Across the Mississippi from St. Louis, the Wood River refinery at Roxana is one of the largest in the Midwest, with tank farms, terminals and pipelines in Hartford and around it. Granite City makes steel, and Madison and Alton add fabrication and barge terminals. Here tank work (API 653 shell and floor surveys), refinery piping and steel-plant maintenance inspection run side by side. See Wood River, Madison and Alton steel.

Southern Illinois: Patoka, Robinson and the oil patch

Patoka is a major crude-oil terminal and pipeline hub where long-haul lines from the north and west meet lines heading south and east, and it holds large tank farms. Robinson, on the Indiana border, has its own refinery. The Illinois Basin oil fields in the south of the state add small-diameter flowlines, tank batteries and gathering systems. Inspection here is dominated by tank floor and shell surveys, pipeline girth welds to API 1104 and integrity-dig thickness work. Our Robinson page covers the refinery side.

Central and northern Illinois: Peoria, Decatur, Rockford, Springfield and the Quad Cities

Heavy-equipment manufacturing in Peoria and the Quad Cities, aerospace component and actuation suppliers in Rockford, and grain and corn-processing plants in Decatur all run pressure vessels, boilers, dryers, reactors and heavily welded structures. Inspection leans toward MT and UT of structural welds and castings, PT on aerospace parts, and pressure equipment surveys for the processing plants. Related pages: Peoria, Decatur, Rockford and Springfield.

The nuclear fleet

Illinois has more nuclear generating capacity than any other US state, with stations at Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle and Quad Cities. In-service inspection at these plants follows ASME Section XI and utility-specific qualification rules, and outage contractors need technicians whose certification records and procedures withstand nuclear quality assurance review. Even when a contractor is not on the primary-side scope, balance-of-plant piping, tanks, structural welds and heat-exchanger work during outages draw on the same disciplined documentation. Our Peru page, near LaSalle, covers the Level III side of that region.

NDT methods we deliver in Illinois

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers UT thickness and shear-wave UT, PAUT, TOFD, corrosion mapping, RT through Illinois-licensed and Illinois-certified radiography crews, MT, PT, VT and ET. The right method depends on the asset, the damage mechanism and the code; the table shows typical Illinois uses.

MethodTypical Illinois applicationCode / standard usually cited
UT thicknessCML surveys on Joliet, Lemont, Wood River and Robinson refinery piping; tank shells at Patoka and HartfordAPI 570, API 510, API 653
Shear-wave UT and PAUTRefinery and petrochemical piping welds, heavy-equipment weldments in Peoria and the Quad Cities, structural connectionsASME Section V Article 4, ASME B31.3, AWS D1.1
TOFDThick-wall vessel seams and repair welds where through-wall sizing is requiredASME Section V, owner specifications
Corrosion mappingRepeatable wall-loss maps on vessels, exchangers, large-bore piping and tank critical zonesAPI 510, API 570, API 653
RT (licensed and certified crews)Pipeline girth welds, plant piping where radiography is specified, construction tie-insAPI 1104, ASME B31.3, ASME Section V Article 2
MTCastings and weldments in heavy equipment, crane and rail components, nozzle welds during turnaroundsASTM E1444, ASME Section V Article 7
PTAerospace parts in Rockford, stainless process piping in food and chemical plantsASTM E1417, ASME Section V Article 6
VTVessel internals, tank externals and roofs, structural welds, weld fit-up on constructionASME Section V Article 9, API 653, AWS D1.1
ETSurface-crack checks on machined and aerospace parts, tubing and bar where specifiedASME Section V Article 8, ASTM E-series

For technique depth see corrosion mapping, TOFD testing, CUI inspection and the Chicago pages for ultrasonic and radiographic testing.

API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in Illinois

Direct answer: we support Illinois owners' API 510, 570 and 653 programmes with NDE crews, thickness and weld data, corrosion-rate and remaining-life calculations and written findings handed to your own API-certified Authorized Inspector. Atlantis is not an Authorized Inspector and does not act as inspector of record.

API 510 pressure vessels. Refinery reactors, drums and exchangers in Joliet, Lemont and Wood River, and process vessels in Decatur's corn-processing plants and the Channahon chemical cluster, all need external, on-stream and internal inspection at intervals your inspector sets. We provide UT thickness grids, PAUT or TOFD on welds of concern, wet fluorescent MT where cracking is suspected, and VT of internals, then reduce the data to corrosion rates. More on our API 510 services page.

API 570 piping. Most of a refinery's inspection hours go into piping circuits. We take readings at your CMLs, highlight short-term and long-term corrosion rates, propose additional CMLs where readings look anomalous, and screen likely CUI locations on insulated lines, especially in the freeze-thaw cycles that Illinois winters produce. See API 570 piping services and corrosion inspection in Chicago.

API 653 tanks. Illinois has some of the densest tank populations in the Midwest at Patoka, Hartford, Wood River and the Chicago-area terminals. We provide shell UT surveys, floor MFL scanning with UT prove-up, weld MT or PT and settlement survey support for out-of-service inspections, and external inspection support between them, delivering everything to your API 653 inspector. See API 653 tank services and aboveground storage tank inspection.

Pipelines. For crude, product and gas lines crossing the state, we inspect construction welds and support integrity digs; see pipeline inspection services and Chicago pipeline inspection.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: Illinois refinery and petrochemical turnarounds cluster in spring and autumn, nuclear refuelling outages follow each plant's cycle, and grain processors usually schedule maintenance outside harvest. Each window is short, so procedures, certifications and equipment must be ready before units come down.

The Chicago-area refineries compete for the same regional pool of inspectors every spring and autumn, and the shortage shows up as late crews, unfamiliar technicians and rushed paperwork. The way around it is early scoping. We start with your equipment list and work out, item by item, which inspection can be done on-stream beforehand, which needs the equipment open, and which can wait until after start-up. On-stream UT thickness, external VT, corrosion mapping through insulation windows and many PAUT examinations can be completed weeks before a turnaround, leaving the shutdown window for internal inspection, repairs and post-repair NDE.

Before mobilisation our Level III reviews the owner's inspection specification against our procedures, flags any technique that needs qualification or demonstration, and sends the certification package for your contractor-approval process. During the turnaround the crew records data straight into our reporting platform, so the inspection coordinator sees results daily rather than at the end. Critical findings are escalated immediately. Talk to us about your next Illinois turnaround while there is still time to plan it properly.

Winter work deserves its own plan. Lake-effect wind on the Chicago shoreline and sub-zero mornings across the state affect couplant, instruments, batteries, film processing and personnel. We plan enclosures, cold-weather couplants and equipment checks into the scope rather than improvising on site.

Illinois regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: the key Illinois rules are boiler and pressure vessel law administered by the Office of the State Fire Marshal, radiation licensing and individual radiographer certification by the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security, pipeline safety by the Illinois Commerce Commission and PHMSA, and federal OSHA and EPA rules for process safety and oil storage.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Office of the State Fire Marshal's Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety enforces the state's boiler and pressure vessel safety law, requiring certificate inspections by commissioned inspectors and repairs and alterations to the National Board Inspection Code. The City of Chicago runs its own boiler inspection within city limits, so confirm which jurisdiction covers your site. Our NDE on repairs is documented so the commissioned inspector and the repair organisation can use it.

Radiography. Illinois has been an NRC Agreement State since 1987, so radioactive-material licences are issued by the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security (IEMA-OHS), Division of Nuclear Safety. Illinois goes further than many states: individual industrial radiographers and radiographer trainees must be certified by the state under 32 Illinois Administrative Code Part 405, which sets training and examination requirements and fixed certification periods. Atlantis does not hold an Illinois radiography licence; radiography is carried out by crews licensed in Illinois whose radiographers hold the state certification.

Pipelines. The Illinois Commerce Commission's pipeline safety programme oversees intrastate natural gas operators, while interstate pipelines and hazardous liquid lines, including the crude systems converging on Patoka, fall under PHMSA and 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Construction welds are usually inspected to API 1104.

Process safety and oil storage. Private-sector employers in Illinois are covered by federal OSHA. Refineries and chemical plants must maintain a mechanical integrity programme under the Process Safety Management standard, 29 CFR 1910.119, which is why inspection records have to be complete, traceable and code-referenced. Aboveground oil storage falls under the EPA SPCC rule, which expects integrity testing to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001. The State Fire Marshal also administers petroleum storage tank rules.

Always confirm current requirements with the relevant agency. For written practices, procedures and audits, see our Illinois NDT consulting hub.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Atlantis reports are produced on our own digital reporting platform. Data is captured on site, reviewed by a Level III and issued with the procedure, code, acceptance criteria, technician certification level and equipment calibration stated, so your Authorized Inspector, auditor or nuclear QA reviewer can trace every result.

Thickness data comes organised by circuit and CML with previous readings alongside for trending. Weld results reference the weld map and the acceptance standard. Every indication has a location, size, evaluation and photograph. Nothing is retyped from handwritten sheets, so the numbers in the report are the numbers the instrument recorded. That matters on Illinois jobs where an owner's integrity team, an insurer's inspector and sometimes a nuclear QA auditor all read the same report for different reasons. The platform is described on our NDT inspection software and reporting software pages.

Results do not have to stop at a report. Owners can see inspection data on a 3D model of a unit or tank farm through our digital twin platform; see the Joliet and Illinois examples. NDT service companies can run scheduling, certification tracking and invoicing in the Atlantis ERP. One provider covers Level III-led inspection, digital reporting and, if you want it, a twin of the results.

Cities we cover across Illinois

Direct answer: we mobilise crews anywhere in Illinois. The cities below already have their own Atlantis pages for inspection, consulting, training or practice; anywhere else, just name the site in your request.

  • Chicago: pipeline inspection, Level III consulting, refining NDT consulting, NDT training, practical NDT, digital twin.
  • Joliet and Lemont: refinery consulting pages listed above plus Lemont refining.
  • Wood River, Hartford and Madison: Wood River consulting and Hartford refining.
  • Robinson: Robinson refining NDT.
  • Peoria: steel NDT consulting and practical NDT.
  • Rockford: steel NDT consulting.
  • Springfield and Decatur: Springfield consulting and Decatur practice pages.

For your own people, see NDT training in Illinois (ASNT SNT-TC-1A, online, live-virtual or onsite at your facility) and the Practical NDT simulator for Illinois.

Level III oversight on every Illinois job

Direct answer: every Atlantis inspection runs under an ASNT NDT Level III, Anoop Rayavarapu, founder of Atlantis NDT, who approves the procedures, reviews results and stands behind the method choices. That gives Illinois owners a single accountable technical authority from scoping to report.

Illinois buyers are among the most audit-heavy in the country. Nuclear utilities, refinery inspection groups and aerospace primes in Rockford all ask which written practice certified the technician, which procedure was used, whether it was qualified, and who reviewed the data. A Level III in the loop means those answers exist before the question is asked. Technically, the Level III decides when PAUT can replace RT, when TOFD sizing is warranted, and whether a scan plan really covers the weld and heat-affected zone. Where a technique has to be demonstrated, we prepare the procedure and run the demonstration. Employers building their own NDT programme can use our written practice development service.

How to request inspection

Direct answer: send the asset, site, method if known, governing code, target dates and the report you need. We come back with questions or a quote, agree scope and schedule, then mobilise to your Illinois site.

  1. Describe the work. Asset type, location in Illinois, reason for inspection or suspected damage, owner specification and any access constraints.
  2. Scoping with the Level III. Method stack, coverage, acceptance criteria and any procedure qualification are agreed.
  3. Quote and calendar. Written scope and quote; dates fixed around your turnaround, outage or production plan.
  4. Pre-mobilisation pack. Certifications, procedures, calibration records, radiography licence and certification documents (for RT) and safety paperwork go to your contractor approval team.
  5. Inspection on site. Data captured digitally; critical findings escalated immediately.
  6. Report and hand-off. Level III-reviewed report issued through the platform, with data in the format your inspector or integrity team uses.

Start your Illinois inspection request or book a Level III scoping call.

Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in Illinois

What NDT inspection services do you provide in Illinois?

UT thickness, shear-wave UT, PAUT, TOFD, corrosion mapping, MT, PT, VT and ET by ASNT-certified technicians under Level III oversight, RT through Illinois-licensed crews with state-certified radiographers, and NDE support for API 510, 570 and 653 programmes.

Do industrial radiographers need state certification in Illinois?

Yes. Illinois requires individual industrial radiographers and trainees to be certified by IEMA-OHS under 32 Illinois Administrative Code Part 405, in addition to the company's radioactive materials licence. We only use crews that meet those requirements.

Who inspects boilers and pressure vessels in Illinois?

The Office of the State Fire Marshal's Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety oversees certificate inspections by commissioned inspectors; the City of Chicago runs its own programme within city limits.

Can you support API 653 tank inspections at Patoka or Wood River?

Yes. We provide shell UT, floor MFL with UT prove-up, weld MT or PT and settlement survey support, with results delivered to your API 653 inspector, who remains inspector of record.

Are you an Authorized Inspector for API 510 or 570?

No. We provide NDE data, calculations and findings; your own API-certified inspector or inspection agency signs the inspection report.

Do you have a branch in Chicago?

No. We do not operate a local Illinois base. Crews are mobilised to your site and the schedule is agreed during scoping.

How much do NDT inspection services cost in Illinois?

Every job is quoted on request. Cost depends on methods and coverage, quantity of items, access such as scaffolding or confined space, shift pattern, travel and the reporting format required.

Can you work on nuclear plant outages?

We can support balance-of-plant and contractor scopes where our procedures and certifications meet the utility's requirements; this is confirmed during scoping against the utility's quality programme.

Can thickness testing be done while the unit is running?

Usually yes. On-stream UT thickness and corrosion mapping are routine, within surface-temperature limits and your site's permit rules.

Do you inspect pipeline welds in Illinois?

Yes, construction girth welds to API 1104 and integrity-dig work for operators, using UT, PAUT, MT and RT through licensed crews where radiography is specified.

What happens when you find a serious defect?

The technician records the finding and notifies your site contact immediately, and our Level III reviews the data the same day so you can decide on isolation, repair or further examination.

Can you also train our Illinois technicians?

Yes. ASNT SNT-TC-1A training for Level I, II and III is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at your facility; see NDT training in Illinois.

NDT Inspection Services in Indiana

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides NDT inspection services across Indiana with ASNT-certified technicians working under ASNT Level III oversight: UT thickness surveys, PAUT, TOFD, corrosion mapping, MT, PT, VT and ET, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Indiana, and NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes. Indiana makes more steel than any other state, runs the largest refinery in the Midwest on the Lake Michigan shore, and builds engines, vehicles, pharmaceuticals and plastics in plants spread from Fort Wayne to Mount Vernon. Its inspection market is therefore shaped less by oilfields and more by mills, heavy manufacturing and the Calumet Region's industrial shoreline. This page explains where Indiana's inspection work is, which NDT methods and codes apply, which Indiana regulators sit behind it (including the change to radioactive-materials licensing that took effect at the start of October 2026), and how to scope a job with us. Ready now? Request an Indiana inspection quote.

Where inspection work is in Indiana

Direct answer: Indiana inspection demand is heaviest in the Calumet Region of Lake County and Porter County (Whiting, East Chicago, Gary, Hammond, Burns Harbor), followed by central Indiana's engine, pharmaceutical and construction cluster around Indianapolis and Columbus, the southwest river corridor of Evansville and Mount Vernon, and the manufacturing towns of the north and northeast such as Fort Wayne, South Bend and the steel minimills.

The Calumet Region: Whiting, East Chicago, Hammond and Gary

The Whiting refinery is the largest in the Midwest, and its crude units, cokers, hydrotreaters, tank farms and docks generate a year-round inspection workload: UT thickness at piping CMLs, PAUT and TOFD on new and repaired welds, MT and PT during turnarounds, VT of vessel internals and tank surveys. Immediately east, integrated steelworks at East Chicago, Indiana Harbor and Gary, plus the Burns Harbor works in Porter County, run blast furnaces, coke batteries, hot-strip mills and enormous cranes and structures. Mill inspection is about rotating equipment shafts, crane girders and runways, boiler and power-house piping, gas mains, ladles and structural weld repairs, where UT and MT do most of the work. Hammond adds component manufacturing and corn milling. Related Atlantis pages: Whiting, Whiting refining NDT, East Chicago, Gary steel NDT and Hammond.

Porter and LaPorte counties: Burns Harbor, Portage and La Porte

The Port of Indiana at Burns Harbor handles steel, bulk and liquid cargoes on Lake Michigan, with fabrication and terminal operators around Portage. La Porte has metal fabrication and processing plants. Here inspection mixes steel-plant maintenance, terminal tank surveys and structural weld inspection on port and plant projects. See Portage and La Porte.

Central Indiana: Indianapolis, Columbus, Lebanon and Lafayette

Indianapolis builds aero engines and transmissions, Columbus is home to a major diesel-engine maker, and Lafayette and the surrounding counties assemble vehicles. In Boone County, very large pharmaceutical manufacturing construction around Lebanon has brought high-purity process piping, utilities and structural steel on a scale few Midwest sites have seen. Inspection demand here includes weld inspection on construction (stainless and carbon steel piping to ASME B31.3, structural steel to AWS D1.1), PT and ET of aerospace and engine parts, and periodic inspection of boilers, autoclaves and pressure vessels in operating plants. Indianapolis already has Atlantis pages for weld inspection, pressure vessels, piping and third-party inspection.

Southwest Indiana: Evansville, Mount Vernon and the Ohio River

Mount Vernon has an in-state refinery and a large engineering-plastics plant, Newburgh has aluminium smelting and rolling, and the Evansville area holds chemical, pharmaceutical and power plants along with Ohio River barge terminals and the Port of Indiana at Mount Vernon. Coal-fired and gas-fired generating stations in the region run boilers, high-energy piping and storage tanks. Typical inspection: refinery and chemical piping thickness, boiler tube and header checks, tank floor and shell surveys at river terminals. See Evansville consulting and Evansville steel NDT.

Northern and northeast Indiana: Fort Wayne, South Bend, Elkhart and the minimills

Fort Wayne and the surrounding counties assemble trucks and make engine and drivetrain components, and electric-arc steel minimills operate across the north-east. South Bend and Elkhart add RV, trailer and component manufacturing with high weld volumes. Inspection is mostly weld quality (VT, MT, UT) and maintenance NDE on mill and press equipment. See the South Bend practical NDT page.

Southern Indiana: Crane and the defence corridor

Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane in Martin County is one of the largest naval installations in the country by area, and its contractors and suppliers work to Navy technical requirements. Defence-related fabrication across southern Indiana can therefore call for NDT to NAVSEA-style specifications alongside ASME and AWS, which affects procedure content and certification evidence.

Turnarounds, mill outages and planned inspection

Direct answer: Indiana's planned inspection follows two calendars: refinery and chemical turnarounds, usually in spring or autumn, and steel-mill outages, which are scheduled around production and often run over holidays. Both are short and crowded, so inspection scope, procedures and crews must be ready before the shutdown starts.

In a mill outage, the inspection list is long and the window is measured in days: crane runways and girders, ladle and transfer-car structures, roll shafts, coupling spindles, gas-main sections and power-house piping all compete for the same few shifts. Refinery turnarounds at Whiting add thousands of inspection items and draw contractors from across the Midwest. In both cases the winning approach is to separate what can be done beforehand from what truly needs the equipment stopped. On-stream UT thickness, external VT, corrosion mapping and much of the PAUT can be done weeks ahead; the outage then focuses on internal inspection, repair welds and post-repair NDE.

Our Level III reviews the owner's specification against our procedures before mobilisation, identifies any technique needing qualification or demonstration, and sends technician certifications for your contractor approval. During the outage, data goes straight into our reporting platform so your coordinator sees results daily. Critical findings are escalated to your site contact at once. Plan your Indiana outage inspection early and you get a crew that has already read your specification.

Northwest Indiana winters are harsh on the lakefront. We plan for cold-weather couplant, instrument and battery performance, film processing limits and personnel welfare rather than discovering the problems in a January outage.

Indiana regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: Indiana inspection sits under the boiler and pressure vessel rules of the Indiana Department of Homeland Security, state and federal radiation rules for radiography (which changed when Indiana became an NRC Agreement State on 1 October 2026), pipeline safety by the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission and PHMSA, and Indiana OSHA (IOSHA) plus federal EPA rules for process safety and oil storage.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Boilers and Pressure Vessels Section of the Indiana Department of Homeland Security enforces the Indiana Boiler and Pressure Vessel Rules (675 IAC 30). Regulated equipment needs an operating permit, operating-permit inspections must be performed by inspectors licensed by the Department (state, insurance or owner-user inspection agency inspectors), and inspection reports go to the Department within a set period. NDE we perform on repairs and alterations is documented so the licensed inspector and the repair organisation can rely on it.

Radiography. Indiana signed an agreement with the NRC in September 2026 and became the 41st Agreement State on 1 October 2026, with the Indiana Department of Homeland Security's Radioactive Materials Control Program taking over licensing, inspection and enforcement for most radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, from the NRC. Because the transition is so recent, confirm the current licensing authority with the state before any radiography job, and check how existing NRC licences are being carried over. Atlantis does not claim its own Indiana radiography licence; RT is performed by radiography crews licensed in Indiana, using our procedures and reporting format.

Pipelines. The Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission's Pipeline Safety Division oversees intrastate gas pipeline operators, while interstate gas lines and hazardous liquid lines, including the crude systems running into the Whiting area, fall under PHMSA and 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Construction welds are usually inspected to API 1104.

Process safety and oil storage. Indiana runs its own OSHA-approved state plan, IOSHA, under the Indiana Department of Labor, which enforces process safety management requirements equivalent to OSHA's 29 CFR 1910.119 at refineries and chemical plants. The mechanical integrity element of PSM is what makes documented, code-referenced inspection mandatory. Aboveground oil storage falls under the EPA's SPCC rule, which expects integrity testing to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001.

Regulations change, and Indiana's radiation programme has just changed; check with the agency before relying on any summary. Our Level III can help map requirements to inspections; see the Indiana NDT consulting hub.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Atlantis inspection results are captured on site in our own digital reporting platform, reviewed by a Level III and issued with the procedure, code, acceptance criteria, technician certification level and instrument calibration recorded, so an Authorized Inspector, insurer or auditor can trace each finding back to its source.

Thickness data is organised by circuit or component and CML, with prior readings for trend. Weld results reference the weld map and the acceptance standard. Mill inspection is reported by asset tag so maintenance planners can schedule repairs. Every indication carries a location, dimensions, evaluation and photo. There is no handwritten-sheet transcription step, which removes a common source of error. Read more on our NDT inspection software and reporting software pages.

The same data can go further if you want it to: owners can see results on a 3D model of a unit, tank farm or mill structure through our digital twin platform (see the Whiting example), and NDT service companies can run scheduling, certification tracking and invoicing in the Atlantis ERP. Steel producers, engine makers, pharmaceutical owners and the Whiting refinery all audit their contractors. With a Level III involved from the start, the answers are prepared before anyone asks. The Level III also makes the technical calls: whether PAUT can replace RT on a construction package, when TOFD sizing is justified, how to cover a crane-girder weld with restricted access. Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in Indiana

Which NDT inspection services do you offer in Indiana?

UT thickness, shear-wave UT, PAUT, TOFD, corrosion mapping, MT, PT, VT and ET by ASNT-certified technicians under Level III oversight, RT through radiography crews licensed in Indiana, and NDE support for API 510, 570 and 653 programmes.

Is Indiana an NRC Agreement State now?

NDT Inspection Services in Louisiana

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers non-destructive testing inspection across Louisiana, from the Mississippi River industrial corridor between Baton Rouge and New Orleans to the Lake Charles LNG and refining cluster and the bayou fabrication yards of Houma and Port Fourchon. Services include UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT and TOFD weld inspection, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Louisiana, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes, all under ASNT NDT Level III oversight with code-referenced digital reports.

Louisiana's inspection market is shaped by water. The Mississippi River carries a chain of refineries, chemical plants, fertiliser complexes and grain and bulk terminals for more than a hundred miles; the Calcasieu Ship Channel and the Sabine and Cameron coast host some of the largest LNG export terminals in the world; and the coastal parishes build and service vessels and platforms for the Gulf offshore sector. Heat, humidity, salt air and flood risk drive corrosion everywhere. This page sets out where the work is, which Louisiana agencies matter, and how Atlantis scopes, executes and reports an inspection. If you already have a scope, request a Louisiana inspection quote.

Where inspection work is in Louisiana

Direct answer: Louisiana inspection demand clusters in five places: the Baton Rouge and river parishes chemical and refining corridor, the New Orleans east and west bank refineries and terminals, the Lake Charles and Cameron Parish LNG and petrochemical hub, the Houma, Morgan City and Port Fourchon offshore support and shipbuilding coast, and the Shreveport and Haynesville gas region in the north-west.

Baton Rouge and the river parishes

The stretch of the Mississippi from Baton Rouge downriver through Plaquemine, Geismar, Donaldsonville, Convent and the St. James and St. John parishes is often called the chemical corridor. ExxonMobil's Baton Rouge refinery and chemical plant, the Dow Louisiana operations at Plaquemine, the large chlor-alkali, polymer and isocyanate units at Geismar and the CF Industries nitrogen complex at Donaldsonville define the scale. Typical inspection scope here is UT thickness on process piping in corrosive service (chlorine, caustic, acids, ammonia), PAUT and RT on repair welds, PT on stainless and alloy piping, and API 510 internal inspections on columns, reactors and exchangers during turnarounds. See our Baton Rouge third-party inspection and API 653 tank inspection in Baton Rouge pages.

New Orleans, Norco, Garyville and Chalmette

Further downriver sit refineries such as Marathon's Garyville refinery, the Shell Norco site and Chalmette Refining, plus petroleum and chemical terminals on both banks and the Port of South Louisiana and Port of New Orleans facilities. Tank farms are a major share of scope: API 653 floor and shell work, settlement surveys on soft deltaic soils, and SPCC-driven integrity testing on bulk storage. Marine terminals and docks add UT and visual inspection of piping and structures over water. See New Orleans tank inspection and New Orleans piping inspection.

Lake Charles, Sulphur, Westlake and Cameron Parish

South-west Louisiana combines refining (Citgo Lake Charles and Phillips 66 Lake Charles), petrochemicals at Westlake and the Sasol complex, and LNG export at Cameron LNG, Sabine Pass LNG and Calcasieu Pass, with further terminals under construction. LNG means cryogenic stainless and nickel-alloy piping, where PT, RT and increasingly PAUT on new construction are central, and large storage tanks and process vessels on a corrosive coast. The 2020 hurricanes showed how storm damage creates sudden surges of inspection demand. See Lake Charles third-party inspection and pipeline NDT consulting in Lake Charles.

Houma, Morgan City, Lafayette and Port Fourchon

The coastal parishes are the shore base for much of the Gulf offshore industry. Shipyards and fabrication yards in Houma, Lockport, Morgan City and Amelia build supply vessels, liftboats, barges and platform modules, while Port Fourchon supports most deepwater activity. That work is weld-inspection heavy: UT and RT on structural and pressure welds, MT on structural steel to AWS D1.1, and class-society or owner specifications for vessels. Lafayette is home to many oilfield service companies whose equipment, from pressure-control gear to lifting equipment, needs periodic NDE. See NDT consulting in Lafayette and Practical NDT in Houma.

Shreveport, Monroe and north Louisiana

North-west Louisiana sits on the Haynesville shale, with gas gathering, compression, processing and new pipeline capacity feeding the coastal LNG terminals. Inspection here is weighted toward pipeline girth welds to API 1104, vessel and separator thickness surveys, and tank inspection at gathering facilities. A refinery in Shreveport and paper, chemical and manufacturing plants around Monroe add plant inspection scope. See NDT consulting in Shreveport and Monroe.

NDT methods we deliver in Louisiana

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional shear-wave UT, radiography through Louisiana-licensed radiography crews, MT, PT, VT and ET. The table shows how each method is typically used in Louisiana and the code usually cited; the final technique is agreed with your inspector of record during scoping.

API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in Louisiana

Direct answer: Atlantis performs the NDE that Louisiana API 510, API 570 and API 653 inspections rely on, including CML thickness surveys, weld examination, tank floor and shell work and external visual inspection, and delivers documented results to your API-certified Authorized Inspector, who remains the inspector of record and signs the report.

API 510 pressure vessels. River-corridor and Lake Charles units run columns, reactors, drums and exchangers in some of the most corrosive services in the industry. We carry out external visual examination, UT thickness at each CML, PAUT or TOFD on welds where cracking mechanisms or prior repairs are a concern, and MT or PT inside vessels during entries. Readings are reported against prior surveys so your inspector can set corrosion rates and intervals. See API 510 pressure vessel inspection support and Baton Rouge pressure vessel inspection.

API 570 piping. Chemical plants on the river carry long runs of piping in chlorine, caustic, acid and ammonia service, and refineries add sulfidation and CUI concerns. We survey CMLs to your isometrics, add scanning at injection points and deadlegs, and support CUI screening where insulation is stripped. See API 570 piping inspection support and Baton Rouge piping inspection.

API 653 storage tanks. Louisiana's tank population is huge, from crude and product terminals on the river to the tank farms that feed export docks. Soft, settling soils make settlement surveys especially important. For out-of-service inspections we perform floor scanning with UT confirmation, shell thickness, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination and nozzle work; for external inspections, shell thickness, visual examination of roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and settlement measurement presented against API 653 Annex B. See API 653 tank inspection support, Baton Rouge tank inspection and New Orleans tank inspection.

Atlantis does not sell risk-based inspection (API 580/581) or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments. Our job is to give your integrity programme accurate, traceable data.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: Most Louisiana plant inspection is planned around spring and autumn turnarounds and around hurricane season. Atlantis joins scope planning early, agrees methods and procedures, and mobilises crews to your site on dates fixed during scoping, so NDE stays off the critical path and repair welds are re-examined before start-up.

A sound turnaround inspection plan has three phases. On-stream work before the outage covers thickness surveys, external visual and the welds that can be examined in service; this is how scope gets pulled out of the shutdown window. Outage work covers entries, tank floors, exchanger bundles and welds under insulation. Post-repair work re-examines every repair weld before the unit comes back. We help you sequence those phases and agree with your inspector which items can move on-stream.

Louisiana adds its own constraints. Hurricane season runs from June to November, and owners often avoid planning major outages in the peak weeks; after a storm, damage assessments create a sudden spike in inspection demand across the coast. River stage and fog affect access to dock-side assets. High humidity limits coating and some couplant choices. Plant contractor prequalification and site-specific safety orientation are completed before mobilisation. Offshore and yard work follows owner and class schedules rather than turnaround seasons. Plan a Louisiana turnaround inspection.

Louisiana regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: In Louisiana, boilers fall under the Office of State Fire Marshal's boiler inspection programme, industrial radiography under the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality, intrastate pipelines under the state Department of Conservation and Energy's pipeline safety programme with PHMSA, and process safety under federal OSHA's PSM standard. Tanks are subject to EPA SPCC.

Boilers and pressure vessels: Office of State Fire Marshal

Louisiana's boiler law is administered by the Office of State Fire Marshal, whose boiler inspection section issues certificates of inspection for regulated boilers, with inspections by state inspectors or authorised insurance inspectors commissioned through the National Board. The state rules are not designed as a routine inspection programme for most unfired pressure vessels, so vessel inspection on Louisiana plants is driven mainly by OSHA PSM mechanical integrity, insurers and owner-user programmes built on API 510. Confirm the status of a specific item with the Fire Marshal's office.

Radiography: LDEQ and Agreement State status

Louisiana is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive material licences, industrial radiography rules and individual industrial radiographer certification are administered by the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ). Atlantis does not claim to hold a Louisiana radioactive material licence; radiography on Atlantis scopes is carried out by radiography crews licensed in Louisiana, working to procedures reviewed under our Level III. Where a radiation exclusion zone would disrupt a running unit, PAUT or TOFD can be proposed if your code and owner accept it.

Pipelines: Department of Conservation and Energy and PHMSA

Intrastate natural gas and hazardous liquid pipeline safety in Louisiana is overseen by the state's pipeline safety programme, part of the Louisiana Department of Conservation and Energy (formerly the Department of Natural Resources, later the Department of Energy and Natural Resources), acting as PHMSA's state partner; PHMSA regulates interstate lines under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Agency names have changed recently, so confirm the current licensing and oversight authority with the state. Offshore facilities on the outer continental shelf fall under federal agencies including BSEE. See pipeline inspection services and Baton Rouge pipeline inspection.

Process safety and tanks

Louisiana private-sector employers fall under federal OSHA. The PSM standard (29 CFR 1910.119) requires inspection and testing of covered process equipment following recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, with each inspection documented. Aboveground oil storage is subject to EPA's SPCC rule (40 CFR Part 112), which expects integrity testing to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001. LDEQ also regulates air and water permits that can drive inspection of specific equipment.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers every Louisiana inspection as a digital report from our own reporting platform: readings, indications and photos tied to asset and location, with the procedure, acceptance criteria, technician certification and instrument calibration recorded. Reports are reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight before release.

Reports get rejected for the same reasons everywhere: untraceable readings, missing acceptance criteria, unknown technician qualifications and absent calibration records. Our platform captures data in the field (offline where there is no signal, which is common on remote pipeline right-of-ways and inside units), structures it per asset and CML, and exports it in formats your inspection database can import. See NDT inspection software and NDT reporting in New Orleans.

Results can also flow further: into Atlantis ERP for scheduling, technician certifications and invoicing, or onto a 3D model in our digital twin platform (see digital twins in Louisiana). Level III-led inspection, digital report and optional twin from one company is a combination the large inspection firms do not offer on a single page.

Cities we cover across Louisiana

Direct answer: Atlantis mobilises inspection crews to client sites anywhere in Louisiana. There is no physical Atlantis office in the state; crews travel to your plant, terminal, yard or pipeline and the schedule is agreed during scoping.   • Baton Rouge and the chemical corridor: third-party inspection, pipeline inspection, corrosion inspection, Donaldsonville and petrochemical NDT consulting.
  • New Orleans and the lower river: weld inspection, pressure vessel inspection, pipeline inspection, Garyville, Norco and Chalmette.
  • Lake Charles and the south-west: third-party inspection, refining NDT consulting and maritime NDT consulting.
  • Acadiana and the coast: Lafayette, Houma and maritime NDT in New Orleans.
  • North Louisiana: Shreveport, Monroe and Alexandria.

Related Louisiana hubs: NDT consulting in Louisiana for Level III services and written practices, and NDT training in Louisiana for ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based courses.

How to request inspection

Direct answer: Send Atlantis the asset, method, site, governing code, dates and deliverable. We reply with questions or a scoped quote, share procedures and technician certifications for your review, mobilise crews on the agreed date and deliver a Level III-reviewed digital report.

  1. Describe the job. Asset type, method if known, Louisiana site, governing code (API 510/570/653, ASME, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or class rules), target dates, quantities and report format. Send your Louisiana RFQ.
  2. Scoping call. Method and technique, access (scaffold, rope access, insulation removal, entry, marine access), site safety and whether RT or an ultrasonic alternative fits.
  3. Quote and procedures. Scope, quote, procedures and certifications for your inspector of record.
  4. Mobilisation. Site orientation and crew mobilisation on the date agreed during scoping.
  5. Inspection. Critical findings are reported to your representative during the shift they are found.
  6. Report. A digital, code-referenced report reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight.

Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in Louisiana

What NDT inspection services do you provide in Louisiana?

UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional UT, radiography through Louisiana-licensed crews, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes and pipeline inspection, all under ASNT Level III oversight.

Do you have an office in Baton Rouge or Lake Charles?

No. Atlantis has no physical office in Louisiana. Crews mobilise to your site and the schedule is agreed during scoping.

Who licenses industrial radiography in Louisiana?

Louisiana is an NRC Agreement State, and the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality licenses radioactive material and certifies industrial radiographers. Radiography on our scopes is done by crews licensed in Louisiana.

Does the state inspect pressure vessels in Louisiana?

The Office of State Fire Marshal inspects regulated boilers. Its rules are not a routine inspection programme for most unfired pressure vessels, so plant vessels are usually inspected under OSHA PSM, insurer and owner-user programmes based on API 510. Check specific items with the Fire Marshal.

Can you support API 653 inspections at river terminals?

Yes. We perform floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell thickness, weld examination and settlement measurement. Your API 653-certified Authorized Inspector remains the inspector of record.

Can you work at LNG terminals in Cameron Parish?

Yes, subject to the owner's contractor prequalification and site safety requirements. Typical LNG scope is PT, RT and PAUT on stainless and nickel-alloy welds and thickness surveys on tanks and vessels.

How much does NDT inspection cost in Louisiana?

Atlantis quotes on request. Cost depends on method, quantity, access, travel, crew size, schedule (turnaround or routine) and the report format. Send the scope for a written quote.

Can inspection be done on-stream?

Many thickness surveys, external visual examinations and some weld examinations can be done while the unit runs, within temperature limits and site permits. Doing them before a turnaround reduces outage scope.

Who regulates pipelines in Louisiana?

Intrastate pipelines are overseen by the state pipeline safety programme in the Louisiana Department of Conservation and Energy, as PHMSA's state partner; PHMSA regulates interstate lines. Agency names have changed recently, so confirm the current authority with the state.

Do you inspect shipyard and offshore fabrication welds?

Yes. UT, RT, MT and VT on structural and pressure welds in Houma, Morgan City and similar yards, to AWS D1.1, ASME or the class and owner specifications that apply.

What happens after a hurricane?

Post-storm inspection usually starts with visual and thickness checks on tanks, piping supports and docks, then targeted NDE where damage is found. Contact us with the assets affected and we will scope a campaign.

Do you provide RBI or fitness-for-service assessments?

No. Atlantis does not offer API 580/581 RBI or API 579 FFS assessments; we provide the inspection data those programmes rely on.

Get a Louisiana inspection scope

A turnaround weld list in Geismar, a tank floor at a Garyville terminal, LNG piping welds in Cameron Parish, a separator survey in the Haynesville or yard welds in Houma all start the same way: send the asset, method, code and dates. Get a quote for NDT inspection in Louisiana, or talk to our ASNT Level III about method selection. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. See also all inspection services.

contentHtml:

NDT Inspection Services in Michigan

In brief: Atlantis NDT carries out non-destructive testing for plants, mills, utilities, pipelines and fabricators across Michigan, from Detroit and Downriver to the Great Lakes Bay Region, West Michigan and the Upper Peninsula. Services cover ultrasonic thickness and corrosion surveys, phased array (PAUT) and TOFD weld examination, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual and eddy current testing, and radiography performed by radiography crews licensed in Michigan. Every job runs on Level III-approved procedures, uses ASNT-certified technicians, and ends in a code-referenced digital report.

Michigan's inspection market looks nothing like the Gulf Coast. The state has a single crude refinery, but it has one of the largest chemical complexes in the Midwest, the biggest underground natural gas storage capacity of any state, three nuclear sites on its lake shores, a heavy coal-and-gas utility fleet, integrated and mini-mill steelmaking, an automotive and battery manufacturing base that is being rebuilt plant by plant, and a winter that turns corrosion under insulation and freeze-thaw damage into routine findings. Those assets are owned by very different organisations, and each asks for something slightly different from an NDT contractor. This page sets out where the work is, which methods and codes apply, who regulates what in Michigan, and how we scope a job. If you already know what you need, send us your Michigan inspection request.

Where inspection work is in Michigan

Direct answer: Michigan inspection demand clusters in six areas: Detroit, Downriver and the Rouge industrial corridor; Monroe and the Lake Erie shoreline; the Great Lakes Bay Region around Midland, Saginaw and Bay City; West Michigan from Grand Rapids to the lakeshore nuclear plants; the Lansing and I-94 manufacturing belt; and the northern Lower Peninsula and Upper Peninsula, with pipelines, gas storage, mines and paper mills.

Detroit, Downriver and the Rouge

Southwest Detroit is home to the Marathon Detroit refinery, the only operating crude refinery in Michigan, surrounded by terminals, rail racks and product pipelines. Along the Rouge River and Downriver communities sit steelmaking at Dearborn, chemical sites such as BASF's Wyandotte operations, cement and aggregate terminals, wastewater treatment plants and the assembly and stamping plants of the Detroit automakers and their tier suppliers. Refinery and terminal work is classic mechanical-integrity NDE: thickness readings at condition monitoring locations on process piping, weld examination after repairs and tie-ins, and API 653 tank work. Steel and automotive sites generate a different mix: magnetic particle and ultrasonic inspection of crane runways, press frames, ladles and rolling-mill components, weld inspection on structural steel to AWS D1.1, and shaft and gear inspection during planned outages. Large crossings over the Detroit River, including the new Gordie Howe International Bridge, keep structural weld inspection and bridge-related NDT in demand around the city.

Monroe and the Lake Erie shoreline

Monroe County hosts one of the largest coal-fired generating stations in the country at Monroe and the Fermi 2 nuclear plant near Newport. Fossil units need boiler tube thickness surveys, header and steam-line weld examination, and inspection of high-energy piping, ductwork and coal-handling structures during spring and autumn outages. Nuclear work is governed by the owner's ASME Section XI programme and its own qualification requirements; independent contractors normally support balance-of-plant and non-safety scopes unless the owner qualifies them for more.

Great Lakes Bay Region: Midland, Saginaw and Bay City

Midland is built around Dow's Michigan Operations, a large chemical manufacturing complex, with polysilicon production at Hemlock Semiconductor nearby and chemical, food and materials plants spread through Saginaw and Bay County. Chemical units bring a heavy load of pressure vessels, heat exchangers, process piping and storage tanks, much of it in stainless and alloy steels where penetrant testing and PAUT matter. Corrosion under insulation is a persistent theme on lines that cycle between warm process temperatures and Michigan winters. Saginaw's castings and powertrain plants and Bay City's port terminals add machinery and structural scopes.

West Michigan: Grand Rapids, Muskegon and the lakeshore

The Grand Rapids, Holland and Muskegon area is a dense manufacturing region with aerospace electronics and structures suppliers, office-furniture and automotive component makers, foundries, food processing and paper converting. Aerospace parts flow down customer NDT requirements, often NAS 410-based, while foundries and fabricators need UT, MT and PT on castings and weldments. Along the shoreline sit the D.C. Cook nuclear plant at Bridgman, the Palisades plant near Covert, where Holtec has been working through its return-to-service programme, and the Ludington pumped storage plant, whose penstocks and mechanical equipment are classic structural NDT subjects. Kalamazoo and Portage add pharmaceutical manufacturing with stainless piping and vessels.

Lansing and the I-94 manufacturing belt

Mid-Michigan combines vehicle assembly around Lansing, battery cell manufacturing, power generation, university campuses with central heating plants, and a long belt of machining, casting and fabrication shops from Jackson through Battle Creek toward Kalamazoo. Typical requests are weld inspection on new structural steel and equipment skids, boiler and pressure-vessel NDE for campus and industrial steam systems, and ultrasonic testing of rotating equipment and press components during scheduled shutdowns.

Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula

North of the Saginaw Bay line the work changes again. Michigan holds the largest underground natural gas storage capacity in the United States, with storage fields, compressor stations and transmission lines feeding the Midwest. Enbridge's Line 5 crosses the Straits of Mackinac, the Antrim Shale and other gas fields have gathering systems and processing plants, and the Upper Peninsula has the Tilden iron mine near Ishpeming, the Eagle nickel-copper mine, paper and pulp mills, and the Soo Locks at Sault Ste. Marie, which serve the Great Lakes bulk fleet. Pipeline welds, compressor-station piping, mining equipment, mill digesters and recovery boilers, and vessel and dock structures all need periodic NDT. Distances and winter access mean scopes are best planned in campaigns.

NDT methods we deliver in Michigan

Direct answer: Atlantis performs UT thickness and corrosion mapping, conventional shear-wave UT, PAUT, TOFD, radiography via radiography crews licensed in Michigan, MT, PT, VT and eddy current. The table shows how each method is typically used on Michigan assets and the code or standard most often cited. Method choice is confirmed with your inspector of record or engineer during scoping.

MethodTypical Michigan applicationCode / standard usually cited
UT thickness and corrosion mappingCML surveys on refinery and chemical piping; boiler tube and header wall-loss surveys at utility plants; tank shells at Detroit-area terminals; CUI follow-up after insulation removalAPI 570, API 510, API 653; ASME Section V Article 23 (SE-797 practice)
Phased array UT (PAUT)Repair and tie-in welds in chemical and refinery units; new piping and pressure equipment at battery and manufacturing plants; crack detection on high-energy piping weldsASME Section V Article 4; ASME B31.1 and B31.3 acceptance; ASME Section VIII; API 1104 on pipelines
TOFDThick-wall vessel welds and heavy headers; sizing of planar flaws found by PAUT or conventional UTASME Section V Article 4 and owner-specified code cases
Radiography (RT)Small-bore and socket welds; gas pipeline girth welds; shop fabrication of vessels and spools; casting radiography where specifiedASME Section V Article 2; API 1104; ASME B31.1/B31.3
Magnetic particle (MT)Crane runways, press frames and mill components in steel and automotive plants; nozzle and attachment welds; mining equipmentASME Section V Article 7; AWS D1.1; ASTM E709 practice
Penetrant (PT)Stainless and alloy welds in chemical, polysilicon and pharmaceutical plants; aluminium and non-magnetic componentsASME Section V Article 6; ASTM E165 practice
Visual (VT)External inspection of vessels, piping, tanks and supports; weld fit-up and final visual on structural steel and bridgesAPI 510/570/653 practices; AWS D1.1 and D1.5; ASME Section V Article 9
Eddy current (ET)Surface-crack screening through coatings; heat-exchanger and condenser tube inspection where scoped; aerospace and automotive componentsASME Section V Article 8; customer and owner procedures

All techniques are performed to written procedures approved by an ASNT NDT Level III, by technicians certified under an SNT-TC-1A written practice. If your plant uses its own procedures or requires technique demonstrations before work starts, we qualify to those. City-level method pages exist for ultrasonic testing in Detroit, radiographic testing in Detroit, magnetic particle testing in Detroit, penetrant testing in Detroit, eddy current testing in Detroit and visual testing in Detroit.

API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in Michigan

Direct answer: For Michigan owners running API 510, API 570 or API 653 programmes, Atlantis supplies the nondestructive examination those inspections are built on, including thickness data, weld examination, tank floor follow-up and visual findings, and passes the documented results to the owner's API-certified Authorized Inspector. That inspector stays the inspector of record and signs the inspection report.

Pressure vessels (API 510). Chemical reactors, columns, drums and exchangers in the Great Lakes Bay Region, refinery vessels in Detroit and process vessels at food, pharmaceutical and gas-processing plants all follow similar patterns. We take UT thickness at each vessel's CMLs, examine nozzle and attachment welds with MT or PT during entries, apply PAUT or TOFD where cracking, prior repairs or service conditions justify it, and record external visual condition including insulation and supports. Readings are reported beside the previous survey so your inspector can work out corrosion rates and intervals. More detail: API 510 pressure vessel inspection support and pressure vessel inspection in Detroit.

Process piping (API 570). In Michigan the biggest piping risk is often external: insulated lines that sit cold and wet for months, then warm up, are prime CUI candidates. We survey CMLs to your isometrics, add scanning at injection points, deadlegs and soil-to-air interfaces where your programme requires it, and support CUI campaigns with UT once insulation is stripped. Results are delivered per CML for import into your inspection data system. See API 570 piping inspection support and piping inspection in Detroit.

Storage tanks (API 653). Michigan's tank population sits mostly at Detroit-area terminals, refinery and chemical tank farms, utility fuel-oil storage and pipeline breakout stations. For out-of-service work we perform floor scanning with UT prove-up, shell course thickness, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination, and nozzle work; for in-service externals we measure shell thickness, inspect the shell, roof, foundation and appurtenances, and take settlement readings for your inspector's Annex B evaluation. Frost heave at the foundation and ice damage to roofs and appurtenances are Michigan-specific items worth adding to the checklist. See API 653 tank inspection support and tank inspection in Detroit.

Atlantis does not provide risk-based inspection (API 580/581) studies or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments. We give your engineers well-organised, traceable data; integrity decisions stay inside your programme.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: Michigan inspection work follows two calendars: refinery and chemical turnarounds, and utility outages, which both favour spring and autumn because summer demand and winter conditions make those seasons hard. Atlantis joins at the planning stage, agrees methods and procedures, and mobilises crews to your site on the dates fixed during scoping.

Weather drives more of the planning here than in southern states. Outdoor tank, pipeline and structural work in January and February means cold-weather couplant, heated enclosures for some techniques, and attention to temperature limits: standard penetrant procedures under ASME Section V are qualified for a limited temperature range, and work outside it needs a procedure qualified for the actual conditions. Snow cover and frozen ground also complicate access to tank foundations and pipeline digs. Our advice to Michigan owners is to move as much on-stream work as possible, such as thickness surveys, external visual and many weld examinations, into the warmer months ahead of an outage, so the outage itself carries only the work that needs isolation or entry.

Utility outages have their own rhythm. Fossil plants schedule boiler inspections around reduced spring and autumn load; nuclear plants run refuelling outages on cycles set by the owner, with tight contractor processing and training requirements that start weeks before the outage. Chemical plants in Midland and the Detroit refinery plan turnarounds years ahead, with NDE scopes frozen months before the start date. Manufacturing plants, especially automotive, often have short windows around summer and year-end shutdowns, when presses, cranes and furnaces are available. Tell us which calendar you work to and we will plan backwards from it. Plan a Michigan outage or shutdown inspection.

Michigan regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: In Michigan, boilers fall under the Michigan Boiler Code enforced by the Boiler Division of LARA's Bureau of Construction Codes; Michigan is not an NRC Agreement State, so NRC Region III licenses radioactive sources; the Michigan Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipelines with PHMSA; and MIOSHA enforces process safety management through General Industry Part 91.

Boilers and pressure vessels: LARA Boiler Division

The Boiler Division within the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA) Bureau of Construction Codes administers the Michigan Boiler Code, including installation permits, in-service inspections of boilers, repairs and accident investigations, with the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and the National Board Inspection Code adopted by reference. The state programme is centred on boilers; for unfired pressure vessels, inspection is usually driven by owner-user programmes built on API 510, insurer requirements and process safety rules. Confirm whether a specific item falls under state jurisdiction with the Boiler Division. Repairs and alterations to code items are made by organisations holding the appropriate National Board authorisation, with NDE performed to the construction or repair code.

Radiography: a non-Agreement State

Michigan is one of the few states that has not signed an Agreement with the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Radioactive material licences for industrial radiography sources such as iridium-192 are therefore issued and inspected by the NRC through its Region III office, and radiographers using those sources work under NRC rules in 10 CFR Part 34. Industrial X-ray machines are a state matter and are registered with Michigan's radiation safety programme; responsibilities have moved between state departments over the years, so confirm the current registering agency before an X-ray job. Atlantis does not claim to hold any radioactive material licence or registration in Michigan: radiography on our scopes is performed by radiography crews licensed in Michigan (or under NRC licence for source work), working to Atlantis procedures with Level III review. Where an exclusion zone would disrupt a running unit, PAUT or TOFD may replace radiography if your code and owner accept it.

Pipelines: MPSC and PHMSA

The Michigan Public Service Commission's gas safety programme acts as PHMSA's state partner for intrastate natural gas pipelines and distribution systems, while PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous liquid lines directly under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, including the large liquids lines that cross the state. New-construction girth welds normally follow API 1104. See pipeline inspection services and pipeline inspection in Detroit.

Process safety, tanks and the environment

Michigan runs its own occupational safety and health plan. MIOSHA's General Industry Part 91 adopts the federal process safety management standard (29 CFR 1910.119) by reference, so covered processes need mechanical integrity procedures, inspection and testing to recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, and documentation of every inspection. Aboveground oil storage is subject to EPA's SPCC rule (40 CFR Part 112), which expects integrity testing to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001, and the Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) administers state rules on storage tanks and the protection of the Great Lakes watershed, which raises the stakes on any tank or pipeline release.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Each Michigan job ends with a digital report built in Atlantis's own reporting platform. Every reading, indication and photograph is linked to the asset, location, procedure, technician certification and instrument calibration, the governing acceptance criteria are quoted, and the report is reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight before release.

A report is only useful if the inspector of record, an auditor, an insurer or a MIOSHA compliance officer can follow it without calling the technician. That is why we tie every thickness reading to a named CML, every indication to the procedure and acceptance criterion applied, and every result to the technician's certification and the instrument's calibration record. Field data is captured digitally, offline where plant networks are unavailable, and structured per asset, so it can be exported to your inspection data management system rather than retyped. Read about the platform on our NDT inspection software page or compare tools in best NDT reporting software 2026.

Because Atlantis also builds business software, the data can go further than a PDF. Results can feed scheduling, certification tracking and invoicing in Atlantis ERP for Michigan inspection companies, or be placed on a 3D model of the unit in our digital twin platform; see digital twins in Michigan and digital twins in Detroit. One provider covering Level III-led inspection, the digital report and an optional twin is rare among inspection contractors.

Cities we cover across Michigan

Direct answer: Atlantis mobilises inspection crews to sites anywhere in Michigan. There is no Atlantis office or lab in the state; crews travel to your plant, terminal, mill, yard or right-of-way, with dates agreed during scoping. These pages cover individual Michigan cities in more depth.

  • Detroit and Downriver: third-party inspection in Detroit, weld inspection, corrosion inspection, NDT consulting in Detroit, refining NDT consulting, steel NDT consulting and Trenton.
  • Dearborn: digital twins in Dearborn and inspection management software in Dearborn.
  • Great Lakes Bay Region: NDT consulting in Bay City, Saginaw practical NDT and Saginaw inspection software; Midland chemical sites by arrangement.
  • West Michigan: steel NDT consulting in Grand Rapids and Grand Rapids practical NDT; Muskegon, Holland, Kalamazoo and the lakeshore plants by arrangement.
  • Flint and Mid-Michigan: steel NDT consulting in Flint and Flint practical NDT; Lansing and the I-94 belt by arrangement.
  • Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula: pipeline, gas storage, mine and mill sites by arrangement, planned as multi-site campaigns.

Related Michigan hubs: NDT consulting in Michigan for Level III services, written practices and procedure work, and NDT training in Michigan for ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based technician courses. Technicians in Detroit can also look at NDT training in Detroit and the Practical NDT simulator for Michigan.

How to request inspection

Direct answer: Tell us the asset, location, method, governing code, dates and the deliverable you need. We come back with questions or a scope and quote, share procedures and technician certifications for approval, mobilise on the agreed date and deliver a Level III-reviewed digital report.

  1. Send the request. Include the asset type (vessel, piping circuit, tank, boiler, pipeline, structure or component), the site location in Michigan, the method if you know it, the governing code (API 510/570/653, ASME, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or D1.5), quantities, dates and report format. Submit your Michigan RFQ.
  2. Scoping discussion. We confirm technique, access (scaffold, insulation removal, confined-space entry, winter access), site safety and contractor prequalification, and whether radiography or an ultrasonic alternative suits your unit.
  3. Scope, quote and documents. You receive a written scope and quote with the procedures and technician certifications your inspector of record needs to review.
  4. Mobilisation. The crew completes your site orientation and arrives on the agreed date.
  5. Inspection. Significant findings are reported to your representative during the shift, not saved for the final report.
  6. Report and close-out. A digital report reviewed under Level III oversight, traceable to code, procedure, technician and instrument, ready for your inspector and your records.

Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in Michigan

What NDT inspection services does Atlantis provide in Michigan?

UT thickness and corrosion mapping, conventional UT, PAUT, TOFD, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Michigan, MT, PT, VT and eddy current, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes and pipeline work, all under ASNT Level III oversight.

Does Atlantis have an office in Detroit or Grand Rapids?

No. Atlantis has no physical office or laboratory in Michigan. Crews are mobilised to your site anywhere in the state, and the schedule is agreed during scoping.

Is Michigan an NRC Agreement State for radiography?

No. Michigan has not signed an Agreement with the NRC, so licences for radioactive sources used in industrial radiography are issued by the NRC through Region III. Industrial X-ray machines are registered with the state. Radiography on our jobs is carried out by appropriately licensed radiography crews.

Who inspects boilers in Michigan?

The Boiler Division of LARA's Bureau of Construction Codes administers the Michigan Boiler Code, including permits and in-service inspections. For unfired pressure vessels, inspection is usually driven by owner programmes based on API 510, insurers and process safety rules; confirm jurisdiction for specific items with the Boiler Division.

Can you perform API 653 tank inspection in Michigan?

We perform the NDE an API 653 inspection relies on, including floor scanning with UT prove-up, shell thickness, weld examination and settlement measurement. Your API 653-certified Authorized Inspector remains the inspector of record and signs the report.

Can NDT be done in a Michigan winter?

Yes, with planning. Cold affects couplants, penetrant temperature limits and access to foundations and digs, so outdoor scopes may need heated enclosures or procedures qualified for low temperatures. Where possible we move on-stream work into warmer months ahead of an outage.

Do you inspect for corrosion under insulation?

Yes. We support CUI programmes with visual inspection, UT thickness and corrosion mapping once insulation is removed, focusing on locations your programme identifies, such as low points, supports and damaged jacketing.

How much does NDT inspection cost in Michigan?

Atlantis quotes on request. Cost depends on the method, the number of locations or welds, access requirements, travel to the site, crew size, schedule, weather protection and report format. Send the scope and you will receive a written quote.

Who regulates pipelines in Michigan?

The Michigan Public Service Commission oversees intrastate natural gas pipeline safety as PHMSA's state partner, while PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous liquid pipelines directly. Girth welds on new lines usually follow API 1104.

Do MIOSHA process safety rules require inspection records?

Yes. MIOSHA General Industry Part 91 adopts the federal PSM standard, which requires inspection and testing of covered equipment to recognised good engineering practice and documentation of each inspection. Our reports are structured to support that record.

Do you work in the Upper Peninsula?

Yes, by arrangement. Because of distances and seasonal access, we plan Upper Peninsula and northern Michigan work as campaigns covering several sites, such as compressor stations, mills or mine equipment, per mobilisation.

Do you offer RBI or fitness-for-service studies?

No. Atlantis does not sell API 580/581 risk-based inspection or API 579 fitness-for-service assessments. We provide the inspection data those programmes rely on.

A tank due for its out-of-service inspection at a Detroit terminal, a chemical unit turnaround in Midland, a boiler outage at a lakeshore power plant, a crane runway in a Dearborn mill or a pipeline tie-in up north all start the same way: send the asset, method, code and dates.
