HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Inspection Services in Mississippi

In brief: Atlantis NDT supplies non-destructive testing to Mississippi refineries, shipyards, LNG and chemical plants, power stations, steel and aluminium mills, automotive and aerospace manufacturers and pipeline operators. Methods include UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT and TOFD weld examination, radiography carried out by radiography crews licensed in Mississippi, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual and eddy current testing, plus the NDE that API 510, API 570 and API 653 inspections rely on. Work is performed by ASNT-certified technicians under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, crews are mobilised to your site, and results arrive as a code-referenced digital report.

Mississippi's inspection work is concentrated in fewer places than in its larger neighbours, but those places are heavy. Pascagoula alone has the state's largest refinery, a Navy shipyard, an LNG terminal and a port chemical district within a few miles of each other. The Mississippi River side has a second refinery and a large nuclear station. The Golden Triangle in the northeast has become a steel and aluminium centre, central and north Mississippi build cars, and the Pine Belt and southwest corner produce oil and gas and store natural gas in salt caverns. Pipelines that move fuel and gas from the Gulf to the rest of the country cross the whole state. This page maps that market, sets out which Mississippi and federal regulators shape inspection, and explains how Atlantis scopes, performs and reports a job. To start now, send your Mississippi inspection request.

Where inspection work is in Mississippi

Direct answer: Mississippi inspection demand centres on the Gulf Coast (Pascagoula's refinery, shipyards, LNG and chemical plants, Gulfport and Stennis), the Mississippi River corridor (Vicksburg refinery, Grand Gulf nuclear, Natchez terminals), metro Jackson and Canton, the Golden Triangle steel and aerospace cluster around Columbus, north Mississippi manufacturing around Tupelo, and the Pine Belt oil, gas and storage area around Hattiesburg and Laurel.

Pascagoula and Jackson County

Pascagoula is the most inspection-intensive square mile in the state. Chevron's Pascagoula refinery, the largest in Mississippi, runs crude units, cokers, hydroprocessing and a large tank farm, with turnaround NDE scopes typical of a major Gulf Coast refinery: CML thickness surveys on piping circuits, PAUT and radiography on repair and tie-in welds, exchanger and vessel work during entries, and API 653 tank inspections. Next door, Ingalls Shipbuilding builds destroyers, amphibious ships and Coast Guard cutters, where weld inspection follows Navy requirements such as NAVSEA Technical Publication 271 and MIL-STD-2035 rather than commercial codes, and other yards in the area build and repair commercial and government vessels. The Gulf LNG terminal and the Bayou Casotte port district add cryogenic piping, tankage and chemical plant scopes, and Mississippi Power's Plant Daniel near Escatawpa adds boiler, high-energy piping and balance-of-plant inspection. Coastal heat, salt air and humidity make atmospheric corrosion and CUI the normal damage mechanisms, and hurricane season shapes both scheduling and post-storm inspection.

Gulfport, Biloxi and Hancock County

The Port of Gulfport handles containers, fruit and bulk cargo, and its cranes, wharf structures and fuel facilities need periodic structural and corrosion inspection. Military installations along the coast, including the Naval Construction Battalion Center in Gulfport and Keesler Air Force Base in Biloxi, drive maintenance and construction work. A titanium dioxide plant at DeLisle and other chemical and manufacturing sites around Bay St. Louis and Pass Christian generate vessel, piping and tank scopes. Further west, NASA's Stennis Space Center tests rocket engines and stages using high-pressure gas and cryogenic propellant systems, an environment where pressure-system integrity and weld quality are tightly controlled by the agency and its contractors.

The Mississippi River corridor: Vicksburg, Port Gibson and Natchez

Ergon's refinery at Vicksburg processes crude into specialty products such as asphalt and naphthenic oils, which brings its own corrosion and weld-inspection programme, and river terminals at Vicksburg and Natchez store and transfer fuels, chemicals and fertiliser. Near Port Gibson, Entergy's Grand Gulf Nuclear Station, a large single-unit boiling water reactor, runs its NDE under ASME Section XI and owner programmes, with refuelling outages that draw in qualified contractors under tight processing rules. River bridges, locks and port structures add structural steel inspection, typically to AWS D1.1 or D1.5.

Metro Jackson and Canton

The capital area mixes state and federal facilities, hospitals and universities with central steam and chilled-water plants, power generation, and manufacturing. Nissan's Canton assembly plant and its supplier park generate weld inspection on new structures and equipment, press and die inspection, and boiler and pressure-vessel NDE for plant utilities. Fabrication shops serving the oil, gas and power sectors in the Jackson area need UT, MT, PT and radiography on vessels, skids and piping spools built to ASME Section VIII and B31.3.

The Golden Triangle: Columbus, Starkville and West Point

Lowndes County has become one of the South's metals centres. Steel Dynamics operates a flat-rolled steel mill at Columbus and has added an aluminium flat-rolled mill nearby, while Airbus Helicopters, Aurora Flight Sciences and Columbus Air Force Base give the area an aerospace layer. Mills generate constant demand for UT and MT on crane runways, rolls, gearboxes, shafts and structural steel, plus weld inspection on expansions; aerospace work follows the prime's NDT requirements, usually NAS 410-based. Pulp, paper and wood products in the surrounding counties add digester and boiler scopes.

North Mississippi and the Pine Belt

Around Tupelo, Toyota's Blue Springs plant, furniture manufacturing and a wide supplier base need structural and equipment weld inspection. In the south, the Pine Belt around Hattiesburg and Laurel and the southwest Mississippi oil fields produce crude and gas, salt-cavern storage near Hattiesburg holds natural gas, and the Collins area is a major junction for refined-products pipelines moving fuel from the Gulf toward the Southeast. Gathering lines, compressor stations, storage wellhead piping, tank farms and transmission lines all need API 1104 weld inspection, UT thickness surveys and tank inspection. Meridian adds naval aviation at NAS Meridian and power generation in east-central Mississippi.

Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in Mississippi

Which NDT inspection services does Atlantis offer in Mississippi?

UT thickness and corrosion mapping, conventional UT, PAUT, TOFD, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Mississippi, MT, PT, VT and eddy current, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes and pipeline work, all under ASNT Level III oversight.

Do you have an office in Pascagoula or Jackson?

No. Atlantis has no physical office or lab in Mississippi. Crews are mobilised to your site anywhere in the state, with dates agreed during scoping.

Who inspects boilers and pressure vessels in Mississippi?

The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety program of the Mississippi State Department of Health administers the state's boiler and pressure vessel law. State inspectors and commissioned inspectors from insurers or owner-user organisations carry out inspections of regulated equipment.

Is Mississippi an NRC Agreement State?

Yes. Mississippi has been an Agreement State since 1962, and the State Department of Health's Division of Radiological Health licenses radioactive materials used in industrial radiography. Radiography on our scopes is performed by crews licensed in Mississippi.

Can inspection be done without shutting the unit down?

Often. Thickness surveys, external visual, many weld examinations and some corrosion mapping can be done on-stream, subject to temperature limits and site permits. Doing them before a turnaround shrinks the scope that must wait for the outage.

How much does NDT inspection cost in Mississippi?

Atlantis quotes on request. Cost depends on the method, number of locations or welds, access requirements, travel to the site, crew size, schedule, weather contingency and report format. Send your scope and you will receive a written quote.

Who regulates pipelines in Mississippi?

Do you inspect steel and aluminium mill equipment in Columbus?

Yes. UT and MT on crane runways, rolls, shafts, gearboxes and structural steel, plus weld inspection on expansions and repairs, are typical mill scopes, usually planned into short shutdown windows.

Can you support post-hurricane inspections?

Yes. Once a site is safe to enter we can carry out visual, thickness and weld checks on tanks, wharves, piping and structures. Agree weather triggers and remobilisation terms during scoping so the plan is ready before a storm.

NDT Inspection Services in New Jersey

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides non-destructive testing inspection across New Jersey: ultrasonic thickness surveys and corrosion mapping, phased array (PAUT) and TOFD weld inspection, radiography through radiography crews licensed in New Jersey, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual and eddy current testing, plus the NDE that API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank programmes rely on. Work is performed by ASNT-certified technicians under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, crews are mobilised to your site, and results arrive as a code-referenced digital report your inspector of record can use.

New Jersey packs an unusual amount of inspection-heavy industry into a small state. The Linden-Carteret-Bayonne waterfront holds a refinery, some of the largest petroleum storage terminals on the East Coast and the northern end of major products pipelines. South Jersey along the Delaware River has another refinery, chemical plants and the Salem and Hope Creek nuclear stations. Between them sit pharmaceutical and specialty-chemical plants, gas utilities, power stations, fabrication shops and some of the busiest bridges and port terminals in the country. New Jersey also adds state rules that many states do not have, including a state boiler and pressure vessel programme, a state discharge-prevention programme and the Toxic Catastrophe Prevention Act. This page maps the market, explains the regulators, and states what Atlantis delivers and what it does not. When you are ready, request a New Jersey inspection quote.

Where inspection work is in New Jersey

Direct answer: New Jersey inspection demand concentrates on the Arthur Kill and Kill Van Kull waterfront from Linden and Carteret to Bayonne and Perth Amboy, at Port Newark-Elizabeth, in the central New Jersey pharmaceutical and chemical belt, along the Delaware River from Trenton and Camden down to Paulsboro, Deepwater and Salem County, and on the state's transmission pipelines, power plants and bridges.

Linden, Carteret, Bayonne and Perth Amboy: the northern refining and terminal belt

The Bayway refinery in Linden sits beside a dense cluster of bulk liquid terminals in Linden, Carteret, Sewaren, Perth Amboy and Bayonne, connected to products pipelines from the Gulf Coast and to barge and ship traffic in New York Harbor. The tank population in this corridor is very large, so API 653 work dominates: MFL floor scanning and UT follow-up on out-of-service tanks, shell thickness surveys and settlement measurements on in-service tanks, and weld inspection on repairs. The refinery itself runs CML thickness surveys on piping, vessel inspections, turnaround weld inspection and CUI screening. Storm surge from Hurricane Sandy in 2012 damaged tanks and terminals along this shoreline, and flood-exposed foundations and tank bottoms remain a reasonable inspection focus. See Linden, Linden refining and Perth Amboy.

Newark, Elizabeth and the Port of New York and New Jersey

Port Newark-Elizabeth is the main container gateway of the Port of New York and New Jersey, with cranes, berths, rail yards and warehousing, while Newark Liberty International Airport adds fuel farms and hydrant systems. Inspection here covers crane and lifting-equipment weld inspection with MT and UT, structural steel, aviation fuel tanks and piping, and industrial plants in the Ironbound and along the Passaic. See refining NDT consulting in Newark and NDT training in Newark.

Central Jersey: pharmaceutical, specialty chemical and manufacturing

From Rahway and Edison through Middlesex, Somerset and Mercer counties, pharmaceutical and specialty-chemical plants operate reactors, high-purity stainless piping, clean-steam generators, boilers, autoclaves and pressure vessels. Inspection here is less about wall loss on carbon steel and more about weld quality on stainless and alloy systems, PT and VT on sanitary welds, UT thickness on utility piping, vessel inspections required by the state's pressure vessel programme, and documentation that satisfies a quality system. Fabrication shops building vessels, skids and spools for these plants need RT, UT, MT and PT to ASME Section VIII and B31.3.

Trenton, Camden and the Delaware River

The Delaware River corridor has steel and metal-working heritage around Trenton, port terminals and industrial plants around Camden and Gloucester City, and power and utility assets. Typical scopes include weld inspection for fabricators and structural steel, thickness surveys at utility and industrial plants, and tank inspection at terminals. See steel NDT consulting in Trenton and practical NDT in Trenton.

Paulsboro, Deepwater and Salem County

Further south, the Paulsboro refinery, the Chambers Works chemical site at Deepwater, marine terminals and the Delaware River port facilities form a second refining and chemical cluster, with pipeline connections around Westville. On Artificial Island in Lower Alloways Creek Township, PSEG's Salem and Hope Creek stations make up one of the largest nuclear generating sites in the country; nuclear plant NDE is controlled by owner programmes and ASME Section XI, so we support those sites only within the owner's qualification requirements. The river ports also host heavy fabrication and offshore-wind-related infrastructure. See Paulsboro, Westville and pipeline NDT consulting in Westville.

Pipelines, power and bridges statewide

Interstate gas transmission lines cross the state, gas utilities run large distribution systems, and products pipelines terminate in the Linden area. Gas-fired power plants and cogeneration units need boiler, HRSG and piping inspection. New Jersey's bridges, operated by NJDOT, the New Jersey Turnpike Authority, the Port Authority and the Delaware River bridge authorities, need structural steel weld inspection on rehabilitation projects. Military installations, including Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst and Picatinny Arsenal, add contractor fabrication and facility work.

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional shear-wave UT, radiography through New Jersey-licensed radiography crews, MT, PT, VT, eddy current and MFL tank floor scanning. API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in New Jersey

Direct answer: Atlantis performs the NDE that API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank inspections rely on, including thickness surveys, weld examination, tank floor scanning and visual examination, and hands documented results to your API-certified Authorized Inspector, who remains the inspector of record and signs the inspection report.

API 510 pressure vessels. New Jersey refineries, chemical and pharmaceutical plants run towers, drums, reactors and exchangers on API 510 programmes, alongside the state's own pressure vessel inspection requirements. We carry out external visual examination, UT thickness at the vessel's CMLs, corrosion mapping where localised loss is expected, PAUT or TOFD on welds with a cracking history or prior repairs, and MT or PT on nozzles and attachments during entries, reported against previous surveys so your inspector can calculate corrosion rates and intervals. See API 510 pressure vessel inspection support.

API 570 piping. Refinery and terminal piping in Linden and Paulsboro, transfer lines between docks and tank farms, and process piping at chemical plants are surveyed against your circuit isometrics, with injection-point, mix-point and deadleg scanning and CUI screening where insulation is removed. Results are delivered per CML so they load into your inspection data system. See API 570 piping inspection support.

API 653 storage tanks. North Jersey's terminals hold one of the highest concentrations of aboveground petroleum storage on the East Coast. For out-of-service inspections we perform MFL floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell course thickness surveys, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination, nozzle and sump work and floating-roof checks; for external inspections we survey shell thickness, examine roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and take settlement measurements presented against API 653 Annex B, which matters on the soft, filled ground common along the waterfront. See API 653 tank inspection support.

What we do not do: Atlantis does not sell risk-based inspection (API 580/581) or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments, and it does not act as the Authorized Inspector. Our reports give your engineers clean, traceable data; the integrity decisions built on it stay with your programme.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: At New Jersey refineries and chemical plants, inspection volume is planned months ahead around turnarounds, while terminals schedule tanks out of service on rolling programmes. Atlantis joins the planning stage, agrees methods and procedures, and mobilises crews to your site on dates fixed during scoping.

A turnaround scope has three layers. Pre-shutdown, on-stream work covers thickness surveys, external visual inspection and in-service weld examination, and it shrinks the list of items that must be opened. Shutdown work covers vessel internals, tank floors, exchanger shells and welds behind insulation. Post-repair work is the re-examination of every repair weld before start-up. We help you sequence those layers so that scope moves out of the outage window wherever your code and inspector allow.

New Jersey specifics: terminal tank programmes often run back-to-back, so floor scanning and shell work need to keep pace with cleaning and repair contractors; pharmaceutical plants plan shutdowns around production campaigns and validation, so NDE has to fit tight windows and their documentation rules; winter weather affects outdoor PT and MT and couplant choice; and refinery and terminal access requires site-specific safety orientation, TWIC cards at many maritime facilities, and contractor prequalification completed before mobilisation. Plan a New Jersey turnaround or tank programme.

New Jersey regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: In New Jersey, boilers and pressure vessels are regulated by the Department of Labor and Workforce Development's Office of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Compliance, radiation sources by the Department of Environmental Protection, intrastate gas pipelines by the Board of Public Utilities with PHMSA, process safety by federal OSHA plus the state Toxic Catastrophe Prevention Act, and oil and hazardous-substance storage by NJDEP discharge-prevention rules and EPA SPCC.

Boilers and pressure vessels: NJDOL

New Jersey regulates both boilers and pressure vessels. The Office of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Compliance within the Department of Labor and Workforce Development registers equipment, issues certificates and oversees periodic inspection by state inspectors and authorised insurance or owner-user inspectors, under rules in N.J.A.C. 12:90. That framework expects documented inspection of in-service vessels, and plants generally build their vessel programmes on API 510 and the National Board Inspection Code. NDE data from Atlantis supports those inspections; it does not replace the commissioned inspector. Confirm the status of a specific vessel with the Office.

Radiography: NJDEP and Agreement State status

New Jersey is an NRC Agreement State, so licences for radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, are issued and inspected by the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection's radiation protection programme rather than by the NRC directly. Atlantis does not claim to hold a New Jersey radioactive material licence: radiography on Atlantis scopes is performed by radiography crews licensed in New Jersey, working to reviewed procedures under our Level III. Where exclusion zones would disrupt a live unit, a busy terminal or a dense urban site, PAUT or TOFD may be an alternative if your code and owner accept it.

Pipelines: Board of Public Utilities and PHMSA

The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities runs the state pipeline safety programme for intrastate natural gas pipelines and distribution systems in partnership with PHMSA, which regulates interstate gas and hazardous liquid lines under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Girth-weld inspection on new construction normally follows API 1104. See our pipeline inspection services and pipeline inspection in the New York metro area.

Process safety: OSHA PSM and the Toxic Catastrophe Prevention Act

Private-sector employers in New Jersey fall under federal OSHA, whose process safety management standard (29 CFR 1910.119) requires written inspection and testing procedures, inspection following recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, and documentation of each inspection for covered equipment. New Jersey adds the Toxic Catastrophe Prevention Act, administered by NJDEP under N.J.A.C. 7:31, which requires risk management programmes at facilities handling extraordinarily hazardous substances, including attention to the mechanical integrity of covered equipment. Owners should confirm their obligations with NJDEP; for inspection, the effect is a strong need for traceable records.

Tanks: discharge prevention and SPCC

Major facilities storing petroleum or hazardous substances are subject to NJDEP's Discharge Prevention, Containment and Countermeasure rules (N.J.A.C. 7:1E) in addition to EPA's SPCC rule (40 CFR Part 112), which expects tank integrity testing to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001. Together they keep tank condition, inspection schedules and documentation in front of New Jersey terminal operators.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Every Atlantis inspection in New Jersey produces a digital report built in our own reporting platform: each reading, indication and photo tied to the asset, location, procedure, technician certification and instrument calibration, with acceptance criteria quoted from the governing code. Reports are reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight before release.

Inspectors of record, state boiler inspectors, NJDEP and quality auditors reject reports for predictable reasons: thickness readings that cannot be traced to a CML, indications without a procedure and acceptance criterion, technicians whose certification cannot be shown, and instruments without calibration records. Pharmaceutical clients add their own documentation expectations. Our reporting software is built around those failure points: field capture, offline where needed, structured per asset and location, and exports your inspection data management or quality system can import. Read more on our NDT inspection software page, or compare options in best NDT reporting software 2026.

The data can go further than a PDF. Results can feed scheduling, certification tracking and invoicing in Atlantis ERP (see NDT ERP in Linden and Paulsboro), or be placed on a 3D model of the unit or tank farm in our digital twin platform (see digital twins in Linden and Paulsboro). That route from Level III-led inspection to digital report to optional twin is not offered as one package by the large inspection firms.

Cities we cover across New Jersey

Direct answer: Atlantis mobilises inspection crews to client sites anywhere in New Jersey, from Bergen County to Cape May. Atlantis has no physical office in New Jersey, so crews travel to your plant, terminal, yard or right-of-way, with the schedule agreed during scoping. Which NDT inspection services does Atlantis offer in New Jersey?

UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional UT, radiography through New Jersey-licensed radiography crews, MT, PT, VT, ET and MFL tank floor scanning, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes and pipeline inspection, under ASNT Level III oversight.

Do you have an office in New Jersey?

Does New Jersey require pressure vessel inspections?

A New Jersey law, administered by NJDEP, that requires risk management programmes at facilities handling extraordinarily hazardous substances. It sits alongside federal OSHA PSM and EPA rules and increases the value of complete inspection records.

Can inspection be done without shutting the unit down?

NDT Inspection Services in New York

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides non-destructive testing inspection across New York State: ultrasonic thickness surveys and corrosion mapping, phased array (PAUT) and TOFD weld inspection, radiography through radiography crews licensed in New York, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual and eddy current testing, plus the NDE that API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank programmes rely on. Work is performed by ASNT-certified technicians under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, crews are mobilised to your site, from New York City and Long Island to Albany, Syracuse, Rochester and Buffalo, and results arrive as a code-referenced digital report.

New York's inspection market looks different from the Gulf Coast. The state has no operating petroleum refinery, but it has large fuel terminals around New York Harbor, the Hudson at Albany and the Great Lakes ports; three operating nuclear generating stations on Lake Ontario; the large hydropower plants at Niagara and on the St. Lawrence; one of the biggest district steam systems in the world under Manhattan; thousands of bridges exposed to road salt and freeze-thaw; and an upstate manufacturing base that builds turbines, semiconductors, aerospace systems and glass. New York also splits some regulation between the state and New York City. This page maps the market by region, explains the agencies that shape inspection scope, and states what Atlantis delivers and what it does not. When you are ready, request a New York inspection quote with the asset, method, code and dates.

Where inspection work is in New York

Direct answer: New York inspection demand concentrates in the New York City and Long Island metro area (terminals, utilities, steam, bridges and construction), the Hudson Valley and Capital Region (Port of Albany terminals, power and advanced manufacturing), Central New York (Syracuse and the Oswego nuclear sites), and Western New York (Rochester, Buffalo and Niagara Falls industry and hydropower).

New York City, Long Island and the harbor

Petroleum products reach the metro area by tanker, barge and pipeline and are stored at terminals in Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island and on Long Island, with more terminals across the harbor in New Jersey. Those tank farms run API 653 programmes. Con Edison's Manhattan steam system, utility gas mains, power plants in Queens and on Long Island, and building boilers and pressure vessels add piping, weld and thickness work. Construction is the other big driver: structural steel welding on high-rise and infrastructure projects needs UT, MT and VT under the engineer of record's specification. In New York City, structural special inspections are performed under the Department of Buildings' special inspection rules by registered agencies; where your project needs one, ask during scoping how NDT fits under that agency's responsibilities. See third-party inspection in New York, New York tank inspection and New York weld inspection.

Hudson Valley and the Capital Region

The Port of Albany and Rensselaer hold large petroleum terminals that supply much of upstate New York and New England by barge, rail and truck, and their tank populations need floor scanning, shell surveys and weld inspection. The Capital Region also has a deep manufacturing base: gas and steam turbine manufacturing in Schenectady, semiconductor fabrication in Malta, the Watervliet Arsenal, naval nuclear research and power plants along the Hudson. Indian Point in Westchester County shut down in 2021 and is being decommissioned. Typical scopes are tank inspection at terminals, weld and fabrication NDE for heavy manufacturing, and boiler and piping thickness surveys at plants. See practical NDT in Albany.

Central New York: Syracuse and the Oswego nuclear sites

On Lake Ontario near Oswego, the Nine Mile Point and James A. FitzPatrick stations form one of the largest nuclear generating complexes in the Northeast, with the R.E. Ginna station further west near Rochester. Nuclear NDE is controlled by owner programmes and ASME Section XI, so we support those sites only within the owner's qualification requirements, typically on balance-of-plant and non-safety-related scopes. Syracuse adds defence electronics and manufacturing, and a large semiconductor project in Onondaga County is bringing major construction to the region, with structural, piping and pressure equipment that needs fabrication and installation NDE. See NDT consulting in Oswego and nuclear NDT consulting in Oswego.

Rochester and the Finger Lakes

Rochester's industrial base includes optics, imaging and chemical production at the Eastman Business Park, precision manufacturing and food processing, with glass and ceramics manufacturing in Corning to the south. Inspection here is weighted toward boiler and pressure vessel NDE, process piping thickness surveys, weld inspection for fabricators, and plant utilities. See NDT consulting in Rochester and practical NDT in Rochester.

Buffalo, Niagara Falls and the Western New York lakeshore

Western New York combines chemical plants in Niagara Falls, the Robert Moses Niagara hydroelectric plant, petroleum terminals on the Buffalo waterfront, steel fabrication and heavy manufacturing, aerospace and motion-control suppliers around Buffalo, and grain and bulk handling. Lake-effect winters, road salt and freeze-thaw cycles drive atmospheric corrosion and make outdoor NDT a seasonal planning problem. Typical scopes include penstock and gate weld inspection at hydro sites, chemical-plant vessel and piping NDE, tank inspection and structural steel. See NDT consulting in Buffalo, Buffalo refining and fuels and Niagara Falls.

North Country and statewide infrastructure

The St. Lawrence-FDR power project at Massena, paper mills and aluminium production in the North Country, and interstate gas pipelines crossing the Southern Tier and Hudson Valley add work across the state. New York's bridges, from the Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge and the Verrazzano-Narrows to thousands of state and county spans, need steel weld inspection on rehabilitation, and offshore wind projects are using port facilities in New York City and the Capital Region for staging and fabrication.

NDT methods we deliver in New York

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional shear-wave UT, radiography through New York-licensed radiography crews, MT, PT, VT, eddy current and MFL tank floor scanning. The table maps each method to typical New York applications and the code usually cited; final selection is agreed with your inspector of record during scoping.

Every technique runs on a written procedure reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III, and every technician is certified under an SNT-TC-1A written practice. API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in New York

Direct answer: Atlantis performs the NDE that API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank inspections rely on, including thickness surveys, weld examination, tank floor scanning and visual examination, and hands documented results to your API-certified Authorized Inspector, who remains the inspector of record and signs the inspection report.

API 653 storage tanks. Because New York has no operating refinery, tanks are the largest API scope in the state: terminals in the harbor, at Albany and Rensselaer, on the Buffalo waterfront and on Long Island, plus fuel storage at airports, utilities and industrial plants. For out-of-service inspections we perform MFL floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell course thickness surveys, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination and nozzle and sump work; for external inspections we survey shell thickness, examine roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and take settlement measurements presented against API 653 Annex B. See API 653 tank inspection support and New York tank inspection.

API 510 pressure vessels. Chemical plants in Niagara Falls and Rochester, pharmaceutical and food plants, power stations and semiconductor utility systems operate pressure vessels that owners manage under API 510 or the National Board Inspection Code. We carry out external visual examination, UT thickness at CMLs, corrosion mapping, PAUT or TOFD on welds of concern and MT or PT on nozzles and attachments during entries, reported against previous surveys. See API 510 pressure vessel inspection support and New York pressure vessel inspection.

API 570 piping. Terminal transfer lines, chemical process piping and plant utilities are surveyed against your circuit drawings, with injection-point and deadleg scanning and CUI screening where insulation is removed; freeze-thaw cycles make wet insulation a common New York problem. See API 570 piping inspection support, New York piping inspection and New York corrosion inspection.

What we do not do: Atlantis does not sell risk-based inspection (API 580/581) or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments, and it does not act as the Authorized Inspector. Our reports give your engineers clean, traceable data; the integrity decisions built on it stay with your programme.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: In New York, planned inspection is driven by terminal tank programmes, power-plant and hydro outages, chemical-plant shutdowns and construction schedules. Atlantis joins the planning stage, agrees methods and procedures, and mobilises crews to your site on dates fixed during scoping, so NDE does not become the critical path.

A good outage scope still has three layers: on-stream work before the shutdown (thickness surveys, external visual and in-service weld examination), work that needs entry or isolation during the outage (vessel internals, tank floors, penstocks, exchanger shells), and re-examination of every repair weld before start-up. For terminals, the rhythm is different: tanks rotate out of service one or two at a time, so floor scanning and shell work have to keep pace with cleaning and repair contractors. For construction projects, NDE is tied to fabrication and erection sequences, and the engineer of record sets acceptance criteria.

New York specifics: upstate winters limit outdoor PT and MT and make couplant choice and heated enclosures part of the plan, so many owners push tank and outdoor work into the April to November window; New York City work involves street permits, building access and tight laydown space; many maritime facilities require TWIC cards; and power, chemical and terminal sites need site-specific orientation and contractor prequalification completed before mobilisation. Plan a New York outage or tank programme.

Direct answer: In New York, boilers and the construction of unfired pressure vessels fall under the Department of Labor Boiler Safety Bureau (with the NYC Department of Buildings covering boilers in the city), radioactive materials under the Department of Health (and the NYC health department within the city), intrastate gas pipelines under the Public Service Commission with PHMSA, process safety under federal OSHA, and petroleum and chemical bulk storage under NYSDEC.

Boilers and pressure vessels: NYS DOL Boiler Safety Bureau

New York regulates high-pressure boilers under Industrial Code Rule 14 (12 NYCRR Part 14), administered by the Department of Labor's Boiler Safety Bureau, with periodic inspections by state inspectors or authorised insurance-company inspectors. The same rule sets construction requirements for unfired pressure vessels, which must be built and stamped to ASME Section VIII and registered with the National Board. In-service vessel inspection beyond that is generally driven by owners, insurers, OSHA PSM where it applies and API 510-based programmes. Within New York City, the Department of Buildings handles boiler inspection and filing. Confirm the requirements for a specific item with the Bureau or the city.

Radiography: Agreement State with a state and city split

New York is an NRC Agreement State. Licences for radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, are issued by the New York State Department of Health, whose radioactive materials programme absorbed the former Department of Labor programme; the radiography rules sit in Industrial Code Rule 38. Within New York City, the city Department of Health and Mental Hygiene runs its own radiation control programme, so confirm the licensing authority for your site. Atlantis does not claim to hold a New York radioactive material licence: radiography on Atlantis scopes is performed by radiography crews licensed in New York, working to reviewed procedures under our Level III. In dense urban sites where an exclusion zone is impractical, PAUT or TOFD may be an alternative if your code and owner accept it.

Pipelines: Public Service Commission and PHMSA

The New York State Public Service Commission, through the Department of Public Service, runs the state pipeline safety programme for intrastate gas transmission and distribution in partnership with PHMSA, which regulates interstate gas and hazardous liquid lines under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Girth-weld inspection on new construction normally follows API 1104. See our pipeline inspection services and New York pipeline inspection.

Process safety and bulk storage

Private-sector employers in New York fall under federal OSHA (the state's PESH programme covers public employees), whose process safety management standard (29 CFR 1910.119) requires written inspection and testing procedures, inspection following recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, and documentation of each inspection. For tanks, NYSDEC administers the Petroleum Bulk Storage rules (6 NYCRR Part 613), Major Oil Storage Facility licensing (Part 610) and Chemical Bulk Storage rules, which include inspection and recordkeeping requirements, alongside EPA's SPCC rule (40 CFR Part 112), which expects tank integrity testing to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Every Atlantis inspection in New York produces a digital report built in our own reporting platform: each reading, indication and photo tied to the asset, location, procedure, technician certification and instrument calibration, with acceptance criteria quoted from the governing code. Reports are reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight before release.

Inspectors of record, boiler inspectors, NYSDEC, insurers and engineers of record reject reports for predictable reasons: thickness readings that cannot be traced to a location, indications without a procedure and acceptance criterion, technicians whose certification cannot be shown, and instruments without calibration records. Our reporting software is designed around those failure points, with field capture (offline where needed), structure per asset and location, and exports your inspection data management or project document system can import. Read more on our NDT inspection software page, or compare options in best NDT reporting software 2026.

The data can go further than a PDF. Results can feed scheduling, certification tracking and invoicing in Atlantis ERP (see NDT ERP in New York State), or be placed on a 3D model of the tank farm, plant or structure in our digital twin platform (see digital twins in New York State). That route from Level III-led inspection to digital report to optional twin is not offered as one package by the large inspection firms.

NDT Inspection Services in Ohio

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides NDT inspection services across Ohio with ASNT-certified technicians working under ASNT Level III oversight: UT thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD weld inspection, MT, PT, VT and ET, radiography through crews licensed in Ohio, and NDE support for API 510 pressure-vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage-tank programmes. Crews are mobilised to your site, the schedule is agreed during scoping, and every result arrives as a digital report traceable to the governing code.

Ohio is not one inspection market but five or six. A refinery turnaround in Oregon or Lima, a nuclear outage on the Lake Erie shore, a pipe mill in the Mahoning Valley, an aerospace supplier in the Cincinnati suburbs, a gas processing plant in the Utica counties and a chemical plant on the Ohio River each ask for a different method mix, a different code basis and a different report format. This page sets out where that work is, which methods and codes apply, which Ohio regulators sit behind the inspection, and how to scope a job with us. If you already know what you need, request an Ohio inspection quote and we reply with questions or a proposal.

Where inspection work is in Ohio

Direct answer: most Ohio NDT inspection demand comes from the Toledo and Lima refining corridor, the Lake Erie steel and nuclear belt, the Mahoning and Stark valley mills, southwest Ohio aerospace and chemicals, the central Ohio construction boom and the Utica shale gas counties in the east. Each sub-region has its own anchor assets, owners' specifications and seasonal turnaround calendar.

Northwest Ohio: Toledo, Oregon and Lima

Two refineries sit side by side in Oregon, just east of Toledo on the Maumee Bay shoreline, and a third refinery operates in Lima, about an hour south. Around them are product terminals, the Port of Toledo's bulk and liquid docks, and a chemical complex in Lima that runs pressure equipment of its own. This corridor generates the classic refinery inspection workload: UT thickness readings at condition monitoring locations on process piping, PAUT and TOFD on new and repaired welds, MT and PT on nozzle and attachment welds, VT of vessels and exchangers when they are opened, and corrosion mapping on areas where wall loss is suspected. Findlay, the headquarters city of a major US refiner, adds engineering and procurement activity that often decides how inspection scopes are written. See our Level III pages for Toledo, Oregon and Lima for the procedure side of that work.

Northeast Ohio: Cleveland, Lorain, Akron and the nuclear stations

Cleveland still makes steel on the Cuyahoga River, Lorain produces tubular products, and the region is full of forge shops, foundries, valve and pump makers and heavy machine builders. Inspection here leans toward MT and PT of forgings and castings, UT of plate, bar and welded fabrications, and ET of tubing and bar. Akron's polymer and rubber plants run boilers, autoclaves and pressure vessels that need periodic inspection. On the lake shore, the Perry nuclear station east of Cleveland and the Davis-Besse station near Oak Harbor plan outage inspection years ahead under ASME Section XI, and the contractors who support them depend on qualified UT, ET and VT personnel with spotless paperwork.

Mahoning Valley and Stark County: Youngstown, Warren and Canton

Youngstown and Warren grew on steel, and seamless pipe, tube and specialty bar are still made in the valley. Mills rely on automated UT and ET lines with manual MT and UT for prove-up and end inspection, and their customers expect every automated system to be verified against reference standards under a Level III-approved procedure. Canton adds specialty steel and a refinery, so a Stark County crew can spend one week on mill product and the next on refinery piping. Our Canton and Akron steel pages go further into mill-specific procedure work.

Southwest Ohio: Cincinnati, Dayton and the Ohio River

Greater Cincinnati is one of the largest jet-engine manufacturing and overhaul centres in the world, and its supplier base lives on PT, MT, ET and UT performed under tightly controlled written practices. Dayton is home to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base and a dense ring of defence and aerospace contractors. Along the Ohio River, chemical plants, power stations and river terminals generate tank, vessel and piping inspection. We already publish city pages for Cincinnati covering pressure vessels, piping, tanks and welds.

Central Ohio: Columbus and the construction ring

Columbus combines automotive assembly to the northwest, logistics and air cargo to the south, and large advanced-manufacturing and battery-plant construction to the east and southwest. Construction phases create structural weld inspection to AWS D1.1, process and utility piping inspection to ASME B31.3 and B31.9, and receiving inspection of fabricated spools and skids. Owners on these projects want inspection reports that drop straight into their turnover packages.

Eastern Ohio: the Utica shale and the upper Ohio River valley

Carroll, Harrison, Belmont, Monroe, Guernsey and Noble counties sit over the Utica and Point Pleasant shale. Gathering lines, compressor stations, gas processing and fractionation plants and their storage tanks need weld inspection during construction and thickness surveys in service. Marietta and the river towns south of it add polymer and chemical plants; see our Marietta page. Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: Ohio refinery and chemical turnarounds usually fall in spring and autumn, because winters on Lake Erie and in the Ohio valley make outdoor work slow and summer is peak fuel demand. Book inspection scopes well before the window opens so procedures, crews and equipment are ready the day units come down.

Turnaround inspection fails for predictable reasons: the scope is finalised too late, the procedures have not been reviewed against the owner's specification, the crew's certifications are not ready for the owner's contractor-qualification check, or the data arrives as handwritten sheets that nobody can trend. We work backwards from your shutdown date. During scoping we agree the equipment list, the methods and coverage per item, the code and acceptance criteria, the report template and the hand-off route to your inspector. Our Level III reviews or writes the procedures before mobilisation, and technician certifications are packaged for your gate.

Not all inspection needs a shutdown. On-stream UT thickness surveys, external VT, corrosion mapping through access windows and many PAUT examinations can be performed while units run, which takes pressure off the turnaround itself. For nuclear outages and mill shutdowns the same principle applies: anything that can be inspected beforehand should be, so the outage window is reserved for the items that genuinely need the equipment opened. When we know your calendar we can propose a split between pre-turnaround, turnaround and post-turnaround work. Plan an Ohio turnaround inspection scope with us early and you avoid the last-minute scramble for crews that every spring brings.

Weather matters too. Couplant behaviour, battery life, film processing and personnel safety all change below freezing, and lakefront sites in Toledo and Lorain can be windy and wet into May. We plan heated enclosures, temperature-appropriate couplants and equipment checks into winter work rather than discovering the problem on site.

Ohio regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: four layers of rules shape inspection in Ohio: the Ohio boiler and pressure-vessel law administered by the Department of Commerce, radiation licensing under the Ohio Department of Health for radiography, state and federal pipeline safety rules, and federal OSHA and EPA requirements for process safety and oil storage. Owners' and insurers' specifications sit on top.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Boiler Section of the Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Industrial Compliance, administers Ohio Revised Code Chapter 4104 and the boiler rules in Ohio Administrative Code 4101:4. Boilers and unfired pressure vessels must be built, installed, repaired and altered to ASME and National Board Inspection Code (NBIC) requirements, and certificate inspections are carried out by inspectors who hold an Ohio commission. NDE we perform on repairs or alterations is reported so that the commissioned inspector and the repair organisation can use it in their NBIC documentation.

Radiography. Ohio is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with sealed sources is licensed by the Ohio Department of Health's Bureau of Radiation Protection rather than by the NRC, and X-ray equipment is registered with the state. Atlantis does not claim to hold an Ohio radiography licence; RT is performed by radiography crews licensed in Ohio, working to our procedures and reporting format, with exclusion zones agreed with your site safety team.

Pipelines. The Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO) runs the state gas pipeline safety programme for intrastate operators, while interstate gas and hazardous liquid lines fall to the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. Construction weld inspection is usually specified to API 1104, and operator qualification rules apply to the people doing covered tasks.

Process safety and storage. Ohio's private-sector employers fall under federal OSHA. Refineries and chemical plants handling highly hazardous chemicals must run a mechanical integrity programme under OSHA's Process Safety Management standard (29 CFR 1910.119), which is where documented, code-referenced inspection becomes a compliance requirement. Aboveground oil storage is covered by the EPA's Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) rule, which expects tank integrity testing to an industry standard such as API 653 or STI SP001. Underground petroleum tanks are regulated by the Bureau of Underground Storage Tank Regulations within the State Fire Marshal's office.

Regulations change; confirm the current requirement with the agency before relying on any summary, including this one. Our Level III can help you map which requirement drives which inspection in your plant; the procedure side is covered on our Ohio NDT consulting hub.

NDT Inspection Services in Oklahoma

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers NDT inspection services across Oklahoma with ASNT-certified technicians under ASNT Level III oversight: UT thickness surveys, PAUT, TOFD, corrosion mapping, MT, PT, VT and ET, radiography through crews licensed in Oklahoma, and NDE support for API 510 vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 tank programmes. Crews are mobilised to your site, the schedule is agreed during scoping, and every job ends in a Level III-reviewed digital report traceable to the code.

Oklahoma's inspection market is built on oil and gas from wellhead to tank. Cushing is the most famous crude storage hub in North America, refineries run in Tulsa, Ponca City, Ardmore and Wynnewood, gathering and processing systems spread across the Anadarko and Arkoma basins, and Tulsa is a national centre for heat-exchanger and pressure-equipment fabrication. On top of that, Oklahoma City and Tulsa host some of the largest aircraft maintenance operations in the country. This page maps that work, the methods and codes that go with it, the Oklahoma agencies behind it, and how to request inspection. If you are ready, request an Oklahoma inspection quote.

Where inspection work is in Oklahoma

Direct answer: Oklahoma inspection demand is centred on the Cushing tank hub, the four refining cities (Tulsa, Ponca City, Ardmore and Wynnewood), the Tulsa fabrication and aerospace cluster, the Oklahoma City aerospace and energy corridor, and the oil and gas producing basins of western, central and eastern Oklahoma, with military aviation at Enid, Altus and Lawton adding specialist work.

Cushing: the crude storage hub

Cushing, in Payne County, is where many of the continent's crude pipelines meet and where the benchmark US light sweet crude contract is physically delivered. The town is ringed by tank farms holding a large share of US commercial crude storage, along with manifolds, pump stations and pipeline terminals. Inspection here is dominated by API 653 work: shell UT thickness surveys, floor MFL scanning with UT prove-up, weld MT and VT on shell-to-bottom joints, and settlement survey support during out-of-service inspections, plus pipeline and manifold weld inspection during expansions. Earthquakes in north-central Oklahoma during the last decade, including one near Cushing in 2016, also raised owners' interest in foundation and settlement checks. See our Cushing page for the procedure side.

Tulsa: refining, heat-exchanger fabrication and aircraft maintenance

Tulsa has a refinery operating as two plants on the Arkansas River, and the metro is widely known for fabricating air-cooled and shell-and-tube heat exchangers, pressure vessels and process skids for the energy industry. That fabrication base generates shop inspection to ASME Section VIII and ASME B31.3: RT or UT of butt welds, PT and MT of nozzle and attachment welds, VT of finished welds and hydrotest support. Tulsa also hosts a very large airline maintenance base, and the Tulsa Port of Catoosa links the region to the inland waterway system. Atlantis already publishes Tulsa pages for pressure vessels, piping, tanks, welds and corrosion.

Ponca City, Ardmore and Wynnewood: the other refineries

Ponca City in the north has a large refinery and associated chemical and terminal operations. Ardmore and Wynnewood in southern Oklahoma each have a refinery, and Wynnewood sits close to the Interstate 35 pipeline corridor. Refinery inspection across these sites follows the familiar pattern: UT thickness at piping CMLs, PAUT and TOFD on new and repair welds, MT and PT during turnarounds, internal VT of vessels and exchangers, and tank surveys in the tank farms. See Ponca City, Ponca City refining and Ardmore.

Oklahoma City: aerospace depot work, energy companies and construction

Tinker Air Force Base, southeast of Oklahoma City, is home to the Oklahoma City Air Logistics Complex, one of the Air Force's largest depot maintenance operations for aircraft and engines, and the FAA's Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center is on the west side of the city. Aerospace contractors around them rely on PT, MT, ET and UT under tightly controlled written practices. Oklahoma City is also an energy headquarters city, so many upstream and midstream inspection scopes are written there even when the work is in the field. Pages: Oklahoma City consulting and Oklahoma City refining NDT.

The producing basins: SCOOP, STACK, Arkoma and the Panhandle

The Anadarko Basin plays known as SCOOP and STACK in central and western Oklahoma, the Arkoma Basin in the southeast and older fields across the state feed gathering systems, compressor stations, gas processing plants and tank batteries. Inspection here means weld inspection on new gathering and plant piping (often to API 1104 or ASME B31.3), UT thickness on produced-water and condensate lines prone to internal corrosion, tank inspection at batteries and saltwater disposal sites, and pressure-vessel checks on separators and treaters.

Military aviation and the rest of the state

Vance Air Force Base at Enid, Altus Air Force Base in the southwest and Fort Sill at Lawton bring aviation and vehicle maintenance work. Enid also hosts nitrogen fertilizer production with high-pressure equipment. Hydroelectric dams on the Grand and Arkansas rivers, wind farms across western Oklahoma and gas-fired power stations add structural and pressure-equipment inspection. See Lawton for the technician side.

Direct answer: Oklahoma refinery turnarounds usually fall in spring or autumn, tank out-of-service inspections at Cushing and terminals are scheduled around storage commitments, and fabrication shops need inspection on their production schedule. Each calendar is tight, so scope, procedures and crews should be fixed before the window opens.

For a tank, the expensive part of an internal inspection is the time the tank is out of service: draining, cleaning, gas-freeing, inspecting, repairing and returning it. Inspection that is slow, incomplete or has to be repeated adds days of lost storage. We plan tank floors, shell surveys and weld checks so the crew finishes in one visit and the API 653 inspector has everything needed to set the next interval. For refinery turnarounds in Tulsa, Ponca City, Ardmore and Wynnewood, we separate on-stream work (UT thickness, external VT, corrosion mapping, much of the PAUT) from items that need the unit open, so the turnaround window is used for internal inspection and repairs.

For fabricators, the issue is flow: inspection must keep pace with welding so that repairs are found while the welder is still on the job. Shop inspection can be scheduled by shift or by batch. Oklahoma weather has its own hazards: summer heat on tank floors and in shop bays, ice storms in winter, and severe thunderstorms and tornado warnings in spring. Heat-stress plans, lightning stand-down rules and cold-weather equipment checks are built into our site plans.

NDT Inspection Services in Pennsylvania

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers non-destructive testing inspection across Pennsylvania: UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT and TOFD weld inspection, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Pennsylvania, MT, PT, VT and ET, and NDE support for API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank programmes. ASNT-certified technicians work under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, crews are mobilised to your site, and results are delivered as a code-referenced digital report.

Pennsylvania's inspection market looks nothing like the Gulf Coast. Instead of one dense refinery corridor, it has a refining and NGL export hub at Marcus Hook and along the Delaware River, the Marcellus and Utica shale gas fields across the north and west, steelmaking in the Monongahela Valley, a large nuclear fleet, heavy fabrication and rail manufacturing, thousands of steel highway bridges, and a state regulatory regime that reaches further than most: Pennsylvania regulates unfired pressure vessels as well as boilers, and it requires DEP-certified inspectors for regulated aboveground storage tanks. This page maps that market and explains how Atlantis fits. To start, request a Pennsylvania inspection quote.

Where inspection work is in Pennsylvania

Direct answer: Pennsylvania inspection demand clusters in the Philadelphia and Delaware River industrial belt including Marcus Hook, the Pittsburgh region's steel, petrochemical and nuclear engineering base, the Marcellus and Utica shale gas fields and their pipelines, the nuclear power plants, the Harrisburg-Lehigh Valley fabrication and logistics corridor, and Erie's rail and manufacturing industry, plus statewide bridge work.

Philadelphia, Marcus Hook and the Delaware River

Southeastern Pennsylvania's industrial waterfront runs from Philadelphia south through Delaware County to Marcus Hook on the state line. The Marcus Hook industrial complex has become a hub for natural gas liquids storage, processing and export fed by the Mariner East pipelines, and the Monroe Energy refinery at Trainer, chemical plants, tank terminals and the Philly Shipyard make up the rest of the cluster. Inspection scope here includes API 653 work on product and NGL storage, UT and PAUT on process and transfer piping, refrigerated storage and pressure vessel inspection, weld inspection for shipbuilding, and corrosion work on waterfront assets. See Marcus Hook refining NDT consulting, Philadelphia tank inspection and Philadelphia refining NDT consulting.

Pittsburgh, the Mon Valley and Beaver County

Western Pennsylvania remains a steel and heavy-industry region. U.S. Steel's Mon Valley Works, including the Clairton coke plant and the Edgar Thomson and Irvin plants, along with specialty metals and forging companies, drives inspection of cranes, ladles, pressure equipment and structural steel. The ethane cracker at Monaca in Beaver County added a major petrochemical site to the region, and Pittsburgh has a cluster of nuclear engineering and component suppliers. Methods range from MT and UT on heavy weldments and lifting equipment to thickness surveys and PAUT on petrochemical piping. See steel NDT consulting in Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh weld inspection and ultrasonic testing in Pittsburgh.

Marcellus and Utica shale: the north and south-west

Pennsylvania is one of the largest natural gas producers in the country. Production in counties such as Washington, Greene, Susquehanna, Bradford and Lycoming feeds gathering systems, compressor stations, processing plants and long-distance transmission pipelines. Inspection here is pipeline-heavy: API 1104 girth-weld inspection with RT and AUT or PAUT on new construction, UT thickness and corrosion surveys on station piping and vessels, and tank inspection at production and processing sites. Winter conditions and remote, hilly right-of-ways shape scheduling. See Pittsburgh pipeline inspection and Philadelphia pipeline inspection.

Nuclear power

Pennsylvania hosts several nuclear stations, including Beaver Valley, Susquehanna, Limerick and Peach Bottom, and a planned restart of the former Three Mile Island Unit 1 site. In-service inspection at nuclear plants follows ASME Section XI and owner programmes with their own performance demonstration requirements, so Atlantis's role there is typically supplier and contractor support (procedures, Level III review, inspection of non-nuclear balance-of-plant equipment) rather than reactor coolant system examinations. See nuclear NDT consulting in Pittsburgh.

Harrisburg, the Lehigh Valley and central Pennsylvania

The I-81 and I-78 corridors carry steel fabricators, pressure vessel and tank builders, food and pharmaceutical plants with stainless process piping, and defence depots. Fabrication NDE to ASME Section VIII and AWS D1.1, PT on stainless sanitary piping and boiler and pressure vessel inspection support for permitted equipment are common scopes. See steel NDT consulting in Harrisburg, Allentown and Scranton.

Erie and the north-west

Erie is a centre of locomotive and rail manufacturing, along with plastics, forging and port activity on Lake Erie. Rail work brings MT, UT and VT on cast and welded components to customer and AAR-related specifications, and further east, the United Refining plant at Warren adds refinery inspection. See rail NDT consulting in Erie and NDT consulting in Erie.

Bridges and infrastructure

Pennsylvania has one of the largest state bridge inventories in the country, many of them steel structures that need weld inspection for fabrication, rehabilitation and fatigue-crack follow-up. Bridge welding follows AWS D1.5 and PennDOT specifications; UT, MT and VT are the core methods.

NDT methods we deliver in Pennsylvania

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional UT, radiography through Pennsylvania-licensed radiography crews, MT, PT, VT and ET. The table maps each method to typical Pennsylvania work and the code usually cited; the technique is agreed with your inspector of record during scoping.

API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in Pennsylvania

Direct answer: Atlantis performs the NDE behind API 510, API 570 and API 653 inspections in Pennsylvania, including CML thickness surveys, weld examination, tank floor and shell work and external visual, and hands documented results to your API-certified Authorized Inspector. Where a tank needs a DEP-certified inspector or a vessel needs a state-commissioned inspector, our data supports that inspector.

API 510 pressure vessels. Refinery, NGL and petrochemical vessels, plus process vessels in chemical and pharmaceutical plants, get external visual, UT thickness at CMLs, PAUT or TOFD where cracking is suspected and MT or PT inside during entries, reported against prior surveys. See API 510 pressure vessel inspection support, Philadelphia pressure vessel inspection and Pittsburgh pressure vessel inspection.

API 570 piping. We survey CMLs on process, transfer and station piping to your isometrics, add injection-point and deadleg scanning, and support CUI screening, which is a real issue where freeze-thaw cycles damage insulation jacketing. See API 570 piping inspection support and Pittsburgh piping inspection.

API 653 storage tanks. Pennsylvania is unusual in requiring regulated aboveground tanks to be inspected by DEP-certified tank inspectors. For out-of-service inspections we perform floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell thickness, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination and nozzle work; for externals, shell thickness, visual examination of roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and settlement measurement presented against API 653 Annex B. See API 653 tank inspection support and Pittsburgh tank inspection.

Atlantis does not sell risk-based inspection (API 580/581) or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments; our reports provide the data those programmes use.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: Pennsylvania outages follow several calendars: refinery and petrochemical turnarounds, steel-mill maintenance outages, nuclear refuelling outages, pipeline construction seasons and winter weather. Atlantis joins planning early, agrees methods and procedures, and mobilises crews on dates fixed during scoping so inspection and repair re-examination stay off the critical path.

We split a scope into on-stream work before the outage (thickness surveys, external visual, in-service weld examination), outage work (entries, tank floors, exchanger bundles, welds under insulation) and post-repair re-examination. Moving scope on-stream wherever your inspector agrees shortens outages more than anything else.

Pennsylvania-specific planning points: winter cold limits UT couplant performance, coating work and some PT on outdoor equipment, so many owners push field inspection into the April to November window; pipeline construction in the shale fields is seasonal and right-of-way access is often weather-dependent; steel mills schedule short, intense outages around production; and nuclear-adjacent work has to fit refuelling outage windows set by the owner. Contractor safety prequalification and site orientation are completed before mobilisation. Plan a Pennsylvania outage inspection.

Pennsylvania regulations that shape inspection

Direct answer: In Pennsylvania, boilers and unfired pressure vessels are regulated by the Department of Labor and Industry's Boiler Division, radiography by the Department of Environmental Protection's Bureau of Radiation Protection, aboveground storage tanks by DEP's storage tank programme, pipelines by the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission with PHMSA, and process safety by federal OSHA's PSM standard.

Boilers and unfired pressure vessels: Labor and Industry

Pennsylvania's Boiler and Unfired Pressure Vessel Law is administered by the Department of Labor and Industry's Boiler Division. Unlike Texas, Pennsylvania brings many unfired pressure vessels, not just boilers, into the state inspection programme, with inspections by commonwealth inspectors or commissioned insurance-company inspectors. Exemptions and inspection frequencies are set in the regulations, so confirm specific vessels with the Boiler Division. Atlantis is not a commissioned inspector; our NDE results support yours.

Aboveground storage tanks: DEP and the Storage Tank Act

Under the Storage Tank and Spill Prevention Act and 25 Pa. Code Chapter 245, regulated aboveground storage tanks are subject to installation, modification, in-service and out-of-service inspections that must be performed by DEP-certified aboveground storage tank inspectors. The regulations distinguish large tanks (more than 21,000 gallons) from small tanks, and the 2018 revisions shortened the in-service inspection interval for small tanks to five years. Atlantis provides the NDE a certified inspector relies on (floor scanning, shell thickness, weld examination, settlement) and does not claim DEP inspector certification. Confirm current intervals for your tanks with DEP.

Radiography: DEP and Agreement State status

Pennsylvania is an NRC Agreement State, so radioactive material licensing and industrial radiography are regulated by the DEP Bureau of Radiation Protection rather than by the NRC directly. Atlantis does not claim to hold a Pennsylvania radioactive material licence; radiography on our scopes is carried out by radiography crews licensed in Pennsylvania, working to procedures reviewed under our Level III. Where exclusion zones would disrupt operations, PAUT or TOFD can be proposed if your code and owner accept it.

Pipelines, gas wells and process safety

The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission enforces pipeline safety for intrastate gas and hazardous liquid pipelines as PHMSA's state partner, and Act 127 of 2011 extended its oversight to many non-utility pipeline operators, including much of the gathering built for the shale fields; PHMSA regulates interstate lines under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195. DEP's Office of Oil and Gas Management regulates well sites. Private-sector plants fall under federal OSHA, where the PSM standard (29 CFR 1910.119) requires documented inspection and testing of covered process equipment, and EPA's SPCC rule applies to oil storage. See pipeline inspection services.

Inspection reports clients can use

Direct answer: Every Pennsylvania inspection is delivered as a digital report from Atlantis's own reporting platform, with readings, indications and photos tied to asset, location, procedure, acceptance criterion, technician certification and instrument calibration, and reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight before release.

In Pennsylvania the reader of an NDE report is often not the plant engineer alone: it may be a DEP-certified tank inspector, a commissioned boiler and pressure vessel inspector, an insurer or a PUC pipeline auditor. Each wants the same things: readings traceable to locations, the procedure and acceptance criteria used, technician qualifications and calibration records. Our platform captures data in the field, offline where there is no signal, which is common on rural right-of-ways, structures it per asset and CML, and exports it in formats your inspection system can import. See NDT inspection software and best NDT reporting software 2026.

Results can also flow into Atlantis ERP for scheduling, certifications and invoicing, or onto a 3D asset model on our digital twin platform; see digital twins in Pennsylvania and Marcus Hook. One company running Level III-led inspection, digital reporting and an optional twin is not something the large inspection firms package together.

Cities we cover across Pennsylvania

Direct answer: Atlantis mobilises inspection crews to client sites anywhere in Pennsylvania. Atlantis has no physical office in Pennsylvania; crews travel to your plant, terminal, mill, yard or right-of-way, with dates agreed during scoping. These pages cover individual Pennsylvania cities in more depth.

  • Philadelphia and the Delaware Valley: weld inspection, corrosion inspection, pipeline inspection, NDT consulting in Philadelphia and Marcus Hook.
  • Pittsburgh and western Pennsylvania: pressure vessel inspection, tank inspection, pipeline inspection and NDT consulting in Pittsburgh.
  • Central Pennsylvania: Harrisburg, Harrisburg steel, Allentown and Scranton.
  • North-west: Erie and Practical NDT in Erie.
  • Shale country: Washington, Greene, Susquehanna, Bradford and Lycoming counties by arrangement.

Related Pennsylvania hubs: NDT consulting in Pennsylvania for Level III services and written practices, and NDT training in Pennsylvania for ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based courses.

How to request inspection

Direct answer: Send Atlantis the asset, method, site, governing code, any state inspector involved, dates and the deliverable. We reply with questions or a scoped quote, share procedures and certifications for review, mobilise on the agreed date and deliver a Level III-reviewed digital report.

  1. Describe the job. Asset, method if known, Pennsylvania site, governing code (API 510/570/653, ASME, API 1104, AWS D1.1/D1.5), whether a DEP-certified tank inspector or commissioned vessel inspector is involved, dates, quantities and report format. Send your Pennsylvania RFQ.
  2. Scoping call. Technique, access, weather window, site safety and whether RT or an ultrasonic alternative fits.
  3. Quote and procedures. Scope, quote, procedures and technician certifications.
  4. Mobilisation. Orientation and crew mobilisation on the date agreed during scoping.
  5. Inspection. Critical findings reported to your representative during the shift.
  6. Report. Digital, code-referenced, reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight.

Frequently asked questions about NDT inspection in Pennsylvania

What NDT inspection services does Atlantis offer in Pennsylvania?

UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT, TOFD, conventional UT, radiography through Pennsylvania-licensed crews, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus NDE support for API 510, API 570 and API 653 programmes and pipeline inspection, under ASNT Level III oversight.

Do you have an office in Philadelphia or Pittsburgh?

No. Atlantis has no physical office in Pennsylvania; crews mobilise to your site and dates are agreed during scoping.

Does Pennsylvania require tank inspections by a certified inspector?

Yes, for regulated aboveground storage tanks. DEP requires installation, modification, in-service and out-of-service inspections by DEP-certified inspectors under 25 Pa. Code Chapter 245. We provide the NDE that supports the certified inspector.

Are unfired pressure vessels regulated in Pennsylvania?

Yes. The Boiler and Unfired Pressure Vessel Law, administered by the Department of Labor and Industry, covers many unfired pressure vessels as well as boilers. Check exemptions and frequencies for your vessels with the Boiler Division.
