NDT Inspection Services in Texas

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides non-destructive testing inspection across Texas: ultrasonic thickness surveys, phased array (PAUT) and TOFD weld inspection, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Texas, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual and eddy current testing, plus NDE support for API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank programmes. All work is performed by ASNT-certified technicians under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, crews are mobilised to your site, and results arrive as a code-referenced digital report.

Texas is not one inspection market but five or six. A refinery on the Houston Ship Channel, a tank battery outside Pecos, an LNG train at Sabine Pass, an aerospace supplier in Fort Worth and a gas processing plant in the Eagle Ford all buy "NDT inspection", yet they ask for different methods, cite different codes and answer to different regulators. This page maps that market region by region, explains which state and federal rules shape inspection scope in Texas, and sets out exactly what Atlantis delivers and what it does not. When you are ready, request a Texas inspection quote with the asset, method, code and dates, and we will come back with questions or a scope.

Where inspection work is in Texas

Direct answer: Texas inspection demand concentrates in the Houston Ship Channel and Galveston Bay refining and petrochemical belt, the Beaumont-Port Arthur-Orange corridor, the Coastal Bend around Corpus Christi, the Permian Basin and Eagle Ford oil and gas fields, East Texas gas and pipeline country, and the Dallas-Fort Worth and San Antonio aerospace and manufacturing base. Each region leans on different methods and codes.

Houston, Pasadena, Deer Park, Baytown and Texas City

The Ship Channel corridor from the east side of Houston through Pasadena, Deer Park, Channelview and Baytown down to Texas City and Freeport is one of the densest clusters of refining and chemical capacity on earth. Large refineries such as ExxonMobil Baytown, Deer Park, Marathon Galveston Bay and Valero Texas City sit beside olefins crackers, polymer plants, terminals and the Dow complex at Freeport. Here inspection is governed by mechanical integrity programmes under OSHA's process safety management standard, so the daily work is ultrasonic thickness readings at condition monitoring locations (CMLs) on piping circuits, shear-wave UT and PAUT on repair and tie-in welds, radiography of small-bore and socket welds, MT and PT on nozzles and attachment welds, and API 653 tank-floor and shell work at the terminals that line the channel. Spring and autumn turnarounds concentrate months of scope into a few weeks.

Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange (the Golden Triangle)

Jefferson and Orange counties host some of North America's largest refineries, including Motiva Port Arthur, ExxonMobil Beaumont and Valero Port Arthur, plus chemical plants along the Neches River and LNG export construction around Sabine Pass and Port Arthur. LNG projects bring heavy weld-inspection scopes on stainless and nickel-alloy cryogenic piping, where penetrant testing, radiography and, where the owner and code allow, PAUT and TOFD in place of film are all in demand. Fabrication shops that build pressure vessels, exchangers and spools to ASME Section VIII and B31.3 also need UT, RT, MT and PT on a steady schedule.

Corpus Christi, Ingleside and the Coastal Bend

Corpus Christi combines refining (Flint Hills Resources, Valero and Citgo all operate there), the Cheniere Corpus Christi LNG terminal and a port that has become one of the largest crude export gateways in the United States. That mix produces demand for corrosion mapping and thickness surveys at crude terminals and tank farms, weld inspection on new export infrastructure, and visual and UT inspection of marine and dock structures exposed to a hot, salty climate where corrosion under insulation (CUI) and atmospheric corrosion are constant concerns.

Permian Basin and West Texas

Midland, Odessa and the surrounding counties sit on the most productive oil field in the country. Inspection here means gathering and transmission pipelines (API 1104 girth-weld inspection, UT and RT on new spreads), aboveground storage tanks at terminals and tank batteries, gas processing plants, compressor stations and saltwater disposal facilities. Sour service and produced water drive internal corrosion, so UT thickness and corrosion mapping on tanks, vessels and piping are common scopes. Distances are long, so scopes are planned to cover several sites per mobilisation.

Eagle Ford, East Texas and the Haynesville

South Texas between San Antonio and Laredo carries Eagle Ford gathering systems and processing plants, while East Texas around Longview and Tyler and the Haynesville play toward the Louisiana line run gas gathering, midstream compression and older pipeline networks. Work is weighted toward pipeline welds, vessel and separator thickness surveys, and tank inspection at gathering facilities.

Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio and Austin

North Texas has a large aerospace and defence manufacturing base around Fort Worth and Arlington, plus heavy fabrication, power generation and data-centre construction. San Antonio hosts aircraft maintenance at Port San Antonio and military aviation at Joint Base San Antonio. Inspection here is more often weld and structural inspection to AWS D1.1, fabrication NDE to ASME codes and component inspection, with aerospace work governed by customer and NAS 410 requirements. Texas also has two nuclear plants, Comanche Peak near Glen Rose and the South Texas Project near Bay City, where NDE is controlled by owner programmes and ASME Section XI.

NDT methods we deliver in Texas

API 510, 570 and 653 inspection support in Texas

Direct answer: Atlantis performs the NDE that API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank inspections depend on, such as thickness surveys, weld examination, floor scanning follow-up and visual inspection, and hands documented results to your API-certified Authorized Inspector, who remains the inspector of record and signs the inspection report.

API 510 pressure vessels. For towers, drums, exchangers and reactors across Texas plants we carry out external visual examination, UT thickness at the vessel's CMLs, PAUT or TOFD on welds where cracking or prior repairs are of concern, and MT or PT on nozzles and internal attachments during entries. Readings are reported against the previous survey so your inspector can calculate corrosion rates and set the next interval. See API 510 pressure vessel inspection support and our Houston pressure vessel inspection and Beaumont pressure vessel inspection pages.

API 570 piping. Ship Channel and Golden Triangle plants carry thousands of CMLs per unit. We survey them to your circuit drawings, add scanning at injection points, deadlegs and mix points where your programme calls for it, and support CUI screening where insulation is removed. Results are delivered per CML so they load straight into your inspection data system. See API 570 piping inspection support, Houston piping inspection, Corpus Christi piping inspection and Dallas piping inspection.

API 653 storage tanks. Texas has an enormous tank population, from Houston and Corpus Christi terminals to Permian tank batteries. For out-of-service inspections we perform floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell course thickness surveys, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination, and nozzle and sump work; for external inspections we survey shell thickness, examine roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and take settlement measurements presented against API 653 Annex B. See API 653 tank inspection support and Houston tank inspection.

What we do not do: Atlantis does not sell risk-based inspection (API 580/581) or fitness-for-service (API 579) assessments. Our reports give your engineers clean, traceable data; the integrity decisions built on it stay with your programme.

Turnarounds, shutdowns and planned inspection

Direct answer: On the Texas Gulf Coast most inspection volume is planned months ahead around spring and autumn turnarounds. Atlantis joins the planning stage, agrees methods and procedures, and mobilises crews to your site on dates fixed during scoping, so NDE does not become the critical path when equipment opens.

A turnaround inspection scope usually has three layers. Pre-shutdown work is done on-stream: thickness surveys, PAUT or radiography of welds that can be examined hot or in service, and external visual inspection, which together shrink the list of items that must be opened. Shutdown work is everything that needs entry or isolation: vessel internals, tank floors, exchanger bundles and welds behind insulation. Post-repair work is the re-examination of every repair weld before the unit returns to service. We help you sequence those layers so that scope moves out of the outage window wherever the code and your inspector allow.

Practical points that matter in Texas: summer heat limits couplant choice and working hours on exposed tank shells; hurricane season (June to November) can move dates; and refinery access requires site-specific safety orientations and contractor prequalification that we complete ahead of mobilisation. Texas private-sector employers fall under federal OSHA; the process safety management standard (29 CFR 1910.119) requires written procedures, inspection and testing following recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice, and documentation of each inspection for covered process equipment. NDT Inspection Services in Washington State

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides non-destructive testing inspection across Washington State: ultrasonic thickness surveys and corrosion mapping, phased array (PAUT) and TOFD weld inspection, radiography through radiography crews licensed in Washington, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual and eddy current testing, plus the NDE that API 510 pressure vessel, API 570 piping and API 653 storage tank programmes depend on. Work is performed by ASNT-certified technicians under ASNT NDT Level III oversight, crews are mobilised to your site, and results arrive as a code-referenced digital report your inspector of record can sign off.

Washington is a compact inspection market with a very particular shape. Five petroleum refineries sit on the northern Puget Sound shoreline and in Tacoma, a products pipeline runs the length of the I-5 corridor, the largest aircraft factories in the world build airframes in Everett and Renton, the Navy maintains submarines and carriers at Bremerton, and the Columbia River carries hydropower dams, the state's only nuclear power plant and the Hanford cleanup site. Each of those buyers asks for NDT in a different language: API codes at March Point, AWS D1.1 and customer specifications at an aerospace supplier, NAVSEA requirements on a naval contract, ASME Section XI at a nuclear station. This page maps that market region by region, explains which Washington agencies shape inspection scope, and states plainly what Atlantis delivers and what it does not. When you are ready, request a Washington inspection quote with the asset, method, code and dates.

Where inspection work is in Washington State

Direct answer: Washington inspection demand concentrates in the refinery cluster of Whatcom and Skagit counties (Cherry Point, Ferndale and Anacortes), the Tacoma tideflats, the Seattle-Everett aerospace and port corridor, the Kitsap Peninsula naval yards, the lower Columbia River ports at Vancouver, Kalama and Longview, and the Tri-Cities and Spokane in eastern Washington. Each region leans on different methods and codes.

Cherry Point, Ferndale and Anacortes: the refinery coast

Four of Washington's five refineries sit within a short drive of each other in the northwest corner of the state: BP Cherry Point near Blaine and Ferndale, Phillips 66 Ferndale, and the two March Point refineries at Anacortes, Marathon Anacortes and HF Sinclair's Puget Sound Refinery. Together they process Alaska North Slope, Canadian and other crudes delivered by tanker, pipeline and rail, and they supply most of the gasoline, diesel and jet fuel used in the Pacific Northwest. Inspection here is the classic refinery mix: UT thickness readings at condition monitoring locations on piping circuits, corrosion mapping on vessels and exchanger shells, PAUT and radiography on repair and tie-in welds, MT and PT on nozzles and attachments, and API 653 tank work at the tank farms and marine terminals. The wet, salty marine climate makes corrosion under insulation and atmospheric corrosion of external surfaces a persistent concern, and turnarounds pack large weld and vessel-entry scopes into short windows. See our Anacortes and Ferndale pages and the Anacortes refining Level III page.

Tacoma and the Port of Tacoma tideflats

The Tacoma tideflats combine the fifth refinery, U.S. Oil and Refining, with bulk liquid terminals, an LNG facility serving marine fuelling, chemical and manufacturing plants and the container terminals of the Northwest Seaport Alliance. Typical scopes are tank shell and floor inspection at terminals, thickness surveys on process and transfer piping, weld inspection on new terminal and dock construction, and structural inspection of cranes, dock steel and lifting gear with MT and VT. See the Tacoma NDT consulting page and practical NDT in Tacoma.

Seattle, Everett, Renton and the aerospace corridor

Boeing's Everett and Renton plants anchor a supply chain of machine shops, composite fabricators, heat treaters and special-process suppliers stretching from Everett through Seattle and Kent to Auburn and beyond. Aerospace NDT is normally governed by the prime's specifications, NAS 410 personnel certification and Nadcap accreditation of the supplier's own NDT; an outside field-inspection contractor is rarely the right answer for production parts. Where Atlantis is useful in this corridor is the industrial side: weld inspection for fabricators and structural steel to AWS D1.1, UT and MT on tooling, lifting and test equipment, thickness surveys on plant utilities, and pressure vessel and piping NDE at manufacturing sites. Seattle also has a working waterfront, with ship repair yards, fishing-fleet maintenance on the Lake Washington Ship Canal and the Port of Seattle terminals, where UT gauging and weld inspection are routine. See Seattle weld inspection and Everett NDT consulting.

Bremerton and the Kitsap naval yards

Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility in Bremerton maintains and overhauls nuclear-powered carriers and submarines, and Naval Base Kitsap at Bangor supports the submarine fleet. Navy work is governed by NAVSEA technical publications and contract-specific requirements, and much of it is performed by the shipyard's own workforce. Contractors and their suppliers, however, need inspection on fabricated parts, piping and structural repairs to Navy and commercial marine standards, and the surrounding marine industry needs hull gauging and weld inspection. See our maritime NDT consulting in Bremerton page.

Vancouver, Kalama and Longview on the lower Columbia

The lower Columbia River ports handle grain, bulk liquids, chemicals, forest products and steel. Longview and Kelso have pulp and paper mills whose digesters, recovery boilers, pressure vessels and process piping need regular UT thickness and weld inspection, and the Port of Vancouver USA hosts bulk liquid and industrial tenants with tanks and transfer lines. See the Vancouver, Washington and Longview, Washington pages.

Tri-Cities, Hanford, the Columbia dams and Spokane

In eastern Washington, Energy Northwest's Columbia Generating Station near Richland is the state's only commercial nuclear power plant, and the Department of Energy's Hanford Site carries a large, long-running cleanup programme with tank, piping and treatment-plant work governed by DOE and contract quality requirements. Grand Coulee, Chief Joseph and the Columbia and Snake River dams need penstock, gate, crane and structural weld inspection. Spokane adds aerospace and metals manufacturing, Fairchild Air Force Base and food processing, while wind farms across the Columbia Basin bring tower flange and weld inspection. Nuclear plant NDE is controlled by owner programmes and ASME Section XI, so we support those sites only within the owner's qualification requirements. See NDT training in Richland and practical NDT in Spokane.

API 510 pressure vessels. Washington refineries, chemical plants and pulp mills operate towers, drums, reactors, exchangers and digesters that run on API 510 inspection programmes. For these we carry out external visual examination, UT thickness at each vessel's CMLs, corrosion mapping where localised loss is expected, PAUT or TOFD on welds with a cracking history or previous repairs, and MT or PT on nozzles and internal attachments during entries. Readings are reported against the previous survey so your inspector can calculate corrosion rates and set the next interval. See API 510 pressure vessel inspection support and Seattle pressure vessel inspection.

API 570 piping. Refinery units on the Puget Sound carry thousands of piping CMLs. We survey them against your circuit isometrics, add scanning at injection points, mix points and deadlegs where your programme calls for it, and support CUI screening where insulation is stripped, which matters in a climate where insulation stays wet for months. Results are delivered per CML in a format your inspection data system can import. See API 570 piping inspection support, Seattle piping inspection and Seattle corrosion inspection.

API 653 storage tanks. Washington's tank population sits at refineries, marine terminals at Cherry Point, Anacortes, Tacoma, Seattle and Vancouver, and inland distribution terminals. For out-of-service inspections we perform MFL floor scanning with UT follow-up, shell course thickness surveys, shell-to-bottom and repair weld examination, nozzle and sump work and floating-roof seal and pontoon checks; for external inspections we survey shell thickness, examine roof, shell, foundation and appurtenances, and take settlement measurements presented against API 653 Annex B. Direct answer: At Washington refineries and mills, most inspection volume is planned months ahead around turnarounds and annual outages. Atlantis joins the planning stage, agrees methods and procedures, and mobilises crews to your site on dates fixed during scoping, so NDE does not become the critical path when equipment opens.

A turnaround inspection scope has three layers. Pre-shutdown work is done on-stream: thickness surveys, external visual inspection and PAUT or radiography of welds that can be examined in service. That work shrinks the list of items that must be opened. Shutdown work covers everything that needs entry or isolation: vessel internals, tank floors, exchanger shells and welds behind insulation. Post-repair work is the re-examination of every repair weld before start-up. We help you sequence those layers so scope moves out of the outage window wherever your code and inspector allow.

Points that matter in Washington: the refinery coast is wet for much of the year, so insulation removal, surface preparation and couplant choice need planning, and outdoor PT and MT need dry, protected work areas; winter weather in eastern Washington limits outdoor work at dams and wind sites; refinery access requires site-specific safety orientation and contractor prequalification, completed before mobilisation; and the refineries' new process safety rule (see below) raises the bar on documented mechanical-integrity evidence, which increases the value of a clean NDE record. Reports quote the procedure, acceptance criteria and code, list technician certifications and instrument calibration, and are reviewed under ASNT Level III oversight, which is what inspectors of record and auditors look for. Agree the format with us during scoping.

Do you offer RBI or fitness-for-service assessments?

No. Atlantis does not sell API 580/581 risk-based inspection or API 579 fitness-for-service assessments. We provide the inspection data those programmes use.

Get a Washington inspection scope

Whether you have a vessel due for its next API 510 inspection at March Point, a tank coming out of service at a Tacoma terminal, a turnaround weld list at Cherry Point, a pulp-mill outage in Longview or penstock welds on the Columbia, the starting point is the same: tell us the asset, method, code and dates. Get a quote for NDT inspection in Washington, or book a call with our ASNT Level III to talk through method selection first. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Also see all inspection services.

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Australia

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Australia, with its vast distances, fly-in fly-out rosters and resource-heavy economy, is one of the countries where that portal fits best. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician opens a job in a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, chooses and sets up the technique, carries out the inspection, records the indications and receives a score when the job closes. Australian inspection work runs from LNG trains on the Burrup Peninsula, Barrow Island, Curtis Island and Darwin Harbour, to iron ore and copper processing in the Pilbara and South Australia, alumina refineries in Gladstone and Kwinana, coal ports and power stations in the Hunter and Latrobe Valley, steelmaking at Port Kembla, naval shipbuilding at Osborne and Henderson, aerospace maintenance and manufacturing around every capital, and hydro schemes in Tasmania and the Snowy Mountains. Practical NDT gives trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in every state a place to practise without booking a bench, a specimen or a flight.

This page is the Australia hub. It links every state hub and the existing city pages, explains how the simulator's environments map to Australian industries, sets out the national and state regulatory picture, and shows how to arrange a demo. Practical NDT is practice. It is not a certification and never replaces a practical examination on real specimens under AINDT, ISO 9712 or an employer's written practice.

Practical NDT by state and territory

Short answer: each Australian state and the Northern Territory has its own Practical NDT hub with local industry, regulators and the simulator environments that fit. Three capital cities also have city pages. Use the table to jump to the page for your state.

State or territoryMain NDT sectorsEnvironments & methods to practiseCity pages
Western AustraliaOffshore and onshore LNG, iron ore, gold, nickel and lithium processing, Kwinana industry, naval shipbuilding at HendersonOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank, Welding Workshop; UT, PAUT, IRIS, PMI, LRUT, MFLPerth
QueenslandCurtis Island LNG, Gladstone alumina and power, Bowen Basin coal, Mount Isa, Defence aviation, sugar millsOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank, Aircraft Hangar; UT, IRIS, PMI, ET, MTBrisbane
New South WalesHunter coal and power, Port Kembla steel, Sydney aviation maintenance, naval dockyard, fuel terminalsWelding Workshop, Aircraft Hangar, Storage Tank; UT, PAUT, ET, PT, MT, MFLNone yet
VictoriaGeelong refinery, Gippsland gas, Latrobe Valley power, Melbourne aerospace manufacturing, Williamstown shipyardOil & Gas Site, Aircraft Hangar, Welding Workshop; IRIS, PMI, ET, PT, PAUTMelbourne
South AustraliaOsborne naval shipbuilding, Olympic Dam, Moomba gas, Whyalla steel, Port Pirie smeltingWelding Workshop, Oil & Gas Site; PAUT, TOFD, UT, IRIS, PMINone yet
Northern TerritoryIchthys and Darwin LNG, East Arm port, Defence bases, gas pipelines, remote miningOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank, Aircraft Hangar; UT, IRIS, PMI, MFL, ETNone yet
TasmaniaHydro-electric system, Bell Bay aluminium, Hobart zinc works, aluminium ferry building, portsWelding Workshop, Storage Tank, NDT Lab; UT, PAUT, TOFD, PT, ETNone yet

Western Australia. The state's inspection market is dominated by the resources sector: LNG on the Burrup Peninsula near Karratha, on Barrow Island and near Onslow; offshore platforms and floating facilities; iron ore mines, rail and ports in the Pilbara; and the Kwinana industrial strip south of Perth with alumina, nickel, lithium and fuel import facilities. Much of the workforce is FIFO from Perth. The Western Australia hub and the Perth page cover this in detail.

Queensland. Gladstone is the heart of Queensland's heavy industry, with three LNG plants on Curtis Island, alumina refineries, an aluminium smelter, power stations and a major port. Coal mines in the Bowen Basin, minerals processing at Mount Isa and Townsville, and Defence aviation at Amberley and Townsville add to the mix. See the Queensland hub and the Brisbane page.

New South Wales. The Hunter Valley and Newcastle carry coal export, power generation and heavy fabrication; Port Kembla near Wollongong is the home of steelmaking and a bulk port; Sydney has aviation maintenance, the naval base at Garden Island, fuel import terminals and the research reactor at Lucas Heights. See the New South Wales hub.

Victoria. Victoria combines the Geelong refinery, Bass Strait gas processing in Gippsland, coal and transitioning power assets in the Latrobe Valley, aerospace manufacturing and maintenance around Melbourne, and shipbuilding and defence vehicle manufacturing. See the Victoria hub and the Melbourne page.

South Australia, the Northern Territory and Tasmania. South Australia's naval shipbuilding at Osborne and its copper, gas and steel assets; the Territory's two Darwin LNG plants, Defence bases and remote mines; and Tasmania's hydro, smelting and marine industries each have their own hub: South Australia, Northern Territory and Tasmania. The Australian Capital Territory has little heavy industry and is covered by the New South Wales hub for practical purposes.

Australia's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Australian NDT work follows the resources and energy economy: LNG and gas processing, mining and minerals processing, power generation, refining and fuel storage, steelmaking and fabrication, defence shipbuilding and aviation, and transport infrastructure. Much of it is remote, rostered and shutdown-driven.

LNG and gas. Australia is one of the world's largest LNG exporters, with plants in Western Australia, Queensland and the Northern Territory. These plants combine cryogenic tanks, stainless and alloy piping, large heat exchangers, compressors and marine loading facilities. Their inspection programmes include corrosion monitoring and corrosion under insulation, heat exchanger tube inspection, positive material identification, tank inspection and weld inspection during shutdowns and modifications. Domestic gas processing at Moomba, in Gippsland and in the Surat and Bowen basins adds similar work, and long-distance pipelines need integrity programmes under AS 2885.

Mining and minerals processing. Iron ore, coal, gold, copper, nickel, lithium, zinc, lead, bauxite and uranium are mined across the country. Processing plants, alumina refineries and smelters run mills, kilns, digesters, thickeners, leach tanks and acid plants that need structural weld inspection, wear and thickness surveys, tank inspection and pressure equipment inspection. Shutdowns compress large inspection scopes into tight windows.

Power and utilities. Coal-fired stations in New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria are being retired over time, but boiler, turbine and pressure part inspection remains necessary while they operate. Gas-fired plants, hydro schemes in Tasmania and the Snowy Mountains, large wind and solar farms, batteries and new transmission lines create new inspection needs on structures, towers and bolted connections.

Refining and fuel storage. Australia now has two operating refineries, in Geelong and Brisbane, and relies heavily on fuel import terminals around the coast. Terminals and refineries need tank shell and floor inspection, pipeline and piping corrosion surveys and exchanger work.

Defence. Naval shipbuilding at Osborne in South Australia and Henderson in Western Australia, sustainment in Sydney, Perth, Cairns and Darwin, and the AUKUS submarine programme create long-term demand for weld inspection to demanding standards. Air force bases and aerospace maintenance across the country need eddy current, penetrant and ultrasonic inspection of aircraft structure and components.

Infrastructure and fabrication. Bridges, rail, stadiums, high-rise buildings and water infrastructure rely on structural steel fabrication to AS/NZS 1554 and on in-service inspection. Fabrication shops in every capital and regional centre need weld inspectors.

Environments and methods that match Australian work

Short answer: the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments match LNG, gas, refining, terminals and minerals processing; the Welding Workshop matches shipbuilding, fabrication, pipelines and mining structures; the Aircraft Hangar matches Defence and civil aviation; and the NDT Lab is where every trainee starts.

The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five workplace environments. The NDT Lab provides bench specimens and reference blocks for calibration and fundamentals. The Welding Workshop provides weld coupons and fabrication joints. The Aircraft Hangar covers airframe and component inspection. The Oil & Gas Site provides weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice inside a process plant. The Storage Tank environment covers UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank.

There are twelve methods. Surface methods are PT, MT and VT. Volumetric methods are UT contact, PAUT, TOFD and RT. Electromagnetic methods are ET and MFL. Specialised methods are LRUT guided-wave screening, IRIS internal rotary UT for heat exchanger and boiler tubes, and PMI alloy verification. The product includes 33 guided lessons and a job library of 52 NDT Lab jobs, 52 Welding Workshop jobs, 54 Aircraft Hangar jobs and 73 Oil & Gas Site jobs.

For Australia the mapping is broad because the economy is broad. LNG and gas processing need IRIS, PMI, corrosion mapping with UT and PAUT, LRUT pipe screening and tank surveys. Mining and minerals processing need structural weld inspection with UT and MT, wear and thickness surveys, and tank work. Shipbuilding needs PAUT and TOFD on thick welds, MT, PT and VT. Aviation needs ET, PT and UT. Fuel terminals need MFL floor screening and UT shell surveys. Power stations need boiler tube and exchanger inspection. A technician who moves between these sectors, as many Australians do over a career, can use the full library to stay current in each.

Regulators and requirements Australian technicians meet

Short answer: radiation is regulated by each state and territory under ARPANSA's national codes; pressure equipment and plant fall under state work health and safety regulators; pipelines follow AS 2885; offshore facilities in Commonwealth waters are regulated by NOPSEMA; and most NDT personnel hold AINDT certification under its ISO 9712 based scheme.

Radiation. ARPANSA sets national codes and standards, but licensing of industrial radiography is done by each jurisdiction: the Radiological Council in Western Australia, Queensland Health, the NSW Environment Protection Authority, the Department of Health in Victoria, the Environment Protection Authority in South Australia, NT Health in the Northern Territory, the Department of Health in Tasmania and ACT Health in the Australian Capital Territory. Requirements for licences and recognised qualifications differ between jurisdictions, and several refer to AINDT radiography and radiation safety certification. Confirm current requirements with the relevant regulator. Simulator radiography involves no radiation and needs no licence, but it does not substitute for licensing or safety training.

Plant and pressure equipment. Most jurisdictions apply the national model work health and safety laws, administered by bodies such as WorkSafe WA, Workplace Health and Safety Queensland, SafeWork NSW, SafeWork SA, NT WorkSafe and WorkSafe Tasmania. Victoria has its own Occupational Health and Safety Act and regulations, administered by WorkSafe Victoria. Boilers and pressure vessels above certain hazard levels need design and item registration, and in-service inspection commonly follows AS/NZS 3788. Design and fabrication reference AS 1210, AS 4037, AS 4041 and AS/NZS 1554, among others. AS 3978 gives general guidance on NDT.

Pipelines and offshore. Gas and liquid petroleum pipelines are designed and operated to AS 2885 under state and territory pipeline legislation. Offshore petroleum facilities in Commonwealth waters are regulated by NOPSEMA.

Certification. The Australian Institute for Non-Destructive Testing (AINDT) runs the main personnel certification scheme in Australia, aligned with ISO 9712, and most Australian employers and regulators reference it. Some employers working for US-owned operators, US OEMs or on US-code equipment use ASNT SNT-TC-1A, under which the employer's written practice governs qualification and certification. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only and does not train toward or administer AINDT or ISO 9712 certification. The simulator is scheme-neutral practice suitable for technicians under any scheme.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs across Australia

Short answer: trainees get guided fundamentals before limited bench time; working technicians keep less-used methods fresh between rosters; Level IIIs build scenario sets, benchmark crews and prepare teams for shutdowns.

Trainees. Australian NDT trainees typically combine a training course with on-the-job experience under supervision. Bench time on real specimens is limited and often far from where the trainee lives or works. The 33 guided lessons give a structured start: probe selection, calibration, scan planning, recognising indications and recording results. Trainees reach the bench or the site with the basics already in place.

Working technicians. FIFO rosters, long shutdown seasons and frequent moves between sectors mean many technicians use some methods only occasionally. Rare defect types are hard to see on real specimens at all. Short scored jobs on a laptop or tablet between swings keep those skills fresh.

Level IIIs and team leads. Before a shutdown, a Level III can build a scenario set matching the planned scope and assign it to the crew. The scores show who is ready and where support is needed. The same approach helps screen new hires and gives inspection companies a structured record of skills practice to discuss with clients.

Why simulator practice suits Australia

Short answer: distance, rostered work, compressed shutdowns and a tight labour market all make specimen-based practice hard to schedule. A browser-based simulator puts the same practice in front of every technician wherever they are.

Australia's main industrial sites are often thousands of kilometres from the capitals where training rooms and specimen collections sit. A Pilbara technician, a Moomba operator, a Gladstone contractor and a Darwin LNG crew cannot share one set of reference blocks. Flying people to a training room for practice is expensive and takes them off the roster.

The labour market is also tight. Resources, defence and energy transition projects compete for the same experienced inspectors, so companies need to bring new people up to speed faster and keep existing people consistent. Scored scenario sets give a measurable way to do both.

Practice in a simulator is safe. There is no radiation, no work at height, no confined space entry, no heat stress and no hot work. Mistakes cost points rather than reinspection or harm.

Supervised field experience remains essential. The simulator's role is to make the time on real assets count for more.

Practice vs certification

Short answer: Practical NDT is a skills-practice and readiness tool. It does not grant certification, it is not an AINDT or ISO 9712 examination, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens required by an employer's written practice under ASNT SNT-TC-1A.

Every recognised certification scheme combines training, documented experience and examinations, including a practical examination on real specimens. Under AINDT's scheme those examinations are run by the certification body; under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer's written practice sets the rules and the employer certifies. Simulator scores are not examination results under either.

What the simulator does is prepare people. Repeated set-up, scanning, interpretation and sizing build habits that exams and real jobs test, and a Level III can use the results to judge readiness. For radiography, state licensing and radiation safety training remain separate legal requirements.

Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. See ASNT NDT training in Australia and city pages for Perth, Brisbane, Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide and Darwin. Atlantis has no training centre in Australia.

Bring Practical NDT to your Australian team

Short answer: request a demo, tell us which states, sectors and methods your team covers, and we will show the matching environments and agree a pilot. Pricing is quote on request.

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and its scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. It is affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Inspection companies, asset owners' maintenance teams, Defence suppliers, registered training organisations and TAFE programmes can use it as supplied or ask for scenario sets aligned to their own procedures and job mix.

Getting started is simple. A short call establishes your work, whether that is LNG shutdowns, mining maintenance, shipbuilding, aviation or fabrication. We demonstrate the relevant environments, agree a pilot group and set up accounts so technicians can practise in a browser or app wherever they are. Team leads see results. Nothing needs to be installed.

  • Request a Practical NDT demo for your Australian team
  • Ask for an Australia quote for a crew, a cohort or a national workforce
  • Discuss pre-shutdown scenario sets for LNG, mining or power work

Read the Practical NDT overview for the full environment and method list.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator available in Australia?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so it can be used in every state and territory, including remote sites with a connection. There is no Australian centre to visit; demos are arranged through the contact form.

Does Practical NDT count towards AINDT certification?

No. It is practice only. AINDT certification follows its own ISO 9712 based training, experience and examination rules, and Atlantis does not provide AINDT or ISO 9712 training or examinations.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation in Australia?

Yes, as preparation. Scored jobs build the habits practical exams test. The exam itself must be taken on real specimens under the relevant scheme or written practice.

Is it suitable for FIFO technicians?

Yes. Jobs are short and run on a laptop, tablet or phone, so technicians can practise between swings or during downtime in camp.

Does it cover LNG and mining shutdown work?

The Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments cover IRIS, PMI, corrosion mapping, LRUT screening, weld inspection and tank surveys, which together match much of a typical LNG or minerals processing shutdown scope.

Does it cover aviation NDT?

Yes. The Aircraft Hangar environment has 54 jobs covering airframe and component inspection with ET, PT, UT and VT. Aviation qualification and airworthiness rules still apply to real work.

Does simulator radiography need a state licence?

No radiation is involved, so practice needs no licence. Real industrial radiography requires a licence from the state or territory radiation regulator.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: trainees on guided lessons, working technicians refreshing less-used methods and rare defects, and Level IIIs building and assigning scenario sets.

Can an Australian inspection company use it to benchmark new hires?

Yes. A Level III can assign the same scenario set to every candidate and compare scores objectively.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Australia?

Yes, ASNT SNT-TC-1A training only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility, for employers who need SNT-TC-1A personnel. See NDT training in Australia.

How do we start?

Request a demo. Pricing is quote on request.

contentHtml:
HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Bahrain

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Bahrain shows clearly why that matters in a small country with a dense industrial core. Within less than an hour's drive sit the Sitra refinery, newly expanded through the Bapco Modernisation Programme, one of the world's largest single-site aluminium smelters, a regional ship repair yard on Hidd, an LNG import terminal, gas plants, a petrochemical and fertiliser complex, the onshore Bahrain Field around Awali, and the power and desalination plants that supply the islands. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician enters a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, takes a job, sets up the technique, scans or interprets, and is scored the moment the job is closed. For Bahraini crews it means more practice on the exchanger tubes, vessel welds, tank floors and hull welds they meet at work, without consuming specimens or booking lab time.

This is the Bahrain hub for Practical NDT. It covers where Bahrain's NDT work happens, which simulator environments and methods fit it, the regulators and certification expectations technicians in Bahrain work under, and a plain explanation of what a simulator can and cannot do for certification. To see it applied to your own work, request a Practical NDT demo for Bahrain.

Bahrain's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Bahraini NDT work is driven by refining at Sitra, onshore oil and gas production, gas processing, LNG import, petrochemicals and fertilisers, aluminium smelting and downstream metals, ship repair, ports, power and desalination, and aviation maintenance. Almost all of it is concentrated on the east coast of the main island, around Sitra, Ma'ameer, Askar, Hidd and Awali.

Sitra and the refinery. The Sitra refinery is Bahrain's only refinery and one of the oldest in the Gulf. The Bapco Modernisation Programme, a multi-billion-dollar upgrade, replaced several of its oldest crude and vacuum units with a new integrated unit and lifts crude capacity from about 267,000 to about 400,000 barrels a day, with large increases in diesel and jet fuel output. That leaves Sitra with a rare mix: brand-new process units heading into their first inspection cycles alongside long-serving plant, tank farms, product pipelines and the marine terminal. Turnaround work here means IRIS on exchanger and air-cooler tubes, PMI on alloy circuits, TOFD and PAUT on pressure vessel welds, corrosion mapping on piping and MFL and UT on storage tanks.

Ma'ameer and Sitra industrial area. Next to the refinery, the petrochemical complex produces ammonia, methanol and urea, and nearby industrial estates host fabrication shops, coating and maintenance contractors, chemical plants and tank storage. Process-plant NDT and shop testing of spools, vessels and structures are daily work.

Awali and the Bahrain Field. The onshore Bahrain Field, where oil was first discovered on the Arabian side of the Gulf in 1932, is still producing, with ongoing drilling, gas development and enhanced recovery. Gas processing plants handle associated and non-associated gas. Upstream inspection covers flowlines, gathering stations, gas-plant vessels and exchangers, and storage, with corrosion surveys, guided-wave screening and weld inspection on new facilities.

Askar and the aluminium cluster. Aluminium Bahrain's smelter at Askar, expanded with its Line 6 potline, is one of the largest single-site smelters in the world, with its own power station and a cluster of downstream rolling, extrusion and cable plants around it. Smelter maintenance means structural steel, cranes, gas-treatment ducting, carbon plant equipment, power station boilers and turbines, and the welds and castings throughout them.

Hidd and the ship repair yard. The Arab Shipbuilding and Repair Yard on Hidd dry-docks and repairs large vessels, including tankers and gas carriers, and fabricates steel structures. Hidd is also home to Khalifa Bin Salman Port, the Bahrain LNG import terminal and large power and water plants. Ship repair brings hull and structural weld inspection by UT, PAUT, MT and VT; the LNG terminal brings cryogenic piping and storage; the power plants bring boiler and condenser tube work.

Manama, Muharraq and the airport. The capital hosts operator and contractor offices, engineering consultancies and inspection companies, and Bahrain International Airport on Muharraq supports airline and aircraft maintenance where eddy current, penetrant and UT inspection are routine.

Practical NDT by area in Bahrain

Direct answer: Atlantis does not yet have Practical NDT pages for individual Bahraini cities, so this hub covers the main work areas directly. Because the island is compact, many technicians work across several of them in a single year. The table maps each area to the environments and methods that match its everyday jobs.

AreaMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise
SitraRefining (modernised units and older plant), tank farms, marine terminal, product pipelinesOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; IRIS, PMI, TOFD, PAUT, MFL, UT
Ma'ameer and Sitra industrial areaPetrochemicals and fertilisers, chemicals, fabrication, storageOil & Gas Site, Welding Workshop, NDT Lab; UT, RT, PMI, PT, MT
Awali and the Bahrain FieldOnshore oil production, gas processing, flowlines, storageOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; UT, LRUT, PAUT corrosion mapping, RT
AskarAluminium smelting, captive power, downstream metalsNDT Lab, Welding Workshop, Oil & Gas Site; UT, MT, VT, PT, IRIS
HiddShip repair and fabrication, port, LNG import terminal, power and waterWelding Workshop, Storage Tank, Oil & Gas Site; PAUT, UT, MT, VT, IRIS
Manama and MuharraqOffices and inspection company bases, aviation maintenanceNDT Lab, Aircraft Hangar; UT, ET, PT

Sitra. The modernised refinery is the heart of Bahraini inspection demand. New units need baseline and first-turnaround inspection, older units need careful corrosion and cracking assessment, and both need exchanger tube work. The Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments match that work closely. Atlantis has a Sitra NDT ERP page and an asset integrity digital twin page for Sitra.

Ma'ameer. Ammonia, methanol and urea plants have their own damage mechanisms, so PMI, UT thickness surveys and weld inspection on vessels and piping are routine. The NDT Lab and Welding Workshop serve the fabrication shops nearby.

Awali. Production and gas-plant integrity is mostly corrosion data plus weld inspection on new facilities. The Oil & Gas Site's corrosion mapping and LRUT jobs, and the Storage Tank's shell and floor surveys, are the closest match.

Askar. Smelter maintenance relies heavily on visual, magnetic particle and ultrasonic inspection of structural welds, cranes and rotating equipment, with boiler and condenser tube work at the captive power station. The NDT Lab and Welding Workshop cover the fundamentals; IRIS practice in the Oil & Gas Site fits the power plant.

Hidd. Ship repair needs consistent weld inspectors, which makes the Welding Workshop the core, while the LNG terminal and power plants bring tank, piping and tube inspection.

Manama and Muharraq. Inspection companies based in the capital can roll the simulator out across their whole workforce, and aviation teams use the Aircraft Hangar. See NDT training in Manama, the Manama NDT consulting page and the Manama ERP page.

Environments and methods that match Bahraini work

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. In Bahrain the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank cover refining, gas, petrochemical and LNG integrity; the Welding Workshop covers ship repair and fabrication; the NDT Lab covers fundamentals and smelter maintenance basics; and the Aircraft Hangar covers aviation.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). Weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant: contact UT and PAUT corrosion mapping, TOFD on pressure welds, IRIS internal rotary UT on exchanger and boiler tubes, LRUT guided-wave screening on long pipe runs and PMI alloy verification. It mirrors turnaround work at Sitra, the gas plants, the petrochemical complex and power station outages.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank. Sitra's tank farms, upstream storage and terminal tankage make this one of the most directly useful environments in Bahrain.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints for RT film and digital image interpretation, UT and PAUT detection and sizing, TOFD, MT and VT against acceptance criteria. It serves ship repair and steel fabrication at Hidd, fabrication shops in the Sitra and Ma'ameer area, and construction work on new plant.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks for calibration, probe handling, sensitivity setting, scan coverage and indication recognition. It is the starting point for trainees and a quick check for experienced technicians before a practical examination.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection with eddy current, penetrant and UT, relevant to aircraft maintenance at Bahrain International Airport and to technicians who move between aviation and industrial work.

Across the twelve methods, surface methods (PT, MT, VT) cover structural welds, cranes and finished parts; volumetric methods (UT contact, PAUT, TOFD, RT) carry weld quality and corrosion assessment; electromagnetic methods (ET, MFL) cover aviation parts, tubes and tank floors; and the specialist techniques (LRUT, IRIS, PMI) reflect the integrity programmes run at the refinery, gas plants and petrochemical complex.

Regulators and requirements Bahraini technicians meet

Short answer: in Bahrain, industrial uses of radiation, including radiography sources and devices, are licensed by the Supreme Council for Environment; personnel certification follows the operator's or contractor's requirements, where ASNT SNT-TC-1A based written practices and ISO 9712 certification are both widely used; and design and inspection follow operator specifications and ASME, API and AWS codes.

Radiation safety. The Supreme Council for Environment regulates peaceful uses of radiation in the Kingdom, licensing facilities and activities that use radioactive materials, radiation sources and radiation-emitting devices, which includes industrial radiography. Importing sources also involves customs clearance with the council's approval. The National Health Regulatory Authority regulates healthcare facilities and professionals rather than industrial radiography. Confirm current licensing and training requirements directly with the Supreme Council for Environment before planning radiography work. The RT jobs in Practical NDT involve no radiation source and count toward no Bahraini radiation licence; they are technique and image interpretation practice only.

Personnel certification. Bahraini operators and their contractors set NDT personnel requirements in contracts and vendor qualification documents. Technicians in Bahrain typically hold ASNT SNT-TC-1A based certifications under an employer's written practice, ISO 9712 certifications from recognised certification bodies, or both, and operators may add their own competence checks for techniques such as PAUT or TOFD. The specification on your contract decides. Atlantis training aligns with ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, and Atlantis does not train toward, certify or administer ISO 9712 or any operator approval. Practical NDT is practice for whichever scheme you work under.

Codes and standards. Bahraini projects commonly reference operator engineering specifications together with ASME Section V, VIII and B31.3, API 650 and 653 for tanks, API 1104 for pipelines and AWS D1.1 for structures, while ship repair at Hidd follows classification society rules. These are mentioned as working context only. Real acceptance criteria always come from your procedure and your Level III.

Workforce development. Bahrain has long encouraged the training and employment of Bahraini nationals in technical roles, and many employers combine classroom training with structured on-the-job development. A simulator can support that work as a practice tool; it is not a qualification in its own right.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Bahrain

Direct answer: Practical NDT adapts to three kinds of user. New trainees get guided fundamentals, working technicians get rare-defect refreshers between assignments, and Level IIIs and team leads build and assign scenario sets, benchmark crews objectively and find coverage gaps before a campaign.

New trainees. Young Bahrainis entering inspection careers, and new hires joining contractors from abroad, all need hands-on repetition that a busy lab cannot always provide. Guided fundamentals in the NDT Lab let a trainee practise calibration, angle-beam setup, scan coverage and indication interpretation with instant feedback, so a real reference block is never the first attempt. It is good NDT practical exam preparation, with the clear understanding that the real exam is taken on real specimens.

Working technicians. On a small island, a technician may move from a ship repair job at Hidd to a smelter shutdown at Askar and then to a refinery turnaround at Sitra within months. Each needs different skills: PAUT on hull welds, MT on crane structures, IRIS on exchanger bundles. Rare-defect refreshers on lack of fusion, fatigue cracking, stress corrosion cracking, hydrogen damage, tube pitting and wall loss help them switch between jobs without relearning on site.

Level IIIs and team leads. The modernised refinery's first major turnarounds will bring together large crews from several contractors. A Level III can send one scenario set to every technician, compare results like for like and see where support is needed before the shutdown starts. The same approach helps check that new or revised procedures written for the new units are understood before they reach the field.

Practice vs certification

Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification. It does not grant a level under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, ISO 9712, an operator's competence scheme or any employer's written practice. It does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that those schemes require, and it does not satisfy any Supreme Council for Environment radiation requirement. What it adds is realistic repetition: more chances to set up, scan, interpret and get feedback than a lab timetable or specimen store allows. It complements formal NDT training and on-the-job experience; the formal practical exam remains the step that counts.

Why virtual NDT training suits Bahraini employers

Direct answer: Bahrain's inspection demand is concentrated in a few large assets with intense shutdown peaks, including a refinery entering a new era after modernisation, and the same pool of technicians serves them all. A browser-based ultrasonic testing simulator and phased array simulator let employers build and check skills ahead of each peak.

The economics are simple. Turnarounds at Sitra, smelter shutdowns at Askar and dry-dock schedules at Hidd all compete for the same experienced people, often at the same time of year. Lab time, flawed specimens and senior supervisors are limited, and summer heat makes outdoor practice impractical for months. The simulator runs on a laptop at home, in an office or in a site cabin, subject to company IT rules, so technicians can practise in the weeks before a peak and supervisors can see scores rather than self-assessments. For a contractor mobilising crews that have not worked together, a common scenario set gives a quick, fair picture of who is ready for IRIS, TOFD or PAUT. None of this replaces time on real equipment; it makes that time count for more.

The simulator's jobs and feedback are presented in English. If Arabic or another language matters for your team, ask about it during the demo.

Who in Bahrain typically looks at Practical NDT

Groups that tend to find a simulator useful in Bahrain include inspection service companies supporting refinery, gas, petrochemical and power work; contractors mobilising for turnarounds at Sitra; ship repair and steel fabrication teams; maintenance and inspection teams in the aluminium and downstream metals cluster; training providers developing Bahraini technicians; aviation maintenance teams; and individual technicians preparing for an exam, a new method or a move into advanced UT. These are industry descriptions, not a customer list; Atlantis does not name customers on this page, and the companies and assets mentioned are local industry context only.

For Bahraini employers working to ASME and API codes or for US-owned contractors and OEMs, Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A aligned NDT training online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility, and Level III consulting on procedures, techniques and written practices. The Atlantis ERP for Bahrain can record ISO 9712 certificates and operator approvals alongside ASNT-based ones for companies managing mixed crews, and Atlantis also has pages on radiographic testing in Bahrain and an asset integrity digital twin for Bahrain.

Bring Practical NDT to your Bahrain team

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience. The scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who also leads Atlantis training. A rollout starts with a short online demo, then a conversation about your work: a Sitra turnaround contractor, a gas-plant integrity team at Awali, a smelter maintenance group at Askar, a Hidd ship repair quality department or a training provider in Manama. Together we choose the environments and methods that fit your jobs, set up scenario sets for your Level III, and technicians get access by browser or app wherever they are. Everything is delivered online; there is no physical centre to visit.

Pricing is quote on request, and the offer is built to be affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Book a Bahrain Practical NDT demo, read the Practical NDT overview, or write to info@atlantisndt.com.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in Bahrain?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so it works anywhere in Bahrain with a connection, from Manama and Muharraq to Sitra, Awali, Askar and Hidd. There is no physical centre to visit.

Does Practical NDT count toward ASNT, ISO 9712 or operator approval in Bahrain?

No. It is practice only. Certifications and operator competence checks need their own training, experience and examinations, including practical tests on real specimens or equipment. The simulator helps you prepare.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation?

Yes, it builds familiarity, speed and confidence with setups, scanning and interpretation before a practical exam. It does not replace the exam or the experience hours your scheme or employer requires.

Is it useful for turnarounds at the Sitra refinery?

Yes for the underlying skills: IRIS on exchanger tubes, PMI on alloy piping, TOFD and PAUT on vessel welds, corrosion mapping and tank surveys. Turnaround procedures and acceptance criteria still come from the operator, your employer and your Level III.

Does it help with ship repair weld inspection at Hidd?

Yes. The Welding Workshop covers UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT, VT and RT interpretation on fabrication welds. Classification society requirements still apply on real work.

Is it relevant to aluminium smelter maintenance?

For the core methods, yes: VT, MT and UT on structural welds and components in the NDT Lab and Welding Workshop, and IRIS for power plant tubes. Smelter-specific procedures still come from the plant and your Level III.

Does it include radiography, and does that count toward a radiation licence?

It includes RT technique and image interpretation practice with no radiation source. It does not count toward any Supreme Council for Environment licence or radiation protection requirement.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: guided fundamentals for new trainees, rare-defect refreshers for working technicians, and scenario building and crew benchmarking for Level IIIs and team leads.

Is the simulator available in Arabic?

The simulator's jobs and feedback are presented in English. Ask during the demo if Arabic or another language matters for your team.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Bahrain?

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A and is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. It suits employers working to US codes or US clients. It is not ISO 9712 training. See NDT training in Manama.

How do we start?
