contentHtml:
HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Belgium

Belgium splits its NDT work between two very different industrial worlds. In Flanders, the Port of Antwerp-Bruges holds Europe's largest integrated chemical cluster, refineries and vast tank farms, with a steelworks and more chemicals at Ghent and an LNG terminal at Zeebrugge. In Wallonia, Liège and Charleroi anchor an aerospace industry that builds engine and airframe parts for the world's major aircraft programmes. Between them sit nuclear stations at Doel and Tihange, a dense gas transmission hub and a growing offshore wind sector off the coast. Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator gives Belgian technicians in both worlds a place to practise. It is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app: a technician enters a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, sets up the technique, inspects, reports and receives a score when the job is closed. Trainees, working technicians and Level 3s can all use it, without reserving bench time or consuming a single physical specimen.

This hub covers all of Belgium. It sets out where the work is, which environments and methods match Belgian industry, how simulator practice relates to EN ISO 9712 and EN 4179 certification, and how to arrange a demo. The Antwerp page goes into more detail on the port.

Belgium's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Belgian NDT work concentrates in the Antwerp port and chemical cluster, the Ghent canal zone, the Zeebrugge and coastal energy hub, the Doel and Tihange nuclear sites, and the Walloon aerospace and industrial belt around Liège, Charleroi and Hainaut, with Brussels as a base for engineering, aviation and certification activity.

Antwerp. The port of Antwerp, now part of Port of Antwerp-Bruges, hosts the largest integrated chemical cluster in Europe. Refineries, steam crackers, base-chemical and polymer plants, industrial gas plants and some of Europe's largest independent tank terminals run along both banks of the Scheldt. A large new ethane cracker project has added years of heavy construction work on the left bank. The inspection workload is huge and continuous: in-service inspection of piping, vessels, exchangers and furnaces during turnarounds; tank shell and floor inspection at the terminals; alloy verification; and weld inspection on new construction and modifications. Contractors come from across Belgium, the Netherlands, France and Germany.

Ghent and the canal zone. The canal from Ghent to Terneuzen is lined with heavy industry, including a large integrated steelworks, chemical and bio-based plants, power generation and a car assembly plant. The port is part of North Sea Port, a cross-border port shared with Vlissingen and Terneuzen in the Netherlands. The steelworks brings structural, crane, gas-holder and vessel inspection, and the chemical plants bring classic plant inspection.

Zeebrugge, Ostend and the coast. Zeebrugge hosts a major LNG terminal and is a landing point for gas pipelines from Norway and the UK, making it one of Europe's important gas hubs. Ostend is the service base for Belgium's offshore wind farms in the North Sea, and an artificial energy island is under construction offshore to connect future wind capacity. Belgian dredging and marine contractors, among the largest in the world, build and maintain offshore infrastructure globally and employ inspection staff for their vessels and projects.

Nuclear: Doel and Tihange. Belgium's two nuclear sites are Doel, on the Scheldt near Antwerp, and Tihange, on the Meuse near Huy. Belgium's nuclear story is closely tied to NDT: in 2012, ultrasonic inspection of the reactor pressure vessels at Doel 3 and Tihange 2 revealed large numbers of hydrogen-flake indications, leading to years of analysis and eventually the permanent shutdown of both units. Several older units have since closed, Doel 4 and Tihange 3 continue under a life-extension programme, and Belgium's parliament repealed the 2003 nuclear phase-out law in 2025. Outage inspections at the operating units remain a significant source of qualified NDT work.

Liège. Liège is the centre of Wallonia's aerospace industry, with aero-engine compressor and module manufacturing around Herstal and Milmort, a major air cargo airport at Bierset and a long engineering tradition. The steel industry that once dominated the Meuse valley has largely closed, but fabrication, mechanical engineering and the Tihange site keep plant inspection work in the region.

Charleroi and Hainaut. The Gosselies area near Charleroi hosts aerostructures manufacturers producing wing and fuselage parts and assemblies, along with aviation maintenance. Hainaut also has a petrochemical site at Feluy, chemical plants at Tertre and a broad base of metalworking and fabrication companies.

Brussels and Flemish Brabant. Brussels Airport has aircraft maintenance and component operations, and many engineering firms, inspection bodies and certification organisations are based in and around the capital, including the Belgian NDT association BANT.

Practical NDT by city and region in Belgium

Short answer: Antwerp has its own Practical NDT page. The table below covers Antwerp and Belgium's other main clusters, with the environments and methods that fit each.

City or regionMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise
AntwerpChemicals, refining, tank storage, nuclear (Doel), constructionOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank, Welding Workshop; UT, PAUT, IRIS, PMI, MFL, TOFD
Ghent and the canal zoneSteel, chemicals, power, automotiveWelding Workshop, Oil & Gas Site; UT, MT, PAUT, PMI
Zeebrugge and OstendLNG, gas pipelines, offshore wind, marine contractorsStorage Tank, Oil & Gas Site, Welding Workshop; UT, LRUT, PAUT, TOFD
Liège and the Meuse valleyAero-engines, air cargo, nuclear (Tihange), fabricationAircraft Hangar, NDT Lab, Welding Workshop; ET, PT, UT, RT
Charleroi and HainautAerostructures, petrochemicals, chemicals, metalworkingAircraft Hangar, Oil & Gas Site; ET, UT, PT, PMI, IRIS
BrusselsAviation maintenance, engineering and inspection officesAircraft Hangar, NDT Lab; ET, PT, UT, VT

Antwerp is Belgium's largest pool of NDT work by a wide margin. Turnarounds at the refineries and crackers draw international crews for short, intense periods, and technicians need to be immediately productive on exchanger tubes, corroded piping, alloy lines and furnace components. The Oil & Gas Site environment, with 73 jobs, covers that work, including IRIS, PMI and LRUT screening. The terminals keep the Storage Tank environment busy with shell thickness and MFL floor screening practice, and new construction brings PAUT and TOFD weld inspection in the Welding Workshop. Atlantis also has an ASNT SNT-TC-1A training page for Antwerp for employers who work to US codes.

Ghent and the canal zone combine steel and chemicals. Steelworks inspection involves welded structures, cranes and runways, vessels, gas systems and rotating equipment, where MT and UT are the core methods. The chemical and power plants along the canal add plant inspection practice in the Oil & Gas Site.

Zeebrugge and Ostend are about gas and the sea. LNG tanks, cryogenic piping and pipeline reception facilities suit the Storage Tank and Oil & Gas Site environments, including LRUT screening of long pipe runs. Offshore wind foundations and marine structures bring thick-section weld inspection with PAUT and TOFD.

Liège is the aerospace capital of Wallonia. Aero-engine compressor parts and modules are inspected with penetrant, eddy current, ultrasound and visual methods to tight acceptance criteria, which maps to the Aircraft Hangar environment and its 54 jobs and to NDT Lab fundamentals. Fabrication and the nearby nuclear site add weld inspection.

Charleroi and Hainaut combine aerostructures with petrochemicals. Aerostructure inspection relies on UT of composite and metallic parts and ET around fasteners. The Feluy and Tertre sites need plant inspection with UT, IRIS and PMI.

Brussels is the base for aviation maintenance at Brussels Airport and for many engineering and inspection offices. Aviation technicians use the Aircraft Hangar environment, and engineers and Level 3s use the platform to build and assign scenario sets for teams working elsewhere in the country.

Environments and methods that match Belgian work

Short answer: the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments match Flanders' port and chemical industry, the Aircraft Hangar matches Wallonia's aerospace sector and Brussels aviation, the Welding Workshop matches steel, offshore and construction work, and the NDT Lab covers fundamentals.

The simulator has five environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. The methods are grouped as surface (PT, MT, VT), volumetric (contact UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT), electromagnetic (ET, MFL) and three specialist techniques: LRUT guided-wave screening, IRIS internal rotary UT for heat-exchanger and boiler tubes, and PMI for alloy verification.

  • Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs): weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant. The core environment for Antwerp, Ghent, Feluy and Tertre.
  • Storage Tank: UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank. Relevant to Antwerp's terminals and to LNG and product storage at Zeebrugge and elsewhere.
  • Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs): airframe and component inspection. The core environment for Liège, Gosselies and Brussels aviation.
  • Welding Workshop (52 jobs): weld coupons and fabrication joints. Relevant to steelworks maintenance, new plant construction, offshore wind foundations and metal fabrication across Wallonia and Flanders.
  • NDT Lab (52 jobs): bench specimens and reference blocks. Relevant to trainees, students and quality staff building calibration and set-up skills.

Belgium's mix creates an unusual training challenge. A technician in Antwerp might spend years on plant inspection and never see an aerospace component, while a Liège technician may be expert in penetrant and eddy current on engine parts but rarely touch a corroded pipe. When people move between sectors, or when a company wins work outside its usual field, the simulator lets them build the unfamiliar skills before they arrive on the job. Belgium's nuclear history also illustrates why careful ultrasonic technique and interpretation matter: indications in thick sections must be set up, scanned and characterised consistently, and repetition in a safe environment helps build that discipline.

Regulators and requirements Belgian technicians meet

Short answer: Belgian NDT personnel are usually certified to EN ISO 9712, often through BANT, which also certifies aerospace NDT personnel to EN 4179 and NAS 410; radiation is regulated by FANC; and pressure equipment follows the PED and Belgian in-service rules. Practical NDT is practice for any scheme and is not a certification.

Personnel certification. BANT, the Belgian Association for Non-Destructive Testing, was founded in 1984 and runs personnel certification in two sectors: a metallic products sector for manufacturing and in-service testing to ISO 9712, and an aeronautic sector for Level 1 and 2 examination and certification to EN 4179 and NAS 410. Many Belgian technicians also hold certificates from other EN ISO 9712 bodies, such as PCN or certifications from neighbouring countries, because crews regularly work across borders. Some employers serving US-owned operators, US OEMs or EPCs on US-code projects also qualify staff to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis training covers ASNT SNT-TC-1A only; Atlantis does not provide EN ISO 9712, BANT, EN 4179 or NAS 410 training or examinations.

Radiation protection. The Federal Agency for Nuclear Control (FANC, also known as AFCN) regulates ionising radiation in Belgium, including the authorisation of industrial radiography, and oversees the nuclear power plants together with its technical subsidiary Bel V. Industrial radiographers work under authorisations, radiation protection supervision and dosimetry requirements set by the Belgian radiation protection regulations. The simulator involves no radiation, so practising radiographic technique and interpretation in it needs none of these controls.

Pressure equipment and major hazards. New pressure equipment is placed on the market under the Belgian transposition of the Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU, while in-service rules for certain pressure equipment and steam installations require periodic examination by approved inspection bodies, with NDT often part of those examinations. Seveso sites, which are concentrated in the Antwerp and Ghent port areas, are subject to joint federal and regional major-accident inspections. If you are unsure which in-service regime applies to a specific item of equipment, confirm with the plant's approved inspection body.

Aviation and codes. Aviation maintenance is overseen by the Belgian Civil Aviation Authority under EASA rules, with NDT personnel controlled through Part-145 organisations' procedures. Codes in daily use include EN ISO weld testing standards, EN 13445 for pressure vessels, and ASME and API codes on US-specified plants and projects.

For written practices, procedures and audits for Belgian projects that work to US codes, see NDT Level III consulting in Belgium. To track BANT, EN ISO 9712, EN 4179 and ASNT certificates in one system, see the Atlantis ERP for Belgian inspection companies.

For trainees, working technicians and Level 3s in Belgium

Short answer: trainees build fundamentals with 33 guided lessons, working technicians refresh rare defects and less-used methods, and Level 3s and team leads benchmark crews objectively before turnarounds, outages and production campaigns.

Trainees. Belgian trainees come through technical secondary and higher education, welding and mechanical trades, aviation maintenance training and company programmes. The common problem is getting enough supervised hands-on time. The guided lessons start with calibration and reference blocks in the NDT Lab, progress to weld coupons, and then move to plant, tank and aircraft jobs. Each attempt is scored, so trainees can see their own progress.

Working technicians. Antwerp technicians may go from a cracker turnaround to a tank terminal to a construction project in a single season. Aerospace technicians may work one product line for months and then switch. The job library includes rare and hard-to-source flaws, from lack of fusion and transverse cracks in welds to tube wall loss at baffles, pitting under insulation and fatigue cracks around fastener holes, so technicians can practise the findings that matter before they meet them on a real asset.

Level 3s and team leads. A responsible Level 3 can build a scenario set for the work ahead, assign it to staff and incoming contractors, and compare results. That supports decisions on crew make-up and refresher training and shows whether a procedure is being interpreted consistently. For companies working in both Flanders and Wallonia, with staff certified under different schemes, a common practice set is a fair, neutral comparison.

Practice vs certification

Short answer: Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It does not grant BANT, EN ISO 9712, EN 4179, NAS 410 or ASNT certification, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens.

Every certification route used in Belgium requires documented training, supervised industrial experience and examinations, including a practical examination on real specimens. Under EN ISO 9712 that is handled by the certification body and its examination centres; in aerospace, by the certification body or the employer's responsible Level 3 according to EN 4179; under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, by the employer according to its written practice. Simulator practice is not counted as industrial experience by any of these schemes unless an employer's own procedures choose to recognise it, and Atlantis makes no claim that it is.

The value is in readiness. A candidate who has worked many virtual jobs goes into the practical exam knowing the set-up, scanning, interpretation and sizing routine. A supervisor has objective evidence of progress. An experienced technician can warm up on a less-used method before a job. For formal ASNT SNT-TC-1A training, see Atlantis NDT training.

Two industries, two languages, one practice library: why Belgian teams practise virtually

Short answer: Belgium's NDT work is divided between sectors, regions and languages, crews often cross borders, and physical practice specimens are scarce. An online simulator gives every technician the same practice jobs wherever they are.

Belgium's inspection industry has to bridge differences. Flanders and Wallonia have different industrial profiles and different working languages, and many companies operate in both. Crews on an Antwerp turnaround might include technicians from the Netherlands, France and Germany alongside Belgians. Aerospace suppliers in Wallonia work to the requirements of several international customers. In that environment, a shared set of practice jobs that everyone can access online is one of the simplest ways to set a common standard.

The work is also campaign-driven. Chemical and refinery turnarounds, nuclear outages and aerospace production ramps all compress inspection into tight windows. When the window opens, there is no time for someone to learn a method they have not used in months. Practising beforehand, at home or at the office, keeps skills ready for when they are needed.

Like its neighbours, Belgium faces an ageing NDT workforce and growing demand from energy transition projects, offshore wind, new chemical capacity and nuclear long-term operation. Bringing new entrants up to speed faster and giving experienced staff a structured way to stay sharp is a practical response that does not depend on building new labs.

Simulator practice is also completely safe: no radiation, no confined spaces, no work at height and no hot work. Trainees learn from a score, not from an incident.

Bring Practical NDT to your Belgian team

Short answer: request a demo, tell us what your team inspects, and we will show the right environments and set up a pilot. Pricing is quote on request.

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and its scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Practical NDT is affordable, accessible and fully customisable: Belgian inspection companies, plant operators, aerospace manufacturers, maintenance organisations and schools can use the standard library or ask for scenario sets built around their own procedures.

A typical start is a short call to understand your work, whether that is turnaround inspection in Antwerp, steel and chemical work in Ghent, LNG and offshore work on the coast or aerospace inspection in Liège and Charleroi. We demonstrate the relevant environments, agree a pilot group and set up access in a browser or app. Team leads can follow results from the first day. Delivery is online; Atlantis has no physical training location in Belgium.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in Belgium?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs online in a browser or app, so it can be used anywhere in Flanders, Wallonia or Brussels. Demos are arranged through the contact form.

Does Practical NDT count towards BANT or EN ISO 9712 certification?

No. BANT and other EN ISO 9712 certifications require training, industrial experience and examinations through the certification body. The simulator is practice only, and Atlantis does not provide BANT or EN ISO 9712 training or exams.

Is it useful for aerospace NDT in Liège and Charleroi?

Yes. The Aircraft Hangar environment has 54 jobs covering airframe and component inspection with ET, PT, UT and VT. It supports practice but does not replace EN 4179 or NAS 410 qualification.

Is it useful for Antwerp turnarounds?

Yes. The Oil & Gas Site environment covers corrosion, weld, tube and screening jobs, including IRIS, PMI and LRUT, and the Storage Tank environment covers tank shell and floor inspection.

Does it include radiography?

Yes, focused on technique and interpretation. No radiation is involved, so FANC authorisation does not apply to simulator practice; real radiography remains regulated by FANC.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation?

Yes, as preparation. It builds set-up, scanning, interpretation and sizing habits, but the exam must still be taken on real specimens under the relevant scheme.

Can it help with nuclear outage preparation at Doel or Tihange?

It supports general method practice, especially UT, PAUT and surface methods. Nuclear inspection relies on qualified techniques and personnel requirements that the simulator does not replace.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: trainees on guided lessons, working technicians refreshing methods and rare defects, and Level 3s who build and assign scenario sets.

Can Dutch, French or German contractors on a Belgian project use it?

Yes. Access is online, so everyone on a mixed crew can work the same scenario set before mobilisation, wherever they are based.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Belgium?

Yes, ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility for employers that need SNT-TC-1A personnel. See training.

contentHtml:
HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Denmark

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Denmark is a country where that kind of flexible practice suits an unusual industrial mix. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician steps into a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, takes a job, sets up the technique, scans or interprets, and gets a score the moment the job is closed. Denmark's NDT work is shaped by three things: the wind industry, in which Danish companies and ports have played a leading role for decades; the Danish sector of the North Sea, with its oil and gas fields and the redeveloped Tyra gas hub; and a compact but energy-intensive onshore industry of refineries, power and heat plants, district heating networks, cement, pharmaceuticals, food processing and shipbuilding heritage now turned to offshore fabrication. Practical NDT lets technicians keep their hands and eyes sharp between real jobs, at any level from first-week trainee to working Level III, without booking lab time or consuming specimens.

This page is the Denmark hub for Practical NDT. It covers where Danish NDT work actually happens, how the simulator's environments and methods map onto it, the certification and regulatory framework Danish technicians work inside, and an honest account of what a simulator can and cannot do. To see it with your own team's work in mind, request a Practical NDT demo for Denmark.

Denmark's NDT workforce and where the work is

Denmark's NDT work is concentrated on the west coast of Jutland around Esbjerg, in the wind manufacturing belt across Jutland and Funen, at the refinery and terminal towns of Fredericia and Kalundborg, and in the Copenhagen region. Offshore wind and North Sea oil and gas account for much of the specialised demand.

Esbjerg and the west coast. Esbjerg is Denmark's offshore capital. The port has served dozens of North Sea offshore wind projects as an installation and logistics base, and it is the supply and service hub for Danish oil and gas fields. Tyra, Denmark's largest gas field, located some 225 kilometres west of Esbjerg, was shut down in 2019 for a full redevelopment and resumed production in 2024 as a new offshore gas hub. Other fields and platforms in the Danish sector need ongoing integrity inspection, and some older facilities are moving toward decommissioning. The Thor offshore wind farm, Denmark's largest to date, is due to be installed from Esbjerg. Inspection companies, rope-access firms and offshore service contractors based in Esbjerg work on platforms, wind turbine foundations, towers, transition pieces and the vessels that install and service them.

Wind manufacturing across Jutland and Funen. Denmark is home to two of the world's largest wind turbine manufacturers and a long supply chain of tower, flange, foundation, casting and blade producers. Aalborg has blade production and a yard making transition pieces and foundations; the Lindø industrial port near Odense, a former shipyard, now fabricates and marshals offshore wind components; and towns across Jutland host factories and test centres. NDT here means weld inspection on towers and monopiles, ultrasonic inspection of large castings and forgings, and quality inspection of composite blades.

Refineries and terminals. Fredericia is the landing point for crude oil from the Danish North Sea and has a refinery and oil terminal, while Kalundborg on Zealand has a refinery inside an industrial symbiosis that also includes power generation and large pharmaceutical and biotech plants. Refinery turnarounds bring exchanger tube testing, alloy verification, corrosion mapping and tank inspection.

Power, heat and gas infrastructure. Denmark's combined heat and power plants, many converted from coal to biomass, waste-to-energy plants and very extensive district heating networks create steady demand for boiler tube, pressure part and pipe weld inspection. The Baltic Pipe gas link crossing Denmark to Poland, gas storage, planned hydrogen infrastructure and carbon capture and storage projects in the North Sea add pipeline and pressure equipment work.

Copenhagen and Zealand. Copenhagen Airport's maintenance operations, ferries and ports, bridges and tunnels including the major crossings to Sweden and between the Danish islands, and a cluster of engineering and testing organisations make the capital region a mixed market for aviation, structural and industrial NDT.

Practical NDT by region in Denmark

Denmark does not yet have city-level Practical NDT pages, so this table maps its main industrial centres to the environments and methods that fit. Danish crews often work across the North Sea basin, so neighbouring Practical NDT pages for Stavanger, Aberdeen, Hamburg and Rotterdam are linked below as well.

City or areaMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise
Esbjerg and the west coastOffshore wind installation and service, North Sea oil and gas, Tyra, supply baseOil & Gas Site, Welding Workshop; PAUT, TOFD, LRUT, UT, MT

Esbjerg. Two offshore industries share one port. Oil and gas platforms need corrosion mapping, guided-wave screening of risers and pipe runs, and weld inspection on modifications; wind foundations and towers need PAUT and TOFD on thick circumferential welds, MT on secondary steel, and UT on bolted flanges and structural details. Blade production adds composite quality inspection, and cement and port industry add maintenance work. The Welding Workshop is the main environment; the NDT Lab supports newcomers.

Odense and Lindø. The former shipyard site now fabricates and pre-assembles offshore wind structures, so weld inspection on large structures, with PAUT, TOFD, RT interpretation and VT, is the core practice set.

Kalundborg. A refinery, a power plant and large pharmaceutical and biotech production sites sit side by side. Refinery work is classic process plant inspection; pharmaceutical plants rely on stainless steel piping and vessels where PT, VT and weld UT matter.

Aarhus. Wind turbine engineering, manufacturing suppliers and a container port make central Jutland a mixed market for UT, ET, MT and PT on components.

Copenhagen. Airport maintenance brings eddy current, ultrasonic, penetrant and visual inspection of aircraft, while district heating and the large bridge and tunnel crossings bring weld and structural work. For the German side of the Baltic and North Sea, see Practical NDT Hamburg; for the ARA port cluster, see Practical NDT Rotterdam.

Environments and methods that match Danish work

The short answer: offshore wind and fabrication map to the Welding Workshop, North Sea oil and gas and refineries to the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank, aviation to the Aircraft Hangar, and manufacturing and component work to the NDT Lab. All twelve methods are available in every rollout.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints for monopiles, transition pieces, jackets, towers, flanges and pressure equipment: PAUT and TOFD on thick sections, RT interpretation, MT on structural welds and VT. For Danish wind fabrication this is the most important environment.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). The largest scenario set, covering weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant. It matches North Sea topsides, the Fredericia and Kalundborg refineries, and power and heat plants: UT and PAUT corrosion mapping, LRUT guided-wave screening, IRIS on exchanger and boiler tubes, PMI alloy verification and RT on piping.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank, matching the crude and product tanks at Fredericia, Kalundborg and coastal depots.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks for calibration habits and fundamentals, used by apprentices and by technicians moving into a new method, and by manufacturing quality teams inspecting castings, forgings and machined components.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection for Copenhagen and Billund airport maintenance and Danish helicopter operations supporting offshore work: eddy current, ultrasonic, penetrant and visual practice.

The twelve methods are PT, MT and VT; UT contact, PAUT, TOFD and RT; ET and MFL; and LRUT, IRIS and PMI, supported by 33 guided lessons.

Regulators and requirements Danish technicians meet

In Denmark, NDT personnel are normally certified to EN ISO 9712 under the Nordtest scheme, run by accredited Nordic certification bodies. Offshore oil and gas safety is supervised by the Danish Working Environment Authority. Practical NDT is practice for any scheme and is not part of Nordtest or other EN ISO 9712 certification.

Personnel certification. The Nordtest scheme for examination and certification of NDT personnel, aligned with EN ISO 9712, is the main scheme across the Nordic countries, with certificates issued by accredited certification bodies. Offshore wind and oil and gas projects often reference DNV standards and project specifications for NDT. US-owned assets, US OEM equipment and projects to ASME, API or AWS codes may also specify ASNT SNT-TC-1A, which is where Atlantis's ASNT experience is relevant.

Offshore oil and gas. The Danish Working Environment Authority is responsible for safety and health on offshore oil and gas installations, including review of the design of production facilities and pipelines and permits for operation, modification and decommissioning. The Danish Energy Agency handles licences, and the Danish Environmental Protection Agency handles the marine environment.

Pressure equipment. Pressure equipment is placed on the market under rules implementing the EU Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU, and in-service requirements for pressure equipment onshore come under the working environment rules administered by the Danish Working Environment Authority. Confirm the current inspection requirements for your installation with the authority or your inspection body.

Radiography. Use of radiation sources for industrial radiography requires authorisation under Danish radiation protection rules, administered by the radiation protection function of the Danish Health Authority (Sundhedsstyrelsen); confirm current requirements with the authority. The simulator's RT scenarios involve no source and do not count toward any radiation protection qualification.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Denmark

The short answer: apprentices and new entrants get guided fundamentals, working technicians get rare-defect refreshers between offshore and fabrication assignments, and Level IIIs get objective crew benchmarking and scenario control.

Trainees and apprentices. Denmark's vocational education system trains welders, industrial technicians and other skilled workers through combined school and company training, and the wind and offshore industries recruit heavily from it. NDT newcomers need repetitions that scarce specimens and busy labs cannot always provide. Guided lessons, then NDT Lab and Welding Workshop jobs with instant scored feedback, give them a structured start.

Working technicians. A technician may spend months on a single wind fabrication contract doing PAUT on circumferential welds, then move to a refinery turnaround or an offshore campaign. Practising rare and hard-to-source defects, such as lack of sidewall fusion, fatigue cracking at welded attachments, corrosion under insulation and exchanger tube pitting, keeps the other methods current.

Level IIIs and team leads. Level IIIs and QA managers can assign scenario sets, compare results across crews, suppliers and shifts, and find gaps before a fabrication campaign or installation season. The results support their judgement; they do not replace procedures, project specifications or certification records.

Practice vs certification

Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification, it does not grant or renew Nordtest, EN ISO 9712 or ASNT qualifications, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that every scheme requires.

Under EN ISO 9712 and the Nordtest scheme, certification requires documented training, industrial experience and an examination including a practical part on real specimens, administered by an accredited certification body. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer's written practice sets training, experience and examinations, including a practical exam on real specimens, and the employer certifies. A simulator builds familiarity and confidence; the formal steps remain.

Atlantis's training product follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A only and is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility; Atlantis does not train toward Nordtest or other EN ISO 9712 certification. For Danish employers, ASNT-based training mainly matters for work to US codes, for US-owned assets or for US clients. See NDT training and SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Installation seasons, fabrication peaks and offshore hitches: why Danish teams use virtual NDT training

Danish NDT demand is lumpy. Offshore wind fabrication peaks when a large project is in production, installation seasons run from Esbjerg and other ports in concentrated windows, and North Sea work runs on rotations and campaigns. A browser-based NDT simulator lets employers add practice capacity in those peaks without adding lab space, and lets technicians practise wherever they are.

Wind monopiles and transition pieces involve very long, thick welds where consistent PAUT and TOFD coverage, setup and sizing are essential, and where a missed or mis-sized indication is costly to find later. Rehearsing setups and interpretation before a fabrication campaign helps new operators reach consistency quickly. Offshore campaigns on platforms and turbines are expensive per day; arriving well-practised matters.

Representative flawed specimens in thick plate, castings and forgings are expensive and quickly memorised. The simulator's job library keeps defects varied and lets Level IIIs assign different sets to different people, so results stay meaningful.

Many Danish technicians also work in Norway, Germany, the Netherlands and the UK. A practice platform that goes wherever they go, and that a supervisor can use to benchmark crews from different countries on the same scenarios, fits that cross-border North Sea labour market well.

Bring Practical NDT to your Danish team

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience. The scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Access is by browser or app, so fabrication, offshore and plant staff use the same platform, and there is no physical centre to visit.

A rollout starts with a demo and a short scoping call on your methods, assets and crew levels. A wind fabricator might focus on PAUT, TOFD and MT in the Welding Workshop; an offshore service company on corrosion mapping, LRUT and weld inspection in the Oil & Gas Site; a refinery contractor on IRIS, PMI and tank work; an aviation maintenance team on the Aircraft Hangar. Level IIIs then assign scenario sets and follow results.

The offer is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with a quote on request. Book a Practical NDT demo for your Danish team, read the Practical NDT overview, or write to info@atlantisndt.com.

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in Denmark?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app and works anywhere in Denmark with an internet connection, from Esbjerg to Copenhagen. There is no physical Atlantis centre in Denmark; access is online.

No. It is practice only. Nordtest certification requires training, experience and examinations, including a practical exam on real specimens, through an accredited certification body. The simulator helps you prepare.

It can help you build familiarity, speed and confidence with setups, scanning and interpretation before a practical exam. It does not replace the exam or any required hands-on hours.

Yes for the underlying skills: PAUT and TOFD on thick welds, RT interpretation, MT and VT. Acceptance criteria and procedures for a given project still come from the project specification and your Level III.

Yes. The Oil & Gas Site covers corrosion mapping, guided-wave screening, exchanger tube testing, PMI and weld inspection in a process plant setting, which matches topsides and onshore terminal work.

Yes, as technique and image interpretation practice with no radiation source. It does not satisfy Danish radiation protection requirements for radiographers.

Is it an ultrasonic testing simulator?

Among other things, yes. It covers UT contact, PAUT and TOFD, plus IRIS for tubes and LRUT guided-wave screening, alongside surface, electromagnetic and PMI methods.

All levels: guided fundamentals for apprentices and trainees, rare-defect refreshers for working technicians, and scenario building and crew benchmarking for Level IIIs and QA managers.

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in France

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and France is a country where the demand for well-practised inspectors is unusually concentrated in two very exacting industries: nuclear power and aerospace. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. Technicians walk into a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, pick a job, set up the technique, scan or interpret, and receive a score the moment the job is closed. Around those two pillars France adds refining and petrochemicals at Fos-Lavéra, the Seine estuary and Donges, steel and LNG at Dunkirk, a chemical valley south of Lyon, naval and commercial shipbuilding on the Atlantic and Channel coasts, offshore wind farms now operating off Brittany and Normandy, and rail, automotive and heavy engineering across the country. Practical NDT lets technicians keep their hands and eyes sharp between real jobs at any level, from first-week trainee to working Level III, without booking lab time or using up flawed specimens.

This page is the France hub for Practical NDT. It explains where French NDT work actually happens, how the simulator's environments and methods map onto it, which certification and regulatory frameworks French technicians work inside, and what a simulator honestly can and cannot do. To see it with your own team's work in mind, request a Practical NDT demo for France.

France's NDT workforce and where the work is

French NDT work clusters around the nuclear fleet, the aerospace corridor from Toulouse to Bordeaux and the Paris region, the Mediterranean and Seine refining and petrochemical hubs, the northern steel and energy coast, and the Atlantic shipyards. Each cluster has its own method mix and its own customer specifications.

Nuclear power across the regions. France generates most of its electricity from a fleet of more than fifty pressurised water reactors operated by EDF, spread along rivers and coasts from Gravelines in the north to Tricastin in the Rhône valley and Blayais on the Gironde. Flamanville 3, an EPR, was connected to the grid in late 2024, and the government has backed a programme of new EPR2 reactors. Outages and the long-term life-extension programme known as the grand carénage generate a large volume of inspection: ultrasonic and eddy current examinations of welds, piping and steam generator tubes, radiography, surface methods and visual inspection, carried out by EDF teams and by a large supplier base. The discovery of stress corrosion cracking in certain safety-injection piping in 2021 and 2022 led to extensive checks across the fleet and underlined how much depends on reliable ultrasonic detection and sizing. Fuel-cycle facilities in the Rhône valley and on the Cotentin peninsula, and naval nuclear work at Cherbourg and Brest, add further specialised demand.

Aerospace: Toulouse, Bordeaux, Paris region. Toulouse is one of the world's two great centres of civil airliner assembly, surrounded by structure, systems and engine suppliers in Occitanie. Bordeaux and the wider Nouvelle-Aquitaine region host business jet, military aircraft, space and solid-propulsion work. The Paris region and the Seine valley carry engine manufacturing, helicopter work further south, and the maintenance bases of the main airports. Aerospace NDT is heavy in eddy current, ultrasonic inspection of composites and metallic parts, penetrant and visual work, all under tight customer and authority control.

Refining and petrochemicals. The Fos-sur-Mer and Étang de Berre complex near Marseille, the Lavéra petrochemical site, the Gonfreville and Port-Jérôme refineries in the Seine estuary near Le Havre, Donges on the Loire estuary, Feyzin in the Lyon chemical valley, and Dunkirk's energy coast with its LNG terminal together form France's process industry backbone. Shutdowns there involve exchanger tube testing, corrosion mapping, alloy verification and tank inspection.

Shipbuilding and offshore wind. Saint-Nazaire builds some of the largest cruise ships in the world and has become a base for offshore wind substations and foundations; Lorient, Brest and Cherbourg build and maintain naval vessels and submarines. France's first commercial offshore wind farms, off Saint-Nazaire, Fécamp and Saint-Brieuc, are now operating, with more under construction and planned. That brings PAUT, TOFD and RT on thick structural welds.

Steel, rail and heavy engineering. Steelmaking at Dunkirk and Fos, rail rolling stock and component plants in Hauts-de-France and eastern France, automotive plants across several regions, and pressure-equipment and boiler fabricators complete the picture.

Toulouse and Occitanie. Final assembly lines, aerostructure suppliers and engine and systems firms make Toulouse the heart of French aerospace NDT. Eddy current around fasteners and on bores, ultrasonic inspection of composite panels and metallic parts, and penetrant on machined components are daily work. The Aircraft Hangar environment is the obvious starting point; the NDT Lab supports newcomers learning instrument setup.

Bordeaux and Nouvelle-Aquitaine. Business and military aircraft, space and propulsion work bring aerospace inspection, while the Blayais nuclear plant on the Gironde estuary adds outage work. Technicians who move between both benefit from practising ET and UT in the hangar and weld inspection in the Welding Workshop.

Marseille and Fos. The Fos and Étang de Berre complex includes refineries, petrochemical crackers, chemical plants, a steelworks, LNG terminals and large tank farms. That is the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank in real life: IRIS on exchangers, PMI on alloy piping, MFL on tank floors, LRUT on pipe racks. Atlantis has an NDT training page for Marseille.

Le Havre and the Seine estuary. France's largest refining and petrochemical cluster sits between Le Havre and Port-Jérôme, alongside a major container port and offshore wind logistics. Turnaround crews practise exchanger tube testing, corrosion mapping and tank surveys. See the Le Havre digital twin page and Le Havre ERP page.

Paris region. Engine plants, MRO bases at the main airports, rail engineering and the head offices of many inspection and engineering firms make the Paris region a training and coordination hub. See the Paris NDT training page.

Saint-Nazaire. Large cruise ship blocks, offshore wind substations and aerostructure work share the same estuary. PAUT and TOFD on thick welds and RT interpretation are the core practice, done in the Welding Workshop.

Lyon and the Rhône valley. The chemical valley south of Lyon, the Feyzin refinery and the nuclear plants and fuel-cycle sites along the Rhône combine process plant work with nuclear examinations, so a mix of Oil & Gas Site and NDT Lab practice fits.

Dunkirk. Steelmaking, an LNG terminal and the Gravelines nuclear plant make Dunkirk a mixed industrial coast where weld, plate and tank inspection all matter.

Environments and methods that match French work

The short answer: aerospace maps to the Aircraft Hangar, refining and chemicals to the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank, shipbuilding and offshore wind to the Welding Workshop, and nuclear and manufacturing to the NDT Lab plus volumetric weld practice. All twelve methods are available in every rollout.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection for Toulouse, Bordeaux and Paris-region aerospace: eddy current around fastener holes and on wheels, ultrasonic thickness and bond checks, penetrant on components and structured visual inspection. It is where aerospace trainees build the habits that EN 4179-based written practices expect.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks for calibration, sensitivity setting and fundamental technique. Nuclear suppliers and manufacturing quality teams use it for UT on plate, bar and forgings, ET on tubes and machined parts, and MT and PT on components.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints for Saint-Nazaire, Brest, Cherbourg and the offshore wind supply chain, and for pressure-equipment fabricators: PAUT, TOFD, RT interpretation, MT and VT. Nuclear piping and component weld examinations rely on the same core skills of detection, characterisation and sizing.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). The largest scenario set covers weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant: IRIS on exchanger and boiler tubes, PMI alloy verification, UT and PAUT corrosion mapping, LRUT guided-wave screening, RT on piping. It suits Fos, Lavéra, the Seine estuary, Donges, Feyzin and Dunkirk.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank, matching the large terminals and tank farms at Fos, Le Havre, Donges and Dunkirk.

The twelve methods are PT, MT and VT; UT contact, PAUT, TOFD and RT; ET and MFL; and LRUT, IRIS and PMI, supported by 33 guided lessons.

Regulators and requirements French technicians meet

In France, NDT personnel are normally certified to NF EN ISO 9712 through COFREND, the French Confederation for Non-Destructive Testing, which runs sector-based certification schemes. Practical NDT is practice for any scheme and is not part of COFREND certification.

Personnel certification. COFREND certification by method, level and sector is the national reference for industry and for much of the nuclear and process work. Aerospace NDT personnel are typically qualified under EN 4179 through their employer's written practice, with national aerospace arrangements behind it. Nuclear operators and their suppliers also apply their own qualification requirements for specific examinations and qualified procedures. Projects for US-owned plants, US OEMs or work to ASME, API and AWS codes may additionally specify ASNT SNT-TC-1A, which is where Atlantis's ASNT experience is relevant.

Nuclear and radiation regulation. Since 1 January 2025, nuclear safety and radiation protection in France have been overseen by the ASNR (Autorité de sûreté nucléaire et de radioprotection), formed by merging the ASN and the IRSN. Industrial radiography is subject to radiation protection rules, and operators of industrial radiography and gamma radiography equipment must hold the CAMARI certificate of aptitude in addition to their NDT certification. Nuclear pressure equipment follows its own regulatory regime, and nuclear components are commonly designed and built to RCC-M. The simulator's RT scenarios involve no source and do not count toward CAMARI or any radiation protection qualification.

Pressure equipment. Conventional pressure equipment is placed on the market under the EU Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU, with in-service monitoring, periodic inspection and requalification under French pressure-equipment regulations overseen by the regional environment and industry directorates (DREAL) and carried out with notified or authorised bodies. EN 13445 and CODAP are common construction codes.

Codes in daily use. French technicians work to the EN ISO weld testing family (17635, 17640, 17636, 10675, 13588), to RCC-M and RSE-M in nuclear, to aerospace customer specifications, and to project specifications for offshore wind and oil and gas.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in France

The short answer: trainees in French vocational and alternance programmes get guided fundamentals, working technicians get rare-defect refreshers between outages and production campaigns, and Level IIIs get objective crew benchmarking and scenario control.

New entrants need repetitions they cannot always get on scarce lab specimens. Guided lessons, then NDT Lab and Welding Workshop jobs with instant feedback, give them a structured way to build technique before they are assessed for real.

Working technicians. Outage work is seasonal and intense; a technician may perform a particular examination only during a few weeks each year. Aerospace technicians may specialise on one structure for months. The simulator lets them rehearse rare and hard-to-find indications, such as stress corrosion cracking, lack of fusion, tube wall loss or fatigue cracks at fastener holes, before the next campaign.

Level IIIs and team leads. Level IIIs and supervisors can assign scenario sets, compare results across teams and sites, and spot weaknesses before an outage or production ramp-up. The data supports their judgement; it does not replace their procedures, qualification files or examinations.

Practice vs certification

Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification. It does not grant, renew or substitute for COFREND, EN ISO 9712, EN 4179, CAMARI or ASNT qualifications, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that every one of these schemes requires.

Under EN ISO 9712, certification requires documented training, industrial experience and an examination including a practical part on real specimens, administered under an accredited certification body such as COFREND. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer's written practice sets the training, experience and examinations, including a practical exam on real specimens, and the employer certifies. A simulator builds familiarity and confidence; the formal process remains.

Atlantis's training product follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A only and is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. Outages, ramp-ups and scarce specimens: why French teams use virtual NDT training

France's two biggest NDT customers, nuclear and aerospace, both demand very high consistency and both have been recruiting heavily. Nuclear new build and life extension, and airliner production ramp-ups, need more qualified inspectors than the existing pool, while experienced staff retire. A browser-based NDT simulator helps employers add practice capacity without adding lab space.

Nuclear outages compress inspection into tight windows, often far from home bases, with strict access and dose management. Rehearsing the logic of an examination beforehand, from setup to scan plan to indication characterisation, helps crews arrive ready. Aerospace production and MRO run in shifts with little slack; short virtual sessions fit around them.

Flawed specimens with known, documented defects are expensive and quickly memorised. In nuclear work in particular, representative specimens can be hard to obtain. The simulator's job library keeps scenarios varied, and Level IIIs can assign different sets to different people so results stay meaningful.

The same applies on the process side: Fos, Le Havre and Donges shutdowns bring contractors from all over France and abroad. A common set of practice scenarios gives a supervisor a quick, objective view of who is ready for which task.

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Germany

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Germany is a country where steady, repeatable practice matters a great deal. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician steps into a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, takes a job, sets up the technique, scans or interprets, and gets a score as soon as the job is closed. Germany's inspection work is unusually broad: automotive and supplier plants in Bavaria, Baden-Württemberg and Lower Saxony, rail vehicle and wheelset manufacturing, the chemical parks of the Rhine and central Germany, refineries and import terminals on the North Sea coast, aircraft assembly and maintenance around Hamburg, shipbuilding on the Baltic and North Sea, a fast-growing offshore wind supply chain, and a power sector that has moved from nuclear operation to decommissioning while building new gas, hydrogen and grid infrastructure. Practical NDT gives technicians a way to keep hands and eyes sharp between real jobs, at any level from first-week trainee to working Level III, without booking lab time or consuming specimens.

This page is the Germany hub for Practical NDT. It covers where German NDT work actually happens, how the simulator's five environments and twelve methods map onto that work, the certification and regulatory framework German technicians work inside, and an honest account of what a simulator can and cannot do. If you want to see it with your own team's jobs in mind, request a Practical NDT demo for Germany.

Germany's NDT workforce and where the work is

Germany's NDT work follows its industrial geography: series manufacturing in the south, chemicals and steel along the Rhine and Ruhr, energy and ports in the north, and a dense network of fabricators, test laboratories and inspection bodies everywhere in between. Each region asks for a different mix of methods, so a technician in Stuttgart has a very different week from one in Wilhelmshaven or Leuna.

The south: automotive, machinery and aerospace. Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg hold much of Germany's car and truck production, its powertrain and chassis suppliers, and a deep base of machine-tool, gear and bearing manufacturers. NDT here is production-line work: eddy current and magnetic particle testing of forged and machined parts, ultrasonic testing of welds and castings, penetrant testing of aluminium and safety-critical components, and visual inspection tied to quality systems. Southern Germany also has a significant aerospace and defence cluster, with engine, helicopter and military aircraft work around Munich and the Danube, which brings composite inspection and aerospace NDT personnel rules into play.

The Rhine, Ruhr and chemical belt. North Rhine-Westphalia and the Rhine valley carry Germany's heavy industry: steelworks around Duisburg, refineries in the Cologne and Gelsenkirchen areas, and large chemical sites along the river, with Ludwigshafen in Rhineland-Palatinate one of the biggest integrated chemical complexes in the world. Chemical and refinery work means pressure vessels, heat exchangers, alloy piping, furnaces and tank farms, with planned shutdowns that bring large inspection crews on site. Corrosion mapping, exchanger tube testing, alloy verification and weld inspection on repairs are routine.

Central Germany. The Leuna and Schkopau area in Saxony-Anhalt and the wider central German chemical triangle combine a refinery, chemical parks and industrial gas production. The east also has a refinery at Schwedt on the Oder, which has had to adapt its crude supply, plus pipeline and storage infrastructure.

The north coast: ports, energy and ships. Hamburg, Bremen, Bremerhaven, Cuxhaven, Wilhelmshaven and the Kiel area concentrate shipbuilding and ship repair, naval yards, oil and chemical terminals, the floating LNG import terminals added from 2022 at sites such as Wilhelmshaven and Brunsbüttel, and the ports and fabrication yards that serve offshore wind in the German Bight and the Baltic. Hamburg is also one of the world's main civil aircraft production and maintenance centres. Work here ranges from PAUT and TOFD on thick structural welds to storage tank surveys and airframe eddy current inspection.

Rail, energy and grids. Germany manufactures and maintains rail vehicles, bogies and wheelsets, which carry their own NDT requirements for wheels, axles and welded structures. In power, the last nuclear plants stopped operating in April 2023 and are now in decommissioning, while gas plants, district heating, the planned hydrogen core network and onshore and offshore grid connections create new inspection work on pipelines, vessels and structural steel.

Practical NDT by city in Germany

Germany's port city of Hamburg already has its own Practical NDT page. The table below links it and adds the other major industrial centres, mapped to the simulator environments and methods that fit their work.

City or areaMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise
HamburgCivil aircraft assembly and MRO, shipbuilding and repair, port terminals, refiningAircraft Hangar, Welding Workshop, Storage Tank; ET, UT, PAUT, PT
Ludwigshafen and the Rhine-NeckarIntegrated chemical production, process equipment, tank farmsOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; IRIS, PMI, UT, MFL
Leuna and central GermanyRefining, chemical parks, industrial gasesOil & Gas Site, NDT Lab; UT, RT, PMI, LRUT
Wilhelmshaven and the JadeCrude and LNG import terminals, tank storage, port energy projectsStorage Tank, Oil & Gas Site; MFL, UT thickness, LRUT
Stuttgart and Munich regionsAutomotive, suppliers, machinery, aerospace engines and helicoptersNDT Lab, Aircraft Hangar; ET, MT, PT, UT
Ruhr and Lower RhineSteel, refining, power and district heating, fabricationWelding Workshop, Oil & Gas Site; UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT

Hamburg. Hamburg combines one of the largest civil aircraft final assembly and cabin completion sites in Europe with a busy commercial port, shipyards, ship repair docks and a refinery on the Elbe. Aircraft work leans on eddy current around fastener holes, ultrasonic bond and thickness checks and penetrant on components, so the Aircraft Hangar environment is the natural start. Yard and port work calls for weld inspection and tank surveys. The Practical NDT Hamburg page has more detail, and Atlantis also has an NDT training page for Hamburg.

Ludwigshafen and the Rhine-Neckar. A chemical site of this scale contains thousands of pressure vessels, columns, exchangers and kilometres of alloy and carbon steel piping. Exchanger bundles make IRIS and eddy current tube testing a staple, mixed-alloy piping makes PMI part of almost every repair, and tank farms need floor screening. The Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments carry most of that practice. See the Ludwigshafen digital twin page for how Atlantis approaches asset data there.

Leuna and central Germany. Leuna's refinery and chemical park and the neighbouring sites around Schkopau and Bitterfeld bring turnaround-driven inspection: thickness surveys, weld radiography on repairs, alloy verification and guided-wave screening on pipe racks and road crossings. New technicians recruited in Saxony-Anhalt and Saxony can build fundamentals in the NDT Lab before going on site. See the Leuna ERP page for the inspection-company side.

Wilhelmshaven. Germany's deepest-water port handles crude oil, petroleum products and LNG, with large tank storage and a growing set of energy import projects. Storage tanks dominate: MFL floor screening, UT shell thickness and weld inspection on tank repairs. Pipelines running inland add LRUT practice. See the Wilhelmshaven digital twin page.

Stuttgart and Munich regions. Automotive and supplier quality departments depend on fast, consistent ET, MT and PT on high-volume parts, while the aerospace and engine cluster around Munich adds composite and component inspection. The NDT Lab's bench specimens and the Aircraft Hangar fit this mix well, and they let a quality team run the same scenario across shifts.

Ruhr and Lower Rhine. Steel, fabrication, power and district heating work means a steady flow of welds: UT, PAUT and TOFD on thick sections, RT on piping, MT on structural steel. The Welding Workshop environment is the closest match.

Environments and methods that match German work

The simulator's five environments and twelve methods line up closely with the main strands of German industry. The short answer is: automotive and rail favour the NDT Lab, aerospace favours the Aircraft Hangar, chemicals and refining favour the Oil & Gas Site, terminals favour the Storage Tank, and shipbuilding, steel and wind fabrication favour the Welding Workshop.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks are where calibration habits are formed. For German automotive suppliers and rail component makers, the lab environment is where a technician practises eddy current on machined parts, MT on forgings, PT on castings and UT on bar and plate. It is also the right place for apprentices and career changers to learn instrument setup before they touch a production line.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints cover the core of German heavy fabrication: shipyard block welds, steel structures for bridges and halls, offshore wind monopiles, transition pieces and jacket nodes, pressure-equipment fabrication to EN 13445 or AD 2000, and welded rail vehicle structures. PAUT and TOFD on thick welds, RT film or digital image interpretation, MT on fillet welds and VT are all practised here.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection fits Hamburg, Bremen and the southern aerospace cluster: eddy current around fastener holes and on wheels, ultrasonic thickness and bond checks, penetrant on components, and visual inspection of structures.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). The largest scenario set covers weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant. For the Rhine chemical belt, Leuna, the Ruhr refineries and the coastal terminals, it is where technicians practise IRIS internal rotary UT on exchanger tubes, PMI alloy verification, corrosion mapping with UT and PAUT, LRUT guided-wave screening on pipe runs and RT on piping welds.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank match the tank farms at Wilhelmshaven, Hamburg, the Rhine ports and inland refineries.

Across all environments the twelve methods are PT, MT and VT (surface); UT contact, PAUT, TOFD and RT (volumetric); ET and MFL (electromagnetic); and LRUT, IRIS and PMI. 33 guided lessons support the jobs for people who are new to a method.

Regulators and requirements German technicians meet

In Germany, NDT personnel are normally certified to DIN EN ISO 9712, and DGZfP, the German Society for Non-Destructive Testing, operates a widely used national personnel certification body. Practical NDT is practice for any scheme; it is not part of DGZfP certification and does not replace its examinations.

Personnel certification. Most German employers, inspection bodies and customers expect EN ISO 9712 certificates by method, level and industry sector. Aerospace NDT personnel are commonly qualified under EN 4179, usually through an employer's written practice and a national aerospace NDT board structure, and rail has its own qualification rules for wheelset and vehicle inspection staff. US-owned plants, US OEM supply chains and projects built to ASME, API or AWS codes may instead or additionally ask for ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ASNT certification, which is where Atlantis's ASNT expertise is relevant.

Pressure equipment. New pressure equipment is placed on the market under the EU Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU, with design and fabrication typically to EN 13445 or the AD 2000 rules. In-service inspection of equipment requiring monitoring falls under the Industrial Safety Regulation (Betriebssicherheitsverordnung), with periodic inspections by approved inspection bodies (zugelassene Überwachungsstellen). NDT findings feed those inspections, so test quality matters.

Radiography. Industrial radiography is regulated under the Radiation Protection Act (Strahlenschutzgesetz) and the Radiation Protection Ordinance (Strahlenschutzverordnung). Licences and supervision are handled by the radiation protection authorities of the federal states, and radiographers need the required radiation protection qualification (Fachkunde) in addition to their NDT certification. The simulator's RT scenarios involve no source and no radiation; they train technique choice and image interpretation only.

Codes in daily use. German technicians commonly work to EN ISO 17635 and the EN ISO 17640, 10675, 17636 and 13588 family for welds, to EN 10228 and EN 10160 for forgings and plate, and to customer and OEM specifications in automotive and aerospace. Offshore wind and oil and gas jobs bring their own project specifications, often referencing DNV or NORSOK standards.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Germany

Practical NDT adapts to three kinds of user, and German employers usually have all three on the same payroll. The direct answer: trainees get guided fundamentals, working technicians get rare-defect refreshers between jobs, and Level IIIs get a tool to build scenario sets and benchmark crews objectively.

Trainees and apprentices. Germany's dual vocational system produces materials testers (Werkstoffprüfer) and other technical apprentices who combine school with company training. The simulator gives them more repetitions than a lab can easily schedule: guided lessons, then jobs in the NDT Lab and Welding Workshop with instant scored feedback on setup, coverage and interpretation. Career changers and technicians moving into a new method get the same structured start.

Working technicians. A technician who spends months on automotive ET may suddenly be asked to help on a chemical plant shutdown; a shipyard UT operator may not have seen a particular crack morphology in a year. The simulator lets them rehearse rare and hard-to-source defects, such as stress corrosion cracking, lack of sidewall fusion, hydrogen cracking or exchanger tube pitting, between real assignments. That matters in Germany, where many inspection companies move staff between sectors.

Level IIIs and team leads. Level IIIs and NDT supervisors can build and assign scenario sets, compare results across crews or shifts, and find coverage gaps, for example a team that sizes well with PAUT but misinterprets TOFD lateral wave disturbances. It does not replace the Level III's own judgement, procedures or examinations; it gives them consistent, objective data on how their people perform on the same tasks.

Practice vs certification

Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification, it does not grant or renew any EN ISO 9712, DGZfP, EN 4179 or ASNT qualification, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that every scheme requires.

Under EN ISO 9712, a candidate needs documented training, industrial experience and a qualification examination with general, specific and practical parts, conducted by or under an accredited certification body. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer's written practice sets training hours, experience and examinations, including a practical examination on real specimens, and the employer certifies the person. A simulator can help build the familiarity and confidence that make those exams and the first weeks on a real site go better, but it cannot stand in for them.

Atlantis's own training product follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A only and is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility; Atlantis does not train toward DGZfP or other EN ISO 9712 certification. For German companies, ASNT-based training is mainly relevant where work is done to US codes, for US-owned plants, or for US OEM customers. See NDT training and SNT-TC-1A training and certification for details.

Shift patterns, shutdowns and skilled-worker shortages: why German teams use virtual NDT training

Germany has a shortage of skilled technical workers, and NDT is no exception. Employers recruit apprentices, retrain staff from other trades and bring in technicians from other EU countries, and all of them need practice time that real specimens and laboratory slots cannot always supply. A browser-based NDT simulator gives that practice wherever the person is.

Production plants run in shifts, and quality departments find it hard to pull people off the line for training. A virtual NDT training session can be done in a short block at the start or end of a shift. Chemical and refinery shutdowns compress a year's worth of inspection into a few intense weeks; teams that have rehearsed exchanger, alloy and corrosion work beforehand arrive ready. Offshore wind and shipyard projects run on tight schedules where a weld rejected late is expensive; PAUT and TOFD practice before the project starts helps operators get consistent quickly.

Specimens with real, well-characterised flaws are expensive to make and quickly become familiar. Once a team has seen a flawed block a few times, it stops being a test. The simulator's job library keeps the defects fresh, and Level IIIs can assign different sets to different people.

Finally, German companies take documentation seriously. Practice results in the simulator give supervisors a record of who has practised what, which can support internal competence discussions, though it is not a substitute for the qualification records your certification scheme or written practice requires.

Bring Practical NDT to your German team

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and the scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Getting started in Germany is straightforward because there is nothing to install on site and no physical centre to visit: technicians use a browser or app.

A typical rollout starts with a demo, then a short scoping conversation about your sector, methods and crew levels. For an automotive supplier that might mean ET, MT and PT jobs in the NDT Lab; for a chemical site, IRIS, PMI and corrosion work in the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank; for a shipyard or wind fabricator, PAUT, TOFD and RT in the Welding Workshop; for an MRO, the Aircraft Hangar. Level IIIs then assign scenario sets and track results.

The offer is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with a quote on request. Book a Practical NDT demo for your German team, read the Practical NDT overview, or write to info@atlantisndt.com. Companies that also need inspection-company software can look at Atlantis ERP in Germany.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in Germany?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so it works anywhere in Germany with an internet connection, from Hamburg to Munich. There is no physical Atlantis centre in Germany; access is online.

Does Practical NDT count toward DGZfP or EN ISO 9712 certification?

No. It is practice only. EN ISO 9712 certification requires training, experience and an examination, including a practical exam on real specimens, through an accredited certification body. The simulator helps you prepare.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation?

It can help you build familiarity, speed and confidence with setups, scanning and interpretation before a practical exam. It does not replace the exam or the hands-on hours your scheme or employer requires.

Is the simulator available in German?

Ask during the demo. Language options and customisation for German-speaking crews are discussed during scoping.

Which German industries is it most useful for?

Automotive and suppliers, rail, aerospace manufacturing and MRO, chemicals and refining, tank terminals and LNG import, shipbuilding, offshore wind fabrication, steel and power. Ask for a demo mapped to your sector.

Does it include radiography?

Yes, as technique and image interpretation practice with no radiation source. It does not satisfy any radiation protection qualification (Fachkunde) under German radiation protection law.

Is it a phased array or ultrasonic testing simulator?

Both, among others. It covers UT contact, PAUT and TOFD, plus IRIS for tubes and LRUT guided-wave screening, alongside surface, electromagnetic and PMI methods.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: guided fundamentals for apprentices and trainees, rare-defect refreshers for working technicians, and scenario building and crew benchmarking for Level IIIs and team leads.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Germany?

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A and is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. It suits German employers working to US codes or for US clients. It is not DGZfP or EN ISO 9712 training. See NDT training.

How do we start?

Request a demo. We will map the environments and methods to your German work and provide a quote on request.
