Halifax. Halifax is where most of Nova Scotia's NDT technicians work. Shipyard inspectors spend their days on hull, bulkhead and pressure-system welds, using PAUT and TOFD for sizing, RT for interpretation and MT and VT for surface checks. The Welding Workshop is the obvious environment. Aerospace inspectors maintaining helicopters and military aircraft work eddy current, penetrant and UT jobs, which map to the Aircraft Hangar. Terminal and tank work at the harbour fits the Storage Tank. See Practical NDT Halifax and NDT training in Halifax.

Dartmouth and Burnside. The fabrication and service shops on the Dartmouth side of the harbour build and repair structures, tanks, piping and marine components for the shipyard, the navy, the port and energy clients. Weld inspection and thickness surveys are routine, and many firms take on new trainees who need guided fundamentals.

Port Hawkesbury and Point Tupper. Terminal tanks, marine loading arms, transfer piping and mill equipment call for UT shell thickness, MFL floor screening and LRUT screening of long pipe runs, plus IRIS on exchanger and boiler tubes at the mill and power station.

Sydney and Cape Breton. Power stations need boiler-tube inspection, thickness surveys and weld inspection during outages. Harbour and marine work adds structural welds and corrosion, and local fabrication brings RT and MT.

Mainland wind and manufacturing. Wind tower flange and foundation welds, gearbox and blade-root components, tire plant pressure equipment and food plant boilers all need MT, UT, PT and VT. These are good starting points in the NDT Lab.

Environments and methods that match Nova Scotia work

Practical NDT has five environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. In Nova Scotia the weight falls on the Welding Workshop and Aircraft Hangar, with tank and plant work close behind.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints for RT interpretation, UT and PAUT sizing, TOFD, MT and VT against acceptance criteria. For shipyard and marine fabrication technicians this is the core of the library, and the closest match to day-to-day work on hull and structural welds.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection jobs suited to Halifax's helicopter and military aircraft maintenance and civil aviation. Eddy current, penetrant, UT and VT are practised here.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank, matching fuel terminals in Halifax Harbour and at the Strait of Canso.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). Weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant: UT and PAUT corrosion mapping, TOFD, IRIS on exchanger and boiler tubes, LRUT guided-wave screening, and PMI alloy verification. Power stations, the paper mill and terminals all have equipment that maps here.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks for fundamentals and exam rehearsal under any scheme.

Across the twelve methods, Nova Scotia leans on PAUT, TOFD, RT and MT for shipbuilding; ET and PT for aerospace; UT thickness and MFL for tanks; and IRIS and LRUT for power and terminal work.

Regulators and requirements Nova Scotia technicians meet

Short answer: NDT personnel certification is national, radiography sources are federally licensed, ships follow naval and classification requirements, offshore work falls under a joint federal-provincial regulator, and pressure equipment is regulated by the province. Practical NDT is practice for any of these and replaces none.

National NDT certification. Canada's national NDT personnel certification scheme is based on CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, and Nova Scotia employers commonly expect technicians to hold it. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published the standard, closed on 1 April 2026; Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body has said it continues to operate and the standard remains valid, but confirm the current certification body and arrangements before planning a route. Aerospace employers usually qualify personnel to NAS 410 or EN 4179, and some employers serving US clients use ASNT SNT-TC-1A. This is market context. Atlantis training aligns with ASNT SNT-TC-1A only and does not train toward, certify or administer other schemes.

Shipbuilding and marine. Naval construction follows the Department of National Defence's specifications and the applicable classification and welding standards, and commercial vessels follow Transport Canada marine safety rules and classification society requirements. Welding fabricators in Canada are commonly certified under CSA W47.1, with structural welds to CSA W59.

Radiation safety. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) licenses radioactive sources used in industrial radiography, and only a CNSC-certified exposure device operator, or a trainee under direct supervision, may operate a gamma exposure device. Shipyard radiography is a common reason for radiation safety controls. Practical NDT's RT jobs involve no radiation and do not count toward CNSC certification.

Pressure equipment. In Nova Scotia, boilers, pressure vessels, fittings and pressure piping are regulated under the Technical Safety Act and its Boiler and Pressure Equipment Regulations, administered by the Technical Safety Division of the Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration. Equipment needs a Canadian Registration Number before it is manufactured, installed or operated. CSA B51 and ASME codes apply.

Offshore. Offshore energy activity is regulated by the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Energy Regulator, which now covers offshore renewables as well as petroleum.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Nova Scotia

New trainees. Shipbuilding and its supply chain draw new people into welding inspection and NDT, and the constant challenge is giving them enough hands-on hours before they are inspecting production welds. Guided fundamentals in the NDT Lab and Welding Workshop let trainees repeat calibration, angle-beam setup, PAUT setup and RT interpretation as often as they need, with instant feedback. It is useful NDT practical exam preparation, provided everyone understands the real exam happens on real specimens.

Working technicians. Shipyard work is steady but repetitive, so technicians can go a long time without seeing certain defect types. Aerospace technicians face the same issue with rare cracks and corrosion. Industrial technicians in Cape Breton or at the Strait of Canso may move between power outages, tank work and mill inspection. Rare-defect refreshers between assignments keep them ready.

Level IIIs and team leads. Level IIIs can build and assign scenario sets, benchmark crews objectively and find coverage gaps. In a shipyard with large inspection teams, a consistent scenario set helps compare technicians fairly and target refreshers before a new block or module starts.

Practice vs certification

Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification. It does not grant a level under CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ASNT SNT-TC-1A, NAS 410, EN 4179 or an employer's written practice, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens these schemes require. It does not satisfy CNSC exposure device operator requirements, naval qualification requirements or Transport Canada requirements. It gives technicians more realistic repetition before exams and between jobs, alongside formal NDT training. The formal practical exam remains the step that counts.

Shipyards, hangars and offshore wind: why Nova Scotia crews use virtual NDT training

Nova Scotia's NDT demand is growing in a way that strains hands-on training capacity. Shipbuilding programmes run for many years and need a steady supply of qualified inspectors. Offshore and onshore wind will add tower, foundation and structural inspection. Aerospace maintenance needs technicians who can recognize rare defects reliably. And the province's employers are mostly small to medium firms that cannot keep a full specimen library for every method.

A browser-based phased array simulator and ultrasonic testing simulator let these employers give their people far more repetitions than a lab alone would allow. Trainees can practise at home or in the shop office. Experienced technicians can rehearse a TOFD setup or an eddy current inspection before a job. Level IIIs can measure readiness across a team. None of this replaces time on real welds, real aircraft or real specimens, but it makes that time count for more.

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Oman

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Oman is a country where inspection crews are spread across enormous distances: desert oilfields and gas plants in the interior, refineries at Muscat, Sohar and Duqm, an LNG plant on the coast near Sur, a heavy-industry port at Sohar, and ports and new industry at Duqm and Salalah. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician enters a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, takes a job, sets up the technique, scans or interprets, and is scored the moment the job is closed. For Omani employers whose people may be several hundred kilometres from the nearest lab, it is a way to keep skills current between rotations without moving specimens or people.

This is the Oman hub for Practical NDT. It describes where Omani NDT work happens, which simulator environments and methods fit it, the regulators and certification expectations technicians in Oman work under, and an honest account of what a simulator can and cannot do for certification. To see it applied to your own jobs, request a Practical NDT demo for Oman.

Oman's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Omani NDT work is driven by onshore oil and gas production, including thermal and other enhanced recovery projects, gas processing, three refineries, LNG export, petrochemicals and plastics, aluminium and steel, ports and ship repair, power and desalination, and a growing pipeline of hydrogen and new-energy projects. It stretches from the interior fields to Batinah, Muscat, Sur, Duqm and Dhofar.

The interior oil and gas fields. Petroleum Development Oman runs the large Block 6 concession, with production centres and stations across the north and south of the country, from Fahud, Yibal and Qarn Alam to Nimr and Marmul. Other operators run major gas developments such as Khazzan and Ghazeer in central Oman and thermal enhanced oil recovery projects that use steam injection. That mix creates a wide spread of inspection: corrosion surveys on flowlines and gathering systems, high-temperature steam piping, gas-plant pressure vessels and exchangers, produced-water systems, crude storage, and weld inspection on a constant flow of new facilities and pipelines. Crews work long rotations in camps far from any training centre.

Muscat. The capital area hosts the Mina Al Fahal refinery and crude export terminal, operator and contractor headquarters, engineering offices, inspection company bases, the Rusayl and other industrial estates, and the international airport with its aircraft maintenance activity. It is where many technicians are recruited, trained and mobilised from.

Sohar and Batinah. The Port of Sohar and its free zone form one of the Gulf's larger heavy-industry clusters: a refinery operated by OQ, an integrated plastics complex, an aluminium smelter, steel and iron plants, chemical and fertiliser plants, tank terminals and power and desalination plants. Process-plant turnarounds, fabrication and erection work, tank terminals and smelter maintenance all generate NDT within a short distance of each other.

Sur and Qalhat. The Oman LNG complex at Qalhat near Sur liquefies gas piped from the interior for export, alongside fertiliser production in the Sur industrial area. LNG trains mean cryogenic piping and tanks, rotating equipment and pressure-vessel inspection during planned shutdowns.

Duqm. The Special Economic Zone at Duqm has grown around a port, a dry dock and ship repair yard, the OQ8 refinery (a 230,000 barrel-a-day joint venture between OQ and Kuwait Petroleum International that reached full capacity in 2024), crude storage at nearby Ras Markaz, and a pipeline of new-energy and hydrogen projects. Duqm combines refinery turnaround work, ship repair weld inspection and construction-phase NDT.

Salalah and Dhofar. Salalah's container port and free zone host methanol, gas processing and other industrial plants, and the south of the country is a focus for future hydrogen and renewable projects. Process-plant integrity, storage and port infrastructure all need inspection.

Direct answer: Atlantis does not yet have Practical NDT pages for individual Omani cities, so this hub covers the main work centres directly. The table maps each area to the simulator environments and methods that match its everyday jobs, and the notes below link the Oman pages Atlantis already has for training, consulting and ERP.

Muscat. Inspection companies headquartered in Muscat can roll the simulator out to their whole workforce from one place, and refinery, terminal and aviation teams find IRIS, PMI, ET and PT practice directly relevant. See NDT training in Muscat and the Muscat NDT consulting page.

Sohar. The port's mix of refinery, plastics, smelter, steel and tank terminals makes it a strong fit for the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank, with TOFD and PAUT for vessel welds. See NDT training in Sohar, the Sohar consulting page and the Sohar ERP page.

Duqm. Ship repair and new construction need consistent weld inspectors, so the Welding Workshop is central, with the Oil & Gas Site for refinery turnarounds. See the Duqm consulting page and the Duqm NDT ERP page.

Salalah. Process plants and storage around the port suit the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank, with the NDT Lab for building fundamentals in newer staff. See the Salalah NDT ERP page.

Environments and methods that match Omani work

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. In Oman the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank cover upstream, gas, refining and LNG integrity; the Welding Workshop covers construction, pipelines and ship repair; the NDT Lab builds fundamentals; and the Aircraft Hangar covers aviation maintenance.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). Weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant: contact UT and PAUT corrosion mapping, TOFD on pressure welds, IRIS internal rotary UT on exchanger and boiler tubes, LRUT guided-wave screening on long pipe runs and PMI alloy verification. It mirrors work at PDO production stations, gas plants, the Muscat, Sohar and Duqm refineries and the LNG trains at Qalhat.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank. Oman has crude tanks at production centres and export terminals, product tanks at the refineries, large terminals at Sohar and crude storage near Duqm, so tank practice applies widely.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints for RT film and digital image interpretation, UT and PAUT detection and sizing, TOFD, MT and VT against acceptance criteria. It serves pipeline and station construction, fabrication yards in Muscat and Sohar, and ship repair at Duqm.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks for calibration, probe handling, sensitivity, scan coverage and indication recognition. It is the starting point for trainees, including the many young Omanis entering technical careers, and a quick check for experienced technicians before a practical exam.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection with eddy current, penetrant and UT, relevant to aircraft maintenance in Muscat and to technicians who cross between aviation and industrial work.

Across the twelve methods, surface methods (PT, MT, VT) cover structural and attachment welds; volumetric methods (UT contact, PAUT, TOFD, RT) carry weld quality and corrosion assessment; electromagnetic methods (ET, MFL) cover aviation parts, tubes and tank floors; and the specialist techniques (LRUT, IRIS, PMI) reflect the integrity programmes Omani operators run on pipelines, exchangers and alloy circuits.

Regulators and requirements Omani technicians meet

Short answer: in Oman, radioactive sources used in industrial radiography are licensed by the Environment Authority through its radiation protection function; personnel certification follows the operator's or contractor's requirements, where ASNT SNT-TC-1A based written practices and ISO 9712 certification are both widely used; and design and inspection follow operator specifications and ASME, API and AWS codes.

Radiation safety. The Environment Authority regulates radiation protection and the safety and security of radiation sources in Oman. Companies that import, store, transport or use radioactive sources for industrial radiography need licences and permits, and the authority also issues radiation protection supervisor licences. Customs, storage and transport permissions involve other agencies as well. Confirm current requirements directly with the Environment Authority before planning radiography work. The RT jobs in Practical NDT involve no radiation source and count toward no Omani radiation licence; they are technique and image interpretation practice only.

Personnel certification. Omani operators and their main contractors set NDT personnel requirements in contracts and vendor qualification documents. Technicians in Oman typically hold ASNT SNT-TC-1A based certifications under an employer's written practice, ISO 9712 certifications from recognised certification bodies, or both, and operators may add their own competence assessments for specific techniques. NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Poland

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Poland, in the middle of an energy and industrial build-out, has more NDT work arriving than it has experienced hands to do it. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician steps into a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, takes a job, sets up the technique, scans or interprets, and is scored the moment the job is closed. Polish NDT work stretches from the shipyards and refinery of the Tricity and the LNG terminal at Świnoujście, through the country's largest refinery and petrochemical complex at Płock, to the steel, power and chemical plants of Silesia and Lesser Poland, the aviation valley of Subcarpathia and the copper basin of Lower Silesia. On top of that, the first large Baltic offshore wind farms, a floating LNG terminal planned for the Gulf of Gdańsk and preparations for Poland's first nuclear power plant are adding demanding new work. The simulator gives trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs a way to build and keep skills between jobs without booking lab time or consuming specimens.

This is the Poland hub for Practical NDT. It covers where Polish NDT work happens by region, how the simulator's environments and methods fit it, the regulators and certification schemes Polish technicians deal with, and an honest account of what a simulator can and cannot do for certification. To see it with your own jobs in mind, request a Practical NDT demo for Poland.

Poland's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Polish NDT work is driven by shipbuilding and ship repair, refining and petrochemicals, gas and LNG infrastructure, coal and gas-fired power, steel and heavy fabrication, offshore wind, aerospace manufacturing and copper mining and smelting. It is concentrated on the Baltic coast, in central Poland around Płock, in the south's industrial belt and in the south-east's aviation cluster.

Pomerania and the Tricity. Gdańsk, Gdynia and Sopot form the Tricity, the heart of Polish maritime industry. Gdańsk has ship and steel-structure yards, one of the largest ship repair groups in the Baltic, the country's second refinery and a deep-water crude oil terminal; Gdynia has commercial, naval and specialised shipyards and a container port. Shipyard work means hull and block welds, offshore and naval structures and ship repair, which call for UT, PAUT, MT, VT and RT every day. The Tricity is also becoming a hub for offshore wind: installation and service bases, tower and foundation component fabrication and the supply chain behind the first Polish Baltic wind farms. Gaz-System is developing a floating storage and regasification terminal in the Gulf of Gdańsk, with its first unit expected toward the end of 2027 and a second planned later. To the west of the Tricity, at Lubiatowo-Kopalino, preparatory work is under way for Poland's first nuclear power plant.

West Pomerania. Świnoujście hosts Poland's first LNG terminal, which has been expanded with additional storage and capacity, and Szczecin and Police combine a port, ship repair, offshore wind component manufacturing and a large chemical and fertiliser complex. The Baltic Pipe gas pipeline from Norway comes ashore on this coast. Terminal and tank inspection, weld inspection on marine and offshore structures and process-plant work in chemicals all feature here.

Mazovia and central Poland. Płock on the Vistula is home to Poland's largest refinery and petrochemical complex, which has been expanding its petrochemical capacity, along with the crude and product pipelines and storage that feed it. Turnarounds at Płock are among the biggest inspection events in the country. Warsaw is the headquarters city for energy companies, engineering contractors and many inspection firms. Large coal and gas-fired power stations, including Bełchatów in the Łódź region and Kozienice in Mazovia, bring boiler, pressure-part and turbine inspection, and new gas-fired units have added fresh construction work.

Silesia and Lesser Poland. The south's industrial belt around Katowice, Gliwice, Dąbrowa Górnicza, Kraków and Opole combines coal mining, integrated and long-product steelmaking, power stations, boiler and pressure-equipment manufacturing, chemical plants and automotive manufacturing. Boiler tube surveys, weld inspection on pressure parts, structural MT on mining equipment, UT of forgings and castings and ET on automotive parts all happen within a short drive of each other.

Subcarpathia and the east. The area around Rzeszów is known as Aviation Valley, with aero-engine and component manufacturing and a dense supplier network. Mielec produces aircraft and helicopters, and Świdnik near Lublin has a long helicopter manufacturing tradition. Aerospace NDT here means penetrant and eddy current inspection, UT of metallic and composite parts and radiography of castings under strict aerospace procedures.

Lower Silesia and elsewhere. The Legnica-Głogów copper basin has mines, concentrators and smelters with heavy plant, tanks and structures. Wrocław and Poznań add automotive, rail vehicle and engineering manufacturing, Włocławek and Kędzierzyn-Koźle have large chemical plants, and Poland's gas transmission and crude pipeline networks run across the whole country.

Practical NDT by region in Poland

Atlantis does not yet have Practical NDT pages for individual Polish cities, so this hub covers the main centres directly. The table maps each to the environments and methods that match its everyday jobs.

Szczecin, Police, ŚwinoujścieLNG terminal, port, chemicals and fertilisers, offshore wind components, ship repairStorage Tank, Welding Workshop, Oil & Gas Site; MFL, UT, PAUT, PMI

Gdańsk and Gdynia. Shipyards and offshore fabricators need consistent weld inspectors, increasingly with PAUT and TOFD alongside UT, MT and RT. The Welding Workshop is the core for them. The Gdańsk refinery and crude terminal map to the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments, and offshore wind and the future FSRU will add both. Atlantis also has an ASNT NDT training page for Gdańsk for employers who work to US codes, plus radiographic testing in Gdańsk and Gdańsk ERP pages.

Szczecin, Police and Świnoujście. LNG and chemical storage generate tank shell surveys and floor screening, while offshore wind component manufacturing and ship repair need weld inspection. PMI and corrosion work feature in the chemical complex.

Płock. Refinery and petrochemical turnarounds require IRIS on exchanger bundles, PMI on alloy circuits, TOFD and PAUT on vessel welds, corrosion mapping on piping, LRUT on long pipe racks and MFL on tank floors, all present in the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments.

Warsaw and the Łódź region. Power station outages need boiler tube thickness surveys, IRIS on condenser and feedwater heater tubes, UT of pressure-part welds and MT and PT on turbine and structural components. New gas-fired units add construction-phase weld inspection.

Silesia and Lesser Poland. The south's mix of steel, boilers, mining and automotive makes the NDT Lab and Welding Workshop the most used environments, with ET for automotive parts and IRIS for power plant tubes.

Subcarpathia. Aero-engine and airframe production make the Aircraft Hangar the key environment, with eddy current, penetrant and UT jobs that match daily work in the aviation valley.

Lower Silesia. Copper smelters and concentrators run heavy plant, large tanks and structures in aggressive service, while automotive and rail manufacturing add component NDT.

Environments and methods that match Polish work

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. In Poland the Welding Workshop serves shipbuilding, offshore wind and heavy fabrication; the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank serve refining, petrochemicals, LNG and power; the Aircraft Hangar serves the aviation valley; and the NDT Lab builds fundamentals for everyone.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints for RT film and digital image interpretation, UT and PAUT detection and sizing, TOFD, MT and VT against acceptance criteria. This is the workhorse for Tricity and Szczecin shipyards, offshore wind tower and foundation fabricators, boiler and pressure equipment makers and steel structure fabricators.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). Weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant: contact UT and PAUT corrosion mapping, TOFD on pressure welds, IRIS internal rotary UT on exchanger and boiler tubes, LRUT guided-wave screening on long pipe runs and PMI alloy verification. It mirrors turnaround work at Płock and Gdańsk, chemical plants and power station outages.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank, for refinery and terminal tank farms, crude and product storage along the pipeline network, chemical storage and LNG-related tankage.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection with eddy current, penetrant and UT, matching Subcarpathia's aerospace manufacturing, helicopter production and airline and military maintenance.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks for calibration, probe handling, sensitivity, scan coverage and indication recognition. It suits new trainees, forging and casting inspectors and anyone preparing for a practical examination.

Across the twelve methods, surface methods (PT, MT, VT) cover finished parts and structural welds; volumetric methods (UT contact, PAUT, TOFD, RT) carry weld and corrosion assessment; electromagnetic methods (ET, MFL) serve aerospace, tubes and tank floors; and the specialist techniques (LRUT, IRIS, PMI) reflect refinery, chemical and power plant integrity programmes.

Regulators and requirements Polish technicians meet

Short answer: Polish NDT personnel are normally certified to PN-EN ISO 9712 through accredited certification bodies; pressure equipment is overseen by the Office of Technical Inspection (UDT); and industrial radiography falls under the Atomic Law, with the National Atomic Energy Agency (PAA) as regulator. Practical NDT is practice for any of these frameworks and replaces none of them.

Personnel certification. Poland applies PN-EN ISO 9712. Several accredited certification bodies operate. UDT-CERT, the personnel certification body of the Office of Technical Inspection, runs an NDT certification programme recognised under the ICNDT multilateral recognition agreement, and other accredited bodies certify NDT personnel as well. The Polish Society for Non-Destructive Testing and Technical Diagnostics represents the technical community. Employers working for US-owned operators, on ASME and API projects or in the US-designed nuclear programme may also keep ASNT SNT-TC-1A based written practices. That is market context only. Atlantis training aligns with ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, and Atlantis does not train toward, certify or administer PN-EN ISO 9712 or UDT-CERT certification. Practical NDT is practice for whichever scheme you work under.

Pressure equipment and technical inspection. New pressure equipment is placed on the market under the Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU. Equipment in use, including boilers, pressure vessels and many tanks and lifting devices, falls under the Act on Technical Inspection and is supervised by the Office of Technical Inspection (Urząd Dozoru Technicznego, UDT), with the Transport Technical Inspection (TDT) covering transport-related equipment. Ships and offshore structures are classed by classification societies such as the Polish Register of Shipping. Confirm current requirements with UDT or your inspection body.

Radiation safety. The National Atomic Energy Agency (Państwowa Agencja Atomistyki, PAA) regulates nuclear safety and radiation protection under the Atomic Law. Industrial radiography requires the appropriate permits and a radiation protection officer, and the PAA is also the nuclear safety regulator for the planned nuclear power plant. Practical NDT's RT jobs involve no radiation source and count toward no radiation protection requirement.

Codes and standards in daily use. Polish fabrication commonly references the PN-EN ISO weld testing and acceptance standards, EN 13445 and EN 13480, and ASME and API codes for export, refinery and US-designed projects; shipyards and offshore wind fabricators work to classification and project specifications. Mentioned as context only.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Poland

New trainees. Poland's build-out means many new entrants: welders and fitters moving into inspection, graduates of technical schools and engineering faculties, and technicians retraining from mining and other declining sectors. Rare-defect refreshers between assignments, on lack of fusion, laminations, hydrogen cracking, stress corrosion cracking and tube pitting, help them arrive ready.

What it adds is realistic repetition: more chances to set up, scan, interpret and get feedback than a lab timetable or specimen store allows. NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Qatar

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Qatar is a country where focused, repeatable practice pays off. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician opens a job in a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, sets up the technique, inspects, records what was found and gets a score as soon as the job closes. Qatar's inspection work is concentrated in a few very large places: the LNG trains, gas-to-liquids plants and expansion projects at Ras Laffan, the refinery, fertiliser, steel, aluminium and petrochemical plants at Mesaieed, the Dukhan onshore field on the west coast, offshore platforms and the Halul Island terminal, and Doha's port, airport and construction. Plant integrity standards are demanding, turnarounds are large, and the North Field expansion has added a wave of new construction that needs weld inspection on a huge scale.

This page is the Qatar hub for Practical NDT. It maps where the country's NDT work is, which simulator environments match each cluster, how practice relates to the ASNT SNT-TC-1A and ISO 9712 certification that Qatar employers ask for, which regulator controls radiography, and how to arrange a demo. The Doha Practical NDT page has more city detail.

Where Qatar's NDT work is

Short answer: Qatar's NDT demand is concentrated in four clusters: Ras Laffan Industrial City in the north, with LNG, gas-to-liquids, condensate refining and power; Mesaieed Industrial City in the south, with refining, fertilisers, steel, aluminium and petrochemicals; the oil fields at Dukhan and offshore; and Doha with its port, airport, utilities and construction. The same crews often work all four.

Ras Laffan. Ras Laffan Industrial City is the centre of Qatar's gas economy. Gas from the offshore North Field comes ashore here to LNG trains, gas-to-liquids plants, condensate refineries, helium and sulphur facilities, and large power and water plants, with a port for LNG carriers and a ship repair yard. The North Field expansion projects are adding new LNG trains and associated plant, bringing years of new construction alongside the maintenance of existing units. Cryogenic and high-pressure piping, large-diameter welds, heat exchangers, columns and storage tanks all need inspection, from construction weld inspection with radiography, PAUT and TOFD to in-service corrosion monitoring, IRIS on exchanger tubes and PMI on alloy materials.

Mesaieed. Mesaieed Industrial City south of Doha is Qatar's older industrial hub, with a refinery, petrochemical and fertiliser complexes, a steel plant, an aluminium smelter, natural gas liquids facilities and a port. Turnarounds here bring the classic refinery and petrochemical inspection mix: exchanger bundles, reactors, columns, alloy piping, boilers and tanks.

Dukhan and offshore. The Dukhan field on the west coast is Qatar's main onshore oil field, with gathering systems, degassing stations and pipelines. Offshore, oil fields and the North Field gas platforms are linked by subsea pipelines to Halul Island and to shore. Corrosion monitoring, pipeline inspection and structural work on platforms are routine, and offshore rotations limit time for practice.

Doha and Al Wakrah. Doha hosts most inspection companies, laboratories, EPC offices and owners' headquarters. Hamad Port, Hamad International Airport with its large airline engineering base, power and desalination plants, district cooling and continuous construction add structural, tank, piping and aviation inspection.

Practical NDT across Qatar's cities and industrial areas

Short answer: Doha already has its own Practical NDT page. The table below covers Doha and Qatar's other main inspection centres, with the simulator environments and methods that suit each. Every user can open every environment; the table shows where to start.

City or areaMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise

Ras LaffanLNG, gas-to-liquids, condensate refining, power and water, ship repairWelding Workshop, Oil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; PAUT, TOFD, RT, IRIS, PMI
MesaieedRefining, fertilisers, petrochemicals, steel, aluminiumOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; IRIS, ET, PMI, UT, MFL

Doha is where technicians are hired, inducted and certified before they go to Ras Laffan, Mesaieed or offshore. Trainees use guided lessons and the NDT Lab here, and aviation technicians at the airport use the Aircraft Hangar environment with its 54 jobs. Doha employers can also use ASNT training in Doha.

Ras Laffan has two distinct needs. Construction on the expansion projects needs weld inspection on large volumes of piping and structures, so PAUT, TOFD and RT in the Welding Workshop are the core practice. Operating plants need turnaround methods, IRIS, ET and PMI, plus tank surveys. See ASNT training in Ras Laffan and the Ras Laffan NDT ERP page.

Mesaieed turnarounds are dominated by exchangers, alloy piping, reactors and tanks. The Oil & Gas Site environment, with 73 jobs, covers IRIS, ET, PMI and corrosion mapping, and the Storage Tank environment covers shell surveys and MFL floor screening. See ASNT training in Mesaieed.

Dukhan crews work flowlines, gathering stations and pipelines spread over a long field. Corrosion mapping with UT and PAUT and LRUT screening of pipe runs are the main practice areas.

Offshore and Halul Island technicians have long rotations with no lab access. Practising corrosion mapping, LRUT and tank surveys between hitches keeps less-used methods current.

Environments and methods that match Qatar work

Short answer: the simulator has five environments and twelve methods. In Qatar, the Welding Workshop matches LNG expansion construction, the Oil & Gas Site matches operating LNG, GTL, refinery and fertiliser plants, the Storage Tank matches LNG, product and crude tank farms, the Aircraft Hangar matches airport MRO, and the NDT Lab supports trainees.

The five workplace environments are the NDT Lab (bench specimens and reference blocks, 52 jobs), the Welding Workshop (weld coupons and fabrication joints, 52 jobs), the Aircraft Hangar (airframe and component inspection, 54 jobs), the Oil & Gas Site (weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant, 73 jobs) and the Storage Tank (UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank). Thirty-three guided lessons cover the fundamentals. The twelve methods are PT, MT and VT; contact UT, PAUT, TOFD and RT; ET and MFL; and LRUT guided-wave screening, IRIS for heat-exchanger and boiler tubes, and PMI for alloy verification.

LNG work has a few features worth noting. Cryogenic piping and equipment use austenitic stainless steels and nickel alloys, where ultrasonic inspection of welds is harder because of coarse-grained, anisotropic weld metal, and where PMI and PT are routine. The simulator does not model a specific LNG train, but practising PAUT and TOFD on fabrication welds, PT on stainless joints and PMI on alloy lines builds the core habits that work needs. A company's Level III should then set the specific techniques and acceptance criteria its procedures require.

Radiography is still used heavily on construction, often around the clock in shifts, and it is tightly regulated. The simulator lets technicians practise RT technique choice and image interpretation without any source, so radiation licensing does not apply to simulator practice.

Certification, vendor requirements and regulators in Qatar

Short answer: Qatar employers commonly ask for NDT personnel certified to ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ISO 9712 schemes, and QatarEnergy and other owners add their own contractor requirements. Industrial radiography is licensed by the Radiation Protection Department of the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change. Simulator practice supports all of these but substitutes for none.

Personnel certification. Qatar's inspection workforce comes from many countries and serves owners, joint ventures, EPCs and licensors from around the world. ASNT SNT-TC-1A employer-based certification, ASNT central certification and ISO 9712 schemes such as PCN are all seen, sometimes on the same project. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only; Atlantis does not train for or issue ISO 9712, PCN or CSWIP certificates.

Owner and contractor requirements. QatarEnergy and its affiliates and joint ventures set engineering standards, contractor approval and quality requirements, including requirements for NDT procedures and personnel, and programmes such as Tawteen aim to localise more of the supply chain. Requirements are owner-specific and change, so work from the documents your contract names. Atlantis claims no approval or registration with QatarEnergy or any other owner, and Practical NDT is not an owner-approved qualification.

Radiation regulation. Qatar's Radiation Protection Law (Decree-Law No. 31 of 2002) and its executive regulations govern radiation sources. The Radiation Protection Department of the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change reviews licence applications, inspects facilities and enforces compliance, which covers industrial radiography and other source uses common in the oil and gas sector. Confirm current requirements with the department before any exposure work.

Codes and standards. Qatar's plants are built and maintained mainly to ASME, API, AWS and owner specifications, with ISO and EN standards in some areas and licensor requirements for specialised units. ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3, API 650 and 653, API 1104 and AWS D1.1 are everyday references. The simulator teaches method skills, not code acceptance criteria. Atlantis does not offer API 510, 570 or 653 or CWI training.

For procedures and written practices, see NDT consulting in Qatar; to track ASNT and ISO 9712 certificates side by side, see the Qatar NDT ERP page.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Qatar

Short answer: trainees use guided lessons and NDT Lab jobs to learn fundamentals; working technicians refresh turnaround methods and rare defects between projects; Level IIIs and team leads assign common scenario sets to compare large, mixed crews objectively before they reach Ras Laffan or Mesaieed.

New trainees. Qatar's industry is developing more local technical talent, and contractors take on new hires from many countries. The 33 guided lessons give each trainee a structured route through set-up, calibration, scanning and interpretation, and NDT Lab jobs can be repeated without using reference blocks or a senior technician's time.

Working technicians. A technician may spend months on construction radiography at Ras Laffan and then be assigned to IRIS or PMI on a Mesaieed turnaround. Rehearsing the next method in the simulator, at the accommodation or at home, is faster and cheaper than relearning it on a live unit.

Level IIIs and team leads. Large crews from different backgrounds are hard to compare from certificates alone. A common scenario set gives an objective view of who is ready for what, which methods need refreshers, and how the crew is improving. The results support conversations with clients but are not a certification.

Practice vs certification

Short answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is for practice and readiness. It is not a certification, does not issue certificates, is not an owner or operator approval and does not replace the practical examination on real specimens required by ASNT SNT-TC-1A written practices or ISO 9712 schemes.

Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer's written practice governs training, experience and the general, specific and practical examinations under Level III oversight, with the practical exam on real specimens. ISO 9712 bodies set their own training, experience and exams, and Qatar's owners add their own requirements on top. Simulator scores replace none of these. What the simulator offers is preparation: candidates arrive at real exams with established habits, and technicians arrive at real jobs having rehearsed the method. Treat scores as one piece of evidence alongside supervised work and certification.

Construction peaks, turnarounds and heat: why Qatar crews practise virtually

Short answer: Qatar's expansion projects create peaks in weld-inspection demand, turnarounds call for methods technicians rarely use, crews rotate offshore, and summer heat restricts outdoor work. A browser-based simulator lets people practise anywhere and lets employers check readiness before mobilising.

Construction peaks are the first reason. Expansion projects need many weld inspectors at once, and new hires must be brought to a consistent standard quickly. A common set of Welding Workshop jobs gives every new technician the same practice and the Level III the same yardstick. Turnarounds are the second: IRIS, ET and PMI are used heavily for a few weeks and then not at all, so a refresher before mobilising helps. Offshore rotations are the third, with long shifts and no lab access. Safety and climate are the fourth: practising radiography without a source and tank and plant surveys without heat, height or confined spaces takes risk out of learning, while real work keeps every usual control.

ASNT training, consulting and ERP for Qatar employers

Short answer: beyond the simulator, Atlantis offers Qatar companies ASNT SNT-TC-1A training, Level III consulting and an NDT ERP, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. There is no Atlantis training centre in Qatar.

Employers whose clients specify SNT-TC-1A can use ASNT SNT-TC-1A training in Qatar for Level I, II and III candidates, led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, with written practice development. Level III procedure, technique and audit support is available through Qatar consulting, and the Atlantis NDT ERP keeps ASNT and ISO 9712 certificates, calibration records, jobs and reports in one system. City pages cover training in Doha, Ras Laffan and Mesaieed. All are quoted on request.

Bring Practical NDT to your Qatar team

Short answer: request a demo through the contact form. Atlantis will show the environments that match your work, agree a pilot group and set up accounts. Nothing needs installing beyond a browser or app, and pricing is quote on request. Affordable, accessible and fully customizable.

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and the scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Inspection contractors, EPCs, fabricators, laboratories and training institutes in Qatar can use it as it stands or ask for scenario sets aligned to their procedures. A typical start is a short call about your work, a live demonstration of the matching environments, a pilot group and accounts for your technicians, with results visible to team leads.

  • Request a Practical NDT demo for your Qatar team
  • Ask for a Qatar quote for a crew, a project team or a whole company
  • Discuss a custom scenario set for LNG construction, turnaround or tank work

Read the Practical NDT overview for the full list of environments and methods.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator available in Qatar?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app and works anywhere in Qatar with an internet connection. There is no centre to visit; demos are arranged through the contact form.

Is Practical NDT approved by QatarEnergy?

No. It is a practice tool, not an owner-approved qualification. Owner requirements must be met through the certification and approval routes your contract specifies.

Does it replace the SNT-TC-1A or ISO 9712 practical exam?

No. Practical exams are taken on real specimens under the employer's written practice or the certification body's rules. The simulator helps you prepare.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation in Doha?

Yes. Repeating set-up, scanning, interpretation and sizing builds the habits a practical exam checks.

Is it relevant to LNG construction at Ras Laffan?

Yes for the methods involved. Welding Workshop jobs cover PAUT, TOFD, RT, PT and VT on fabrication welds, and PMI is in the Oil & Gas Site environment. It does not model a specific LNG train.

Does it include radiography, and does simulator practice need a licence?

RT is included for technique and interpretation. No radiation is used, so no licence is needed for practice. Real industrial radiography is licensed by the Radiation Protection Department of the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change.

Does it cover turnaround methods like IRIS and PMI?

Yes. The Oil & Gas Site environment, with 73 jobs, includes IRIS, ET, PMI, corrosion mapping and weld inspection.

Can it be used for tank inspection practice?

Yes. The Storage Tank environment covers UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank.

Can a Qatar contractor use it to assess new hires?

Yes. A Level III can assign one scenario set to all candidates and compare scores objectively, alongside certification and supervised work.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Qatar?

Yes, ASNT SNT-TC-1A training only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. See NDT training in Qatar.

How much does it cost and how do we start?

Pricing is quote on request, depending on users and any custom scenarios. Request a demo to see the environments that fit your work.

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Queensland

Queensland's inspection work runs from the LNG trains on Curtis Island to coal mines in the Bowen Basin, a refinery on the Brisbane River, metal refineries in Townsville and sugar mill boilers up and down the coast. Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is designed for a workforce like that: spread out, busy in bursts, and often a long drive from any practical NDT facility. It is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. Technicians work through realistic jobs in a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, set up and carry out the inspection, record their findings, and receive a score and feedback as soon as the job is done. Trainees use it to build fundamentals, working technicians use it to keep less-used methods fresh, and Level IIIs use it to assign and compare scenario sets across a crew.

This page is the Queensland hub. It covers where the state's NDT work is, how the simulator's environments and methods map onto Queensland industries, the regulators and standards Queensland technicians work under, and how to arrange a demo. It links the city pages Atlantis already has, including Brisbane and Gladstone.

Queensland's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Queensland's NDT demand is concentrated in six areas: Gladstone's LNG, alumina and port complex; the Surat and Bowen basin gas fields and their pipelines; the Bowen Basin coal mines served from Mackay; south-east Queensland around Brisbane, Ipswich and the Port of Brisbane; Townsville and the North West Minerals Province; and the sugar, power and port towns along the coast.

Gladstone and Curtis Island. Gladstone is Queensland's heavy industry capital. Three LNG export plants on Curtis Island (Queensland Curtis LNG, Australia Pacific LNG and Gladstone LNG) liquefy coal seam gas piped from inland fields. On the mainland, two alumina refineries, the Boyne Island aluminium smelter, a coal-fired power station, chemical plants and one of the state's largest bulk ports keep inspection companies working all year. Turnarounds at the LNG plants and the alumina refineries bring large crews into the city for short, intense periods. Corrosion mapping, weld inspection on piping and vessels, exchanger tube inspection, PMI and tank inspection are the core work.

The gas fields and pipelines. Coal seam gas production in the Surat Basin around Roma, Miles, Chinchilla and Dalby, and in parts of the Bowen Basin, feeds the Gladstone plants through long transmission pipelines and thousands of wells, gathering lines, compressor stations and water treatment plants. Pipeline construction and integrity work rely on radiography and automated or manual UT of girth welds, coating and corrosion assessment, and guided-wave screening at crossings and above-ground sections.

The Bowen Basin coal fields and Mackay. Queensland is a major exporter of metallurgical coal, and the Bowen Basin mines run fleets of draglines, shovels, haul trucks, wash plants, conveyors and train loaders. Mackay, with the Paget industrial area and the Hay Point and Dalrymple Bay coal terminals nearby, is the maintenance and engineering base for much of that activity. Fatigue cracking in booms, buckets, frames and structures makes MT, PT, UT and VT the everyday methods. Rail and port structures on the coal chains add more of the same.

Brisbane, Ipswich and the south-east. The Brisbane region has Lytton refinery near the river mouth, one of only two oil refineries still operating in Australia, alongside the Port of Brisbane's fuel, chemical and bulk terminals. Brisbane Airport hosts airline engineering and maintenance facilities, RAAF Base Amberley near Ipswich is the country's largest air force base, and the defence industry around Redbank and the south-west corridor builds and supports military vehicles. Fabrication shops, engineering consultancies and most inspection company head offices in the state sit in the south-east.

Townsville and the north-west. Townsville has a zinc refinery and a copper refinery, a busy port, and large army and air force bases. Inland, the North West Minerals Province around Mount Isa and Cloncurry mines and processes copper, zinc, lead and other minerals. Processing plants, tanks, acid plants, pressure vessels and long-distance rail and pipelines create steady inspection demand in a region where practical NDT facilities are far apart.

Sugar, power and the coast. Queensland's sugar mills, from the Burdekin to Bundaberg and the Mackay district, run large boilers during the crushing season and carry out their main maintenance and inspection in the slack season. Coal-fired power stations such as Callide, Stanwell, Tarong and Gladstone have boiler tubes, headers and steam piping that are inspected during outages. Ports at Gladstone, Hay Point, Abbot Point, Townsville and Brisbane add marine structures and loaders. Each of these creates seasonal peaks, which is exactly when skills that have been idle for months are suddenly needed.

Practical NDT by city in Queensland

Short answer: Brisbane has its own Practical NDT page, and Gladstone and Mackay have related Atlantis pages. The table maps these and the other main Queensland centres to the environments and methods that suit their industries.

GladstoneLNG, alumina, aluminium smelting, power, portOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; PAUT, IRIS, PMI, MFL, RT
MackayCoal mining maintenance, coal terminals, sugarWelding Workshop, NDT Lab; MT, PT, UT, VT
Surat Basin (Roma, Miles, Chinchilla)Coal seam gas wells, compressors, pipelinesOil & Gas Site, Welding Workshop; RT, UT, LRUT, PAUT

Brisbane combines refinery and terminal work at Lytton and the port with aviation and defence maintenance and a large fabrication base. That mix makes it the most varied city in the state for NDT. Refinery technicians practise IRIS, PMI and corrosion mapping in the Oil & Gas Site; aviation technicians use the Aircraft Hangar's 54 jobs for eddy current, penetrant and ultrasonic inspection of airframes and components; and fabrication shops use the Welding Workshop for weld inspection. Atlantis has ASNT SNT-TC-1A training for Brisbane employers, Level III consulting in Brisbane and a third-party inspection page for Brisbane.

Gladstone is LNG, alumina and power, and its technicians face some of the state's most demanding turnaround schedules. The Oil & Gas Site's 73 jobs cover weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant, and the Storage Tank environment covers shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening, both of which match the plants on Curtis Island and the refinery tank farms. Related pages: ASNT training in Gladstone, third-party inspection in Gladstone and NDT ERP for Gladstone inspection companies.

Mackay services the Bowen Basin. The work is crack detection on heavy mining equipment, structural welds on draglines and conveyors, shafts and pins, and the coal terminals' stackers, reclaimers and ship loaders. MT and PT on fabrication joints in the Welding Workshop and UT of components in the NDT Lab are the closest matches. See NDT ERP for Mackay.

The Surat Basin towns host the gas field contractors. Pipeline girth welds, compressor station piping, separators and water treatment plants need radiography, UT and corrosion assessment, and long buried or above-ground runs suit guided-wave screening. Technicians here often work long distances from any training room, which makes browser-based practice more valuable.

Townsville mixes metal refining with defence. Acid-resistant alloys, tanks and process piping in the refineries make PMI, UT thickness and tank floor screening routine, while military aviation at RAAF Base Townsville and the army's presence add aircraft and vehicle inspection.

Mount Isa and Cloncurry are remote mining and processing centres. Crusher and mill components, concentrator plant, tanks and structures need MT, UT and PT on a steady basis, and practice that does not require travelling to the coast is welcome.

Ipswich and Amberley are defined by RAAF Base Amberley, defence vehicle work and rail workshops. Eddy current and penetrant inspection of aircraft components, plus weld inspection on vehicle hulls and rail rolling stock, fit the Aircraft Hangar and Welding Workshop environments.

Bundaberg, the Burdekin and the other mill towns are about boilers. Sugar mill boilers and the coastal power stations have tubes, drums, headers and steam lines that are inspected in a compressed off-season window. IRIS, UT thickness and surface methods are the skills to sharpen before that window opens.

Environments and methods that match Queensland work

Short answer: use the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank for LNG, refining, alumina, metal refining and power; the Welding Workshop for mining equipment, pipelines, fabrication and defence vehicles; the Aircraft Hangar for airline and military aviation; and the NDT Lab for fundamentals and component work.

The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five workplace environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. The methods are grouped as surface methods (PT, MT, VT), volumetric methods (UT contact, PAUT, TOFD, RT), electromagnetic methods (ET, MFL), and three specialist techniques: LRUT guided-wave screening, IRIS internal rotary UT for heat-exchanger and boiler tubes, and PMI for alloy verification. Here is how they line up with Queensland work.

  • Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). Process plant practice covering weld inspection, corrosion mapping, tube inspection and screening. It suits the Curtis Island LNG plants, Lytton refinery, the alumina refineries and the zinc and copper refineries, gas field compressor stations and power station outage work.
  • Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank, matching LNG and condensate storage, port fuel terminals, alumina refinery process tanks and mining process tanks.
  • Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints for the fabrication shops of Brisbane, Gladstone, Mackay and Townsville, for mining equipment repair, for pipeline construction in the gas fields and for defence vehicle manufacturing.
  • Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection, relevant to airline maintenance at Brisbane, to regional aviation operators, and to military aviation at Amberley and Townsville.
  • NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks for trainees, TAFE programmes, calibration practice and component inspection of shafts, pins, castings and forgings.

A few methods matter particularly in Queensland. MT and PT are the daily bread of the coal industry, where crack detection on large welded structures under fatigue loading is constant. IRIS is essential for exchanger tubes at the LNG plants and refineries and for boiler tubes in sugar mills and power stations, and good IRIS interpretation depends on having seen many wall-loss patterns. RT and UT of girth welds dominate pipeline construction in the gas fields. PAUT is increasingly used for corrosion mapping and weld inspection in all of the process industries. Each of these can be practised repeatedly in the simulator with realistic defects and immediate scoring.

Regulators and requirements Queensland technicians meet

Short answer: AINDT certification, based on ISO 9712, is the local norm for Queensland NDT personnel, with ASNT SNT-TC-1A used by some employers on US-code work. Radiography is licensed under the Radiation Safety Act 1999 through Queensland Health. Workplace and plant safety sit with Workplace Health and Safety Queensland, and mines and petroleum and gas with Resources Safety and Health Queensland. Practical NDT is practice for any scheme.

Personnel certification. Most Queensland employers and asset owners specify AINDT certification for NDT technicians. Some operators, EPC contractors and suppliers working to US codes, or for US-owned assets and OEMs, also qualify staff under ASNT SNT-TC-1A through an employer written practice, and aviation NDT follows aerospace employer schemes. Atlantis's training covers ASNT SNT-TC-1A only; Atlantis does not provide AINDT or ISO 9712 training or exams. The simulator is useful whichever scheme a technician is working towards. See ASNT training in Australia for the SNT-TC-1A option.

Radiation safety. Industrial radiography in Queensland is regulated under the Radiation Safety Act 1999 (Qld), administered by Queensland Health. Using radioactive sources or X-ray equipment for radiography needs a use licence, possessing the sources needs a possession licence, and a radiation safety and protection plan applies to the practice. National codes and guidance from ARPANSA inform the state requirements. Confirm current licence conditions with Queensland Health before any real exposure. Simulator practice involves no radiation.

Plant, pressure equipment, mines and gas. General workplace safety, including the registration of certain plant designs and items such as boilers and pressure vessels, is administered by Workplace Health and Safety Queensland under the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld). Resources Safety and Health Queensland regulates coal mines, metalliferous mines and quarries, and petroleum and gas operations, including pipelines under the Petroleum and Gas (Production and Safety) Act 2004. Pressure equipment is commonly designed and inspected to AS 1210, AS 4041, AS 4037 and AS/NZS 3788, and pipelines to AS 2885.

Codes and standards. Queensland technicians work to Australian Standards and AS ISO adoptions for the individual NDT methods, to AS/NZS 1554 for structural welding, and on LNG, gas and some refinery and mining projects to ASME, API and AWS codes as well. The simulator does not certify compliance with any of them. It trains the habits they depend on: calibration, coverage, recording and sizing against acceptance criteria.

For written practices and procedures on Queensland sites that work to US codes, see NDT Level III consulting in Brisbane. To keep AINDT and ASNT certificates, equipment calibration and jobs in one system, see the Atlantis ERP for Brisbane inspection companies.

Turnarounds, crushing seasons and outages: the Queensland practice gap

Short answer: Queensland inspection demand peaks at predictable times, from LNG and refinery turnarounds to sugar mill slack seasons and power station outages, and technicians often go months between uses of a method. A browser-based simulator lets crews refresh the exact skills a campaign will need, before it starts.

Ask an inspection manager in Gladstone or Mackay when they are busiest and the answer is a calendar: the LNG train turnaround, the alumina refinery shutdown, the power station outage, the slack season at the mills, the dragline rebuild. Between those peaks, many technicians do a narrow range of routine work, and the methods they are not using fade. The first shift of a turnaround is the worst possible time to find that out.

Queensland's geography makes physical refresher training hard. The distance from Mount Isa to Brisbane is roughly the distance from Brisbane to Melbourne, and technicians in Roma, Emerald, Moranbah or Townsville cannot easily attend a practical session at a city laboratory. Reference specimens with realistic flaws are expensive and rarely spare. A simulator job on a laptop in a motel room or a mine camp is far easier to arrange.

The workforce itself is under pressure too. Queensland competes with Western Australia and with overseas projects for experienced NDT technicians, and the resources and energy sectors are changing as gas, coal and new energy projects ebb and flow. New entrants come from trades, apprenticeships, the defence force and interstate. Getting them useful quickly, and giving experienced people a structured way to show what good inspection looks like, are both things a shared scenario library supports.

Finally, simulator practice is safe. There is no confined space entry into a vessel, no work at height on a dragline boom, no heat stress in a Central Queensland summer and no radiation. Mistakes cost nothing except a lower score and a chance to try again.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Queensland

Short answer: trainees follow the 33 guided lessons from bench fundamentals to plant jobs, working technicians keep rarely used methods and defects fresh between campaigns, and Level IIIs and supervisors build and assign scenario sets to benchmark crews objectively.

Trainees. Queensland's new NDT technicians come from TAFE courses, fitter and boilermaker apprenticeships, mining maintenance roles, the defence force and other states. Theory courses and short supervised practicals are only the start; the logged industrial experience needed for certification takes months, and on a busy site a trainee may watch more than they inspect. The guided lessons start in the NDT Lab with calibration and simple flaws, then progress to weld coupons, process plant and tank jobs. A trainee arriving at Gladstone or Moranbah has already practised the basics many times over.

Working technicians. A Level II who spends most of the year on thickness surveys may be asked to run PAUT on a weld or IRIS on a bundle during the next turnaround. Rare-defect refreshers keep those skills ready: hydrogen-related cracking, lack of sidewall fusion, pitting on a single tube, a wrong alloy in a spool, a lamination near a nozzle, a fatigue crack at a weld toe on a mining structure.

Level IIIs and team leads. A Level III responsible for a Queensland crew can assign the job mix that a coming campaign demands, compare results objectively across employees and contractors, and spot coverage gaps before mobilisation. This is especially useful when bringing interstate or overseas technicians into a Queensland team, or when combining crews from several contractors on a shutdown. The results are an extra piece of evidence for supervisors, not a replacement for the employer's own practical assessments.

Practice vs certification

Short answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is for practice and readiness. It is not a certification under AINDT, ISO 9712 or ASNT SNT-TC-1A and it does not replace any practical examination on real specimens.

Every NDT certification route used in Queensland requires training, documented industrial experience and a practical examination on real specimens. Under AINDT certification the examination follows the scheme's own rules; under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer administers it according to its written practice under a Level III. No scheme counts simulator time as industrial experience unless an employer's own procedures explicitly say so, and Atlantis makes no such claim.

What practice does is reduce the gap between knowing and doing. A candidate who has set up a scan plan many times, interpreted a range of radiographs and sized indications against acceptance criteria goes into the practical with more confidence and fewer surprises. A supervisor who has seen a technician's simulator results over several weeks has more to go on when deciding who is ready for which job. For formal training, see Atlantis NDT training, which is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility.

Bring Practical NDT to your Queensland team

Short answer: book a demo, tell Atlantis which Queensland sectors and methods your team works in, and agree a pilot group. Pricing is quote on request.

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience. Its scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. The product is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, so an inspection company in Gladstone, a mining maintenance contractor in Mackay, a training provider in Brisbane or an asset owner's integrity team can use it as it stands or ask for scenario sets aligned to their procedures and job mix. There is no Queensland centre to visit; access is online.

Getting started takes a short call about your work, whether that is LNG turnarounds, coal mining equipment, pipeline construction, refinery and terminal integrity, aviation or sugar mill boilers. Atlantis then demonstrates the matching environments live, agrees a pilot group, and sets up accounts so technicians can practise in a browser or app wherever they are. Supervisors can see progress and results. Demos are scheduled to suit Brisbane time.

  • Book a Practical NDT demo for your Queensland team
  • Get a Queensland quote for a turnaround crew, a trainee intake or a whole company
  • Ask about a custom scenario set for LNG, coal mining, pipelines or boilers

See the Practical NDT overview for the full list of environments and methods.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator available in Queensland?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so technicians can use it in Brisbane, Gladstone, Mackay, Townsville, a gas field camp or at home. There is no physical centre; demos are arranged through the contact form.

Does simulator practice count towards AINDT certification?

No. AINDT certification needs training, documented industrial experience and examinations under the scheme's rules, including a practical on real specimens. The simulator can help a candidate prepare, but Atlantis does not offer AINDT or ISO 9712 training or examinations.

Can it help me prepare for an NDT practical exam?

Yes, as preparation. Repeated set-up, scanning, interpretation and sizing jobs build the habits a practical exam tests. The exam itself is still taken on real specimens.

Is it relevant to Gladstone LNG and alumina turnarounds?

Yes. The Oil & Gas Site covers corrosion mapping, weld inspection, IRIS on exchanger tubes, PMI and LRUT screening, and the Storage Tank environment covers shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening, which together match most turnaround inspection scopes.

Does it help with coal mining equipment inspection?

For the core methods, yes. MT, PT, UT and VT practice on weld joints and components maps well to crack detection on draglines, shovels, conveyors and terminal machinery, although site procedures and acceptance criteria still apply.

Does it include a phased array and ultrasonic testing simulator?

Yes. UT contact, PAUT and TOFD are all included, across the NDT Lab, Welding Workshop and Oil & Gas Site, with set-up, scanning and sizing on realistic welds and corrosion.

Can it be used for sugar mill and power station boiler work?

Yes as practice. IRIS and UT thickness on tubes, plus surface methods on headers and welds, are covered in the Oil & Gas Site and NDT Lab. It is a useful refresher before the slack-season or outage window.

Does it include radiography?

Yes, RT is one of the twelve methods, focused on technique and film or digital image interpretation. There is no radiation, so simulator use needs no licence under the Radiation Safety Act 1999; real exposures still do.

Can a supervisor benchmark a crew before a shutdown?

Yes. A Level III or supervisor can assign the same scenario set to every technician and contractor and compare results objectively, which helps allocate people to jobs.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Queensland?

Yes, ASNT SNT-TC-1A training only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility for employers whose projects or clients require SNT-TC-1A personnel. See NDT training in Brisbane.

Who is it for?

New trainees on guided lessons, working technicians refreshing less-used methods and rare defects, and Level IIIs and supervisors building scenario sets for their teams.

How do we get started?

Request a demo and Atlantis will show the environments that fit your work and agree a pilot. Pricing is quote on request.
