h1: NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Saskatchewan
contentHtml:
HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Saskatchewan

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Saskatchewan is a province where that kind of practice pays off. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. Technicians walk into a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, pick up a job, set up the technique, scan or interpret, and get a score the moment the job is closed. Saskatchewan's inspection work is spread across a very large and thinly populated map: heavy oil around Lloydminster, light oil in the southeast, a major refinery and a steel pipe mill in Regina, potash mines and mills across the centre and east of the province, uranium mines and mills in the far north, coal and gas-fired power plants, and thousands of kilometres of crude oil and gas pipelines. Technicians often drive hours between jobs and may go weeks without touching a particular method. Practical NDT gives them a way to keep their hands and eyes sharp between assignments, at any level from first-week trainee to working Level III, without booking lab time or using up specimens.

This page is the Saskatchewan hub for Practical NDT. It covers where Saskatchewan's NDT work actually happens, how the simulator's environments and methods map onto that work, the regulators and codes Saskatchewan technicians deal with, and an honest explanation of what a simulator can and cannot do for certification. If you want to see it with your own crew's jobs in mind, request a Practical NDT demo for Saskatchewan.

Saskatchewan's NDT workforce and where the work is

Saskatchewan's NDT work is driven by four resource systems: oil and gas, potash, uranium and power. Each sits in a different part of the province and asks for a different mix of methods, so a technician's week can look very different in Lloydminster than it does in Esterhazy or at a northern mine site.

Regina and the south. Regina is the provincial capital and the province's main heavy-industry centre. The Co-op Refinery Complex on the city's north side is one of the larger refineries in Western Canada, with the usual refinery inventory of pressure vessels, heat exchangers, fired heaters, alloy piping and tankage, and periodic turnarounds that bring in large inspection crews. Regina is also home to a steel mill and pipe-making operation that produces line pipe and tubular products, which means weld and plate inspection in a manufacturing setting. Fabrication shops, agricultural equipment manufacturers and pipeline service companies round out the city's industrial base. Further south, Moose Jaw hosts a military flying training base and a mix of processing and manufacturing.

The southeast oil patch. Around Estevan, Weyburn and Carlyle, the Saskatchewan portion of the Bakken and other light-oil plays support wells, batteries, gas plants, gathering lines and the service companies that build and maintain them. The Weyburn area has long been known for enhanced oil recovery using carbon dioxide, and the coal-fired Boundary Dam station near Estevan includes one of the world's first commercial-scale carbon capture units. That combination produces steady demand for weld inspection on new facilities and pipelines, corrosion monitoring on production equipment, and boiler and pressure-part inspection at power plants.

Lloydminster and the west. Lloydminster straddles the Alberta border and is the centre of Canada's conventional heavy oil industry. Thermal heavy-oil projects, a heavy oil upgrader on the Saskatchewan side, and an asphalt refinery on the Alberta side generate high-temperature service, erosion, sand-laden production and steam-generation equipment, along with dense field pipeline networks. Thickness surveys, corrosion mapping and tank inspection are everyday work here.

The potash belt. Saskatchewan holds a very large share of the world's known potash reserves. Conventional underground mines and solution mines stretch from the Esterhazy and Rocanville area in the east, through Lanigan, Allan, Cory and Vanscoy around Saskatoon, to Belle Plaine west of Regina, and new capacity has been under construction near Jansen. Potash mills are hard on equipment: brine, chlorides and abrasive slurries attack tanks, piping, crystallizers, evaporators and structural steel. Hoist and headframe structures, dryers and steam systems all need regular inspection.

Saskatoon. Saskatoon is the headquarters city for much of the province's mining industry and an engineering, manufacturing and research centre, home to the Canadian Light Source synchrotron at the University of Saskatchewan. Many inspection, engineering and fabrication firms serving potash and uranium operate from here.

The north. The Athabasca Basin in northern Saskatchewan hosts the world's highest-grade uranium deposits, with mines and mills reached by long roads or fly-in rotations. Pulp, forestry and the Prince Albert area add mill work further south. Remote rotations make it hard to keep any kind of practice routine, which is exactly where a browser-based simulator fits.

Practical NDT by city in Saskatchewan

Saskatchewan's two largest cities each have their own Practical NDT page with more local detail. The table below links them and adds the other major work centres, mapped to the environments and methods that fit.

City or areaMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise
ReginaRefining, steel and line pipe manufacturing, fabrication, pipeline servicesOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank, Welding Workshop; IRIS, PMI, UT, PAUT, RT
SaskatoonPotash and uranium headquarters, engineering, manufacturing, researchNDT Lab, Welding Workshop, Storage Tank; UT, MT, PT, MFL
LloydminsterHeavy oil, thermal projects, upgrading, field pipelinesOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; UT, PAUT, LRUT, MFL
Estevan and the southeastLight oil, gas processing, coal power with carbon captureOil & Gas Site, Welding Workshop; RT, UT, TOFD, MT
Potash belt (Esterhazy to Belle Plaine)Underground and solution potash mining and millingStorage Tank, NDT Lab; UT thickness, MT, PT, VT

Regina. Regina's inspection work is dominated by the refinery and by manufacturing. Refinery turnarounds call for exchanger tube inspection, alloy verification on piping circuits, thickness surveys and tank work, so IRIS, PMI and the Storage Tank environment are the obvious starting points for plant crews. The pipe and steel mill side of the city leans toward automated and manual UT of welds and plate, along with RT and MT on fabricated products. Regina technicians who also work pipeline construction can use the Welding Workshop to keep girth-weld RT interpretation and PAUT sizing current. See the Practical NDT Regina page for more.

Saskatoon. Saskatoon is where many potash and uranium engineering and maintenance decisions are made, and where a large share of the province's fabrication and inspection firms are based. Work is varied: tank and vessel thickness surveys in corrosive brine service, MT and PT on mill structures and rotating-equipment components, weld inspection on new fabrication, and MFL floor screening on large process tanks. The NDT Lab is useful for new hires coming out of local trades and technical programmes. See the Practical NDT Saskatoon page.

Lloydminster. Heavy oil production brings sand, heat and steam. Erosion in production piping, corrosion under insulation and thinning in steam lines make UT and PAUT corrosion mapping routine, while LRUT guided-wave screening is useful on long runs of above-ground and road-crossing pipe. Tank farms at batteries and terminals add MFL floor screening. Lloydminster technicians often split time between the two provinces, so a portable practice tool is handy.

Estevan and the southeast. New facility construction and pipeline tie-ins keep RT and UT of welds in steady demand, and gas plants add TOFD and PAUT work on pressure welds. Power stations in the area bring boiler-tube and pressure-part inspection, where thickness surveys and surface methods matter. The Welding Workshop and Oil & Gas Site together cover most of what a southeast crew sees in a year.

The potash belt. Mill technicians and contract inspectors work in highly corrosive conditions, often on large fibreglass, rubber-lined and steel tanks, piping and structures. Steel tank shell thickness surveys and floor screening map well to the Storage Tank environment, while MT, PT and VT on structural welds, hoist components and supports map to the NDT Lab and Welding Workshop.

Environments and methods that match Saskatchewan work

Practical NDT has five workplace environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. In Saskatchewan the mix leans heavily toward process-plant, tank and weld work, with a smaller aerospace and manufacturing share.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). This is the environment closest to a Saskatchewan refinery, upgrader, gas plant or battery. It covers weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant: contact UT and PAUT corrosion mapping on piping and vessels, TOFD on pressure welds, IRIS internal rotary UT on exchanger and boiler tubes, LRUT guided-wave screening on long pipe runs, and PMI alloy verification on alloy circuits. For Regina turnaround crews and Lloydminster heavy-oil technicians it is the core of the library.

Storage Tank. Saskatchewan's oil batteries, terminals, refinery tank farms and potash mills all run large tank inventories. The Storage Tank environment covers UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank, the same work that fills many technicians' summers.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints support RT film and digital image interpretation, UT and PAUT flaw sizing, TOFD, MT and VT against acceptance criteria. This fits the fabrication shops of Regina and Saskatoon, pipe and steel manufacturing, and the pipeline and facility construction season across the south.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks build the fundamentals: calibration, probe handling, sensitivity setting, scan coverage and indication recognition. New trainees and anyone preparing for a practical examination under any scheme will spend time here.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Saskatchewan's aviation sector is smaller than its resource sector, but it is real: northern air services that support mines and remote communities, agricultural aviation, air ambulance, maintenance shops in Regina and Saskatoon, and military flying training at Moose Jaw. Eddy current, penetrant and UT on airframe and component jobs are the relevant skills.

Across the twelve methods, surface methods (PT, MT, VT) cover most mill and structural work; volumetric methods (UT contact, PAUT, TOFD, RT) carry weld and corrosion assessment; electromagnetic methods (ET, MFL) serve aviation and tank floors; and the specialist techniques (LRUT, IRIS, PMI) match what refinery, upgrader and plant integrity programmes ask for.

Regulators and requirements Saskatchewan technicians meet

Short answer: NDT personnel certification in Canada is national, radiation sources are federally licensed, and pressure equipment and provincial pipelines are regulated by the province. Practical NDT is a practice tool that is useful under any of these schemes, and it does not replace any of them.

National NDT certification. The national NDT personnel certification scheme in Canada is based on CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, and many Saskatchewan employers expect technicians to hold Level 1, 2 or 3 certification under it. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published the standard, closed on 1 April 2026; Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body has said it continues to operate and the standard remains valid, but confirm the current certification body and arrangements before planning a route. Some employers, particularly US-owned operators and contractors working to US codes, also maintain written practices based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. This is market context. Atlantis training aligns with ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, and Atlantis does not train toward, certify or administer the CGSB/ISO 9712 scheme.

Radiation safety. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) licenses radioactive sources used for industrial radiography, and only a CNSC-certified exposure device operator, or a trainee under direct supervision, may operate a gamma exposure device. The CNSC also regulates uranium mining and milling, which is relevant for technicians who work at northern sites. X-ray equipment falls under provincial radiation health and safety legislation. Practical NDT's RT jobs involve no radiation source and do not count toward exposure device operator certification.

Pressure equipment. The Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan (TSASK) administers the province's boiler and pressure vessel safety programme, including design registration, inspection and related requirements. Codes commonly met in Saskatchewan plants include CSA B51, ASME Section V and Section VIII, ASME B31.1 and B31.3, and API 510, 570 and 653 for in-service inspection.

Pipelines. Provincially regulated pipelines are licensed by the Saskatchewan Ministry of Energy and Resources under The Pipelines Act, 1998, with Directive PNG034, the Saskatchewan Pipelines Code, and CSA Z662 setting technical requirements, including for weld examination. Interprovincial and international lines that cross the province fall under the Canada Energy Regulator. Structural and fabrication work commonly references CSA W59 and CSA W47.1, again as context rather than anything Atlantis certifies.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Saskatchewan

Practical NDT adapts to three kinds of user, and each has a distinct problem in Saskatchewan.

New trainees. Saskatchewan's trainees often come into NDT from welding, millwright, power engineering or general trades backgrounds, and the hardest thing to get is enough hands-on time before the first field job. Hours on real equipment are limited by specimen availability, supervisor time and, for much of the year, cold weather. Guided fundamentals in the NDT Lab let a trainee repeat calibration, angle-beam setup, scan coverage and indication interpretation as often as they need, with instant feedback, so their first time on a real block is not their first attempt. It is also useful NDT practical exam preparation, as long as everyone understands the real exam still has to be done on real specimens.

Working technicians. The province's work is seasonal and lumpy. Pipeline and facility construction concentrates in the warmer months, refinery and mill turnarounds come in blocks, and rotational schedules at northern mines leave long stretches away from some methods. A technician who spent the winter on tank floors may be asked to run IRIS on an exchanger bundle in the spring. Rare-defect refreshers between assignments, on things like stress corrosion cracking, erosion patterns, lack of fusion and tube pitting, help them arrive ready instead of relearning on the client's equipment.

Level IIIs and team leads. Level IIIs in Regina and Saskatoon can build and assign scenario sets, benchmark crews objectively and find coverage gaps before a campaign. When a turnaround brings in contract technicians from Alberta, Manitoba and beyond, a consistent scenario set gives a like-for-like comparison of who is ready for which method. It also helps a Level III check whether a new procedure is clear before it goes to the field.

Practice vs certification

Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification, it does not grant a level under CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ASNT SNT-TC-1A or any employer's written practice, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that those schemes require. It does not satisfy CNSC exposure device operator requirements. What it adds is realistic repetition: more chances to set up, scan, interpret and get feedback than a lab schedule or a specimen cupboard allows. It complements formal NDT training and on-the-job experience. The formal practical exam is still the step that counts.

Remote work, winters and distance: why a simulator suits Saskatchewan

Saskatchewan's geography is the strongest argument for virtual NDT training in the province. Work sites are spread across hundreds of kilometres of prairie, parkland and boreal forest, and many technicians live in one town and work in several others. Northern uranium operations rely on fly-in rotations, potash mills are scattered across the centre and east, and oil and gas work stretches from the Alberta border to Manitoba.

That spread makes it hard to keep a practice routine. A shop that wants its people to rehearse a PAUT setup or an RT interpretation before a job has to find a free lab, a qualified supervisor and the right specimens, all at the same time. Winters limit outdoor practice for months. And many smaller employers simply do not own the reference blocks and flawed specimens needed to cover rare defects.

A browser-based ultrasonic testing simulator and phased array simulator remove most of that friction. Technicians can practise at home, in a camp room or in the shop office between jobs, subject to connectivity at the site. Supervisors can see scores rather than relying on self-reported confidence. Scenario sets built by a Level III can be pushed to a whole crew before a turnaround starts, so the first morning on site is not spent discovering who is rusty. None of this replaces time on real equipment, but it makes the real time more productive.

Bring Practical NDT to your Saskatchewan team

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience. The scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who also leads Atlantis training. Rollout is simple. It starts with a short demo, then a conversation about your work, whether that is a Regina refinery turnaround crew, a Saskatoon fabrication and inspection firm, a potash mill maintenance group, a Lloydminster heavy-oil contractor or a southeast pipeline crew. Together we choose the environments and methods that match your jobs, and technicians get access by browser or app wherever they are.

Pricing is quote on request, and the offer is built to be affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Book a Saskatchewan Practical NDT demo, read the Practical NDT overview, or write to info@atlantisndt.com.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in Saskatchewan?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so it works anywhere in Saskatchewan with a connection, from Regina and Saskatoon to camp rooms at remote sites. There is no physical centre to visit.

Does Practical NDT count toward CGSB (ISO 9712) certification?

No. It is practice only. Certification under CAN/CGSB-48.9712 requires its own training, experience and examinations, including a practical exam on real specimens. Confirm the current certification body before you plan. The simulator helps you prepare.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation?

It can help you build familiarity, speed and confidence with setups, scanning and interpretation before a practical exam. It does not replace the exam or the hands-on hours your scheme or employer requires.

Which Saskatchewan industries is it most useful for?

Refining in Regina, heavy oil around Lloydminster, light oil and gas processing in the southeast, potash milling, power generation, pipeline construction, fabrication and steel manufacturing, and aviation maintenance. Ask for a demo mapped to your sector.

Does it include radiography?

Yes, as technique and image interpretation practice with no radiation source. It does not count toward CNSC exposure device operator certification.

Is it useful for potash mill inspection?

Yes for the underlying skills: UT thickness surveys on tanks and piping, MFL floor screening, and MT, PT and VT on structural welds and components. Mill-specific procedures still come from your employer and Level III.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: guided fundamentals for new trainees, rare-defect refreshers for working technicians, and scenario building and crew benchmarking for Level IIIs and team leads.

Can technicians on northern rotation use it?

Yes, during time off or downtime, subject to the site's connectivity and rules. That is one of the main reasons Saskatchewan employers look at it.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Saskatchewan?

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A and is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. It suits employers working to US codes or for US clients. See NDT training.

How do we start?

Request a demo. We will map the environments and methods to your Saskatchewan work and provide a quote on request.

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Saudi Arabia

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Saudi Arabia is one of the largest inspection markets that tool can serve. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician opens a job in a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, sets up the technique, inspects, records the finding and gets a score as soon as the job is closed. The Kingdom's inspection work is enormous and concentrated: the oil and gas fields, gas plants, refineries and export terminals of the Eastern Province, the petrochemical complexes of Jubail and Yanbu, the Red Sea refining and power coast from Rabigh to Jazan, a fast-growing manufacturing and aerospace base around Riyadh and Jeddah, and giant new construction and shipbuilding projects. Turnarounds are large, crews are multinational and the pressure to show competence before mobilising is high.

This page is the Saudi Arabia hub for Practical NDT. It maps where the Kingdom's NDT work is, which simulator environments match each region, how practice sits alongside the ASNT SNT-TC-1A and ISO 9712 certification that Saudi employers ask for, which regulators matter, and how to arrange a demo. City pages for Dammam and Riyadh carry more local detail.

Where Saudi Arabia's NDT work is, region by region

Short answer: Saudi NDT demand clusters in four areas: the Eastern Province oil, gas and terminal belt from Dammam and Dhahran to Ras Tanura, Abqaiq and Jubail; the Red Sea industrial coast of Yanbu, Rabigh, Jeddah and Jazan; Riyadh and the central region's manufacturing, power and defence industries; and the new giga-projects and maritime yards. Each needs a different mix of methods.

The Eastern Province. This is the heart of Saudi inspection work. Onshore and offshore fields, gas-oil separation plants, the Abqaiq processing facilities, large gas plants, the Ras Tanura refinery and export terminal, and thousands of kilometres of flowlines and trunk pipelines create continuous demand for corrosion monitoring, weld inspection on new construction and modifications, and shutdown inspection of pressure equipment. Newer unconventional gas developments add new plant and pipelines. Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran are where most inspection companies, laboratories and contractor offices are based, and where technicians arrive before being sent to site.

Jubail. Jubail Industrial City, administered by the Royal Commission for Jubail and Yanbu, is one of the largest petrochemical and industrial complexes in the world, with refineries, petrochemical and fertiliser plants, steel and metals plants, desalination and power. Plant turnarounds there are major events that bring in large inspection crews for heat exchangers, columns, reactors, piping and tanks. Nearby, the Ras Al-Khair area hosts mineral processing, a large desalination and power plant and a major new maritime yard for ship and offshore rig building and repair.

Yanbu and the Red Sea coast. Yanbu Industrial City, also under the Royal Commission, combines export refineries, petrochemicals and the western terminus of the cross-country pipelines. Further south, Rabigh has an integrated refining and petrochemical complex, Jeddah has a large port, fuel terminals, power and desalination plants and aircraft maintenance at King Abdulaziz International Airport, and Jazan has a newer refinery and industrial city. Coastal heat and humidity make external corrosion and corrosion under insulation recurring themes.

Riyadh and the central region. Riyadh has a refinery, power plants, a dense fabrication and manufacturing base, and a growing defence and aerospace manufacturing sector supported by national industrial programmes. Many owners, engineering firms and EPC contractors have headquarters or project offices there.

Giga-projects and new industry. Large construction programmes on the Red Sea coast and in the north-west, new industrial cities, renewable energy projects and expanding water infrastructure add structural steel, pipeline and fabrication inspection across the country. Localisation programmes such as Aramco's IKTVA (In-Kingdom Total Value Add) have also brought more manufacturing of valves, pipe, vessels and other equipment into the Kingdom, each with its own inspection needs.

Practical NDT across Saudi cities and industrial areas

Short answer: Dammam and Riyadh already have their own Practical NDT pages. The table below covers those and the Kingdom's other main inspection centres, with the environments and methods that best match local work. Every user can open every environment; the table shows where to start.

Dammam, together with Al Khobar and Dhahran, is the Kingdom's inspection capital. Technicians based here rotate through field facilities, gas plants and pipeline projects, so the Oil & Gas Site environment, with 73 jobs covering weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice, is the core of their practice, and the Storage Tank environment covers terminal and tank-farm surveys. Employers here can also use ASNT training for Dammam employers, Al Khobar training and Level III consulting in Dammam.

Riyadh combines refinery and power plant maintenance with a fast-growing manufacturing base. Fabricators of vessels, structures and pipe spools need PAUT, TOFD and RT weld inspection in the Welding Workshop, while defence and aerospace manufacturers need ET and PT in the Aircraft Hangar and NDT Lab. See also ASNT training in Riyadh and consulting in Riyadh.

Jubail and Ras Al-Khair turnarounds are dominated by exchanger bundles, columns, reactors and alloy piping. IRIS on exchanger tubes and PMI on alloy lines are where many technicians feel least practised, and the Oil & Gas Site environment covers both. New fabrication and shipbuilding add PAUT and TOFD weld inspection. See ASNT training in Jubail.

Ras Tanura and Abqaiq combine large tank farms, terminals and crude processing. The Storage Tank environment, with UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank, matches terminal work closely, and LRUT screening of long pipe runs suits the pipework between units and jetties.

Yanbu has export refineries and petrochemical plants at the western end of the cross-country pipelines. Turnaround work mirrors Jubail, so IRIS, PMI and corrosion mapping are priorities. See ASNT training in Yanbu.

Jeddah and Rabigh mix refining and petrochemicals with power, desalination, port infrastructure and aircraft maintenance. The Aircraft Hangar environment, with 54 airframe and component jobs, suits aviation technicians, while plant crews use the Oil & Gas Site.

Jazan is newer industry, so construction-phase weld inspection with PAUT, TOFD and RT and PMI on alloy components are the most useful practice.

Environments and methods that match Saudi work

Short answer: the simulator has five environments and twelve methods. In Saudi Arabia the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments match upstream, gas plant, refinery and terminal work, the Welding Workshop matches construction and fabrication, the Aircraft Hangar matches aviation and defence, and the NDT Lab supports trainees everywhere.

The five workplace environments are the NDT Lab (bench specimens and reference blocks, 52 jobs), the Welding Workshop (weld coupons and fabrication joints, 52 jobs), the Aircraft Hangar (airframe and component inspection, 54 jobs), the Oil & Gas Site (weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant, 73 jobs) and the Storage Tank (UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank). Thirty-three guided lessons cover the fundamentals.

The twelve methods are PT, MT and VT (surface); contact UT, PAUT, TOFD and RT (volumetric); ET and MFL (electromagnetic); and LRUT guided-wave screening, IRIS internal rotary UT for heat-exchanger and boiler tubes, and PMI for alloy verification.

Two methods deserve special mention in the Saudi context. PMI is heavily used in Saudi plants, where alloy verification of piping, fittings and weld metal is a routine requirement in many owners' specifications, and a mix-up of materials in sour or high-temperature service can be serious. Practising instrument use, test-point selection and result recording in the simulator helps new technicians avoid basic errors. Radiography is still widely used on pipeline and plant construction, but sources carry strict licensing and exclusion-zone duties. The simulator lets technicians practise RT technique selection and film or digital image interpretation with no source at all, so radiation protection rules for real exposures do not apply to simulator practice.

Certification, vendor requirements and regulators in Saudi Arabia

Short answer: Saudi employers commonly ask for NDT personnel certified to ASNT SNT-TC-1A or ISO 9712 schemes, and major owners add their own vendor and personnel requirements. Radiation use is regulated by the Nuclear and Radiological Regulatory Commission (NRRC). Simulator practice is useful under any of these systems but satisfies none of them.

Personnel certification. Both ASNT SNT-TC-1A employer-based certification and ISO 9712 third-party certification are used across the Kingdom, often side by side in the same company, because inspection contractors serve owners, EPCs and licensors from many countries. Some work also asks for ASNT central certification such as ACCP. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility; Atlantis does not train for or issue ISO 9712, PCN or other third-party certificates.

Owner and vendor requirements. The major national operators publish their own engineering standards, procedures and contractor quality requirements. Saudi Aramco, for example, issues Saudi Aramco Engineering Standards (SAES) and Engineering Procedures (SAEP) and applies contractual quality requirements to vendors and contractors, including requirements for NDT personnel and procedures. Large petrochemical and utility owners have comparable requirements. These rules are set by each owner and change over time, so inspection companies should work from the current documents their contract names. Atlantis makes no claim of approval or registration with Saudi Aramco or any other owner, and the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is not an owner-approved qualification.

Radiation regulation. The Nuclear and Radiological Regulatory Commission (NRRC) is the Kingdom's regulator for radiation sources and practices, including industrial radiography. Companies using gamma sources or X-ray equipment need the appropriate licences, trained and authorised personnel and radiation protection programmes. Confirm current licensing requirements with the NRRC before any exposure work.

Codes and standards in daily use. Saudi plants are built and maintained mainly to ASME, API, AWS and NACE/AMPP-based codes, adopted and supplemented by owners' standards, with Saudi Standards (SASO) and ISO standards in some sectors. ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3, API 1104 for pipelines, API 650 and 653 for tanks and AWS D1.1 for structures are common reference points. The simulator teaches method skills rather than any one code's acceptance criteria, so a company's Level III sets the acceptance rules its procedures use. Atlantis does not offer API 510, 570 or 653 or CWI training.

For procedure and written-practice support, see NDT consulting in Saudi Arabia; to track ASNT and ISO 9712 certificates side by side, see the Saudi NDT ERP page.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Saudi Arabia

Short answer: trainees, including young Saudi technicians joining the industry, use guided lessons and NDT Lab jobs to learn fundamentals; working technicians refresh methods and rare defects between turnarounds; Level IIIs and team leads build scenario sets to benchmark large, multinational crews and spot coverage gaps before mobilising.

New trainees. Saudisation targets and localisation programmes mean many companies are bringing new Saudi technicians into NDT, often straight from technical colleges. The 33 guided lessons give each trainee a structured path through set-up, calibration, scanning and interpretation, and the NDT Lab gives them bench jobs to repeat without tying up a senior technician or a reference block. Time on real specimens can then focus on supervised practice that matters.

Working technicians. A technician who spends a year on pipeline radiography may then be assigned to IRIS on a Jubail turnaround. A tank inspector may need PAUT for the first time on a new project. The simulator lets technicians rehearse a less-used method or a rare defect before the job, in camp, at the office or at home, in a browser or app.

Level IIIs and team leads. Saudi inspection companies often field large crews of mixed nationality, experience and certification background for a single turnaround. A Level III can assign the same scenario set to everyone and compare scores objectively, which helps decide who goes to which unit, which methods need a refresher, and how the crew compares with the previous year's. The results are evidence of readiness to discuss with clients, not a certification.

Practice vs certification

Short answer: Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification, it does not issue certificates, it is not an owner or operator approval, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that ASNT SNT-TC-1A written practices or ISO 9712 schemes require.

Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer's written practice sets training, experience and the general, specific and practical examinations, administered under Level III oversight, and the practical exam is performed on real specimens. Under ISO 9712, the certification body sets training, experience and examinations. Owner requirements in Saudi Arabia add their own layers on top. None of these accepts simulator scores as a substitute, and they should not.

What the simulator does is make real exams and real jobs less of a first attempt. A candidate who has set up, scanned and interpreted many virtual flaws arrives at the practical exam with established habits. A technician who has rehearsed a rare defect type is more likely to recognise it on a live unit. Employers should treat scores as one piece of evidence alongside supervised work and formal certification.

Turnarounds, heat and remote sites: why Saudi crews practise virtually

Short answer: Saudi turnarounds bring very large crews together at short notice, field sites are remote and hot, and specimen sets are limited. A browser-based simulator lets technicians practise in camp or at home, lets employers check readiness before mobilising, and takes the learning stage away from live units and radiation sources.

Turnarounds are the first reason. Jubail, Yanbu, Ras Tanura and the gas plants run major shutdowns where inspection crews scale up quickly, often with contract technicians who have not worked together. A short scenario set in the right environment before arrival gives the Level III a fast picture of the crew and gives each technician a refresher in exactly the methods that unit needs.

Remote sites are the second. Technicians in field camps across the Eastern Province or on offshore facilities have long rotations with limited access to labs or specimens. A simulator on a laptop or tablet is available in the evening in camp, between shifts, wherever there is a connection.

Specimens are the third. Flawed specimens are expensive, wear out and quickly become familiar. A library of jobs across five environments keeps practice varied and fair.

Safety is the fourth. Practising radiography technique and interpretation without a source, and tank and plant surveys without heat exposure, working at height or confined-space entry, removes risk from learning. Real work still needs all the usual controls, but technicians arrive with the method rehearsed.

ASNT training, consulting and ERP for Saudi employers

Short answer: beyond the simulator, Atlantis offers Saudi companies ASNT SNT-TC-1A training, Level III consulting and an NDT ERP, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. There is no Atlantis training centre in the Kingdom.

Saudi employers whose clients specify SNT-TC-1A can use ASNT SNT-TC-1A training in Saudi Arabia for Level I, II and III candidates, led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, with written practice development for the company's own certification system. Level III procedure, technique and audit support comes through Saudi consulting, and the Atlantis NDT ERP tracks ASNT and ISO 9712 certificates, equipment calibration, jobs and reports in one place. City training pages cover Dammam, Jubail, Al Khobar, Riyadh and Yanbu. All are quoted on request.

Bring Practical NDT to your Saudi team

Short answer: request a demo through the contact form. Atlantis will show the environments that match your work, agree a pilot group and set up accounts. There is nothing to install beyond a browser or app, and pricing is quote on request. Affordable, accessible and fully customizable.

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and the scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Inspection contractors, EPCs, fabricators, laboratories and technical training institutes in Saudi Arabia can use it as it stands or ask for scenario sets aligned to their procedures and job mix.

A typical start: a short call to understand your work, whether upstream, gas plant, refinery turnaround, terminal, pipeline construction or aviation; a live demonstration of the matching environments; a pilot group; then accounts for your technicians. Team leads see results so they can track progress and find gaps before the next mobilisation.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator available in Saudi Arabia?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so it works anywhere in the Kingdom with an internet connection, from Dammam to Jeddah. There is no centre to visit; demos are arranged through the contact form.

Is Practical NDT approved by Saudi Aramco or other owners?

No. It is a practice tool, not an owner-approved qualification. Owners' personnel and procedure requirements must be met through the certification and approval routes their contracts specify.

Does it replace the SNT-TC-1A or ISO 9712 practical exam?

No. Practical exams must be taken on real specimens under the employer's written practice or the certification body's rules. The simulator helps you prepare.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation?

Yes. Repeating set-up, scanning, interpretation and sizing builds the habits a practical exam checks, so candidates arrive better prepared.

Does it cover refinery and petrochemical turnaround methods like IRIS and PMI?

Yes. The Oil & Gas Site environment, with 73 jobs, includes IRIS on exchanger and boiler tubes, PMI for alloy verification, ET, corrosion mapping and weld inspection.

Does it include radiography, and does it need an NRRC licence?

RT is included, focused on technique and interpretation. No radiation is used, so simulator practice needs no licence. Real industrial radiography requires NRRC licensing and the employer's radiation protection programme.

Can it be used for tank inspection practice?

Yes. The Storage Tank environment covers UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank, which suits terminal and tank-farm work.

Is it useful for training new Saudi technicians?

Yes. The 33 guided lessons and NDT Lab jobs give new trainees a structured path through the fundamentals before supervised work on real specimens.

Can an inspection company use it to assess a turnaround crew?

Yes. A Level III can assign the same scenario set to every technician and compare scores objectively, as one input alongside certification and supervised work.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Saudi Arabia?

Yes, ASNT SNT-TC-1A training only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. See NDT training in Saudi Arabia.

How much does it cost and how do we start?

Pricing is quote on request, depending on users and any custom scenarios. Request a demo and we will show the environments that match your work.

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in South Australia

The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is what Atlantis built as the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and South Australia is a state where that kind of practice has a clear job to do. It is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician opens a job in a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, sets up the technique, carries out the inspection, records the indications and receives a score when the job is closed. South Australian inspection work spans an unusual range for a state of under two million people: naval shipbuilding at Osborne on the Lefevre Peninsula, which is being expanded to build nuclear-powered submarines under AUKUS; copper and uranium processing at Olympic Dam; gas processing at Moomba in the Cooper Basin and the liquids plant at Port Bonython; steelmaking at Whyalla; lead and zinc smelting at Port Pirie; defence aviation at RAAF Base Edinburgh; and a growing fleet of wind farms, transmission lines and hydrogen projects. Practical NDT gives trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs a place to put hours into the methods that work needs without booking a bench, a reference block or a radiation area.

This page is the South Australia hub. It maps where the state's NDT work is, which simulator environments suit each region, how simulator practice sits alongside AINDT certification and the EPA's radiation licensing, and how to arrange a demo. Practical NDT is practice. It is not a certification and it does not replace a practical examination on real specimens under any scheme.

South Australia's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: South Australia's NDT work clusters in five areas: the Port Adelaide and Lefevre Peninsula defence shipbuilding precinct; metropolitan Adelaide's fabrication, defence aerospace and power assets; the Upper Spencer Gulf industrial triangle of Whyalla, Port Pirie and Port Augusta; the Far North mining and gas fields around Olympic Dam, Prominent Hill, Carrapateena and Moomba; and the renewable energy and transmission build-out across the regions.

Osborne and the Lefevre Peninsula. The Osborne Naval Shipyard is the centre of Australian naval shipbuilding. The keel of the first Hunter class frigate was laid there in August 2026, with most of the first ship's blocks already in construction, and the site is being enlarged for SSN-AUKUS submarine construction from the 2030s. That means a sustained demand for weld inspection on thick structural steel: ultrasonic and phased array examination of butt and fillet welds, magnetic particle and penetrant testing on fabricated assemblies, visual inspection at every stage, and radiography where the code or the drawing calls for it. Defence work is controlled to demanding quality requirements, and the supply chain of fabricators, machinists and coating contractors around Port Adelaide and Osborne inherits those requirements.

Metropolitan Adelaide. The northern suburbs host RAAF Base Edinburgh, home to maritime patrol and surveillance aircraft, and the Edinburgh Parks and Salisbury defence and electronics precinct. Torrens Island and Pelican Point gas-fired power stations, water and wastewater assets, and the structural and pressure-equipment fabrication shops of Wingfield, Regency Park and Lonsdale provide steady inspection work. Adelaide no longer has an operating oil refinery, so its process-plant work is centred on fuel terminals, power plant boilers and heat exchangers, and industrial gas and chemical sites.

The Upper Spencer Gulf. Whyalla's integrated steelworks has been in administration since early 2025, its blast furnace has been offline since April 2026 and a closure of the furnace was announced in September 2026, while the state and federal governments run a sale process and plan a lower-emissions rebuild. Whatever form the site takes next, it will involve large amounts of plant demolition, refurbishment and new fabrication, all of which bring inspection. Port Pirie hosts a large lead and multi-metals smelter, and Port Augusta is the hub for transmission, solar and wind projects in the region. Port Bonython near Whyalla receives liquids from the Cooper Basin for processing and export.

The Far North. Olympic Dam, near Roxby Downs, is one of the world's largest deposits of copper and uranium, with an underground mine, concentrator, smelter, refinery and hydrometallurgical plant. Prominent Hill and Carrapateena add further copper operations. Moomba, in the Cooper Basin, is the processing hub for South Australian gas and liquids, connected by long pipelines to Adelaide, Sydney and Port Bonython. These remote sites run on fly-in fly-out rosters, and their inspection programmes include corrosion monitoring on piping and vessels, tank inspection, heat exchanger tube testing, alloy verification and structural weld inspection on mills, crushers and conveyors.

Regional energy and agriculture. Wind farms in the Mid North and on the Eyre and Yorke peninsulas, large batteries, new interconnector transmission lines and planned hydrogen projects bring structural steel, tower flange and bolted-connection inspection. Wine, grain and food processing across the Barossa, Riverland and Limestone Coast use pressure vessels, boilers and storage tanks that need periodic in-service inspection under work health and safety law.

Practical NDT by city and region in South Australia

Short answer: South Australia does not yet have a city-level Practical NDT page, so this hub covers the whole state. Adelaide has an Atlantis ASNT training page, linked below. The table matches each South Australian cluster to the simulator environments and methods that fit its work.

Adelaide. Technicians in Adelaide work across the widest mix in the state: shop inspection at structural and pressure-equipment fabricators, boiler and heat exchanger work at the gas-fired power stations, tank and pipework inspection at fuel terminals, and component work linked to defence aviation. A trainee joining an Adelaide inspection company can begin with guided NDT Lab lessons on reference blocks before moving to Welding Workshop jobs. Employers who need ASNT SNT-TC-1A personnel can see ASNT training for Adelaide.

Osborne and Port Adelaide. Shipyard inspection is weld inspection at scale. Thick plate butt welds, T-joints and complex block connections suit PAUT and TOFD practice in the Welding Workshop, along with MT on fillet welds and VT at fit-up and after welding. Inspectors who move between the frigate programme and supply-chain fabricators can use the simulator to keep sizing and characterisation consistent between jobs.

Whyalla. The steelworks transition will mean structural assessment of existing plant, refurbishment and new-build fabrication, alongside port, rail and liquids-plant work at Port Bonython. Welding Workshop jobs build weld inspection skills, while Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank jobs suit tank and pipework surveys on process and storage assets.

Port Pirie and Port Augusta. Smelter maintenance brings corrosion and wear surveys, alloy checks on replacement components and weld inspection on repairs. Port Augusta's transmission and renewable projects add structural steel and bolted-connection inspection. NDT Lab and Oil & Gas Site jobs cover the core methods.

Olympic Dam and the copper province. Mining and metallurgical plants combine structural inspection on mills and conveyors with process-plant inspection on vessels, tanks, piping and heat exchangers. IRIS on exchanger tubes and PMI on alloy piping are especially useful refreshers for FIFO technicians who meet them only during shutdowns.

Moomba and the Cooper Basin. Gas processing plants and long-distance pipelines rely on corrosion monitoring, weld inspection on tie-ins and repairs, tank surveys and guided-wave screening of pipe runs. The Oil & Gas Site environment, with LRUT screening and IRIS tube inspection, matches this work closely.

Environments and methods that match South Australian work

Short answer: the Welding Workshop fits Osborne and the fabrication supply chain; the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank fit Moomba, Port Bonython, Olympic Dam and the smelters; the Aircraft Hangar fits defence aviation around Edinburgh; and the NDT Lab is where every trainee starts.

The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five workplace environments and twelve methods. In the NDT Lab a technician works on bench specimens and reference blocks, building calibration habits, probe handling and signal interpretation before meeting real geometry. The Welding Workshop holds weld coupons and fabrication joints, with jobs in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT and VT. The Aircraft Hangar covers airframe and component inspection, especially ET, PT and UT. The Oil & Gas Site puts weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice into a process plant setting. The Storage Tank environment covers UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank.

The twelve methods are grouped as surface (PT, MT, VT), volumetric (UT contact, PAUT, TOFD, RT), electromagnetic (ET, MFL) and specialised (LRUT guided-wave screening, IRIS internal rotary UT for heat exchanger and boiler tubes, and PMI alloy verification). There are 33 guided lessons, and the job library includes 52 NDT Lab jobs, 52 Welding Workshop jobs, 54 Aircraft Hangar jobs and 73 Oil & Gas Site jobs.

For South Australia, the mapping looks like this. Shipbuilding and defence fabrication lean on PAUT and TOFD for full-penetration welds in thick sections, MT for fillet and attachment welds, and VT throughout; the Welding Workshop is the main environment. Gas processing and pipelines need UT corrosion mapping, LRUT screening, IRIS on exchanger tubes, PMI on alloy piping and RT on welds; the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments carry those jobs. Mining and metallurgy mix both: weld and structural inspection on mills, kilns and conveyors, and process-plant inspection on leach tanks, thickeners and acid plant equipment. Power generation needs boiler tube and exchanger work, so IRIS and UT thickness surveys are valuable. Defence aviation relies on eddy current, penetrant and ultrasonic inspection of components, which the Aircraft Hangar environment covers.

Because the jobs are scored, a technician can repeat the same scenario until the result is consistent, then move on to harder variations. That is useful in a state where a technician may spend months on one kind of work and then be asked to switch, for example from shipyard weld inspection to a shutdown at a mining or gas plant.

Regulators and requirements South Australian technicians meet

Short answer: in South Australia, industrial radiography is licensed by the Environment Protection Authority under the Radiation Protection and Control Act 2021; pressure equipment, plant and workplace safety fall under the Work Health and Safety Act and SafeWork SA; and most NDT personnel are certified through AINDT, whose scheme is based on ISO 9712. Practical NDT is practice for whichever scheme a technician works under.

Radiation. The EPA administers the Radiation Protection and Control Act 2021 and the Radiation Protection and Control Regulations 2022, which adopt ARPANSA codes and standards. People who operate X-ray apparatus or sealed sources for industrial radiography need an EPA licence, and the EPA's guidance points to certification in NDT radiography and radiation safety from a provider endorsed by the AINDT Certification Board, or an EPA radiation examination, as supporting evidence. Businesses that possess sources also need registration and a radiation management plan. Simulator RT practice involves no radiation at all, so it sits entirely outside this licensing, and it is no substitute for the licence or the safety training.

Plant and pressure equipment. South Australia applies the model Work Health and Safety laws, administered by SafeWork SA. Pressure vessels and boilers are plant, with design and item registration requirements for certain hazard levels, and in-service inspection is normally carried out to AS/NZS 3788. Design and fabrication usually reference AS 1210 for pressure vessels, AS 4037 for examination and testing, AS/NZS 1554 for structural welding and AS 4041 for pressure piping. Confirm current registration requirements with SafeWork SA for any specific item.

Pipelines and petroleum. Onshore pipelines in the state are designed, built and operated to AS 2885, and petroleum and pipeline activities are regulated by the state's Department for Energy and Mining under the Petroleum and Geothermal Energy Act 2000. Offshore activities in Commonwealth waters fall under NOPSEMA.

Defence. Naval shipbuilding follows defence and classification-society requirements on top of Australian standards, and prime contractors set their own qualification rules for inspectors on their programmes.

Certification. AINDT certification, aligned with ISO 9712, is the usual personnel certification in Australia, and many South Australian employers require it. Some employers working for US-owned operators, US OEMs or on US-code projects also use ASNT SNT-TC-1A, where the employer's written practice controls qualification and certification. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only; it does not train toward or administer AINDT or ISO 9712 certification. The simulator itself is scheme-neutral practice.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in South Australia

Short answer: trainees use guided lessons to learn fundamentals; working technicians use rare-defect jobs to stay sharp between assignments; Level IIIs and team leads build scenario sets, benchmark crews and find coverage gaps.

Trainees. South Australia is growing its defence and energy workforce, with TAFE SA, university engineering programmes and industry pathways all feeding new entrants. A new trainee often learns theory in a classroom, then waits for limited time on real equipment. The 33 guided lessons in the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator let a trainee build the basics first: choosing a probe, setting range and sensitivity, scanning a weld, recognising common indications. When they reach a real bench or a real site, the first hours are spent refining technique instead of learning where the controls are.

Working technicians. A shipyard UT technician may go months without a corrosion survey, and a FIFO technician at a mine may go a year without TOFD. Skills fade quietly. Short, scored jobs between swings, during a slow week or before a shutdown let technicians refresh the methods and defect types they meet least, including rare flaws that are hard to find in real specimens.

Level IIIs and team leads. A Level III can assemble a scenario set that mirrors a client's job mix, assign it to every new starter, and compare the results objectively. That gives a clearer picture of who is ready for which work, where the crew's gaps are, and which methods need more training time. For inspection companies bidding into defence or resources supply chains, it is also a structured way to show that people are being kept current between jobs.

Why simulator practice suits South Australia's projects

Short answer: long programmes, remote sites and a stretched workforce make it hard to give technicians enough varied practice on real specimens. Browser-based practice fills those gaps without travel, specimens or radiation.

South Australia's biggest inspection programmes run for years. The frigate and submarine work at Osborne is a multi-decade effort, the Whyalla rebuild will take years, and mining and gas plants run continuously with planned shutdowns. Programmes of that length need a steady supply of competent technicians and a way to keep existing staff consistent. At the same time, the state competes with Western Australia, Queensland and the eastern states for the same experienced people.

Distance matters too. Olympic Dam is more than five hundred kilometres north of Adelaide by road, and Moomba is further still. A technician on a FIFO roster cannot easily book an hour in an Adelaide training room. Reference specimens with realistic, well-characterised flaws are expensive and scarce, and a shared set cannot be in Osborne, Whyalla and Roxby Downs at once. A browser-based simulator removes those constraints.

Safety is the other benefit. Simulator practice involves no radiation, no confined space entry, no working at height and no hot work permit. Trainees can make mistakes, see the result in their score and learn from it without risk to themselves or to a client's asset.

None of this replaces supervised field experience. Real welds, real corrosion and real access problems teach things that no simulator can. The point is to make the time on real work count for more.

Practice vs certification

Short answer: Practical NDT is a skills-practice and readiness tool. It does not grant certification, it does not count as an AINDT or ISO 9712 examination, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens required by an employer's written practice under ASNT SNT-TC-1A.

Certification in NDT always involves training, documented experience and examinations, including a practical examination on real specimens. Under AINDT's ISO 9712 based scheme those examinations are set and controlled by the certification body. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer's written practice sets the requirements and the employer certifies its own personnel. Either way, simulator scores are not examination results.

What the simulator does is help people arrive at their examinations, and at their first real jobs, better prepared. Repeated set-up, scanning, interpretation and sizing build habits that carry over. A Level III can use simulator results to judge when a candidate is ready to sit a practical exam, but the exam itself happens on real specimens under the relevant scheme. For radiography, the simulator gives interpretation and technique practice; the EPA licence and radiation safety training remain separate legal requirements.

Atlantis's own training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. See Atlantis NDT training and ASNT training in Australia for details. Atlantis has no South Australian training centre.

Bring Practical NDT to your South Australian team

Short answer: request a demo, tell us which South Australian sectors and methods matter to your team, and we will show the matching environments and agree a pilot. Pricing is quote on request.

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and the scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. The product is affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Shipyard suppliers, inspection companies, mining and gas operators, training providers and TAFE programmes can use it as supplied or ask for scenario sets aligned to their own procedures and job mix.

A typical start is simple. We hold a short call to understand your work, whether that is defence weld inspection, gas plant integrity, smelter maintenance or shop fabrication. We then demonstrate the relevant environments live, agree a pilot group and set up accounts so people can practise in a browser or app. Team leads see results so they can track progress and spot gaps. There is no hardware to install and no lab to book.

  • Request a Practical NDT demo for your South Australian team
  • Ask for a South Australia quote for a crew, a cohort or a whole company
  • Discuss scenario sets for shipbuilding, mining or gas work

Read the Practical NDT overview for the full environment and method list, or go back to the Australia hub to compare other states.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in South Australia?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so it works in Adelaide, Whyalla, Port Pirie, Roxby Downs or a Moomba camp wherever there is a connection. There is no South Australian centre to visit. Demos are arranged through the contact form.

Does Practical NDT count towards AINDT certification?

No. AINDT certification requires training, documented experience and examinations under its ISO 9712 based scheme. Simulator practice can help a candidate prepare, but it is not part of that scheme, and Atlantis does not provide AINDT or ISO 9712 training or examinations.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation?

Yes, as preparation. Scored set-up, scanning, interpretation and sizing jobs build the habits a practical exam tests. The exam itself must still be taken on real specimens under the relevant scheme or written practice.

Is it useful for shipyard weld inspection at Osborne?

It is relevant practice. The Welding Workshop covers PAUT, TOFD, UT, MT, PT, RT and VT on weld coupons and fabrication joints. Defence programmes set their own qualification requirements, which the simulator does not replace.

Does it cover the work at Moomba and Olympic Dam?

The Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments cover corrosion mapping, weld inspection, IRIS tube inspection, LRUT screening, PMI and tank surveys, which are typical of gas processing and metallurgical plants.

Does simulator radiography need an EPA licence?

No. No radiation is involved in the simulator. Real industrial radiography in South Australia requires an EPA licence under the Radiation Protection and Control Act 2021, and the simulator does not satisfy any part of that requirement.

Can an Adelaide inspection company use it to benchmark new hires?

Yes. A Level III can assign the same scenario set to every candidate and compare scores objectively before deciding who goes to which job.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: trainees on guided lessons, working technicians refreshing less-used methods and rare defects, and Level IIIs building and assigning scenario sets.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in South Australia?

Yes, ASNT SNT-TC-1A training only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. See NDT training in Adelaide.
