NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Spain

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Spain's mix of refineries, LNG terminals, wind manufacturing, naval yards, aerospace plants and nuclear stations gives it plenty to practise for. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician enters a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, takes a job, sets up the technique, scans or interprets, and is scored the moment the job is closed. Spanish inspection work is spread around the coast and a few inland hubs: refining and petrochemicals at Tarragona, Cartagena, Huelva, Algeciras, Castellón, Bilbao, A Coruña and Puertollano; LNG terminals from Barcelona to Huelva and from Bilbao to Gijón; wind tower and offshore foundation fabrication in the north; naval and commercial shipbuilding at Ferrol, Cartagena, the Bay of Cádiz and Vigo; aerospace at Getafe, Illescas, Seville, Cádiz and the Basque Country; and nuclear power in Catalonia, Valencia, Extremadura and Castilla-La Mancha. Technicians rarely use every method every month, and the right flawed specimens are hard to come by. The simulator gives trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs a way to stay sharp without booking lab time or using up specimens.

This is the Spain hub for Practical NDT. It covers where Spanish NDT work happens by region, how the simulator's environments and methods fit that work, the regulators and certification schemes Spanish technicians deal with, and an honest account of what a simulator can and cannot do for certification. To see it with your own jobs in mind, request a Practical NDT demo for Spain.

Spain's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Spanish NDT work is driven by refining and petrochemicals, gas and LNG infrastructure, wind energy manufacturing, shipbuilding, aerospace, nuclear power and general metal fabrication. Most of it sits on the coasts, with Madrid and a few inland industrial centres as the exceptions, so each region has a recognisably different mix of methods.

Catalonia. The Tarragona area holds the largest chemical and petrochemical complex in southern Europe, with a refinery, steam crackers and dozens of chemical plants spread across its north and south industrial estates and served by the port of Tarragona. In the same province are the Ascó and Vandellós II nuclear plants. Barcelona adds one of Spain's busiest ports, a large LNG regasification terminal, automotive manufacturing at Martorell and a broad engineering and fabrication base. Turnaround inspection, exchanger and tube work, alloy verification, tank surveys and nuclear outage work make Catalonia one of the most varied NDT markets in the country.

The Basque Country and Cantabria. Bilbao has long been an industrial capital: a refinery at Muskiz, an LNG terminal at the port, steel and forging works, heavy machinery, aero-engine design and manufacturing at Zamudio and a wind supply chain that includes tower and offshore foundation fabrication in the port area. Forgings, castings and thick welded structures mean plenty of UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT and PT, and aero-engine work adds eddy current and penetrant to aerospace procedures.

Asturias and Galicia. Asturias has integrated steelmaking at Avilés and Gijón, an LNG terminal at El Musel in Gijón, and fabrication of wind towers and offshore wind components. In Galicia, Ferrol and Fene are home to naval shipbuilding and offshore wind jacket fabrication, Vigo has a large cluster of private shipyards and automotive manufacturing, A Coruña has a refinery and Mugardos an LNG terminal. Weld inspection on hulls, jackets, monopiles and towers is the everyday work here.

The Valencian Community and Murcia. Castellón has a coastal refinery and a chemical cluster, Sagunto an LNG terminal, Almussafes an automotive plant and Cofrentes a nuclear power station. Further south, the Escombreras valley at Cartagena combines one of Spain's largest refineries, an LNG terminal, power plants and chemical industry, while the Cartagena naval yard builds submarines and naval vessels. Refinery IRIS, PMI and tank work sit next to naval PAUT and TOFD.

Andalusia. Huelva has a refinery and one of Spain's main chemical poles, together with an LNG terminal. The Bay of Algeciras, home to one of Europe's busiest container ports, hosts a large refinery and petrochemical complex at San Roque. The Bay of Cádiz has naval and commercial shipyards at Puerto Real, San Fernando and Cádiz, and aerostructures plants. Seville is an aerospace centre with military transport aircraft final assembly and a strong supplier base, and southern Spain's large solar thermal plants add pressure piping, heat exchangers and molten-salt tanks.

Madrid and the interior. Madrid is the headquarters city for Spanish engineering, procurement and construction firms, utilities and inspection companies, and Getafe, Illescas and Albacete host aircraft, composite and helicopter plants. Puertollano in Castilla-La Mancha has an inland refinery and petrochemical complex, Trillo a nuclear plant, and Almaraz in Extremadura a two-unit nuclear station. Aragon and Navarre add automotive, wind turbine manufacturing and general engineering.

Practical NDT by region in Spain

Atlantis does not yet have Practical NDT pages for individual Spanish cities, so this hub covers the main centres directly. The table maps each to the environments and methods that match its everyday jobs.

City or regionMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise
TarragonaRefining, petrochemicals, chemical plants, nuclear (Ascó, Vandellós II)Oil & Gas Site, Storage Tank, NDT Lab; IRIS, PMI, TOFD, PAUT, MFL
BarcelonaPort, LNG terminal, automotive, engineering and fabricationWelding Workshop, Storage Tank, NDT Lab; UT, PAUT, MT, ET, MFL
Bilbao and the Basque CountryRefining, LNG, forgings, heavy machinery, aero-engines, wind and offshore foundationsWelding Workshop, NDT Lab, Aircraft Hangar; UT, PAUT, TOFD, ET, PT
Asturias and GaliciaSteel, naval and commercial shipbuilding, offshore wind jackets and towers, refining, LNGWelding Workshop, Storage Tank; PAUT, TOFD, UT, MT, RT
Castellón, Sagunto, ValenciaRefining, chemicals, LNG, automotive, nuclear (Cofrentes)Oil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; IRIS, PMI, UT, MFL
CartagenaRefining, LNG, power, naval shipbuildingOil & Gas Site, Welding Workshop, Storage Tank; IRIS, TOFD, PAUT, PMI
Huelva and AlgecirasRefining, petrochemicals, chemicals, LNG, portsOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; IRIS, PMI, LRUT, MFL, PAUT
Seville and the Bay of CádizAircraft assembly, aerostructures, naval and commercial shipyards, solar thermalAircraft Hangar, Welding Workshop; ET, PT, UT, PAUT
Madrid and Castilla-La ManchaAircraft and composites, helicopters, inland refining, nuclear (Trillo)Aircraft Hangar, Oil & Gas Site; ET, UT, PT, IRIS

Tarragona. Petrochemical turnarounds in Tarragona call for large crews and fast mobilisation. IRIS on exchanger bundles, PMI on alloy circuits, TOFD and PAUT on vessel and nozzle welds, corrosion mapping on piping and MFL floor screening on tanks are the core skills, all present in the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank environments. Nuclear outages at Ascó and Vandellós II add UT, eddy current and visual work under strict procedures. See also the Tarragona ERP page and the Tarragona digital twin page.

Barcelona. Port terminals, LNG storage, automotive suppliers and fabrication shops make Barcelona a mixed market. Tank surveys, weld inspection on fabricated equipment, eddy current on automotive parts and fundamentals training for new hires all fit. Atlantis also has an ASNT NDT training page for Barcelona for employers who work to US codes.

Bilbao and the Basque Country. Forging and casting inspection relies on UT and MT, wind and offshore foundation fabrication on PAUT and TOFD of thick welds, and aero-engine manufacturing on eddy current and penetrant inspection. The NDT Lab, Welding Workshop and Aircraft Hangar cover all three.

Asturias and Galicia. Shipyard and offshore wind fabrication generate long runs of thick welds, where PAUT and TOFD have become routine alongside UT, MT and RT. The Welding Workshop is the natural home, while LNG terminals at Gijón and Mugardos and the A Coruña refinery map to Storage Tank and Oil & Gas Site jobs.

Castellón, Sagunto and Valencia. Refinery and chemical plant maintenance, LNG tank work and nuclear outages at Cofrentes mean exchanger, tube and tank skills are in demand.

Cartagena. The Escombreras refinery and LNG terminal and the naval yard sit a few kilometres apart, so one inspection company can need both IRIS and PMI for a turnaround and PAUT and TOFD for naval welds in the same quarter.

Huelva and Algeciras. Two of Spain's largest refining and chemical complexes, plus LNG and busy port terminals, keep turnaround and tank crews busy. LRUT guided-wave screening is useful on long pipe racks and jetty lines.

Seville and the Bay of Cádiz. Aerospace assembly and aerostructure plants lean on eddy current, penetrant and UT of composites and metallic parts, mapped to the Aircraft Hangar. Shipyards in the bay add weld inspection, and solar thermal plants add piping and tank work.

Madrid and Castilla-La Mancha. Aircraft, composites and helicopter plants make the Aircraft Hangar the key environment, while the Puertollano refinery and nuclear outages at Trillo add process and power-plant methods.

Environments and methods that match Spanish work

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. In Spain the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank serve refining, petrochemicals and LNG; the Welding Workshop serves shipbuilding, wind and fabrication; the Aircraft Hangar serves aerospace; and the NDT Lab builds fundamentals for everyone.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). Weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant: contact UT and PAUT corrosion mapping, TOFD on pressure welds, IRIS internal rotary UT on exchanger and boiler tubes, LRUT guided-wave screening on long pipe runs and PMI alloy verification. It mirrors turnaround work at Tarragona, Cartagena, Huelva, Algeciras, Castellón, Bilbao, A Coruña and Puertollano.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank. Refinery tank farms, port oil terminals and the tank inventories around Spain's LNG terminals generate this work.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints for RT film and digital image interpretation, UT and PAUT detection and sizing, TOFD, MT and VT against acceptance criteria. It fits shipyards, wind tower and offshore foundation fabricators, pressure equipment shops and structural steel.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection with eddy current, penetrant and UT, matching Spain's aircraft assembly, composites, helicopter and aero-engine sectors and airline maintenance at Madrid, Barcelona and other hubs.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks for calibration, probe handling, sensitivity, scan coverage and indication recognition. It suits new trainees, forging and casting inspectors and anyone preparing for a practical examination.

Across the twelve methods, surface methods (PT, MT, VT) cover finished parts and structural welds; volumetric methods (UT contact, PAUT, TOFD, RT) carry weld and corrosion assessment; electromagnetic methods (ET, MFL) serve aerospace, tubes and tank floors; and the specialist techniques (LRUT, IRIS, PMI) reflect refinery and chemical plant integrity programmes.

Regulators and requirements Spanish technicians meet

Short answer: Spanish NDT personnel are normally certified to UNE-EN ISO 9712, mainly through CERTIAEND; industrial radiography staff need personal licences from the Nuclear Safety Council (CSN); and pressure equipment in service is governed by the Pressure Equipment Regulation approved by Royal Decree 809/2021. Practical NDT is practice for any of these frameworks and replaces none of them.

Personnel certification. Spain applies UNE-EN ISO 9712. CERTIAEND, the certification body operated by the Spanish NDT association AEND and accredited by ENAC, certifies NDT personnel to that standard. Employers working on US-designed plants, for US-owned operators or on ASME and API projects sometimes keep ASNT SNT-TC-1A based written practices as well. That is market context only. Atlantis training aligns with ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, and Atlantis does not train toward, certify or administer UNE-EN ISO 9712 or CERTIAEND certification. Practical NDT is practice for whichever scheme you work under.

Radiation safety. The Consejo de Seguridad Nuclear (CSN) is Spain's regulator for nuclear safety and radiation protection. Industrial radiography is carried out in authorised radioactive installations, and people who operate or supervise the equipment need personal, non-transferable operator or supervisor licences issued by the CSN for the industrial radiography field of application, which must be renewed periodically. Practical NDT's RT jobs involve no radiation source and do not count toward a CSN licence.

Pressure equipment. New pressure equipment is placed on the market under the Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU as transposed into Spanish law. Equipment in use is covered by the Reglamento de Equipos a Presión and its complementary technical instructions, approved by Royal Decree 809/2021, with periodic inspections carried out by authorised control bodies and oversight by the industry departments of the autonomous communities. Confirm the current requirements with your autonomous community or control body before relying on any detail.

Nuclear and codes in daily use. Nuclear in-service inspection is overseen by the CSN, and Spanish plants work to their own inspection programmes, which reference ASME Section XI for several plant designs. Fabrication commonly references the EN ISO weld testing and acceptance standards, EN 13445 and EN 13480, and ASME and API codes for export and refinery work; shipyards and offshore wind fabricators work to classification society and project specifications. Mentioned as context only.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Spain

Practical NDT adapts to three kinds of user, each with a distinct challenge in Spain.

New trainees. Spanish trainees often come from vocational training (formación profesional) in welding, mechanics or quality, or move across from production roles. The hardest thing early on is enough hands-on time. Guided fundamentals in the NDT Lab let a trainee repeat calibration, angle-beam setup, scan coverage and indication interpretation with instant feedback, so a real block is never the first attempt. It is good NDT practical exam preparation, with the clear understanding that the real exam is taken on real specimens.

Working technicians. Spanish work comes in waves: spring and autumn turnarounds on the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts, nuclear refuelling outages, wind and shipyard production peaks. A technician who spent months on wind tower UT may be called to run IRIS on an exchanger bundle in Huelva or TOFD on a reactor nozzle in Tarragona. Rare-defect refreshers between assignments, on lack of fusion, laminations, hydrogen damage, stress corrosion cracking and tube pitting, help them arrive ready rather than relearn on the client's equipment.

Level IIIs and team leads. Level IIIs can build and assign scenario sets, benchmark crews objectively and find coverage gaps before a campaign. When a turnaround brings in contract technicians from across Spain and Portugal, a consistent scenario set gives a like-for-like view of readiness and helps confirm that new procedures are understood before they reach the field.

Practice vs certification

Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification. It does not grant a level under UNE-EN ISO 9712, ASNT SNT-TC-1A or any employer's written practice, it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens those schemes require, and it does not count toward a CSN radiography licence. What it adds is realistic repetition: more chances to set up, scan, interpret and get feedback than a lab timetable or specimen store allows. It complements formal NDT training and on-the-job experience; the formal practical exam remains the step that counts.

Why virtual NDT training suits Spanish employers

Direct answer: Spain's NDT work is spread around a long Mediterranean and Atlantic coastline plus a few inland hubs, it arrives in turnaround and outage waves, and many inspection firms are small. A browser-based ultrasonic testing simulator and phased array simulator let them give staff structured practice without tying up a lab, a supervisor and a set of flawed specimens.

A crew based in Tarragona may finish a turnaround and move to Huelva, then to a wind fabrication yard in Asturias. Organising consistent practice between those moves is difficult, and smaller firms rarely own specimens with the full range of defect types. With the simulator, technicians practise at home, in a hotel room on a turnaround or in the shop office, subject to company IT rules. Supervisors see scores, not self-assessments. A Level III can send one scenario set to everyone on a campaign. None of this replaces real equipment time, but it makes real time count for more. The simulator's jobs and feedback are presented in English; ask during the demo if Spanish-language support matters for your team.

Who in Spain typically looks at Practical NDT

Groups that tend to find a simulator useful in Spain include inspection service companies that staff refinery, chemical and nuclear outages; wind tower and offshore foundation fabricators; shipyards and their subcontractors; aerospace manufacturers and maintenance organisations; pressure equipment and forging manufacturers; vocational training centres that want more practice time for students; and individual technicians preparing for an exam or returning to a method. These are industry descriptions, not a customer list; Atlantis does not name customers on this page.

For Spanish employers who work to ASME and API codes or for US-owned plants and OEMs, Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A aligned NDT training online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility, and Level III consulting on procedures, techniques and written practices. The Atlantis ERP for Spain can record UNE-EN ISO 9712 certificates alongside ASNT-based ones for companies managing mixed crews.

Bring Practical NDT to your Spanish team

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience. The scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who also leads Atlantis training. Rollout starts with a short online demo, then a conversation about your work, whether that is a Tarragona turnaround crew, a Basque forging or wind fabrication NDT team, a Galician or Andalusian shipyard subcontractor, an aerospace quality group in Seville or Madrid, or a nuclear outage contractor. Together we choose the environments and methods that match your jobs, and technicians get access by browser or app wherever they are. Everything is delivered online; there is no physical centre to visit.

Pricing is quote on request, and the offer is built to be affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Book a Spain Practical NDT demo, read the Practical NDT overview, or write to info@atlantisndt.com.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in Spain?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so it works anywhere in Spain with a connection, from Bilbao to Algeciras. There is no physical centre to visit.

Does Practical NDT count toward UNE-EN ISO 9712 or CERTIAEND certification?

No. It is practice only. Certification under UNE-EN ISO 9712 requires its own training, experience and examinations, including a practical exam on real specimens. The simulator helps you prepare.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation?

It can build familiarity, speed and confidence with setups, scanning and interpretation before a practical exam. It does not replace the exam or the experience your scheme or employer requires.

Does it include radiography, and does it count toward a CSN licence?

It includes RT as technique and image interpretation practice with no radiation source. It does not count toward a CSN operator or supervisor licence.

Is it useful for wind tower and offshore foundation fabrication?

Yes for the underlying skills: UT, PAUT and TOFD on thick welds, MT on fillet and attachment welds and RT interpretation. Project procedures and acceptance criteria still come from your employer and Level III.

Is it useful for refinery turnarounds in Tarragona, Huelva or Cartagena?

Yes. The Oil & Gas Site environment covers IRIS, PMI, TOFD, PAUT corrosion mapping and LRUT, and the Storage Tank environment covers shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening.

Which Spanish industries is it most useful for?

Refining and petrochemicals, LNG and gas infrastructure, wind energy manufacturing, shipbuilding, aerospace, nuclear power, steel and forgings, and general pressure equipment fabrication.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: guided fundamentals for new trainees, rare-defect refreshers for working technicians, and scenario building and crew benchmarking for Level IIIs and team leads.

Is the simulator available in Spanish?

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Spain?

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A and is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. It suits employers working to US codes or for US clients. It is not UNE-EN ISO 9712 training. See NDT training.

contentHtml:
HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Sweden

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Sweden is a country where that kind of practice earns its keep. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician steps into a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, picks up a job, sets up the technique, scans or interprets, and gets a score the moment the job is closed. Swedish inspection work is unusually varied for a country of its size: special steel and tube mills in Bergslagen, iron ore and steel in Norrbotten, three nuclear power sites on the coast, a refinery and petrochemical cluster on the west coast, truck, car and bearing manufacturing around Gothenburg and Södertälje, military aircraft in Linköping, aero-engine parts in Trollhättan, naval shipbuilding in Karlskrona, and hundreds of district heating, combined heat and power and pulp mill boilers spread across the country. A technician can go months without touching a particular method, then need it on a Monday morning. The simulator lets trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs keep their hands and eyes sharp between assignments without booking lab time or using up specimens.

This page is the Sweden hub for Practical NDT. It covers where Swedish NDT work actually happens, how the simulator's environments and methods map onto that work, the regulators and schemes Swedish technicians deal with, and a plain explanation of what a simulator can and cannot do for certification. If you would like to see it with your own jobs in mind, request a Practical NDT demo for Sweden.

Sweden's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Swedish NDT work clusters around five industrial systems, namely special steel and metals, nuclear power, energy and process plants, automotive and engineering manufacturing, and defence aerospace and naval work. Each sits in a different part of the country and asks for a different mix of methods, so a technician in Luleå and one in Stenungsund can have very different working weeks.

Norrbotten and the north. The far north is Sweden's iron ore and primary steel country. The Kiruna and Malmberget mines feed pellet plants and the ore railway to the ports of Luleå and Narvik, and the Luleå steelworks has been the centre of Swedish primary steelmaking for decades. New fossil-free steel and hydrogen projects in the Luleå and Boden area have added large construction sites with heavy structural, piping and pressure work. Further south along the coast, Skellefteå hosts a major copper and precious-metals smelter, and the Norrland coast as a whole is lined with pulp and paper mills whose recovery boilers, digesters and bleach plant equipment need careful, regular inspection. The great rivers of the north, the Lule, Skellefte and Ume among them, carry hydropower stations with penstocks, turbines and gates. Inspection here means boiler tube thickness surveys, weld inspection on new construction, corrosion work in aggressive chemical service, and structural MT and VT on heavy plant and mining equipment, often in long, cold winters and at sites hours apart.

Bergslagen and the special steel belt. Central Sweden, from Dalarna through Gästrikland and Värmland to Västmanland, is where the country's special steel tradition lives: strip production in Borlänge, tube and advanced-materials manufacturing in Sandviken, bearing steel in Hofors, stainless steel in Avesta, tool steel in Hagfors, and plate in Oxelösund on the coast south of Stockholm. Mill NDT is a different world from field inspection. It involves automated and manual UT of bars, plate and forgings, eddy current testing of tubes, PMI alloy verification of high-alloy grades, and MT and PT on finished parts. A technician who calibrates an immersion or contact UT system every shift still benefits from rehearsing manual flaw sizing, because the hard calls come when a mill indication needs a manual follow-up.

The nuclear coast. Sweden's three operating nuclear sites are Forsmark in Uppland, Oskarshamn on the Småland coast and Ringhals in Halland south of Gothenburg. Annual outages bring large inspection programmes on reactor components, primary and auxiliary piping, steam generators at the pressurised water reactors, and turbine-hall equipment. Nuclear NDT in Sweden is notable for its qualification regime (see the regulators section below), and outage crews are judged on precision and procedure discipline. Västerås, west of Stockholm, adds nuclear fuel manufacturing and a long history of power engineering.

The west coast process cluster. Lysekil hosts the largest refinery in Scandinavia, Gothenburg has two further refineries and one of the Nordic region's busiest ports, and Stenungsund is home to Sweden's main petrochemical cluster with a steam cracker and chemical plants. Refinery and petrochemical turnarounds call for heat exchanger tube inspection, alloy verification, corrosion mapping on piping and vessels, TOFD and PAUT on pressure welds, and tank inspection at terminals. This is the part of Sweden that looks most like the Oil & Gas Site environment in the simulator.

Gothenburg, Trollhättan and the engineering west. Gothenburg is Sweden's automotive and engineering capital, with car and truck manufacturing, bearing production and a dense supplier base. Trollhättan, inland, has a long aero-engine component tradition, where castings, forgings and welded engine structures go through penetrant, eddy current, UT and radiographic inspection to strict aerospace procedures.

Stockholm, Södertälje, Linköping and the east. Heavy truck and engine manufacturing in Södertälje, power and automation engineering in Västerås, combat aircraft design and production in Linköping, and the many combined heat and power plants that serve Stockholm and other cities give the east a mix of manufacturing, aerospace and boiler work.

Karlskrona and the south. Karlskrona is Sweden's main naval base and home to its submarine and surface naval shipbuilding, where hull welds, pressure-hull structures and high-strength steels demand demanding UT, PAUT, MT and RT work. Skåne in the far south adds food, packaging and engineering manufacturing, the Öresund ports and offshore wind activity in the southern Baltic.

Practical NDT by region in Sweden

Atlantis does not yet have separate Practical NDT city pages in Sweden, so this hub covers the main work centres directly. The table maps each to the environments and methods in the simulator that fit its everyday jobs.

City or regionMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise
Luleå, Boden and NorrbottenIron ore, primary steel, new fossil-free steel projects, hydropower, portsWelding Workshop, NDT Lab, Storage Tank; UT, PAUT, MT, VT, RT
Bergslagen (Borlänge, Sandviken, Hofors, Avesta)Special steel, tubes, bearings, stainless, forgingsNDT Lab, Welding Workshop; UT, ET, PMI, MT, PT
Forsmark, Oskarshamn, RinghalsNuclear power outages and plant maintenanceNDT Lab, Oil & Gas Site; UT, PAUT, TOFD, ET, VT
Lysekil, Gothenburg, StenungsundRefining, petrochemicals, port terminals, tank farmsOil & Gas Site, Storage Tank; IRIS, PMI, PAUT, TOFD, MFL, LRUT
Gothenburg and TrollhättanAutomotive, bearings, aero-engine componentsAircraft Hangar, NDT Lab; ET, PT, UT, RT
Stockholm, Södertälje, Västerås, LinköpingTrucks and engines, power engineering, combat aircraft, CHP plantsAircraft Hangar, NDT Lab, Oil & Gas Site; ET, UT, PT, IRIS
Karlskrona and the southNaval shipbuilding, ports, engineering, southern Baltic offshore windWelding Workshop; PAUT, TOFD, UT, MT, RT

Norrbotten. New steel and hydrogen plants mean a long construction phase with structural steel, process piping, pressure equipment and large tanks, alongside maintenance on existing blast furnace, coke and pellet plant equipment. Weld inspection dominates construction, so RT interpretation, PAUT sizing and MT on fillet welds are the skills to keep current. The Welding Workshop and NDT Lab are the natural starting points, and the Storage Tank environment fits tank construction and in-service surveys. Cold, distance and rotational schedules make a browser-based tool especially practical.

Bergslagen. Mill technicians spend most of their time on automated lines, but the decisions that matter often come down to a manual UT check, an eddy current indication on a tube or a PMI reading on a mixed-up bundle. NDT Lab jobs on reference blocks and bench specimens rehearse calibration, sensitivity setting and manual sizing; ET jobs build tube inspection habits; PMI jobs reinforce alloy verification discipline.

The nuclear sites. Outage work rewards precision and strict procedure. The simulator does not replace the qualified procedures and equipment used in Swedish plants, but it gives technicians a place to rehearse UT and PAUT setups, TOFD on pressure welds, eddy current tube work and visual examination before a demanding outage window, and gives team leads an objective view of readiness.

The west coast. Refinery and petrochemical crews benefit most from the Oil & Gas Site environment, where IRIS on exchanger tubes, PMI on alloy circuits, PAUT corrosion mapping, TOFD on vessel welds and LRUT guided-wave screening all appear. Tank terminals in Gothenburg and Lysekil map to the Storage Tank environment's shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening.

Gothenburg and Trollhättan. Automotive and bearing manufacturing lean on eddy current, UT and surface methods on high-volume parts, while aero-engine work brings penetrant inspection, eddy current and radiography under aerospace procedures. The Aircraft Hangar environment and the NDT Lab cover the fundamentals that both share.

The east. Linköping's aerospace work maps to the Aircraft Hangar environment, while the many CHP and district heating plants around Stockholm, Västerås and Uppsala bring boiler tube thickness surveys, IRIS on heat exchanger tubes and weld inspection on pressure piping. Truck and engine plants add manufacturing UT and ET.

Karlskrona and the south. Naval shipbuilding asks for consistent weld inspection on thick, high-strength steel, so PAUT, TOFD and RT interpretation in the Welding Workshop are the core. Offshore wind and port work in the southern Baltic add structural weld and corrosion jobs.

Environments and methods that match Swedish work

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five workplace environments, twelve methods and 33 guided lessons. In Sweden the most used will be the NDT Lab for mill and nuclear fundamentals, the Welding Workshop for construction and shipbuilding, the Oil & Gas Site for refining, petrochemicals and energy plants, the Aircraft Hangar for aerospace and engine work, and the Storage Tank for terminals and tank construction.

NDT Lab (52 jobs). Bench specimens and reference blocks build the fundamentals: calibration, probe handling, sensitivity, scan coverage and indication recognition. It suits new trainees from Swedish vocational and upper-secondary technical programmes, mill technicians who want manual practice, and anyone preparing for a practical examination under any scheme.

Welding Workshop (52 jobs). Weld coupons and fabrication joints support RT film and digital image interpretation, UT and PAUT flaw detection and sizing, TOFD, MT and VT against acceptance criteria. This fits Norrbotten construction, naval shipbuilding, pressure-equipment fabrication and the many structural and bridge fabricators across the country.

Oil & Gas Site (73 jobs). The largest environment covers weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant. For Sweden it maps to the west coast refineries and petrochemical cluster, but also to CHP plants, pulp mill recovery boilers and chemical plants, which share the same equipment types: piping, vessels, exchangers and boilers. IRIS internal rotary UT on exchanger and boiler tubes, PMI alloy verification, LRUT guided-wave screening, PAUT corrosion mapping and TOFD are all here.

Aircraft Hangar (54 jobs). Airframe and component inspection with eddy current, penetrant and UT. It serves Linköping and Trollhättan aerospace work, airline and business aviation maintenance at Arlanda, Landvetter and other airports, and military aviation maintenance.

Storage Tank. UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank. Port terminals, refinery tank farms, pulp mill chemical storage and new tank construction in the north all generate this work.

Across the twelve methods, surface methods (PT, MT, VT) cover structural and finished-part work; volumetric methods (UT contact, PAUT, TOFD, RT) carry weld and corrosion assessment; electromagnetic methods (ET, MFL) serve tubes, aerospace and tank floors; and the specialist techniques (LRUT, IRIS, PMI) match what refinery, energy and special steel quality programmes ask for.

Regulators and requirements Swedish technicians meet

Short answer: Swedish NDT personnel are normally certified to EN ISO 9712, industrial radiography is regulated by the Swedish Radiation Safety Authority, pressure equipment in use falls under the Swedish Work Environment Authority, and nuclear plant NDT has its own qualification regime. Practical NDT is a practice tool that is useful under any of these frameworks and replaces none of them.

Personnel certification. Sweden applies SS-EN ISO 9712, the Swedish adoption of the international standard for qualification and certification of NDT personnel. Much Nordic certification is issued under the Nordtest scheme, which runs across the Nordic countries through several certifying bodies, and other accredited certification bodies also operate. Employers working for US-owned plants, US OEMs or on US-code projects sometimes keep a written practice based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A as well. That is market context only. Atlantis training aligns with ASNT SNT-TC-1A only; Atlantis does not train toward, certify or administer EN ISO 9712 or Nordtest certification, and Practical NDT is practice for whichever scheme you work under.

Radiation safety. The Swedish Radiation Safety Authority (Strålsäkerhetsmyndigheten, SSM) regulates ionising radiation, and industrial radiography is covered by its regulations SSMFS 2018:6 on industrial radiography, alongside SSM's general rules for licensed radiation activities. Employers carrying out radiography need the appropriate authorisation and must meet SSM's requirements on competence, controlled areas and dose. Practical NDT's RT jobs involve no radiation source and do not count toward any radiation protection training or authorisation.

Pressure equipment. New pressure equipment is placed on the market under the Pressure Equipment Directive 2014/68/EU. Equipment in use is covered by the Swedish Work Environment Authority (Arbetsmiljöverket). Since 1 January 2025 its rules on the use and inspection of pressure equipment sit in AFS 2023:11, which replaced the earlier AFS 2017:3 provisions, with requirements such as classification, documented risk assessment and inspection by accredited inspection bodies. Confirm the current provisions with Arbetsmiljöverket or your inspection body before relying on any detail.

Nuclear NDT qualification. SSM requires that NDT of reactor components and connected piping in Swedish nuclear plants is qualified. Qualification of NDT systems, meaning procedure, equipment and personnel, is carried out by an independent qualification body; the Swedish Qualification Centre (SQC) has performed this role since the 1990s. A simulator does not qualify anything, but it can help technicians rehearse before demanding qualified work.

Codes and standards in daily use. Swedish fabrication and in-service work commonly references EN and ISO standards for weld examination and acceptance (for example the EN ISO 17635 family and its method-specific standards), EN 13445 for unfired pressure vessels and EN 13480 for industrial piping, along with ASME and API codes where the owner or licensor requires them. Mentioned as context only.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Sweden

Practical NDT adapts to three kinds of user, and each has a distinct problem in Sweden.

New trainees. Many Swedish trainees come into NDT from welding, industrial or technical programmes, or move across from mill operations. The hardest thing to get early on is enough time on equipment and specimens. Guided fundamentals in the NDT Lab let a trainee repeat calibration, angle-beam setup, scan coverage and indication interpretation as often as needed, with instant feedback, so the first time on a real block is not the first attempt. It is also useful NDT practical exam preparation, provided everyone understands that the real exam is still taken on real specimens.

Working technicians. Swedish work is lumpy. Nuclear outages, refinery turnarounds and pulp mill shutdowns come in blocks, often in spring and summer, and a construction season in the north can pull technicians away from their usual methods for months. A technician who has been on tank floors may be asked to run IRIS on an exchanger bundle or PAUT on a nozzle weld. Rare-defect refreshers between assignments, on stress corrosion cracking, lack of fusion, tube pitting, hydrogen damage and similar, help them arrive ready instead of relearning on the client's equipment.

Level IIIs and team leads. Level IIIs can build and assign scenario sets, benchmark crews objectively and find coverage gaps before a campaign. When an outage or turnaround brings in contract technicians from other Nordic countries and further afield, a consistent scenario set gives a like-for-like view of who is ready for which method. It also helps check whether a new procedure is understood before it goes to the field.

Practice vs certification

Practical NDT is a practice and readiness tool. It is not a certification, it does not grant a level under EN ISO 9712, the Nordtest scheme, ASNT SNT-TC-1A or any employer's written practice, and it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens those schemes require. It does not qualify procedures or personnel for Swedish nuclear work and does not satisfy any SSM requirement for radiography. What it adds is realistic repetition: more chances to set up, scan, interpret and get feedback than a lab schedule or a specimen cupboard allows. It complements formal NDT training and on-the-job experience; the formal practical exam remains the step that counts.

Distance, seasons and shift work: why virtual NDT training suits Sweden

Direct answer: Sweden's long distances, dark winters, shift-based mills and concentrated outage seasons make it hard to keep a hands-on practice routine, and a browser-based ultrasonic testing simulator and phased array simulator remove most of that friction.

Sweden stretches well over a thousand kilometres from Skåne to the northern ore fields, and many inspection firms cover large territories from a handful of bases. A shop that wants its people to rehearse a PAUT setup or an RT interpretation before a job has to line up a free lab, a qualified supervisor and the right specimens at the same time. Smaller employers often do not own flawed specimens covering rare defect types at all. Mill technicians work rotating shifts that rarely coincide with a supervisor's free afternoon. And the outage and shutdown calendar means that the moment practice is most needed is also the moment everyone is busiest.

With the simulator, technicians can practise at home, in the shop office between jobs or during quiet hours on shift, subject to the site's IT rules. Supervisors can see scores rather than relying on self-reported confidence. Scenario sets built by a Level III can be pushed to a whole crew before an outage or turnaround starts, so the first morning on site is not spent discovering who is rusty. None of this replaces time on real equipment, but it makes real time more productive. Many Swedish technicians work comfortably in English, and the simulator's jobs and feedback are presented in English.

Who in Sweden typically looks at Practical NDT

The groups that tend to find a simulator useful in Sweden are inspection service companies that staff outages, turnarounds and construction projects; special steel and tube mills with in-house NDT departments; manufacturers of trucks, engines, bearings and aerospace parts with internal quality teams; fabricators of pressure equipment, structures and ships; vocational and technical education providers who want more practice time for students; and individual technicians preparing for an examination or a return to a method they have not used for a while. These are industry descriptions, not a customer list; Atlantis does not name customers on this page.

For employers who work to US codes or for US-owned plants and OEMs, Atlantis also offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A aligned NDT training delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility, and Level III consulting on procedures, techniques and written practices. The Atlantis ERP can record EN ISO 9712 and Nordtest certificates alongside ASNT-based ones for companies that manage mixed crews.

Bring Practical NDT to your Swedish team

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience. The scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who also leads Atlantis training. Rollout is straightforward. It starts with a short online demo, then a conversation about your work, whether that is an outage crew for a nuclear site, a west coast refinery turnaround team, a special steel mill NDT department, an aerospace quality group or a construction inspection crew in Norrbotten. Together we choose the environments and methods that match your jobs, and technicians get access by browser or app wherever they are. There is no physical centre to visit; everything is delivered online.

Pricing is quote on request, and the offer is built to be affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Book a Sweden Practical NDT demo, read the Practical NDT overview, or write to info@atlantisndt.com.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in Sweden?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app, so it works anywhere in Sweden with a connection, from Malmö to Kiruna. There is no physical centre to visit.

Does Practical NDT count toward EN ISO 9712 or Nordtest certification?

No. It is practice only. Certification under EN ISO 9712, whether through the Nordtest scheme or another accredited body, needs its own training, experience and examinations, including a practical exam on real specimens. The simulator helps you prepare.

Can it help with NDT practical exam preparation?

It can help build familiarity, speed and confidence with setups, scanning and interpretation before a practical exam. It does not replace the exam or the hours of experience your scheme or employer requires.

Is it useful for nuclear outage work in Sweden?

For rehearsal, yes: UT, PAUT, TOFD, eddy current and visual skills can be practised before an outage. It does not qualify procedures or personnel, which in Swedish nuclear plants is done through SSM's qualification regime and an independent qualification body.

Does it include radiography?

Yes, as technique and image interpretation practice with no radiation source. It does not count toward SSM requirements for industrial radiography.

Which Swedish industries is it most useful for?

Special steel and tube mills, primary steel and mining in the north, nuclear power, refining and petrochemicals on the west coast, CHP and pulp mill boilers, automotive and bearing manufacturing, aerospace, naval shipbuilding and structural fabrication.

Is there an ultrasonic testing simulator or phased array simulator in it?

Yes. Contact UT, PAUT and TOFD jobs appear across the NDT Lab, Welding Workshop and Oil & Gas Site environments, with UT thickness surveys in the Storage Tank environment and IRIS on tubes.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: guided fundamentals for new trainees, rare-defect refreshers for working technicians, and scenario building and crew benchmarking for Level IIIs and team leads.

Is the simulator in Swedish?

The simulator's jobs and feedback are in English. Ask during the demo if language support matters for your team.

Does Atlantis offer ASNT training in Sweden?

Atlantis training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A and is delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility. It suits employers working to US codes or for US clients. It is not EN ISO 9712 training. See NDT training.

How do we start?

Request a demo. We will map the environments and methods to your Swedish work and provide a quote on request.

contentHtml:
HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Simulator & Practical NDT Training in Tasmania

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and Tasmania shows clearly why a portal beats a lab for many inspection teams. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator is an immersive, 3D, game-like platform that runs in a browser or app. A technician opens a job in a virtual NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site or full-size storage tank, sets up the technique, carries out the inspection and gets a score when the job closes. Tasmania's inspection work is shaped by water, metal and the sea: a state-wide hydro-electric system of dams, tunnels, penstocks and power stations; the Bell Bay aluminium smelter on the Tamar; the zinc works on the Derwent at Hobart; mines on the West Coast; aluminium shipbuilding at Hobart; and ports at Burnie, Devonport, Bell Bay and Hobart serving Bass Strait shipping and Antarctic operations. The workforce is small and spread across an island, and specimen-based practice is hard to arrange. Practical NDT lets trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs build and keep skills without travelling to the mainland.

This is the Tasmania hub. It covers where the state's NDT work is, which simulator environments match it, how practice relates to AINDT certification and Tasmanian radiation licensing, and how to request a demo. Practical NDT is practice; it is not certification and never replaces a practical examination on real specimens.

Tasmania's NDT workforce and where the work is

Short answer: Tasmanian NDT work concentrates in four places: the hydro-electric system across the Central Highlands and West Coast; the Tamar Valley and Bell Bay industrial zone in the north; Hobart's zinc works, shipyards and port in the south; and the North West coast's ports, paper, cement and mining links around Burnie and Devonport.

The hydro system. Tasmania generates most of its electricity from hydro power, through a network of dams, canals, tunnels, penstocks and power stations operated by the state-owned Hydro Tasmania. Assets range from the Gordon Dam in the south-west to the Poatina and Tarraleah stations in the Central Highlands and the stations of the West Coast schemes. Many components are decades old, and refurbishment and redevelopment are continuing. Penstocks need weld and thickness inspection, turbine runners and shafts need surface and ultrasonic inspection for fatigue cracking, and gates, valves and steel structures need corrosion and weld surveys. The Basslink cable and the planned Marinus Link interconnector to Victoria add converter station and transmission work.

Bell Bay and the Tamar. The Bell Bay aluminium smelter at George Town is one of the state's largest industrial employers, and in October 2026 a federal and state support package and power deal were announced to keep it operating through to the end of 2031. Smelters need structural and crane inspection, potline and busbar maintenance, and weld inspection on repairs. The neighbouring manganese alloy smelter closed in July 2026 after administration, and the future of that site is unresolved. Bell Bay also has a gas-fired power station, the port and a range of fabrication and engineering shops serving the zone.

Hobart and the Derwent. The zinc works at Lutana on the Derwent is a long-running electrolytic zinc refinery, supported by government funding through 2026 while its owner studies diversification into other metals. It needs inspection of tanks, piping, acid plant equipment and structures in a corrosive environment. Hobart is also home to a builder of large aluminium catamaran ferries, including battery-electric vessels for overseas operators, which makes aluminium weld inspection a local speciality. The port is the base for Australia's Antarctic programme and its icebreaker, alongside fishing, cruise and naval visits.

The North West and West Coast. Burnie and Devonport are the main Bass Strait ports, with the Spirit of Tasmania ferries at Devonport and bulk and container trade at Burnie. Inland, the West Coast has a long mining history, with iron ore at Savage River piped as slurry to the Port Latta pellet plant, and zinc-lead mining at Rosebery. Pulp and paper, cement and food processing add pressure vessels, boilers, dryers and tanks that need routine in-service inspection.

Gas and energy. The Tasmanian Gas Pipeline brings gas from Victoria under Bass Strait to the north of the state and on to Hobart, feeding industry and the Tamar Valley power station. Wind farms in the north-west and on the Central Plateau, and proposed renewable hydrogen projects at Bell Bay, extend the energy work.

Practical NDT by city and region in Tasmania

Short answer: Tasmania has no city-level Practical NDT or Atlantis training page yet, so this hub covers the whole island. The table maps each region to the simulator environments and methods that suit its work.

City or regionMain local sectorsEnvironments & methods to practise
Hobart and the DerwentZinc refining, aluminium ship and ferry building, port, Antarctic logisticsWelding Workshop, Storage Tank, NDT Lab; UT, PAUT, PT, ET, VT
Launceston, George Town and Bell BayAluminium smelting, gas power, port, fabricationOil & Gas Site, Welding Workshop; UT, MT, PMI, IRIS, VT
Burnie and DevonportBass Strait ports, ferries, paper, cement, food processingWelding Workshop, Storage Tank, NDT Lab; UT, MT, MFL, PT
Central Highlands and West Coast hydroDams, penstocks, turbines, transmissionWelding Workshop, NDT Lab; UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT, PT
West Coast mining (Rosebery, Savage River, Port Latta)Zinc-lead and iron ore mining, pellet plant, slurry pipelineWelding Workshop, Oil & Gas Site; UT, MT, LRUT, VT

Hobart. Southern Tasmania's inspection work combines heavy process plant at the zinc works with marine and shipbuilding work. Aluminium hulls bring weld inspection with penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic methods suited to non-ferrous material, while the refinery needs tank, piping and structural surveys in an acidic, corrosive environment. Hobart technicians can practise surface and ultrasonic methods in the Welding Workshop and NDT Lab and tank surveys in the Storage Tank environment.

Launceston and Bell Bay. The Tamar Valley's smelters, power station and port make the north the state's heaviest industrial zone. Shutdown work mixes structural weld inspection, crane and lifting equipment inspection, exchanger work at the power station and alloy checks on replacement parts. Oil & Gas Site jobs with IRIS and PMI and Welding Workshop jobs with UT and MT fit this mix.

Burnie and Devonport. Ports, ferries and the North West's processing industries bring a steady stream of pressure vessel, tank and structural inspection. MFL and UT tank surveys, MT on structural welds and PT on components are core methods, practised in the Storage Tank and Welding Workshop environments.

The hydro system. Penstock and turbine inspection requires careful ultrasonic and magnetic particle work on thick welds and highly stressed components. PAUT and TOFD in the Welding Workshop, plus MT and PT, match the techniques used on refurbishment projects.

West Coast mining. Mills, crushers, conveyors, thickeners and the slurry pipeline need structural, wear and corrosion inspection, often in wet, cold and remote conditions. Practice between site visits keeps technicians ready for intensive shutdowns.

Environments and methods that match Tasmanian work

Short answer: the Welding Workshop fits hydro refurbishment, shipbuilding and structural work; the Oil & Gas Site and Storage Tank fit the smelters, zinc works, gas power and ports; the Aircraft Hangar covers ET and PT on high-value components; and the NDT Lab is the starting point.

The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator has five environments. The NDT Lab has bench specimens and reference blocks. The Welding Workshop has weld coupons and fabrication joints. The Aircraft Hangar covers airframe and component inspection. The Oil & Gas Site provides weld, corrosion, tube and screening practice in a process plant. The Storage Tank environment covers UT shell thickness surveys and MFL floor screening on a full-size tank.

There are twelve methods: PT, MT and VT (surface); UT contact, PAUT, TOFD and RT (volumetric); ET and MFL (electromagnetic); and LRUT guided-wave screening, IRIS internal rotary UT on heat exchanger and boiler tubes, and PMI alloy verification. The product includes 33 guided lessons, with 52 NDT Lab jobs, 52 Welding Workshop jobs, 54 Aircraft Hangar jobs and 73 Oil & Gas Site jobs.

Tasmania's mapping is distinctive. Hydro refurbishment calls for volumetric inspection of thick penstock welds and surface crack detection on turbine components, so PAUT, TOFD, UT, MT and PT are the priority. Aluminium fabrication for ferries and marine structures cannot use MT, so PT, ET and UT become central; the Aircraft Hangar environment's eddy current and penetrant jobs on non-ferrous components are useful practice for that, alongside Welding Workshop jobs. Smelting and refining need tank and piping surveys, IRIS on exchangers, PMI on alloy replacements and structural weld inspection. Ports and processing need tank floor screening with MFL, shell thickness surveys and pressure vessel inspection.

That breadth is why a Tasmanian technician benefits from a full library. In a small market, the same person may inspect a penstock in one month, a zinc works tank the next and a ferry hull after that.

Regulators and requirements Tasmanian technicians meet

Short answer: industrial radiography in Tasmania is licensed by the Department of Health under the Radiation Protection Act 2005; plant and pressure equipment come under WorkSafe Tasmania and the state's work health and safety laws; and most NDT personnel are certified through AINDT, whose scheme is based on ISO 9712.

Radiation. Anyone who deals with a radiation source in Tasmania, including using, possessing, storing or transporting it, needs a licence under the Radiation Protection Act 2005, administered by the Department of Health's Radiation Protection Unit. The Department's published guidance for industrial radiographers expects AINDT Level 2 or PCN certification in radiography, or an equivalent, together with a recognised course in radiation safety for industrial radiography. Simulator RT practice involves no radiation and is outside this regime; it is no substitute for the licence or the safety course.

Plant and pressure equipment. Tasmania applies the national model work health and safety laws through WorkSafe Tasmania. Boilers and pressure vessels are plant, with design and item registration for certain hazard levels. In-service inspection is commonly done to AS/NZS 3788, with design and fabrication to AS 1210, AS 4037, AS 4041 and AS/NZS 1554, and to AS/NZS 1665 for aluminium structures. Dams follow Tasmanian dam safety regulation and national guidelines. Confirm current requirements with the relevant regulator for any item.

Gas and pipelines. Gas transmission pipelines are designed and operated to AS 2885 under Tasmanian gas safety and pipeline legislation. Confirm the current regulator with the Tasmanian Government for specific work.

Marine. Commercial vessels are surveyed under national marine safety law and classification-society rules, which carry their own NDT and inspector requirements.

Certification. AINDT certification, aligned with ISO 9712, is the normal Australian scheme, and PCN is also referenced in Tasmanian radiation guidance. Some employers working on US-code equipment or for US clients use ASNT SNT-TC-1A, where the employer's written practice controls certification. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only and does not train toward or administer AINDT, PCN or ISO 9712 certification. The simulator is practice for any scheme.

For trainees, working technicians and Level IIIs in Tasmania

Short answer: trainees use guided lessons to learn fundamentals locally; working technicians keep a wide range of methods fresh; Level IIIs build scenario sets and benchmark small crews objectively.

Trainees. Tasmanian trainees often have to travel to the mainland for formal NDT courses and practical work on specimens. The 33 guided lessons give them a solid start at home: probe choice, calibration, scanning patterns, indication recognition and recording. When they do sit in a mainland course or start real work, they spend less time on basics.

Working technicians. A small market means generalists. A technician who covers hydro, smelter, port and marine work cannot practise every method every week, and rare flaw types may appear only once in years. Short scored jobs on rarely used methods and defects keep the whole range current.

Level IIIs and team leads. With few senior people on the island, a Level III's time is precious. A scenario set assigned to a whole crew shows quickly where the gaps are and who is ready for which job, without the Level III supervising every practice session. The same set can screen new hires or prepare a crew for a hydro outage or smelter shutdown.

Why simulator practice suits Tasmania

Short answer: an island workforce, mainland-based training facilities and a wide spread of asset types make specimen-based practice hard to arrange. A browser-based simulator removes the travel and the specimen shortage.

Crossing Bass Strait for practice costs time and money, and reference specimens with realistic flaws are scarce and expensive to keep locally. Within Tasmania, the drive from Hobart to the West Coast mines or the north-west ports takes hours on winding roads. A browser simulator puts the same practice library in front of a technician in Hobart, Launceston, Burnie or Queenstown.

Tasmania's major assets also run on long cycles. Hydro outages, smelter shutdowns and ship construction milestones come at planned intervals, and crews need to be ready at the right moment. Scored practice in the weeks before an outage means people arrive confident in the methods the scope demands.

Simulator work is safe: no radiation, no confined spaces in penstocks or tanks, no work at height on smelter structures. Mistakes cost points, not reinspection or harm.

Real field experience remains essential. The simulator makes the time spent on real assets more productive.

Practice vs certification

Short answer: Practical NDT does not grant certification, is not an AINDT, PCN or ISO 9712 examination, and does not replace the practical examination on real specimens required by an employer's written practice under ASNT SNT-TC-1A.

All recognised NDT certification combines training, documented experience and examinations, including a practical exam on real specimens. AINDT's examinations are run under its ISO 9712 based scheme; under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer's written practice sets the rules and the employer certifies. Simulator scores are not examination results.

The simulator helps candidates arrive prepared. Repetition builds the habits that exams and real jobs test, and a Level III can use the results to judge readiness. For radiography, the Department of Health licence and radiation safety training remain separate legal requirements.

Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, delivered online, live-virtual or onsite at the client's facility; see Atlantis NDT training and ASNT training in Australia. Atlantis has no training centre in Tasmania.

Bring Practical NDT to your Tasmanian team

Short answer: request a demo, tell us which Tasmanian assets and methods your team covers, and we will show the matching environments and agree a pilot. Pricing is quote on request.

Atlantis built the first-ever online practical NDT simulation portal for practice and hands-on experience, and its scenario library was designed by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. It is affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Inspection contractors, maintenance teams at power, smelting and processing sites, shipyard quality teams and training providers can use it as supplied or ask for scenario sets aligned to their procedures.

A short call establishes your work, whether hydro refurbishment, smelter maintenance, aluminium fabrication or port and plant inspection. We demonstrate the relevant environments, agree a pilot group and set up accounts. Team leads see results to track progress. Nothing is installed on site.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an NDT simulator I can use in Tasmania?

Yes. The Atlantis Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser or app anywhere in Tasmania with a connection, from Hobart and Launceston to Burnie and the West Coast. There is no Tasmanian centre to visit; demos are arranged through the contact form.

Can I practise NDT in Tasmania without travelling to the mainland?

For practice, yes. The guided lessons and job library run online. Formal certification courses and practical examinations on real specimens may still require travel, depending on the scheme and provider.

Does Practical NDT count towards AINDT certification?

No. It is practice only. AINDT certification follows its own training, experience and examination rules, and Atlantis does not provide AINDT, PCN or ISO 9712 training.

Is it useful for hydro penstock and turbine inspection?

It is relevant practice. Welding Workshop and NDT Lab jobs cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT and PT on welds and components of the kind found in penstocks and turbines. Asset owners' procedures and qualification rules still govern real work.

Does it help with aluminium weld inspection?

It covers PT, ET and UT, the methods typically used on non-ferrous welds and components, through the Welding Workshop and Aircraft Hangar environments.

Does simulator radiography need a Tasmanian licence?

No radiation is involved, so no licence is needed for practice. Real radiography requires a licence under the Radiation Protection Act 2005.

What experience level is it for?

All levels: trainees on guided lessons, working technicians refreshing rare defects and less-used methods, and Level IIIs building scenario sets.

Can a Tasmanian company use it to assess new hires?

Yes. A Level III can assign the same scenario set to every candidate and compare scores objectively.
