Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepStainless and alloy piping, valves, pumps, machined componentsEmployer requirements only
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual on US-code fabrication, in-service pressure equipment, tanksEmployer requirements only
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepHeat exchanger tubing in refineries and gas plants, aircraft and helicopter maintenanceEmployer requirements only

For Level III, the ASNT Level III training programme prepares candidates for the Basic and method examinations online, so Alberta candidates do not have to travel. If your target is a CGSB Level 3, you need a CGSB-specific route. We will tell you so rather than sell you the wrong course.

NDT training by city in Alberta

Direct answer: Atlantis has dedicated NDT training pages for Calgary, Edmonton and Fort McMurray, plus Practical NDT simulator pages for Red Deer and Lethbridge. Every Alberta city is served the same way: live online classes plus onsite delivery at the employer's site. We have no classroom in any Alberta city.

Calgary. Calgary employers usually need engineers and coordinators who understand NDT as much as they need field technicians. Integrity engineers, QA/QC leads and procurement staff who specify NDT for pipeline and facility projects often take Level II theory or Level III preparation to read procedures and reports with confidence. Field crews working out of Calgary on US-bound projects take UT, RT and MT Level II under their employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice.

Edmonton. Edmonton has more NDT technicians than anywhere else in the province. It is also where the split between CGSB and SNT-TC-1A is most visible. Module fabricators and pressure-equipment shops building ASME-stamped equipment for US sites often run an SNT-TC-1A written practice beside their CGSB-certified staff. We train crews onsite in the shop, so nobody loses a shift to travel.

Fort McMurray. Oil sands contractors plan training around turnaround schedules and rotations. The usual pattern is online theory completed during days off, followed by a short onsite practical block at the contractor's yard or the owner's site before the turnaround starts.

Red Deer and Lethbridge. Smaller employers in central and southern Alberta tend to need one or two Level II technicians, refresher training or a written practice rewrite rather than a large cohort. Live online seats plus the Practical NDT simulator suit them well.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Alberta, step by step

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. You complete classroom training and documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you to its written practice. Certification is tied to that employer and is not a Canadian national certificate.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A. It sets training hours, experience hours, exam rules and recertification intervals. If your Alberta company does not have one, we can write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Take the formal training hours your written practice requires for the method and level, live online or onsite. The training requirements matrix lists the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience. Log supervised hours in the method on real work: refinery piping, pipeline welds, shop fabrication. Your employer keeps the records.
  4. Examinations. Sit the general (theory), specific (procedures, codes and equipment your employer uses) and practical (real specimens) examinations, administered under a Level III.
  5. Vision examination. Pass near-vision and colour contrast checks, repeated annually under most written practices.
  6. Certification. Your employer's Level III recommends you and the employer certifies you for the method and level. If you change employers, the new employer must review and recertify you under its own written practice.
  7. Recertification. Recertify at the interval in your written practice, usually by exam or documented continued work. Annual vision checks continue.

If you also need CGSB certification, keep your experience logs in a format that satisfies both schemes. The certification body sets its own evidence requirements, so confirm them early.

Radiography licensing and other Alberta requirements

Direct answer: industrial gamma radiography in Alberta is regulated federally by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC). Operators must be CNSC-certified exposure device operators (EDOs) or work under the direct supervision of one. Pressure equipment falls under ABSA. Pipelines inside Alberta fall under the Alberta Energy Regulator, and interprovincial lines under the Canada Energy Regulator.

Industrial radiography

Canada does not have a US-style Agreement State system. The CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices across every province, including Alberta. To operate an exposure device you must hold CNSC exposure device operator certification or be directly supervised by a certified EDO. CNSC guidance requires candidates to complete formal EDO vocational training and a substantial supervised on-the-job programme before the CNSC written examination. CSA PCP-09 is the reference guide for certification. Atlantis RT training covers radiographic theory, technique, film and digital interpretation, and code acceptance criteria. It does not replace EDO certification, and we do not run the CNSC exam. X-ray equipment is not a nuclear substance, so it is regulated provincially under Alberta's radiation protection legislation. Your radiation safety officer will know the current registration and worker requirements.

Pressure equipment: ABSA

ABSA administers pressure equipment safety in Alberta under the Safety Codes Act and the Pressure Equipment Safety Regulation. ABSA documents set the rules for owner-user programmes, Integrity Assessment Organizations, quality management systems and repairs. AB-506 contains the NDE examiner certification rules summarised above. Code work commonly references ASME Section V for methods, ASME Section VIII and CSA B51 for vessels, and ASME B31.1 and B31.3 for piping.

Pipelines

The Alberta Energy Regulator regulates pipelines inside the province, with CSA Z662 as the core design, construction and integrity standard. Interprovincial and international lines fall under the Canada Energy Regulator. API 1104 still appears on many projects, especially those with US owners, US contractors or cross-border systems. CSA Z662 sets its own NDT personnel requirements, so check the project specification before relying on SNT-TC-1A alone.

Other things Alberta employers ask for

Alberta site access usually means safety prequalification through networks such as ISNetworld, Avetta or ComplyWorks. Industry safety tickets and a Certificate of Recognition (COR) programme for the employer are also common. Structural steel work under CSA W59 is done by CWB-certified companies whose NDT personnel are normally certified through CSA W178.1 and CGSB. Atlantis training does not replace any of these requirements. It sits beside them for the work where SNT-TC-1A applies.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Alberta

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers Alberta training three ways: live online classes for individual seats, live-virtual cohorts for one company's crew, and onsite delivery at your shop, plant or camp with a Level III instructor. Theory goes online. Practical sessions happen on real specimens at your site.

Alberta's geography and work patterns make this model practical. Rotational crews in Wood Buffalo can do theory on days off. Edmonton and Calgary shops can run evening or split-shift sessions without stopping production. Remote employers in the Peace Region or southern Alberta avoid travel altogether. We schedule around the realities of Alberta work: spring and fall turnaround seasons in the oil sands and the Heartland, winter pipeline construction, and summer maintenance shutdowns at gas plants and mills.

  • Live online seats: individuals join a scheduled class from anywhere in Alberta, with live instruction and questions answered by the instructor.
  • Private live-virtual cohort: your crew only, built around your procedures, codes and equipment.
  • Onsite at your facility: the instructor comes to your Edmonton shop, Fort McMurray yard or Calgary office, uses your equipment and specimens, and supports practical examinations under your written practice.
  • Blended: online theory, simulator practice and a short onsite practical block. This is the most popular option for rotational crews.

We have no classroom in Alberta and we do not suggest otherwise. Ask about onsite training for your Alberta crew, or see online NDT training and corporate NDT training.

For Alberta employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Alberta employers who need SNT-TC-1A certification for US-code work need a written practice, a Level III to administer examinations, and training and experience records an auditor can follow. Atlantis provides all three remotely or onsite. That includes shops that keep CGSB-certified staff for Canadian work and an SNT-TC-1A programme for US clients.

The most common Alberta request is not a single course. It is a programme. Typical examples are an Edmonton fabricator winning its first US ASME-stamped order, a Calgary-based contractor bidding on US pipeline work, or a US-owned operator that wants one written practice covering its Alberta and US sites. We can:

  • write or rewrite your SNT-TC-1A written practice, aligned with your ASME, API or client requirements (written practice development);
  • act as your outside Level III: prepare and grade general, specific and practical exams, review procedures and sign technique sheets;
  • map how your SNT-TC-1A programme and your CGSB-certified staff fit together, so certification records are clear on each job;
  • prepare for client, ABSA-related and third-party audits of your NDT programme;
  • keep certification, training and vision records in order. Our NDT ERP for Alberta inspection companies tracks CGSB and ASNT certifications side by side.

Read more on SNT-TC-1A training and certification for employers or our NDT consulting in Canada. Book a Level III consultation for your Alberta programme.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator lets Alberta trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments in a browser before they touch real specimens. It is practice only. It does not replace the hands-on practical examination your written practice requires, or the practical examination in a CGSB scheme.

The simulator includes an NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. Those environments match much of Alberta's work: piping and vessel welds, tank floors and shells, and plant equipment. Trainees on rotation can practise probe handling, scan planning and indication recognition between shifts. Supervisors can use it to check readiness before booking practical exam time. See Practical NDT or the Alberta page, Practical NDT in Alberta. Written practice questions are on the blog, for example the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop designs the course content, the examinations and the written practices we prepare for employers. He is also the Level III you speak with when you need to decide whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or both are right for your Alberta work.

NDT training in Alberta: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Alberta?

There are two routes. For most Canadian code work you need CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712) certification from an accredited certification body; confirm the current certification body, because arrangements changed in 2026. For US-code work, US clients or US employers you are certified by your employer under SNT-TC-1A after training, experience, exams and a vision test. Atlantis trains for the SNT-TC-1A route only.

Is there NDT training online in Alberta?

Yes. Atlantis runs live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes that Alberta technicians can join from Calgary, Edmonton, Fort McMurray or anywhere else. Practical training and exams take place on real specimens, usually at your employer's site. See NDT training online.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB or ISO 9712 training in Alberta?

No. Atlantis does not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or any ISO 9712 scheme and does not claim CGSB recognition. If CGSB certification is what your job needs, use a CGSB-route provider. We are happy to say so on the first call.

Does ABSA accept SNT-TC-1A certification?

In some in-service situations, yes. ABSA's AB-506 (Edition 4, issued 2025-10-21) permits SNT-TC-1A Level II for shear-wave UT if the owner accepts it, and CGSB or SNT Level I/II for contractor UT thickness, MT and PT on in-service equipment. Check the current edition and your owner's specification.

Do I need a licence to do radiography in Alberta?

For gamma radiography, yes. You must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator or work under the direct supervision of one, and your employer must hold a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment is regulated provincially. NDT training in RT does not by itself let you operate a source.

How much does NDT training cost in Alberta?

It is quoted on request. The price depends on the method and level, the number of trainees, live online versus onsite delivery, and whether you also need a written practice or Level III exam administration. Cohort and onsite quotes usually come back within one business day. Request an Alberta quote.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Alberta?

UT is the workhorse: thickness surveys, PAUT corrosion mapping and weld inspection across the oil sands, refineries and pipelines. RT stays important for pipeline and piping welds, and MT and PT are needed on almost every maintenance job. ET matters for heat exchangers and aviation.

Can you train our crew onsite in Edmonton, Calgary or Fort McMurray?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your shop, yard, plant or camp is our standard option for Alberta employers. The instructor works with your equipment and specimens and can support practical examinations under your written practice.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets the classroom and experience hours. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums, listed in our training requirements matrix. Experience hours usually take far longer than classroom hours. CGSB has its own separate requirements.

Can a US company use its SNT-TC-1A programme for its Alberta crew?

For work where the owner and the code accept SNT-TC-1A, yes. One written practice can cover Alberta and US sites. Where Alberta rules or the client require CGSB certification, those technicians also need CGSB certificates.

Can I become a Level III in Alberta?

Yes, by either route. ASNT Level III candidates prepare for the Basic and method exams; our Level III preparation runs online. A CGSB Level 3 follows the certification body's own requirements.

What do NDT technicians earn in Alberta?

Pay depends on method, level, certification scheme, rotation and overtime. We do not publish our own salary figures. For context, read the NDT salary guide.

Get a quote for NDT training in Alberta

You might need one Edmonton technician trained to UT Level II for a US order, a Fort McMurray turnaround crew refreshed before spring, or a written practice and outside Level III for a Calgary contractor bidding south of the border. Atlantis NDT will build the programme around your work, your codes and your rotation. We will also tell you plainly when CGSB is what you actually need. Request your Alberta training quote, read about Atlantis NDT training, or see NDT training across Canada. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

contentHtml:

NDT Training and Certification in Arizona

Short answer: an Arizona technician or employer gets ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual sessions, or onsite delivery at the employer's plant, hangar, mine, fab construction site or shop anywhere in Arizona. Courses cover Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III, and certification is issued by your employer under its written practice.

Arizona has no petroleum refinery, yet it is one of the most varied NDT markets in the West. Phoenix and Tucson are major aerospace and defence manufacturing centres, with engine, helicopter and missile production plus several Air Force bases and aircraft storage and maintenance yards. The largest nuclear generating station in the United States sits west of Phoenix. Southeastern Arizona produces most of the country's copper. And the semiconductor and battery plants now being built around Phoenix are some of the largest construction projects in the nation, with thousands of welds in high-purity and process piping. Each of these employers asks for different methods and a different style of written practice. This page explains how training and certification work for Arizona technicians and employers, what Arizona regulators require, and how to get a quote. Request an Arizona NDT training quote and we reply with options within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Arizona

Direct answer: Arizona NDT work clusters in five areas: metro Phoenix (aerospace engines and helicopters, semiconductor and battery plant construction, Luke Air Force Base, power), the Palo Verde nuclear station west of Phoenix, Tucson and southern Arizona (missiles, Davis-Monthan, aircraft storage and MRO), the Copper Triangle and other mining districts, and northern and western Arizona (rail, dams, pipelines and military test ranges).

Metro Phoenix: aerospace, defence and advanced manufacturing

Phoenix, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler and Glendale form one of the largest aerospace clusters in the Southwest. A major aerospace company designs and builds turbine engines, auxiliary power units and avionics in Phoenix and Tempe; attack helicopters are built in Mesa; and hundreds of machine shops, forging and casting houses, heat treaters and special-process suppliers support them. These suppliers live on PT, MT, ET and UT performed under tightly controlled written practices, and their customers' quality systems often reference NAS 410 alongside SNT-TC-1A. Luke Air Force Base in Glendale trains fighter pilots and supports aircraft maintenance, and Phoenix Sky Harbor, Phoenix-Mesa Gateway and Goodyear airports host airline and third-party maintenance, repair and aircraft storage work that uses ET, PT and UT on airframes, wheels and engines.

Semiconductor, battery and data-centre construction

North Phoenix and Chandler host some of the largest semiconductor fabrication campuses in the world, and battery, electric-vehicle and data-centre projects have spread across Pinal and Maricopa counties. These projects involve huge volumes of process, gas, chemical, ultra-pure water and cooling piping, structural steel and pressure equipment. Owners and mechanical contractors need VT inspectors, RT and UT technicians for piping welds to ASME B31.3, borescope and visual inspection of orbital welds, and MT and UT on structural steel to AWS D1.1. Demand rises and falls with each construction phase, so contractors often need to qualify inspectors quickly.

Palo Verde and the power sector

The Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station near Wintersburg, west of Phoenix, is the largest nuclear power station in the United States by generation. Refuelling outages bring in-service inspection to ASME Section XI, with UT, ET of steam-generator tubing and VT carried out by qualified personnel. Arizona utilities also operate gas-fired and remaining coal-fired plants, large solar and battery installations, and high-voltage transmission, all of which need boiler-tube, piping and structural inspection.

Tucson and southern Arizona

Tucson is home to one of the country's largest missile design and production operations, along with a wider defence and optics supply chain. Davis-Monthan Air Force Base hosts the military's aircraft storage and regeneration group, the famous desert boneyard, where aircraft and parts are preserved, inspected and returned to service. Pinal Airpark near Marana adds commercial aircraft storage, maintenance and teardown. All of this work relies on ET, PT, UT and RT on airframes and components. Fort Huachuca near Sierra Vista and the border ports of entry add defence and infrastructure work, and the copper mines south of Tucson connect the city to the mining sector.

The Copper Triangle and Arizona mining

Arizona produces most of the copper mined in the United States. Large open-pit mines and processing plants operate around Morenci, Safford, Bagdad, Globe-Miami, Hayden, Superior and south of Tucson, with smelters, concentrators, solvent extraction and electrowinning plants, leach pads and long slurry and water pipelines. Haul trucks, shovels, crushers, grinding mills, conveyors, pressure vessels and tanks need regular MT, UT, PT and VT on shafts, gears, welds and structural members. Mine maintenance teams increasingly want their own certified Level IIs so they can check critical components between contractor visits.

Northern and western Arizona: rail, dams, pipelines and test ranges

The BNSF transcontinental main line runs through Flagstaff, Winslow, Holbrook and Kingman, and the Union Pacific Sunset Route crosses the south of the state; both bring rail, car and bridge inspection. Glen Canyon Dam near Page and Hoover Dam on the Nevada border involve penstock, turbine and structural inspection. Interstate natural gas and refined-products pipelines enter from Texas, New Mexico and California to supply Phoenix and Tucson, and their construction and integrity programmes use RT, UT and VT. Yuma has a large Army proving ground and a Marine Corps air station, and the state's interstate bridges are inspected and maintained by the Arizona Department of Transportation.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Arizona employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table shows each method, the levels available, how Arizona employers typically use it, and what a trainee needs before starting. Your employer's written practice sets the exact hours and experience required.

MethodLevelsWhat Arizona employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepAerospace forgings and engine parts, mining shafts and gears, fab construction piping and steel, nuclear outage work, pipeline weldsLevel I: none beyond employer requirements. Level II: Level I training plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepPiping weld inspection on large construction projects, power plant welds, aerospace and structural componentsUT Level II recommended before PAUT
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepHeavy-wall vessels and piping in power and mining process plantsUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepProcess and gas piping on semiconductor and battery projects, pipelines, aerospace castings, power plant pipingRadiation safety training required under Arizona rules before handling sources; employer-specific
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepMining equipment, aerospace steel parts and landing gear, structural steel, rail componentsNone beyond employer requirements
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepTurbine engine and helicopter components, missile hardware, stainless and aluminium weldsNone beyond employer requirements
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepOrbital and process piping welds on fab construction, structural steel, pressure equipment, nuclear outagesVision test per written practice
Electromagnetic Testing (ET)I, II, III prepAirframes, wheels and bolt holes at MRO and storage sites, aerospace surface inspection, heat-exchanger and steam-generator tubingNone beyond employer requirements

Arizona employers often combine methods into a pathway. An aerospace supplier may certify a technician in PT and MT Level II first, then add ET. A mechanical contractor on a fab project may start new hires on VT, then add RT or UT as the project moves from structural steel to process piping. A mine maintenance department may want MT and UT Level II for its own staff. We plan those pathways around your written practice so classroom hours, exams and on-the-job experience line up. Level III candidates can see the ASNT Level III training and exam preparation page.

NDT training by city in Arizona

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT serves every Arizona city through online and onsite delivery. Phoenix and Tucson have Practical NDT simulator pages, and Phoenix has local method service pages; Mesa, Chandler, Glendale, Yuma, Flagstaff and the mining towns are covered by this hub. The table links each existing local page, and the paragraphs below explain which NDT work dominates in each city.

CityMain NDT sectorsPage
PhoenixAerospace engines, semiconductor construction, airport MRO, powerPhoenix practice / UT in Phoenix
TucsonMissiles and defence, aircraft storage and regeneration, miningTucson practice
Mesa and ChandlerHelicopter production, semiconductor fabs, aerospace suppliers, Gateway airport MROCovered by this page
Glendale and GoodyearAir Force base, aircraft storage and MRO, manufacturingCovered by this page
Buckeye and the West ValleyNuclear outages, power, distribution and constructionCovered by this page
Globe, Safford and MorenciCopper mining, smelting and processingCovered by this page
Yuma, Flagstaff and KingmanMilitary test ranges, rail, pipelines, manufacturingCovered by this page

Phoenix. Phoenix is Arizona's largest NDT labour market. Aerospace suppliers need PT, MT, ET and UT technicians under written practices that pass prime-contractor and customer audits. Mechanical contractors on semiconductor and battery projects need VT, RT and UT technicians who understand ASME B31.3. Utilities and airport maintenance operations add steady demand. See the Phoenix Practical NDT page and the radiographic testing in Phoenix service page.

Tucson. Missile and defence production, the Davis-Monthan aircraft storage group and commercial aircraft storage at Marana make Tucson an ET, PT, UT and RT city. Employers need documented certification that stands up to military and prime-contractor reviews. See the Tucson Practical NDT page.

Mesa and Chandler. Helicopter production, aerospace suppliers and semiconductor fabs sit side by side. Technicians who can move between aerospace PT and ET and construction VT and RT are especially valuable here.

Glendale and Goodyear. Air Force maintenance, aircraft storage and teardown, and West Valley manufacturing and distribution create demand for ET, PT and UT on aircraft and VT and MT on structural work.

Buckeye and the West Valley. Palo Verde outages draw qualified UT, ET and VT personnel, and the fast-growing industrial parks along I-10 add construction and fabrication inspection.

Globe, Safford and Morenci. Remote mining towns are hours from any classroom. Online theory with onsite practicals at the mine shop is usually the only realistic way to certify maintenance staff in MT and UT.

Yuma, Flagstaff and Kingman. Test ranges, rail lines, pipelines and manufacturing plants need small, well-documented teams in UT, MT, RT and VT.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Arizona, step by step

Direct answer: under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, certification in Arizona is employer-based. Your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. Arizona has no separate state NDT licence, but radiography is regulated by the state.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. Based on SNT-TC-1A, it sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks, vision requirements and recertification intervals for each method and level. If your company has none, we write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Take Level I and then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours per method and level.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience in the method at your Arizona workplace, logged and verified by your employer.
  4. Pass the general exam on the principles of the method.
  5. Pass the specific exam on the procedures, codes and equipment you actually use, for example ASME Section V, ASME B31.3, AWS D1.1 or your customer's aerospace specifications.
  6. Pass the practical exam on real specimens with real flaws, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Pass the vision exam for near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated at the interval in your written practice.
  8. Get certified by your employer. Certification is tied to that employer and based on documented training, experience and exams.
  9. Maintain and recertify at the interval in your written practice, and add methods or levels as your career develops.

For more detail on the employer-based system, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Arizona requirements

Direct answer: Arizona is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the Arizona Department of Health Services, Bureau of Radiation Control, which took over the work of the former Arizona Radiation Regulatory Agency. Boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Industrial Commission of Arizona; intrastate pipeline safety under the Arizona Corporation Commission's Office of Pipeline Safety.

Industrial radiography

Because Arizona is an Agreement State, the Bureau of Radiation Control rather than the NRC licenses most radioactive material used in the state. A company doing gamma radiography with iridium-192 or similar sources needs an Arizona radioactive materials licence, or must use reciprocity, which requires advance written notice to the Bureau before work starts, if it holds an NRC or other Agreement State licence. Industrial X-ray equipment is registered with the state. Radiographers and radiographer's assistants must meet the state's sealed-source industrial radiography requirements for training, examination, supervision and certification, which parallel the federal rules in 10 CFR Part 34. Federal installations in Arizona may have their own arrangements, so confirm with the site owner. RT method training under SNT-TC-1A, which is what Atlantis provides, covers technique, exposure, film and digital imaging and interpretation; it sits alongside, not instead of, the radiation safety training and radiographer certification Arizona requires. Always confirm current requirements with the Bureau before you deploy a crew.

Boilers and pressure vessels

Arizona's boiler and pressure vessel safety programme sits within the Industrial Commission of Arizona's occupational safety and health division. Arizona follows the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board inspection practice, so repairs and alterations need NDT performed to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme.

Pipelines

The Arizona Corporation Commission's Office of Pipeline Safety oversees intrastate pipeline operators in the state under its arrangement with PHMSA, which regulates interstate pipelines directly. Construction and integrity work commonly follows API 1104 for welding and inspection and ASME B31.8 or B31.4 for design, which keeps RT, UT and VT technicians in demand on transmission, distribution and products lines.

Nuclear

Palo Verde is licensed by the NRC, and its in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI. Personnel performing that work are qualified under the owner's and vendors' nuclear programmes, which generally go beyond basic SNT-TC-1A certification; SNT-TC-1A training is a common starting point for technicians moving toward nuclear work.

Codes Arizona employers commonly use

  • ASME B31.3 and Section V on semiconductor, battery and process plant construction
  • ASME Section XI at Palo Verde and ASME Section I and B31.1 at conventional power plants
  • API 1104 and ASME B31.8 on gas and products pipelines
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for ADOT bridge fabrication
  • NAS 410 and military specifications as context for aerospace and defence suppliers (Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A; your employer documents any additional aerospace requirements)

Some Arizona employers also ask for CWI or API inspector credentials for specific roles. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train; our programmes cover ASNT SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Arizona

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Arizona. Theory is delivered through live online or live-virtual classes, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility, using your equipment and specimens under ASNT Level III oversight. Arizona crews train without long desert drives and without losing shifts.

For individual technicians, online NDT training covers the classroom portion of Level I and Level II. You attend live sessions with a Level III instructor, ask questions in real time, and work through method principles, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation. Practical hours and the practical exam are then completed with your employer.

For employers training a group, onsite delivery is usually most efficient. We schedule classroom and practical sessions at your shop, hangar, mine or project site, use your instruments, reference standards and specimens, and build the course around your procedures. A Tempe aerospace supplier gets PT, MT and ET on its own parts; a Chandler mechanical contractor gets VT and RT on piping welds that match its project; a Morenci or Globe mine shop gets MT and UT on the components its team inspects.

Arizona's calendar is shaped by heat. Many outdoor projects and field inspections shift to early-morning shifts from late spring to early autumn, and some employers prefer to schedule classroom training in the hottest months. Palo Verde outages follow the station's refuelling cycle, construction projects follow their phases, and aerospace plants often have holiday shutdowns. We plan cohorts to finish before your busy window. Larger programmes run through corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Arizona crew.

For Arizona employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A makes the employer responsible for certification, so every Arizona NDT employer needs a written practice and access to a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams, and provides Level III services for companies without a Level III on staff.

Many Arizona NDT employers are small: a machine shop or special-process house in the aerospace supply chain, a mechanical contractor's QC team on a fab project, a mine maintenance department, an MRO shop at a regional airport. They need certified technicians but cannot justify a full-time Level III. That gap is where most audit findings come from: training records without hour counts, practical exams with no graded checklist, vision tests out of date, or a written practice copied from another company that does not match how work is actually done. Aerospace suppliers in particular face customer audits that check every certification record line by line.

  • Written practice development and revision aligned with the current edition of SNT-TC-1A and your customers' requirements. See written practice development.
  • Exam administration: general, specific and practical exams prepared and graded under Level III oversight, with records your auditors can follow.
  • Procedure review for UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET procedures against ASME, AWS, API and customer requirements.
  • Audit preparation for prime-contractor and customer audits, National Board or ASME reviews and ISO 9001 or AS9100 surveillance.
  • Corporate programmes for multi-site companies through corporate NDT training.

For broader Level III consulting, see our NDT consulting services and our guide to SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Arizona company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT simulator lets Arizona trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before their practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique, scan patterns and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Arizona, the aircraft hangar matches the Phoenix and Tucson aerospace and MRO sector, the welding workshop matches construction, mining and fabrication work, and the oil and gas site and tank cover pipelines and terminals. Trainees can repeat scans and explore indication types before handling real equipment in front of an examiner.

Local simulator pages are available for Phoenix and Tucson. For written-exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Direct answer: Arizona programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop leads course design, delivers Level III-led instruction, and oversees the exams and records that make certification defensible under SNT-TC-1A. His focus is practical: connecting method theory to the procedures, codes and parts your Arizona crew actually inspects, and helping employers build written practices that hold up in audits. Ask about his availability when you contact us about Arizona training.

NDT training in Arizona: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Arizona?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. Complete Level I and Level II classroom training in a method, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then issues certification under its written practice. If you are not yet employed, online classroom training prepares you, and certification follows once an employer documents your experience.

Is there NDT training online in Arizona?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online and live-virtual Level I and Level II classes that Arizona technicians can join from Phoenix, Tucson, Yuma, Flagstaff or a mining town. Practical training and practical exams are completed with your employer because they need real equipment and specimens.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Arizona?

Arizona is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the Arizona Department of Health Services, Bureau of Radiation Control. The company holds the licence, and individual radiographers and assistants must meet state training, exam, supervision and certification requirements equivalent to 10 CFR Part 34. Confirm current requirements with the Bureau before starting work.

How much does NDT training cost in Arizona?

Cost is quoted on request. It depends on the method and level, the number of trainees, whether sessions are live online or onsite, and whether you need exam administration or written practice support. Send your requirements and we return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Arizona?

PT, ET and UT lead in aerospace and MRO around Phoenix and Tucson. VT, RT and UT dominate semiconductor and battery plant construction. MT and UT are essential in copper mining, and UT and ET support nuclear and power outages.

Can you train our crew onsite in Phoenix, Tucson or at a mine site?

Yes. We deliver classroom and practical sessions at your facility anywhere in Arizona, using your equipment and specimens, and schedule around construction phases, outages and summer heat.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Arizona employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer certification in US industry, including aerospace suppliers, construction, power, mining and pipelines. Customer-specific requirements can be added to your written practice.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums; see the training requirements matrix. Experience hours usually take much longer than the classroom portion.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in Arizona?

Yes. Level III candidates normally have substantial Level II experience and prepare for the ASNT Level III basic and method exams. See ASNT Level III training for exam preparation options.

Do you offer CWI or API training in Arizona?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some Arizona construction and pipeline employers also ask for CWI or API credentials, but those are separate programmes.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Arizona?

No. We deliver training live online and onsite at your facility. There is no Atlantis classroom building in Phoenix, Tucson or elsewhere in Arizona.

What do NDT technicians earn in Arizona?

Pay varies with method, level, sector and travel. For published ranges by level, read our NDT salary guide.

Start NDT training in Arizona

Whether you are one technician in Tucson, an aerospace supplier in Tempe, a mechanical contractor on a Phoenix fab project or a mine maintenance team in the Copper Triangle, Atlantis NDT can build an ASNT SNT-TC-1A programme that fits your work and your written practice. Training is quoted on request, and programmes are affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Request your Arizona training quote, explore all NDT training courses, or talk to us about certifying your Arizona crew.

contentHtml:
HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Training and Certification in British Columbia

Short answer: British Columbia technicians and employers can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and II, plus Level III exam preparation. Training is delivered as live online classes, a private live-virtual cohort, or onsite at the employer's shipyard, mill, plant or yard. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every course, and your employer certifies you under its own written practice.

Start with the honest picture. Canada's national NDT certification scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, and a lot of BC work is specified around it. That includes CSA W59 structural steel and bridges, many provincially regulated pressure-equipment jobs and Canadian federal work. Atlantis NDT does not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712, and we make no claim to CGSB recognition. We teach the American employer-based scheme, SNT-TC-1A. In British Columbia that fits a clear set of people: fabricators and module yards building to ASME or API codes for US or US-owned projects, LNG and pipeline contractors whose owners or EPCs specify SNT-TC-1A, aerospace maintenance and component shops serving US customers, Lower Mainland companies working across the border in Washington State, and technicians who want to work on US sites. This page sets out when SNT-TC-1A makes sense in BC, maps the province's NDT economy from the Lower Mainland to the Peace, and explains how to request a British Columbia training quote. We usually answer within one business day.

SNT-TC-1A or CAN/CGSB-48.9712: which does BC work require?

Direct answer: Canadian-code work in British Columbia usually asks for CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification. That covers structural steel, bridges, many pressure-equipment jobs and federal projects. SNT-TC-1A fits US-code fabrication, US or US-owned clients, some LNG, pipeline and EPC specifications, aerospace work for US customers, and technicians heading to Washington State or further south. Always let the contract and the owner's specification decide.

BC situationScheme usually expectedDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
Bridges, highway structures and building steel under CSA S6 / CSA W59CAN/CGSB-48.9712 through CSA W178.1 inspection organisationsNo, not on its own
Federal shipbuilding and naval workContract specification, typically CGSB or ISO 9712 basedUsually no; check the contract
ASME vessels, B31.3 piping and modules built in BC for US sitesSNT-TC-1A through ASME Section V and the clientYes. This is the core case
LNG, pipeline and gas-plant projects where the owner or EPC specification names SNT-TC-1A or accepts it alongside CGSBProject specificationYes, where the specification accepts it
Aircraft maintenance and component shops with US customersCustomer or regulator specification, often NAS 410 for aerospace productionSNT-TC-1A where it applies; NAS 410 is a separate route we do not offer
BC technicians working in Washington State shipyards, refineries or aerospaceThe US employer's SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410 programmeYes for SNT-TC-1A

The Canadian scheme itself is changing. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Published guidance says the standard remains valid through its current cycle and that existing certificates are unaffected. Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body has said its certification services continue without interruption, and the CWB Group remains accredited to certify NDT personnel to the same standard. Confirm the current certification body before you plan a CGSB route. We will always tell you when a CGSB certificate is what the job needs.

Where NDT technicians work in British Columbia

Direct answer: BC NDT work clusters in six areas. They are the Lower Mainland's port, refinery, pipeline terminal, shipyard and fabrication economy, Vancouver Island's naval and ship repair yards, the north coast LNG and aluminium corridor around Kitimat and Prince Rupert, the Peace Region's Montney gas fields and hydro projects, the Interior's mines and pulp mills, and the aerospace maintenance base at airports across the province.

Metro Vancouver and the Lower Mainland

The Port of Vancouver is Canada's largest port. Around it sit bulk and container terminals, grain elevators, chemical plants, the Burnaby refinery, and the Westridge marine terminal at the end of the Trans Mountain pipeline. The expanded line went into service in 2024. Seaspan's Vancouver Shipyards in North Vancouver builds federal vessels under Canada's national shipbuilding programme. Fabrication shops, module builders and steel erectors across Burnaby, Surrey, Delta, Richmond and Langley supply BC projects and US buyers in the Pacific Northwest. The typical workload is UT and PAUT on piping, tanks and vessels, RT on piping and pipeline welds, MT and PT on terminals, cranes and structural steel, and VT throughout. See NDT training in Vancouver and Vancouver Level III consulting.

Vancouver Island: Esquimalt, Victoria and ship repair

CFB Esquimalt is home to Canada's Pacific fleet. The large federal graving dock at Esquimalt and Seaspan's Victoria Shipyards carry out refit and repair work on naval, coast guard, ferry and commercial ships. Ship repair is heavy on UT thickness gauging of hull plating, MT and PT on welds and machinery, and UT on shafts and rudders. Naval and federal work follows contract specifications that often call for Canadian or ISO 9712-based certification, so check before assuming SNT-TC-1A is enough. Pulp mills, ferries and island power infrastructure add more work.

The north coast: Kitimat, Terrace and Prince Rupert

Kitimat is home to the LNG Canada export terminal, which shipped its first cargo in 2025, and to a long-established aluminium smelter. Cedar LNG is being built nearby, and the Coastal GasLink pipeline carries gas across the province to the coast. Prince Rupert's port handles containers, coal, grain and propane exports. LNG plants mean cryogenic stainless and nickel-steel piping, large storage tanks and heavy-wall vessels, with PAUT, RT, PT and UT on welds and plenty of VT. Many LNG and pipeline projects are run by international owners and EPCs whose specifications reference ASME, API and US practice, and some of them accept SNT-TC-1A certification alongside Canadian certification.

The Peace Region: Fort St. John, Dawson Creek and the Montney

North-eastern BC sits on the Montney gas play. Gas plants, gathering pipelines, compressor stations and the shops of Fort St. John and Dawson Creek create steady radiography, UT and VT work. Pipeline work follows CSA Z662 and, on some projects, API 1104. The Site C hydroelectric project on the Peace River and the older dams upstream add penstock, gate and turbine inspection. As in Alberta, work is seasonal: winter for pipeline construction, summer for plant turnarounds.

The Interior: Prince George, Kamloops, the Kootenays and the Okanagan

Prince George is the north's industrial centre, with pulp mills, a refinery, rail yards and forestry equipment shops. Kamloops and the Highland Valley hold some of Canada's largest copper mining operations. The Elk Valley in the Kootenays produces steelmaking coal, and Trail has a large lead-zinc smelter. Pulp mills mean recovery boilers, digesters and pressure piping that need UT thickness, MT, PT and ET during shutdowns. Mines and smelters need MT and UT on haul trucks, shovels, crushers, mills and structural welds. See Practical NDT in Prince George.

Aerospace and aviation maintenance

Vancouver International, Abbotsford, Kelowna and Victoria airports host airline, cargo, helicopter and military-contract maintenance organisations. PT, MT, ET and UT are used on landing gear, engines, structures and wheels. Aviation maintenance NDT follows the aircraft manufacturer's NDT manual and the applicable aviation regulator. Production aerospace often runs NAS 410 programmes, which Atlantis does not train toward. SNT-TC-1A remains common at shops serving US customers outside NAS 410 scopes.

Bridges, rail and public infrastructure

BC's long-span bridges, the rail lines through the Fraser Canyon and over the Rockies, SkyTrain, and BC Hydro's dams and substations all need periodic NDT. Public owners in Canada usually specify CSA W59, CSA S6 and CGSB-certified personnel. We say this plainly because it is the most common reason an SNT-TC-1A certification is not enough on a BC job.

Most of them work under a CGSB requirement on at least some jobs, so we help them keep both systems straight.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in British Columbia, step by step

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A, a BC employer certifies its own technicians. That happens after classroom training, documented on-the-job experience, general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and a vision test, all as set out in the employer's written practice. The certification sits with that employer. It is not a Canadian national certificate.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A written practice that sets hours, exams and recertification. We can prepare one with you: written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete the formal hours for your method and level, live online or onsite. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. Experience. Log supervised on-the-job hours on real work, recorded by your employer.
  4. Exams. General, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III.
  5. Vision test. Near-vision and colour contrast, normally annual.
  6. Employer certification. Your employer certifies you for the method and level. A new employer recertifies you under its own practice.
  7. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets.

If you also want CGSB certification, keep experience records that can support both schemes, and check the certification body's evidence rules at the start.

Radiography licensing and other BC requirements

Direct answer: gamma radiography in British Columbia is federally regulated by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. Operators must be CNSC-certified exposure device operators or work under the direct supervision of one. Pressure equipment is regulated by Technical Safety BC under the Safety Standards Act. Oil and gas pipelines and facilities within BC are regulated by the BC Energy Regulator.

Industrial radiography

Canada does not use a US-style Agreement State model. The CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices in British Columbia as in every province. You need CNSC exposure device operator (EDO) certification, or direct supervision by a certified EDO, to operate a gamma camera. CNSC guidance sets out formal EDO vocational training and a supervised on-the-job programme before the written exam, and CSA PCP-09 is the certification guide. Atlantis RT training covers radiographic technique, image quality and interpretation against code acceptance criteria. It does not replace EDO certification. X-ray equipment is handled under provincial occupational health and safety rules, so ask your radiation safety officer what currently applies.

Pressure equipment: Technical Safety BC

Technical Safety BC administers boilers, pressure vessels and refrigeration under the Safety Standards Act and its Power Engineers, Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Safety Regulation. That includes design registration, contractor licensing and quality control programmes. Pressure equipment at oil and gas facilities still needs Technical Safety BC design registration, whatever the BC Energy Regulator requires. Our Technical Safety BC compliance guide covers the inspection-company side. Ask Technical Safety BC and your owner which NDE certifications they accept for each job.

Pipelines and energy facilities

The BC Energy Regulator (formerly the BC Oil and Gas Commission) regulates oil and gas activities, pipelines and facilities in the province. Interprovincial and international pipelines, including Trans Mountain, fall under the Canada Energy Regulator. CSA Z662 is the core pipeline standard. API 1104 appears on projects with US or international owners and contractors.

Codes common in BC work

ASME Section V, VIII and IX, ASME B31.1 and B31.3, CSA B51, CSA Z662, API 650 and 620 for storage tanks (including LNG tanks), CSA W59 and CSA S6 for structures and bridges, AWS D1.1 for US-bound structural steel, and class-society and federal specifications for ships. Projects in BC routinely mix Canadian and US codes, which is why many employers run both a CGSB and an SNT-TC-1A system.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across BC

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers British Columbia training as live online seats, private live-virtual cohorts, or onsite training at your shipyard, mill, plant or camp with a Level III instructor. Theory can be done from anywhere in the province. Practicals use real specimens at your site.

BC's geography makes this model useful. Moving a crew from Fort St. John, Kitimat or the Kootenays to a classroom in the Lower Mainland costs days of travel, and ferries and mountain passes add more. Online theory removes most of that. Onsite practicals keep training tied to the welds, alloys and procedures your people inspect. We schedule around pulp mill and smelter shutdowns, LNG and pipeline construction phases, ship refit windows and spring and fall turnarounds.

  • Live online seats for individuals anywhere in BC.
  • Private live-virtual cohorts built around your codes, procedures and equipment.
  • Onsite at your facility with your specimens, including practical exam support under your written practice.
  • Blended online theory, simulator practice and a short onsite practical block.

We have no classroom in British Columbia. Ask about onsite training for your BC crew, or see online NDT training and corporate NDT training.

For BC employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: BC employers that need SNT-TC-1A certification for US clients or US-code projects need a written practice, a Level III to run examinations and approve procedures, and records an auditor can check. Atlantis provides these remotely or onsite. That includes employers that also keep CGSB-certified technicians for Canadian work.

Typical BC examples include a Delta fabricator building ASME vessels for a Washington refinery, a north-coast contractor whose LNG owner wants named SNT-TC-1A Level IIIs on procedures, an aviation maintenance shop with a US component customer, and a Prince George contractor that sends crews to Alberta and the US. Our services include:

  • SNT-TC-1A written practice development and revision (written practice development);
  • outside Level III: exams, procedure and technique review, sign-off;
  • clear mapping of which technicians hold which certification for each BC job;
  • preparation for owner, EPC and third-party audits of your NDT programme;
  • certification and training records managed in software that tracks ASNT and CGSB certificates side by side (Atlantis NDT ERP).

See SNT-TC-1A for employers and NDT consulting in Canada. Book a Level III consultation for your BC company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator gives BC trainees browser-based practice in 12 methods across 5 virtual environments before they reach real specimens. It is a practice tool. It does not replace the hands-on practical exam that your written practice, or a CGSB scheme, requires.

The environments are an NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. They match a good share of BC work: process piping, tanks and terminals, fabrication welds and aircraft parts. Trainees in remote camps or on ships can practise between shifts. Supervisors can check readiness before booking practical exam time. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT in British Columbia. For written practice questions, try the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He writes the course content, examinations and employer written practices. He is also the Level III who will give you a direct answer on whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or both fit your British Columbia work.

NDT training in British Columbia: frequently asked questions

How do I get NDT certified in British Columbia?

For most Canadian-code work, get CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712) certification through an accredited certification body. Confirm the current certification body, since arrangements changed in 2026. For US clients and US-code work, your employer certifies you under SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis trains for the SNT-TC-1A route only.

Is there online NDT training in BC?

Yes. Atlantis runs live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes for BC technicians, with practicals on real specimens at your employer's site. See NDT training online.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB or ISO 9712 training in British Columbia?

No. We do not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or ISO 9712 and claim no CGSB recognition. If your job needs a CGSB certificate, use a CGSB-route provider.

Do I need a licence for radiography in British Columbia?

For gamma radiography, yes. You need CNSC exposure device operator certification, or direct supervision by a certified EDO, and your employer needs a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment follows provincial rules.

How much does NDT training cost in BC?

It is quoted on request. The price depends on the method and level, group size, online or onsite delivery, travel to remote sites, and whether you need a written practice or Level III services. Cohort and onsite quotes usually come back within one business day. Request a BC quote.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted on BC LNG and pipeline projects?

Sometimes. It depends on the owner's and EPC's specification. Some accept SNT-TC-1A alongside Canadian certification. Others require CGSB. Read the project specification first, and we can help you interpret it.

Which NDT methods are in demand in British Columbia?

UT and PAUT lead in terminals, refining, LNG and ship repair. RT is used for pipeline and piping welds, MT and PT are needed in mining, forestry and fabrication, and ET in aviation and mill exchangers.

Can you train our crew onsite in Vancouver, Prince George or Kitimat?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your shop, mill, yard or project site is standard. The instructor works with your equipment and specimens and supports practical exams under your written practice.

How long does UT Level II training take?

Your employer's written practice decides. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours, listed in our training requirements matrix, and the experience usually takes longest.

Can I use SNT-TC-1A certification to work in Washington State?

SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the issuing employer. A Washington employer will review your documented training and experience and certify you under its own written practice. Good training records from Atlantis help with that review.

Can I become an ASNT Level III in BC?

Yes. Prepare for the ASNT Basic and method exams online with our Level III preparation. A CGSB Level 3 is a separate path through the certification body.

What do NDT technicians earn in British Columbia?

Pay depends on method, level, sector, remote-site allowances and overtime. We do not publish our own salary figures. For context, read the NDT salary guide.

We build the programme around your work and tell you plainly when CGSB is the right answer instead. NDT Training and Certification in California

Short answer: California technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, a private live-virtual cohort, or onsite delivery at the employer's refinery, shipyard, hangar or shop anywhere in the state. An ASNT NDT Level III leads each programme, practical exams use real specimens at your facility, and certification is issued by the employer under its written practice.

California's NDT market looks nothing like the Gulf Coast. Refining is concentrated in two clusters, the Los Angeles basin and the San Francisco Bay Area, and it operates under some of the strictest process-safety rules in the country. Aerospace and space launch are far bigger here than anywhere else, from El Segundo and Hawthorne to Palmdale and Vandenberg. San Diego builds and repairs Navy ships, the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach handle a huge share of US container traffic, Caltrans and the seismic-retrofit programme keep bridge and structural steel inspection busy, and the Central Valley still produces oil around Bakersfield. This hub sets out where California NDT work happens, which methods and codes each sector uses, what the California Department of Public Health requires from radiography crews, and how we deliver training without anyone travelling to a centre. To price a group, request a California training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in California

Direct answer: California NDT jobs concentrate in Southern California aerospace and space (El Segundo, Hawthorne, Long Beach, Palmdale), Los Angeles basin and Bay Area refineries, San Diego naval shipbuilding and repair, the Kern County oil fields around Bakersfield, and statewide bridge, seismic and port infrastructure. Aerospace pushes ET, PT and UT; refining pushes UT, PAUT and RT.

Los Angeles basin and the South Bay

The South Bay holds the Chevron El Segundo refinery and the refineries of Carson, Wilmington and Torrance, along with tank farms and marine terminals around the twin ports. Here, refinery safety rules under Cal/OSHA's process safety management regulation for petroleum refineries (adopted after the 2012 Richmond fire) drive rigorous damage-mechanism reviews and mechanical-integrity inspection, so UT thickness surveys, PAUT corrosion mapping, radiography of process piping and ET on exchanger tubes are all in demand. The same area is the heart of US space and aerospace: satellite and launch-vehicle builders in El Segundo and Hawthorne, the Los Angeles Air Force Base and Space Systems Command, and aerospace suppliers across Torrance, Long Beach and Orange County. Aerospace and space work leans heavily on penetrant, eddy current, ultrasonic and radiographic inspection of structures, welds, composites and castings.

Antelope Valley and the high desert

Palmdale's Air Force Plant 42 hosts major defence aircraft programmes, and Edwards Air Force Base nearby is the home of flight testing. Mojave hosts commercial space and flight-test firms. Inspection here is aerospace-grade, typically certified to NAS 410, with large demand for UT on composites, ET on metallic structures and PT on components.

San Francisco Bay Area

The Bay Area's refining cluster includes Chevron's Richmond refinery and the Martinez refining complex, together with renewable-fuel conversions at Rodeo and nearby chemical and terminal operations along the Carquinez Strait. Bay Area refinery inspection carries the same Cal/OSHA process-safety requirements as the South Bay. The region also has ship repair, bridge maintenance on some of the country's largest steel and concrete spans, and a growing battery and advanced-manufacturing sector across the East Bay and South Bay.

San Diego

San Diego is the main West Coast hub for Navy shipbuilding and repair. The NASSCO shipyard builds auxiliary and commercial ships, and Naval Base San Diego and Naval Air Station North Island support large fleet maintenance and aircraft repair. Ship work follows NAVSEA technical publications (for example the NAVSEA NDT requirements used on Navy work) alongside AWS D1.1 and class rules, which means UT, MT, PT, RT and VT on hull and piping welds. Aerospace suppliers and drone manufacturers round out the market.

Central Valley, Kern County and the Central Coast

Kern County around Bakersfield remains California's oil and gas heartland, with producing fields, steam-flood operations, gathering lines, tanks and a refinery. NDT work includes pipeline and tank inspection, UT thickness on steam lines and vessels, and radiography of welds. Fresno and Sacramento add agricultural processing, food plants and state infrastructure, while the Central Coast hosts Vandenberg Space Force Base (orbital launches) and Diablo Canyon, California's last operating nuclear plant, where outage work follows ASME Section XI.

Ports, bridges and seismic work statewide

The Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, Oakland and smaller ports rely on cranes, wharves and terminal tanks that need structural and corrosion inspection. Caltrans' toll-bridge and seismic-retrofit programmes made welded steel inspection to AWS D1.5 and ultrasonic testing of large welds a familiar part of California work, and building-code special inspection of structural welds adds a constant base of UT and MT for construction projects.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for California employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT delivers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for California employers, plus Level III exam preparation. Refineries and construction lean on UT, PAUT and RT; aerospace and space lean on PT, ET and UT; shipyards lean on UT, MT, PT and VT.

One honest note for California aerospace: many primes and their suppliers certify NDT personnel to NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A. Our method theory content is relevant either way, but your certification must follow whatever standard your customer contract specifies, so we confirm it before quoting.

Los Angeles and El Segundo. The South Bay mixes refinery inspection with aerospace and space manufacturing, so a single training request can cover UT and RT for a refinery contractor and PT and ET for a satellite supplier in the same postcode. Refinery contractors usually ask for UT, PAUT and RT Level II and help with written practices that will stand up to owner audits.

San Diego. Ship repair contractors and their subcontractors need UT, MT, PT and VT technicians who understand Navy requirements. Because Navy work follows NAVSEA documents for personnel qualification, we confirm the governing requirement first and use SNT-TC-1A-based training where the employer's programme allows it.

Martinez, Richmond and the Bay Area. Bay Area refinery contractors face the same Cal/OSHA process-safety regime as the South Bay. Training demand is for UT thickness and corrosion mapping, ET for exchanger bundles and RT for piping, timed around planned turnarounds.

Bakersfield. Kern County oilfield and pipeline employers need UT and RT technicians for steam lines, gathering lines and tanks. Crews are spread across the valley, so live online theory followed by a short onsite practical block works best.

Sacramento and Fresno. Central Valley employers in food processing, equipment fabrication and infrastructure maintenance tend to need VT, MT, PT and UT Level I and II for in-house quality control.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in California, step by step

Direct answer: California NDT certification under ASNT SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. The employer's written practice sets the rules, you complete classroom training and supervised experience, a Level III gives general, specific and practical exams, you pass a vision test, and the employer certifies you. Radiographers also need state radiation credentials.

  1. Employer written practice. The employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. Need one? See written practice development.
  2. Formal training. Complete the classroom hours the written practice requires, documented with course records.
  3. Supervised experience. Log on-the-job hours in the method; the training requirements matrix shows typical figures.
  4. General and specific exams. Written exams on theory and on your employer's procedures and codes (ASME V, B31.3, AWS D1.1 or D1.5, customer specifications).
  5. Practical exam. Hands-on testing on flawed specimens, graded by a Level III, held at your facility.
  6. Vision test. Near-vision and colour-contrast checks at the written-practice interval.
  7. Certification and recertification. The employer certifies and later recertifies you; see Level II recertification.

California employers in aerospace and defence often run more than one scheme side by side, with SNT-TC-1A for industrial work and NAS 410 for flight hardware. If that applies to you, keep separate records for each and make sure your written practice says which scheme covers which work. Background: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other California requirements

Direct answer: California has been an NRC Agreement State since 1962. Industrial radiography is regulated by the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) Radiologic Health Branch under Title 17 of the California Code of Regulations. Radiographers must meet the state's certification requirements in addition to their employer's SNT-TC-1A level.

CDPH licenses radioactive-material radiography and registers X-ray equipment used for industrial radiography. Under Title 17, a radiographer must be certified as the regulations require (the rules refer to Section 30335.2, with alternatives set out in related sections), and radiographer trainers must meet additional experience requirements. CDPH also publishes guidance on what inspectors check during field radiography inspections, covering things such as surveys, posting, personnel monitoring and documentation. Rules change, so confirm current requirements with CDPH before planning a programme.

Atlantis NDT's RT courses cover radiographic technique, exposure, film and digital interpretation and acceptance criteria for SNT-TC-1A Level I and II. The state radiation-safety training and certification are separate requirements, handled through your radiation safety officer. We help employers plan both so trainees progress in parallel.

Boilers and pressure vessels. In California, boiler and pressure vessel safety sits with Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit within the Department of Industrial Relations. NDT work on repairs and alterations follows the National Board Inspection Code and ASME Sections I and VIII.

Refinery process safety. Cal/OSHA's process safety management regulation for petroleum refineries sets demanding requirements for damage-mechanism reviews and mechanical integrity, which directly drive inspection volume and documentation quality at California refineries.

Pipelines. The California Public Utilities Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety, and the Office of the State Fire Marshal's pipeline safety programme covers intrastate hazardous-liquid pipelines, with PHMSA for interstate lines. API 1104 governs most pipeline weld inspection.

Codes commonly used in California. ASME V, VIII and B31.3 in refineries; AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structural and bridge steel, along with building-code special inspection of structural welds; NAVSEA requirements on Navy ships in San Diego; ASME Section XI at Diablo Canyon; NAS 410 for aerospace; and API 1104 for pipelines. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI, ICC special-inspector or API inspector credentials for particular roles. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only; we mention these only as local context.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across California

Direct answer: California technicians can take theory live online, join a private live-virtual cohort for their employer, or have an Atlantis Level III deliver the course onsite at their refinery, yard, hangar or shop. Atlantis has no training centre in California; practical exams happen at the client's facility on real specimens.

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory with attendance records, ideal across a state where a drive from Bakersfield to the Bay Area or San Diego eats a whole day. See online NDT training.
  • Private live-virtual cohort. A group from one employer, scheduled around shifts, with content mapped to that employer's written practice, procedures and customer specifications.
  • Onsite. A Level III teaches the hands-on portion and runs practical exams at your facility. See corporate NDT training.

Owner audits and customer source inspections look at precisely these records.

Gaps we often find include written practices that do not cover PAUT or digital radiography, no defined rule for crediting previous experience, missing vision-test records, and practical exams without documented grading. How do I become NDT certified in California?

Join or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its classroom and experience requirements, pass general, specific and practical exams from a Level III and a vision test, and the employer certifies you. Aerospace employers may use NAS 410 instead.

Do I need a license to do industrial radiography in California?

Yes. CDPH's Radiologic Health Branch regulates industrial radiography under Title 17. Radiographers must meet state certification requirements and work for a licensed or registered employer, in addition to holding an SNT-TC-1A level.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted by California aerospace companies?

Many aerospace primes and suppliers require NAS 410 for flight hardware. SNT-TC-1A is widely accepted in refining, construction, pipelines and general industry. Always check your customer's specification.
