NDT Training and Certification in Charlotte, NC

Charlotte technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT as live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite courses at their own plant, shop or outage site anywhere in the Charlotte metro. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every programme, and the hours are recorded against your employer's written practice so they count toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

Charlotte is a power-generation city first. Duke Energy is headquartered uptown, two nuclear stations sit within an hour's drive, the EPRI NDE Center on West W.T. Harris Boulevard qualifies ultrasonic examiners for the whole US nuclear fleet, and Siemens Energy builds large generators and turbine components on the west side. Around that core sit aerospace (Collins Aerospace's headquarters and the American Airlines hub at Charlotte Douglas), motorsport engineering in Concord and Mooresville, structural steel fabricators along I-85 and I-77, and the Paw Creek fuel terminals fed by the Colonial and Plantation pipelines. This page is built around that map. If you already know what you need, request a Charlotte training quote and we reply within one business day.

Quick facts for CharlotteAnswer
Certification schemeASNT SNT-TC-1A, employer-based: your written practice governs
Training hours and experienceSet per method and level by your written practice; see the NDT training requirements matrix for the recommended minimums
DeliveryLive online, live-virtual cohort, or onsite at your Charlotte-area facility. No physical Atlantis centre in Charlotte
ExamsGeneral, specific and practical, administered under a Level III, plus an annual vision test
Radiography licensingNorth Carolina is an NRC Agreement State; RT is licensed by the NC DHHS Radiation Protection Section
PriceQuote on request, usually within one business day

NDT training in Charlotte: how it works for Charlotte employers and technicians

In Charlotte, NDT certification is issued by your employer, not by a school. You complete classroom training for each method and level, log on-the-job experience, then pass general, specific and practical exams administered under an ASNT Level III, plus a vision test. Atlantis NDT supplies the training, the Level III oversight and the paperwork, delivered online or onsite at your facility.

That distinction matters because most "NDT training Charlotte" searches mix three different things: a two-year college programme, a short certification course, and the employer certification itself. Under ASNT's Recommended Practice SNT-TC-1A, a Level II UT technician at a Charlotte fabricator is certified by that fabricator, against its own written practice, signed by its responsible Level III. A training provider can give you documented hours and exam preparation; it cannot hand you a portable "licence" that every employer must accept. A good course is one your employer's Level III can audit and accept without argument.

Atlantis builds training to be accepted that way. Every course record shows the method, level, topics, instructor, contact hours and exam results, laid out so a Level III or a customer auditor can trace it back to the written practice. For employers, we can also review or write the written practice itself, act as an outside Level III, and run the exams. For individual technicians, we explain exactly which parts you can complete online and which need hands-on time with real specimens.

Two hypothetical Charlotte scenarios show how this plays out. Suppose a structural fabricator in Gastonia needs three welders cross-trained to VT and MT Level II for AWS D1.1 work: we run a live-online theory block, then an onsite practical session on their own weldments, then exams against their written practice. A contractor supporting an outage at McGuire needs UT technicians refreshed before they sit an EPRI performance demonstration: we deliver focused UT theory and practice so they arrive ready, while the demonstration itself remains EPRI's process, not ours.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Charlotte

Atlantis NDT offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods and Level III exam preparation. Charlotte employers most often ask for UT and PAUT (power-plant welds and fabrication), MT and VT (structural steel), PT and ET (aircraft and turbine parts) and RT (piping and pressure parts).

MethodLevelsWhat Charlotte employers use it forPrerequisite

Course pages with more detail: UT Level 1, UT Level 2, PAUT Level 2, TOFD, RT Level 2, MT Level 2, PT Level 2, VT Level 2 and ET Level 2. For Level III candidates, see ASNT Level III training. Charlotte has two specialist pages too: nuclear NDT training in Charlotte and power generation NDT training in Charlotte.

Method spotlight for Charlotte: UT and PAUT for power generation. If one method defines the Charlotte market it is ultrasonics on power-plant components. Nuclear in-service inspection under ASME Section XI requires UT examiners to pass performance demonstrations, which for the US fleet are administered through the EPRI Performance Demonstration Initiative here in Charlotte. Fossil and gas-turbine plants use UT and PAUT on boiler headers, steam piping, rotor bores and generator retaining rings. A technician who is solid on UT Level II fundamentals, calibration and flaw characterisation is the person every outage contractor in the region is looking for.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Charlotte, step by step

The path is the same in Charlotte as anywhere in the US: written practice, formal training, experience, three exams, vision test, certification, then recertification on the cycle your written practice sets. What changes locally is which methods and codes your employer needs.

  1. Find the governing written practice. Your employer's written practice sets the training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks for each method and level. If your company does not have one, see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Theory hours for the method and level, delivered live online or onsite. The recommended minimums are summarised in the training requirements matrix; your written practice may require more.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Supervised experience in the method, recorded with dates, hours and the supervising certified person. Many Charlotte technicians build this on outages and fabrication jobs.
  4. Pass the general exam. A closed-book written exam on method principles.
  5. Pass the specific exam. Questions on your employer's procedures, equipment, codes and acceptance criteria, for example ASME Section V, Section XI or AWS D1.1.
  6. Pass the practical exam. Hands-on examination of real specimens with known flaws, graded under a Level III. This is the part that cannot be done purely online.
  7. Pass the vision test. Near-vision acuity annually and colour contrast differentiation as required.
  8. Get certified by your employer. The Level III and the employer sign the certification, which stays valid while you work for that employer.
  9. Recertify. On the interval your written practice sets, by exam or by documented continuing performance. Level III candidates also look at ASNT's own Level III certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Charlotte crews

Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Charlotte. Theory is delivered live online or in live-virtual cohorts, and practical training and exams take place onsite at your Charlotte-area facility, or at a site arranged with you, under Level III supervision. That keeps crews close to work and lets you schedule around outages.

The Charlotte calendar is driven by outages. Nuclear refuelling outages at McGuire and Catawba, gas-turbine and generator overhauls, and spring and fall maintenance seasons at fossil and combined-cycle plants all pull NDT technicians away for weeks at a time. Live online theory can be split into shorter blocks so technicians do not lose a full week, and onsite practical sessions can be booked into the gaps between outages. For fabricators, onsite delivery means training on your own joint designs, thicknesses and acceptance criteria rather than generic samples.

  • Live online: scheduled instructor-led classes with a Level III, suitable for individual technicians across the Carolinas.
  • Live-virtual cohort: a private online class for your crew, run on your schedule.
  • Onsite at your facility: theory and practical in your shop, plant or outage trailer, with your specimens and equipment.
  • Blended: theory online, then a short onsite block for practical training and exams.

See NDT training online for how remote theory works and corporate NDT training for crew programmes. To plan a cohort around your next outage, ask about onsite training for your Charlotte crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Charlotte

Charlotte NDT jobs cluster in nuclear and fossil power, power-equipment manufacturing, aerospace and airline maintenance, motorsport engineering, structural steel and fuel distribution. Each sector asks for different methods, codes and documentation, so training should match the employer.

Nuclear and power generation

Duke Energy, headquartered in Charlotte, operates McGuire Nuclear Station on Lake Norman near Huntersville and Catawba Nuclear Station just across the state line in York County, South Carolina, along with coal, gas and hydro plants across the Catawba River basin. Outage work brings in ISI contractors who need UT, PAUT, ET, VT and PT under ASME Section XI, with the strict documentation and quality-assurance culture of 10 CFR 50 Appendix B suppliers. The EPRI NDE Center in Charlotte develops inspection techniques and runs the Performance Demonstration Initiative for ultrasonic examination qualification.

Power-equipment manufacturing

Siemens Energy's Charlotte facility manufactures large generators and turbine components, and the region has a cluster of power-equipment suppliers and service shops. Forgings, castings and welded assemblies are inspected with UT, MT, PT and RT, often to customer specifications on top of ASME codes.

Aerospace and aviation

Collins Aerospace is headquartered in Charlotte, and Charlotte Douglas International Airport is a major American Airlines hub with maintenance operations. Aerospace work uses ET, PT, UT and MT on structures and components. Many aerospace primes certify personnel under NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based, so check what your employer requires.

Motorsport and advanced manufacturing

Concord and Mooresville host many NASCAR race shops and their suppliers. Chassis, suspension and drivetrain parts are routinely checked with MT and PT, and some teams use UT and ET. It is a small but distinctive local niche for NDT technicians.

Structural steel, bridges and fuel terminals

Structural fabricators and erectors across Mecklenburg, Gaston, Cabarrus and York counties inspect to AWS D1.1, and NCDOT bridges use AWS D1.5. The Paw Creek terminal area west of the airport receives fuel through the Colonial and Plantation pipelines, adding API 653-style tank work and pipeline weld inspection to API 1104 (Atlantis teaches the NDT methods, not API inspector programmes). Interstate gas transmission lines cross the Piedmont as well.

Radiography licensing and other North Carolina requirements

North Carolina is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the Radiation Protection Section of the NC Department of Health and Human Services (Division of Health Service Regulation), under 10A NCAC 15, which mirrors 10 CFR Part 34. X-ray equipment is registered with the same Section.

For a Charlotte RT technician this means the employer holds the radioactive materials licence, and you work as a radiographer or radiographer's assistant under that licence, with radiation safety training, personnel monitoring and the radiographer certification required by the rules. An NDT RT Level II certificate under SNT-TC-1A is a separate thing from radiation safety qualification; you need both to work independently. Atlantis RT courses cover the NDT method; radiation safety qualification follows your employer's licence and the state rules. Confirm current requirements with the Radiation Protection Section before starting RT work.

Work at McGuire is regulated by the NRC directly as a reactor licensee. Catawba is in South Carolina, which is also an Agreement State with its own radiation programme, so crews crossing the state line should check which licence covers their work.

Other local authorities: boilers and pressure vessels are inspected under the North Carolina Department of Labor Boiler Safety Bureau; intrastate gas pipeline safety sits with the North Carolina Utilities Commission, with interstate lines under PHMSA. Charlotte is inland, but technicians who travel to the Port of Wilmington or to coastal terminals may need a TWIC card for secure areas. Codes you will meet locally: ASME Section V and Section XI, ASME B31.1 and B31.3, AWS D1.1 and D1.5, and API 1104.

Local options compared: Charlotte NDT schools and Atlantis

Charlotte has a strong public option: Central Piedmont Community College runs an associate degree in Nondestructive Examination Technology. The ASNT Charlotte Section holds local meetings. Atlantis NDT is different: short, employer-focused SNT-TC-1A courses delivered online or onsite, with Level III and written-practice support.

These are not either-or. A CPCC graduate still needs employer certification and often extra methods; an employer with a CPCC hire may use Atlantis to add PAUT or a Level III-run exam. Pick what fits your timeline and your employer's written practice.

Level III services and written practices for Charlotte NDT companies

Charlotte NDT companies, fabricators and plant contractors can use Atlantis NDT for a written practice, an outside Level III, exam administration and audit preparation. That turns training into certifications an auditor will accept.

Smaller Charlotte shops often have certified technicians but no Level III on staff, or a written practice that has not been revised since it was copied from a former employer. When a customer auditor or an ASME/nuclear supplier audit arrives, the gaps show: missing experience logs, exams that do not match the procedure, vision tests out of date. Atlantis can write or revise the written practice (written practice development), act as Level III, prepare and grade exams, and organise the records. If your Charlotte company works for nuclear customers, our consulting team covers supplier-audit readiness at nuclear NDT consulting in Charlotte; for Level III consulting across the state, see NDT consulting in North Carolina. Practise before the practical exam

The practical exam is done on real specimens under a Level III, onsite at your employer or at an arranged site. Before that, the Practical NDT 3D simulator lets Charlotte trainees practise 12 methods in five virtual environments. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam.

Practical NDT includes an NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank, so a trainee can rehearse scanning patterns, probe handling and indication recognition before touching real equipment. Charlotte trainees can start at Practical NDT in Charlotte or the main Practical NDT page; the state version is at Practical NDT in North Carolina.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He designs the course content, reviews written practices and oversees exams so that training records stand up to employer and customer audits.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Charlotte

How do I get NDT certified in Charlotte, NC?

Get hired or sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete formal training for the method and level, log the required experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis can provide the training and, for employers, the Level III and exams.

How much does an NDT course cost in Charlotte?

It depends on the methods, the levels, the number of trainees, whether theory is online or onsite, and the practical specimens needed. Atlantis quotes on request, usually within one business day. Request a Charlotte NDT course quote.

How much does NDT school cost compared with a short course?

A two-year college programme like CPCC's and a short employer-focused certification course are different products, priced differently. College tuition is published by the college; short-course pricing depends on scope. The cost question to ask is which path gets you certified by the employer you want to work for.

How long is the NDT training course?

Each method and level has its own recommended training hours and experience hours, and your employer's written practice may require more. See the training requirements matrix. Online theory can be split into shorter blocks around work.

Which NDT course is best to start with?

For Charlotte, VT, MT and PT are the usual first methods, and UT is the most useful next step because of power-generation demand. PAUT and TOFD come after UT Level II.

Which NDT certification is best?

The one your employer and its customers require. For most US industrial work that is SNT-TC-1A employer certification; nuclear ISI adds performance demonstration; many aerospace primes use NAS 410. Level III candidates often add ASNT's own Level III certificate.

Can I take NDT training online in North Carolina?

Yes for theory. The practical training and exam need real specimens and a Level III, done onsite at your employer or at an arranged site. See NDT training online.

Do I need a license for radiography in North Carolina?

The employer needs a radioactive materials licence from the NC DHHS Radiation Protection Section, and radiographers must meet the state's training and certification rules. An SNT-TC-1A RT certificate alone is not enough to work independently.

Can you train our crew onsite in Charlotte, Concord or Gastonia?

Yes. Onsite delivery is the main way Atlantis trains crews: theory and practical at your facility, scheduled around outages or production. Plan onsite NDT training in the Charlotte area.

Is ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification recognised by Charlotte employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer certification in US industry, including power generation and fabrication. Recognition always runs through the employer's written practice, which is why training records need to line up with it.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training?

Those programmes generally require an approved school or provider. Atlantis does not claim those approvals; check with the programme administrator. Many Charlotte technicians are trained through employer-paid programmes instead.

Do I need an EPRI qualification for nuclear UT work?

For ASME Section XI ultrasonic examinations covered by performance demonstration requirements, yes, the examiner must be qualified through the demonstration programme. Solid UT Level II training comes first; the demonstration is a separate step.

NDT Training and Certification in Colorado

Short answer: a Colorado technician or employer gets ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual sessions, or onsite delivery at the employer's own shop, plant, base contract site or field location anywhere in the state. Courses cover Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III, and certification is issued by your employer under its written practice.

Colorado is not the first state people think of for NDT, but its inspection market is wide and unusual. The Front Range combines one of the largest space and defence manufacturing clusters in the country with the state's only petroleum refinery. Weld County sits on the Denver-Julesburg Basin, one of the most active oil and gas fields in the West. Pueblo has a steel mill and a national rail-testing site. The Western Slope has the Piceance gas basin, molybdenum and coal mining, and Bureau of Reclamation dams. Each of these employers asks for a different mix of methods and a different style of written practice, and very few of them can send a crew out of state for a week of classroom time. This page explains how training and certification work for each group, what Colorado regulators require, and how to get a quote for one technician or a full crew. Request a Colorado NDT training quote and we reply with options within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Colorado

Direct answer: Colorado NDT work clusters in five areas: metro Denver (the Commerce City refinery, aerospace and space manufacturing, Denver International Airport and rail), northern Colorado and Weld County (DJ Basin oil and gas, wind-component factories), Colorado Springs (military space and defence bases), Pueblo and the southern Front Range (steel, rail testing, power), and the Western Slope (Piceance gas, mining, dams and pipelines).

Metro Denver and Commerce City

Commerce City, just north of downtown Denver, is home to Colorado's only petroleum refinery, which supplies a large share of the state's gasoline, diesel and asphalt. Turnarounds and routine mechanical integrity work there draw UT thickness surveyors, PAUT weld inspectors, radiographers for new piping welds, and PT and MT technicians for repairs and alterations. The surrounding industrial corridor along the South Platte River adds tank terminals, a gas-fired power station, rail yards and heavy fabrication shops. Further south and west, the Denver metro area is a national centre for spacecraft and launch-vehicle work: large space and defence primes operate engineering and manufacturing campuses in the Littleton, Centennial, Broomfield, Westminster, Louisville and Boulder area, building satellites, spacecraft structures, instruments and launch hardware. Their supply chains of machine shops, welders, composite fabricators and special-process houses depend on PT, MT, UT, ET and RT performed under tightly controlled written practices. Denver International Airport and its maintenance and airline operations add aviation inspection work, and Buckley Space Force Base in Aurora brings defence contractors into the metro area.

Northern Colorado and the DJ Basin

Weld County, centred on Greeley, is the heart of the Denver-Julesburg Basin. Thousands of wells feed gathering lines, compressor stations, gas processing plants and crude terminals around Greeley, Fort Lupton, Platteville, Brighton and Fort Collins. Construction of gathering and transmission lines keeps radiographers and UT shear-wave inspectors busy on API 1104 welds, while processing plants and compressor stations need UT thickness, VT and PT on pressure piping to ASME B31.3 and B31.8. The same region builds wind-turbine components: blade, nacelle and tower factories along the I-25 and I-76 corridors need UT on composite blades and thick-plate tower welds, MT on structural welds and VT throughout production. Agricultural equipment and food-processing plants add maintenance inspection.

Colorado Springs and the military space corridor

Colorado Springs hosts Peterson and Schriever Space Force Bases, the US Air Force Academy, Fort Carson and the Cheyenne Mountain complex. Most NDT demand here comes from the defence contractors and electronics, aerospace and vehicle-maintenance suppliers that support those installations, plus the city utility's power plants and gas distribution network. Contractors generally need documented certification that stands up to prime-contractor and government audits, which makes the written practice as important as the course itself.

Pueblo and the southern Front Range

Pueblo has been a steel town for more than a century, and its electric-arc steel mill still produces rail, rod and pipe products that rely on automated UT and ET lines plus MT and visual end inspection. East of the city, a large national rail research and test centre runs track, car and component testing that involves UT, MT and VT of wheels, axles, rail and welds. Pueblo also has a large coal and gas power station, a wind-tower factory, a chemical depot and rail car work. Further south, Trinidad and the Raton Basin add natural gas production and gathering lines.

The Western Slope: Grand Junction, Rifle and the mountain mines

Grand Junction is the service centre for the Piceance Basin, where natural gas wells, gathering systems and processing plants around Parachute, Rifle and Rio Blanco County need pipeline radiography, UT and VT. Interstate gas transmission lines cross the region toward the Front Range and neighbouring states. In the mountains, large molybdenum mines near Leadville and Empire, gold mining in the Cripple Creek district and coal mines in the North Fork valley operate crushers, mills, haul trucks and conveyors that need UT, MT and PT on shafts, welds and structural steel. Bureau of Reclamation dams and penstocks on the Gunnison and Colorado river systems, and high-pressure hydroelectric equipment, bring periodic weld and penstock inspection.

Bridges, highways, rail and water

The Colorado Department of Transportation and county engineers commission fabrication and in-service inspection of steel bridges along I-25, I-70 and I-76, including the mountain viaducts and canyon structures of the I-70 corridor. Bridge fabrication work typically follows AASHTO/AWS D1.5, with heavy use of UT and MT. Union Pacific and BNSF main lines, Denver's light-rail system and the large water utilities on the Front Range, with their pipelines, pumping stations and treatment plants, add more structural and weld inspection work.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Colorado employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table shows each method, the levels available, how Colorado employers typically use it, and what a trainee needs before starting. Your employer's written practice sets the exact hours and experience required.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Colorado, step by step

Direct answer: under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, certification in Colorado is employer-based. Your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. Colorado has no separate state NDT licence, but radiography is regulated by the state.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. Based on SNT-TC-1A, it sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks, vision requirements and recertification intervals for each method and level. If your company has none, we write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Take Level I and then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours per method and level.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience. Log supervised hours in the method at your Colorado workplace, verified by your employer.
  4. Pass the general exam on the principles of the method.
  5. Pass the specific exam on the procedures, codes and equipment you actually use, for example ASME Section V, API 1104 or AWS D1.1.
  6. Pass the practical exam on real specimens with real flaws, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Pass the vision exam for near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated at the interval in your written practice.
  8. Get certified by your employer. Certification is tied to that employer and based on documented training, experience and exams.
  9. Maintain and recertify at the interval in your written practice, and add methods or levels as your career develops.

For more detail on the employer-based system, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Colorado requirements

Direct answer: Colorado is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (CDPHE), Hazardous Materials and Waste Management Division, under the state radiation rules (6 CCR 1007-1, Part 5 covers industrial radiography). Boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Colorado Department of Labor and Employment; intrastate gas pipeline safety under the Colorado Public Utilities Commission.

Industrial radiography

Because Colorado is an Agreement State, CDPHE rather than the NRC licenses most radioactive material used in the state. A company doing gamma radiography with iridium-192 or similar sources needs a Colorado radioactive materials licence, or reciprocity recognition if it is licensed by the NRC or another Agreement State and is working temporarily in Colorado. Industrial X-ray equipment is registered with the state too. Radiographers and radiographer's assistants must meet the state's training, examination, supervision and certification requirements, which parallel the federal rules in 10 CFR Part 34. RT method training under SNT-TC-1A, which is what Atlantis provides, covers technique, exposure, film and digital imaging and interpretation; it sits alongside, not instead of, the radiation safety training and radiographer certification Colorado requires. Always confirm current requirements with CDPHE before you deploy a crew.

Boilers and pressure vessels

The Colorado Department of Labor and Employment, Division of Oil and Public Safety, runs the state's boiler inspection programme. Colorado adopts the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board inspection practice, so repairs and alterations on boilers and vessels need NDT performed to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme. That is one reason refinery contractors and repair shops care about clean, auditable certification records.

Pipelines and oil and gas facilities

Interstate pipelines in Colorado are regulated by PHMSA. The Colorado Public Utilities Commission's gas pipeline safety programme oversees intrastate gas pipeline operators, and the Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission (formerly the Colorado Oil and Gas Conservation Commission) regulates oil and gas operations, including flowline integrity rules. Construction and integrity work commonly follows API 1104 for welding and inspection and ASME B31.4 or B31.8 for design, which keeps RT, UT and VT technicians in demand across Weld County and the Western Slope.

Codes Colorado employers commonly use

  • ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3 at the Commerce City refinery and in gas processing plants
  • API 1104 and ASME B31.8 on DJ Basin and Piceance pipelines
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for CDOT bridge fabrication
  • Rail industry and steel product specifications in Pueblo
  • NAS 410 as context for aerospace and space suppliers (Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A; your employer documents any additional aerospace requirements)

Some Colorado employers also ask for API inspector or CWI credentials for specific roles. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train; our programmes cover ASNT SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Colorado

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Colorado. Theory is delivered through live online or live-virtual classes, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility, using your equipment and specimens under ASNT Level III oversight. Colorado crews train without long mountain drives and without losing field days.

Distance is the defining problem for Colorado training. A technician based in Grand Junction, Craig or Durango faces a long drive over mountain passes to reach a Front Range classroom, and winter weather on I-70 can close the route entirely. Online NDT training removes that problem for the classroom portion of Level I and Level II. You attend live sessions with a Level III instructor, ask questions in real time, and work through method principles, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation. Practical hours and the practical exam then happen with your employer.

For employers training a group, onsite delivery is usually the most efficient option. We schedule classroom and practical sessions at your plant, shop, yard or project site, use your instruments, reference standards and part samples, and build the course around the procedures your crew actually follows. A Commerce City contractor gets UT and PAUT on piping mock-ups; a Weld County pipeline contractor gets RT and UT on weld coupons that match its procedures; a Broomfield space supplier gets PT and ET on its own parts.

Colorado's calendar shapes scheduling. Pipeline construction and bridge work peak from spring to autumn, refinery turnarounds follow the owner's cycle, and mountain mines and Western Slope operators often prefer winter training when field access is limited. We plan cohorts to finish before your busy window. Larger programmes run through corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Colorado crew.

For Colorado employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A makes the employer responsible for certification, so every Colorado NDT employer needs a written practice and access to a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams, and provides Level III services for companies that do not have a Level III on staff.

Many Colorado NDT employers are small: a two-truck radiography contractor in Weld County, a machine shop supplying Front Range space programmes, a fabrication shop in Pueblo, a mine maintenance department on the Western Slope. They need certified technicians but cannot justify a full-time Level III. That gap is where most audit findings come from: training records without hour counts, practical exams with no graded checklist, vision tests out of date, or a written practice copied from another company that does not match how work is actually done.

  • Written practice development and revision aligned with the current edition of SNT-TC-1A and your customers' requirements. See written practice development.
  • Exam administration: general, specific and practical exams prepared and graded under Level III oversight, with records your auditors can follow.
  • Procedure review for UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET procedures against ASME, AWS and API requirements.
  • Audit preparation for prime-contractor audits, National Board or ASME reviews and ISO 9001 surveillance.
  • Corporate programmes for multi-site companies through corporate NDT training.

For broader Level III consulting, see NDT consulting in Colorado and our guide to SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Colorado company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT simulator lets Colorado trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before their practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique, scan patterns and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. That mix fits Colorado well: the welding workshop for fabrication, bridge and tower steel; the hangar for Front Range aerospace and airport work; the oil and gas site for DJ Basin and Piceance pipelines and plants; and the tank for refinery and terminal inspection. Trainees can repeat scans and explore indication types before handling real equipment in front of an examiner.

There is a statewide Practical NDT in Colorado page, plus city pages for Denver, Colorado Springs, Greeley, Pueblo and Grand Junction linked in the city table above. For written-exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Direct answer: Colorado programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop leads course design, delivers Level III-led instruction, and oversees the exams and records that make certification defensible under SNT-TC-1A. His focus is practical: connecting method theory to the procedures, codes and parts your Colorado crew actually works with, and helping employers build written practices that hold up in audits. Ask about his availability when you contact us about Colorado training.

NDT training in Colorado: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Colorado?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. Complete Level I and Level II classroom training in a method, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then issues certification under its written practice. If you are not yet employed, online classroom training prepares you, and certification follows once an employer documents your experience.

Is there NDT training online in Colorado?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online and live-virtual Level I and Level II classes that Colorado technicians can join from Denver, Greeley, Pueblo, Grand Junction or anywhere else. Practical training and practical exams are completed with your employer because they need real equipment and specimens.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Colorado?

Colorado is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by CDPHE. The company holds the licence, and individual radiographers and assistants must meet state training, exam, supervision and certification requirements equivalent to 10 CFR Part 34. Confirm current requirements with CDPHE before starting work.

How much does NDT training cost in Colorado?

Cost is quoted on request. It depends on the method and level, the number of trainees, whether sessions are live online or onsite, and whether you need exam administration or written practice support. Send your requirements and we return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Colorado?

RT and UT lead in the DJ Basin and on the Western Slope because of pipeline and plant construction. UT and PAUT dominate refinery work in Commerce City. PT and ET are essential for Front Range aerospace and space suppliers, and MT and UT matter in Pueblo's steel, rail and mining sectors.

Can you train our crew onsite in Greeley, Denver or Grand Junction?

Yes. We deliver classroom and practical sessions at your facility anywhere in Colorado, using your equipment and specimens, and schedule around construction seasons, turnarounds and winter access.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Colorado employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer certification in US industry, including refining, pipelines, fabrication and many aerospace suppliers. Customers that add their own requirements can have them documented in your written practice.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums; see the training requirements matrix. Experience hours usually take much longer than the classroom portion.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in Colorado?

Yes. Level III candidates normally have substantial Level II experience and prepare for the ASNT Level III basic and method exams. See ASNT Level III training for exam preparation options.

Do you offer API 510 or CWI training in Colorado?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some Colorado employers also ask for API or CWI credentials for particular roles, but those are separate programmes.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Colorado?

No. We deliver training live online and onsite at your facility. There is no Atlantis classroom building in Denver or elsewhere in the state.

What do NDT technicians earn in Colorado?

Pay varies with method, level, sector and travel. For published ranges by level, read our NDT salary guide.

Training is quoted on request, and programmes are affordable, accessible and fully customizable. NDT Training and Certification in Columbus, OH

Columbus technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, private live-virtual cohorts, or onsite courses at their own plant, shop or construction site in Central Ohio. Every course is led by an ASNT NDT Level III and recorded against the employer's written practice, so the hours count toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

Columbus has an unusual place in the NDT world: the American Society for Nondestructive Testing, which publishes SNT-TC-1A, is headquartered here. The city is also home to EWI (the former Edison Welding Institute), The Ohio State University's welding engineering programme and Battelle. Its NDT work, though, comes from industry: Honda's assembly and engine plants to the north-west, a fast-growing ring of data-centre and battery construction to the east and south, utility and gas-distribution networks run from Columbus headquarters, pressure-cylinder and steel processors, and the defence and logistics base at Rickenbacker. This page is written around that map. If you already know what you need, request a Columbus training quote and we reply within one business day.

NDT training in Columbus: how it works for Columbus employers and technicians

In Columbus, as everywhere in the US, NDT certification under SNT-TC-1A is granted by your employer. You take classroom training for each method and level, build supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Atlantis NDT supplies the training, Level III oversight and records, online or onsite.

Because ASNT is based in Columbus, people searching "NDT training Columbus" often land on ASNT's own education pages first. ASNT is the standards and certification body: it publishes SNT-TC-1A and the ANSI/ASNT CP-189 standard, runs the ASNT Level III and ACCP certification programmes, and offers its own educational material. What ASNT does not do is certify you to work for a particular employer under SNT-TC-1A. That step belongs to the employer and its responsible Level III, using a written practice that sets the training hours, experience, exams and pass marks.

So the useful question for a Columbus technician is not "where is the nearest NDT school" but "which training will my employer's Level III accept". Atlantis designs every course for that test. Each record shows method, level, topics, contact hours, instructor and exam results, ready to be filed against the written practice and shown to a customer auditor. Employers can also have us write or revise the written practice, act as outside Level III and run the exams.

Two hypothetical Columbus examples show how this works. Suppose a steel processor in Groveport wants two maintenance technicians qualified in UT thickness and MT Level II for in-house equipment checks: live-online theory, then a day onsite with their own parts and exams under their written practice. A contractor erecting a data-centre campus in New Albany needs VT and UT Level II structural weld inspectors to AWS D1.1: a private cohort scheduled around the construction programme, with practical training on mock-ups from the site.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Columbus

Atlantis NDT runs SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. Columbus employers most often ask for VT, MT and UT for welded steel and construction, UT and ET for automotive and battery manufacturing, RT and PAUT for gas and power piping, and PT for castings and non-ferrous parts.

Method spotlight for Columbus: VT and UT for welded construction. Central Ohio's biggest new source of NDT demand is construction: data-centre campuses, the Intel site in Licking County (which Intel now expects to open around 2030-2031), battery and manufacturing plants, and the utility substations and gas lines that feed them. Structural steel to AWS D1.1 needs VT on every weld and UT on complete-joint-penetration welds as specified. A technician who can read a weld map, set up a UT angle-beam calibration, and write a clear report is the hire every steel erector and testing agency in the region is looking for.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Columbus, step by step

The steps are written practice, formal training, experience, general, specific and practical exams, vision test, employer certification and recertification. The details (hours, exam lengths, pass marks) come from your employer's written practice, which follows SNT-TC-1A.

  1. Identify the written practice. It sets requirements for each method and level. No written practice yet? See written practice development.
  2. Complete formal training. Classroom hours, live online or onsite. Recommended minimums are in the training requirements matrix; your employer may require more.
  3. Build supervised experience. Logged hours in the method under a certified person. Construction and maintenance work in Central Ohio offers plenty of it.
  4. Pass the general exam on method principles.
  5. Pass the specific exam on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, such as AWS D1.1, ASME Section V or API 1104.
  6. Pass the practical exam on real specimens under a Level III. This cannot be done purely online.
  7. Pass the vision test: near-vision acuity and colour contrast as your written practice requires.
  8. Receive employer certification, signed by the Level III, valid while you work for that employer.
  9. Recertify on the interval your written practice sets.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Columbus crews

Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Columbus. Theory is taught live online or as a private live-virtual cohort; practical training and exams happen onsite at your Columbus-area facility or an arranged site, under Level III supervision. That fits construction schedules, plant shifts and utility maintenance seasons.

Central Ohio employers often run multiple shifts and tight construction programmes, so taking a crew off site for a week of classroom training is expensive. Live online theory can be scheduled in shorter blocks, and onsite practical days can be booked when the work allows. Onsite delivery also means training on your own joints, thicknesses, castings or tubing, with your equipment and your acceptance criteria.

  • Live online: scheduled instructor-led classes with a Level III, open to individual technicians.
  • Live-virtual cohort: a private online class for your team on your timetable.
  • Onsite: theory and practical at your plant, shop or jobsite in Franklin, Delaware, Licking, Union, Fairfield or Pickaway counties.
  • Blended: theory online, then a short onsite block for practical training and exams.

More on online NDT training and corporate NDT training programmes. To plan a cohort, ask about onsite NDT training for your Columbus crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Columbus

Columbus NDT work comes from automotive and battery manufacturing, large-scale construction (data centres, the Intel site, warehouses), gas and electric utilities, steel processing and pressure cylinders, defence and logistics, and research and welding engineering. Different sectors need different methods and codes.

Automotive and battery manufacturing

Honda's Marysville Auto Plant and East Liberty plant sit north-west of Columbus, and Honda and LG Energy Solution have built a battery plant in Fayette County to the south-west. The supplier base around them welds, casts and machines thousands of parts. NDT here includes UT on spot welds and joints, ET for material and coating checks, PT on aluminium castings and VT throughout, often under customer-specific procedures alongside an SNT-TC-1A written practice.

Construction: data centres, Intel and logistics

New Albany, Licking County and the I-270 ring have become one of the busiest data-centre and advanced-manufacturing construction markets in the country, and the Rickenbacker area is a major logistics hub. Testing agencies and steel erectors need VT, MT and UT inspectors to AWS D1.1, plus inspectors for the substations, generators and piping that support these sites.

Utilities and gas distribution

American Electric Power and Columbia Gas of Ohio are both headquartered in Columbus. Gas distribution and transmission pipelines across Ohio need weld inspection to API 1104, with RT and increasingly PAUT on transmission welds, while power plants and substations need UT, MT and VT during maintenance. Eastern Ohio's Utica shale adds midstream pipeline and compressor-station work.

Steel, pressure cylinders and fabrication

Central Ohio has steel processors, pressure-cylinder makers and structural and plate fabricators, including Worthington-area businesses that produce steel products and pressure cylinders. Work includes UT thickness and weld inspection, MT on structural steel and forgings, and hydrotest-related inspection under DOT or ASME rules.

Defence, aerospace and research

Rickenbacker Air National Guard Base hosts an air refuelling wing, and Defense Logistics Agency Land and Maritime is based at Defense Supply Center Columbus. Wright-Patterson Air Force Base and aerospace manufacturers around Dayton and Cincinnati are within reach. EWI, Ohio State and Battelle add research and development work, where NDT technicians support weld trials and materials testing. Aerospace employers may require NAS 410 certification instead of SNT-TC-1A, so check what your employer needs.

Radiography licensing and other Ohio requirements

Ohio became an NRC Agreement State in 1999. Industrial radiography with sealed sources is licensed by the Ohio Department of Health, Bureau of Environmental Health and Radiation Protection, headquartered in Columbus, under Ohio Administrative Code Chapter 3701:1-48, which follows 10 CFR Part 34.

For a Columbus RT technician that means your employer holds the licence, and you work as a radiographer or radiographer's assistant under it with radiation safety training, dosimetry and the radiographer certification the rules require. SNT-TC-1A RT Level II and radiation safety qualification are two separate requirements; you need both to work independently. Atlantis RT courses teach the NDT method; radiation safety qualification follows your employer's licence and Ohio's rules. Confirm current requirements with ODH before starting RT work. X-ray equipment registration is also handled by ODH.

Other authorities: boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Industrial Compliance; intrastate gas pipeline safety is enforced by the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio, with interstate lines under PHMSA. Columbus is inland, but technicians who travel to Lake Erie ports such as Toledo or Cleveland may need a TWIC card for secure port and terminal areas. Codes commonly seen around Columbus: AWS D1.1, ASME Section V and VIII, ASME B31.1 and B31.3, API 1104, and ASME Section XI for crews who travel to Ohio's nuclear plants.

Local options compared: Columbus NDT training and Atlantis

Columbus has ASNT's headquarters and educational resources, community colleges that publish NDT career information, and national training companies with Ohio classrooms. Atlantis NDT is employer-focused: SNT-TC-1A courses live online or onsite, plus Level III and written-practice support.

Level III services and written practices for Columbus NDT companies

Columbus testing agencies, fabricators and manufacturers can use Atlantis NDT for a written practice, an outside Level III, exam administration and audit preparation, so training turns into certifications that stand up to customer and code audits.

Construction testing agencies growing fast with the data-centre boom often hire technicians certified elsewhere and need to bring them under their own written practice quickly, with exams that reflect their procedures. Manufacturers in the Honda supply chain may have NDT inside a quality system that customers audit regularly. Both need tidy records: training hours, experience logs, exam papers, vision tests and Level III sign-off. Atlantis can write or revise the written practice (written practice development), act as Level III of record, and set and grade exams. For Level III consulting across Ohio, see NDT consulting in Ohio. To discuss your programme, book a Level III consultation for your Columbus company.

Practise before the practical exam

The practical exam uses real specimens and is graded by a Level III, onsite at your employer or at an arranged site. Before it, Columbus trainees can rehearse 12 methods in five environments on the Practical NDT 3D simulator. It is practice only, not a replacement for the practical exam.

The simulator includes an NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank, so trainees can practise scan coverage, probe handling and indication recognition before using real equipment. Start at Practical NDT in Columbus, the Ohio Practical NDT page or the main Practical NDT page.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He builds the course content, reviews written practices and oversees exams so that training records hold up under employer and customer audits.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Columbus

How do I get NDT certified in Columbus, Ohio?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete formal training, log the required experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and, for employers, Level III services and exams.

How much does an NDT course cost in Columbus?

It depends on the methods, levels, number of trainees, online versus onsite delivery and the practical specimens required. Atlantis quotes on request, usually within one business day. Get a quote for NDT training in Columbus.

How much does NDT school cost?

A college programme and a short certification course are different products. Colleges publish their tuition; short-course pricing depends on scope. The better question is which route gets you certified by the employer you want to work for, and how quickly.

How long is the NDT training course?

Each method and level has recommended training and experience hours, and your employer's written practice can require more. See the training requirements matrix. Online theory can be split into shorter sessions around work.

Which NDT course is best?

For Columbus, VT and UT are the most useful starting pair because of construction and manufacturing demand, with MT for structural steel. RT suits pipeline and utility work; PAUT and TOFD come after UT Level II.

Is ASNT based in Columbus, and can I get certified there?

ASNT's headquarters are in Columbus. ASNT runs its own certification programmes, such as ASNT Level III and ACCP, but SNT-TC-1A certification for a job is issued by your employer, not by ASNT.

Can I take NDT training online in Ohio?

Yes, for theory. The practical training and exam need real specimens and a Level III, done onsite at your employer or an arranged site. See NDT training online.

Do I need a license for radiography in Ohio?

Your employer needs an industrial radiography licence from the Ohio Department of Health, and radiographers must meet Ohio's training and certification rules. An SNT-TC-1A RT certificate alone does not let you work independently.

Can you train our crew onsite in Columbus, New Albany or Marysville?

Yes. Onsite delivery is how Atlantis trains most crews: theory and practical at your site, scheduled around shifts and construction milestones. Plan onsite NDT training in Central Ohio.

Is SNT-TC-1A certification recognised by Columbus employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most common basis for employer certification in US industry and construction testing. Recognition always runs through the employer's written practice, so training records must match it.

What is the highest-paying NDT job?

Generally Level III roles and advanced ultrasonic work (PAUT, TOFD) pay more than entry-level methods, and travel and outage work add to earnings. We do not quote salary figures; check current public wage data for Ohio.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training?

Those programmes generally require an approved school or provider, and Atlantis does not claim those approvals. Check with the programme administrator; many Columbus technicians train through employer-paid programmes.

Where else in Ohio does Atlantis offer NDT training?

See the Ohio NDT training hub, NDT training in Cleveland, NDT training in Cincinnati, the Midwest hub and the US training locations.

Get started

Send your methods, levels, headcount and timing, and we will reply with a plan and quote within one business day. Request your Columbus NDT training quote, or start with the training overview.

NDT Training and Certification in Connecticut

Connecticut technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite courses at their own plant, shop, yard or hangar. An ASNT NDT Level III leads each programme and aligns it with the employer's written practice, so training time counts toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

Connecticut's NDT market is shaped by two industries more than any other: submarines and jet engines. Electric Boat in Groton and the Naval Submarine Base New London anchor the eastern shoreline, while Pratt & Whitney, Sikorsky, Collins Aerospace and a dense web of precision suppliers fill the Hartford-to-Stratford aerospace corridor. Add the Millstone nuclear station, the State Pier offshore wind hub in New London, gas-fired power plants and an ageing network of I-95 and I-84 bridges, and you have a state where documentation discipline counts as much as method skill. Connecticut also became an NRC Agreement State in 2025, which changed who licenses radiography crews. This page is built around that map. If you already know what you need, request a Connecticut training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Connecticut

Connecticut NDT work concentrates in four areas: submarine construction and naval support in southeastern Connecticut, jet-engine and aerospace manufacturing in the Hartford area and the Connecticut River valley, helicopter and precision manufacturing along the coast from Stratford to New Haven, and power, nuclear and infrastructure work spread across the state. Each area relies on different methods and specifications.

Southeastern Connecticut: Groton, New London and Waterford

General Dynamics Electric Boat designs and builds the Navy's Virginia-class and Columbia-class submarines, with major operations in Groton and engineering work across the region, and a large supplier base for hull, piping and component work. Across the Thames River, the Naval Submarine Base New London is home port for attack submarines. Submarine work is among the most demanding NDT anywhere: VT, MT, PT, UT and RT on hull, piping and structural welds, all under Navy technical publications and NAVSEA requirements with tight records and qualification control. In Waterford, Dominion Energy's Millstone Power Station is the state's nuclear plant, and its refuelling outages bring in-service inspection crews working to ASME Section XI with UT, PAUT, ET and VT. In New London, State Pier has been redeveloped as a staging port for offshore wind turbine components, adding heavy-steel inspection demand.

Hartford and the Connecticut River valley

Pratt & Whitney, part of RTX, designs and builds military and commercial jet engines with main operations in East Hartford and Middletown. Collins Aerospace, also part of RTX, is headquartered in Charlotte but runs large operations in Windsor Locks next to Bradley International Airport. Around them sits one of the densest concentrations of aerospace suppliers in the country: machine shops, forge and casting houses, coating and heat-treat specialists and repair stations from Manchester and Newington to Bloomfield, Windsor and Bristol. PT, MT, ET and UT on engine and airframe parts are everyday work, often under prime-contractor process specifications and NAS 410 requirements on top of the supplier's own written practice. Repair stations add ET and UT on in-service parts.

The coastal corridor: Stratford, Bridgeport and New Haven

Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company, builds military helicopters in Stratford, with suppliers across Fairfield and New Haven counties. Bridgeport and New Haven add harbour terminals, fuel and chemical storage, gas-fired power plants, and fabrication and machining shops. Methods here range from PT, ET and UT on rotorcraft structures to UT thickness on tanks and terminal piping and VT and MT on structural steel.

Power, pipelines and infrastructure

Beyond Millstone, Connecticut's electricity comes heavily from gas-fired combined-cycle plants in places such as Middletown, Oxford and Bridgeport, and their outages need boiler, HRSG and piping inspection. Interstate natural gas transmission pipelines cross the state and connect to the Long Island Sound region, and distribution utilities run ongoing pipe replacement. The Connecticut Department of Transportation maintains a large inventory of steel bridges on I-95, I-84 and I-91, including the long river crossings at New London and Hartford, alongside Metro-North and Amtrak rail structures along the shoreline. That work means AWS D1.5 bridge welding inspection, API 1104 pipeline welds, and MT, UT and VT on structural steel.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Connecticut employers

Atlantis NDT runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based courses in eight methods at Level I and Level II, plus Level III preparation. Connecticut employers most often need PT, MT, ET and UT for aerospace parts, VT, MT, PT, UT and RT for submarine and naval work, and UT, PAUT and ET for nuclear and power outages.

Deeper method courses include UT Level 2 training and the PAUT Level 2 course. NDT training by city in Connecticut

Atlantis NDT has dedicated pages for Groton and East Hartford, including maritime and aerospace NDT training pages, plus Practical NDT simulator pages for Groton and Hartford. Every other Connecticut city is served through live online classes or onsite delivery at the employer's facility. There is no Atlantis training centre in Connecticut.

Groton. Submarine construction sets the tone. Inspectors need to work to Navy technical requirements, keep immaculate records and pass audits by people who read them line by line. VT, MT, PT and UT are daily methods, with RT on piping. Our Groton programmes stress procedure compliance and documentation alongside technique, and suppliers to the shipyard often use them to stand up a compliant NDT function.

East Hartford and the Hartford area. Engine work drives demand for PT, MT, ET and UT on rotating parts, castings and forgings, and repair stations need ET and UT on returned hardware. Technicians here are frequently qualified to NAS 410 by their employer or customer; our training is SNT-TC-1A-based, and we help employers document how it fits their customer's requirements.

Stratford and Bridgeport. Rotorcraft structures and dynamic components need PT, MT, ET and UT, while harbour terminals and power stations add thickness and weld inspection. Many smaller suppliers along the coast are building their first formal programme.

Waterford and New London. Millstone outages call for nuclear-grade UT, PAUT, ET and VT, while offshore wind staging at State Pier brings heavy-steel VT, MT and UT. Train ahead of the outage or campaign window.

New Haven, Middletown and Windsor Locks. A mix of terminals, power generation, aerospace systems and rail infrastructure creates steady demand for UT, MT, PT and VT technicians.

Neighbouring hubs: NDT training across the Northeast, Providence and Rhode Island for Electric Boat suppliers and Quonset-area crews, New York for Fairfield County employers, and Boston for teams with Massachusetts sites.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Connecticut, step by step

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you, not the State of Connecticut and not a training school. You complete method training, log documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you to its written practice.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer needs a written practice defining levels, training, experience, examinations and recertification, and in naval and aerospace work it must also satisfy the customer's requirements. If there is no written practice, we can write one.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete the method training required by the written practice, online, live-virtual or onsite. The training requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience on real work, whether engine parts in East Hartford, hull welds in Groton or outage examinations at Millstone. Records are signed and retained.
  4. General exam. A written test on method principles.
  5. Specific exam. A written test on the specifications, procedures and equipment your employer uses, such as a Navy technical publication, a prime contractor's process specification or ASME Section V.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on inspection of specimens with known discontinuities, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast checks, annually.
  8. Certification. Issued by your employer and valid for that employer. A new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice, though your documented training and experience carry forward.
  9. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets, by evidence of continued satisfactory work or re-examination.

Read more on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Radiography licensing and other Connecticut requirements

Connecticut became the 40th NRC Agreement State when its agreement with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission took effect at the end of September 2025. Licensing of radioactive materials, including sealed sources used for industrial radiography, moved from the NRC to the Radiation Division of the Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP), which already registered X-ray equipment. RT crews need state radiation safety compliance in addition to SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Because the transfer is recent, Connecticut companies that previously held NRC licences for industrial radiography should check how and when their licences convert to state licences, and out-of-state companies working in Connecticut should confirm current reciprocity arrangements with DEEP rather than relying on older NRC guidance. Individual radiographers and assistants still need radiation safety training, radiographer certification for sealed-source work, and supervised field experience under the licensee's programme, following the industrial radiography model in 10 CFR Part 34 as adopted by the state. Our RT Level I and II courses cover the method itself: exposure technique, image quality and interpretation. Radiation safety qualification is a separate track. Work inside federal facilities such as the naval base and the shipyard's nuclear work is governed by federal and Navy requirements, so check with the site before deploying a crew. When in doubt, confirm the current licensing authority with the state.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Bureau of Boilers in the Office of the State Building Inspector, part of the Department of Administrative Services' Division of Construction Services, administers and enforces the Connecticut Safety Code for Boilers and Hot Water Heaters, with inspectors working under a National Board commission system. Repairs and alterations follow the National Board Inspection Code, which draws its NDT requirements from ASME Section V and the construction code.

Pipelines. The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety in partnership with the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), which regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines. Pipeline weld inspection commonly follows API 1104.

Codes you will meet in Connecticut. As local context only: NAVSEA and Navy technical publications for submarine work, NAS 410 and prime-contractor process specifications in aerospace, ASTM practices for PT, MT, UT and ET, ASME Section XI for Millstone, ASME Section V and VIII for pressure equipment, ASME B31.1 and B31.3 for power and process piping, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structural steel and bridges, and API 1104 for pipelines. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials; those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train for. Our training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Connecticut

Connecticut crews can take theory live online, join a live-virtual cohort, or have an Atlantis Level III-led programme delivered onsite at their facility. Practical training and practical exams use real specimens, at the employer's site or through a partner arrangement agreed beforehand.

The state is compact, but I-95 and I-84 traffic and shift patterns at the shipyard and engine plants make daytime classroom attendance hard. Live online theory lets a second-shift technician in Groton and a day-shift technician in Windsor join the sessions that suit them, with the instructor present rather than recorded videos alone. See NDT training online for how it works.

Onsite delivery suits shipyard suppliers, engine and rotorcraft suppliers, and plants that want a group trained on their own parts and procedures. Facilities with security or controlled-access requirements often prefer training on their own premises. We schedule around refuelling outages at Millstone, spring and fall outages at the gas-fired plants, production rate changes and audits at aerospace suppliers, and offshore wind staging campaigns at State Pier. Train before the outage or audit, not during it.

Hands-on skill is built on hardware. Practical sessions use real specimens, your production parts where appropriate, and the instruments your team actually uses. For employers with sites in Connecticut and other states, our corporate NDT training programme keeps training records consistent. Ask about onsite training for your Connecticut team.

For Connecticut employers: written practice and Level III services

Every Connecticut company certifying NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, administers and grades exams, reviews procedures and acts as an outside Level III for companies without one in-house.

In Connecticut the trigger is usually a customer requirement. A machine shop approved as a special-process source for an engine maker, a fabricator joining the submarine supply chain, a repair station adding ET, or a company whose Level III has retired all need the written practice and Level III oversight in place before anyone can be certified, and before the next customer audit. Our written practice development service builds a document that fits your methods, specifications and audits, and our SNT-TC-1A guidance explains what auditors look for.

Level III support includes procedure and technique writing, exam administration and grading, review of training and experience files, and audit preparation. For outsourced Level III and programme work in the state, see NDT consulting in Connecticut. Book a Level III consultation for your Connecticut company.

Practise before your practical exam

Practical NDT is Atlantis NDT's 3D simulator. Trainees practise 12 inspection methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It builds familiarity and confidence but is practice only; it does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

For Connecticut trainees, the NDT lab mirrors inspection rooms at engine and rotorcraft suppliers, the aircraft hangar matches repair stations and aviation work around Bradley and Stratford, the welding workshop reflects naval and offshore wind fabrication in southeastern Connecticut, and the storage tank scene matches the terminals of New Haven and Bridgeport harbours. Trainees can rehearse set-ups and scan patterns between classes and arrive at the practical exam knowing what to expect.

Simulator time does not count as on-the-job experience and is not a practical exam. See the Practical NDT simulator overview, or the city pages for Groton and Hartford.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As Level III he oversees course content, written practices, exams and practical assessment criteria, so training is tied directly to how Connecticut technicians will be examined and certified. Questions about methods, written practices or a Connecticut requirement can go to him through the contact form.

NDT training in Connecticut: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Connecticut?

Most Connecticut technicians are certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A: method training, documented on-the-job experience, general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and a vision test. Aerospace and naval customers often add their own requirements, which the employer's written practice should cover.

Is there NDT training online in Connecticut?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online theory classes that technicians can join from Groton, Hartford, Stratford, New Haven or anywhere else in the state. Practical training and practical exams still need real specimens, arranged onsite at your employer or through an agreed partner.

Who licenses industrial radiography in Connecticut now?

Since Connecticut became an NRC Agreement State in 2025, the state Department of Energy and Environmental Protection's Radiation Division licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, and it continues to register X-ray equipment. Confirm current licence and reciprocity requirements with DEEP, because the transfer from the NRC is recent.

How much does NDT training cost in Connecticut?

Quote on request. It depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and whether you also need a written practice or exam administration. Send your crew size and methods and we will reply with a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in Connecticut?

PT, MT, ET and UT dominate because aerospace manufacturing is the largest NDT employer base. VT, MT, PT, UT and RT are core for submarine and naval work, and UT, PAUT and ET for nuclear and power outages.

Can you train our crew onsite in Groton or East Hartford?

Yes. Onsite delivery is available at your facility anywhere in Connecticut, scheduled around production, audits and outages. Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in the state; onsite means at your site.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Connecticut employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used employer-based framework in US industry and is referenced by ASME, AWS and many aerospace and defence documents. Navy work and some aerospace customers impose additional or different qualification requirements, so check your customer's specification.

Do I need NAS 410 for aerospace NDT jobs in Connecticut?

Many aerospace primes and suppliers in the Hartford area qualify personnel to NAS 410. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based; if your customer requires NAS 410, confirm with them how training and certification must be documented.

How long does UT Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom training and experience for each level. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums are on our training requirements matrix. Experience usually takes longer than classroom time.

Can I prepare for the ASNT Level III exams from Connecticut?

Yes. Our ASNT Level III training runs live online and covers the Basic and method exams. Level II candidates can also use the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Does my certification transfer to another Connecticut employer?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the issuing employer. A new employer reviews your records and re-certifies you under its own written practice, which may require new specific and practical exams.

What do NDT technicians earn in Connecticut?

Earnings vary by method, level, sector, shift and overtime. For published ranges, see the NDT Level 2 salary and NDT Level 3 salary guides.

Start NDT training in Connecticut

Whether you are a technician in New Haven working toward UT Level II, a Groton supplier preparing for shipyard audits, an East Hartford machine shop that needs PT and ET qualified people, or a company that needs a written practice and an outside Level III, Atlantis NDT will build the programme around your work. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Request your Connecticut NDT training quote, tell us about your crew and methods, or browse the full training catalogue and the national NDT training in the USA hub.

contentHtml:
