NDT Training and Certification in El Paso, TX

Short answer: El Paso technicians and employers can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, in a private live-virtual cohort, or onsite at the employer's refinery contract site, fabrication shop, pipeline yard or plant in the El Paso and Borderplex area. Courses cover Level I and II in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation, all led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Your employer certifies you under its written practice.

El Paso sits a long way from the Texas NDT schools that dominate search results. Most of them are around Houston, more than 700 miles east, and even the Permian Basin oilfield towns of Midland and Odessa are a four-hour drive. Yet El Paso has real inspection demand: a large refinery east of downtown, interstate natural gas and refined-products pipelines, a major Army installation, power plants, rail yards, cross-border manufacturing in the Borderplex, and aerospace and test-range work in nearby New Mexico. Sending a crew to Houston for training means hotel nights and lost production, which is why El Paso employers increasingly ask for training delivered at their own facility or live online. Atlantis NDT has no El Paso campus; we teach online and onsite, and the practical exam is done on real specimens under a Level III. Request an El Paso NDT training quote and we reply within one business day.

Key pointFor El Paso trainees and employers
SchemeASNT SNT-TC-1A; certification is issued by your employer under its written practice
Training hours and experienceSet per method and level; see the training requirements matrix and your written practice
ExamsGeneral, specific and practical, administered by a Level III; annual vision test
DeliveryLive online, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite anywhere in El Paso County, southern New Mexico or West Texas
RadiographyTexas is an NRC Agreement State; the Texas Department of State Health Services licenses industrial radiography and certifies radiographers
CommercialsQuote on request; cohort and onsite quotes within one business day

NDT training in El Paso: how it works for El Paso employers and technicians

Direct answer: certification under SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. You complete formal training, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass a vision test; your employer then certifies you. Atlantis delivers the training and, when needed, the written practice and Level III services behind it.

In El Paso the typical buyer of NDT training is a contractor or plant team rather than a walk-in student. A mechanical contractor bidding refinery turnaround work needs UT and PT technicians who can show certification records to the owner. A fabrication shop building pressure vessels or structural steel for projects in Texas, New Mexico and Mexico needs VT and MT inspectors under a written practice it controls. A pipeline contractor needs radiographers who also hold the Texas radiographer credential. A manufacturer with plants on both sides of the border wants a consistent programme for quality technicians. For each of them the course matters, but so does the paper trail an auditor will read.

Individual technicians use the same path. If you are moving into NDT from welding, the military at Fort Bliss, or aviation maintenance, the training hours you complete with Atlantis are documented so that your current or next employer's Level III can review and accept them. We say clearly at the start that a training certificate on its own is a training record, and certification happens when an employer qualifies you under its written practice. Employers who want the full programme can use our SNT-TC-1A training and certification support.

Where NDT technicians work in El Paso

Direct answer: El Paso NDT work centres on the refinery and fuel terminals east of downtown, interstate gas and products pipelines, power generation, Fort Bliss and defence contracting, rail and cross-border logistics, maquiladora-linked manufacturing, water infrastructure, and nearby New Mexico aerospace, test-range and oilfield work.

Refining and fuel terminals

El Paso's refinery, about three miles east of downtown, processes roughly 130,000 barrels of crude a day and supplies fuel to West Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and northern Mexico. It began as two plants built in the late 1920s and early 1930s, which means a mix of older and newer piping, vessels and tanks. Routine mechanical integrity work and periodic turnarounds draw UT thickness technicians, PAUT and TOFD crews for weld and corrosion assessment, radiographers for new piping welds, and PT and MT technicians for repairs. Tank farms and fuel terminals around the refinery and along the products pipelines add tank-floor, shell and nozzle inspection, with ASME B31.3 and API codes used as the governing documents.

Pipelines

El Paso is a pipeline crossroads. Interstate natural gas transmission lines carry gas from the Permian Basin west to Arizona and California, and refined-products lines run from El Paso to Phoenix, Tucson and Albuquerque. New construction, integrity digs, valve and station work, and line replacements all require radiography or UT on girth welds to API 1104, plus VT and MT. Gas distribution work in the city adds steady demand.

Power, water and utilities

Gas-fired power stations in and around El Paso, transmission structures, and the region's water system, including one of the world's largest inland desalination plants, create weld, corrosion and structural inspection work. Boilers, heat-recovery steam generators and high-pressure piping in these plants rely on UT, RT and MT.

Fort Bliss, defence and aerospace

Fort Bliss is one of the largest Army installations in the country, and its vehicle, aviation and construction programmes support a network of defence contractors and maintenance shops. Across the state line, White Sands Missile Range, Holloman Air Force Base and Spaceport America bring aerospace and test-range work within driving distance, and a commercial launch site operates in West Texas east of the city. These employers need ET, PT, MT and UT on aircraft and vehicle components under controlled written practices.

Rail, logistics and cross-border manufacturing

Two major Class I railroads run through El Paso, with yards and intermodal facilities that need MT and UT on wheels, axles, couplers and structural repairs. Across the border, Ciudad Juárez hosts a large concentration of export manufacturing plants in automotive, electronics, medical devices and aerospace, and many have support operations, warehouses or suppliers in El Paso and Santa Teresa. Quality teams in those plants often follow US customer specifications, which makes an SNT-TC-1A written practice a natural fit.

Fabrication and the Permian connection

El Paso fabrication shops build structural steel, skids, tanks and pressure equipment for projects in Texas, New Mexico and Mexico, often to AWS D1.1 and ASME Section VIII. Many El Paso technicians also travel east to the Permian Basin for oilfield construction and gas-processing work, where UT, RT and VT are the core methods.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in El Paso

Direct answer: Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation, live online or onsite in El Paso. The table links each method to typical El Paso work and lists what a trainee needs before starting.

Method spotlight: UT thickness and PAUT for refinery and pipeline work

In El Paso, the method most local contractors ask for first is ultrasonic testing, starting with thickness surveys on refinery and terminal piping and moving to shear-wave and phased array weld inspection. A technician who holds UT Level II and has started PAUT is useful to refinery contractors, pipeline contractors and fabricators alike. If your crew supports turnaround work, schedule UT training well ahead of the outage so new Level IIs have time to log experience. Ask about UT and PAUT training for your El Paso crew.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in El Paso, step by step

Direct answer: written practice, formal training, supervised experience, Level III-administered general, specific and practical exams, a vision test, and employer certification, then recertification at the set interval. Use the training requirements matrix and your written practice for exact hours.

  1. Written practice. Your employer's SNT-TC-1A-based document sets training, experience, exam and recertification rules. Atlantis can prepare one: see NDT written practice development.
  2. Formal training in the method and level, live online or onsite in El Paso, with records of attendance and topics.
  3. Supervised experience on real work, logged by your employer.
  4. General exam on method principles.
  5. Specific exam on your employer's procedures and the codes you work to, for example API 1104, ASME Section V or AWS D1.1.
  6. Practical exam on specimens with known discontinuities, under a Level III.
  7. Vision test, repeated annually.
  8. Employer certification in writing.
  9. Recertification as the written practice requires.

Radiographers in Texas have an extra, separate track: the state radiation safety credential, described below.

How the practical works when you train online

Direct answer: classroom theory can be online, but the practical exam always happens on real specimens under a Level III, normally onsite at your El Paso facility using your own equipment and procedures, or at a location agreed with your employer before training starts. The simulator is for rehearsal only.

For a refinery contractor or fabricator with equipment and weld samples, the Level III visits, checks the procedure, and examines each trainee on the work they will actually do. For a smaller company without suitable specimens, we agree how the practical will run before the course starts. The outcome is the same: graded exam records, training records and vision tests in a file that an owner's QA team or auditor can review.

Local NDT training options in El Paso

Direct answer: El Paso has welding and trade programmes at local colleges and career schools, but few dedicated NDT schools. Most campus-based Texas NDT schools are in the Houston and Dallas-Fort Worth areas. Atlantis fills the gap with live online and onsite employer training; we do not have an El Paso campus.

  • Local colleges and career schools in El Paso teach welding and related trades, and some have introduced students to welding inspection and NDE. They are a good starting point for people new to the trades.
  • Campus-based Texas NDT schools in the Houston and Dallas-Fort Worth areas run full programmes and scheduled courses, but attending means travel and lodging.
  • Local inspection companies in El Paso train their own technicians under their written practices and are a common first employer.
  • Atlantis NDT trains employer crews onsite in El Paso or live online, aligned to their written practice, with Level III services available.

Radiography licensing, TWIC and other Texas requirements

Direct answer: Texas is an NRC Agreement State. The Texas Department of State Health Services Radiation Control Program licenses industrial radiography under 25 TAC 289.255 and certifies industrial radiographers. Boilers fall under the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, and intrastate pipelines under the Railroad Commission of Texas. Confirm current requirements with each agency before starting work.

Industrial radiography in Texas

Employers performing radiography hold a DSHS licence or registration. Individuals start as radiographer trainees: they complete a radiation safety course that meets the state rule, obtain a trainee status card, and then log documented on-the-job training under a qualified radiographer trainer before applying for radiographer certification. The exact course and supervised-hour requirements are set by DSHS and differ between radioactive-material and X-ray work, so check the current DSHS guidance. This state credential is separate from your RT Level I or II certification under SNT-TC-1A; you need both to work as a radiographer.

Working across the state line

Many El Paso crews also work in southern New Mexico, which is also an NRC Agreement State with its own radiation control programme. Radiography crews crossing into New Mexico need to follow its reciprocity process, and work in Mexico is subject to Mexican regulations. Confirm the current licensing authority before mobilising.

Boilers, pipelines and codes

The Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation administers the state boiler programme, with the National Board Inspection Code applying to repairs and alterations. The Railroad Commission of Texas Pipeline Safety Department oversees intrastate pipelines, and PHMSA regulates interstate lines. Codes commonly used by El Paso employers include ASME Section V and VIII, ASME B31.3 and B31.8, API 1104 and AWS D1.1. Some local employers also ask for CWI or API inspector credentials; those are separate programmes Atlantis does not teach.

TWIC

El Paso has no maritime-regulated port facilities, so most local work does not require a Transportation Worker Identification Credential. Technicians who travel to Gulf Coast refineries and terminals for turnarounds will usually need one there.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for El Paso crews

Direct answer: choose live online classes for individuals, a private live-virtual cohort for a company team, or onsite training at your El Paso facility. Every format is Level III-led, and we schedule around refinery turnarounds, pipeline construction seasons and shift work.

El Paso is in the Mountain time zone, an hour behind most of Texas, and our live online sessions are scheduled with that in mind. Contractors that send crews to Permian Basin or Gulf Coast projects often want theory completed before a job starts, with the practical onsite once the crew is back. Plants that run shifts prefer short live sessions over several weeks. For bilingual crews we can plan the delivery to suit the team, while exams follow the language set in your written practice. See NDT training online and corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your El Paso crew.

Level III services and written practices for El Paso NDT companies

Direct answer: many El Paso contractors and manufacturers need a written practice, procedures and an outside Level III as much as training. Atlantis provides those services remotely and onsite, so training, exams and records line up when an owner or auditor reviews your programme.

Our consulting work in the region is described on NDT consulting in El Paso, and further east on NDT consulting in Midland and NDT consulting in Odessa, with the statewide view on Texas NDT Level III consulting. Typical El Paso work includes a first written practice for a growing inspection company, procedures for refinery and pipeline contracts, an outside Level III to administer and grade exams, and audit preparation before an owner's prequalification review. Start with written practice development or book a Level III consultation for your El Paso company.

Practise before the practical exam

Direct answer: the Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five environments, including an oil and gas site, a storage tank and a welding workshop. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The oil and gas and storage-tank environments match El Paso's refinery, terminal and pipeline work closely. Local users can also see Practical NDT in El Paso.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He teaches the classroom content, oversees practical examinations and supports employers with written practices and Level III services.

NDT training in El Paso, Texas and New Mexico: related pages

The statewide page is NDT training in Texas, and the regional overview is NDT training in inland Texas. Permian Basin employers can see NDT training in Midland and NDT training in Odessa. For crews working in southern New Mexico, see NDT training in New Mexico and NDT training in Albuquerque.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in El Paso

How do I get NDT certified in El Paso?

Complete the formal training your employer's written practice requires, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training online or onsite in El Paso, and Level III services if your employer needs them.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes, the classroom portion. Atlantis runs live online classes led by an ASNT Level III, scheduled for Mountain time. The practical exam is done on real specimens under a Level III.

How much does an NDT course cost in El Paso?

We quote on request. Cost depends on method, level, group size and whether training is online or onsite. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day. Request an El Paso course quote.

How much does NDT certification cost?

Certification under SNT-TC-1A is issued by your employer, so the cost is a combination of training, the employer's time for supervised experience, and Level III exam administration. Many employers pay for it. For a specific quote on the training and Level III services, contact us.

How much does an NDT technician course cost compared with a full school programme?

A campus programme covering several methods over months is a bigger commitment, often with travel from El Paso. Targeted training in the methods your employer uses is shorter. The better value depends on whether you need career-entry training or a specific qualification.

How long is the NDT training course?

It depends on the method, the level and your written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends hours and experience for each; see the training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

Yes. Texas is an Agreement State. DSHS licenses employers and certifies industrial radiographers; trainees work under a trainee status card and a radiographer trainer before certification.

Which NDT method is most in demand in El Paso?

UT and RT for refinery, pipeline and power work, followed by VT and MT for fabrication and PT for repairs. Defence and aerospace employers also use ET.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by El Paso employers?

Yes. It is the most widely used employer certification guideline in US industry, and most refinery, pipeline and fabrication contractors in El Paso work under SNT-TC-1A-based written practices.

Can you train our crew onsite in El Paso or southern New Mexico?

Yes. A Level III can deliver training and practical exams at your facility in El Paso, Horizon City, Socorro, Santa Teresa, Las Cruces or elsewhere in the region.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in El Paso?

No. Atlantis delivers training live online and onsite at the employer's facility. We do not have a physical campus in Texas.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training in El Paso?

Those programmes require an approved school or an eligible training provider listing. Atlantis does not claim those approvals. Check with the VA or Workforce Solutions Borderplex; employer-paid training is the common alternative.

Do you offer CWI or API inspector training in El Paso?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, covering UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

NDT Training and Certification in Florida

Short answer: Florida technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual sessions, or onsite delivery at their own hangar, shipyard, plant or fabrication shop. Courses cover Level I and II in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation, all led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Your employer certifies you under its written practice, and we help build that written practice.

Florida's NDT market looks nothing like the Gulf Coast refining states. Florida has no oil refineries; instead, NDT demand comes from aerospace and space launch, aircraft maintenance and overhaul, naval and commercial shipyards, nuclear and gas-fired power generation, phosphate and fertilizer chemical plants, pulp and paper mills, ports and fuel terminals, natural gas pipelines and an enormous bridge and construction programme. That makes Florida one of the most PT-, ET- and UT-heavy states, with strong aerospace quality expectations and a growing need for PAUT in power and pipeline work. This page shows how training and certification work for Florida employers, what Florida regulators require, and where the work is by region and city. Request a Florida NDT training quote and we respond within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Florida

Direct answer: Florida NDT work clusters on the Space Coast (launch, satellites, avionics), in South Florida (aircraft MRO, cargo, nuclear power), around Jacksonville (naval aviation, ship repair, port, paper), in Tampa Bay (power, phosphate, ship repair, port), in Orlando (defence and simulation manufacturing) and across the Panhandle (air bases, naval aviation training and shipbuilding).

The Space Coast: Cape Canaveral, Titusville and Melbourne, Florida

Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station host commercial and government launch providers, rocket and spacecraft processing, and a supply chain of precision fabricators and test labs. Launch vehicle structures, pressure vessels, propellant lines and ground-support equipment rely on PT, UT, RT, ET and VT, often under strict aerospace quality systems. Further south, Melbourne and Palm Bay host avionics, defence electronics and business-jet assembly, adding aerospace NDT demand. Port Canaveral adds marine and cruise-ship work.

South Florida: Miami, Fort Lauderdale and the Treasure Coast

Miami International Airport is one of the largest cargo and international passenger gateways in the country, and the area around it holds a dense cluster of FAA-certificated repair stations overhauling engines, landing gear, components and airframes. Those shops depend on ET, PT, MT and UT technicians under written practices that satisfy airline customers and repair station quality manuals. South Florida also has two nuclear stations, Turkey Point near Homestead and St. Lucie on Hutchinson Island, where refuelling outages bring ASME Section XI in-service inspection. Port Everglades and PortMiami add fuel terminal and marine work. Further north, the Jupiter and West Palm Beach area is home to jet-engine and helicopter development and test facilities.

Northeast Florida: Jacksonville

Jacksonville combines Naval Air Station Jacksonville, home of a major Navy fleet readiness and aircraft overhaul centre, with Naval Station Mayport, commercial and naval ship repair yards on the St. Johns River, JAXPORT terminals, pulp and paper mills in the region and power generation. Ship repair brings UT, MT, VT and RT under NAVSEA and ABS requirements; naval aviation brings ET, PT and UT under military maintenance standards; mills bring boiler and pressure vessel inspection.

Tampa Bay and central-west Florida

Tampa Bay has large coal- and gas-fired power stations, Port Tampa Bay's fuel and bulk terminals, ship repair yards, and the phosphate mining and fertilizer industry of Polk and Hillsborough counties, whose chemical plants operate sulfuric acid plants, pressure vessels, tanks and process piping that need UT thickness, PAUT, VT and PT/MT on repairs. MacDill Air Force Base adds aircraft maintenance work. The region also has a large construction and bridge programme.

Central Florida: Orlando

Orlando is a centre for defence manufacturing, missiles and fire control systems, and training and simulation. Manufacturers and suppliers use PT, MT, UT and ET on machined and welded components, while theme-park ride engineering and large construction projects add structural weld inspection to AWS D1.1.

The Panhandle: Pensacola, Fort Walton Beach and Panama City

Northwest Florida is dominated by military aviation: Naval Air Station Pensacola, Eglin Air Force Base, Hurlburt Field and Tyndall Air Force Base, plus commercial aircraft MRO at Pensacola's airport. Panama City has shipbuilding for government and commercial vessels. Aircraft and ship work bring ET, PT, UT, MT, RT and VT demand under military and classification-society standards.

Pipelines, power and infrastructure statewide

Florida imports most of its natural gas through interstate transmission pipelines from the north, and laterals feed gas-fired power plants around the state. New construction and integrity work follow API 1104 and ASME B31.8. Florida's utilities run a large fleet of combined-cycle plants with HRSGs, steam piping and condensers that need UT, PAUT, ET and VT during outages. The Florida Department of Transportation's bridge programme and Florida's coastal environment drive steel bridge fabrication inspection and corrosion monitoring.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Florida employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table shows each method, the levels available, how Florida employers use it and prerequisites. Your employer's written practice sets exact hours and experience.

MethodLevelsWhat Florida employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepShip hull and structure inspection in Jacksonville and Tampa, power plant piping, phosphate plant thickness surveys, aircraft structuresLevel I: per employer. Level II: Level I training plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepPower plant and HRSG welds, pipeline welds, corrosion mapping in chemical plants, aerospace composite and metal structuresUT Level II recommended
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-section vessels and power piping, heavy fabricationUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline welds, shipyard welds, power piping, aerospace castingsFlorida radiation safety and radiographer requirements apply before working with sources

Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepAerospace components on the Space Coast and in Miami MRO, stainless welds, launch hardwarePer employer
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld inspection in shipyards and construction, nuclear outage VT, tank and terminal inspectionVision test per written practice
Electromagnetic Testing (ET)I, II, III prepAircraft structure and engine component inspection, condenser and heat exchanger tubing, steam generator tubing at nuclear stationsPer employer

Florida aerospace and MRO employers often start technicians in PT and MT, then add ET and UT. Shipyards start welding inspectors in VT, then MT and UT. Power plant contractors focus on UT, PAUT and ET. Many aerospace customers reference NAS 410 in addition to SNT-TC-1A; we train to SNT-TC-1A and help your written practice document any extra requirements. For Level III candidates, see ASNT Level III training and exam preparation.

NDT training by city in Florida

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT serves all of Florida online and onsite, with dedicated training pages for Miami, Jacksonville, Tampa and Orlando and simulator practice pages for those cities plus Pensacola. The table links each page; city notes follow.

CityMain NDT sectorsPage
MiamiAircraft MRO and cargo, nuclear power, ports, constructionNDT training in Miami / Miami practice
JacksonvilleNaval aviation overhaul, ship repair, port, paper mills, powerNDT training in Jacksonville / Jacksonville practice
TampaPower stations, phosphate and fertilizer plants, ship repair, port, air baseNDT training in Tampa / Tampa practice

PensacolaNaval aviation, aircraft MRO, power, Panhandle air basesPensacola practice
Cape Canaveral and TitusvilleLaunch vehicles, spacecraft processing, ground support equipmentOnline and onsite (no city page)

Miami. Miami's MRO cluster makes it Florida's busiest aerospace NDT city. Repair stations need ET, PT, MT and UT technicians and must keep certification records tidy for airline audits. Many shops hire experienced technicians and need help maintaining written practices and exam records. See the Miami NDT training page.

Jacksonville. Naval aviation overhaul and ship repair make Jacksonville a mixed aerospace and marine market. Ship repair contractors need VT, MT, UT and RT inspectors familiar with NAVSEA or ABS requirements; aviation suppliers need ET and PT. See the Jacksonville NDT training page.

Tampa. Tampa's power stations, phosphate chemical plants and port terminals give it the most process-industry NDT work in Florida: UT thickness surveys, PAUT and RT of piping, VT of tanks and vessels, and ET of heat exchangers. See the Tampa NDT training page.

Orlando. Orlando is a manufacturing and engineering hub between the Space Coast and Tampa, with defence and simulation employers and fast-growing construction. Manufacturers need PT, MT and UT; construction inspection firms need VT and UT on structural welds. See the Orlando NDT training page.

Pensacola and the Panhandle. Military aviation and aircraft MRO drive ET, PT and UT demand, and shipbuilding in Panama City adds structural weld inspection. Contractors often need technicians who can move between military and commercial standards.

The Space Coast. Launch and spacecraft suppliers need technicians who can work to strict aerospace procedures on pressure vessels, tanks, welded structures and composite parts. Space Coast employers are typically served through the Orlando page and onsite delivery.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Florida, step by step

Direct answer: NDT certification in Florida is employer-based under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. Radiography adds Florida radiation safety requirements.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A. If it does not have one, we write it with you: written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Level I, then Level II, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. On-the-job experience. Documented, supervised hours in the method at your Florida workplace.
  4. General exam on method principles.
  5. Specific exam on your procedures, codes and equipment, for example ASME Section V, AWS D1.1, API 1104, or the employer's aerospace and marine procedures.
  6. Practical exam on flawed specimens, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision exam for near-vision acuity and colour contrast.
  8. Employer certification based on documented training, experience and exams.
  9. Recertification at the interval in your written practice, with current vision tests.

Read more about SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Florida requirements

Direct answer: Florida is an NRC Agreement State and was one of the earliest, in 1964. The Florida Department of Health's Bureau of Radiation Control licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, and registers radiation machines. Boilers fall under the Division of State Fire Marshal's Boiler Safety Program; intrastate gas pipeline safety under the Florida Public Service Commission.

Industrial radiography

Because Florida is an Agreement State, companies performing industrial radiography with radioactive sources hold a Florida radioactive materials licence rather than an NRC licence, and industrial X-ray equipment is registered with the state. Florida's industrial radiography rules follow the federal model in 10 CFR Part 34: radiation safety training, a radiation safety exam, a supervised period as a radiographer's assistant, recognised radiographer certification, personnel dosimetry and survey instruments, and strict source security. Out-of-state licensees working in Florida use reciprocity. Atlantis RT method training under SNT-TC-1A covers technique, exposure and film and digital interpretation; it is separate from, and does not replace, the radiation safety training and radiographer certification required by Florida rules. Confirm current requirements with the Bureau of Radiation Control before mobilising a crew.

Boilers and pressure vessels

Florida's Boiler Safety Act (Chapter 554, Florida Statutes) is administered by the Department of Financial Services, Division of State Fire Marshal, Bureau of Fire Prevention, through its Boiler Safety Program. Florida's programme focuses on boilers in public assembly locations and applies ASME and National Board rules. Repair and alteration work on boilers and pressure vessels requires NDT to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's programme.

Pipelines

Interstate natural gas pipelines are regulated by PHMSA. The Florida Public Service Commission enforces pipeline safety rules for intrastate gas systems. Pipeline welding inspection follows API 1104 and ASME B31.8.

Aerospace, marine and nuclear

FAA repair stations, military depots and launch providers set their own NDT personnel requirements, often referencing NAS 410 or military standards in addition to SNT-TC-1A. Shipyards work to NAVSEA technical publications for naval work and ABS rules for commercial vessels. Turkey Point and St. Lucie are NRC-licensed, with in-service inspection to ASME Section XI. Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A method training as the foundation; additional programme-specific qualifications are managed by the employer.

Codes Florida employers commonly use

  • ASME Section V, Section VIII, B31.1 and B31.3 in power and chemical plants
  • ASME Section XI for nuclear in-service inspection
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for bridges
  • API 1104 and ASME B31.8 for gas pipelines
  • NAVSEA and ABS requirements in shipyards (context)
  • NAS 410 for aerospace suppliers (context)

Some Florida employers also ask for CWI or API credentials; those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Florida

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Florida. Classroom training is delivered live online or live-virtual, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility, on your equipment and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight.

Individual technicians join online NDT training for Level I and Level II classroom hours: live sessions with a Level III instructor covering principles, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation. Practical training and exams then happen with your employer.

Employers training a group typically choose onsite delivery. We bring classroom and practical sessions to your hangar, shipyard, plant or shop and build the course around your procedures and parts. A Miami repair station trains ET and PT on its own components; a Jacksonville ship repair contractor trains VT and MT on hull and deck welds; a Tampa chemical plant trains UT thickness and PAUT on its own piping.

Florida scheduling has its own rhythm: hurricane season from June through November can disrupt plans, power plant outages are usually scheduled in spring and fall to avoid peak summer demand, and launch and aircraft overhaul schedules drive aerospace availability. We plan cohorts around those windows and can shift sessions to live online when weather intervenes. Multi-site programmes run through corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Florida crew.

For Florida employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: every Florida employer certifying NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and Level III oversight. Atlantis NDT writes and revises written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams and provides Level III services for companies without an in-house Level III.

Florida has many small and mid-sized repair stations, machine shops, fabricators and marine contractors that employ certified technicians but not a Level III. Customer audits by airlines, primes, shipyards and utilities often find gaps: undocumented training hours, practical exams without graded checklists, expired vision tests, or written practices that do not reflect actual work.

  • Written practice development to the current SNT-TC-1A edition and your customers' requirements: written practice development.
  • Exam administration with traceable records under Level III oversight.
  • Procedure review against ASME, AWS, API and customer specifications.
  • Audit preparation for customer, quality-system and ISO 9001 audits.
  • Corporate programmes via corporate NDT training.

See also NDT consulting in Florida and SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Florida company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Practical NDT simulator lets Florida trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before their practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace a practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. The aircraft hangar fits Florida particularly well, from Miami MRO to Jacksonville and Pensacola naval aviation; the welding workshop maps to shipyards and fabrication; the storage tank to port terminals and phosphate plants. See the Practical NDT in Florida page and city pages for Miami, Jacksonville, Tampa, Orlando and Pensacola. For written-exam practice, use UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Direct answer: Florida programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop designs the courses, leads instruction and oversees exams and records so certification holds up under SNT-TC-1A and customer audits. He ties method theory to the parts, codes and procedures your Florida team uses. Ask about scheduling a Florida programme.

NDT training in Florida: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Florida?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete classroom training, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and a vision test. Online training covers the classroom portion; practical work and exams happen with your employer.

Is there NDT training online in Florida?

Yes. Atlantis runs live online and live-virtual Level I and II classes that Florida technicians can join from anywhere in the state.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Florida?

Florida is an Agreement State. The company needs a Florida radioactive materials licence (or registration for X-ray equipment), and radiographers and assistants must meet state training, exam, supervision and certification requirements. Confirm current rules with the Bureau of Radiation Control.

How much does NDT training cost in Florida?

Quoted on request. Cost depends on the method and level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and any written practice or exam support. We return a quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Florida?

Aerospace and MRO make ET and PT unusually important in Florida, alongside UT, which is used everywhere from shipyards to power plants. PAUT is growing in power and pipeline work, and MT and VT are core shipyard and construction methods.

Are there oil refineries in Florida?

No. Florida's NDT work comes from aerospace, MRO, shipyards, power, phosphate chemicals, ports, pipelines and construction rather than refining.

Can you train our crew onsite in Miami, Jacksonville or Tampa?

Yes. We deliver onsite anywhere in Florida, on your equipment and parts, scheduled around outages, overhauls and hurricane season.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted by Florida aerospace employers?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used, but many aerospace customers also reference NAS 410. Your employer's written practice determines which applies; we train to SNT-TC-1A and help document extra requirements.

How long does Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and the method. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Florida?

No. Training is delivered live online and onsite at your facility.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in Florida?

Yes. See ASNT Level III training for exam preparation options delivered online.

Do you offer CWI or API training in Florida?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only.

Start NDT training in Florida

From Miami repair stations and Space Coast launch suppliers to Jacksonville shipyards, Tampa power and chemical plants and Panhandle aviation contractors, Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training online and onsite across Florida. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Request your Florida NDT training quote, explore NDT training programmes, or start with online NDT training.

NDT Training and Certification in Georgia

Short answer: Georgia technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, in live-virtual cohorts, or onsite at their own hangar, plant, shipyard or construction site, led and overseen by an ASNT NDT Level III. Your employer certifies you under its written practice. Atlantis has no training centre in Georgia; delivery is online or at your facility.

Georgia's NDT market looks very different from the Gulf Coast or the Great Lakes. Its heaviest demand comes from aerospace (business jets in Savannah, military airlifters in Marietta, depot maintenance at Robins Air Force Base, airline heavy maintenance in Atlanta and engine work in Columbus), from nuclear power (Plant Vogtle, the only US site with four operating units, and Plant Hatch), from ports and LNG on the coast, from a fast-growing automotive and battery manufacturing belt, and from pulp and paper mills across the south of the state. Pipelines that carry fuel from the Gulf Coast to the East Coast also pass through metro Atlanta. This page explains how Atlantis NDT training works for Georgia, what Georgia employers need, how Georgia regulates radiography, and how to request a Georgia training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in Georgia

Direct answer: Georgia NDT work clusters in metro Atlanta (airline MRO, aerospace manufacturing, construction, pipelines), coastal Georgia around Savannah and Brunswick (business-jet manufacturing, ports, LNG, shipbuilding, a new automotive plant), Middle Georgia (Robins AFB depot maintenance, power), the Augusta and Waynesboro area (nuclear), West Georgia and Columbus (engines, automotive) and South Georgia (paper mills, Plant Hatch, military bases).

Metro Atlanta and Marietta

Delta TechOps at Hartsfield-Jackson is one of the largest airline maintenance, repair and overhaul operations in North America, and airline MRO is NDT-heavy: eddy current on fastener holes and skins, ultrasonic inspection of composites and bonded structures, penetrant and magnetic particle on landing-gear and engine parts, and visual inspection everywhere. Lockheed Martin's Marietta site builds the C-130J and supports other aircraft programmes, adding aerospace manufacturing NDT under prime-contractor specifications. Beyond aerospace, metro Atlanta has a huge construction market (data centres, stadiums, high-rise and hospital work) where AWS D1.1 structural steel inspection, UT of welds and VT are in demand, plus GDOT bridge work and the Colonial and Plantation pipelines that run through the metro area to the Northeast. See NDT training in Atlanta.

Coastal Georgia: Savannah, Ellabell and Brunswick

Gulfstream Aerospace's headquarters and main manufacturing and service centre in Savannah make the city a major aerospace NDT employer base, with composites UT, eddy current, penetrant and radiography on airframes and components. The Port of Savannah is one of the busiest container ports in the US, with cranes, terminals and heavy structures, and Kinder Morgan's Elba Island LNG terminal adds cryogenic tank and piping work. Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America at Ellabell in Bryan County and its suppliers are building out a large automotive and battery cluster west of Savannah. Brunswick has the Port of Brunswick, roll-on/roll-off vehicle terminals and pulp and paper, and Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay near St. Marys adds naval maintenance work under NAVSEA requirements. See NDT training in Savannah and aerospace NDT training in Savannah.

Middle Georgia: Warner Robins and Macon

Robins Air Force Base hosts the Warner Robins Air Logistics Complex, which performs depot maintenance on large military aircraft such as the C-130, C-5, C-17 and F-15. Depot maintenance relies heavily on eddy current, ultrasonic, penetrant, magnetic particle and radiographic inspection, under military technical orders and contractor procedures. Contractors and suppliers around Warner Robins and Macon employ NDT technicians for that work. Georgia Power's Plant Scherer near Juliette adds power-plant outage work.

Augusta and Waynesboro

Plant Vogtle in Burke County, near Waynesboro, has four nuclear units including the two newest reactors in the US. Nuclear in-service inspection under ASME Section XI, ET of steam-generator tubing, UT of piping welds and VT of supports and components is outage-driven work that pulls in many contract technicians. Augusta is also across the river from the Savannah River Site in South Carolina, and the area has chemical, paper and manufacturing plants.

Columbus and West Georgia

Pratt and Whitney's Columbus Engine Center overhauls and manufactures aero-engine parts, which brings penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic inspection of rotating parts. Kia's plant at West Point and its suppliers add automotive manufacturing and welding work.

South Georgia

Southern Nuclear's Plant Hatch near Baxley is Georgia's second nuclear site. South Georgia is also home to many pulp and paper mills, where recovery boilers, digesters and pressure vessels need regular UT, MT, PT and VT, plus military installations such as Moody AFB near Valdosta and the Marine Corps Logistics Base at Albany.

For any of these regions you can ask about onsite training for your Georgia crew.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Georgia employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT teaches UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and II, plus Level III exam preparation, to ASNT SNT-TC-1A and your written practice. Here is how each method maps to Georgia work.

Atlanta. Airline MRO and aerospace manufacturing dominate the specialist end of the market, while construction and infrastructure dominate volume. A technician who wants a long Atlanta career often holds ET and UT for aerospace work, or UT and VT with structural-steel code knowledge for construction. See the Atlanta training page.

Savannah. Gulfstream and its supplier base, the port, the LNG terminal and the new Hyundai cluster give Savannah unusually diverse NDT demand for a mid-sized city. Onsite training works well for supplier plants that need several technicians qualified at once.

Augusta. Vogtle outages create surges of nuclear inspection work; contractor technicians often study theory online between outages. Paper and chemical plants provide steadier, year-round demand.

Warner Robins and Macon. Depot maintenance on military aircraft is ET-, UT- and PT-heavy and works under technical orders. Our SNT-TC-1A training covers the method fundamentals those programmes build on.

Columbus and Brunswick. Engine overhaul in Columbus means PT, ET and UT on rotating parts; Brunswick and Kings Bay add marine, port and paper-mill work.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Georgia, step by step

Direct answer: Georgia does not certify NDT technicians. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you meet its written practice: training hours, experience, general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and a vision test.

  1. The written practice. Your employer's document, based on SNT-TC-1A, sets methods, levels, training and experience, exams and recertification. No practice yet? See written practice development.
  2. Formal classroom training. Hours per method and level per the written practice; see the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline figures.
  3. On-the-job experience. Logged in the method on the work you will perform, under qualified supervision.
  4. General, specific and practical exams. Prepared and administered by a Level III; practicals are performed on real specimens.
  5. Vision tests. Annual near-vision acuity and colour contrast as required.
  6. Employer certification. Documented and valid with that employer.
  7. Recertification. At the interval and by the method the practice defines.

The ASNT NDT Level III certificate is issued by ASNT through examination; the employer then certifies its Level III. More on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Georgia requirements

Direct answer: Georgia is an NRC Agreement State, and has been since 1969. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources in Georgia is licensed and inspected by the Radioactive Materials Program of the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD) under the Georgia Rules and Regulations for Radioactive Materials, Chapter 391-3-17, rather than by the NRC.

Georgia's rules for industrial radiography (Rule 391-3-17-.04) are compatible with the NRC's 10 CFR Part 34 and cover radiation-safety training, radiographer and radiographer-trainee qualification, personnel monitoring, survey instruments, field crews and recordkeeping. Industrial radiography licensees are in the programme's highest inspection-frequency category, and the programme administers an industrial radiographer examination route. X-ray equipment is handled separately from radioactive-materials licensing; ask the state which office covers your equipment. Out-of-state radiography companies bringing isotope cameras into Georgia need to address reciprocity before working. Radiation-safety training and radiographer certification are separate from SNT-TC-1A RT method training, which teaches technique and interpretation; your crew needs both. Confirm current requirements with Georgia EPD before field work.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Georgia's Boilers and Pressure Vessels programme is administered by the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire. Georgia adopts ASME and National Board codes, so ASME Section V NDT and Section I or VIII acceptance criteria apply to new construction, and National Board Inspection Code rules apply to repairs.

Pipelines. The Georgia Public Service Commission oversees intrastate natural gas pipeline safety; interstate gas lines and hazardous-liquid lines such as the Colonial and Plantation pipelines are regulated by PHMSA. Weld inspection generally follows API 1104 and operator qualification programmes.

Codes common in Georgia. ASME Section XI at Vogtle and Hatch; ASME Section I and B31.1 in power and paper; ASME V, VIII and B31.3 in process plants and LNG; AWS D1.1 in construction and AASHTO/AWS D1.5 on GDOT bridges; API 1104 on pipelines; NAVSEA requirements at Kings Bay; and aerospace specifications such as NAS 410 and military technical orders in aviation (context only).

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Georgia

Direct answer: Georgia crews can take Atlantis NDT theory live online or in live-virtual cohorts, or receive Level III-led training onsite at their facility. Practical exams always use real specimens under Level III oversight.

Georgia scheduling has its own patterns. Nuclear refuelling outages at Vogtle and Hatch pull contract technicians into intense multi-week assignments, so online theory between outages is the practical option. Airline MRO and depot maintenance run year-round on shift patterns, so evening or split-shift online sessions suit those technicians. Construction work is steady but deadline-driven, and onsite sessions at a fabrication yard or shop fit between pours and erection sequences. Paper mills schedule annual outages, and summer heat and hurricane season on the coast affect field work in Savannah and Brunswick. Onsite delivery uses your equipment, procedures and parts, and suits supplier plants in the new automotive cluster that need several technicians qualified quickly. Read about online NDT training and corporate NDT training, then request a cohort or onsite quote for Georgia; we reply within one business day.

For Georgia employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Georgia employers that certify their own NDT staff need an SNT-TC-1A written practice, a qualified Level III and clean records. Atlantis NDT writes and reviews written practices, provides Level III services and runs corporate training programmes for Georgia companies.

New manufacturing plants and their suppliers are a particular focus in Georgia right now. A supplier setting up near Savannah or in West Georgia may need to stand up an NDT function quickly, with a written practice, procedures, trained staff and exams, to satisfy an automotive or aerospace customer. Established companies often need a review because their practice has drifted from what they actually do. We help with:

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A.
  • Level III services, procedures and exam administration; see NDT consulting in Georgia.
  • Corporate training programmes for multi-site Georgia employers.
  • Guidance on SNT-TC-1A certification.

Planning a new NDT function or facing an audit? Book a Level III consultation for your Georgia company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets Georgia trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments before the hands-on exam. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The aircraft hangar environment is especially relevant in Georgia, matching airline MRO in Atlanta, business-jet work in Savannah and depot maintenance in Warner Robins. The welding workshop matches construction and fabrication, and the oil and gas site and storage tank environments match pipeline, LNG and process work. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT Georgia.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, written practices, exams and Level III services for Georgia clients.

NDT training in Georgia: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Georgia?

Join or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the training hours and experience it requires, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass the vision test. Your employer then certifies you.

Is there NDT training online in Georgia?

Yes. Theory for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET is available live online anywhere in Georgia; practical exams use real specimens under Level III oversight.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Georgia?

Georgia is an Agreement State, so the radiography company must hold a Georgia EPD radioactive-materials licence for isotope work, and radiographers must be trained and qualified under Georgia's rules. Confirm details with Georgia EPD's Radioactive Materials Program.

How much does NDT training cost in Georgia?

Training is quoted on request based on method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery and any written-practice support. Quotes are returned within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Georgia?

ET and UT for aerospace MRO and manufacturing, UT and VT for construction, and ET, UT and VT for nuclear outages. PT is widely used in aero-engine work.

Can you train our crew onsite in Savannah or Atlanta?

Yes. Onsite training is available at your Georgia facility, subject to your site access and safety requirements.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Georgia employers?

Yes, across construction, power, process and much of manufacturing. Aerospace and military work may reference NAS 410 or technical orders, so check your customer's requirement.

How long does Level II take?

It depends on the written practice, the method and your experience. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline hours.

Can I get NDT jobs in aviation in Georgia with SNT-TC-1A training?

SNT-TC-1A method training is a strong foundation, and many aviation employers then qualify you to their own aerospace system. Ask the employer which standard it uses.

Can I take NDT training without an employer?

Yes, classroom training can be taken as an individual. Certification still requires an employer and its written practice.

Do you offer ASNT Level III exam preparation in Georgia?

Yes, online. See ASNT Level III training.

What does an NDT technician earn in Georgia?

Pay varies by method, level, sector and travel. See our NDT salary guide.

NDT Training and Certification in Illinois

Short answer: Illinois technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual sessions, or onsite delivery at their own plant, shop, rail yard or outage site. We offer Level I and II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation, all led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Your employer certifies you under its written practice, and we can build or review that written practice too.

Illinois is an unusual NDT state. It runs more nuclear reactors than any other state in the country, it has four large refineries split between the Chicago area and the south of the state, it is the busiest rail crossroads in North America, and it is home to heavy-equipment, agricultural-machinery and aerospace-component manufacturing that depends on weld and casting inspection. Downstate, Patoka is one of the country's key crude-oil hubs, and pipelines run across the state in every direction. Each of those industries wants something different from its NDT people. This page explains how training and certification work in Illinois, what the state's regulators expect, where the work is, and how to get a quote. Request an Illinois NDT training quote and we reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Illinois

Direct answer: Illinois NDT work clusters in the Chicago metro and Will County refining and manufacturing belt, the northern Illinois nuclear corridor, the Rockford aerospace cluster, the Peoria and Quad Cities heavy-equipment region, the central Illinois agri-processing and power region around Decatur and Springfield, and the Metro East refining and pipeline hub across the river from St. Louis.

Chicago metro and Will County

The Chicago area combines two refineries in the southwest suburbs (near Joliet and Lemont), chemical plants, tank terminals, steel service centres, large fabrication shops and some of the densest construction activity in the Midwest. Refinery turnarounds bring heavy seasonal demand for UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT weld inspection, RT of piping welds, VT of pressure equipment and ET of heat exchanger tubing. Construction projects downtown and in the suburbs use structural steel welded to AWS D1.1, which leans on VT, UT and MT. Chicago's movable bridges, elevated rail structures and expressway bridges add fabrication and in-service inspection work under the AWS D1.5 Bridge Welding Code. O'Hare is also a major airline hub with associated maintenance activity.

The northern Illinois nuclear corridor

Illinois has six operating nuclear stations: Braidwood, Byron, Dresden, LaSalle, Quad Cities and, in central Illinois, Clinton. Refuelling outages bring large in-service inspection programmes under ASME Section XI, with UT of piping and vessel welds, ET of steam generator and heat exchanger tubing, VT of components and supports, and PT and MT on repairs. Outage contractors need technicians whose certification records are clean, current and auditable, and nuclear quality programmes are among the strictest that SNT-TC-1A-certified personnel work under.

Rockford and the aerospace cluster

Rockford has long been one of the country's important aerospace-component centres, with makers of aircraft actuation, power, fuel and control systems and a deep base of precision machining and special-process suppliers. Those suppliers rely on PT, MT, ET and UT done under tightly controlled written practices, often with customer aerospace requirements such as NAS 410 referenced alongside SNT-TC-1A.

Peoria, the Quad Cities and heavy equipment

Peoria and East Peoria are synonymous with earth-moving equipment, and the Quad Cities (Moline and Rock Island) are home to agricultural-equipment manufacturing and the Rock Island Arsenal. Heavy welded frames, booms, axles, castings and forgings need MT, UT and VT, and large welding programmes need inspectors who understand AWS D1.1 and company weld standards. The arsenal adds defence manufacturing work.

Central Illinois: Decatur, Springfield and Champaign

Decatur is an agri-processing city with large corn and soybean processing plants and heavy-equipment manufacturing. Agri-processing plants run boilers, pressure vessels, steam piping and storage tanks that need routine UT thickness, VT and MT/PT on repairs. Springfield, the state capital, has municipal and regional power generation, state agencies and rail. Ethanol plants and grain facilities across central Illinois add tank and pressure equipment inspection.

Southern Illinois and the Metro East

The Metro East, across the Mississippi from St. Louis, holds a large refinery at Wood River and Roxana, petroleum terminals and chemical plants. Further south and east, Robinson has another refinery, and Patoka is a major crude-oil storage and pipeline hub where several large crude pipelines terminate or interconnect. Pipeline construction and integrity work across the region follows API 1104 and ASME B31.4 and B31.8, generating RT, UT and VT demand. Scott Air Force Base near Belleville adds aerospace and defence activity, and coal-fired and gas-fired power plants dot the southern half of the state.

Rail, barges and transportation

Chicago is the meeting point of the major North American freight railroads, and rail car shops, locomotive facilities and component suppliers across Illinois use UT, MT and ET on axles, wheels, couplers and welded car structures. Barge terminals on the Illinois and Mississippi rivers and the Illinois Department of Transportation's bridge inventory add structural inspection work.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Illinois employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table shows each method, the levels available, how Illinois employers use it, and prerequisites. Your employer's written practice sets the exact hours and experience.

Illinois employers often stack methods. An outage contractor might certify a new hire in VT Level I and II, then UT, then ET as they gain outage experience. A heavy-equipment plant might certify welding inspectors in VT and MT first, then UT for critical welds. We plan these pathways around your written practice. For Level III candidates, see ASNT Level III training and exam preparation.

NDT training by city in Illinois

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT serves every Illinois city through online and onsite delivery, with dedicated training pages for Chicago and Springfield and simulator practice pages for Chicago, Rockford, Peoria and Decatur. Chicago. Chicago demand is the broadest in the state: refinery and terminal contractors need UT, PAUT, RT and ET technicians; construction inspection firms need VT and UT inspectors for structural steel; bridge fabricators need AWS D1.5-qualified UT and MT; and fabrication shops need a clean written practice. Many Chicago employers want live-virtual classroom sessions so technicians can stay on their shifts. See the Chicago NDT training page.

Springfield. Springfield sits in the middle of central Illinois, where power plants, rail and state infrastructure drive steady UT, MT and VT work. It is also within reach of the Clinton nuclear station and central Illinois agri-processing plants. See the Springfield NDT training page.

Rockford. Rockford's aerospace supply chain needs PT, MT and ET technicians certified under well-documented written practices, often with additional customer requirements. Precision machining and special-process shops are frequent clients for written practice and exam administration support.

Peoria and the Quad Cities. Heavy welded structures and castings mean MT and UT dominate, along with VT for large welding programmes. Plants often want onsite training on their own parts so inspectors learn exactly the indications they will see on the line.

Decatur. Agri-processing plants run boilers, steam systems, pressure vessels and tanks, so UT thickness, VT and MT/PT dominate. Heavy-equipment manufacturing adds weld inspection.

Joliet, Lemont and the Metro East. These are Illinois's refining towns. Turnaround season pulls in contractors from across the Midwest, and companies often want a cohort certified in UT, PAUT or RT just before the work starts.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Illinois, step by step

Direct answer: Illinois follows the national, employer-based model for NDT certification. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. Radiographers also need state certification from IEMA.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A that defines hours, exams, vision requirements and recertification. We can write it; see written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete Level I, then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. On-the-job experience. Log documented, supervised experience hours in the method.
  4. General exam. Written exam on method principles.
  5. Specific exam. Covers the procedures, codes and equipment you actually use, such as ASME Section V, ASME Section XI for nuclear work, AWS D1.1 or API 1104.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on demonstration on flawed specimens, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast checks.
  8. Employer certification. Your employer issues certification based on documented training, experience and exams.
  9. For radiographers: state certification. Industrial radiographers in Illinois must also hold radiographer certification issued by IEMA, in addition to SNT-TC-1A method certification.
  10. Recertification. Recertify at the interval in your written practice and keep vision tests current.

Read more on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Illinois requirements

Direct answer: Illinois is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, are licensed by the Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security (IEMA-OHS) under Title 32 of the Illinois Administrative Code, and IEMA issues its own certification for industrial radiographers. Boilers fall under the Office of the State Fire Marshal; intrastate pipelines under the Illinois Commerce Commission.

Industrial radiography

Illinois has been an Agreement State since the late 1980s, so state rather than federal regulators license radioactive material use inside Illinois. Companies performing industrial radiography need an IEMA licence or registration, and their radiation safety programme must describe initial, periodic and on-the-job training for radiographic personnel. Illinois goes further than many states by issuing its own radiographer certification under Title 32: individuals who perform or personally supervise industrial radiography must hold IEMA radiographer certification. Radiographer's assistants must complete required training and work under supervision. Out-of-state licensees use reciprocity to work in Illinois. Atlantis RT training covers the SNT-TC-1A method side (technique, exposure, film and digital interpretation); it complements but does not replace the radiation safety training and state certification steps. Always confirm current requirements with IEMA-OHS before a crew starts work.

Boilers and pressure vessels

The Office of the Illinois State Fire Marshal administers boiler and pressure vessel safety through its Division of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety. Illinois adopts the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board inspection rules, so repair and alteration work needs NDT to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme.

Pipelines

Interstate pipelines are regulated by PHMSA. Intrastate gas pipeline safety in Illinois is enforced by the Illinois Commerce Commission's pipeline safety programme. With the Patoka hub and major crude and products lines crossing the state, API 1104 radiography and UT, ASME B31.4 and B31.8, and operator-specific procedures are central to pipeline NDT work.

Nuclear

Nuclear power plants themselves are licensed by the NRC regardless of Agreement State status. In-service inspection at Illinois's six stations follows ASME Section XI, with performance-demonstration requirements for some UT examinations. Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A method training as a foundation; nuclear-specific qualifications are handled by the licensee's programme.

Codes Illinois employers commonly use

  • ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3 in refining and chemicals
  • ASME Section XI for nuclear in-service inspection
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and heavy equipment; AWS D1.5 for bridges
  • API 1104 and ASME B31.4/B31.8 for pipelines
  • NAS 410 as aerospace supplier context in Rockford (Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A)

Some employers also ask for API inspector or CWI credentials for specific roles; those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Illinois

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Illinois. Classroom training is delivered live online or live-virtual, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight, using your equipment and specimens.

Individual technicians use online NDT training for the classroom portion of Level I and Level II: live sessions with a Level III instructor covering principles, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation. Practical hours and exams then happen with your employer.

Employers with a group usually prefer onsite delivery. We run sessions at your plant, shop, rail facility or contractor yard, build the course around your procedures, and use your instruments, calibration blocks and part samples. A Peoria plant trains MT and UT on its own welded frames; a Chicago-area refinery contractor trains UT and PAUT on piping mock-ups; a Rockford supplier trains PT and ET on its own components.

Illinois scheduling revolves around nuclear refuelling outages (spring and fall at most stations), refinery turnarounds, the summer construction season and winter production shutdowns. We schedule cohorts to finish before each window. Multi-site programmes run through corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Illinois crew.

For Illinois employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: every Illinois NDT employer certifying personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and Level III oversight. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams and provides Level III services to companies without an in-house Level III.

Illinois has many mid-sized manufacturers and fabricators that need certified NDT personnel but do not employ a Level III. Common audit findings include missing training-hour records, practical exams without graded checklists, expired vision tests and written practices that do not reflect actual work. Nuclear and aerospace customers in particular expect records that stand up to scrutiny.

  • Written practice development to the current SNT-TC-1A edition and your customers' requirements: written practice development.
  • Exam administration under Level III oversight with traceable records.
  • Procedure review against ASME, AWS and API.
  • Audit preparation for customer, ASME, National Board and ISO 9001 audits.
  • Corporate programmes through corporate NDT training.

See also NDT consulting in Illinois and SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Illinois company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Practical NDT simulator lets Illinois trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before the practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique and indications; it is practice only and does not replace a practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. For Illinois work, the welding workshop maps to heavy-equipment and bridge fabrication, the hangar to Rockford's aerospace chain and airline maintenance, the oil and gas site to refinery and pipeline work, and the storage tank to terminals and agri-processing. See the Practical NDT in Illinois page plus city pages for Chicago, Rockford, Peoria and Decatur. For written-exam practice, try UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Direct answer: Illinois programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop designs the courses, delivers Level III-led instruction, and oversees exams and records so that certification is defensible under SNT-TC-1A. His approach ties method theory to the codes, procedures and parts your Illinois crew uses every day. Ask about scheduling an Illinois programme.

NDT training in Illinois: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Illinois?

Your employer certifies you under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Complete classroom training, log documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. If you will perform radiography, you also need IEMA radiographer certification.

Is there NDT training online in Illinois?

Yes. Atlantis runs live online and live-virtual Level I and II classes for Illinois technicians. Practical training and exams are completed onsite with your employer.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Illinois?

Yes. Illinois is an Agreement State; the company needs an IEMA licence or registration, and individuals who perform or supervise industrial radiography need IEMA radiographer certification. Assistants must be trained and supervised. Confirm current rules with IEMA-OHS.

How much does NDT training cost in Illinois?

Quoted on request. Cost depends on method and level, group size, online or onsite delivery, and whether you need exam administration or written practice support. We return a quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Illinois?

UT is the broadest, used in refining, nuclear, heavy equipment and rail. ET and VT are heavily used during nuclear outages, MT dominates heavy equipment, PT is central in Rockford aerospace, and RT stays important on pipelines.

Can you train our crew onsite in Chicago, Peoria or Rockford?

Yes. We deliver onsite anywhere in Illinois, on your equipment and parts, scheduled around outages, turnarounds and production.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Illinois employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer certification in US refining, power, fabrication and manufacturing, and many aerospace suppliers use it alongside customer requirements.

How long does Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and the method. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimum classroom and experience hours; see the training requirements matrix.

Can I work at an Illinois nuclear plant with SNT-TC-1A certification?

Nuclear outage contractors certify personnel under their own programmes, often based on SNT-TC-1A or ASNT CP-189, plus additional qualifications for some UT examinations. SNT-TC-1A method training is a common foundation.

Do you offer CWI or API training in Illinois?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Illinois?

No. Training is delivered live online and onsite at your facility.

Can you help us become a Level III?

Yes. We offer ASNT Level III exam preparation; see ASNT Level III training.
