NDT Training and Certification in Indiana

Short answer: Indiana technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, in live-virtual cohorts, or onsite at their own mill, refinery, plant or shop, with an ASNT NDT Level III leading and overseeing the programme. Certification is employer-based and follows your company written practice. Atlantis has no training centre in Indiana; we teach online or travel to your facility.

Indiana is the most steel-intensive state in the country and one of the most manufacturing-intensive. Northwest Indiana's lakefront holds integrated steel mills and the largest inland refinery in the US, Central Indiana builds aircraft engines, transmissions and diesel engines, Southern Indiana runs coal and gas power stations, an aluminium smelter and a naval research centre, and Northern Indiana builds a large share of the country's recreational vehicles. Almost every one of those products depends on welds, castings, forgings or pressure equipment that someone has to inspect. This page explains how Atlantis NDT training works for Indiana, which methods Indiana employers rely on, how Indiana's radiography licensing is changing, and how to request an Indiana training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in Indiana

Direct answer: Indiana NDT demand is concentrated in Northwest Indiana (steel, refining, power, heavy fabrication), Central Indiana (aerospace engines, powertrain, pharma and construction), Northern Indiana (RV and trailer manufacturing, defence electronics, foundries), West Central Indiana (aerospace assembly, automotive, steel) and Southern Indiana (power generation, aluminium, a refinery and the Crane naval centre).

Northwest Indiana: Whiting, East Chicago, Gary, Burns Harbor and Michigan City

The Lake Michigan shoreline is one of the densest heavy-industry corridors in North America. BP's Whiting refinery is the largest refinery in the Midwest, and its turnarounds pull in large numbers of contract inspectors for UT thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD on pressure-vessel welds, radiography of piping welds and visual inspection of tanks and structures. The integrated steel mills, U.S. Steel's Gary Works and Cleveland-Cliffs' Indiana Harbor and Burns Harbor works, need inspection of blast-furnace components, cranes and crane rails, rolling-mill rolls and shafts, gas mains and structural steel, where MT, UT and VT are the daily methods. NIPSCO's generating stations at Michigan City and Wheatfield add boiler tube and header inspection during outages, and the Port of Indiana at Burns Harbor and the heavy fabrication shops around Portage, Hammond and LaPorte add structural welding work. See our Whiting NDT training page and manufacturing and fabrication NDT training in Gary.

Central Indiana: Indianapolis, Columbus and Kokomo

Indianapolis is home to Rolls-Royce's large aero-engine operation and to Allison Transmission, so aerospace-grade penetrant, eddy current, ultrasonic and radiographic inspection of rotating parts, castings and welded assemblies is a major source of demand, often under prime-contractor specifications. Cummins in Columbus designs and builds engines and components, which brings casting and machined-part inspection. Kokomo has transmission and casting plants and electronics manufacturing. The Indianapolis metro also has heavy construction, INDOT bridge and highway work, hospital and pharma construction with stainless process piping, and a large base of tooling and machine shops.

Northern Indiana: Elkhart, South Bend and Fort Wayne

Elkhart County builds a large share of North America's recreational vehicles, and the frames, chassis and trailer structures are welded steel and aluminium where VT, PT and MT support weld quality programmes. South Bend has a mix of aerospace and defence suppliers, foundries and manufacturers. Fort Wayne has GM's truck assembly plant, defence electronics and a long industrial history in wire, castings and copper products.

West Central Indiana: Lafayette and Crawfordsville

Lafayette has GE Aerospace's jet-engine assembly operation and Subaru's assembly plant, and Purdue University's engineering research presence adds aerospace and materials activity. Crawfordsville has Nucor's steel mill. Aerospace assembly and steel work make this a strong UT, ET, PT and MT region.

Southern Indiana: Evansville, Mount Vernon, Princeton and Crane

Southwest Indiana is an energy and heavy-process region. Power stations along the Ohio and Wabash rivers, including Gibson, Rockport and Edwardsport, need boiler, piping and structural inspection. Alcoa's Warrick operations near Newburgh and the CountryMark refinery at Mount Vernon add process inspection, and Toyota's Princeton plant adds automotive work. Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane in Martin County is a major defence engineering site. Indiana has no commercial nuclear power plant, so nuclear ISI is less of a factor here than in neighbouring states, although Indiana technicians often travel to outages in Illinois, Michigan and Ohio.

Wherever your crew works, you can ask about onsite training for your Indiana crew.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Indiana employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and II, plus Level III exam preparation, built around ASNT SNT-TC-1A and your written practice. The table shows how each method maps to Indiana work.

MethodLevelsWhat Indiana employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepThickness surveys at Whiting and Mount Vernon, steel-mill shafts and rolls, plate and weld inspection in fabrication, aero-engine and forging inspectionLevel I: per written practice. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, IIPressure-vessel and piping welds during refinery turnarounds, power-plant header welds, pipeline girth welds, corrosion mappingUT Level II recommended
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, IIHeavy-wall welds on vessels and fabrications, crack sizing in mill and plant equipmentUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, IIPiping and pipeline welds, castings at Indiana foundries, aerospace castings and welds, film and digital interpretationRadiation-safety training and the applicable state or federal radiographer qualification
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, IICrane hooks, rails, rolls and shafts in steel mills; forgings and powertrain parts; structural weldsPer written practice; vision test
Penetrant Testing (PT)I, IIAero-engine components, aluminium RV and trailer structures, stainless welds in pharma and food plantsPer written practice; vision and colour test
Visual Testing (VT)I, IIWeld quality in RV, trailer and structural fabrication; tanks and structures at refineries; bridge and highway steelPer written practice; near-vision acuity
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, IIAero-engine parts and fastener holes, condenser and heat-exchanger tubing at power plants and refineries, bar and tube inspection at millsBasic electrical knowledge helpful

Level III candidates in Indiana are often senior technicians in steel, refining or aerospace preparing for the ASNT Basic and a method exam, typically UT, RT or MT. See ASNT Level III training. UT Level II candidates can self-check with our UT Level 2 practice questions.

NDT training by city in Indiana

Direct answer: Indianapolis and Whiting have dedicated Atlantis NDT training pages, Gary has a manufacturing NDT training page, and several Indiana cities have Practical NDT simulator pages. Every Indiana city is served online or onsite at the employer's facility.

Indianapolis. Aerospace work dominates the higher-skill end of the Indianapolis NDT market, with penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic inspection of engine components under strict customer specifications. Construction and infrastructure work, including stadium, hospital and highway projects, adds structural VT and UT. See the Indianapolis training page.

Whiting and East Chicago. Refinery and steel work here is field work: scaffolds, confined spaces, high temperatures and turnaround schedules. Technicians need UT thickness and PAUT skills and a working knowledge of the codes behind API inspection programmes. We train the NDT side; we do not offer API inspector certification courses.

Gary and Burns Harbor. Steel-mill NDT is unusual: large forgings and rolls, heavy cranes, gas mains, furnaces and huge structures. MT and UT on cranes, shafts and rails are constant, and mills often want onsite training using their own components.

Evansville and Southwest Indiana. Power-plant outages, aluminium processing and the Mount Vernon refinery drive UT, ET of tubing, RT and VT. Online theory helps technicians who rotate between plants.

South Bend, Elkhart and Fort Wayne. High-volume welding in RV and trailer plants, truck assembly and defence suppliers means VT, PT and MT are the core methods, with UT for thicker structures.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Indiana, step by step

Direct answer: Indiana does not issue NDT certifications. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after you complete the training, experience, exams and vision test its written practice requires, with exams administered by a Level III.

  1. The employer's written practice. It defines methods, levels, training and experience requirements, exam content and grading, vision tests and recertification. If your Indiana company does not have one, see written practice development.
  2. Formal training. Classroom hours per method and level, set by the written practice from SNT-TC-1A recommendations. The training requirements matrix lists the guideline figures.
  3. On-the-job experience. Documented hours in the method, on the work you will be certified for, under qualified supervision.
  4. Examinations. General (theory), specific (your employer's procedures, codes and equipment) and practical (real specimens), administered by a Level III.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity annually and colour contrast as required.
  6. Certification by the employer. Documented and valid while you work for that employer under that written practice.
  7. Recertification. At the interval and by the method the written practice sets.

ASNT NDT Level III certification is issued by ASNT through examination; your employer then certifies you as its Level III. Read more on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Indiana requirements

Direct answer: Indiana's radioactive-materials licensing has recently been changing. Indiana has moved to become an NRC Agreement State, with the Indiana Department of Homeland Security (IDHS) taking over licensing of byproduct, source and certain special nuclear materials from the NRC. Confirm the current licensing authority with the state before planning isotope radiography work in Indiana.

For many years, industrial radiography using isotope sources in Indiana was licensed directly by the US NRC under 10 CFR Part 34, through NRC Region III. Under the new Agreement State arrangement, the state assumes that role and adopts rules compatible with the NRC's, and existing NRC licences are converted to Indiana licences. For a radiography company this affects who issues and inspects your licence, where you send amendments and reports, and which rulebook your radiation-safety programme cites. What does not change is the substance: radiographers and radiographer trainees need radiation-safety training, an approved certification route, personnel dosimetry, calibrated survey meters and crew arrangements compatible with the federal rules. X-ray equipment is registered separately with the state. Because this transition is recent, confirm the current licensing authority and forms with IDHS before a new crew starts field work.

Our RT method training covers technique, exposure calculations, film and digital imaging and interpretation. It is not a substitute for the radiation-safety training and radiographer certification the licence requires; your crew needs both.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Indiana's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety programme sits within IDHS's Division of Fire and Building Safety. Indiana adopts ASME and National Board codes, so ASME Section V NDT and Section I or VIII acceptance criteria apply to new construction, and National Board Inspection Code requirements apply to repairs and alterations.

Pipelines. The Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission's Pipeline Safety Division oversees intrastate gas pipelines; interstate gas and hazardous-liquid pipelines crossing Indiana are regulated by PHMSA. Weld inspection follows API 1104 and operator qualification programmes.

Codes common in Indiana. ASME V, VIII and B31.3 in refining; ASME Section I and B31.1 in power; AWS D1.1 for structural and mill steel; AASHTO/AWS D1.5 on INDOT bridges; API 1104 on pipelines; aerospace prime and NAS 410 requirements in engine work (context only); and automotive customer standards.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Indiana

Direct answer: Indiana crews can take Atlantis NDT theory live online or in live-virtual cohorts, or have the Level III-led course delivered onsite at their facility. Practical exams are performed on real specimens under Level III oversight in every case.

Indiana scheduling is driven by heavy industry. Steel mills run continuously, with planned outages on blast furnaces, casters and mills; refinery turnarounds at Whiting and Mount Vernon concentrate contractor demand into a few weeks; power plants schedule spring and autumn outages around peak demand; RV and automotive plants have model-year and summer shutdowns. We schedule theory before those peaks and practicals and specific exams during quieter weeks. Onsite delivery is the natural fit for mills and large plants: the instructor uses your equipment, procedures and real components, and the specific exam reflects your actual work. Live online theory suits contractors and smaller shops with one or two technicians per method, and works well in Southern and Northern Indiana where travel to Indianapolis or Chicago takes time.

See online NDT training and corporate NDT training, and request a cohort or onsite quote for Indiana; quotes are returned within one business day.

For Indiana employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Indiana employers that certify their own NDT personnel need an SNT-TC-1A written practice, a qualified Level III and auditable records. Atlantis NDT writes and reviews written practices, provides Level III services and runs corporate training programmes for Indiana companies.

Many Indiana fabricators, foundries and RV manufacturers do some NDT in-house without a full-time Level III, and only find out about documentation gaps during a customer audit or after a quality escape. Common gaps are training hours that do not match the practice, exams written or graded by someone who is not a Level III, missing practical exam records, expired vision tests, and procedures that no longer match the equipment in use. We help with:

  • Written practice development and review aligned to SNT-TC-1A and your customers' requirements.
  • Level III services: procedures, technique sheets, exam administration and audit preparation.
  • Corporate training programmes for multi-plant Indiana employers.
  • Guidance on SNT-TC-1A certification, and broader NDT consulting.

If an audit is approaching, book a Level III consultation for your Indiana company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets Indiana trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments before their hands-on exam. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The environments are an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Indiana users, the oil and gas site and storage tank match refinery and tank-farm work in Whiting and Mount Vernon, the welding workshop matches fabrication, RV and mill structural work, and the aircraft hangar matches aero-engine and aerospace work in Indianapolis and Lafayette. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT Indiana.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, written practices, exams and Level III services for Indiana clients.

NDT training in Indiana: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Indiana?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the required classroom training and experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass the vision test. The employer then certifies you.

Is there NDT training online in Indiana?

Yes. Theory for all eight methods can be taken live online anywhere in Indiana. Practical exams are done on real specimens under Level III oversight.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Indiana?

The company must hold the radioactive-materials licence or X-ray registration, and radiographers need radiation-safety training and certification. Indiana has recently moved to NRC Agreement State status with IDHS as the licensing agency; confirm the current licensing authority with the state.

How much does NDT training cost in Indiana?

Training is quoted on request. Method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery and any written-practice or exam support all affect the quote. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Indiana?

UT and MT are in constant demand in steel and fabrication; UT thickness and PAUT in refining and power; PT, ET and UT in aerospace engine work; VT everywhere welding is done.

Can you train our crew onsite in Gary or Whiting?

Yes. Onsite training is available at your facility anywhere in Indiana, including mills and refineries, subject to your site safety requirements.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Indiana employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most common basis for employer certification in Indiana steel, refining, power and fabrication. Aerospace customers may also reference NAS 410, so confirm your customer's requirement.

How long does UT Level II take?

It depends on your written practice and experience. Classroom and experience hours are both set by the practice; see the training requirements matrix.

Are there NDT jobs in Northwest Indiana?

The Whiting refinery, the integrated steel mills and the power and fabrication base make Northwest Indiana one of the busiest NDT regions in the Midwest, especially during turnarounds and outages.

Can I take NDT training without an employer?

Yes, you can complete classroom training as an individual. Certification still requires an employer and its written practice.

Do you prepare candidates for the ASNT Level III exams in Indiana?

Yes. Level III preparation for the Basic and method exams is available online. See ASNT Level III training.

What does an NDT technician earn in Indiana?

Pay depends on method, level, sector and overtime. See our NDT salary guide for published ranges.

Tell us your methods, levels, headcount and preferred delivery, and we will build the programme. Request your Indiana NDT training quote, see all training options, or start with the Practical NDT simulator. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

NDT Training and Certification in Kansas

Short answer: Kansas technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, as a private live-virtual cohort for one company, or onsite at the employer's hangar, refinery, plant or shop. Every course is led by an ASNT NDT Level III and built around the employer's written practice. Practical exams happen on real parts and welds at your own facility, so certification stays with the employer that issues it.

Kansas is two NDT markets in one state. Wichita, the self-styled Air Capital of the World, builds business jets, airliner fuselage sections and military aircraft modifications, and is surrounded by hundreds of aerospace machine shops, composite fabricators and special-process houses; much of its inspection work runs under aerospace certification schemes. The rest of the state is energy and agriculture: three refineries, the Conway natural gas liquids hub, thousands of miles of oil, gas and NGL pipelines, the Wolf Creek nuclear station, wind farms across the plains, grain elevators, ethanol and fertiliser plants, and rail lines carrying all of it. Add the Kansas City metro on the eastern border and the military posts at Fort Riley, Fort Leavenworth and McConnell, and Kansas needs every common NDT method. This hub maps that demand, lists the methods and levels Kansas employers use, covers radiography, boiler and pipeline regulation, and explains how to train a crew without taking it off the line. To get started, request a Kansas training quote and we will respond within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Kansas

Direct answer: Kansas NDT jobs concentrate in Wichita's aerospace manufacturing and MRO cluster; the refinery and midstream belt from El Dorado and McPherson to Coffeyville; the oil and gas fields of central and western Kansas; the Kansas City metro and Topeka manufacturing and rail base; and the power, military and agricultural-processing sites spread across the state. Aerospace and energy are the two big drivers.

Wichita and the aerospace corridor

Wichita's aircraft industry is the densest in the country for its size. Textron Aviation builds Cessna and Beechcraft aircraft here; the large aerostructures plant long operated by Spirit AeroSystems, which builds fuselage sections for commercial airliners, became part of Boeing again when Boeing completed its acquisition of Spirit; Bombardier operates a major facility; and McConnell Air Force Base flies KC-46 tankers. Around them sit machine shops, sheet-metal and composite fabricators, heat treaters, plating and special-process houses, and MRO shops that maintain business aircraft from across the country. Wichita State University's aviation research institute adds materials and structures testing. Aerospace NDT here is dominated by ultrasonic inspection of composite laminates and bonded structures, penetrant testing of machined and formed parts, eddy current for surface cracks, bolt holes and conductivity, magnetic particle on steel landing-gear and fitting components, and radiography of castings and assemblies. Most of these employers certify production inspectors to NAS 410, which shares its structure with SNT-TC-1A but adds aerospace-specific requirements. See aerospace NDT training in Wichita.

Refineries and the midstream belt

Kansas has three refineries: El Dorado, north-east of Wichita; McPherson in the centre of the state; and Coffeyville in the south-east, where a fertiliser plant sits beside the refinery. Each runs a mechanical integrity programme under OSHA process safety management (29 CFR 1910.119), with ultrasonic thickness surveys on piping circuits and vessels, shear-wave and phased array weld inspection on repairs, radiography of small-bore welds, magnetic particle and penetrant on nozzles and rotating equipment, and visual inspection at every turnaround. Near McPherson, the Conway hub stores and fractionates natural gas liquids in salt caverns and connects a web of NGL and products pipelines, bringing tank, vessel, piping and pipeline inspection. Crude and products pipelines and storage terminals run throughout the state, and construction or integrity digs on them call for API 1104 weld inspection, radiography and PAUT.

Oil and gas fields of central and western Kansas

Western Kansas sits over the Hugoton natural gas field, one of the largest in North America, and central Kansas has produced oil for more than a century. Field work includes compressor stations, gas processing plants, gathering lines, tank batteries and oilfield service shops that inspect tubulars, sucker rods and drilling components. The work is spread over long distances from Liberal, Garden City and Hays to Great Bend and Russell, which makes online theory followed by a short onsite practical the most practical way to train crews. Grain elevators, ethanol plants and meatpacking plants in the same towns add pressure vessel, boiler and structural inspection.

Kansas City, Kansas, Olathe, Lenexa and Topeka

The Kansas side of the Kansas City metro carries automotive assembly at Fairfax, one of the largest rail classification yards in the region, food processing, distribution and a cluster of engineering, utility and inspection firms in Johnson County that send crews across the Midwest. Fort Leavenworth sits upriver. Topeka adds tyre manufacturing, rail maintenance shops, food processing and state government, and Lawrence adds university research and light manufacturing. Rail shops need ultrasonic and magnetic particle inspection of wheels, axles and couplers and weld inspection of car repairs. See NDT training in Kansas City, which covers the whole metro, and Practical NDT in Topeka.

Power, wind, military and the rest of the state

The Wolf Creek Generating Station near Burlington is Kansas's nuclear plant, and its refuelling outages bring contractors working to ASME Section XI for ultrasonic weld examinations, eddy current of steam generator and heat exchanger tubing, and visual examinations. Coal and gas stations near Topeka, Lawrence and in the west run boiler and piping outages. Kansas is also one of the leading wind-energy states, and wind farm construction and maintenance bring structural weld, flange and bolt inspection. Fort Riley near Junction City and Manhattan supports army equipment maintenance, Salina and Hutchinson carry manufacturing and salt mining, and the Kansas Department of Transportation's steel bridge inventory keeps bridge weld inspection to AWS D1.5 active statewide.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Kansas employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation. In Kansas, aerospace employers lean on UT, PT, ET and MT; refineries, pipelines and the Conway hub lean on UT, PAUT, RT and VT; and power, rail and agricultural processing lean on UT, MT and ET.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Kansas, step by step

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A certification in Kansas is issued by your employer, not by the state, a school or ASNT. You complete the classroom training and supervised experience required by the employer's written practice, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, pass a vision test, and the employer certifies you. Aerospace employers using NAS 410 follow a similar but stricter route.

  1. Written practice first. The employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice defines training hours, experience hours, exams and recertification for each method and level. If you need one, we can write it.
  2. Formal training. Complete the classroom hours for your method and level. Typical figures are in the training requirements matrix; your written practice governs.
  3. Supervised experience. Log documented hours in the method under a certified technician. Refinery turnarounds build hours quickly; aerospace production cells build them steadily.
  4. General and specific exams. A Level III gives the theory exam and the specific exam on your employer's procedures, specifications and equipment.
  5. Practical exam. Inspect flawed specimens, record findings and be graded against a documented checklist.
  6. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, usually every year.
  7. Employer certification. Your employer certifies you to Level I or II in that method; it is valid while you work for that employer.
  8. Recertification. At the interval set in the written practice, by exam or by evidence of continuing satisfactory performance.

More detail: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Kansas requirements

Direct answer: Kansas has been an NRC Agreement State since January 1, 1965, so industrial radiography is licensed by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) Radiation Control Program under Kansas Administrative Regulations article 28-35, not directly by the NRC. Radiographers and trainees must meet those state rules in addition to their employer's SNT-TC-1A certification.

Kansas industrial radiography rules follow the structure of the federal rules in 10 CFR Part 34, as Agreement States must keep compatible regulations. The licensee needs a radiation safety officer, operating and emergency procedures and properly maintained and surveyed equipment; individuals complete radiation-safety training and work as trainees or assistants under a qualified radiographer before working independently; radiographers must be certified through a recognised certifying programme; and every person on a radiography job wears dosimetry and uses a calibrated survey meter. X-ray equipment used in Wichita aerospace shops and fabrication plants is registered and regulated by KDHE as well. Crews from Kansas City firms that cross into Missouri work under the NRC there, because Missouri is not an Agreement State. Rules change, so confirm current requirements with KDHE before planning an RT programme.

What Atlantis NDT covers: our RT courses teach radiographic technique, exposure calculation, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance criteria for SNT-TC-1A Level I and II. The state radiation-safety training and radiographer certification are separate obligations your radiation safety officer manages with KDHE; we help employers schedule the two side by side.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Kansas State Fire Marshal's Boiler Safety Unit inspects boilers and pressure vessels under the Kansas Boiler Safety Act, using National Board codes, and requires new, relocated and repaired units to be reported for inspection. NDT technicians meet this through repair and alteration work at refineries, power plants, ethanol and food plants under the National Board Inspection Code and ASME Sections I and VIII.

Pipelines. The Kansas Corporation Commission's pipeline safety programme oversees intrastate gas pipelines in partnership with PHMSA, which regulates interstate gas and hazardous liquid lines, including the NGL and crude systems around Conway. Pipeline weld inspection usually follows API 1104, and operator qualification rules apply to covered tasks.

Codes commonly used in Kansas. ASME Section V (NDE methods), Sections I and VIII (boilers and pressure vessels), B31.3 (process piping), B31.4 and B31.8 (pipelines), API 1104 (pipeline welding), API 650 and 653 context for tanks, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structural and bridge steel, AAR rules for rail cars, ASME Section XI at Wolf Creek, and NAS 410 for aerospace employers. Some Kansas employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials for specific roles. Those are separate schemes; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only, and we mention them so you can read local job postings accurately.

Refineries schedule turnarounds months ahead; aerospace production rates rise and fall with aircraft orders; harvest season ties up rural workforces and grain facilities in summer; pipeline and wind construction peak in the warmer months; and Wolf Creek runs outages on its own cycle. We typically suggest online theory in quieter weeks and a protected onsite practical block. Ask about onsite training for your Kansas crew.

NDT training in Kansas: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Kansas?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its classroom training and supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you. Aerospace employers in Wichita may certify you to NAS 410 instead.

Is there NDT training online in Kansas?

Yes. Atlantis NDT teaches theory live online anywhere in Kansas, from Kansas City to Liberal. Practical training and practical exams are completed on real specimens at your employer's facility or in an arranged practical session.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Kansas?

Kansas is an NRC Agreement State, so KDHE licenses industrial radiography. The employer holds the licence; individuals need state-compliant radiation-safety training, trainee status and radiographer certification. Your SNT-TC-1A certification is a separate, additional requirement.

How much does NDT training cost in Kansas?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size and whether you choose online, a private cohort or onsite delivery. Request a Kansas quote and we reply within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Kansas?

Ultrasonic testing, including phased array for composites, is the most widely used because it spans aerospace and energy. Penetrant and eddy current testing are heavily used in Wichita aerospace, and radiography in refinery and pipeline work.

Is NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A required for Wichita aerospace jobs?

Most aircraft manufacturers and their suppliers certify production inspectors to NAS 410, which is structured like SNT-TC-1A with added aerospace requirements. SNT-TC-1A training builds the method knowledge both schemes need; your employer's written practice decides which scheme applies.

Can you train our crew onsite in Wichita or El Dorado?

Yes. A Level III can deliver the hands-on block at your facility in Wichita, El Dorado, McPherson or anywhere in Kansas, using your equipment and parts, and run the practical exams there.

How long does Level II training take?

It depends on the method and the employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures; supervised experience usually takes longer than the classroom part.

Does Atlantis NDT have a training centre in Wichita?

No. We do not operate a physical training centre in Wichita or anywhere in Kansas. Training is delivered live online, as a live-virtual cohort, or onsite at your employer's facility.

Who regulates pipeline and boiler inspection in Kansas?

The Kansas Corporation Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety, with PHMSA covering interstate lines, and the State Fire Marshal's Boiler Safety Unit oversees boilers and pressure vessels. NDT personnel work to API 1104 on pipelines and to ASME and National Board codes on boilers and vessels.

Do you offer API 510 or CWI courses in Kansas?

No. Atlantis NDT training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training only. Some Kansas employers also ask for those credentials for particular roles, and you would need a provider that specialises in them.

NDT Training and Certification in Kentucky

Short answer: Kentucky technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT in three ways: live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite sessions at your own plant, mill, refinery or job site. An ASNT NDT Level III leads and oversees the training. Certification is employer-based. Your company's written practice defines training, experience and exams, and a Level III administers them. Atlantis has no Kentucky training centre. We teach online or come to your facility.

Kentucky's NDT market is built on heavy manufacturing and metals, not on the coast or the oilfield. The state builds more vehicles per person than almost anywhere in the country, including Toyota's largest plant, two Ford plants in Louisville, the Corvette plant in Bowling Green and a large battery-plant project in Hardin County. Along the Ohio River it melts and rolls stainless steel, carbon steel and aluminium. It runs a large refinery in the northeast, chemical complexes at Calvert City and Louisville, coal and gas power stations, gas transmission pipelines that cross the state, two big Army posts and some of the busiest air-cargo hubs in the world. This page explains where Kentucky NDT work is, what each sector expects, which state agencies regulate radiography, boilers and pipelines, and how to request a Kentucky NDT training quote for your crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Kentucky

Direct answer: Kentucky NDT work clusters in Louisville (automotive, appliances, chemicals, air cargo), the Bluegrass around Lexington and Georgetown (automotive), Northern Kentucky (air cargo, steel, bridges), the Ohio River corridor from Ghent to Owensboro and Paducah (steel, aluminium, power, chemicals), Northeast Kentucky around Ashland (refining), South Central Kentucky (automotive and batteries) and Eastern Kentucky (coal, gas, pipelines).

Louisville and Jefferson County

Ford's Louisville Assembly Plant and Kentucky Truck Plant, GE Appliances' Appliance Park and a large supplier base need production inspection: weld checks on bodies and frames, eddy current sorting and crack detection, and magnetic particle and penetrant inspection of forged and cast parts. The chemical plants in the Rubbertown area along the Ohio River bring process-piping, pressure-vessel and tank inspection during turnarounds. UPS's Worldport hub at Louisville Muhammad Ali International Airport makes Louisville an aircraft-maintenance city, with the eddy current, ultrasonic and penetrant work that goes with it. Louisville Gas and Electric's generating stations add boiler and piping outage work.

The Bluegrass: Lexington, Georgetown, Frankfort and Richmond

Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky in Georgetown is Toyota's largest plant in the world, and its suppliers spread across the Bluegrass. Production NDT, especially UT of spot welds and joints, ET and MT on parts, and VT of welded assemblies, is the main work. Lexington also has aircraft-maintenance and manufacturing employers, and the Blue Grass Army Depot near Richmond has defence-related facilities.

Northern Kentucky and the Ohio River corridor east

Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport in Hebron hosts Amazon's air hub and DHL's Americas hub, which bring aircraft and ground-equipment maintenance. Upriver at Ghent, North American Stainless runs a large stainless steel mill and Nucor runs a steel mill nearby. Both need ultrasonic plate and weld inspection, MT, and inspection of cranes and rolling equipment. The Brent Spence Bridge corridor project between Covington and Cincinnati, and the state's many Ohio River bridges, need structural welding and bridge inspection.

Western Kentucky: Owensboro, Henderson, Paducah and Calvert City

Century Aluminum's smelters at Hawesville and Sebree, the chemical complex at Calvert City, and power stations along the river, including TVA's Shawnee Fossil Plant near Paducah, generate plant and outage inspection. Paducah also has the Department of Energy's former gaseous diffusion plant site, now in environmental clean-up. Owensboro is a gas-pipeline town: Texas Gas Transmission is headquartered there, and interstate gas transmission lines cross western Kentucky. That means API 1104 construction work and integrity work such as UT thickness, PAUT and radiography of welds.

Northeast Kentucky: Ashland and Catlettsburg

Marathon Petroleum's Catlettsburg refinery in Boyd County is Kentucky's refinery. It drives turnaround and in-service inspection work: corrosion mapping, thickness surveys on piping circuits, radiography and phased array of welds, and pressure-vessel and exchanger inspection. Barge, rail and fabrication shops along the Big Sandy and Ohio rivers add more weld inspection.

South Central and Eastern Kentucky

General Motors' Corvette plant in Bowling Green, the BlueOval SK battery project at Glendale in Hardin County, and suppliers along I-65 bring automotive and battery-manufacturing inspection. Fort Knox and Fort Campbell add vehicle, aviation and facility maintenance. In Eastern Kentucky, coal mining, gas production and gathering, and the transmission pipelines that run out of the Appalachian Basin need structural, equipment and pipeline weld inspection.

Wherever your company is, you can ask about onsite training for your Kentucky crew. We schedule around production, shutdowns and turnarounds.

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT teaches UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, plus Level III exam preparation. Every course is structured on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and on your company's written practice. The table maps each method to Kentucky work.

Lexington and Georgetown. Most demand comes from automotive production NDT inside plants and their suppliers. Those inspectors need deep skill in one or two methods on specific part families, and an exact grasp of the customer's acceptance criteria. Louisville's NDT people split three ways: production inspectors in auto and appliance plants, field technicians in chemical plants and power stations, and aircraft-maintenance inspectors at the air cargo hub. Those are three different training profiles, and we build the course around the one your crew needs. See Practical NDT Louisville for simulator practice.

Owensboro, Paducah and Bowling Green. Pipeline contractors need RT and PAUT to API 1104. Chemical and power plants need plant inspection. Auto and battery plants need production inspectors. All are served online and onsite.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Kentucky, step by step

Direct answer: Kentucky does not license NDT technicians in general. Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you based on its written practice. The practice sets training hours, experience, exams and vision tests, a Level III administers the exams, and the employer issues certification once you meet every requirement.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. It covers methods, levels, training and experience hours, exam content, passing grades, vision tests and recertification. If your company needs one, see written practice development.
  2. You complete formal training. Classroom hours per method and level come from the practice, using SNT-TC-1A recommendations. See the training requirements matrix for the guideline figures.
  3. You build documented experience. On-the-job hours in the method, under qualified supervision, on the work you will be certified for.
  4. You pass the general, specific and practical exams. The general exam covers theory, the specific exam covers your employer's procedures, codes and equipment, and the practical exam is done on real specimens. A Level III prepares and administers them.
  5. You pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity is checked annually, and colour contrast as the practice requires.
  6. Your employer certifies you. Certification belongs to that employer. If you move from a Louisville plant to an Ashland contractor, the new employer decides how to recertify you.
  7. You recertify on schedule. The practice sets the interval and the evidence needed.

The ASNT NDT Level III certificate is different. ASNT issues it centrally by examination, and employers then certify their Level III under their own practice. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Kentucky requirements

Direct answer: Kentucky is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the Radiation Health Branch of the Cabinet for Health and Family Services (Department for Public Health) under 902 KAR Chapter 100. The Branch publishes a licensing guide specifically for industrial radiography.

For a Kentucky radiography company, the state licence sets radiation-safety training, radiographer and assistant qualification, personnel monitoring, survey instruments, source storage and transport, and field-crew rules, which follow the model of 10 CFR Part 34. The Radiation Health Branch also registers X-ray equipment. Radiation-safety training is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT method training, which teaches exposure technique, film and digital processing and interpretation. A field radiographer needs both. Work on federal sites, such as Department of Energy property or military installations, can fall under federal rules, so confirm the route before mobilising. Regulations are revised from time to time, so check current requirements with the Branch before a new crew starts work.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Kentucky's Boiler Inspection Section, part of the Division of Plumbing in the Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction (Public Protection Cabinet), inspects new installations of boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping under KRS Chapter 236 and 815 KAR Chapter 15. Kentucky's regulations cover pressure piping as well as boilers and vessels, which matters for plant and fabrication work. ASME Section V NDT methods, with Section I, Section VIII and B31 acceptance criteria, are standard. Repair organisations work to National Board requirements.

Pipelines. The Kentucky Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety, and PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines. Pipeline welding and NDT generally follow API 1104, and operators run their own operator-qualification programmes on top of SNT-TC-1A certification.

Codes and specifications common in Kentucky. Automotive OEM and supplier quality standards in manufacturing. ASME Section V, VIII and B31.3 in refining and chemicals. ASME Section I and B31.1 in power stations. AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AASHTO/AWS D1.5 for bridges. API 1104 for pipelines. Aerospace customer specifications and NAS 410 for aircraft maintenance and aerospace suppliers, mentioned as context only, because Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Kentucky

Direct answer: Kentucky crews can take theory online, join a live-virtual cohort with a Level III instructor, or bring the training onsite to their plant, mill or site. Practical exams always use real specimens under Level III oversight. Video and simulation never replace them.

Training works best when it follows Kentucky's work calendar. Auto plants have summer shutdown weeks and model changeovers, which suit production inspectors. Steel and aluminium mills schedule maintenance outages, when their own inspectors are busiest, so theory is better done before them. The Catlettsburg refinery and the chemical plants schedule turnarounds, and contract technicians are least available during them. Coal and gas power stations schedule outages in the spring and autumn shoulder seasons. Pipeline construction slows in winter, which suits training for pipeline crews. Technicians in Eastern and Western Kentucky benefit most from online theory, because a classroom week in Louisville or Lexington means long drives.

Onsite delivery means the instructor works at your Kentucky facility, with your equipment and procedures and, where possible, your own parts and welds as practice specimens. The specific exam can then reflect your real work. It suits companies with several technicians in a method, or companies that want training tied tightly to their written practice. Live online theory suits mixed groups and individuals. See online NDT training and corporate NDT training. When you're ready, request a cohort or onsite quote for Kentucky. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

For Kentucky employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: A Kentucky company that certifies its own NDT personnel needs a compliant written practice, a responsible Level III, and training and exam records that survive a customer audit. Atlantis NDT writes and reviews written practices, provides Level III services, and runs corporate training for Kentucky employers.

Kentucky's automotive and metals supply chain includes many companies with a few NDT inspectors inside a quality department and no in-house Level III. OEM audits and customer source inspections are where gaps show: missing training records, exams not administered by a qualified Level III, out-of-date vision tests, or a practice that doesn't cover the methods the shop now uses. We help close those gaps with:

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A, aligned with your customers' requirements.
  • Level III services: procedure and technique review, exam preparation and administration, and audit support. See our NDT consulting services.
  • Corporate training programmes for multi-site employers, so plants in Louisville, Georgetown and Bowling Green train to one standard.
  • Guidance on SNT-TC-1A certification for companies writing their first practice.

If an audit is coming, book a Level III consultation. We start by reviewing your current documents.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets Kentucky trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments before their hands-on exam. It builds familiarity with set-up and technique, but it is practice only. It does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The environments are an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Kentucky users, the welding workshop matches automotive, mill and fabrication weld inspection, the aircraft hangar matches cargo-hub maintenance in Louisville and Northern Kentucky, and the oil and gas site and storage tank match refinery, chemical and pipeline work. See Practical NDT, Practical NDT Louisville and Practical NDT Lexington.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, written practices and Level III services, and the live-virtual and onsite training delivered to Kentucky employers.

NDT training in Kentucky: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Kentucky?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Complete the classroom training it requires, build documented experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass the vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and helps employers with the rest.

Is there NDT training online in Kentucky?

Yes. Theory for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET can be taken live online from anywhere in Kentucky. Practical exams still use real specimens under Level III oversight.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Kentucky?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence from the Radiation Health Branch, because Kentucky is an NRC Agreement State. Radiographers and assistants must meet the licence's training and qualification rules under 902 KAR Chapter 100.

How much does NDT training cost in Kentucky?

Training is quoted on request. The quote depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and any written-practice or exam support. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Kentucky?

UT is in demand in nearly every sector. MT, PT and ET are heavily used in automotive and metals plants. PAUT and RT matter for pipelines, refining and power. ET also matters for aircraft maintenance at the cargo hubs.

Can you train our crew onsite in Louisville or Lexington?

Yes. Onsite training is available anywhere in Kentucky, using your equipment and procedures where possible.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Kentucky employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer-based NDT certification in US industry, including Kentucky's automotive, steel, refining and power sectors. Aerospace customers may also reference NAS 410.

How long does Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, the method and your experience. Classroom and experience hours are both set by the practice. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline figures.

Can I take NDT training without an employer in Kentucky?

Yes, you can take classroom training as an individual, and it counts toward the formal training requirement. Certification still needs an employer and its written practice.

Do auto plants in Kentucky need certified NDT inspectors?

Plants that use NDT to accept product, or whose customers require documented qualification, generally certify their inspectors to a written practice. Check what your OEM or Tier 1 customer asks for.

Do you prepare candidates for the ASNT Level III exams?

Yes. We offer preparation for the Basic and method examinations. See ASNT Level III training.

What does an NDT technician earn in Kentucky?

Pay varies by method, level, sector and overtime. See the NDT salary guide for published ranges.

NDT Training and Certification in Louisiana

Short answer: Louisiana technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT as live online classes, a private live-virtual cohort, or onsite delivery at the employer's plant, yard or shop anywhere in the state. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every programme, practical exams are held on real specimens at your facility, and the employer certifies under its own written practice.

Louisiana packs an enormous amount of inspection work into a small footprint. The Mississippi River corridor between Baton Rouge and New Orleans is lined with refineries and chemical plants; the Lake Charles area has become one of the world's busiest LNG and petrochemical construction zones; the bayou parishes around Houma, Morgan City and Lafayette build and service the offshore fleet; and the north of the state adds a major air force base and the Haynesville gas play. This hub explains where Louisiana NDT technicians work, which methods each area needs, what the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality expects from radiography crews, and how to train a crew without losing people during a turnaround. To go straight to pricing for your group, request a Louisiana training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in Louisiana

Direct answer: Louisiana NDT work clusters in four areas: the River Parishes refining and chemical corridor from Baton Rouge to New Orleans, the Lake Charles and Cameron Parish LNG and petrochemical belt, the Acadiana and bayou region of Lafayette, Houma and Morgan City serving offshore oil and gas and shipbuilding, and north Louisiana around Shreveport and Monroe. Refinery and plant maintenance drives the most hours.

Baton Rouge and the River Parishes

The "chemical corridor" along the Mississippi from Baton Rouge to the outskirts of New Orleans is home to ExxonMobil's Baton Rouge refinery and chemical plant, Marathon's Garyville refinery, the Norco and St. Charles refining and chemical complexes, the Chalmette refinery and many large chemical, fertiliser and plastics plants in Ascension, Iberville, St. James, St. John and St. Charles parishes. Process safety management rules keep a steady base of mechanical-integrity inspection on piping, vessels, exchangers and tanks, and planned turnarounds swell crews several times a year. Demand is broad: UT thickness and shear wave, PAUT for weld and corrosion mapping, radiography of process piping, MT and PT on welds and rotating equipment, ET on exchanger tubes, and VT throughout. Two nuclear stations, River Bend near St. Francisville and Waterford 3 at Killona, add outage work under ASME Section XI.

Lake Charles, Westlake and Cameron Parish

Southwest Louisiana combines established refining and chemicals (the Citgo and Phillips 66 refineries and a dense chemical cluster in Westlake and Sulphur) with a wave of LNG export terminals along the Calcasieu Ship Channel and the coast, including Cameron LNG, Sabine Pass LNG and Calcasieu Pass. LNG construction and expansion bring huge weld-inspection volumes on stainless, nickel-alloy and carbon steel piping, storage tanks and modules, so penetrant, radiography, PAUT and TOFD technicians are in steady demand. Hurricane recovery work in this region has also kept structural and tank inspection busy.

Acadiana and the bayou parishes: Lafayette, New Iberia, Houma and Morgan City

Lafayette has long been the service and engineering base for Gulf of Mexico oil and gas, while Houma, Morgan City and the Port Fourchon area host offshore fabrication yards, shipyards and marine service companies. Shipbuilders and repair yards in Terrebonne and Lafourche parishes build workboats, offshore supply vessels and government vessels, and fabrication yards build jackets, decks and modules. Work here is structural weld inspection to AWS D1.1 and class-society rules, UT and MT on heavy plate, drill-pipe and tubular inspection for oilfield-service companies, and corrosion inspection of marine assets.

New Orleans and the lower river

New Orleans adds port and marine work along the river, NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility (where large launch-vehicle structures are built), shipyards and repair yards, and the refining and chemical plants at Chalmette, Belle Chasse and Plaquemines Parish, where the Plaquemines LNG export project is a major construction site. Bridges, flood-control structures and the river's industrial docks add civil and structural inspection.

North Louisiana: Shreveport, Bossier City and Monroe

Barksdale Air Force Base in Bossier City is home to B-52 bomber operations, and its maintenance work draws on eddy current, penetrant and magnetic particle methods. The Haynesville shale gas play around Shreveport supports pipeline construction, gathering systems and gas processing, which need radiography and UT. Monroe and the I-20 corridor add paper mills, chemical plants and fabrication shops.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Louisiana employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT runs SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Louisiana employers, and Level III exam preparation. River Parishes and Lake Charles work leans on UT, PAUT and RT; bayou-region yards lean on UT, MT and VT; Barksdale-related aerospace work leans on ET and PT.

NDT training by city in Louisiana

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has dedicated pages for Baton Rouge, New Orleans and Lake Charles, plus a Gulf Coast regional page. None is a physical centre: each explains local demand and how we deliver online or onsite at your Louisiana facility. Other industrial towns are covered below.

Baton Rouge. The capital is the hub for contractors serving the River Parishes. Most training requests are for Level I and II UT and RT, upgrades to PAUT, and ET for exchanger work, with a strong employer-side interest in written practices because plant owners audit contractor certification files closely. Training tends to be booked in the weeks before a major turnaround so new hires arrive certified.

New Orleans. Employers in the New Orleans area are more varied: shipyards, marine contractors, aerospace manufacturing at Michoud, refineries on the lower river and civil work on bridges and flood structures. That mix means MT, UT and VT for structural welds, PT for aerospace and stainless work, and RT for piping.

Lake Charles. Southwest Louisiana's LNG build-out creates intense short-term demand for weld inspectors, so contractors ask for fast, well-documented Level II programmes in RT, PT, PAUT and TOFD. A private live-virtual cohort followed by an onsite practical block at the contractor's yard is the format that most often fits the construction schedule.

Lafayette, Houma and Morgan City. Oilfield-service companies and fabrication yards need UT, MT and VT technicians for structural and tubular inspection. Crews rotate offshore, so the theory part is usually delivered live online between hitches.

Shreveport and Monroe. North Louisiana employers combine aerospace maintenance, pipeline work in the Haynesville and paper-mill and chemical-plant maintenance, so ET, PT, RT and UT all appear on training requests.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Louisiana, step by step

Direct answer: NDT certification in Louisiana is employer-based under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The employer's written practice sets requirements; you complete classroom training and supervised experience; a Level III administers general, specific and practical exams; you pass a vision test; and the employer certifies you. Radiographers also need state radiation-safety credentials from LDEQ.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. If it needs writing or updating, see written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the formal hours the written practice requires for each method and level, documented with course records.
  3. Supervised experience. You build on-the-job hours in the method. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures so you can plan.
  4. General and specific exams. Written exams on theory and on your employer's procedures and codes, such as ASME V, B31.3, API 1104 or AWS D1.1.
  5. Practical exam. Hands-on testing on flawed specimens, graded by a Level III. In Louisiana we run this at your facility with your equipment.
  6. Vision examination. Near-vision and colour-contrast checks at the interval in the written practice.
  7. Certification and recertification. The employer certifies and later recertifies you. See Level II recertification.

In Louisiana, technicians often move between contractors from one plant turnaround to the next. Each new employer has to recertify you under its own written practice, so keep copies of your course records, experience logs and exam results. More on the framework: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Louisiana requirements

Direct answer: Louisiana has been an NRC Agreement State since 1967. Industrial radiography is regulated by the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ) under LAC 33:XV, Chapter 5. Radiographers must carry a valid radiographer certification card, and trainees need LDEQ trainee status, in addition to their employer's SNT-TC-1A certification.

Louisiana is unusual in that its radiation programme sits in the environmental agency rather than the health department. LDEQ's radiation licensing staff certify industrial radiographers, trainees and instructors. Under the state rule, a person must complete radiation-safety instruction (the regulation refers to at least 40 hours on the subjects in Appendix A of Chapter 5) before acting as a radiographer, and trainee status is not valid until LDEQ issues confirmation and a trainee card, which must be carried during radiographic work. Radiographers must carry a valid certification card issued by LDEQ, another Agreement State, the NRC or ASNT's industrial radiography programme. Applications use LDEQ's industrial radiography certification form. Requirements are updated from time to time, so confirm details with LDEQ before planning a programme.

Atlantis NDT's RT courses cover radiographic technique, exposure, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance criteria for SNT-TC-1A. The state radiation-safety course and LDEQ certification are separate, managed by your radiation safety officer. We help employers schedule both so trainees are not waiting on one to finish the other.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Boiler inspection in Louisiana is handled by the Office of State Fire Marshal's boiler inspection section, working within the National Board framework. NDT technicians meet it on repairs and alterations to boilers and vessels under the National Board Inspection Code and ASME Sections I and VIII.

Pipelines. Intrastate pipeline safety is overseen by the state's Office of Conservation pipeline programme. In 2025 the parent agency, formerly the Department of Energy and Natural Resources, became the Department of Conservation and Energy, so confirm the current agency name on paperwork. PHMSA covers interstate lines. API 1104 governs most pipeline weld inspection.

Codes commonly used in Louisiana. ASME Section V, VIII and B31.3 in refineries and chemical plants; API 1104 on pipelines; AWS D1.1 for structural work in fabrication yards; class-society rules and US Coast Guard requirements in shipyards; ASME Section XI at River Bend and Waterford; and NAS 410 in aerospace work. Some owners also ask for API inspector credentials or AWS CWI for certain roles. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only, so we mention those schemes only as local context.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Louisiana

Direct answer: Louisiana technicians can take theory live online, join a private live-virtual cohort for their employer, or have an Atlantis Level III deliver the programme onsite at their plant, yard or shop. Atlantis has no training centre in Louisiana; practical exams are held at the client's facility on real specimens.

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory classes, with attendance records, for individuals and spread-out crews, including offshore rotators who study between hitches. See online NDT training.
  • Private live-virtual cohort. One employer's group, scheduled around shift and rotation patterns, with content mapped to that employer's written practice and procedures.
  • Onsite. A Level III teaches the hands-on portion and runs practical exams at your facility in Baton Rouge, Lake Charles, Houma or anywhere else in the state. See corporate NDT training.

The Louisiana calendar shapes scheduling. River Parishes and Lake Charles plants run spring and autumn turnarounds, LNG construction follows project milestones, offshore crews rotate on fixed hitches, and hurricane season from June to November can disrupt coastal plans at short notice. We usually suggest theory in the quieter windows and an onsite practical block that your operations team can protect. Ask about onsite training for your Louisiana crew.

For Louisiana employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Louisiana inspection contractors, fabrication yards, shipyards and plant owners use Atlantis NDT to write or update SNT-TC-1A written practices, provide outside Level III services, administer exams and train whole crews. Owner audits in the River Parishes and LNG projects check exactly these records.

Common gaps we find in growing Louisiana contractors include written practices that do not cover newer methods such as PAUT, no clear procedure for accepting experience from a previous employer, incomplete vision-test records, and practical exams that were not graded against a documented checklist. LNG project owners and EPCs typically review contractor NDT personnel files before mobilisation, so fixing these gaps before a bid saves time. We can review your documents, write or revise the written practice, build exam banks, and act as your examining Level III.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Atlantis Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five environments, including an oil and gas site, a storage tank, a welding workshop and an aircraft hangar. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens given by your Level III.

River Parishes and Lake Charles trainees get most from the oil and gas site and storage tank scenes, yard and shipyard trainees from the welding workshop, and north Louisiana aerospace trainees from the aircraft hangar. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT in Louisiana, with local pages for Baton Rouge, New Orleans and Lake Charles. For written exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He builds the course content, maps it to each employer's written practice and oversees examinations. On onsite programmes in Louisiana he works alongside your Level III or serves as the examining Level III if you do not have one.

NDT training in Louisiana: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Louisiana?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its required classroom training and supervised experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you. Starting Level I theory before you are hired can help with Baton Rouge and Lake Charles contractors.

Is there NDT training online in Louisiana?

Yes. Atlantis NDT delivers SNT-TC-1A theory live online to Louisiana technicians, including offshore crews between hitches. Practical training and exams are done onsite at the employer's facility.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Louisiana?

Yes. LDEQ regulates industrial radiography under LAC 33:XV, Chapter 5. You need the required radiation-safety training and LDEQ trainee status to work as a trainee, and a valid radiographer certification card to work as a radiographer, on top of your SNT-TC-1A level. Your employer must hold an LDEQ licence or registration.

How much does NDT training cost in Louisiana?

We quote on request. Cost depends on methods and levels, group size, delivery model and whether you also need exam administration or written-practice work. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Louisiana?

UT is the broadest across refinery and chemical maintenance. RT, PT, PAUT and TOFD are in heavy demand on LNG construction around Lake Charles. Shipyards and fabrication yards lean on UT, MT and VT.

Can you train our crew onsite in Lake Charles or Baton Rouge?

Yes. Onsite training and practical exams at your facility are available anywhere in Louisiana, scheduled around turnarounds and project milestones.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Louisiana employers?

Yes. It is the standard basis for NDT personnel certification across Louisiana refining, chemicals, pipelines, LNG and fabrication. Aerospace work may require NAS 410, and certain owner roles may require additional inspector credentials.

How long does NDT Level II take in Louisiana?

It depends on the method and your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. See the training requirements matrix for typical figures. The supervised experience is usually the longer part.

Can offshore workers complete NDT training around their hitch?

Yes. Live online theory can be scheduled for the weeks onshore, and the practical portion can be arranged at the employer's onshore yard.

Does Atlantis NDT have a training centre in Baton Rouge or New Orleans?

No. Atlantis NDT does not operate a physical training centre in Louisiana. Training is online, live-virtual, or onsite at your employer's facility.

No. Atlantis NDT provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training only. Those separate credentials need a specialist provider.

NDT Training and Certification in Maine

Maine technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at their own shipyard, mill, aerospace plant or fabrication shop. Every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III and built around the employer's written practice, so the classroom hours count toward certification. Methods covered: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

Maine's NDT economy looks nothing like the oil states. Its anchors are naval shipbuilding and submarine maintenance on the southern coast, a large jet-engine parts plant in York County, pulp and paper mills along the inland rivers, petroleum terminals and pipelines feeding the ports of Portland and Searsport, a decommissioned nuclear plant with spent fuel still stored on site, a growing renewable energy sector and a coastline full of boatyards, bridges and marine structures. Each of those employers asks for different methods, codes and paperwork, from NAVSEA requirements at the shipyards to aerospace customer specifications in the engine supply chain and ASME and National Board rules at the mills. This page is organised around that map rather than a generic course list. If you already know what you need, request a Maine NDT training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Maine

Most Maine NDT work sits in five zones: the Midcoast shipbuilding cluster around Bath and Brunswick, the southern coast from Portland to Kittery with its naval shipyard, aerospace plant and fuel terminals, the inland paper-mill towns along the Androscoggin, Kennebec and Penobscot rivers, the Bangor and Penobscot Bay region with its fabrication and port at Searsport, and the energy and infrastructure work spread across the state, from bridges to wind and hydro.

Bath, Brunswick and the Midcoast shipbuilding cluster

Bath Iron Works, a General Dynamics shipyard on the Kennebec River, builds guided-missile destroyers for the US Navy and is one of the largest private employers in Maine. Naval shipbuilding is NDT-intensive: every critical weld on hull structure, piping and machinery foundations is inspected, and the work is governed by Navy technical publications such as NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 for NDT requirements alongside the shipyard's own procedures. VT, MT, PT, UT and RT are all used daily, and the documentation demands are among the toughest in any industry. The surrounding supply chain of machine shops, fabricators and outfitting contractors in Brunswick, Topsham and along the Midcoast needs certified inspectors too. Brunswick Landing, the redeveloped former naval air station, now hosts aerospace, composites and advanced manufacturing tenants. Smaller yachtbuilders and boatyards along the coast add composite, aluminium and steel inspection.

Kittery and the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard

The Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, on an island in Kittery at the New Hampshire border, overhauls, repairs and modernises nuclear-powered submarines. Shipyard and contractor NDT work there runs under NAVSEA requirements and the Navy's nuclear propulsion quality programmes, with heavy use of VT, MT, PT, UT and RT. Large infrastructure investments at the yard, including dry dock construction, have brought further fabrication and construction inspection work. Contractors supporting the yard often need certification records and written practices that survive extremely rigorous audits.

Southern Maine: Portland, South Portland, Westbrook and North Berwick

Portland is the state's largest city and port. South Portland's tank farms and marine terminals, together with the Portland-Montreal crude pipeline, form Maine's biggest petroleum storage hub, which brings API 653 tank inspections (context only), UT thickness and corrosion mapping, and VT and MT on tank and terminal repairs. In York County, Pratt and Whitney's North Berwick plant manufactures jet-engine parts, and its suppliers across southern Maine and New Hampshire rely on PT, MT, ET and UT under aerospace customer requirements that often reference NAS 410 alongside SNT-TC-1A. Westbrook has a paper mill and specialty manufacturing, and the Portland area adds hospitals, universities, commercial construction and the maintenance work that keeps them running.

The paper-mill towns: Rumford, Skowhegan, Jay, Madawaska and Baileyville

Pulp and paper mills remain major industrial employers in inland Maine, even after several closures. Mills run recovery boilers, power boilers, digesters, bleach plants, steam and chemical piping and large rotating machinery, all of which need regular inspection: UT thickness on boiler tubes and digesters, ET on heat-exchanger tubing, MT and PT on welds and repairs, RT on piping welds and VT throughout. Recovery boiler inspections during annual mill shutdowns are among the most demanding NDT jobs in the state. Biomass power plants, sawmills and wood-pellet producers add smaller but steady inspection work.

Bangor, Brewer, Searsport and Penobscot Bay

Bangor is the service centre for northern and eastern Maine, with heavy-equipment dealers, an international airport with aircraft maintenance, and fabrication and construction firms. Brewer, across the Penobscot River, has large module fabrication facilities that build structures and process modules for industrial projects, which need VT, UT and MT on structural welds to AWS D1.1. Searsport is Maine's second-largest port and a fuel and bulk cargo terminal, and the state has selected nearby Sears Island for a planned offshore wind port, which would add fabrication and marine-structure inspection if it proceeds.

Energy, bridges and infrastructure statewide

Maine Yankee in Wiscasset was decommissioned decades ago, but its spent fuel remains in dry cask storage on site under NRC oversight, and the state's hydroelectric dams, wind farms, transmission lines and natural gas pipelines, including the Maritimes and Northeast system, need periodic inspection. The Maine Department of Transportation manages a large bridge inventory with many steel and movable bridges exposed to coastal salt and freeze-thaw cycles; bridge fabrication and repair usually follow the AASHTO/AWS D1.5 Bridge Welding Code, with UT and MT as the core methods.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Maine employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table shows each method, the levels available, how Maine employers typically use it and what a trainee needs before starting. Your employer's written practice sets the exact classroom and experience hours.

A shipyard subcontractor may need VT and MT Level II technicians whose certification records will satisfy a Navy prime; an aerospace parts supplier needs PT and ET certifications that sit cleanly within its customer's requirements; a paper mill reliability team wants UT and ET for its own staff so it can plan shutdown inspections without waiting for outside crews.
