Bath. The centre of Maine NDT. Shipyard inspectors and the subcontractors around them need VT, MT, PT, UT and RT certifications with records that meet Navy requirements. Many Bath-area technicians enter the trade through the shipyard and later move into contractor roles. See the Bath NDT training page and maritime and shipbuilding NDT training in Bath.

Portland and South Portland. Tank farms, marine terminals and the crude pipeline drive UT thickness, corrosion mapping, VT and MT work, while construction and hospital and university maintenance add VT and UT on structural steel and piping. See Practical NDT in Portland, Maine.

Kittery. Submarine overhaul at the naval shipyard and the contractors supporting dry dock and facility construction need technicians with rigorous, auditable certification under NAVSEA-governed programmes.

North Berwick and Sanford. The jet-engine parts plant and its suppliers make York County the PT- and ET-heavy corner of the state, with UT and MT on forgings and machined parts.

Bangor and Brewer. Module fabrication, heavy equipment repair and aviation maintenance call for VT, UT and MT on structural welds and PT and ET on aircraft and machined parts.

Rumford, Jay, Skowhegan and the mill towns. Annual mill shutdowns concentrate UT, ET, MT, PT and RT work into short windows, especially around recovery and power boilers.

Lewiston, Auburn and Augusta. Manufacturing, construction and state infrastructure projects need VT and UT on welds and smaller numbers of MT and PT inspectors.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Maine, step by step

Direct answer: Maine has no state licence for NDT technicians. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete classroom training and documented experience and pass general, specific, practical and vision exams administered under a Level III. Radiography adds state radiation safety requirements, and shipyard and aerospace customers may add their own.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. It sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks, vision requirements and recertification intervals for each method and level, and documents any additional customer or Navy requirements. If your company does not have one, we write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Level I and then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience. Log supervised experience in the shipyard, mill, plant or field, documented and verified by your employer.
  4. Pass the general exam. A written exam on method principles.
  5. Pass the specific exam. Covers your employer's procedures, the applicable codes (for example ASME Section V, AWS D1.1 or the relevant NAVSEA requirements) and your equipment.
  6. Pass the practical exam. A hands-on test on real flawed specimens, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Pass the vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated on schedule.
  8. Get certified by your employer. Certification is issued by, and tied to, your employer.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Keep vision current, recertify at the required interval and add methods or levels as you progress.

For the full background, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification. If you are starting out, see NDT Level 1 training.

Radiography licensing and other Maine requirements

Direct answer: Maine is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention's Radiation Control Program, which also regulates X-ray equipment. Boilers and pressure vessels fall under the state's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Program, and intrastate gas pipeline safety under the Maine Public Utilities Commission.

Industrial radiography

Because Maine has an agreement with the NRC, the state's Radiation Control Program licenses the possession and use of radioactive materials in Maine, including sources used for gamma radiography. Radiography companies need a Maine licence or reciprocity recognition before working in the state. The state's industrial radiography rules follow the federal model in 10 CFR Part 34: radiation safety training, a radiation safety exam, documented on-the-job training as a radiographer's assistant or trainee, radiographer qualification, dosimetry and the two-person rule at field sites. The programme uses its own forms to document radiographer qualification and trainee on-the-job experience. Work inside federal facilities such as the naval shipyard can involve federal jurisdiction as well, so contractors should confirm which authority applies to each job. RT method training under SNT-TC-1A, which is what Atlantis provides, covers technique, exposure, image quality and interpretation; it sits alongside, not instead of, the radiation safety training the licence holder must provide. Confirm current requirements with the Radiation Control Program before deploying a crew.

Boilers and pressure vessels

Maine's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Program, part of the Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation, requires boilers and pressure vessels in use in the state, other than exempt equipment, to be inspected by the chief inspector, deputy inspectors or authorised inspectors. Paper mills, hospitals, universities and power plants all fall under these rules. Repairs and alterations are generally performed to the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board inspection rules, so the NDT on that work is performed to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme. That makes a clean written practice essential for Maine repair organisations and mill maintenance contractors.

Pipelines

Interstate pipelines, including the Maritimes and Northeast natural gas system and the Portland-Montreal crude line, are regulated by PHMSA. The Maine Public Utilities Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety. Weld inspection follows API 1104 with ASME B31.4 and B31.8, and operators expect RT and UT technicians qualified to their procedures.

Codes Maine employers commonly use

  • NAVSEA technical publications, including T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 for NDT requirements, at Bath Iron Works, the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard and their subcontractors (context: the Navy and prime contractors set these requirements)
  • NAS 410 as context for aerospace suppliers in the North Berwick supply chain (Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A; your employer documents any additional aerospace requirements)
  • ASME Section I, Section V, Section VIII and B31.1 for boilers, pressure vessels and power piping at mills and power plants
  • API 650 and API 653 context for South Portland and Searsport tank farms (Atlantis trains the NDT methods, not the API inspector certification)
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and module fabrication, and AWS D1.5 for bridges

Some Maine employers also look for API inspector, CWI or NAS 410 credentials for certain roles. Atlantis does not train those schemes; our programmes focus on ASNT SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Maine

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Maine. Theory is delivered through live online or live-virtual classes, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility, with your own equipment and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight. That model lets coastal shipyard crews and inland mill teams train without travelling out of state.

Individual technicians can join online NDT training from Bath, Portland, Bangor, Rumford or anywhere with a reliable connection. Sessions are live with a Level III instructor, so questions get answered in real time. Practical hours and the practical exam are completed with your employer.

For employers, onsite delivery is usually the most efficient option. We run classroom and practical sessions in your shipyard training room, mill maintenance building or shop, use your instruments, reference standards and part samples, and teach to your procedures. A Midcoast fabricator gets VT and MT built around its weld procedures; a mill reliability team gets UT and ET on its own boiler and exchanger tube samples; an aerospace supplier gets PT and ET on representative parts.

Maine's calendar shapes scheduling. Paper mill shutdowns are usually planned once or twice a year; shipyard work runs year-round but follows ship construction and overhaul schedules; bridge, tank and construction work concentrates in the warmer months; and winter is a good time for classroom training. We plan cohorts so technicians are certified before the shutdown or the season begins. Multi-site employers can use corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Maine crew.

For Maine employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A the employer is responsible for certification, so every Maine NDT employer needs a written practice and access to a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams and acts as an outside Level III for companies without one.

Many Maine NDT employers are small: a machine shop in the shipyard supply chain, a boatyard, a mill maintenance contractor, a Brewer fabricator or an aerospace parts supplier. They need certified inspectors but rarely a full-time Level III. Yet their customers, from Navy primes to aerospace engine makers to National Board inspectors, are some of the most demanding auditors in any industry. The usual findings are a written practice that does not match the work, missing training-hour records, ungraded practical exams or lapsed vision tests.

We help with:

  • Written practice development and revision to the current SNT-TC-1A edition, with your customers' additional requirements documented. See written practice development.
  • Exam administration, with general, specific and practical exams prepared and graded under Level III oversight.
  • Procedure review against ASME, AWS and customer requirements.
  • Audit preparation for prime-contractor, National Board, ASME and ISO 9001 audits.
  • Multi-site programmes through corporate NDT training.

For broader Level III consulting, see NDT consulting in Maine and our guide to SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Maine company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT simulator lets Maine trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before the practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique, scanning and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank environment. For Maine, the welding workshop matches shipyard and fabrication welds, the hangar matches aerospace and aviation maintenance work, and the storage tank matches the South Portland and Searsport terminals. See the Bath and Portland Practical NDT pages, and try the UT Level 2 practice questions for the written exams.

Your instructor

Direct answer: Maine programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop designs the courses, delivers Level III-led instruction and oversees the exams and records that make certification defensible under SNT-TC-1A. He ties method theory to the codes and parts your Maine crew works with, from ship welds to mill boiler tubes and engine components, and helps employers build written practices that hold up in audits. Contact us about Maine training to ask about his availability.

NDT training in Maine: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Maine?

Your employer certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice after you complete Level I and Level II classroom training, log documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Online classroom training can start before you are hired, with certification following once an employer documents your experience.

Is there NDT training online in Maine?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online and live-virtual Level I and Level II classes that Maine technicians can join from anywhere in the state. Practical training and the practical exam are completed onsite with your employer.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Maine?

Maine is an Agreement State, so the company performing gamma radiography needs a licence or reciprocity from the Maine CDC Radiation Control Program, and radiographers and trainees must meet state training, exam, on-the-job and qualification requirements equivalent to 10 CFR Part 34. Confirm current requirements with the programme before starting work.

How much does NDT training cost in Maine?

Training is quoted on request. The quote depends on method and level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and whether you need exam administration or a written practice. We return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Maine?

VT and MT are used constantly in shipbuilding, UT and ET at paper mills and terminals, and PT and ET in the aerospace supply chain. RT remains important on naval and mill piping welds.

Can you train our crew onsite in Bath, Portland or Bangor?

Yes. We deliver classroom and practical sessions at your facility anywhere in Maine and schedule around shutdowns, ship schedules and the construction season.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Maine employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard basis for employer certification across US industry. Navy, aerospace and other customers may add requirements, which your written practice documents.

Does SNT-TC-1A training work for shipyard NDT jobs?

Naval work is governed by NAVSEA requirements set by the Navy and prime contractors. SNT-TC-1A method training gives you the technical foundation; your employer's written practice and qualification programme must also satisfy the applicable Navy requirements, so check them with your employer.

How long does VT or UT Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums. Experience hours usually take longer than classroom training.

Is there an NDT school in Maine I can attend in person?

Atlantis NDT does not operate a physical school or campus in Maine. Training is live online or onsite at your employer's facility.

Can I become a Level III in Maine?

Yes. Candidates with Level II experience can prepare for the ASNT Level III examinations through our online Level III training.

What do NDT technicians earn in Maine?

Pay depends on method, level, employer and sector. For general context, see the NDT salary guide.

NDT Training and Certification in Manitoba

Short answer: Manitoba technicians and employers can train with Atlantis NDT under the ASNT SNT-TC-1A system in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, and prepare for the ASNT Level III examinations. You can join live online classes, book a private live-virtual cohort for your crew, or have a Level III instructor deliver the course onsite at your hangar, shop, mine or plant. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice.

Manitoba's NDT market looks different from the rest of the Prairies. Oil and gas are present but small; the big employers are aerospace in Winnipeg, hydroelectric generation on the Nelson River, nickel and base-metal mining in the north, heavy manufacturing such as buses and steel, and the pipelines and railways that cross the province on their way east and south. That mix means three different certification worlds meet in one province: Canada's national scheme, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712); the aerospace scheme, NAS 410 and its European twin EN 4179; and the US employer-based scheme, SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis teaches SNT-TC-1A only. We do not train toward CGSB or NAS 410 certification and we claim no CGSB recognition. This page is direct about where our training fits in Manitoba, where it does not, and how employers can get a quote. Request a Manitoba NDT training quote and we will reply with options within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Manitoba

Direct answer: most Manitoba NDT work is in Winnipeg's aerospace, manufacturing and rail sector; on Manitoba Hydro's northern generating stations and transmission system; in the nickel and base-metal mines around Thompson, Snow Lake and Flin Flon; in the south-western oilfields around Virden; and in the fertiliser, steel and food-processing plants of Brandon, Selkirk and Portage la Prairie.

Winnipeg: aerospace, transit manufacturing and rail

Winnipeg has the largest aerospace cluster in Western Canada. StandardAero runs a major gas turbine engine repair and overhaul operation in the city, Boeing has a large composite parts plant, and Magellan Aerospace builds aerostructures and engine components. The Royal Canadian Air Force's 17 Wing is based at the airport. Engine overhaul relies on fluorescent penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic inspection of rotating parts, and composite manufacturing relies heavily on ultrasonic inspection. Winnipeg also builds transit and intercity buses for North American customers, and its rail yards and car shops need MT and UT on wheels, axles, couplers and welded structures. More local detail is on the Winnipeg NDT training page, and simulator practice is on Practical NDT in Winnipeg.

The Nelson River and Manitoba Hydro

Almost all of Manitoba's electricity comes from hydro. The large generating stations on the Nelson River in the north, the stations on the Winnipeg River closer to the city, and the long HVDC transmission lines that bring power south create work on turbines, runners, penstocks, gates, draft tubes, generator components and transmission structures. Typical methods are UT and MT on welded steel and castings, PT on stainless components, VT across the board, and UT thickness on penstocks and gates during planned outages. Outages are scheduled well ahead, which suits a planned onsite training block.

The north: Thompson, Snow Lake and Flin Flon

Northern Manitoba is mining country. Vale operates nickel mines at Thompson, and Hudbay runs copper-zinc-gold operations around Snow Lake and processing facilities at Flin Flon on the Saskatchewan border. Hoists, headframes, crushers, mills, conveyors and mobile equipment generate a constant flow of MT, UT and VT work, much of it done by in-house maintenance departments. Rotation schedules and remoteness make online theory and short onsite practical sessions the realistic model here.

South-west Manitoba: oil, fertiliser and food

The province's oil production is concentrated in the south-west around Virden, Waskada and Melita, with batteries, gathering lines and the service companies that support them. Brandon has a large nitrogen fertiliser plant and a major potato-processing plant, both owned by US companies, along with manufacturing and agri-business. Portage la Prairie has large food and pea-protein processing plants. These operations need pressure-equipment, piping and tank inspection, and the US-owned ones are often run to US corporate standards.

Selkirk, the Interlake and the east

Selkirk, north of Winnipeg, has a steel mini-mill that produces bar and structural products. Further east, the decommissioning of the former Whiteshell nuclear research laboratories at Pinawa continues under CNSC licence. The province's pulp, paper and forestry operations add boiler and pressure-vessel inspection during shutdowns.

Pipelines, rail and the Port of Churchill

Major crude oil and natural gas transmission pipelines cross southern Manitoba, with pump and compressor stations along the corridor and a crude terminal near Gretna at the US border. Both Class I railways run through Winnipeg, and the rail line to the Port of Churchill on Hudson Bay serves Canada's only Arctic deep-water port. Rail, terminal and pipeline maintenance all draw on UT, MT and RT.

SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or NAS 410: which one does your Manitoba job need?

Direct answer: Canadian industrial code work in Manitoba usually asks for CAN/CGSB-48.9712. Aerospace manufacturers and repair stations usually certify NDT staff to NAS 410 or EN 4179 under their own and their customers' rules. SNT-TC-1A fits US-code fabrication, US-owned plants, cross-border pipeline and rail work, and technicians heading to US jobs. Atlantis teaches SNT-TC-1A only.

Aerospace deserves a straight answer because it is the biggest NDT employer in Winnipeg. NAS 410 is the aerospace industry's certification standard, and prime contractors and engine OEMs generally require it of their suppliers and repair stations, along with their own approvals. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice written for general industry and is not a substitute. Our method training can strengthen a technician's knowledge of UT, ET or PT physics and technique, but it does not give you an NAS 410 certification. If your employer's written practice is NAS 410-based, follow it.

Your situation in ManitobaScheme usually expectedDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
Aerospace engine overhaul, composite manufacturing or aerostructures in WinnipegNAS 410 / EN 4179, plus OEM and Transport Canada requirementsNo for certification. Method knowledge only, under your employer's rules

Pipeline or oilfield crew working south-west Manitoba and North DakotaSNT-TC-1A on US jobs; project specification on Canadian jobsYes for the US work
Hydro generation, nuclear decommissioning or CSA-only structural workCAN/CGSB-48.9712 or the owner's specificationRarely. Ask the owner first

On the CGSB side: the Canadian General Standards Board, which published CAN/CGSB-48.9712, closed on 1 April 2026. Natural Resources Canada and the CWB Group have said the standard remains valid for its current cycle and that existing certifications are unaffected, and NRCan's NDT Certification Body says it continues operating. Arrangements are still changing, so confirm the current certification body before you plan a CGSB route. Holding both a CGSB certificate and an employer SNT-TC-1A certification is common and workable.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Manitoba employers

Direct answer: Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in eight methods and ASNT Level III exam preparation. Below is how each method maps onto Manitoba work and what a trainee needs first. Your employer's written practice sets the classroom and experience hours.

For Level III candidates, the ASNT Level III training programme prepares you for the Basic and method examinations online. Method pages such as UT Level 2 training, ET Level 2 training and PT Level 2 training show what each course covers. If your goal is an aerospace NAS 410 Level 3 or a CGSB Level 3, those follow their own rules, and we will tell you plainly.

NDT training by city in Manitoba

Direct answer: Atlantis has a dedicated NDT training page and a Practical NDT simulator page for Winnipeg. Brandon, Selkirk, Thompson, Flin Flon and the south-west oilfields are served the same way: live online classes plus onsite delivery at your site. We have no classroom in Manitoba.

BrandonNitrogen fertiliser, food processing, manufacturing, south-west oil servicesServed online and onsite; ask about a Brandon cohort

Winnipeg. Winnipeg has the most NDT jobs in the province, and most are in aerospace. For those technicians, NAS 410 governs, and our role is limited to method knowledge and Level III preparation where the employer wants it. The city's other employers, including bus and rail manufacturers, fabrication shops, utilities contractors and inspection companies, are where SNT-TC-1A comes up, especially when products are built for US customers. Onsite training at the shop avoids pulling people off a production line.

Brandon. The US-owned fertiliser and food plants in Brandon often run corporate inspection standards written in the US. A plant that wants its own UT thickness or PT capability, rather than calling a contractor for every task, can build an SNT-TC-1A programme with a written practice, training and an outside Level III.

Thompson, Snow Lake and Flin Flon. Mine maintenance teams need MT and UT on hoists, shafts and heavy equipment. These sites are far from any classroom, so online theory between rotations and an onsite practical block during a planned maintenance window is the realistic plan.

South-west Manitoba. Oilfield and pipeline crews around Virden and Waskada often cross into North Dakota for work, and SNT-TC-1A certification under their employer's written practice is what US operators expect.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Manitoba, step by step

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A certification is issued by your employer. You complete classroom training and documented experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer certifies you to its written practice. It is not a Canadian national certificate and it does not transfer automatically to a new employer.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A written practice setting training hours, experience hours, exam rules and recertification. We can draft it with you: see written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete the formal hours the written practice requires, online or onsite. The training requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience. Build supervised hours on real Manitoba work, such as plant equipment, fabrication, rail parts or pipeline welds, recorded by your employer.
  4. Examinations. Pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III.
  5. Vision test. Pass near-vision and colour contrast checks, normally every year.
  6. Certification. Your employer certifies you on the Level III's recommendation, for a specific method and level.
  7. Recertification. Renew at the interval set by the written practice.

If you are also pursuing CGSB or NAS 410 certification, keep detailed logs. Each scheme sets its own evidence rules, and it is far easier to record hours properly from day one.

Radiography licensing and other Manitoba requirements

Direct answer: industrial gamma radiography in Manitoba is regulated federally by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission, and only certified exposure device operators, or trainees under their direct supervision, may operate exposure devices. Boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Office of the Fire Commissioner's Inspection and Technical Services. Interprovincial pipelines fall under the Canada Energy Regulator.

Industrial radiography

Canada has no Agreement State model; the CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices in every province. The Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices Regulations allow only a certified exposure device operator (EDO), or a trainee under the direct supervision and continuous observation of a certified EDO, to operate an exposure device. The CNSC's certification guide, CSA PCP-09, and REGDOC-2.2.3 set out the vocational training, supervised on-the-job training and examination requirements. Atlantis RT training covers radiographic principles, technique, interpretation and acceptance criteria. It does not replace EDO certification, and we do not run CNSC examinations. X-ray equipment is regulated provincially, so check current registration and worker rules with your radiation safety officer.

Boilers and pressure vessels

In Manitoba, boiler and pressure vessel safety is administered by Inspection and Technical Services within the Office of the Fire Commissioner, under The Steam and Pressure Plants Act and The Power Engineers Act and their regulations. ITS handles design registration, inspections, examinations and licensing. Commonly referenced codes include CSA B51, ASME Sections I, V and VIII, and ASME B31.1 and B31.3. Whether SNT-TC-1A personnel are acceptable depends on the code, the owner and the contractor's quality programme.

Pipelines and oil and gas

Pipelines that cross provincial or national borders, including the large crude and gas lines through southern Manitoba, are regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator. Oil and gas activity inside the province, including flowlines and gathering systems in the south-west, is regulated by the province under The Oil and Gas Act. CSA Z662 is the core Canadian pipeline standard and sets its own NDT personnel rules; API 1104 appears on projects with US owners.

Aerospace and other requirements

Aerospace repair stations and manufacturers work under Transport Canada approvals and OEM requirements, and their NDT personnel are normally certified to NAS 410 or EN 4179. Industrial sites usually require safety prequalification through ISNetworld, Avetta or ComplyWorks, plus site orientation. Structural steel to CSA W59 is fabricated by CWB-certified companies with CGSB-certified NDT staff. Our training sits beside these requirements, never in place of them.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Manitoba

Direct answer: Atlantis teaches Manitoba students through live online classes, private live-virtual cohorts and onsite delivery at the employer's facility, led by an ASNT Level III. Theory is delivered online; practical sessions use real specimens at your site.

Manitoba's geography makes this model practical. More than half the population lives in Winnipeg, but much of the inspection work is hundreds of kilometres north at mines and generating stations, or in the south-west oilfields. Bringing a crew from Thompson or Flin Flon to a city classroom costs days of travel; an online theory course plus a few days of onsite practical work does not. We plan around Manitoba schedules: Manitoba Hydro outage windows, mine maintenance shutdowns, fertiliser plant turnarounds, winter road season in the north, and spring flooding that can disrupt travel in the Red River valley.

  • Live online seats for individuals anywhere in the province.
  • Private live-virtual cohorts built around your procedures, codes and equipment.
  • Onsite delivery at your Winnipeg shop, Brandon plant or northern mine, using your equipment and specimens, with support for practical examinations under your written practice.
  • Blended programmes combining online theory, simulator practice and a short onsite block.

We have no classroom in Manitoba and say so plainly. Ask about onsite training for your Manitoba crew, or see online NDT training and corporate NDT training.

For Manitoba employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Manitoba employers who need SNT-TC-1A certification need three things: a written practice, a Level III to administer examinations, and training and experience records an auditor can follow. Atlantis provides all three remotely or onsite, and can help companies that also keep CGSB-certified staff keep the two programmes separate and clear.

Common Manitoba scenarios include a Winnipeg manufacturer whose US customers ask for SNT-TC-1A-certified weld inspectors, a US-owned plant in Brandon that wants its own in-house UT and PT capability under the parent company's standard, and a south-west oilfield contractor bidding work in North Dakota. We can:

  • write or revise your SNT-TC-1A written practice (written practice development);
  • serve as your outside Level III for exams, procedure review and technique sign-off;
  • set out clearly which jobs use SNT-TC-1A personnel and which need CGSB or NAS 410 personnel;
  • prepare your NDT programme for customer and third-party audits;
  • keep certification, training, vision and equipment calibration records together in our NDT ERP, which records CGSB, NAS 410 and ASNT certifications side by side (NDT ERP overview).

See SNT-TC-1A training and certification for employers and NDT consulting in Canada. Book a Level III consultation for your Manitoba programme.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator lets Manitoba trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments in a browser. It is practice only and does not replace the hands-on practical examination required by your written practice, by NAS 410 or by a CGSB scheme.

One of the five environments is an aircraft hangar, which is useful for Winnipeg trainees who want to understand how surface and subsurface methods are applied to aircraft structures before they meet the real thing. The others are an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an oil and gas site and a storage tank, which cover most of Manitoba's industrial work. Northern trainees can practise between rotations, and supervisors can use the simulator to check readiness before booking practical exam time. See Practical NDT or Practical NDT in Winnipeg, and try the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop builds the course material, the examinations and the employer written practices, and he is the Level III you speak with when you need to work out whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or NAS 410 is the right scheme for a Manitoba job.

NDT training in Manitoba: frequently asked questions

How do I get NDT certified in Manitoba?

It depends on where you will work. Canadian industrial work usually needs CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification from an accredited certification body; confirm the current certification body, since arrangements changed in 2026. Aerospace work usually needs NAS 410 certification from your employer. US-code and US-client work uses SNT-TC-1A employer certification, which is what Atlantis trains for.

Can I take NDT training online in Manitoba?

Yes. Live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes are open to technicians anywhere in Manitoba, from Winnipeg to Thompson. Practical training and exams take place on real specimens, usually at the employer's site. See NDT training online.

Does Atlantis offer aerospace NAS 410 training in Winnipeg?

No. We teach SNT-TC-1A only and do not offer NAS 410 or EN 4179 certification training. Aerospace employers certify under their own NAS 410 written practice. Our method courses can add background knowledge if your employer wants it.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB training in Manitoba?

No. We do not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712 and claim no CGSB recognition. If CGSB is what the job needs, use a CGSB-route provider.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Manitoba?

For gamma radiography, yes: you must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator or a trainee under direct supervision, and the employer needs a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment falls under provincial rules.

Who inspects boilers and pressure vessels in Manitoba?

Inspection and Technical Services, part of the Office of the Fire Commissioner, under The Steam and Pressure Plants Act. It handles registration, inspection and licensing.

How much does NDT training cost in Manitoba?

Quotes are on request and depend on the method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery, and whether you also need a written practice or Level III exam administration. We usually return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Get a Manitoba training quote.

Which NDT methods are most used in Manitoba?

PT, ET and UT dominate in Winnipeg aerospace. MT and UT dominate in mining, rail and heavy manufacturing. RT matters on pipeline and piping welds, and VT appears everywhere.

Can you deliver NDT training at our Brandon or Thompson site?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your plant or mine is standard, subject to your site's access and safety requirements. The instructor uses your equipment and specimens and supports practical exams under your written practice.

How long does it take to reach UT Level II?

Your employer's written practice sets the classroom and experience hours, using SNT-TC-1A recommendations as a baseline; see the training requirements matrix. Experience usually takes much longer than the classroom part.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Manitoba?

Yes. Our Level III preparation runs online for the Basic and method exams.

What do NDT technicians earn in Manitoba?

It varies with sector, method, level and scheme. We do not publish our own salary figures; see the NDT salary guide for context.

NDT Training and Certification in Maryland

Maryland technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at their own shop, yard, test range or plant. Every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III and is built around the employer's written practice, so the classroom hours count toward certification. Methods covered: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

Maryland is a small state with an unusually dense mix of NDT work. The Port of Baltimore and its industrial waterfront, the defence and aerospace contractors along the I-95 and BW Parkway corridors, Army and Navy test centres at Aberdeen and Patuxent River, a nuclear station and an LNG terminal on the Calvert County shoreline, heavy-truck manufacturing in Hagerstown and a large bridge and transit portfolio all need qualified inspectors. Each of those employers asks for different methods, codes and paperwork. This page is organised around that map rather than a generic course list. If you already know what you need, request a Maryland training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Maryland

Most Maryland NDT work sits in five zones: the Baltimore port and industrial harbour, the defence and aerospace corridor between Baltimore and Washington, the Aberdeen and upper-Chesapeake test and power belt, Southern Maryland's nuclear, LNG and naval aviation sites, and the manufacturing and transport towns of Western Maryland and the Eastern Shore. Each favours a different set of methods and codes.

Baltimore harbour and the industrial waterfront

The Port of Baltimore handles bulk, roll-on/roll-off and container cargo, and its waterfront is lined with terminals, tank farms, marine structures and fabrication yards. Sparrows Point, once one of the largest steelworks in the country, has been redeveloped as the Tradepoint Atlantic logistics and port complex, which brings new berths, cranes and structural steel to inspect. The US Coast Guard Yard at Curtis Bay builds and overhauls Coast Guard cutters, and private ship repair and barge yards work along the Patapsco. The collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge in March 2024 and its rebuild by the Maryland Transportation Authority put bridge and marine-structure inspection at the centre of the region's attention. Methods in demand here are VT and MT on structural and hull welds, UT and PAUT on thick plate and connections, UT thickness surveys on tanks and piping, and RT on pressure piping.

The Baltimore-Washington defence and aerospace corridor

Between Baltimore and the Capital Beltway sits one of the country's densest clusters of defence electronics, aerospace and government contractors. Northrop Grumman's Mission Systems campus in Linthicum, Lockheed Martin's Middle River operations east of Baltimore, satellite and space hardware work in the Greenbelt and Columbia areas around NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center, and hundreds of machine shops and precision suppliers feed into them. Martin State Airport hosts the Maryland Air National Guard, and Joint Base Andrews in Prince George's County supports military aviation. This work leans on PT, ET, UT and RT on aluminium, titanium and composite parts, castings and welded assemblies, often under customer or prime-contractor procedures layered on top of the employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice.

Aberdeen, Harford and Cecil counties

Aberdeen Proving Ground in Harford County is the Army's long-established test and evaluation centre, with vehicle, weapons and materials testing that relies on precise inspection and documentation. Further up the Susquehanna, the Conowingo hydroelectric dam is a major generation and civil structure, and the I-95 corridor toward Delaware carries distribution centres, chemical blending and metal fabrication. Typical methods: UT, MT and VT on welded structures, RT and ET on components, and UT thickness on penstocks, piping and tanks.

Southern Maryland: Calvert Cliffs, Cove Point and Patuxent River

Calvert County holds both the Calvert Cliffs Nuclear Power Plant near Lusby, operated by Constellation, and the Cove Point LNG terminal a few miles south. Nuclear outages draw in-service inspection crews working to ASME Section XI, with UT, PAUT, ET on heat-exchanger and steam-generator tubing, VT on components and supports, and PT on stainless welds. The LNG terminal adds cryogenic piping, storage tanks and pressure equipment. Across the Patuxent, Naval Air Station Patuxent River in St. Mary's County is the Navy's flight test centre, where aircraft structural work calls for ET, UT and PT under aerospace procedures. Southern Maryland's gas-fired generating stations add boiler tube and header inspection during planned outages.

Western Maryland and the Eastern Shore

Hagerstown is home to heavy-truck powertrain manufacturing (the Mack and Volvo powertrain plant) and a cluster of distribution, aviation and fabrication businesses along I-81 and I-70. Frederick's industrial parks add precision machining and life-science equipment. On the Eastern Shore, Salisbury's regional airport supports airline and general aviation maintenance, and poultry processing, agricultural equipment and marine construction keep local welders and inspectors busy. These markets mostly need MT, PT, VT and UT on castings, forgings and welded fabrications.

Pipelines, utilities and infrastructure

Interstate natural gas transmission lines and refined-product pipelines cross Maryland, including systems serving the Baltimore and Washington metropolitan areas and the Cove Point terminal, and the state's gas distribution utilities run extensive pipe replacement programmes. The Maryland Department of Transportation, the Maryland Transportation Authority (which operates the Chesapeake Bay Bridge, the tunnels under Baltimore harbour and the toll bridges) and the regional transit agencies maintain a large inventory of steel bridges, tunnels and rail structures. That work means API 1104 pipeline weld inspection, AWS D1.5 bridge welding inspection and MT, UT and VT on structural steel.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Maryland employers

Atlantis NDT runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based courses in eight methods at Level I and Level II, plus Level III preparation. Maryland employers usually start with VT, MT and UT for port, bridge and fabrication work, add RT, PAUT and TOFD for piping, pressure parts and nuclear outages, and rely on ET and PT for aircraft and defence hardware. The table maps each method to the Maryland work it typically supports.

For candidates aiming at the top of the ladder, our ASNT Level III training covers the Basic exam, method exams and the written-practice knowledge a Level III is expected to apply. Method courses such as UT Level 2 training and the PAUT Level 2 course go deeper into individual techniques. Exact classroom hours and experience by method and level are listed in the training requirements matrix; we do not quote hour figures here because your employer's written practice sets the final numbers.

NDT training by city in Maryland

Atlantis NDT has a dedicated training page and a Practical NDT simulator page for Baltimore, and serves every other Maryland city through live online classes or onsite delivery at the employer's facility. There is no Atlantis training centre in Maryland; the course comes to your crew or to your screen.

Baltimore. The busiest NDT market in the state. A Baltimore inspector may spend one week on VT and MT at a ship repair yard, the next on UT thickness at a tank terminal in Curtis Bay, and the next on bridge welds for a contractor working for the state. Baltimore employers often train several technicians at once, which suits an onsite cohort at the yard or shop, with theory delivered live online so nobody loses a full week to the classroom.

Aberdeen and the upper Bay. Test-range and defence-contractor work demands rigorous procedures, traceable records and repeatable results. UT, RT and ET on components sit alongside MT and VT on welded structures. Employers here often need their written practice to satisfy a government customer's quality requirements as well as SNT-TC-1A.

Lusby, Solomons and Calvert County. Nuclear outage work at Calvert Cliffs and pressure-equipment work at Cove Point make this a specialised market where PAUT, TOFD, ET and PT are as important as everyday UT and VT. Training here is best timed well ahead of outage windows so technicians arrive qualified and current.

Lexington Park. Aircraft test and maintenance around Patuxent River needs ET, UT and PT on airframe structure, landing gear and engine parts, usually under aerospace procedures. Contractors supporting the base often combine SNT-TC-1A training with customer-specific requirements.

Hagerstown and Frederick. Castings, forgings, gears and welded fabrications make MT, PT and UT the core methods. Many manufacturers here are building a formal NDT programme for the first time and need a written practice before anyone can be certified.

Neighbouring hubs: NDT training across the Mid-Atlantic, Washington DC for teams in Montgomery and Prince George's counties, Delaware and Philadelphia for crews working the upper Bay and I-95, Norfolk for shipyard work further down the Chesapeake, and West Virginia for Western Maryland employers with sites across the state line.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Maryland, step by step

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, certification is issued by your employer, not by the State of Maryland or by a training school. You complete method training, log documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you to its written practice.

  1. Employer written practice. Your Maryland employer needs a written practice defining levels, training, experience, exams and recertification. Without it there is nothing to certify you against. We can write or update it (see below).
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete the method-specific classroom training the written practice requires, online, live-virtual or onsite. The training requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience in the method on your employer's real work: hull welds in Curtis Bay, bridge members on a state contract, castings in Hagerstown, aircraft parts at Patuxent River. The log must be signed and retained.
  4. General exam. A written test on the principles and theory of the method.
  5. Specific exam. A written test on the codes, procedures and equipment your employer actually uses, such as AWS D1.5 for bridges or ASME Section V for pressure work.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on inspection of real specimens containing known flaws, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast checks, repeated annually.
  8. Certification. Your employer issues the certification. It stays with that employer: if you move from a Baltimore yard to a Calvert County outage contractor, the new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice, though your documented training and experience carry forward.
  9. Recertification. At the interval the written practice sets, you demonstrate continued satisfactory performance or re-examine.

A fuller explanation of employer-based certification is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Radiography licensing and other Maryland requirements

Maryland is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the Maryland Department of the Environment's Radiological Health Program under COMAR 26.12, the state's regulations for the control of ionizing radiation, which follow the federal industrial radiography model in 10 CFR Part 34. Radiographers and assistants must meet state training, testing and supervision rules in addition to their SNT-TC-1A method certification.

In practice, an RT technician in Maryland needs two separate things. The first is method qualification under the employer's written practice, which is what our RT Level I and II courses support. The second is radiation safety qualification: radiation safety training, radiographer certification for those who work with sealed sources, and supervised work as a radiographer's assistant, all under the employing company's radioactive materials licence. Industrial X-ray equipment falls under the same programme's radiation machine rules. Because the Radiological Health Program functions in place of the NRC for these licences, out-of-state companies bringing sources into Maryland must follow its reciprocity requirements. Confirm current licensing and personnel requirements with MDE before a crew starts field work. Work inside federal facilities such as military installations can involve federal licensing instead, so check with the site.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Maryland's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Inspection Unit sits in the Division of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor. It enforces the state Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act, with periodic inspection of regulated equipment, and boilers and pressure vessels installed in the state must be built to the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and registered with the National Board. Repairs and alterations follow the National Board Inspection Code, which draws its NDT requirements from ASME Section V and the construction code.

Pipelines. The Maryland Public Service Commission's pipeline safety staff oversee intrastate gas pipeline operators in partnership with the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), which regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines. Pipeline welding and inspection commonly follow API 1104, and operator qualification rules apply to covered tasks.

Codes you will meet in Maryland. As local context only: AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for bridges, ASME Section V and VIII for pressure vessels, ASME B31.1 and B31.3 for power and process piping, API 1104 for pipelines, ASME Section XI for in-service inspection at Calvert Cliffs, Navy and Coast Guard shipbuilding standards on the waterfront, and NAS 410 or customer-specific aerospace requirements in the defence corridor and around Patuxent River. Some local employers also ask for API inspector or AWS CWI credentials; those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train for. Our training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Maryland

Maryland crews can take theory live online from anywhere in the state, join a scheduled live-virtual cohort, or have an Atlantis Level III-led programme delivered onsite at their facility. Practical training and practical exams are done on real specimens, at the employer's site or through a partner arrangement agreed in advance.

Online theory suits Maryland because traffic, not distance, is the usual obstacle. A technician in Lexington Park and one in Hagerstown are hours apart on the road, and nobody in the Baltimore-Washington corridor wants to lose half a day a session to the Beltway. Live online sessions are interactive, with the instructor present rather than recorded videos alone, and cover the general and specific knowledge the written exams test. See NDT training online for how the virtual classroom runs.

Onsite delivery suits yards, plants and manufacturers that want a group trained on their own parts, procedures and equipment. We schedule around the dates that matter to you: spring and fall outage seasons at Calvert Cliffs and the gas-fired units, vessel availability periods at the Curtis Bay yard and private ship repairers, bridge-inspection seasons and lane-closure windows on state contracts, and production changeovers at Hagerstown and Frederick plants. If a turnaround is coming, train the crew before it, not during it.

Hands-on skill still has to be built on hardware. We plan practical sessions with real specimens, your production parts where appropriate, and the equipment your technicians will actually use. For employers with several sites in Maryland and neighbouring states, our corporate NDT training programme keeps training records consistent everywhere. Ask about onsite training for your Maryland crew.

For Maryland employers: written practice and Level III services

Every Maryland company that certifies NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and access to a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, administers and grades exams, reviews procedures and acts as an outside Level III for companies without one in-house.

This is often the real bottleneck. A machine shop in Anne Arundel County winning its first defence subcontract, a Baltimore fabricator taking on bridge work, a Hagerstown supplier adding MT to its quality plan, or an outage contractor whose Level III has retired all face the same problem: nobody can be certified until the written practice and Level III oversight are in place. Our written practice development service builds a document that fits your methods, your codes and your customers' audits, and our SNT-TC-1A guidance explains what auditors look for.

Level III support for Maryland employers includes procedure writing and review, technique sheets, exam administration and grading, review of training and experience records, and preparation for customer, prime-contractor and registrar audits. For broader programme work, see our NDT consulting services. Training and Level III services can be combined so your written practice, course content and exams all line up. Book a Level III consultation for your Maryland company.

Practise before your practical exam

Practical NDT is Atlantis NDT's 3D simulator. Trainees practise 12 inspection methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It builds familiarity and confidence, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

For Maryland trainees the environments map well to local work. The welding workshop mirrors the fabrication and ship repair shops along the Baltimore waterfront. The aircraft hangar matches the aircraft maintenance and test work around Patuxent River, Andrews and Martin State. The storage tank and oil and gas site scenes reflect the tank terminals of Curtis Bay and Fairfield and the LNG and pipeline infrastructure in Southern Maryland. Trainees can rehearse scan patterns, set-ups and inspection sequences between classroom sessions, then go into the practical exam already familiar with what they will be asked to do.

Simulator time does not count as on-the-job experience and is not graded as a practical exam. See the Practical NDT simulator overview or the city page, Practical NDT for Baltimore.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As a Level III he oversees course content, written practices, exams and practical assessment criteria, so the training a Maryland technician receives is tied directly to how that technician will be examined and certified. Questions about method choice, written practices or a particular Maryland code requirement can go straight to him through the contact form.

NDT training in Maryland: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Maryland?

Most Maryland NDT technicians are certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. You complete classroom training in a method, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you to its written practice. Atlantis NDT provides the training, exam support and, if needed, the written practice itself.

Is there NDT training online in Maryland?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online NDT theory classes that Maryland technicians can join from Baltimore, Aberdeen, Hagerstown, Lexington Park or anywhere else in the state. Practical training and the practical exam still require real specimens, which we arrange onsite at your employer or through an agreed partner arrangement.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Maryland?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence or radiation machine registration from the Maryland Department of the Environment's Radiological Health Program, and individual radiographers must meet the state's radiation safety training, certification and supervision requirements under COMAR 26.12. That is separate from, and in addition to, your SNT-TC-1A RT method certification. Confirm current personnel rules with MDE before starting field work.

How much does NDT training cost in Maryland?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on the method, the level, the number of trainees, whether the course is online or onsite, and whether you also need a written practice or exam administration. Send us your crew size and methods and we will return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Maryland?

VT, MT and UT are the everyday methods across Baltimore's port, ship repair, bridge and fabrication work. PAUT, TOFD, ET and PT are in demand for nuclear outages, pressure equipment and aircraft, and RT remains important for pipeline and pressure-piping welds and defence components.

Can you train our crew onsite in Baltimore or Calvert County?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your yard, plant or shop in Baltimore, Calvert County or any other Maryland location is available, scheduled around production, vessel and outage dates. Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in Maryland; onsite means at your facility.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Maryland employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used employer-based certification framework in the United States and is referenced by the codes Maryland industries work to, including ASME and AWS. Nuclear, defence and aerospace customers often add their own requirements on top, which your written practice should address.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom training and experience for each level. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums, shown on our training requirements matrix. The experience usually takes longer than the classroom part, because it must be logged on real work.

Do I need a college degree for NDT training in Maryland?

No degree is required for Level I or Level II under SNT-TC-1A. Education can reduce the experience a written practice requires, and a technical degree shortens the path to Level III, but many Maryland technicians start with a high-school diploma and a welding or trade background.

Does my Maryland certification transfer to another employer?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer that issued it. A new employer reviews your documented training and experience and re-certifies you under its own written practice, which may require new specific and practical exams.

Can I prepare for the ASNT Level III exams from Maryland?

Yes. Our ASNT Level III training runs live online and covers the Basic and method exams. Practice material such as the UT Level 2 practice questions also helps Level II candidates.

What do NDT technicians earn in Maryland?

Earnings vary by method, level, sector, outage overtime and travel. For published ranges, see our NDT Level 2 salary and NDT Level 3 salary guides rather than relying on a single figure.

Start NDT training in Maryland

Whether you are a single technician in Frederick preparing for UT Level II, a Baltimore yard needing a VT and MT cohort before the next availability, an outage contractor preparing a crew for Calvert Cliffs, or a defence supplier in the corridor that needs a written practice and an outside Level III, Atlantis NDT can build the programme around your work. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Request your Maryland NDT training quote, tell us about your crew and methods, or browse the full training catalogue and the national NDT training in the USA hub.

NDT Training and Certification in Massachusetts

Massachusetts technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT as live online classes, scheduled live-virtual cohorts, or onsite courses at their own plant, shop, yard or hangar. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every programme and aligns it with the employer's written practice, so classroom time counts toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus preparation for the Level III exams.

The Commonwealth's NDT market looks different from the refinery-heavy states. There are no oil refineries here. Instead, demand comes from jet-engine and defence manufacturing on the North Shore and along Route 128 and I-495, precision forging and machining in Worcester County, a growing offshore wind supply chain in New Bedford and on the South Coast, LNG and fuel terminals around Boston Harbor, a decommissioning nuclear plant in Plymouth, and one of the oldest bridge, tunnel and rail networks in the country. Massachusetts also runs its own industrial radiographer certification, which matters for RT crews. This page is organised around that map. If you already know what you need, request a Massachusetts training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Massachusetts

Massachusetts NDT work concentrates in five areas: aerospace and defence manufacturing around Lynn and the Route 128/I-495 belt, precision metals in Worcester County and the Blackstone Valley, Boston Harbor's energy terminals, ship repair and infrastructure, the South Coast offshore wind and fishing-fleet ports, and the manufacturing and defence towns of the Pioneer Valley and the Berkshires. Each area leans on different methods and codes.

North Shore and the Route 128/I-495 defence belt

GE Aerospace's plant in Lynn has built military and commercial jet engines and helicopter engines for decades, and its supplier base spreads across Essex and Middlesex counties. Raytheon, part of RTX, designs and builds radar and missile systems at sites including Andover and Tewksbury, and Hanscom Air Force Base in Bedford manages major Air Force electronic systems programmes. Hundreds of machine shops, sheet-metal fabricators, plating houses and special-process suppliers serve these primes. That work calls for PT and MT on machined and forged parts, ET on aerospace alloys, UT on bar, plate and bonded structures, and RT on castings and welded assemblies, usually under prime-contractor procedures and often NAS 410 requirements on top of the supplier's own written practice.

Worcester County and the Blackstone Valley

Central Massachusetts has a long metalworking history. Wyman-Gordon's forging operations in Grafton produce large forgings for aircraft engines, airframes and energy applications, and Worcester's industrial base includes abrasives, machinery, valves and precision components. Forgings and castings need UT for internal soundness, MT and PT for surface flaws and VT throughout. These are classic Level II method jobs where employers want technicians who can read a customer specification as well as a screen.

Boston Harbor: energy terminals, ship repair and infrastructure

Boston Harbor and the Mystic River host the Everett LNG import terminal, fuel and chemical tank farms in Chelsea, Everett and East Boston, the Port of Boston's container and cruise terminals, and a large graving dock in South Boston used for ship repair. Tank and piping integrity work means UT thickness surveys on tank shells, floors and piping, VT and MT on welds, and RT on pressure piping. Around the city, the Massachusetts Department of Transportation, the MBTA and Massport maintain bridges, tunnels, rail structures and airport facilities that need UT, MT and VT on structural steel and welds, much of it from the era of the Central Artery/Tunnel project and earlier.

South Coast and Cape Cod: offshore wind and marine

New Bedford's Marine Commerce Terminal was built as a staging port for offshore wind, and Vineyard Wind 1, the first utility-scale offshore wind farm in US federal waters, was marshalled from the South Coast. Monopiles, transition pieces, towers and their welded connections are inspected with UT, PAUT, MT and VT, often under offshore-wind and structural codes and client specifications. New Bedford and Fall River also support fishing vessels, ferries and marine fabricators. In Plymouth, the Pilgrim nuclear station shut down in 2019 and is being decommissioned, which still brings occasional specialist inspection and radiological work.

Pioneer Valley and the Berkshires

Springfield, Chicopee and Holyoke have a long tradition of precision manufacturing, and Westover Air Reserve Base in Chicopee supports large military transport aircraft. In Pittsfield, General Dynamics Mission Systems carries on the city's defence engineering work, alongside plastics, paper and machinery manufacturers. MT, PT, UT and VT on components and fabrications dominate, with ET on aircraft maintenance at Westover.

Pipelines and utilities

Interstate natural gas transmission pipelines bring gas into Massachusetts from the south and west, and the Commonwealth's gas distribution utilities run large pipe-replacement programmes. Since the 2018 Merrimack Valley gas explosions in Lawrence, Andover and North Andover, gas safety has had close regulatory and public scrutiny. Pipeline welding and in-service integrity digs call for API 1104 weld inspection, UT thickness and VT, and operator qualification for covered tasks.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Massachusetts employers

Atlantis NDT runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based courses in eight methods at Level I and Level II, plus Level III preparation. Massachusetts employers most often need PT, MT, ET and UT for aerospace and defence parts, UT, PAUT and MT for forgings and offshore wind steel, and VT, UT and RT for terminals, bridges and pipelines.

Technicians here can find themselves doing UT thickness on a Chelsea tank one week and PT on machined defence parts in Woburn the next. Many Boston employers prefer theory online, because commuting into a classroom costs more time than the lesson itself, with practicals onsite at the shop or terminal.

Lynn and the North Shore. Engine manufacturing and its suppliers make PT, MT, ET and UT the core methods, and documentation discipline is as important as technique. Prime-contractor audits are frequent, so written practices and training records must hold up.
