SNT-TC-1A certification path in Massachusetts, step by step

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you, not the Commonwealth and not a training school. You complete method training, log documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you to its written practice. RT has an extra state layer, covered in the next section.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer needs a written practice that defines levels, training, experience, exams and recertification. If it does not have one, we can write it.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete the method training the written practice requires, online, live-virtual or onsite. The training requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience in the method on real work, whether engine parts in Lynn, forgings in Grafton or wind steel in New Bedford. The record must be signed and kept.
  4. General exam. A written test on method principles.
  5. Specific exam. A written test on the specifications, procedures and equipment your employer uses, such as a prime contractor's process specification or AWS D1.1.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on inspection of real specimens with known discontinuities, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast checks, repeated annually.
  8. Certification. Issued by your employer and valid for work with that employer. A new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice, though your documented training and experience carry forward.
  9. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets, by evidence of continued satisfactory work or by re-examination.

More detail is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Radiography licensing and other Massachusetts requirements

Massachusetts is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is regulated by the Radiation Control Program of the Massachusetts Department of Public Health under 105 CMR 120.000, which includes licensing and registration rules for industrial radiographic operations and a state certification for industrial radiographers. RT technicians therefore need state radiation safety qualification in addition to SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Under the Massachusetts rules, a certified industrial radiographer is an individual authorised by the Radiation Control Program after meeting training and experience requirements and passing an approved examination. The employing company must hold the appropriate licence for sealed-source radiography or registration for industrial X-ray equipment, appoint a qualified radiation safety officer, and run a programme of periodic job-performance inspections of its radiographers. Our RT Level I and II courses cover the method side: exposure technique, film and digital image quality, and interpretation. Radiation safety training and the state certification are a separate track that every Massachusetts RT technician must complete as well. Out-of-state companies working in Massachusetts should check the reciprocity requirements, and everyone should confirm the current rules with the Radiation Control Program before field work.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Department of Public Safety's Engineering Division, within the Office of Public Safety and Inspections, enforces the boiler and pressure vessel law under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 146. Non-residential boilers and pressure vessels must be registered and inspected, and the division also licenses boiler and pressure vessel inspectors and power plant engineers and firemen. Repairs and alterations follow the National Board Inspection Code, which pulls its NDT requirements from ASME Section V and the construction code.

Pipelines. The Pipeline Safety Division of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities oversees intrastate gas pipeline operators, working with the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), which regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines. Weld inspection on pipelines commonly follows API 1104.

Codes you will meet in Massachusetts. As local context only: NAS 410 and prime-contractor process specifications in aerospace and defence, ASTM practices for PT, MT, UT and ET, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structural steel and bridges, ASME Section V and VIII for pressure equipment, ASME B31.3 and B31.8 for process and gas piping, API 1104 for pipelines, and offshore wind client specifications on the South Coast. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials, or ISO 9712 certificates on European-led wind projects; those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train for. Our training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Massachusetts

Massachusetts crews can take theory live online, join a live-virtual cohort, or have an Atlantis Level III-led programme delivered onsite at their facility. Practical training and practical exams use real specimens, at the employer's site or through a partner arrangement agreed beforehand.

Online theory fits the Commonwealth because congestion around Boston makes a daily commute to a classroom expensive in lost hours. A technician in Pittsfield and one in New Bedford can sit the same live session without either one driving across the state. Sessions are live and interactive, not recorded videos alone, and they cover the general and specific knowledge the written exams test. See NDT training online for details.

Onsite delivery suits manufacturers, terminals and yards that want a group trained on their own parts and procedures. We schedule around what matters locally: production ramps and audits at engine and defence suppliers, offshore wind installation and fabrication campaigns that tend to run hardest in the calmer months, terminal maintenance windows, and winter weather that can make field practicals on bridges and tanks harder. If a campaign or audit is coming, train before it starts.

Practical skill is built on hardware. We plan practical sessions around real specimens, your production parts where appropriate, and the instruments your team actually uses. For multi-site employers, our corporate NDT training programme keeps training records consistent across Massachusetts and other states. Ask about onsite training for your Massachusetts team.

For Massachusetts employers: written practice and Level III services

Every Massachusetts company certifying NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, administers and grades exams, reviews procedures and serves as an outside Level III for companies that do not have one in-house.

This is often where Massachusetts suppliers get stuck. A machine shop in the I-495 belt approved as a special-process source for a defence prime, a Worcester forge adding UT to its quality plan, a New Bedford fabricator bidding on offshore wind secondary steel, or a company whose long-serving Level III has retired cannot certify anyone until the written practice and Level III oversight are in place. Our written practice development service builds a document that fits your methods, specifications and customer audits, and our SNT-TC-1A guidance explains what auditors look for.

Level III support includes procedure and technique writing, exam administration and grading, review of training and experience files, and preparation for customer, prime and registrar audits. For broader programme work, see our NDT consulting services. Book a Level III consultation for your Massachusetts company.

Practise before your practical exam

Practical NDT is Atlantis NDT's 3D simulator. Trainees practise 12 inspection methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It builds familiarity and confidence but is practice only; it does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

Massachusetts trainees will find the environments familiar. The NDT lab mirrors the inspection rooms of North Shore and Worcester County manufacturers, the aircraft hangar matches maintenance at Westover and Hanscom, the welding workshop reflects marine and wind fabricators on the South Coast, and the storage tank scene matches the terminals around Boston Harbor. Trainees can rehearse set-ups, scan patterns and sequences between classes, then walk into the practical exam knowing what is expected.

Simulator time does not count as on-the-job experience and is not a practical exam. See the Practical NDT simulator overview, or the city pages for Boston and Pittsfield.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As Level III he oversees course content, written practices, exams and practical assessment criteria, so what a Massachusetts technician learns is tied to how that technician will be examined and certified. Questions about methods, written practices or a specific Massachusetts requirement can go to him directly through the contact form.

NDT training in Massachusetts: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Massachusetts?

Most Massachusetts NDT technicians are certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A: classroom training in a method, documented on-the-job experience, general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and a vision test. Radiographers also need Massachusetts industrial radiographer certification from the Department of Public Health's Radiation Control Program.

Is there NDT training online in Massachusetts?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online theory classes that technicians can join from Boston, Worcester, Lynn, New Bedford, Springfield or anywhere else in the state. Practical training and practical exams still need real specimens, arranged onsite at your employer or through an agreed partner.

Do I need a license to do industrial radiography in Massachusetts?

Yes. The company needs a licence or registration from the Radiation Control Program, and individuals performing industrial radiography must be certified by that programme after meeting training and experience requirements and passing an approved exam. This is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT method certification, which you also need. Confirm current requirements with the programme.

How much does NDT training cost in Massachusetts?

Quote on request. The quote depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and whether you also need a written practice or exam administration. Send your crew size and methods and we will reply with a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in Massachusetts?

PT, MT, ET and UT dominate because aerospace, defence and precision manufacturing are the state's biggest NDT employers. UT, PAUT and MT are in demand for forgings and offshore wind steel, and VT, UT and RT for terminals, bridges and pipelines.

Can you train our team onsite in Boston, Worcester or New Bedford?

Yes. Onsite delivery is available at your facility anywhere in Massachusetts, scheduled around production, audits and campaigns. Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in the state; onsite means at your site.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Massachusetts employers?

Yes. It is the most common employer-based certification framework in US industry and is referenced by ASME, AWS and many aerospace and defence specifications. Some customers add requirements such as NAS 410, which your written practice should address.

Do I need NAS 410 for aerospace NDT jobs in Massachusetts?

Some aerospace primes and their suppliers require personnel to be qualified to NAS 410 rather than, or in addition to, SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based; if your customer requires NAS 410, check with them how they want training and certification documented.

How long does UT Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom training and experience for each level. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums are on our training requirements matrix. Logging the experience usually takes longer than the classroom part.

Can I prepare for the ASNT Level III exams from Massachusetts?

Yes. Our ASNT Level III training runs live online and covers the Basic and method exams. Level II candidates can also use the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Does my certification move with me to a new Massachusetts employer?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer that issued it. A new employer reviews your records and re-certifies you to its own written practice, which may involve new specific and practical exams. A state radiographer certification is personal and follows the state's own renewal rules.

What do NDT technicians earn in Massachusetts?

Earnings depend on method, level, sector and overtime. For published ranges, see the NDT Level 2 salary and NDT Level 3 salary guides rather than a single headline figure.

Start NDT training in Massachusetts

Whether you are a technician in Lowell preparing for PT Level II, a Worcester forge that needs a UT cohort, a New Bedford fabricator preparing for offshore wind work, or a defence supplier that needs a written practice and an outside Level III before its next audit, Atlantis NDT will build the programme around your work. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. NDT Training and Certification in Michigan

Short answer: Michigan technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at your own plant, shop or outage site, all led and overseen by an ASNT NDT Level III. Certification is employer-based: your written practice, your training hours, your on-the-job experience and your exams, administered by a Level III. Atlantis has no Michigan training centre; we come to your facility or teach you online.

Michigan is one of the most demanding NDT markets in the Midwest because it combines high-volume manufacturing with heavy industry. The same state that stamps, casts, welds and machines a large share of North America's vehicles and powertrain parts also runs a refinery in Detroit, three nuclear plant sites on its Lake Michigan and Lake Erie shores, crude and gas pipelines that cross the Straits of Mackinac and the Thumb, steel mills along the Detroit River, chemical plants in the Great Lakes Bay Region, and an Air National Guard base north of the city. Each of those sectors has its own codes, its own customer specifications and its own idea of what a qualified technician looks like. This page explains how NDT training and certification works for Michigan, where the work is, what Michigan employers ask for, which regulators matter, and how to request a Michigan training quote that fits your crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Michigan

Direct answer: NDT work in Michigan clusters in Southeast Michigan (automotive, steel, refining, power), the Great Lakes Bay Region (chemicals, castings, energy), West Michigan (aerospace suppliers, furniture-metal fabrication, food-plant stainless), the Lake Michigan and Lake Erie shorelines (nuclear plants, pumped storage) and Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula (pipelines, mining, locks and bridges).

Southeast Michigan: Detroit, Dearborn, Warren, Monroe and Downriver

Metro Detroit is the centre of gravity. The Detroit Three and hundreds of Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers run stamping, casting, forging, welding and assembly lines where NDT is used for weld verification, casting porosity checks, crack detection in forged and heat-treated parts, adhesive and spot-weld evaluation, and incoming inspection of bought-in components. Ultrasonic spot-weld testing, eddy current sorting and crack detection, magnetic particle inspection of forgings and penetrant testing of aluminium castings are all common. Marathon Petroleum's Detroit refinery, the only refinery in the state, generates turnaround and in-service inspection demand: corrosion mapping, thickness surveys on piping circuits, weld radiography and phased array on new tie-ins. Cleveland-Cliffs' Dearborn Works and the steel and metals plants Downriver bring rolling-mill, crane and structural inspection. DTE Energy's Fermi 2 nuclear plant near Monroe and the coal-to-gas transition at the region's large power stations add boiler, piping and pressure-boundary work. The Gordie Howe International Bridge and the steady flow of MDOT bridge projects keep structural welding inspectors and UT technicians busy.

Great Lakes Bay Region: Midland, Saginaw and Bay City

Midland is home to Dow's large chemical complex, which means process piping, pressure vessels, heat exchangers and storage tanks inspected to ASME and API practice, with frequent shutdown windows. Saginaw has a long casting and powertrain history, and foundry work means radiography and penetrant of castings, plus ultrasonic inspection of machined parts. Bay City and the surrounding area add power generation and marine work on Saginaw Bay.

West Michigan: Grand Rapids, Muskegon, Holland and Kalamazoo

West Michigan has a dense base of precision manufacturers and aerospace suppliers, so you see penetrant and magnetic particle lines working to customer specifications and NAS 410-style aerospace requirements, eddy current on aluminium and fastener holes, and ultrasonic inspection of composites and bonded structures. Muskegon adds foundries and heavy fabrication, Holland has battery and advanced-manufacturing plants, and Kalamazoo has pharmaceutical and food-grade stainless fabrication where orbital welds and visual inspection matter.

Lakeshore power: Bridgman, Covert and Ludington

Michigan's nuclear sites, the D.C. Cook plant at Bridgman and the Palisades plant at Covert, plus Fermi 2 in Monroe County, create ASME Section XI in-service inspection work during refuelling outages, along with UT, ET of steam generator and heat-exchanger tubing, and VT of supports and welds. Consumers Energy's Ludington Pumped Storage plant on Lake Michigan adds penstock, turbine and structural inspection.

Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula

Enbridge's Line 5 crosses the Straits of Mackinac and the Upper Peninsula, and interstate gas transmission lines run across the Lower Peninsula, so pipeline construction and integrity programmes need API 1104 weld radiography, AUT, UT thickness and visual inspection. The Soo Locks at Sault Ste. Marie, where a new lock chamber is being built, the Mackinac Bridge, mining operations in the western UP and paper mills add structural and rotating-equipment work.

If your company works in any of these regions, you can ask about onsite training for your Michigan crew and we will plan around your production schedule or outage window.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Michigan employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT teaches UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, plus Level III exam preparation, all structured around ASNT SNT-TC-1A and your company written practice. The table below maps each method to the Michigan work it is most often used for.

Our ASNT Level III training page explains how preparation is structured. For Level II UT candidates, the UT Level 2 practice questions are a useful self-check before your written exams.

NDT training by city in Michigan

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT serves every Michigan city the same way, online or onsite at the employer's facility. Detroit has a dedicated training page, and several other Michigan cities have Practical NDT simulator pages. The table shows where each city's demand comes from.

Detroit. Detroit crews tend to split between production NDT inside plants, where MT, PT, ET and UT on parts dominate, and field NDT in refining, power and construction, where UT thickness, PAUT, RT and VT on welds dominate. That split matters for training: a production technician may need deep knowledge of one technique on one part family, while a field technician needs broad code knowledge. We build the course content around which of those your crew is doing. See the Detroit training page for city detail.

Grand Rapids. West Michigan's aerospace and precision suppliers work to prime-contractor specifications that often reference NAS 410 alongside or in place of SNT-TC-1A. We are clear about what we teach: our training is SNT-TC-1A-based, and if your customer requires NAS 410 qualification your Level III will need to map our training to that standard. Many Grand Rapids shops use penetrant and eddy current heavily.

Flint and Saginaw. These cities have deep automotive and casting roots. Foundry radiography, penetrant on aluminium castings, MT on steel parts and ultrasonic checks on welded assemblies are the typical work. Onsite training on the customer's own parts and procedures is especially effective here because acceptance criteria are part-specific.

Midland and Bay City. Chemical-plant inspection relies on API 510 and API 570 programmes run by the owner, with UT thickness, PAUT and RT doing the measurement. We do not offer API inspector certification training, but we train the NDT technicians who collect the data those inspectors rely on.

Lansing, Kalamazoo and Monroe. Lansing has automotive assembly and structural work, Kalamazoo has clean-process stainless fabrication and defence suppliers, and Monroe combines a nuclear plant, a large coal-fired station and steel. All are served online and onsite.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Michigan, step by step

Direct answer: In Michigan, as in every other US state, SNT-TC-1A certification is issued by your employer, not by the state or by ASNT. The employer's written practice sets training hours, experience and exam rules; a Level III administers exams; and the employer certifies you once you pass and meet the vision requirements.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. This document, based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, defines the methods, levels, training hours, experience hours, exam content, passing grades, vision tests and recertification interval. If your company does not have one, see written practice development.
  2. You complete formal classroom training. Training hours per method and level are set by the written practice using SNT-TC-1A recommendations. Check the training requirements matrix for the guideline figures.
  3. You build on-the-job experience. Experience is logged under the supervision of qualified personnel, in the method and on the kind of work you will be certified for.
  4. You pass general, specific and practical exams. The general exam covers method theory, the specific exam covers your employer's procedures, codes and equipment, and the practical exam is performed on real specimens. A Level III prepares and administers these.
  5. You pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity is checked annually and colour contrast as the written practice requires.
  6. Your employer certifies you. Certification is documented and is valid for your employer. If you change jobs in Michigan, your new employer decides whether to recertify you under its own practice.
  7. You recertify. Recertification intervals are set in the written practice, commonly through re-examination or evidence of continued satisfactory performance.

For Level III candidates the path is different: the ASNT NDT Level III certificate is issued centrally by ASNT through examination, and employers then certify their Level III under their written practice. More detail is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Radiography licensing and other Michigan requirements

Direct answer: Michigan is not an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources such as Ir-192 or Co-60 in Michigan is licensed by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Region III, under 10 CFR Part 34. The state's radiological protection programme within the Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) regulates X-ray equipment and certain other radiation sources.

This split is important for training. A Michigan radiography company using isotope cameras holds an NRC licence, follows 10 CFR 34 for radiographer and radiographer-trainee qualification, radiation-safety training, personnel monitoring, survey instruments and two-person field crews, and its radiographers must be certified through an NRC-recognised route. A company using only X-ray cabinets or portable X-ray tubes deals with the state for registration and inspection. Radiation-safety training is separate from the SNT-TC-1A RT method training that teaches film or digital technique and interpretation; your crew needs both. Because rules are updated, confirm the current requirements with NRC Region III and EGLE before a new crew starts field work.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Michigan's boiler programme sits within the Boiler Division of the Bureau of Construction Codes in the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA). Michigan adopts ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code sections and the National Board Inspection Code for installation, repair and inspection, so ASME Section V NDT methods and Section VIII or Section I acceptance criteria show up in shop and field work. Repair organisations work to National Board requirements.

Pipelines. Intrastate natural gas pipeline safety in Michigan is overseen by the Michigan Public Service Commission, while interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines, including Line 5, are regulated by PHMSA. Pipeline welding and NDT generally follow API 1104, and operators require NDT technicians to meet their own qualification programmes in addition to SNT-TC-1A certification.

Codes common in Michigan. ASME Section V, VIII and B31.3 in refining and chemicals; ASME Section XI at the nuclear plants; AWS D1.1 for structural steel and bridges (with AASHTO/AWS D1.5 for bridges); API 1104 for pipelines; automotive OEM and customer standards in manufacturing; and NAS 410 in aerospace supply chains, which we mention as context only.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Michigan

Direct answer: Michigan crews can train three ways with Atlantis NDT: self-paced or scheduled online theory, live-virtual cohorts with a Level III instructor, or onsite sessions at your plant or job site. Practical exams are always performed on real specimens under Level III oversight, never replaced by video or simulation.

Michigan scheduling has a rhythm, and training works best when it follows it. Automotive plants have model-year changeovers and summer shutdown weeks, which are good windows for production NDT staff. Refineries and chemical plants schedule turnarounds, often in spring and autumn, which is exactly when contract technicians are least available, so we push theory into the months before. Nuclear sites have refuelling outages on fixed cycles, and contractor technicians are often booked months out; online theory lets them study at home between outages. Pipeline construction slows in the Michigan winter, so pipeline crews often train in the cold months. Northern and Upper Peninsula companies benefit most from online theory, because travelling to Metro Detroit for a classroom week is expensive in time.

Onsite delivery means the instructor comes to your Michigan facility, uses your equipment, your procedures and, where possible, your own parts and welds as practice specimens, and the specific exam can reflect your actual work. It suits companies with five or more technicians in a method, or companies that want training tied tightly to their written practice. Live online theory suits mixed groups and individuals. For details see online NDT training and corporate NDT training, and when you are ready, request a cohort or onsite quote for Michigan; cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

For Michigan employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Michigan companies that certify their own NDT people need a compliant written practice, a Level III to own it, and auditable training and exam records. Atlantis NDT writes and reviews written practices, provides Level III services, and runs corporate training programmes for Michigan employers.

Many Michigan manufacturers have a handful of technicians doing one or two methods inside a quality department, and no in-house Level III. Customer audits by OEMs and aerospace primes are where gaps show up: missing training records, exams not administered by a qualified Level III, vision tests out of date, or a written practice that does not match what the shop actually does. We help close those gaps with:

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A, aligned with your customers' requirements.
  • Level III services: procedure writing and review, technique sheets, exam preparation and administration, and audit support. See NDT consulting in Michigan.
  • Corporate training programmes for multi-site Michigan employers, so the same standard applies in Detroit, Grand Rapids and Saginaw.
  • Guidance on SNT-TC-1A certification for companies writing their first practice.

If an OEM audit is coming up, book a Level III consultation and we will review your current documents first.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets Michigan trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments before their hands-on exam. It builds familiarity with technique and equipment set-up, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank environment. For Michigan users, the welding workshop maps well to fabrication and automotive weld inspection, the oil and gas site and storage tank to Detroit and Midland plant work, and the aircraft hangar to West Michigan aerospace suppliers and Selfridge-area maintenance. Learn more at Practical NDT and the Practical NDT Michigan page.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, written practices and Level III services, and the onsite and live-virtual training delivered to Michigan employers.

NDT training in Michigan: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Michigan?

Get hired or sponsored by an employer that has an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the classroom training hours it requires, build the on-the-job experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass the vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and can help your employer with the rest.

Is there NDT training online in Michigan?

Yes. Theory for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET can be taken live online from anywhere in Michigan, including the Upper Peninsula. Practical exams are still performed on real specimens under Level III oversight.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Michigan?

The company needs the licence or registration, and radiographers need qualification. Michigan is not an NRC Agreement State, so isotope radiography is licensed by the NRC under 10 CFR 34, while X-ray equipment falls under the state's EGLE radiological programme. Confirm current rules with both agencies.

How much does NDT training cost in Michigan?

It is quoted on request. The quote depends on method, level, number of trainees, online versus onsite delivery, and whether you also need written-practice or exam support. We return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Michigan?

UT is in demand across almost every sector. MT and PT are heavily used in automotive, forging and casting; PAUT and RT are in demand for pipelines, refining and power; ET matters for parts sorting and heat-exchanger tubing.

Can you train our crew onsite in Detroit or Grand Rapids?

Yes. Onsite training at your facility is available anywhere in Michigan, using your equipment and procedures where possible.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Michigan employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used guideline for employer-based NDT certification in US industry, including Michigan manufacturing, energy and construction. Some aerospace customers also reference NAS 410, so check your customer's requirement.

How long does Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, the method, and your experience. Classroom hours and experience hours are both set by the practice; see the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline figures.

Can I take NDT training without an employer in Michigan?

You can take the classroom training as an individual, and it counts toward the formal training requirement. Certification itself still needs an employer and its written practice.

Do automotive plants in Michigan need certified NDT technicians?

Plants that use NDT to accept product, or whose customers require documented qualification, generally certify their inspectors to a written practice. Requirements come from the customer and the quality system, so check what your OEM or Tier 1 asks for.

Do you prepare candidates for the ASNT Level III exams?

Yes. We offer Level III exam preparation for the Basic and method examinations. See ASNT Level III training.

What does an NDT technician earn in Michigan?

Pay varies with method, level, sector and overtime. For published ranges, see our NDT salary guide.

Start NDT training in Michigan

Whether you run a production NDT lab in Metro Detroit, a field crew working turnarounds in Midland, a pipeline contractor in Northern Michigan or an aerospace supplier in West Michigan, the route is the same: tell us the methods, levels and number of people, and whether you want online, live-virtual or onsite delivery. Request your Michigan NDT training quote, explore all training options, or try the Practical NDT simulator first. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

NDT Training and Certification in Minnesota

Short answer: A Minnesota technician or employer gets ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II or III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, a private live-virtual cohort for one company, or onsite delivery at the employer's refinery, mine, plant or shop. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every programme. Theory is mapped to your employer's written practice, practical exams are given on real specimens at your facility, and the employer that signs the certification stays in control of it.

Minnesota's NDT market is shaped by geography as much as by industry. The Twin Cities carry two refineries, a dense manufacturing and medical-device base, an airline hub and the head offices of several national inspection and engineering firms. Two hundred miles north, the Iron Range runs taconite mines and pellet plants on some of the heaviest rotating and structural equipment in North America, while Duluth handles ore, grain and crude oil at the head of the Great Lakes. Two nuclear stations sit on the Mississippi, a major crude pipeline corridor crosses the north of the state, and the state's bridge inspection programme has been under close public attention since 2007. This hub maps where that work happens, which methods and levels Minnesota employers ask for, which state agencies matter for radiography and pipeline crews, and how to train people without pulling them off a shutdown or a winter maintenance window. If you already know what you need, request a Minnesota training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Minnesota

Direct answer: Minnesota NDT work clusters in five areas: the Twin Cities metro with its two refineries, manufacturing, medical-device and aviation base; the Mississippi River nuclear and power corridor; the Iron Range taconite mines and pellet plants; Duluth and the North Shore ports; and the regional manufacturing cities of Rochester, St. Cloud and Mankato. Refining, mining and manufacturing quality control drive most of the demand.

The Twin Cities and the south metro refineries

Minnesota has two refineries, both in the south and east metro: the Pine Bend refinery in Rosemount and the St. Paul Park refinery on the Mississippi. Both run mechanical integrity programmes under OSHA process safety management (29 CFR 1910.119), which means ultrasonic thickness surveys on piping circuits and vessels, shear-wave and phased array weld inspection on repairs and tie-ins, radiography of small-bore welds, magnetic particle and penetrant on nozzles and rotating equipment, and visual inspection at every step. Turnarounds swell crews quickly, and contractors in the metro want people certified before the season rather than during it. Around the refineries, the metro has hundreds of fabrication, machining and casting shops, pressure vessel and heat exchanger builders, agricultural and recreational-vehicle suppliers, and one of the largest medical-device clusters in the world, where penetrant, visual, radiographic and ultrasonic inspection support component quality. Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport is a major airline hub with heavy maintenance and component shops, where eddy current, penetrant and ultrasonic inspection of aircraft structures and engine parts is daily work, usually under an aerospace certification scheme.

The Mississippi River nuclear and power corridor

Two nuclear generating stations sit on the Mississippi: Monticello, upstream of the metro, and Prairie Island near Red Wing. Their refuelling outages bring in inspection crews working to ASME Section XI, with ultrasonic examination of piping welds, eddy current examination of steam generator and heat exchanger tubing, and visual examinations of components and supports. Coal and gas-fired stations along the river and around the state add boiler tube thickness surveys, header and piping weld inspection, and condenser tube eddy current during planned outages. Wind and transmission construction across southern and western Minnesota add structural weld and bolt inspection.

The Iron Range

The Mesabi Range, from Grand Rapids east through Hibbing, Virginia and Mountain Iron towards the North Shore, produces most of the iron ore mined in the United States, processed into taconite pellets at large concentrator and pelletising plants. Mining NDT is heavy, rugged and safety-critical: ultrasonic and magnetic particle inspection of crusher and grinding-mill shells and shafts, haul-truck frames and suspension components, shovel booms and dippers, kiln tyres and girth gears, conveyor pulleys and structural steel in plants that run around the clock. A lot of this work is done by maintenance teams who need practical, well-documented Level I and II certification in UT, MT and VT, with a Level III available to write procedures for unusual components. Distances on the Range are long, so live online theory with a short onsite practical block at the plant is usually the only practical way to train a crew.

Duluth and the North Shore

Duluth and neighbouring Superior, Wisconsin form the Twin Ports, the largest port on the Great Lakes by tonnage, shipping iron ore, coal and grain. The ore docks, ship repair yards and grain elevators need structural, weld and corrosion inspection. Duluth is also home to a general-aviation aircraft manufacturer, which brings composite and metallic aerospace inspection, and to fabrication shops that serve the mines and the port. North of the city, the Silver Bay pellet plant and the North Shore power and paper facilities add their own outage work. See NDT training in Duluth.

Pipelines, Rochester, St. Cloud, Mankato and the rest of the state

A major crude-oil pipeline corridor runs across northern Minnesota from the North Dakota border through the Clearbrook terminal to Superior, and the Line 3 replacement project brought a large wave of API 1104 weld inspection and radiography to the region during construction. Integrity work continues with in-line inspection verification digs, where crews use UT, PAUT and MT on exposed pipe. Elsewhere, Rochester carries medical and precision manufacturing; St. Cloud carries bus and vehicle manufacturing, granite and fabrication; Mankato and the southern cities carry agricultural equipment and food processing; and the north-west carries recreational-vehicle manufacturing. MnDOT's steel bridge inventory keeps bridge weld inspection to AWS D1.5 and fracture-critical member inspection in demand across the state.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Minnesota employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation. In Minnesota the highest volume is UT and RT for refinery and pipeline work, UT, MT and VT for Iron Range mining equipment, and ET, PT and UT for power, aviation and precision manufacturing.

For Level III candidates, we prepare you for the ASNT Level III basic and method examinations and the practical side of the role: writing procedures, building exam banks and administering exams for a Minnesota employer. See ASNT Level III training. Each course is matched to your employer's written practice, so a mine's MT course practises on real mining components and a refinery contractor's UT course on piping and vessel welds.

NDT training by city in Minnesota

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has local training pages for Minneapolis and Duluth, plus Practical NDT simulator pages for Minneapolis, Duluth and Rochester. None of these is a physical training centre; each explains what local employers need and how we deliver online or onsite at your facility in that city.

Minneapolis-St. Paul. The state's largest NDT employer base: refinery contractors in the south metro, fabrication and casting shops across the region, medical-device quality labs, airline and component MRO at MSP, and the offices of engineering and inspection firms that send crews across the Upper Midwest. Demand is spread across all eight methods. See NDT training in Minneapolis.

Duluth. Port, dock, ship repair and fabrication work, with aircraft manufacturing adding aerospace inspection. Technicians often work both Duluth and Superior. See NDT training in Duluth and Practical NDT in Duluth.

Rochester. Medical and precision manufacturing with smaller in-house quality teams, mostly needing PT, VT, UT and RT. See Practical NDT in Rochester.

The Iron Range. Mining maintenance crews needing UT, MT and VT certification under a written practice suited to heavy equipment. Training is usually live online theory followed by an onsite practical week at the plant.

Red Wing and Monticello. Nuclear outage work under ASME Section XI. Outage contractors usually hire already-certified Level II technicians, so this market rewards technicians who have built UT and ET experience elsewhere first.

St. Cloud and Mankato. Vehicle, agricultural-equipment and fabrication plants with in-house weld inspection needs, mainly VT, MT and UT.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Minnesota, step by step

Direct answer: Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you, not the state. You complete the classroom training and supervised experience your employer's written practice requires, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, pass a vision test, and the employer certifies you. The path is the same at a refinery contractor, a mine or a machine shop.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer must have a written practice setting training hours, experience hours, exam content and recertification rules for each method and level. If it does not, we can write one.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the formal training hours for your method and level. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures; your written practice governs.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience in the method, documented by your employer. On the Iron Range and in refinery turnarounds this builds quickly; in a small shop it can take longer.
  4. General and specific written exams. A Level III administers the theory exam and the specific exam on your employer's procedures, codes and equipment.
  5. Practical exam. You perform the method on real specimens and document results, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  6. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, typically every year.
  7. Certification. The employer certifies you to Level I or II in that method. Certification is tied to that employer.
  8. Recertification. At the interval set in the written practice, by exam or documented continued satisfactory work.

For a fuller explanation, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Minnesota requirements

Direct answer: Minnesota has been an NRC Agreement State since March 31, 2006, so industrial radiography with sealed sources is licensed by the Minnesota Department of Health (MDH) under Minnesota Rules chapter 4731, not directly by the NRC. Radiographers and trainees must meet those state requirements in addition to their employer's SNT-TC-1A certification.

Minnesota's industrial radiography rules mirror the structure of the federal rules in 10 CFR Part 34: the licensee needs a radiation safety officer, operating and emergency procedures and leak-tested, surveyed equipment; individuals complete radiation-safety training and work as trainees under a qualified radiographer trainer before acting as radiographers; radiographers must be certified through a recognised certifying programme; and personnel wear dosimetry and use survey meters on every job. X-ray equipment, including the cabinet and vault systems common in metro foundries and medical-device plants, is registered and regulated separately by MDH. Rules and forms change, so confirm current requirements with MDH before planning an RT programme.

What Atlantis NDT covers: our RT courses teach radiographic technique, exposure calculation, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance criteria for SNT-TC-1A Level I and II. The state radiation-safety requirements and radiographer certification are separate obligations that your radiation safety officer manages with MDH. We help employers line the two up so trainees progress on both tracks at once.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry (DLI) runs the state boiler and pressure vessel inspection programme within the National Board framework. NDT technicians meet it through repair and alteration work on boilers and vessels at refineries, power plants, mills and food plants, where the National Board Inspection Code and ASME Sections I and VIII govern examination.

Pipelines. Minnesota has its own pipeline regulator, the Minnesota Office of Pipeline Safety (MNOPS) within the Department of Public Safety, which inspects and enforces safety rules for intrastate gas and hazardous liquid pipeline operators under certification from PHMSA. Interstate lines fall under PHMSA. Weld inspection on pipelines usually follows API 1104, and operator qualification rules apply to covered tasks.

Codes commonly used in Minnesota. ASME Section V (NDE methods), Sections I and VIII (boilers and pressure vessels), B31.1 and B31.3 (power and process piping), B31.4 and B31.8 (pipelines), API 1104 (pipeline welding), API 650 and 653 context for tanks, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structural and bridge steel, ASME Section XI at Monticello and Prairie Island, and NAS 410 for aerospace employers. Some Minnesota employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials for specific roles. Those are separate schemes; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only, and we mention them only so you know what local job postings may request.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Minnesota

Direct answer: Minnesota technicians can take theory live online, join a private live-virtual cohort for their employer, or have an Atlantis Level III deliver the programme onsite at their refinery, mine, plant or shop. Atlantis has no training centre in Minnesota; practical exams are held at the client's facility on real specimens.

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory classes with attendance records, ideal for Iron Range crews and technicians spread across greater Minnesota. See online NDT training.
  • Private live-virtual cohort. One employer's group, scheduled around shift rotations, with content tied to your written practice, procedures and components.
  • Onsite. A Level III teaches the hands-on portion and runs practical exams at your facility, whether that is a south metro refinery contractor's yard, a pellet plant on the Range or a shop in St. Cloud. See corporate NDT training.

The Minnesota calendar is distinct. Refineries and power stations schedule turnarounds and outages in spring and autumn, pipeline and bridge field work concentrates in the construction season, and deep winter shifts effort indoors to shops and plants, which is often the best time for training. Great Lakes shipping stops for winter, so port and ship repair work peaks then. We usually suggest online theory in quieter weeks and a protected onsite practical block. Ask about onsite training for your Minnesota crew.

For Minnesota employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Minnesota inspection contractors, mines, fabricators and manufacturers use Atlantis NDT to write or update SNT-TC-1A written practices, provide outside Level III services, administer exams and train whole crews. Refinery owners, OEM customers and auditors check exactly these records.

Common gaps in Minnesota programmes include mining maintenance departments performing UT and MT without a written practice at all, written practices that never added PAUT when the company bought the equipment, procedures referencing superseded code editions, and practical exams without documented grading. Contractors bidding refinery or pipeline work face owner reviews of personnel files before mobilisation. We review your documents, write or revise the written practice and procedures, build exam banks and can act as your examining Level III.

  • Written practice development
  • SNT-TC-1A certification guidance
  • Corporate NDT training for whole crews
  • NDT consulting in Minnesota for procedures and audit preparation

Book a Level III consultation for your Minnesota company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Atlantis Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens given by your Level III.

Refinery and pipeline trainees in the metro and the north get most from the oil and gas site and storage tank scenes, fabrication and mining maintenance trainees from the welding workshop and NDT lab, and MSP and Duluth aviation trainees from the aircraft hangar. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT in Minnesota. For written exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He builds the course content, maps it to each employer's written practice and oversees examinations. On onsite programmes in Minnesota he works alongside your Level III or serves as the examining Level III if you do not have one.

NDT training in Minnesota: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Minnesota?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its classroom training and supervised experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you. Completing Level I theory before you apply can help with refinery contractors and fabricators.

Is there NDT training online in Minnesota?

Yes. Atlantis NDT delivers the theory portion live online anywhere in Minnesota, including the Iron Range and the north-west. Practical training and practical exams are completed on real specimens, at your employer's facility or through an arranged practical session.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Minnesota?

Minnesota is an NRC Agreement State, so the Minnesota Department of Health licenses industrial radiography. The employer holds the licence; individuals need state-compliant radiation-safety training, trainee status and radiographer certification. SNT-TC-1A certification is an additional, separate requirement.

How much does NDT training cost in Minnesota?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, and whether you choose online, a private cohort or onsite delivery. Request a Minnesota quote and we reply within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Minnesota?

Ultrasonic testing is the most widely used, from refinery thickness surveys to mining shaft inspection. Magnetic particle and visual testing are close behind in mining and fabrication, and radiography is important for pipeline and refinery work.

Can you train our crew onsite on the Iron Range?

Yes. A Level III can deliver the hands-on portion at your mine or pellet plant, using your equipment and real components, and run the practical exams there after your crew completes theory online.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Minnesota employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most common basis for NDT certification in Minnesota refining, pipeline, mining, fabrication and power work. Aerospace employers may require NAS 410, and nuclear outage work follows the plant's own programme requirements.

How long does Level II training take?

It depends on the method and your employer's written practice, which sets the classroom and experience hours. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures. Supervised experience usually takes longer than classroom training.

Does Atlantis NDT have a training centre in Minneapolis?

No. We do not operate a physical training centre in Minneapolis or anywhere in Minnesota. Training is delivered live online, as a live-virtual cohort, or onsite at your employer's facility.

Who regulates pipeline inspection in Minnesota?

The Minnesota Office of Pipeline Safety oversees intrastate gas and hazardous liquid pipelines, and PHMSA oversees interstate lines. NDT personnel on pipeline jobs usually work to API 1104 under the operator's or contractor's qualification programme.

Do you offer API 653 or CWI courses in Minnesota?

No. Atlantis NDT training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training only. Some Minnesota employers also ask for those separate credentials for specific roles, and you would need a provider that specialises in them.

NDT Training and Certification in Mississippi

Short answer: Mississippi technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT in three ways: live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite sessions at your own shipyard, refinery, plant or pipeline spread. An ASNT NDT Level III leads and oversees the training. Certification is employer-based. Your written practice sets training, experience and exam rules, and a Level III administers the exams. Atlantis has no Mississippi training centre. We teach online or come to your facility.

Mississippi has a small population but a concentrated, demanding NDT market. The Gulf Coast has the state's largest manufacturing employer, a Navy shipyard building destroyers and amphibious ships, next to the state's largest refinery, an LNG terminal and a cluster of commercial shipyards. Inland there is a nuclear power station on the Mississippi River, a NASA rocket-engine test centre, three military flight-training bases, auto plants at Canton and Blue Springs, a steel-and-aerospace cluster around Columbus, and oil, gas and pipeline work across the south and east. Each sector has its own codes and its own idea of a qualified technician. This page explains where Mississippi NDT work is, what each sector expects, which state agencies regulate radiography, boilers and pipelines, and how to request a Mississippi NDT training quote for your crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Mississippi

Direct answer: Mississippi NDT work clusters on the Gulf Coast (naval and commercial shipbuilding, refining, LNG, power, ports), in the Jackson metro and along the Mississippi River (automotive, refining, nuclear power), at Stennis and the coastal military bases (rocket testing, aircraft), in the Golden Triangle around Columbus (steel, aerospace), in Northeast Mississippi (automotive, furniture, fabrication) and across the Pine Belt and oilfields (oil, gas and pipelines).

The Gulf Coast: Pascagoula, Moss Point, Gulfport and Biloxi

Ingalls Shipbuilding in Pascagoula, part of HII, builds destroyers, amphibious assault ships and amphibious transport docks for the Navy, and has built national security cutters for the Coast Guard. It is Mississippi's largest manufacturing employer. Shipbuilding at that scale means constant weld inspection: visual testing, magnetic particle, penetrant, ultrasonic and radiographic testing of hull, deck, piping and machinery welds, much of it to naval technical publications. Commercial yards such as VT Halter Marine build and repair vessels in the same area. Next door, Chevron's Pascagoula refinery is the largest in the state and generates major turnaround and in-service inspection work. Gulf LNG's import terminal, Mississippi Power's Plant Daniel near Escatawpa, the Port of Gulfport and the Port of Pascagoula add tank, piping, power-plant and structural inspection. Keesler Air Force Base in Biloxi and the Naval Construction Battalion Center in Gulfport add aircraft and equipment maintenance.

Stennis and Hancock County

NASA's John C. Stennis Space Center in Hancock County is the United States' largest rocket-engine test site. Test stands, high-pressure propellant and gas systems, cryogenic piping and the engine hardware tested there need pressure-system, weld and component inspection, and aerospace contractors at the site bring their own aerospace inspection requirements.

Jackson, Canton and the Mississippi River

Nissan's Canton assembly plant and its suppliers need production NDT on welded bodies, frames and components. Ergon's refinery in Vicksburg brings refinery turnaround work. Entergy's Grand Gulf Nuclear Station near Port Gibson, a single-unit plant and one of the largest boiling-water reactors in the country, brings ASME Section XI in-service inspection during refuelling outages. Jackson itself is the base for many of the state's fabrication shops, inspection contractors and engineering firms.

The Golden Triangle: Columbus, Starkville and West Point

Steel Dynamics operates a flat-rolled steel mill near Columbus, and Airbus Helicopters and Aurora Flight Sciences build aircraft there. Columbus Air Force Base trains Air Force pilots. Mill work needs UT of plate and coils, MT of rolls and shafts, and inspection of cranes and structures. Aerospace work needs penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic inspection of metallic and composite structures to aerospace specifications.

Northeast Mississippi: Tupelo, Blue Springs and Corinth

Toyota's Blue Springs plant, upholstered-furniture manufacturing around Tupelo, and metal fabricators and tank builders across the northeast need production and weld inspection. Naval Air Station Meridian, to the south-east, adds aircraft-maintenance work.

The Pine Belt and oilfields: Hattiesburg, Laurel and Natchez

Oil and gas production in south and south-west Mississippi, gas storage and gathering systems, and interstate gas and liquids pipelines crossing the state need API 1104 weld radiography and phased array, UT thickness surveys and visual inspection. Laurel has oilfield-equipment and fabrication shops, and Natchez has river industry and gas facilities.

Wherever your company is, you can ask about onsite training for your Mississippi crew. We schedule around production, ship deliveries, outages and turnarounds.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Mississippi, step by step

Direct answer: Mississippi does not license NDT technicians in general. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you based on its written practice. The practice sets training hours, experience, exams and vision tests, a Level III administers the exams, and the employer issues the certification once you meet every requirement.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. It defines methods, levels, training and experience hours, exam content, passing grades, vision tests and recertification. If your company needs one, see written practice development.
  2. You complete formal training. Classroom hours per method and level come from the practice, using SNT-TC-1A recommendations. See the training requirements matrix for the guideline figures.
  3. You build documented experience. On-the-job hours in the method, under qualified supervision, on ship welds, plant piping, pipeline welds or production parts, depending on your work.
  4. You pass the general, specific and practical exams. The general exam covers theory, the specific exam covers your employer's procedures, codes and equipment, and the practical exam is done on real specimens. A Level III prepares and administers them.
  5. You pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity is checked annually, and colour contrast as the practice requires.
  6. Your employer certifies you. Certification belongs to that employer. If you move from a Pascagoula yard to a Jackson inspection contractor, the new employer decides how to recertify you.
  7. You recertify on schedule. The practice sets the interval and the evidence required.

The ASNT NDT Level III certificate is different. ASNT issues it centrally by examination, and employers then certify their Level III under their own practice. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Mississippi requirements

Direct answer: Mississippi is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the Mississippi State Department of Health's Division of Radiological Health. Work on federal installations, such as military bases, may fall under federal jurisdiction instead, so confirm the licensing route before mobilising.

For a Mississippi radiography company, the state licence sets radiation-safety training, radiographer and assistant qualification, personnel monitoring, survey instruments, source storage and transport, and field-crew rules, which follow the model of 10 CFR Part 34. The state health department also registers X-ray equipment. Radiation-safety training is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT method training, which teaches exposure technique, film and digital processing and interpretation. A field radiographer needs both. Pipeline spreads and refinery turnarounds often bring crews and sources in from neighbouring states, and reciprocity rules apply to out-of-state licensees. Check current requirements with the Division before a crew starts work.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Mississippi's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Division is also part of the Mississippi State Department of Health, under the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act. State and authorised inspectors inspect boilers and pressure vessels to ASME construction rules and National Board inspection rules. ASME Section V NDT methods, with Section I and Section VIII acceptance criteria, therefore apply in shop and field work, and repair organisations work to National Board requirements.

Pipelines. The Mississippi Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety, and PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines. Pipeline welding and NDT generally follow API 1104, and operators run their own operator-qualification programmes on top of SNT-TC-1A certification.

Codes and specifications common in Mississippi. Naval technical publications and Navy fabrication and inspection standards in shipbuilding. ABS rules for commercial vessels. ASME Section V, VIII and B31.3 in refining and LNG. ASME Section XI at Grand Gulf. AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AASHTO/AWS D1.5 for bridges. API 1104 for pipelines. Aerospace customer specifications and NAS 410 in the Columbus aerospace cluster and at Stennis, mentioned as context only, because Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Mississippi

Direct answer: Mississippi crews can take theory online, join a live-virtual cohort with a Level III instructor, or bring the training onsite to their yard, plant or site. Practical exams always use real specimens under Level III oversight. Video and simulation never replace them.

Training works best when it follows Mississippi's work rhythm. Shipyards run to construction milestones and ship deliveries, so short onsite sessions between milestones work better than week-long absences. Refinery and LNG turnarounds on the coast and at Vicksburg pull in contract technicians, who are least available during them, so theory goes in the months before. Grand Gulf refuels on a fixed cycle, and outage technicians are booked well ahead. Hurricane season on the coast runs from June to November and can disrupt schedules at short notice, so coastal employers often prefer live-virtual theory that can be rescheduled. Pipeline crews in the Pine Belt often train in wetter months when spreads slow down. Technicians in the Delta and the northeast benefit most from online theory, because a classroom week on the coast means long drives.

Onsite delivery means the instructor works at your Mississippi facility, with your equipment and procedures and, where possible, your own welds and parts as practice specimens. The specific exam can then reflect your real work. It suits companies with several technicians in a method, or companies that want training tied tightly to their written practice. Live online theory suits mixed groups and individuals. See online NDT training and corporate NDT training. When you're ready, request a cohort or onsite quote for Mississippi. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

For Mississippi employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: A Mississippi company that certifies its own NDT personnel needs a compliant written practice, a responsible Level III, and training, experience and exam records that survive an audit. Atlantis NDT writes and reviews written practices, provides Level III services, and runs corporate training for Mississippi employers.

Shipyard subcontractors, fabrication shops, inspection contractors and manufacturers in Mississippi often have a few certified technicians and no in-house Level III. Prime-contractor audits, operator audits and customer source inspections are where the gaps show: training records that don't match the practice, exams not given by a qualified Level III, expired vision tests, or a practice that doesn't cover a method the company now uses. We help close those gaps with:

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A, mapped to your customers' requirements.
  • Level III services: procedure and technique review, exam preparation and administration, and audit support. See NDT consulting in Mississippi.

  • Guidance on SNT-TC-1A certification for companies writing their first practice.

Practise before your practical exam

The environments are an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Mississippi users, the welding workshop matches shipyard and fabrication weld inspection, the oil and gas site and storage tank match refinery, LNG, terminal and pipeline work, and the aircraft hangar matches Keesler, Columbus and Meridian maintenance and the Columbus aerospace plants. See Practical NDT and the Practical NDT Mississippi page.

Your instructor

NDT training in Mississippi: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Mississippi?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Complete the classroom training it requires, build documented experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass the vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and helps employers with the rest.

Is there NDT training online in Mississippi?

Yes. Theory for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET can be taken live online from anywhere in Mississippi. Practical exams still use real specimens under Level III oversight.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Mississippi?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence from the Mississippi State Department of Health's Division of Radiological Health, because Mississippi is an NRC Agreement State. Radiographers and assistants must meet the licence's training and qualification rules.

How much does NDT training cost in Mississippi?

Training is quoted on request. The quote depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and any written-practice or exam support. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Mississippi?

Weld inspection drives demand on the coast, using VT, MT, PT, UT and RT. PAUT and RT are in demand for pipelines and refining. UT and MT matter for steel and automotive, and ET for aircraft maintenance.

Can you train our crew onsite in Pascagoula or Jackson?

Yes. Onsite training is available anywhere in Mississippi, using your equipment and procedures where possible.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted for shipyard work in Mississippi?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used as the basis for employer certification. Navy and prime-contractor work often adds requirements of its own. Check your contract's NDT qualification clauses and have your Level III map training to them.

How long does Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, the method and your experience. Classroom and experience hours are both set by the practice. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline figures.

Can I take NDT training without an employer in Mississippi?

Yes, you can take classroom training as an individual, and it counts toward the formal training requirement. Certification still needs an employer and its written practice.

Do you train pipeline NDT crews in Mississippi?

Yes. We train RT, PAUT, UT and VT technicians to SNT-TC-1A. Pipeline operators add their own operator-qualification requirements, and work generally follows API 1104.

Do you prepare candidates for the ASNT Level III exams?

Yes. We offer preparation for the Basic and method examinations. See ASNT Level III training.

What does an NDT technician earn in Mississippi?

Pay varies by method, level, sector and overtime. See the NDT salary guide for published ranges.

NDT Training and Certification in Missouri

Short answer: Missouri technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT in three ways: live online classes, a private live-virtual cohort for one company, or onsite delivery at the employer's plant, shop, terminal or power station. An ASNT NDT Level III leads each programme, the content follows your employer's written practice, and practical exams use real specimens at your own facility, so the employer that certifies you keeps full control of the record.

Missouri does not have an operating oil refinery, which surprises people coming from the Gulf Coast, but it has plenty of NDT work. St. Louis builds military aircraft and runs a large aerospace supply chain; both ends of the state assemble cars and trucks; Kansas City is one of the largest rail hubs in the country and hosts a federal national security manufacturing campus; a nuclear plant and several large coal and gas stations generate the state's power; and two great rivers carry barge traffic past terminals, fleeting yards and boat builders. Crude and refined-products pipelines cross the state on their way between the Gulf, Oklahoma and the upper Midwest. Missouri also has one regulatory quirk that matters a lot for radiographers: it is not an NRC Agreement State. This hub explains where the work is, which methods and levels Missouri employers ask for, who regulates radiography, boilers and pipelines, and how to train a crew without stopping production. To get started, request a Missouri training quote; we reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Missouri

Direct answer: Missouri NDT employment centres on five areas: the St. Louis aerospace, automotive and heavy-manufacturing region; the Kansas City manufacturing, rail and federal-industrial base; the central Missouri power and nuclear corridor; the Mississippi and Missouri river terminals and barge yards; and the southern and south-west manufacturing cities of Springfield, Joplin and Cape Girardeau. Aerospace, automotive and power work lead demand.

St. Louis and the eastern Missouri metro

St. Louis is Missouri's aerospace capital. Boeing's St. Louis-area operations build fighter, trainer and unmanned aircraft for the US military, and around them sits a supply chain of machine shops, forgings and castings suppliers, composite fabricators, heat treaters and special-process houses. Aerospace inspection here leans on penetrant testing of machined and cast parts, magnetic particle on steel components, ultrasonic inspection of composites and forgings, eddy current for surface and bolt-hole cracks, and radiography of castings and welded assemblies. Many of these employers certify personnel to NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A, which we explain below. St. Louis County and St. Charles County also carry automotive assembly at Wentzville, specialty chemical and pharmaceutical plants with stainless pressure systems, food and brewing plants, rail car and tank car repair shops, and a long list of structural and pressure vessel fabricators. Riverfront terminals in the St. Louis harbour and the Metro East add tank and dock inspection.

Kansas City, Independence and western Missouri

Kansas City spans the state line, and its Missouri side carries vehicle assembly at Claycomo, the Kansas City National Security Campus where non-nuclear components for the nation's weapons programmes are manufactured under strict quality systems, a large army ammunition plant at Independence, and heavy rail yards and car shops for several Class I railroads. Rail work brings ultrasonic and magnetic particle inspection of wheels, axles and couplers and weld inspection of car repairs. The metro also hosts engineering and inspection firms whose crews serve pipelines, power plants and fabrication shops across Missouri and Kansas. East of the city, Whiteman Air Force Base supports the B-2 bomber fleet, with aircraft maintenance inspection under military requirements.

Central Missouri: power, nuclear and the capital

The Callaway Energy Center near Fulton is Missouri's nuclear plant. Its refuelling outages bring in contractors working to ASME Section XI for ultrasonic weld examinations, eddy current of steam generator and heat exchanger tubing, and visual examinations of components and supports. Large coal and gas stations along the Missouri and Mississippi rivers, including the big plant at Labadie west of St. Louis, run boiler tube thickness surveys, header and piping weld inspection and condenser eddy current during their outages. Jefferson City adds state agencies and manufacturing, Columbia carries the University of Missouri research reactor and a growing manufacturing base, and Fort Leonard Wood and Rolla, home to the state's science and technology university, add engineering and defence activity.

The rivers: barges, terminals and boat yards

The Mississippi from Hannibal through St. Louis to Cape Girardeau and New Madrid, and the Missouri from Kansas City to St. Charles, carry grain, coal, fertiliser, petroleum and aggregates by barge. Barge building and repair yards, fleeting areas, grain and fertiliser terminals and petroleum product terminals all need weld inspection, ultrasonic thickness gauging of hull plate and tank shells, magnetic particle on lifting gear and structural welds, and visual inspection. Hull thickness surveys for barges are routine, repetitive UT work that suits newly certified Level I and II technicians.

Springfield, Joplin, Cape Girardeau and the south

South-west Missouri around Springfield and Joplin carries food processing, trucking and trailer fabrication, metal fabrication and industrial equipment plants. The south-east carries river industry at Cape Girardeau, cement plants along the Mississippi, and the lead and metals belt in the Ozarks, where mining and smelting equipment need heavy-section UT and MT. Crude-oil and refined-products pipelines running between Oklahoma, Illinois and Kansas cross Missouri, and their construction and integrity digs need API 1104 weld inspection, radiography and PAUT. Across the state, MoDOT's large inventory of steel bridges, including major Mississippi and Missouri river crossings, keeps bridge weld inspection to AWS D1.5 in demand.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Missouri employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation. Missouri demand is strongest in PT, MT, UT and ET for aerospace and automotive manufacturing, UT and ET for power and nuclear outages, and UT, MT and RT for rail, barge, pipeline and fabrication work.

Each explains what local employers need and how we deliver online or onsite at your facility in that city; other Missouri cities are covered below.

St. Louis. Missouri's largest and most varied NDT market. Aerospace suppliers want PT, MT, UT and ET under NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A depending on the customer; automotive and fabrication plants want MT, UT and VT; chemical and pharmaceutical plants want UT thickness and PT on stainless. See NDT training in St. Louis and Practical NDT in St. Louis.

Kansas City. Rail, automotive, federal manufacturing and the regional offices of inspection contractors. Rail shops need UT and MT; contractors need broad multi-method crews for pipelines and power. See NDT training in Kansas City and Practical NDT in Kansas City.

Fulton and Jefferson City. Nuclear and power outage work under ASME Section XI. Outage contractors usually hire experienced Level II technicians, so this is a destination after building UT or ET experience elsewhere.
