SNT-TC-1A certification path in Missouri, step by step

Direct answer: In Missouri, as everywhere in the US, SNT-TC-1A certification is issued by your employer, not by the state or a school. You finish the training and experience your employer's written practice requires, pass general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, pass a vision test, and the employer certifies you.

  1. Find the written practice. Your employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and recertification rules for each method and level. If your company has none, we can develop one.
  2. Complete classroom training. Finish the formal training hours for your method and level. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures, but your written practice is what counts.
  3. Build documented experience. Log supervised hours in the method. In a busy barge yard or rail shop this accumulates steadily; in an aerospace cell it may be spread across many part numbers.
  4. Pass the general and specific exams. A Level III administers the theory exam and the specific exam on your employer's procedures, specifications and equipment.
  5. Pass the practical exam. Inspect real specimens with flaws, record results, and be graded against a documented checklist.
  6. Pass the vision test. Near-vision and colour-contrast checks, usually annually.
  7. Receive employer certification. Your employer certifies you to Level I or II in that method; the certification belongs to that employer.
  8. Recertify on schedule. At the interval in your written practice, by exam or evidence of continued satisfactory work.

Read more in SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Missouri requirements

Direct answer: Missouri is not an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with sealed radioactive sources in Missouri is licensed directly by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, overseen from its Region III office in Chicago, under 10 CFR Part 34. The state handles X-ray equipment and certain other sources. Radiographers need both NRC-compliant qualification and their employer's SNT-TC-1A certification.

Because the NRC is the licensing authority, Missouri radiography companies using gamma sources such as iridium-192 work directly under the federal rules. 10 CFR Part 34 requires the licensee to have a radiation safety officer and operating and emergency procedures; requires individuals to complete radiation-safety training and work as radiographer's assistants or trainees under supervision before acting as radiographers; and requires radiographers to be certified through a certifying entity recognised under the rule, such as ASNT's industrial radiography radiation safety personnel programme or an Agreement State programme. Personnel wear dosimetry and use calibrated survey meters on every job. X-ray machines, including cabinet and vault systems used in St. Louis aerospace shops and fabrication plants, are regulated by the state through the Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services. Crews working across the river in Illinois or across the state line in Kansas fall under those states' Agreement State programmes instead, which matters for contractors based in St. Louis or Kansas City. Licensing arrangements can change, so confirm the current licensing authority and requirements with the NRC and the state before planning an RT programme.

What Atlantis NDT covers: our RT courses teach radiographic technique, exposure calculation, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance criteria for SNT-TC-1A Level I and II. Radiation-safety training and radiographer certification under the NRC rules are separate obligations your radiation safety officer manages. We help employers schedule both so they progress together.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Missouri Division of Fire Safety's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Unit oversees boiler and pressure vessel inspection in the state, with commissioned insurance company inspectors carrying out many routine inspections within the National Board framework. NDT technicians meet this through repair and alteration work under the National Board Inspection Code and ASME Sections I and VIII.

Pipelines. The Missouri Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety in partnership with PHMSA, which regulates interstate gas and hazardous liquid lines crossing the state. Pipeline weld inspection usually follows API 1104, and operator qualification rules apply to covered tasks.

Codes commonly used in Missouri. ASME Section V (NDE methods), Sections I and VIII (boilers and pressure vessels), B31.1 and B31.3 (power and process piping), API 1104 (pipeline welding), AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structural and bridge steel, AAR rules for rail cars and tank cars, ASME Section XI at Callaway, and NAS 410 for aerospace employers. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials for specific roles. Those are separate schemes; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only, and we mention them only so you understand local job postings.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Missouri

Direct answer: Missouri technicians can study theory live online, join a private live-virtual cohort for their company, or have an Atlantis Level III deliver the programme onsite at their plant, yard or station. Atlantis has no training centre in Missouri; practical exams take place at the client's facility on real specimens.

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory with attendance records, suited to individual technicians and to crews spread from Kansas City to the Bootheel. See online NDT training.
  • Private live-virtual cohort. One employer's people, scheduled around shifts and production, using your written practice, procedures and part drawings.
  • Onsite. A Level III runs the hands-on block and the practical exams at your facility, whether that is an aerospace supplier in St. Charles, a rail shop in Kansas City or a barge yard on the Mississippi. See corporate NDT training.

Timing in Missouri follows the power-plant outage calendar in spring and autumn, automotive model changeovers, aerospace production rates and the river season, when high water or low water can change barge-yard workloads quickly. We usually plan theory for quieter weeks and a protected onsite practical block. Ask about onsite training for your Missouri crew.

For Missouri employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Missouri manufacturers, rail shops, barge yards, fabricators and inspection contractors use Atlantis NDT to write or update SNT-TC-1A written practices, act as their outside Level III, administer exams and train whole teams. Aerospace primes, automotive customers and plant owners audit exactly these records.

Gaps we often see include a written practice that does not distinguish between SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 for aerospace work, procedures that cite superseded code or specification revisions, missing records of practical exam specimens, experience claimed from a previous employer without verification, and vision tests that lapsed. We review the documents, write or revise the written practice and procedures, build exam banks, and can serve as your examining Level III. For broader engineering and inspection support, see our NDT consulting services.

  • Written practice development
  • SNT-TC-1A certification guidance
  • Corporate NDT training for whole crews
  • NDT consulting for procedures, audits and Level III support

Book a Level III consultation for your Missouri company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Atlantis Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is for practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens given by your Level III.

St. Louis aerospace trainees get most from the aircraft hangar and NDT lab scenes, fabrication, rail and barge-yard trainees from the welding workshop, and pipeline and terminal trainees from the oil and gas site and storage tank scenes. See Practical NDT, with local pages for St. Louis and Kansas City. For written exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He develops the course material, aligns it with each employer's written practice and supervises examinations. On onsite programmes in Missouri he works with your Level III, or acts as the examining Level III if your company does not have one.

NDT training in Missouri: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Missouri?

Join or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its classroom training and supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Taking Level I theory first can help you get hired by Missouri fabricators, rail shops and inspection firms.

Is there NDT training online in Missouri?

Yes. Atlantis NDT teaches the theory portion live online anywhere in Missouri. The practical portion and practical exams are completed on real specimens at your employer's facility or through an arranged practical session.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Missouri?

Missouri is not an NRC Agreement State, so radiography with sealed sources is licensed by the NRC. Your employer holds the licence; you need radiation-safety training, supervised trainee or assistant experience and radiographer certification under 10 CFR Part 34, plus your SNT-TC-1A certification. X-ray equipment is regulated by the state.

How much does NDT training cost in Missouri?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on the method, the level, the group size and whether you choose online, a private cohort or onsite delivery. Request a Missouri quote and we respond within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Missouri?

Ultrasonic testing is the broadest, used in aerospace, rail, power and river work. Penetrant and magnetic particle testing are in heavy demand in the St. Louis aerospace and automotive supply chains, and eddy current in aerospace and power plants.

Can you train our crew onsite in St. Louis or Kansas City?

Yes. A Level III can deliver the hands-on block at your facility in either metro or anywhere else in Missouri, using your equipment and parts, and run the practical exams there.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted by Missouri employers?

Yes, across fabrication, rail, power, pipeline and general manufacturing. Aerospace employers in St. Louis often require NAS 410 for production inspection, and nuclear outage work follows the plant's own programme.

How long does Level II training take?

That depends on the method and your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures; supervised experience is usually the longer part.

Does Atlantis NDT have a training centre in St. Louis?

No. We do not run a physical training centre in St. Louis, Kansas City or anywhere in Missouri. Training is live online, a live-virtual cohort, or onsite at your employer's facility.

We work on both sides of the state line. Which radiography rules apply?

The rules of the state where the work takes place. Work in Missouri falls under the NRC; work in Kansas or Illinois falls under those Agreement State programmes, which may require separate licensing or reciprocity. Your radiation safety officer should confirm before each job.

Do you offer CWI or API inspector courses in Missouri?

No. Atlantis NDT training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training only. Some Missouri employers also ask for those credentials for particular roles, and you would need a specialist provider for them.

Start NDT training in Missouri

Whether you are one technician in Joplin, an aerospace supplier in St. Louis County, a rail shop in Kansas City or a barge yard on the Mississippi, the process is the same: tell us the methods, levels, headcount and preferred delivery. Request a Missouri training quote, ask about a private cohort for your Missouri team, or browse all NDT training courses. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

NDT Training and Certification in Montana

Short answer: a Montana technician or employer gets ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at the employer's own refinery, shop, mine, power plant or pipeline yard. Courses cover Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, and every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Your employer issues certification under its written practice, and we can help build that written practice as well.

Montana is a big state with a small population, and that shapes how NDT training works here. The work is real and steady: four refineries, a coal-fired power complex at Colstrip, hard-rock and platinum-group mines, the western edge of the Bakken oil field, long crude and products pipelines, federal hydroelectric dams, an Air Force missile wing and a rail network that carries a large share of the northern tier's freight. But the inspectors who do that work are spread across hundreds of miles, and few employers can send a whole crew to an out-of-state classroom for weeks. That is why the online-plus-onsite model fits Montana better than almost anywhere else. This page maps where Montana NDT work actually sits, which methods each sector needs, what the state and federal regulators expect, and how to get a quote for a single seat or an entire crew. Request a Montana NDT training quote and we reply with options within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Montana

Direct answer: Montana NDT work concentrates in six areas: the Billings and Laurel refining hub on the Yellowstone River, Great Falls (refinery, Malmstrom Air Force Base and agricultural manufacturing), the Colstrip power complex in the southeast, the Bakken counties around Sidney in the northeast, the Butte and Stillwater mining districts, and the western valleys around Missoula, Kalispell and Helena with their dams, mills and construction work.

Billings, Laurel and the Yellowstone refining corridor

Yellowstone County holds three of Montana's four refineries: Phillips 66 Billings, the Billings refinery operated by Par Pacific since it took over from ExxonMobil in 2023, and the CHS refinery in Laurel just west of the city. Together they make Billings the state's busiest NDT market by a wide margin. Turnarounds bring in UT thickness crews, PAUT and TOFD technicians for weld and corrosion work, radiographers for new piping welds, MT and PT inspectors for repairs, and VT inspectors for pressure equipment and tanks. Between turnarounds, the refineries and their mechanical contractors run continuous corrosion-monitoring programmes on process piping, heaters and storage tanks. Billings is also a regional hub for crude and products pipelines, a large rail yard and the fabrication and service shops that support oil and gas activity in eastern Montana and northern Wyoming. Most contractors here work to ASME Section V for methods, ASME Section VIII for vessels, ASME B31.3 for process piping and API 1104 for pipeline welds.

Great Falls and north-central Montana

Great Falls has the state's fourth refinery, the Calumet plant on the Missouri River, which also produces renewable fuels. Malmstrom Air Force Base, home of a Minuteman III missile wing, brings defence construction, facility maintenance and contractor inspection work. Grain handling, agricultural equipment dealers, fabrication shops and the city's power and water infrastructure add a steady base of MT, PT, UT and VT demand. Contractors working at the base often need certification records that stand up to federal prime-contractor audits.

Southeast Montana: Colstrip and the coal country

The Colstrip Steam Electric Station is one of the largest coal-fired power plants in the western United States, and the surrounding Powder River Basin mines feed it. Power plant outages are a classic NDT workload: UT thickness and ET on boiler tubes, UT and MT of high-energy piping welds, PT and VT on valves and supports, and RT of tube and pipe repair welds. Mine haul trucks, draglines and processing equipment add MT and UT on structural welds, booms and shafts.

Northeast Montana and the Bakken

Richland, Roosevelt and neighbouring counties around Sidney sit on the Montana side of the Bakken formation. Wells, gathering lines, tank batteries, compressor stations and the trucking and fabrication shops that support them generate radiography, UT shear-wave and VT work to API 1104 and ASME B31.8 and B31.4. Much of the crew demand here rises and falls with drilling activity across the border in North Dakota, so contractors value technicians who can be trained quickly when a programme ramps up.

Butte, Anaconda and the Stillwater mining district

Montana's hard-rock heritage is alive in Butte's copper and molybdenum operations and in the platinum and palladium mines of the Stillwater complex near Nye and Columbus, with smelting and processing nearby. Mining and processing equipment is heavy, highly stressed and often operated in harsh conditions, so MT and UT of welds, shafts, crusher components and hoist equipment are routine, along with VT and PT for repairs. Many of these operations have in-house maintenance teams that need a small number of certified Level II inspectors rather than a large contractor crew.

Western Montana: Missoula, Kalispell, Helena and the dams

Western Montana combines wood products and paper-mill legacy sites, aerospace and machining shops, construction, and some of the largest federal dams in the region, including Libby, Hungry Horse and, on the eastern plains, Fort Peck. Dam penstocks, gates, cranes and turbine components need periodic UT, MT and VT inspection. Bozeman and the Gallatin Valley add a growing base of precision manufacturing, optics and technology companies where PT, ET and UT on machined parts are common. Helena, as the state capital, hosts state agencies, construction and fabrication.

Rail, bridges and highways

Two major railroads cross Montana, with shops, yards and bridges along the Hi-Line, through Billings and over the mountain passes. Axle, wheel, coupler and structural weld inspection uses UT and MT. The Montana Department of Transportation manages a large bridge inventory across long distances, and steel bridge fabrication and repair are usually performed to the AASHTO/AWS D1.5 Bridge Welding Code, with UT and MT as the core methods.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Montana employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table shows each method, the levels available, how Montana employers typically use it and what a trainee needs before starting. Your employer's written practice sets the exact classroom and experience hours.

MethodLevelsWhat Montana employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepRefinery thickness surveys in Billings, Laurel and Great Falls; boiler and piping inspection at Colstrip; mining equipment welds and shafts; bridge welds to AWS D1.5Level I: none beyond employer requirements. Level II: Level I training plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepRefinery piping and vessel weld inspection, corrosion mapping during turnarounds, encoded weld scanning on new constructionUT Level II recommended before PAUT
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-wall vessel and heavy-section weld inspection in refining and power generationUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds in the Bakken and along trunk lines, refinery piping welds, boiler tube repairsRadiation safety training and NRC licence-holder requirements before handling sources; employer-specific
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepMining equipment and haul-truck frames, rail components, structural and bridge welds, refinery repairsNone beyond employer requirements
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepStainless and non-magnetic welds, valve and pump repairs, machined parts in Bozeman and Kalispell shopsNone beyond employer requirements
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld inspection on construction and pipeline projects, tank and pressure-equipment inspection, dam and penstock surveysVision test per written practice
Electromagnetic Testing (ET)I, II, III prepHeat-exchanger tubing at refineries, condenser and boiler tubing at power plants, surface crack checks on aerospace and machined partsNone beyond employer requirements

Montana employers usually need breadth more than depth. A small Billings inspection company may want the same two or three technicians certified in UT, MT and VT so they can cover refinery calls, pipeline digs and fabrication shop work in the same month. A mine maintenance department may want two people certified in MT and UT Level II and nothing else. We build those combinations around your written practice so classroom hours, exams and on-the-job experience line up across methods. Method-specific course pages include UT Level 2 training, MT Level 2 training, RT Level 2 training and phased array training. Level III candidates should start with ASNT Level III training and exam preparation.

NDT training by city in Montana

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT serves every Montana city through online and onsite delivery. Billings has dedicated NDT training, oil and gas training and simulator practice pages; other cities are served through the state programme described here. The table summarises the main NDT sectors in each city, and the paragraphs below explain what employers there typically need.

CityMain NDT sectorsPage
BillingsRefineries, pipelines, rail, fabrication, oil field serviceNDT training in Billings / Billings oil and gas training / Billings practice
LaurelRefinery, rail yardServed from this page and the Billings page
Great FallsRefinery and renewable fuels, Air Force base, agricultural equipmentServed from this page
ColstripCoal-fired power, surface miningServed from this page
SidneyBakken oil field services, gathering linesServed from this page
Butte and AnacondaCopper and molybdenum mining, processing, railServed from this page
MissoulaConstruction, wood products, regional servicesServed from this page
KalispellMachining and aerospace parts, construction, nearby damsServed from this page
Bozeman and HelenaPrecision manufacturing, construction, state infrastructureServed from this page

Billings. Billings is where most Montana NDT careers start. The three refineries in Billings and Laurel, the pipeline companies headquartered or operating out of the city, the rail yard and the fabrication shops that build skids, tanks and pressure vessels for the region all hire UT, RT, MT, PT and VT technicians. Contractors here often want a cohort trained in the weeks before a spring or fall turnaround. See the Billings NDT training page and the oil and gas NDT training in Billings page.

Great Falls. Refinery and renewable-fuels work, defence construction around Malmstrom and a solid base of agricultural equipment and fabrication shops make Great Falls a mixed market. UT and VT for the refinery, MT and UT for heavy equipment and structural welds, and PT for stainless work cover most needs.

Colstrip. Power plant outages dominate. Inspectors need UT thickness, ET and VT on boiler tubes, UT and MT on high-energy piping, and RT on repair welds, all planned tightly around outage schedules.

Sidney and the northeast. Oil field service shops and pipeline contractors need radiographers, UT shear-wave technicians and VT inspectors who understand API 1104. Demand moves with drilling activity, so quick-turn training matters.

Butte, Anaconda and the Stillwater district. Mining and processing operations need MT and UT on heavy welded structures, shafts, crushers and hoists, plus VT and PT on repairs. Many prefer to certify their own maintenance staff rather than rely on travelling contractors.

Missoula, Kalispell, Bozeman and Helena. Western Montana's mix of construction, precision manufacturing and federal dams calls for VT and UT on structural steel, PT and ET on machined parts, and UT and MT on penstocks, gates and cranes. Small shops here usually need a written practice and one or two Level II inspectors more than a large training programme.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Montana, step by step

Direct answer: under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, certification in Montana is employer-based. Your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. Montana has no separate state NDT technician licence; radiography is governed by radiation safety rules.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. Based on SNT-TC-1A, it sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks, vision requirements and recertification intervals for every method and level. If your company does not have one, we write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Take Level I and then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method and level.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience. Log supervised experience in the method at your Montana workplace, whether that is a refinery, a mine shop or a pipeline spread. Hours must be documented and verified by your employer.
  4. Pass the general exam. A closed-book written exam on the principles of the method.
  5. Pass the specific exam. Covers the procedures, codes, specifications and equipment you will actually use, for example ASME Section V, ASME B31.3, AWS D1.1 or API 1104.
  6. Pass the practical exam. A hands-on demonstration on real specimens with real flaws, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Pass the vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast checks, repeated at the interval in the written practice.
  8. Get certified by your employer. Your employer issues certification based on documented training, experience and exams. That certification belongs to that employer and does not automatically transfer if you change companies.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Recertify at the interval in your written practice, keep your vision test current, and add methods or levels as your career develops.

For more detail on how the employer-based system works, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification. The general Level 1 and Level 2 training pages explain what each level is expected to do on the job.

Radiography licensing and other Montana requirements

Direct answer: Montana is not an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources such as iridium-192 or cobalt-60 is licensed and inspected directly by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (Region IV) under 10 CFR Part 34. The state keeps authority over X-ray equipment through the Department of Public Health and Human Services. Boilers fall under the Department of Labor and Industry, and intrastate pipeline safety under the Montana Public Service Commission.

Industrial radiography

Because Montana has not signed an agreement with the NRC, a company that uses gamma sources for industrial radiography in Montana needs an NRC materials licence, or, if it is based in an Agreement State, it files for reciprocity with the NRC before working here. The federal rules in 10 CFR Part 34 set the requirements for radiographers and radiographer's assistants: radiation safety training, a radiation safety examination, a supervised period as an assistant, recognised radiographer certification, personal dosimetry, and the two-person rule at temporary job sites. Industrial X-ray equipment is a state matter, so companies using X-ray tubes for radiography should confirm current registration requirements with the Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services. RT method training under SNT-TC-1A, which is what Atlantis provides, covers film and digital technique, exposure calculation, image quality and interpretation; it sits alongside, not instead of, the radiation safety training required by the licence holder and the NRC. Always confirm current licensing requirements with the NRC and the state before deploying a crew.

Boilers and pressure vessels

Montana's boiler inspection programme sits within the Building Codes Program of the Department of Labor and Industry's Business Standards Division. Boilers outside small residential buildings need periodic safety inspection and an operating certificate. Repairs and alterations to boilers and pressure vessels are generally performed to the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board inspection rules, which means the NDT on that work is performed to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme. That is one reason Montana R-stamp holders and fabrication shops care about a clean, auditable written practice.

Pipelines

Interstate pipelines crossing Montana are regulated by the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA). Intrastate natural gas pipeline safety is overseen by the Montana Public Service Commission's pipeline safety programme, which enforces the federal rules for intrastate operators. Pipeline welding inspection commonly follows API 1104, with ASME B31.8 for gas and B31.4 for liquid lines, and operators expect radiographers and UT technicians qualified to their procedures.

Codes Montana employers commonly use

  • ASME Section V (NDT methods), Section VIII (pressure vessels) and B31.3 (process piping) in the Billings, Laurel and Great Falls refineries
  • ASME Section I and B31.1 for boilers and power piping at Colstrip and other generating plants
  • API 1104, ASME B31.4 and B31.8 for Bakken gathering lines and trunk pipelines
  • API 650 and API 653 context for storage tanks at refineries and terminals (Atlantis trains the NDT methods, not the API inspector certification)
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for bridge fabrication and repair
  • Mine operators' own procedures and equipment manufacturers' specifications for heavy mobile equipment

Some Montana employers also ask for API inspector or CWI credentials for particular roles. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train; our programmes focus on ASNT SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Montana

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Montana. Theory is delivered through live online or live-virtual classes, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility, using your equipment and specimens under ASNT Level III oversight. For a state where the drive between work sites can take most of a day, that model saves both travel and lost shifts.

For individual technicians, online NDT training covers the classroom portion of Level I and Level II. You attend live sessions with a Level III instructor, ask questions in real time, and work through method principles, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation from Billings, Sidney, Butte or anywhere with a reliable connection. Practical hours and the practical exam are then completed with your employer or at an employer-arranged facility.

For Montana employers training a group, onsite delivery is usually the most efficient option. We schedule classroom and practical sessions at your refinery training room, shop or mine maintenance building, use your own instruments, reference standards and part samples, and build the course around the procedures your crew actually follows. A Billings refinery contractor gets UT and PAUT on piping mock-ups; a Butte mine maintenance team gets MT and UT on the welded structures it repairs; a Great Falls fabricator gets VT and MT tied to its welding procedures.

Montana's calendar shapes scheduling. Refinery turnarounds in Billings, Laurel and Great Falls cluster in spring and fall; power plant outages follow each unit's maintenance plan; pipeline construction and bridge work are concentrated in the warmer months when ground and weather allow; and winter is often the quietest field season, which makes it the best time for classroom training. We plan cohorts to finish before the busy window so certified technicians are ready when the work starts. Larger programmes run through corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Montana crew.

For Montana employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A puts responsibility for certification on the employer, so every Montana NDT employer needs a written practice and access to a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams and provides Level III services for companies that do not have a Level III in-house.

Most Montana NDT employers are small: a three-person inspection company in Billings, a fabrication shop in Great Falls, a mine maintenance department in Butte, a machine shop in Kalispell. They need certified technicians but cannot justify a full-time Level III, and the nearest one may be several hundred miles away. That gap is where most audit findings come from: training records without hour counts, practical exams with no graded checklist, out-of-date vision tests, or a written practice copied from another company that does not match how the work is actually done.

We help with:

  • Written practice development and revision aligned with the current edition of SNT-TC-1A and your customers' requirements. See written practice development.
  • Exam administration: general, specific and practical exams prepared and graded under Level III oversight, with records your auditors can follow.
  • Procedure review for UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET procedures against ASME, AWS and API requirements.
  • Audit preparation for customer audits, National Board or ASME reviews and ISO 9001 surveillance.
  • Corporate programmes for multi-site companies, through corporate NDT training.

For broader Level III consulting across the state, see NDT consulting in Montana and our guide to SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Montana company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT simulator lets Montana trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before their practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique, scanning patterns and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank environment. For Montana that mix is useful: the oil and gas site for refinery and Bakken work, the storage tank for refinery and terminal tank farms, the welding workshop for fabrication, mining equipment repair and bridge steel, and the hangar for aerospace and machining shops. For a technician who lives two hundred miles from the nearest training specimen set, being able to repeat scans and explore indication types at home before the practical exam is a real advantage. There is also a Billings Practical NDT page. For written-exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Direct answer: Montana programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop leads course design, delivers Level III-led instruction, and oversees the exams and records that make certification defensible under SNT-TC-1A. His focus is practical: connecting method theory to the procedures, codes and equipment your Montana crew actually works with, and helping employers build written practices that hold up in audits. Ask about his availability for your programme when you contact us about Montana training.

NDT training in Montana: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Montana?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. Complete Level I and Level II classroom training in a method, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then issues certification under its written practice. If you are not yet employed, online classroom training prepares you, and certification follows once an employer documents your experience.

Is there NDT training online in Montana?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online and live-virtual Level I and Level II classes that Montana technicians can join from anywhere in the state. Practical training and the practical exam are completed onsite with your employer because they need real equipment and real specimens.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Montana?

Montana is not an Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the NRC under 10 CFR Part 34. The company holds the licence; individual radiographers and assistants must meet the federal training, examination, supervision and certification requirements. X-ray equipment is regulated by the state. Confirm current requirements with the NRC and the Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services before starting work.

How much does NDT training cost in Montana?

Cost is quoted on request. It depends on the method and level, the number of trainees, whether classroom sessions are online or onsite, the travel involved for onsite practical sessions, and whether you need exam administration or written practice support. Send your requirements and we return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Montana?

UT is the broadest, used across refining, power, mining, bridges and pipelines. RT stays in demand on pipeline and refinery welds, MT is essential in mining and heavy equipment, and PAUT is growing in refinery inspection. Many Montana technicians hold UT, MT and VT together.

Can you train our crew onsite in Billings, Great Falls or Butte?

Yes. We deliver classroom and practical sessions at your facility anywhere in Montana, using your equipment and specimens, and schedule around turnarounds, outages and the construction season.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Montana employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer certification in US industry, including the refineries, pipeline operators, power plants and fabrication shops that hire most Montana inspectors. Some customers add their own requirements, which your written practice can document.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums; see the training requirements matrix. Logging the experience hours usually takes much longer than the classroom training itself.

Can I become a Level III in Montana?

Yes. Level III candidates typically hold Level II experience in their methods and then sit the ASNT Level III examinations. Our Level III training covers preparation for the basic and method exams, delivered online so Montana candidates do not need to travel.

Do you have an NDT school in Montana I can attend in person?

No. Atlantis NDT does not operate a physical school or campus in Montana. Classroom training is live online or delivered onsite at your employer's facility, which is often the more practical option given the distances involved.

What NDT jobs are there in Montana?

Refinery inspection in Billings, Laurel and Great Falls, power plant outage work at Colstrip, pipeline and oil field inspection in the northeast, mining equipment inspection in Butte and the Stillwater district, and fabrication and bridge work statewide. For pay context, see the NDT salary guide.

Can a Wyoming or North Dakota company use the same programme for its Montana crew?

Yes. Because SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based, one written practice can cover technicians working across several states. Radiography licensing still follows each state's rules, so plan RT reciprocity separately.

Get a quote for NDT training in Montana

Whether you need one technician trained in UT Level II, a refinery contractor cohort ready before turnaround season, or a written practice and Level III support for a small Montana shop, Atlantis NDT can put together a programme around your work and your schedule. Request your Montana training quote, read more about Atlantis NDT training, or tell us about your crew's methods and dates. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

Short answer: New Brunswick technicians and employers can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, plus ASNT Level III exam preparation. Theory runs live online or as a private live-virtual cohort, and practical sessions happen onsite at your shop, plant or yard with an ASNT NDT Level III. Your employer certifies you under its own written practice once you have the training, experience and exams.

New Brunswick is the province where Canada's industrial NDT world and the US market sit closest together. Saint John has Canada's largest oil refinery, and much of its gasoline and diesel goes to the northeastern United States. An LNG terminal, a natural gas pipeline to New England and a busy port all point south, and Maine is a short drive from Saint John, Fredericton or Edmundston. That makes SNT-TC-1A more relevant here than in most of Atlantic Canada. But we still need to be clear: Canada's national NDT certification scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, and most New Brunswick code work and nuclear work asks for it. Atlantis NDT does not train toward CGSB certification and claims no CGSB recognition. This page explains when SNT-TC-1A is the right tool in New Brunswick, maps where the inspection work is, and shows how to get a quote. Request a New Brunswick NDT training quote and expect options within one business day.

SNT-TC-1A or CGSB in New Brunswick: an honest fit check

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A fits New Brunswick employers and technicians who build to US codes, supply US customers, run cross-border crews into Maine and New England, or plan to work in the US. Nuclear work at Point Lepreau, most Canadian code work and most inspection-company contracts call for CAN/CGSB-48.9712 instead, and our training does not lead to that certificate.

The fit check below is the conversation we have with most New Brunswick callers. It is worth doing before anyone books a course, because the wrong certification costs time on a job site where the client has already decided what it will accept.

Because arrangements are still changing, confirm the current certification body before you plan a CGSB route. Holding both a CGSB certificate and an employer SNT-TC-1A certification is common among cross-border technicians, and the two can be planned together.

Where NDT technicians work in New Brunswick

Direct answer: New Brunswick's NDT work is concentrated in Saint John's refinery, LNG, port and power complex; at the Point Lepreau nuclear station on the Bay of Fundy; in the pulp and paper mills spread across the province; in the hydro and thermal plants of NB Power; at the Belledune port and generating station in the north; and in the manufacturing and logistics base of Moncton and Fredericton.

Saint John: refining, LNG and the port

Saint John's east side holds Irving Oil's refinery, the largest in Canada at roughly 320,000 barrels per day. The refinery runs a major fall 2026 turnaround that includes an overhaul of its residue fluid catalytic cracking unit, the first since that unit was commissioned. Turnarounds on this scale draw in large numbers of UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT and ET technicians for thickness surveys, corrosion mapping, repair-weld examination and exchanger tube inspection. Nearby, the Canaport LNG terminal and the marine crude terminal add tank, piping and cryogenic-service inspection, and a dedicated natural gas pipeline runs from the LNG terminal to the US border. The Port of Saint John, its container and bulk terminals, the Coleson Cove generating station and a large pulp and paper mill at Reversing Falls round out the city's industrial map. See NDT training in Saint John, Saint John simulator practice and NDT ERP for Saint John.

Point Lepreau and the Bay of Fundy

NB Power's Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station, a CANDU 6 reactor west of Saint John, is the only nuclear power plant in Atlantic Canada. Nuclear in-service inspection follows CSA N285-series standards and the licensee's quality programme under CNSC oversight, and personnel are certified under Canadian schemes. It is a major NDT employer during outages, but it is not a market for our SNT-TC-1A training. We mention it so nobody is misled.

Pulp, paper and forestry across the province

Forestry is New Brunswick's oldest heavy industry. Pulp and paper mills in Saint John, Nackawic, Edmundston, Atholville and elsewhere run recovery boilers, digesters, bleach plants and paper machines with demanding inspection needs: UT thickness on boiler tubes and digester shells, MT and PT on welds and rotating equipment, and ET on heat exchangers. Many mills sell into US markets and some have US ownership or customers that audit their programmes.

NB Power and the north shore

Beyond Point Lepreau and Coleson Cove, NB Power operates the Belledune coal-fired station on the north shore and the Mactaquac hydro dam on the Saint John River above Fredericton, which is going through a long life-extension programme. The Port of Belledune is a heavy-cargo and project-cargo port. Hydro and thermal outages drive boiler, piping, turbine and structural inspection.

Moncton, Fredericton and the south-east

Moncton is the province's logistics and distribution centre, with manufacturing, metal fabrication, trailer and equipment builders, and an international airport with aircraft maintenance. Fredericton holds government, engineering and technology firms, and the nearby base at Gagetown is one of the largest military training areas in Canada. Fabricators across the south-east increasingly ship to US customers, which is where SNT-TC-1A demand appears.

Pipelines and cross-border energy

The natural gas transmission line that crosses New Brunswick from Nova Scotia to New England, the LNG terminal's export lateral and the refinery's product flows to the US Northeast make New Brunswick an energy gateway. Pipeline, compressor and terminal maintenance uses RT, UT and MT, often under specifications written with US owners and markets in mind.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in New Brunswick, step by step

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after you complete classroom training and documented experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. It is an employer certification, not a Canadian national certificate.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A-based written practice that sets training, experience, examination and recertification rules. We can help: written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete the hours your written practice requires, online or onsite. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience. Log supervised hours on real work such as refinery piping, mill equipment or fabrication.
  4. Examinations. Pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III.
  5. Vision. Pass near-vision and colour contrast checks, typically every year.
  6. Certification. Your employer certifies you for the method and level.
  7. Recertification. Renew at the interval your written practice sets. If you change employers, the new employer recertifies you under its own written practice.

If you also plan to hold CGSB certification, keep detailed experience records from day one so both schemes can be satisfied.

Radiography licensing and other New Brunswick requirements

Direct answer: industrial gamma radiography in New Brunswick is licensed federally by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission; operators must be certified exposure device operators or trainees under their direct supervision. Boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping are regulated by the province's Technical Inspection Services. Interprovincial and international pipelines fall under the Canada Energy Regulator.

Industrial radiography

Canada has no US-style Agreement State system; the CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices nationwide, and it also licenses Point Lepreau. Only a certified exposure device operator (EDO), or a trainee under the direct supervision and continuous observation of a certified EDO, may operate an exposure device. The CNSC's REGDOC-2.2.3 and the CSA PCP-09 guide set out the vocational training, supervised on-the-job training and examination requirements. Atlantis RT training covers radiographic principles, technique, interpretation and acceptance criteria. It does not replace EDO certification, and we do not run CNSC examinations. X-ray equipment falls under provincial rules; confirm current registration and worker requirements with your radiation safety officer.

Boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping

New Brunswick regulates boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping systems under the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act through Technical Inspection Services in the Department of Justice and Public Safety. Companies that manufacture or install this equipment must register a quality assurance or quality control plan, newly installed or modified equipment must be inspected before service, and in-service equipment is inspected periodically. Design registration and welding procedure registration also apply. Commonly referenced codes include CSA B51, ASME Sections I, V and VIII, and ASME B31.1 and B31.3. Whether SNT-TC-1A personnel are acceptable depends on the code, the owner and the contractor's registered quality programme.

Pipelines and nuclear

The natural gas lines that cross New Brunswick into the US are regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator, with CSA Z662 as the core standard; API 1104 appears where US owners or contractors are involved. Nuclear in-service inspection at Point Lepreau follows CSA N285-series requirements and the licensee's programme under CNSC licence.

Other things New Brunswick employers ask for

Refinery, terminal and mill access usually involves safety prequalification, orientation and the owner's contractor-management requirements. Structural steel is fabricated by CWB-certified companies to CSA W59, normally with CGSB-certified NDT staff. Our training sits beside these requirements, not in place of them.

Atlantis provides all three, remotely or onsite, and helps companies keep SNT-TC-1A and CGSB records separate and clear.

Typical New Brunswick requests include a Saint John fabricator taking on ASME work for a New England customer, a turnaround contractor whose crews also work Maine and Massachusetts refineries, terminals and mills, and a Moncton manufacturer whose US buyer audits weld inspection. We can:

  • write or revise your SNT-TC-1A written practice (written practice development);

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator lets New Brunswick trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments from a browser. It is practice only. It does not replace the hands-on practical exam required by your written practice or by a CGSB scheme.

The oil and gas site and storage tank environments map directly onto Saint John's refinery and terminal work, and the welding workshop suits fabricators across the province. Trainees can practise probe handling, scan coverage and indication recognition before a turnaround, and supervisors can check readiness before booking practical exam time. See Practical NDT or Practical NDT in Saint John, and try the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop writes the course material, examinations and employer written practices, and he is the Level III you talk to when deciding whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or both make sense for your New Brunswick work.

NDT training in New Brunswick: frequently asked questions

How do I get NDT certified in New Brunswick?

For most Canadian work, including nuclear and provincial code work, you need CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification from an accredited certification body; confirm the current certification body, since arrangements changed in 2026. For US-code work, US customers or US employers, you are certified by your employer under SNT-TC-1A, which is the route Atlantis trains for.

Can I take NDT training online in New Brunswick?

Yes. Live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes are open to technicians in Saint John, Moncton, Fredericton and anywhere else in the province. Practical training and exams use real specimens, usually at the employer's site. See NDT training online.

Can I work at Point Lepreau with SNT-TC-1A certification?

Generally no. Nuclear inspection in Canada follows CSA N285-series requirements and the licensee's programme, with Canadian personnel certification. Ask the licensee or its contractor what it requires.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB training in New Brunswick?

No. We teach SNT-TC-1A only and claim no CGSB recognition.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in New Brunswick?

For gamma radiography, yes. You must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator or a trainee under direct supervision, and the employer must hold a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment falls under provincial rules.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in New Brunswick?

Technical Inspection Services in the Department of Justice and Public Safety, under the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act. Manufacturers and installers must register a quality plan.

How much does NDT training cost in New Brunswick?

It is quoted on request, based on method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery, and any written practice or Level III work. Cohort and onsite quotes usually come back within one business day. Get a New Brunswick training quote.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in New Brunswick?

UT and PAUT dominate refinery and mill work, with ET on exchangers, RT on piping and pipeline welds, and MT and PT on rotating equipment and structures.

Can you train our turnaround crew before the Saint John shutdown?

Yes. A common plan is online theory in the weeks before the turnaround and a short onsite practical block at your shop or yard, scheduled around mobilisation dates and the owner's access rules.

Can my crew use SNT-TC-1A in Maine and New England?

US employers and owners generally work to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 employer certification, so an SNT-TC-1A programme suits that work. The certification belongs to the employer, so its written practice must cover the US jobs.

How long does UT Level II take?

Your employer's written practice sets classroom and experience hours, using SNT-TC-1A recommendations as a baseline; see the training requirements matrix. Experience takes far longer than classroom time.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from New Brunswick?

Yes. Our Level III preparation runs online. For pay context by method and level, see the NDT salary guide; we do not publish our own salary figures.

NDT Training and Certification in New Jersey

New Jersey technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, in scheduled live-virtual cohorts, or onsite at their own refinery, plant, shop or terminal. Every course is led by an ASNT NDT Level III and built around the employer's written practice, so the hours count toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

New Jersey packs a remarkable amount of inspection work into a small state. Two large refineries, the busiest container port on the East Coast, three nuclear reactors on one island in the Delaware, a dense web of gas transmission and distribution lines, pharmaceutical plants full of stainless process piping, military research and munitions installations, and some of the most heavily travelled bridges in the country all need qualified NDT people. This page maps that work region by region and explains how certification, radiography licensing and pressure-equipment rules work in New Jersey. To start straight away, request a New Jersey training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in New Jersey

New Jersey NDT work concentrates in the northern port-and-refinery corridor (Newark, Elizabeth, Linden, Bayonne, Perth Amboy), the central pharmaceutical and manufacturing belt along Route 1 and the Turnpike, the South Jersey Delaware River industrial strip (Camden, Paulsboro, Salem County), and statewide gas, bridge and military infrastructure.

North Jersey: Newark, Elizabeth, Linden and the Kill Van Kull

Port Newark-Elizabeth Marine Terminal, the Bayonne and Elizabeth terminals and the tank farms along the Arthur Kill form one of the densest petroleum and cargo logistics zones in the country. The Phillips 66 Bayway refinery in Linden anchors the area, surrounded by product terminals in Linden, Carteret, Sewaren and Perth Amboy. Typical work: UT thickness and corrosion mapping on piping and tanks, VT and MT on structural and crane welds, RT and PAUT on process piping during turnarounds, and storage-tank inspection where the NDT technician supports the owner's certified tank inspector. Newark Liberty International Airport adds aviation maintenance work, mainly ET, PT and VT.

Central Jersey: pharma, manufacturing and power

From New Brunswick and Edison down through Princeton and the Route 1 corridor, pharmaceutical and specialty chemical manufacturing relies on stainless-steel process systems: orbital welds, sanitary tubing, reactors and pressure vessels. VT and PT dominate, with RT and UT on higher-pressure lines, and documentation discipline is as important as the method. The region also has gas-fired generating stations, fabrication shops and machine shops that serve the New York metro market.

South Jersey and the Delaware River

PBF Energy's Paulsboro refinery, the Paulsboro and Gibbstown marine terminals, chemical plants in Gloucester and Salem counties and the Camden waterfront form South Jersey's industrial strip. Further south on Artificial Island, PSEG operates the Salem and Hope Creek nuclear stations, which bring refuelling outage work under ASME Section XI. Camden is home to Holtec's manufacturing campus, which fabricates heavy nuclear components and spent-fuel storage systems, a demanding environment for UT, RT, MT, PT and VT on thick welds. In Ocean County, the former Oyster Creek station is being decommissioned.

Military and research installations

Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst supports airlift and naval air engineering work, Picatinny Arsenal in Morris County develops armaments and munitions, and Naval Weapons Station Earle in Monmouth County handles ordnance logistics. Contractors supporting these sites often need technicians certified under an SNT-TC-1A written practice and familiar with defence documentation.

Bridges, transit and utilities

The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, the Delaware River Port Authority, the New Jersey Turnpike Authority and NJDOT all maintain long-span steel bridges, viaducts and tunnels that need fracture-critical inspection support with UT, MT and VT. Gas utilities and interstate transmission operators run pipelines across the state, with constant replacement and integrity work. Offshore-wind supply-chain projects on the Delaware River and the coast have also brought heavy fabrication work, although that pipeline of projects has changed with federal policy, so treat it as variable demand.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in New Jersey, step by step

New Jersey does not issue NDT certificates. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after you complete method training, document on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III and pass a vision test. The steps:

  1. Written practice. Your employer's written practice defines levels, training, experience, exams and recertification for each method. It must exist before anyone is certified.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the method training hours required, live online, live-virtual or onsite. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised, documented work in the method, for example UT thickness readings at a Bayonne terminal or PT on pharma tubing in Central Jersey.
  4. General exam on method principles.
  5. Specific exam on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, such as ASME Section V, ASME B31.3 or AWS D1.5 for bridges.
  6. Practical exam on real specimens, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour contrast, annually.
  8. Certification by the employer, documented and filed.
  9. Recertification at the interval the written practice sets.

Because certification is employer-based, a technician who moves from a Linden contractor to a Camden fabricator is re-certified by the new employer, using the documented training and experience already earned. More detail on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Radiography licensing and other New Jersey requirements

New Jersey is an NRC Agreement State. The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection's Radiation Protection Element licenses industrial radiography with radioactive sources, and its Bureau of X-Ray Compliance registers and inspects industrial x-ray equipment. Radiographers must meet state radiation safety training and certification rules on top of SNT-TC-1A method certification.

New Jersey's radiation rules for industrial radiography follow the federal model in 10 CFR Part 34: a licensed company, a radiation safety officer, trained and certified radiographers, supervised radiographer's assistants, personnel monitoring, and survey and leak-test requirements. Industrial x-ray machines, including cabinet and field units, are registered with the Bureau of X-Ray Compliance. Companies licensed in another state that send crews into New Jersey normally need reciprocity approval before starting work. Because the state's rule details can change, confirm the current licensing and radiographer requirements directly with NJDEP before work begins.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development's bureau for boiler and pressure vessel compliance, which dates back to 1913, inspects and certifies boilers, pressure vessels and refrigeration systems under the state's Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Refrigeration Law. Inspectors hold National Board commissions, and repairs and alterations follow the National Board Inspection Code, with NDT requirements drawn from ASME Section V and the construction code.

Pipelines. The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety, and PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines. Weld inspection on transmission work usually follows API 1104, and operator qualification rules cover many tasks performed on regulated lines.

Codes in local use (context only). ASME Section V and VIII, ASME B31.1 and B31.3, API 1104, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for bridges, ASME Section XI and plant-specific programmes at Salem and Hope Creek, and ASME BPE practice in pharmaceutical plants. Refinery owners and terminals also follow API inspection codes, and some local employers ask for API inspector or AWS CWI credentials for supervisory roles. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train for; our training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT method training.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across New Jersey

New Jersey technicians can take NDT theory live online, join a live-virtual cohort, or have a Level III-led course delivered onsite at the employer's facility. Practical training and practical exams are done on real specimens at the employer's site or another arrangement agreed in advance.

New Jersey's traffic makes online theory especially practical. A technician in Bayonne should not spend two hours on the Turnpike each way for classroom sessions that can be delivered interactively online. Our online NDT training uses live instruction with a Level III, not just recorded videos, and covers the knowledge that the general and specific exams test.

Onsite courses make sense for refineries, terminals, fabricators and pharma plants that want a group trained on their own equipment, procedures and parts. We time onsite programmes around the calendar that drives New Jersey work: spring and fall refinery turnarounds in Linden and Paulsboro, refuelling outages at Salem and Hope Creek, pharma plant shutdown weeks, and the summer construction season for bridges and gas main replacement. For companies with crews in several states, corporate NDT training keeps records consistent across sites. Ask about onsite training for your New Jersey crew.

For New Jersey employers: written practice and Level III services

Any New Jersey company that certifies NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and Level III oversight. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, administers and grades exams, reviews procedures and acts as an outside Level III for companies without one in-house.

New Jersey has many small and mid-size NDT employers: inspection contractors serving the refinery corridor, fabricators supplying New York construction, and manufacturers whose customers suddenly require certified inspectors. These firms often lose their Level III to retirement or competition, or find during an audit that their written practice no longer matches what they do. Our written practice development service fixes that, and the SNT-TC-1A certification guide explains what auditors and customers check.

Level III services include procedure and technique writing, exam administration and grading, record review, and audit preparation for owner-user, prime-contractor and registrar audits. For wider programme work see NDT consulting in New Jersey. Book a Level III consultation for your New Jersey company.

Practise before your practical exam

Practical NDT, Atlantis NDT's 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is practice only. It does not replace the practical exam on real specimens or count as on-the-job experience.

New Jersey trainees will recognise the scenes. The storage tank and oil and gas site match the tank farms and refineries of Linden, Bayonne and Paulsboro. The welding workshop matches the fabrication shops of Camden and North Jersey. The aircraft hangar matches maintenance work at Newark and the joint base. Practising scan patterns and set-ups in the simulator between classes means trainees walk into the practical exam knowing what to expect. See the Practical NDT simulator and the Newark and Trenton pages.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As the Level III behind the programme, he sets course content, written practices, exam questions and practical grading criteria, so what a New Jersey technician learns lines up with how that technician is examined and certified. Questions about a method, a code requirement or your written practice can be sent through the contact form.

NDT training in New Jersey: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in New Jersey?

Most New Jersey NDT technicians are certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. You take classroom training in a method, log documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis NDT provides the training and exam support, and can write the employer's written practice.

Is there NDT training online in New Jersey?

Yes. Atlantis NDT delivers live online NDT theory that New Jersey technicians can join from anywhere in the state. Hands-on practical training and the practical exam still need real specimens, arranged onsite at your employer or through an agreed arrangement.

Do I need a license to do radiography in New Jersey?

Your company needs an NJDEP radioactive materials licence for source radiography, or registration of its x-ray equipment with the Bureau of X-Ray Compliance. Individual radiographers must meet state radiation safety training and certification rules, and assistants work under supervision. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT method certification. Confirm current requirements with NJDEP.

How much does NDT training cost in New Jersey?

Quote on request. Cost depends on method, level, number of trainees, online versus onsite delivery, and whether you also need written-practice or exam services. Send your crew size and methods and you will receive a quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in New Jersey?

UT is the most widely used, from refinery corrosion surveys to bridge welds. VT and PT are essential in pharmaceutical and chemical plants, RT and PAUT in refinery turnarounds and heavy fabrication, and MT on bridges and structural steel.

Can you train our crew onsite in Linden, Camden or Newark?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your facility anywhere in New Jersey is available, scheduled around turnarounds, outages and production. Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in New Jersey; onsite means at your site.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by New Jersey employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the main employer-based NDT certification framework in the US and is referenced by ASME and AWS codes used across New Jersey industry. Nuclear and aerospace customers may add extra requirements that your written practice should cover.

How long does it take to reach Level II in New Jersey?

It depends on your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training hours and experience by method and level, listed on our training requirements matrix. Experience usually takes longer than classroom training.

Can I work in New York or Pennsylvania with a New Jersey employer's certification?

Yes, SNT-TC-1A certification is not tied to a state, so you can work wherever your employer sends you. Radiography is the exception: radiation licensing and reciprocity rules apply state by state.

Do I need prior experience to start NDT training in New Jersey?

No experience is needed for Level I. Level II requires Level I training and documented experience, as set by the written practice. Many New Jersey technicians start as helpers or radiographer's assistants and train up from there.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from New Jersey?

Yes. Our ASNT Level III training runs live online. For Level II candidates, practice material such as the UT Level 2 practice questions helps with exam readiness.

What do NDT technicians earn in New Jersey?

Pay depends on method, level, sector, travel and overtime. Our NDT Level 2 salary and NDT inspector salary guides cover published ranges.

Start NDT training in New Jersey

Whether you are a technician in Elizabeth working toward UT Level II, a Paulsboro contractor preparing a crew for the next turnaround, a Camden fabricator tightening its written practice, or a pharma plant that needs certified VT and PT inspectors, Atlantis NDT builds training around your work. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Request your New Jersey NDT training quote, tell us your crew size and methods, or explore the full training catalogue and the NDT training in the USA hub.
