contentHtml:
HomeTrainingConsultingERPPractical NDTContact

NDT Training and Certification in Newfoundland and Labrador

Short answer: technicians and employers in Newfoundland and Labrador can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, plus ASNT Level III exam preparation. Because so much of the province's work is offshore, in Labrador or on rotation, theory runs live online or as a private live-virtual cohort, and practical sessions take place onsite at your shop, fabrication yard or plant, led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Your employer certifies you under its written practice.

Newfoundland and Labrador needs the most candid version of this page. The province's biggest NDT employers are offshore oil production, fabrication yards that build for offshore projects, a nickel processing plant, iron ore mines in Labrador, and large hydro and thermal power assets. Offshore operators, their contractors and most Canadian code work generally certify NDT personnel under CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, or under other ISO 9712-based schemes. Atlantis NDT does not train toward CGSB or any ISO 9712 scheme and claims no CGSB recognition. Our SNT-TC-1A training suits a smaller group here: shops building equipment to US codes for US customers, contractors whose crews rotate to US work, employers supplying US-owned projects that name SNT-TC-1A, and Newfoundlanders and Labradorians who plan to work in the US Gulf Coast, Alaska or elsewhere in the US. This page explains that fit, maps the work from the Avalon to Labrador West, and shows how to get a quote. Request a Newfoundland and Labrador training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Is SNT-TC-1A the right certification for your work in Newfoundland and Labrador?

Direct answer: only for some work. Offshore production, provincial code work, mining and utility work in Newfoundland and Labrador usually ask for CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or another ISO 9712-based certification. SNT-TC-1A fits US-code fabrication, US customers and US-based employment. Check the operator or client specification before you book any course.

Many Newfoundland and Labrador technicians have spent part of their careers in Alberta, on US Gulf Coast turnarounds or overseas, so mixed certification histories are normal here. The table shows where SNT-TC-1A training helps and where it does not.

Your situation in Newfoundland and LabradorScheme usually expectedDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
Inspection on offshore production installations, FPSOs or gravity-based platformsThe operator's specification, generally CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or another ISO 9712-based schemeRarely. Confirm with the operator or prime contractor
Construction or in-service NDE on provincially registered boilers and pressure vesselsCAN/CGSB-48.9712 through a Canadian inspection organisationUsually no. Check the owner specification and provincial requirements
Mining and processing work at Voisey's Bay, Long Harbour or Labrador WestThe owner's specification, typically CGSBRarely. Ask the owner first
St. John's or Marystown shop fabricating ASME pressure equipment, skids or AWS D1.1 structures for a US customerSNT-TC-1A per ASME Section V or the client specificationYes. The core use case
Contractor that sends crews to US refinery, petrochemical or pipeline workSNT-TC-1A or CP-189 employer certification on the US sideYes, for the US work
Technician planning to move to US Gulf Coast or Alaska workSNT-TC-1A or CP-189 through the US employerYes. Your training record moves with you

About the CGSB side: the Canadian General Standards Board, which published CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Natural Resources Canada and the CWB Group have said the standard remains valid for its current cycle and existing certifications are not affected, and NRCan's NDT Certification Body continues to operate. Because the arrangements are still settling, confirm the current certification body before planning a CGSB route. Holding a CGSB certificate and an employer SNT-TC-1A certification side by side is common and workable.

Where NDT technicians work in Newfoundland and Labrador

Direct answer: NDT work in Newfoundland and Labrador centres on the Grand Banks offshore oil fields and the St. John's supply base; on the fabrication yards at Bull Arm, Marystown and Argentia; on the Placentia Bay industrial corridor, including the Come By Chance refinery and the Long Harbour nickel plant; on the iron ore mines of Labrador West and the Voisey's Bay nickel mine; and on large hydro and thermal power assets.

The Grand Banks offshore

About 300 to 350 kilometres east of St. John's, the Jeanne d'Arc Basin holds the province's producing oil fields: Hibernia and Hebron, both produced from gravity-based structures, and Terra Nova and White Rose, both produced through floating production, storage and offloading vessels. These installations need constant integrity work: UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT and TOFD on critical welds, MT on structural nodes and lifting gear, ET on heat exchangers and PT on topsides components. Work is done on rotation, and most of the planning, procedure work and onshore inspection happens in St. John's. Further out, the Bay du Nord discovery in the Flemish Pass is in front-end engineering, with its operator, now the sole owner, targeting a final investment decision in early 2027. If it goes ahead, it would add another FPSO and a long fabrication and integrity programme.

St. John's and the Avalon Peninsula

St. John's is the operations and supply base for the offshore industry and home to the province's engineering firms, inspection companies, ship repair yards and machine shops. Offshore supply vessels, fishing and research vessels, and the harbour's dockyard generate marine NDT work. Mount Pearl and Donovans industrial park hold fabrication shops and service companies. The Holyrood thermal generating station on Conception Bay adds boiler and high-energy piping inspection. See Practical NDT simulator practice in St. John's.

Placentia Bay and Trinity Bay: fabrication and processing

The Bull Arm Fabrication Site on Trinity Bay built the Hibernia and Hebron gravity-based structures and topsides and remains the province's largest fabrication site. Marystown on the Burin Peninsula has a shipyard and fabrication facility with offshore module experience, and Argentia is a deep-water port and marshalling area. On Placentia Bay, the Come By Chance refinery has been converted to a renewable diesel plant and is now in commercial operation, with plans for expansion, and Vale's Long Harbour processing plant refines nickel concentrate from Voisey's Bay. Both are pressure-equipment-heavy plants with turnarounds and shutdowns that need UT, PAUT, RT, ET, MT and PT.

Labrador: iron ore, nickel and hydro

Labrador West, around Labrador City and Wabush, has large open-pit iron ore mines and pellet and concentrate plants, with heavy mobile equipment, crushers, conveyors, kilns and rail cars that depend on MT, UT and VT. Vale's Voisey's Bay mine on the north coast supplies the Long Harbour plant. Churchill Falls is one of the largest hydro stations in North America, and Muskrat Falls on the lower Churchill River feeds the HVDC Labrador-Island Link to the island. Turbines, penstocks, gates and transmission structures all need periodic inspection. 5 Wing Goose Bay supports military flying.

Western and central Newfoundland

Corner Brook has a large pulp and paper mill with recovery boilers, digesters and paper machines on regular inspection cycles. Grand Falls-Windsor, Gander, Stephenville and the Botwood area hold airport, hydro, mining and manufacturing operations that need occasional NDT, usually supplied by St. John's or mainland contractors.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Newfoundland and Labrador employers

Direct answer: Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in eight NDT methods plus ASNT Level III exam preparation. The table shows how each method appears in the province's work and what a trainee needs first. Your employer's written practice sets the exact hours.

MethodLevelsWhat Newfoundland and Labrador employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepOffshore and refinery thickness surveys, weld inspection on US-code fabrication, mill and plant equipmentLevel I: employer requirements. Level II: Level I training plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepCorrosion mapping on process piping and vessels, encoded weld scans on modules and structuresUT Level II recommended first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-section welds on vessels, structures and heavy fabricationUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPiping and pressure-equipment welds in plants and fabrication shopsGamma work needs CNSC exposure device operator certification or direct supervision by a certified EDO
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepStructural welds, lifting gear and cranes, mining equipment, rail cars, marine componentsEmployer requirements
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepStainless and non-magnetic components on topsides and in processing plantsEmployer requirements
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual on fabrication, marine repair, tanks and in-service equipmentEmployer requirements
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepHeat exchanger tubing at the refinery, nickel plant, mill and generating stationsEmployer requirements

For senior people, ASNT Level III training prepares candidates for the Basic and method examinations online, which matters in a province where travelling for training often means flying. Method pages such as UT Level 2 training, MT Level 2 training and RT Level 2 training explain each course. A CGSB Level 3 follows the certification body's own requirements, and we will say so.

NDT training by area in Newfoundland and Labrador

Direct answer: Atlantis has no dedicated city training page in Newfoundland and Labrador; its local page is the Practical NDT simulator page for St. John's. Every part of the province is served the same way: live online classes plus onsite delivery at your site. We have no classroom in the province.

City or areaMain NDT sectorsPages
St. John's, Mount Pearl and ParadiseOffshore operations and supply base, inspection companies, ship repair, fabrication, engineeringSt. John's simulator practice; ask about a St. John's cohort
Bull Arm and ClarenvilleOffshore fabrication and module workServed online and onsite
Marystown and the Burin PeninsulaShipyard and offshore fabricationServed online and onsite
Come By Chance, Long Harbour and ArgentiaRenewable diesel refinery, nickel processing, port and marshallingServed online and onsite
Labrador City and WabushIron ore mining and processing, railServed online and onsite at site
Happy Valley-Goose Bay and Churchill FallsHydro generation, military aviation, northern logisticsServed online and onsite
Corner Brook and western NewfoundlandPulp and paper, port, manufacturingServed online and onsite

St. John's. Most of the province's NDT companies and offshore contractors are based here. For offshore work, CGSB or ISO 9712 certification is the norm, so our role is narrower: shops building to US codes, contractors sending crews to US jobs, and individual technicians preparing for US employment. Online theory with an onsite practical in the shop suits these employers.

Bull Arm, Marystown and Argentia. Fabrication volumes rise and fall with offshore projects. When a yard takes a contract for a US client, an SNT-TC-1A written practice and examiners certified under it may be needed quickly, and we can help build that programme.

Placentia Bay plants. Refinery and nickel plant shutdowns need UT, PAUT, ET and RT technicians. Owner specifications decide which certification applies, so check first.

Labrador. Mines and hydro stations run on rotation and fly-in schedules. Online theory between rotations and short onsite practical sessions during maintenance windows is the only realistic model.

Neighbouring Atlantic pages may also help: NDT training in Halifax and NDT training in Saint John.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Newfoundland and Labrador, step by step

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after you complete classroom training and documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. It is an employer certification, not a Canadian national certificate.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A-based written practice. We can write it with you: written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete the hours your written practice sets, online or onsite. The training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience. Log supervised hours on real work, from shop fabrication to plant maintenance.
  4. Examinations. Pass the general, specific and practical exams under a Level III.
  5. Vision. Pass near-vision and colour contrast checks, usually every year.
  6. Certification. Your employer certifies you for the method and level.
  7. Recertification. Renew at the interval in your written practice. A new employer must recertify you under its own written practice.

Technicians with experience from Alberta, the US or overseas often have records under several schemes. Keep your logs detailed and organised so each certification body or employer can verify them.

Radiography licensing and other Newfoundland and Labrador requirements

Direct answer: industrial gamma radiography is licensed federally by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission; operators must be certified exposure device operators or trainees under their direct supervision. Onshore boilers and pressure vessels fall under the province's Engineering and Inspection Services Division. Offshore activity is regulated by the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Energy Regulator.

Industrial radiography

The CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices in every province and offshore; there is no US-style Agreement State system. Only a certified exposure device operator (EDO), or a trainee under the direct supervision and continuous observation of a certified EDO, may operate an exposure device. Certification follows the CNSC's REGDOC-2.2.3 and the CSA PCP-09 guide: formal vocational training, a supervised on-the-job programme and CNSC examinations. Atlantis RT training covers radiographic principles, technique, interpretation and acceptance criteria. It does not replace EDO certification and we do not run CNSC examinations. X-ray equipment falls under provincial rules; your radiation safety officer should confirm current requirements.

Onshore boilers and pressure vessels

The province's Engineering and Inspection Services Division administers pressure equipment safety under the Public Safety Act and the Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Compressed Gas Regulations. Installing or altering a pressure system requires a permit and an inspection when the work is complete, and boilers and pressure vessels are inspected periodically. The division sits within the provincial department responsible for government services, whose name has changed in recent reorganisations, so check the current provincial website for contacts. Commonly referenced codes include CSA B51, ASME Sections I, V and VIII, and ASME B31.1 and B31.3.

Offshore

Offshore petroleum activity is jointly managed by the federal and provincial governments under the Atlantic Accord legislation. The regulator, formerly the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Petroleum Board, became the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Energy Regulator in 2025, with a mandate that now includes offshore renewable energy. Offshore installations also involve independent certifying authorities, and operators set their own personnel certification requirements in their specifications, generally ISO 9712-based. Offshore work also requires offshore safety and survival training. None of this is replaced by our courses.

Other requirements

Industrial sites typically require safety prequalification, orientation and the owner's contractor-management rules. Structural steel to CSA W59 is fabricated by CWB-certified companies with CGSB-certified NDT staff. Our training sits beside these requirements for the work where SNT-TC-1A applies.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Newfoundland and Labrador

Direct answer: Atlantis trains Newfoundland and Labrador students through live online classes, private live-virtual cohorts and onsite delivery at the employer's facility, all led by an ASNT Level III. Theory runs online; practical sessions use real specimens at your site.

No province makes a stronger case for online theory. A technician in Labrador City, a fabricator in Marystown and a rotational offshore worker at home in Gander can all join the same live class without a flight or a ferry. Onsite practical blocks come to the shop or plant when the employer is ready. We plan around the province's rhythms: offshore rotations, refinery and nickel plant shutdowns, mine maintenance windows in Labrador, fabrication contract schedules at the yards, and winter weather that can close roads and ferries.

  • Live online seats for individuals anywhere in the province, including on days off from rotation.
  • Private live-virtual cohorts for one company, built around its procedures and codes.
  • Onsite delivery at your St. John's shop, Placentia Bay plant or Labrador site, using your equipment and specimens.
  • Blended programmes with online theory, simulator practice and a short onsite practical block.

We have no classroom in Newfoundland and Labrador. Ask about onsite training for your crew, or see online NDT training and corporate NDT training.

For Newfoundland and Labrador employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: an employer in the province that needs SNT-TC-1A certification for US-code or US-client work needs a written practice, a Level III to administer examinations, and records an auditor can follow. Atlantis provides all three remotely or onsite, alongside any CGSB-certified staff the company already has.

Typical requests include a St. John's machine shop or fabricator winning work for a US client, a contractor that sends crews to US turnarounds and wants its own employer certification programme, and an inspection company adding an SNT-TC-1A track for staff who work abroad. We can:

  • write or update your SNT-TC-1A written practice (written practice development);
  • act as your outside Level III for examinations, procedure review and technique sign-off;
  • document which jobs use SNT-TC-1A personnel and which require CGSB or ISO 9712 personnel;
  • prepare your NDT programme for customer and third-party audits;
  • track certifications, training, vision tests and calibration in our NDT ERP, which records CGSB, ISO 9712 and ASNT certifications side by side (NDT ERP overview).

Read SNT-TC-1A training and certification for employers or NDT consulting in Canada. Book a Level III consultation for your programme.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator lets trainees in Newfoundland and Labrador practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments from a browser. It is practice only and does not replace the hands-on practical exam required by your written practice or by a CGSB or ISO 9712 scheme.

The oil and gas site, storage tank and welding workshop environments reflect much of the province's work, from process piping and tanks to fabrication welds. For rotational workers, the simulator is a way to keep skills fresh between hitches and to practise probe handling and indication recognition before a practical exam. See Practical NDT or Practical NDT in St. John's, and try the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop develops the course material, examinations and employer written practices, and he is the Level III you speak with when you want a straight answer on whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or both suit your work in Newfoundland and Labrador.

NDT training in Newfoundland and Labrador: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Newfoundland and Labrador?

Most offshore, mining and provincial code work needs CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or another ISO 9712-based certification; confirm the current certification body, since arrangements changed in 2026. Work for US customers or US employers uses SNT-TC-1A employer certification, which is the route Atlantis trains for.

Is there NDT training online in Newfoundland and Labrador?

Yes. Live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes are open to technicians anywhere in the province, including Labrador. Practical training and exams take place on real specimens, usually at the employer's site. See NDT training online.

Will SNT-TC-1A training get me offshore work on the Grand Banks?

Usually not on its own. Offshore operators set their own requirements, which are generally CGSB or ISO 9712-based, and offshore work also needs offshore safety training. Check the operator or contractor specification.

Can I get CGSB / ISO 9712 certified through Atlantis in St. John's?

No. We teach SNT-TC-1A only and claim no CGSB recognition.

Do I need a licence to do radiography in Newfoundland and Labrador?

For gamma radiography, yes. You must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator or a trainee under direct supervision, and the employer needs a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment falls under provincial rules.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in Newfoundland and Labrador?

The provincial Engineering and Inspection Services Division, under the Public Safety Act and the Boiler, Pressure Vessel and Compressed Gas Regulations. Offshore installations fall under the offshore regulator.

How much does NDT training cost in Newfoundland and Labrador?

It is quoted on request, based on method, level, number of trainees, delivery mode and any written practice or Level III work. Cohort and onsite quotes usually come back within one business day. Get a training quote.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in the province?

UT and PAUT dominate offshore and plant integrity work. MT is essential on structures, lifting gear and mining equipment, ET on heat exchangers, and RT on piping and pressure-equipment welds.

Can you train our crew onsite in Labrador City or at Bull Arm?

Yes, subject to your site's access and safety rules. The instructor uses your equipment and specimens and supports practical exams under your written practice.

Can I use SNT-TC-1A certification on the US Gulf Coast?

US employers generally certify technicians under SNT-TC-1A or CP-189, so SNT-TC-1A training is a good fit for US work. Your US employer will review your training and experience and certify you under its own written practice.

How long does UT Level II take?

Your employer's written practice sets classroom and experience hours, using SNT-TC-1A recommendations as a baseline; see the training requirements matrix.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Newfoundland and Labrador?

Yes. Our Level III preparation runs online. For pay context, see the NDT salary guide; we do not publish our own salary figures.

Get a quote for NDT training in Newfoundland and Labrador

Whether you need a St. John's fabricator's first SNT-TC-1A written practice for a US customer, a contractor's crew certified for US turnaround work, or a single technician preparing for a move to the US, Atlantis NDT will build the programme around your work and rotation, and we will tell you plainly when CGSB or ISO 9712 is what the job needs instead. Request your Newfoundland and Labrador training quote, read about Atlantis NDT training, or see NDT training across Canada. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

NDT Training and Certification in North Carolina

North Carolina technicians and employers can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, in live-virtual cohorts, or onsite at their own plant, hangar or shop. Courses are led by an ASNT NDT Level III and aligned with the employer's written practice, so training counts toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

North Carolina's NDT market looks different from the Gulf Coast states. There are no oil refineries here. Instead, demand comes from nuclear and fossil power generation, turbine and generator manufacturing, aerospace manufacturing and military aircraft maintenance, steel and heavy equipment, pipelines and an enormous highway bridge inventory. Charlotte is also home to EPRI's NDE Center, one of the best-known nondestructive evaluation research facilities in the power industry. This page maps that work by region and explains how certification, radiography licensing and boiler rules apply in North Carolina. Ready now? Request a North Carolina training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in North Carolina

North Carolina NDT work clusters around Charlotte's power and energy-equipment sector, the Piedmont Triad's aerospace manufacturing and MRO, the Research Triangle's advanced manufacturing, eastern military aviation at Havelock and Goldsboro, the Wilmington nuclear and port corridor, and Asheville's turbine-component manufacturing, with pipelines and bridges statewide.

Charlotte and the Catawba region

Charlotte is the headquarters of Duke Energy, and the surrounding region has some of the most concentrated power-generation work in the Southeast. Duke's McGuire nuclear station sits on Lake Norman north of the city, and Catawba nuclear station is just across the South Carolina line. Siemens Energy builds gas turbines and generators in Charlotte, and EPRI's NDE Center develops and qualifies inspection techniques used across the nuclear and fossil fleet. Typical work: UT, PAUT and ET in nuclear outages under ASME Section XI, UT and MT on turbine and generator components, RT and UT on power piping, and boiler-tube thickness surveys at fossil plants. See our nuclear NDT training in Charlotte and power-generation NDT training in Charlotte pages.

Piedmont Triad: Greensboro, Winston-Salem and High Point

Greensboro's Piedmont Triad International Airport is an aerospace cluster: HAECO Americas performs heavy aircraft maintenance there, Honda Aircraft Company builds business jets, and Boom Supersonic has built its aircraft factory at the airport. Aircraft MRO is heavy on ET, PT, UT and VT, and manufacturing adds PT and UT on aluminium and composite structures. The Triad also has furniture-industry and heavy-equipment manufacturing, truck and bus plants, and steel fabrication.

Research Triangle: Raleigh, Durham and Cary

The Triangle is better known for life sciences and technology, but it also supports NDT employers: pharmaceutical and biologics manufacturing with stainless process piping (VT, PT, RT on orbital welds), electrical equipment makers, Duke's Shearon Harris nuclear plant at New Hill in Wake County, and the engineering firms that inspect NCDOT bridges. Toyota's battery manufacturing site at Liberty, south of the Triad, adds new automotive-industry demand.

Eastern North Carolina: Havelock, Goldsboro, Fayetteville and Jacksonville

Fleet Readiness Center East at Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point in Havelock is a major military aircraft maintenance depot, with substantial ET, UT, PT, MT and RT work on airframes, engines and components. Seymour Johnson Air Force Base at Goldsboro operates fighter aircraft, Fort Bragg near Fayetteville is one of the largest Army installations in the country, and Camp Lejeune is at Jacksonville. Contractors supporting these sites need SNT-TC-1A-certified technicians and often NAS 410 or military-specific requirements. See NDT training in Fayetteville, NC.

Wilmington and the coast

Wilmington hosts GE's nuclear fuel and engineering operations at Castle Hayne, the Port of Wilmington's terminals, and chemical plants along the Cape Fear River. Duke's Brunswick nuclear plant at Southport and the Port of Morehead City add outage and marine work. Coastal humidity and salt make corrosion monitoring with UT a constant need.

Western North Carolina and the mountains

Pratt and Whitney manufactures turbine airfoils in the Asheville area, a high-precision casting and machining operation where FPI, X-ray and other NDT methods are part of production. The mountain region also has hydroelectric dams, paper and specialty-materials plants and Interstate bridges through difficult terrain.

Steel, pipelines and bridges statewide

Nucor operates a steel plate mill in Hertford County in the northeast. Interstate gas transmission lines and refined-product pipelines, including the Colonial system through the Piedmont, cross the state; Colonial's 2020 gasoline release near Huntersville was a reminder of why in-service integrity inspection matters. NCDOT maintains one of the largest state-owned highway systems in the country, with thousands of bridges that need steel and weld inspection.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in North Carolina, step by step

North Carolina does not license NDT technicians. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete method training, log documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III and pass a vision test.

  1. Employer written practice defines levels, training, experience, exams and recertification for each method.
  2. Classroom training in the method, online, live-virtual or onsite. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums are on the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience, supervised and documented: boiler-tube UT at a Duke fossil unit, ET on airframes at Havelock, MT on bridge girders.
  4. General exam on the principles of the method.
  5. Specific exam on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, such as ASME Section V, ASME Section XI or AWS D1.5.
  6. Practical exam on real specimens with known discontinuities, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision test, near-vision and colour contrast, annually.
  8. Certification issued and documented by the employer.
  9. Recertification at the interval the written practice sets.

Nuclear work adds another layer: in-service UT on certain components is performed under ASME Section XI Appendix VIII performance demonstration, administered through EPRI's Performance Demonstration Initiative. That is beyond SNT-TC-1A method certification, but a strong Level II foundation is the starting point. More on the employer-based model at SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other North Carolina requirements

North Carolina is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive materials is licensed by the Radioactive Materials Branch of the Radiation Protection Section, within the NC Department of Health and Human Services, under state rules in Title 10A, Chapter 15 of the NC Administrative Code, which require compliance with the industrial radiography requirements of 10 CFR Part 34.

The Radiation Protection Section licenses both booth and field industrial radiography and also registers radiation-producing machines such as industrial x-ray units. Licensed companies need a radiation safety officer, trained and certified radiographers, supervised assistants, dosimetry and survey programmes. Out-of-state licensees working in North Carolina use the state's reciprocal recognition process before starting work. SNT-TC-1A RT method certification is separate: an RT technician needs both. Confirm current requirements with the Radiation Protection Section before mobilising a crew.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The North Carolina Department of Labor's Boiler Safety Bureau inspects and certifies boilers and pressure vessels under the state Uniform Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act. Inspectors hold National Board commissions, and repairs and alterations follow the National Board Inspection Code, with NDT requirements from ASME Section V and the construction code. Power plants, mills and manufacturing plants are the main sources of this work.

Pipelines. Intrastate gas pipeline safety is overseen by the North Carolina Utilities Commission's pipeline safety programme, and PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid pipelines. API 1104 governs most pipeline weld inspection, with operator qualification rules covering many tasks.

Codes in local use (context only). ASME Section XI and plant-specific programmes at McGuire, Harris and Brunswick; ASME Section I, V and VIII and B31.1 at fossil and gas plants; AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structural steel and bridges; API 1104 for pipelines; and NAS 410 or military requirements for aerospace and defence work. Some North Carolina employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials, which are separate schemes; Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based.

North Carolina crews can take NDT theory live online, join a live-virtual cohort, or have a Level III-led programme delivered onsite at their facility. Practical training and practical exams are performed on real specimens at the employer's site or another agreed arrangement.

North Carolina is about 500 miles from Murphy to Manteo. Online theory lets a technician in Asheville and one in Havelock join the same live class without travel, with interactive Level III instruction rather than recorded videos alone. See NDT training online for how sessions run.

We plan dates around North Carolina's work calendar: spring and fall refuelling and maintenance outages across the Duke fleet, aircraft induction schedules at depots and MRO hangars, production ramps in aerospace manufacturing, and the bridge-inspection season. Multi-site companies can use corporate NDT training to keep records consistent across states. Ask about onsite training for your North Carolina crew.

For North Carolina employers: written practice and Level III services

North Carolina companies that certify NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A need a written practice and Level III oversight. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, administers and grades exams, reviews procedures and serves as an outside Level III for companies without one.

The Triad's aerospace suppliers, Charlotte's energy-equipment fabricators and eastern North Carolina's defence contractors frequently need certified inspectors before they have the internal structure to certify them. A new supplier qualifying to an aerospace prime, a fabricator taking on power-plant work or a contractor whose Level III has left all need a written practice that matches their actual methods and customers. Our written practice development service delivers that, and the SNT-TC-1A guide explains what customer and registrar auditors look for.

Practise before your practical exam

Practical NDT, Atlantis NDT's 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The aircraft hangar matches the MRO and depot work at Greensboro and Havelock. The welding workshop matches Charlotte's and the Triad's fabricators. The NDT lab scenes help trainees rehearse calibration and set-up before working on real power-plant or aerospace parts. Simulator time is not on-the-job experience and is not graded as a practical exam. Explore the Practical NDT simulator and the state page, Practical NDT for North Carolina.

NDT training in North Carolina: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in North Carolina?

Most North Carolina NDT technicians are certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A: classroom training in a method, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and a vision test. The employer then certifies you to its written practice. Atlantis NDT provides the training, exam support and written practice if needed.

Is there NDT training online in North Carolina?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online NDT theory that technicians can join from Charlotte, Raleigh, Greensboro, Wilmington or anywhere in the state. Practical training and the practical exam require real specimens, arranged onsite at your employer or through an agreed arrangement.

Do I need a license to do radiography in North Carolina?

Your company needs a radioactive materials licence from the NC Radiation Protection Section, or registration for its x-ray equipment, and radiographers must meet state training and certification rules aligned with 10 CFR Part 34. This is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Confirm current requirements with the state.

How much does NDT training cost in North Carolina?

Quote on request. It depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and whether you need written-practice or exam services. Send your details and you will receive a quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in North Carolina?

UT is the most widely used, especially in power generation. ET is in strong demand for aircraft maintenance and tubing inspection, PT and VT for aerospace and pharma manufacturing, and MT for bridges and heavy steel.

Can you train our crew onsite in Charlotte or Greensboro?

Yes. Onsite delivery is available at your facility anywhere in North Carolina, scheduled around outages and production. Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in North Carolina; onsite means at your site.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by North Carolina employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the main employer-based NDT certification framework in the United States and is referenced by ASME and AWS codes. Nuclear and aerospace customers add their own requirements, which your written practice should address.

How long does Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimum hours and experience are listed in the training requirements matrix; logging experience usually takes longer than the classroom part.

Do I need nuclear-specific qualification to work outages in North Carolina?

For many outage tasks, an SNT-TC-1A Level II under the contractor's written practice is the base, with site-specific training and badging on top. Certain UT examinations also require performance demonstration qualification under ASME Section XI Appendix VIII. See nuclear NDT training.

Can I start NDT training with no experience?

Yes. Level I has no experience prerequisite. Many North Carolina technicians start as helpers or trainees with an inspection contractor and train up to Level II as experience builds.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from North Carolina?

Yes. ASNT Level III training runs live online. Level II candidates can also use the UT Level 2 practice questions.

What do NDT technicians earn in North Carolina?

Pay varies by method, level, sector and outage travel. See our NDT Level 2 salary and NDT Level 3 salary guides for published ranges.

NDT Training and Certification in North Dakota

North Dakota technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at their own shop, gas plant, power station or pipeline yard. Every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III and built around the employer's written practice, so the classroom hours count toward certification. Methods covered: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

North Dakota's NDT market is shaped by one fact above all: the Bakken. Since the shale boom, the western half of the state has become one of the largest onshore oil-producing regions in the country, with thousands of wells, a dense web of gathering lines, gas processing plants, compressor stations, rail terminals and the trunk pipelines that carry crude and gas out of the basin. Behind that sits a second economy that is easy to forget: lignite coal mines and the power plants they feed along the Missouri River, a synthetic natural gas plant, a refinery in Mandan, a renewable diesel plant in Dickinson, two Air Force bases, and a manufacturing belt in the Red River Valley around Fargo and Grand Forks that builds agricultural and construction equipment. Each of those employers needs different methods, codes and paperwork. This page is organised around that map. If you already know what you need, request a North Dakota training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in North Dakota

Most North Dakota NDT work sits in four zones: the Bakken oil field in the northwest (Williston, Watford City, Tioga, Stanley), the lignite and energy-conversion belt along the Missouri River north of Bismarck, the Bismarck-Mandan and Dickinson corridor with its refinery and renewable fuels plant, and the Red River Valley manufacturing and agricultural processing cities of Fargo and Grand Forks. The two Air Force bases at Minot and Grand Forks add federal work.

The Bakken: Williston, Watford City, Tioga and Stanley

McKenzie, Williams, Mountrail and Dunn counties hold most of North Dakota's oil production. The NDT work here is pipeline and facility work rather than refinery work: radiography and UT shear-wave inspection of gathering-line and transmission girth welds to API 1104, VT of welds on tank batteries, separators and compressor skids, UT thickness and corrosion surveys on produced-water and saltwater disposal lines, and MT and PT on well-site equipment and fabrication. Large gas processing plants around Tioga, Watford City and Keene run their own maintenance and turnaround programmes, which bring in UT, PAUT, RT and ET work on vessels, exchangers and plant piping to ASME Section VIII and B31.3. The state's radiation control programme has noted that much of the growth in its radioactive-materials licences came from radiography, well-logging and gauge users supporting Bakken activity, which tells you how important RT has been in this region.

The Missouri River energy belt: Beulah, Underwood, Stanton and Center

North of Bismarck, lignite mines feed several large coal-fired power plants, including Coal Creek Station near Underwood and Antelope Valley Station near Beulah, along with the Great Plains Synfuels Plant, which converts lignite to synthetic natural gas, fertiliser and other products. These are classic outage-driven NDT customers: UT thickness and ET on boiler tubes, UT and MT of high-energy piping welds, RT of tube and pipe repairs, VT of pressure parts and supports, and inspection of large rotating equipment, draglines and conveyors at the mines. The synfuels plant behaves more like a chemical complex, with vessel and piping inspection to ASME and API practice.

Bismarck, Mandan and Dickinson

The Marathon refinery in Mandan is North Dakota's main crude oil refinery, and its turnarounds are the largest single draw for refinery-style NDT in the state: UT thickness, PAUT and TOFD on welds and corrosion, RT of new piping, ET of exchanger bundles and VT of pressure equipment. Further west, the Dickinson plant that began life as a small crude refinery has been converted to renewable diesel, and still needs piping and vessel inspection. Bismarck itself, as the capital, hosts state agencies, construction, heavy-equipment manufacturing and the service companies that support the oil field to the west.

The Red River Valley: Fargo, West Fargo, Wahpeton and Grand Forks

The eastern edge of the state is a manufacturing and agricultural processing region. Fargo and West Fargo build agricultural equipment, construction equipment and steel structures; compact equipment is manufactured nearby in Gwinner; Wahpeton and Grand Forks have food processing, sugar beet and ethanol plants with steam systems and pressure vessels. Here MT and PT on welded frames, booms and castings, UT on structural welds and plate, and VT on production welding dominate. These are typically ISO 9001 manufacturers who need an auditable written practice and a handful of certified Level II inspectors rather than large field crews.

Minot, Grand Forks and the Air Force bases

Minot Air Force Base hosts bomber and missile wings, and Grand Forks Air Force Base hosts unmanned aircraft and related missions. Both bring federal construction, facility maintenance and defence-contractor work where documented certification and audit-ready records matter. Minot is also a rail and agricultural hub for the north-central part of the state.

Pipelines, rail and bridges

Major crude and gas pipelines leave the Bakken heading east and south, including the Dakota Access line, and rail loading terminals across the northwest still ship crude by train. New pipeline construction, integrity digs and terminal maintenance all call for RT, UT and VT. Railroad shops and yards add axle, wheel and weld inspection. The North Dakota Department of Transportation manages bridges across the state, with steel bridge fabrication and repair usually done to AWS D1.5.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in North Dakota, step by step

Direct answer: North Dakota has no state NDT technician licence. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete classroom training and documented experience and pass general, specific, practical and vision exams administered under a Level III. Radiography adds state radiation safety requirements on top.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. It defines training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks, vision requirements and recertification intervals for each method and level. If your company does not have one, we write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Take Level I and then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours per method and level.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience. Log supervised experience on a pipeline spread, at a gas plant, in a manufacturing plant or during outages. Your employer documents and verifies the hours.
  4. Pass the general exam. A written exam on method principles.
  5. Pass the specific exam. Covers your employer's procedures, the codes you work to (for example API 1104, ASME Section V or AWS D1.1) and your equipment.
  6. Pass the practical exam. A hands-on test on real specimens with real flaws, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Pass the vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated at the interval in your written practice.
  8. Get certified by your employer. Certification is issued by, and tied to, your employer.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Keep your vision test current, recertify on schedule and add methods or levels as you progress.

Read SNT-TC-1A training and certification for a fuller explanation of the employer-based system, and the Level 2 training page for what a Level II is expected to do independently.

Radiography licensing and other North Dakota requirements

Direct answer: North Dakota has been an NRC Agreement State since 1969. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality's Radiation Control Program, which also registers X-ray equipment. Boilers are inspected by the Department of Environmental Quality's Boiler Inspection Program, and intrastate gas pipeline safety sits with the North Dakota Public Service Commission.

Industrial radiography

Because North Dakota is an Agreement State, a company performing gamma radiography in the state needs a North Dakota radioactive materials licence or, if it is licensed elsewhere, reciprocity recognition from the Radiation Control Program before it works here. The programme moved into the Department of Environmental Quality when that department was created in 2019. The state's industrial radiography rules follow the federal model in 10 CFR Part 34: radiation safety training, a radiation safety examination, a supervised period as a radiographer's assistant, recognised radiographer certification, personal dosimetry and survey instruments, and the two-person rule at field sites. X-ray equipment used for radiography is registered with the same programme. RT method training under SNT-TC-1A, which is what Atlantis provides, covers technique, exposure, image quality and interpretation; it complements, but does not replace, the radiation safety training the licence holder must provide. Confirm current requirements with the Radiation Control Program before deploying a crew, especially for out-of-state companies coming into the Bakken.

Boilers and pressure vessels

North Dakota's Boiler Inspection Program, part of the Department of Environmental Quality, has been in place since 1953 and inspects boilers in public and commercial locations through a chief boiler inspector and deputy inspectors. Repairs and alterations to boilers and pressure vessels are generally carried out to the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board inspection rules, so the NDT on that work is performed to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme. Fabrication shops and repair organisations in Fargo, Bismarck and Williston therefore need written practices that will survive a National Board or ASME review.

Pipelines

Interstate pipelines are regulated by PHMSA. The North Dakota Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety, and the state Industrial Commission's Oil and Gas Division also has a role in oil field gathering lines. Pipeline weld inspection follows API 1104, with ASME B31.4 for liquid lines and B31.8 for gas, and operators expect radiographers and UT technicians qualified to their procedures.

Codes North Dakota employers commonly use

  • API 1104 and ASME B31.4 and B31.8 for Bakken gathering, transmission and crude lines
  • ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3 at the Mandan refinery, gas processing plants and the synfuels plant
  • ASME Section I and B31.1 for boilers and power piping at the lignite power plants
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and equipment manufacturing, and AWS D1.5 for bridges
  • API 650 and API 653 context for tank batteries and terminal tanks (Atlantis trains the NDT methods, not the API inspector certifications)

Some North Dakota employers also want API inspector or CWI credentials for specific roles. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train; our programmes focus on ASNT SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across North Dakota

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in North Dakota. Theory is taught live online or in live-virtual cohorts, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility with your own equipment and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight. That lets Bakken and Red River Valley crews train without long drives or lost rotations.

For individual technicians, online NDT training covers the classroom portion of Level I and Level II. Sessions are live, so you can ask questions and work through problems with a Level III instructor. Many oil field technicians work long rotations, so we can plan classroom blocks around days off rather than forcing you to give up shifts. Practical hours and the practical exam are completed with your employer.

For employers training a group, onsite delivery is usually the best fit. We run classroom and practical sessions at your Williston yard, gas plant training room, Mandan contractor facility or Fargo production plant, using your instruments, reference standards and part samples, and teach to the procedures your crew actually follows. A pipeline contractor gets RT and UT built around API 1104 girth welds; a Fargo manufacturer gets MT and VT on its own welded frames; a power plant gets UT and ET on tube samples from its own boilers.

North Dakota's calendar matters. Pipeline construction and much field work concentrate in the frost-free months, while winter brings extreme cold that slows outdoor work, which makes late autumn and winter the natural time for classroom training. Refinery and gas-plant turnarounds and power plant outages run on their own schedules, usually in spring and fall. We plan cohorts so technicians are certified before the season or the outage begins. Multi-site employers can use corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your North Dakota crew.

For North Dakota employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A the employer is responsible for certification, so every North Dakota NDT employer needs a written practice and access to a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams and acts as an outside Level III for companies without one.

The Bakken created many young inspection and fabrication companies that grew quickly, and many Red River Valley manufacturers added NDT only when a customer demanded it. In both cases the paperwork often lags the work: a written practice borrowed from a former employer, training records without hours, practical exams with no graded checklist, or vision tests that lapsed during a busy season. Those are exactly the findings that appear in customer audits and National Board reviews.

We help with:

  • Written practice development and revision to the current SNT-TC-1A edition and your customers' requirements. See written practice development.
  • Exam administration, with general, specific and practical exams prepared and graded under Level III oversight.
  • Procedure review against API 1104, ASME and AWS requirements.
  • Audit preparation for operator audits, National Board or ASME reviews and ISO 9001 surveillance.
  • Multi-site programmes through corporate NDT training.

For broader Level III consulting in the state, see NDT consulting in North Dakota and our guide to SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your North Dakota company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT simulator lets North Dakota trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before the practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique, scanning patterns and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank environment. For North Dakota technicians, the oil and gas site and storage tank match Bakken facility and tank-battery work, the welding workshop matches Fargo and Bismarck manufacturing, and the hangar suits aerospace and base-related work. Trainees on long rotations can practise between shifts. See Practical NDT in North Dakota, plus the Williston, Bismarck and Fargo pages. For written exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Direct answer: North Dakota programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop designs the courses, teaches Level III-led sessions and oversees the exams and records that make certification defensible under SNT-TC-1A. He connects method theory to the procedures and codes your crew actually uses, whether that is API 1104 on a Bakken spread or AWS D1.1 on a Fargo production line, and helps employers build written practices that hold up in audits. Contact us about North Dakota training to ask about his availability.

NDT training in North Dakota: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in North Dakota?

Your employer certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice. Complete Level I and Level II classroom training, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. If you are not yet working in NDT, online classroom training gets you ready, and certification follows once an employer documents your experience.

Is there NDT training online in North Dakota?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online and live-virtual Level I and Level II classes that North Dakota technicians can join from Williston, Bismarck, Fargo or anywhere else. The practical exam is completed onsite with your employer.

Do I need a license to do radiography in North Dakota?

The company performing radiography needs a North Dakota radioactive materials licence or reciprocity from the Department of Environmental Quality's Radiation Control Program. Individual radiographers and assistants must meet state training, examination, supervision and certification requirements equivalent to 10 CFR Part 34. Confirm current requirements with the programme before starting work.

How much does NDT training cost in North Dakota?

It is quoted on request. The quote depends on method and level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, travel for practical sessions, and whether you also need exam administration or a written practice. We return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in North Dakota?

RT and UT on pipeline welds lead in the Bakken, with VT required almost everywhere. MT and VT dominate in Fargo and Bismarck manufacturing, and UT, ET and PAUT are central to refinery, gas plant and power plant inspection.

Can you train our crew onsite in Williston or Fargo?

Yes. We deliver classroom and practical sessions at your facility anywhere in North Dakota, using your equipment and specimens, and schedule around rotations, construction seasons, turnarounds and outages.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by North Dakota employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard basis for employer certification across US oil and gas, power and manufacturing. Pipeline operators and manufacturers' customers may add requirements, which your written practice can document.

How long does RT or UT Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums. The experience requirement normally takes longer than the classroom training.

Can I train for NDT while working rotations in the Bakken?

Yes. Live online classroom sessions can be scheduled around days off, and practical training happens with your employer when you are on site.

Is there an NDT school in North Dakota I can visit?

Atlantis NDT does not run a physical school or campus in North Dakota. Training is live online or onsite at your employer's facility.

Can I become a Level III in North Dakota?

Yes. Level III candidates usually hold Level II experience and then sit the ASNT Level III examinations. Our Level III training covers preparation online.

What do NDT technicians earn in North Dakota?

Pay varies with method, level, rotation and overtime. For general context, see the NDT salary guide.

Get a quote for NDT training in North Dakota

From a single radiographer moving up to Level II to a full Bakken contractor crew, a Fargo manufacturer's first written practice, or a power plant's pre-outage refresher, Atlantis NDT builds programmes around your work and schedule. Request your North Dakota training quote, explore Atlantis NDT training, or tell us your crew's methods and dates. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.
