NDT Training and Certification in Nova Scotia

Short answer: Nova Scotia technicians and employers can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, along with ASNT Level III exam preparation. Courses run live online, as a private live-virtual cohort for one company, or onsite at your shop, yard or plant, always led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you to its own written practice.

We want to be candid from the first paragraph, because Nova Scotia's NDT market leans harder toward Canada's national scheme than most. Shipbuilding for the Royal Canadian Navy and Coast Guard, naval ship repair, power generation, and offshore energy regulated by a federal-provincial board all tend to specify CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, or the aerospace standard NAS 410. Atlantis NDT does not train toward CGSB or NAS 410 certification and claims no CGSB recognition. Our SNT-TC-1A training fits a narrower but real group in Nova Scotia: fabricators and machine shops building ASME or AWS work for US customers, companies serving US-owned plants and US projects in New England, ship repairers and marine contractors whose US clients name SNT-TC-1A, and technicians who plan to work in US shipyards, refineries or pipelines. This page sets out who that is, maps the province's inspection work from Halifax Harbour to Cape Breton, and explains how to get a quote. Request a Nova Scotia NDT training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Who SNT-TC-1A training suits in Nova Scotia, and who it does not

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A suits Nova Scotia employers and technicians whose work is built to US codes, sold to US customers or done in the US. Naval shipbuilding, defence, aerospace, offshore and most Canadian code work usually require CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or NAS 410 certification instead, and our training does not lead to either.

The province sells a great deal into the northeastern United States, from tires and seafood equipment to fabricated steel and electricity, and Halifax is a short sail from Boston. That creates specific situations where an employer-based SNT-TC-1A programme is the practical answer. The table below is how we work through it with a caller.

Your situation in Nova ScotiaScheme usually expectedDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
Naval shipbuilding and ship repair for the Royal Canadian Navy or Canadian Coast GuardCAN/CGSB-48.9712 under the contract and DND specificationsNo. You need CGSB certification
Aircraft and helicopter maintenance or aerostructure manufacturingNAS 410 / EN 4179 with OEM and Transport Canada requirementsNo for certification. Method knowledge only
Construction or in-service NDE on Nova Scotia-registered boilers and pressure equipment for a Canadian inspection companyCAN/CGSB-48.9712, often through a CSA W178.1-certified organisationUsually no. Check the owner specification and the Technical Safety Division's requirements
Fabricating ASME pressure equipment, skids or AWS D1.1 structures for US customersSNT-TC-1A per ASME Section V or the client specificationYes. The core use case
Commercial ship repair or marine fabrication for a US owner whose specification names SNT-TC-1ASNT-TC-1A, alongside class-society requirementsYes, if the client specification accepts it
Technician planning to move to US shipyards, refineries or pipeline workSNT-TC-1A or CP-189 through the US employerYes. Your training record travels with you

On the CGSB side: the Canadian General Standards Board, which published CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Natural Resources Canada and the CWB Group have said the standard remains valid for its current cycle and existing certifications are unaffected, and NRCan's NDT Certification Body says its services continue. Since arrangements are still settling, confirm the current certification body before you plan a CGSB route. Many Atlantic Canadian technicians hold both a CGSB certificate and an employer SNT-TC-1A certification, and we can help you plan the two together.

Where NDT technicians work in Nova Scotia

Direct answer: Nova Scotia's NDT work centres on Halifax Harbour, with its naval shipyard, dockyard and port; on the aerospace and defence maintenance sector around Halifax Stanfield airport and Shearwater; on power generation and heavy industry in Cape Breton, the Strait of Canso and Pictou County; on manufacturing in the South Shore and Annapolis Valley; and on the emerging offshore wind and hydrogen projects.

Halifax Harbour: shipbuilding, naval repair and the port

Halifax Shipyard, operated by Irving Shipbuilding, builds the Royal Canadian Navy's Arctic and Offshore Patrol Ships and is building the River-class destroyers under the National Shipbuilding Strategy. That is a long-running programme of heavy steel fabrication with extensive UT, RT, MT and VT on hull, deck and system welds. Across the harbour, HMC Dockyard and the navy's fleet maintenance facility support the Atlantic fleet. The Port of Halifax handles container, bulk and cruise traffic, with ship repair, marine fabrication and terminal maintenance work for contractors. Dartmouth's industrial parks hold fabrication shops, machine shops and the inspection companies that serve the whole region. See NDT training in Halifax for more city detail.

Aerospace and defence maintenance

The Halifax region has a significant aerospace maintenance sector. IMP Aerospace and Defence, near Halifax Stanfield International Airport, has long supported military aircraft maintenance, and 12 Wing Shearwater is home to the RCAF's maritime helicopters. On the South Shore, Lunenburg has an aerostructure composites plant. These operations use ET, PT, UT and MT heavily, but under NAS 410 and OEM rules, so they are context for this page rather than our market.

Cape Breton and the Strait of Canso

Cape Breton and the Strait of Canso hold Nova Scotia's heavy-industry base: coal-fired generating stations at Lingan and Point Aconi, the deep-water terminal and industrial park at Point Tupper, a large paper mill at Port Hawkesbury, and the Port of Sydney. Power plant outages create boiler tube, header and high-energy piping inspection, and the Point Tupper area is the focus of proposed green hydrogen and ammonia projects, which would bring new pressure-equipment and piping work if they proceed.

Pictou County, Truro and central Nova Scotia

The Trenton generating station in Pictou County and the manufacturing and fabrication shops around New Glasgow, Stellarton and Truro add steady MT, UT and VT work, much of it on structural steel, process equipment and rotating machinery. A tire manufacturer operates plants in Pictou County, the Annapolis Valley and the South Shore, which need pressure vessel, boiler and machinery inspection.

Halifax-area power, utilities and bridges

The Tufts Cove generating station in Dartmouth, the Maritimes and Northeast natural gas pipeline that crosses the province to New England, local gas distribution, and the two suspension bridges across Halifax Harbour all need inspection. Bridge and structural work is generally fabricated and repaired to CSA S6 and CSA W59 by CWB-certified companies, which normally means CGSB-certified NDT staff.

Offshore energy

Nova Scotia's offshore gas fields, Sable and Deep Panuke, have been decommissioned, so there is no offshore production today. The offshore regulator, now the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Energy Regulator, is overseeing a new phase focused on offshore wind. If offshore wind projects proceed, they will bring large-scale fabrication and marine work, much of it to European or international standards, where ISO 9712-based certification is the norm.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Nova Scotia employers

Direct answer: Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in eight NDT methods and preparation for the ASNT Level III exams. The table shows how each method appears in Nova Scotia work and what a trainee needs first. Your employer's written practice sets the classroom and experience hours.

MethodLevelsWhat Nova Scotia employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepHull and structural welds, ship plate thickness gauging, power plant piping, pressure vessels for US customersLevel I: employer requirements. Level II: Level I training plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepEncoded weld inspection on heavy fabrication, corrosion mapping on plant piping and terminal equipmentUT Level II recommended first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-section welds on vessels and heavy structuresUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPiping and pressure-equipment welds, marine piping systems, pipeline weldsGamma work needs CNSC exposure device operator certification or direct supervision by a certified EDO
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepShip structures, cranes and lifting gear in the port, structural steel, rotating machineryEmployer requirements
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepStainless and aluminium marine fittings, pumps, valves, machined partsEmployer requirements
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual on fabrication and ship repair, tanks, in-service pressure equipmentEmployer requirements
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepHeat exchanger and condenser tubing at power stations, surface crack detectionEmployer requirements

Level III candidates can prepare for the ASNT Basic and method exams online through ASNT Level III training. Course detail is on pages such as UT Level 2 training, PAUT Level 2 training and VT Level 2 training. If your target is a CGSB Level 3, that follows the certification body's rules, and we will point you there.

NDT training by city in Nova Scotia

Direct answer: Atlantis has a dedicated NDT training page, a Practical NDT simulator page and an NDT ERP page for Halifax. The rest of the province is served the same way, with live online classes plus onsite delivery at the employer's site. We have no classroom in Nova Scotia.

City or areaMain NDT sectorsPages
Halifax and DartmouthNaval shipbuilding and repair, port, fabrication, aerospace maintenance, power, inspection companiesNDT training in Halifax; Halifax simulator practice; Halifax NDT ERP; Halifax NDT reporting software
Sydney and industrial Cape BretonCoal-fired power, port, fabricationServed online and onsite; ask about a Cape Breton cohort
Port Hawkesbury and Point TupperPaper mill, deep-water terminal, proposed hydrogen projectsServed online and onsite
New Glasgow, Trenton and TruroPower generation, manufacturing, fabricationServed online and onsite
Lunenburg and BridgewaterAerostructures, manufacturing, boatbuildingServed online and onsite
Annapolis ValleyManufacturing, food processingServed online and onsite

Halifax and Dartmouth. Most of the province's NDT technicians work here, and most of them work under CGSB on naval, defence and Canadian code work. SNT-TC-1A demand comes from fabricators and machine shops supplying US customers, marine contractors with US clients, and technicians preparing for jobs in the US. Halifax employers usually prefer onsite training in the shop so production does not stop.

Cape Breton. Power-plant outages and port work drive demand. Contractors that also travel to New England plant outages sometimes want an SNT-TC-1A programme alongside their CGSB-certified staff.

Strait of Canso and Pictou County. Mill, terminal and generating-station maintenance uses UT, MT, PT and ET during planned shutdowns. Live online theory plus a short onsite practical block fits that schedule.

South Shore and Valley. Smaller manufacturers often need only one or two qualified people and are best served by live online seats and simulator practice.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Nova Scotia, step by step

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you. You complete classroom training and documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. It is an employer certification, not a Canadian national certificate, and a new employer must recertify you.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A-based written practice. We can write it with you: written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete the hours your written practice sets, online or onsite. The training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method and level.
  3. Supervised experience. Build documented hours on real work, whether fabrication, marine repair or plant maintenance.
  4. Examinations. Pass the general, specific and practical exams under a Level III.
  5. Vision. Pass near-vision and colour contrast checks, usually every year.
  6. Certification. Your employer certifies you for the method and level.
  7. Recertification. Renew at the interval your written practice sets.

If you also need CGSB certification, record your experience in enough detail to satisfy both schemes from the start.

Radiography licensing and other Nova Scotia requirements

Direct answer: industrial gamma radiography in Nova Scotia is licensed federally by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission; operators must be certified exposure device operators or trainees under their direct supervision. Boilers and pressure equipment are regulated by the province's Technical Safety Division. Interprovincial pipelines are regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator, and offshore energy by the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Energy Regulator.

Industrial radiography

The CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices in every province; there is no US-style Agreement State system. Only a certified exposure device operator (EDO), or a trainee under the direct supervision and continuous observation of a certified EDO, may operate an exposure device. Certification follows the CNSC's REGDOC-2.2.3 and the CSA PCP-09 guide: formal vocational training, a supervised on-the-job programme and CNSC examinations. Atlantis RT training teaches radiographic principles, technique, interpretation and acceptance criteria, but it does not replace EDO certification and we do not run CNSC examinations. X-ray equipment falls under provincial rules; confirm current registration and worker requirements with your radiation safety officer.

Boilers and pressure equipment

Nova Scotia regulates boilers, pressure vessels, piping systems and fittings through the Technical Safety Division of the Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration, under the Technical Safety Act and its Boiler and Pressure Equipment Regulations. The older Boilers and Pressure Vessels Act was repealed as part of that change. Commonly referenced codes include CSA B51, ASME Sections I, V and VIII, and ASME B31.1 and B31.3. Whether SNT-TC-1A personnel are acceptable on a job depends on the code, the owner and the contractor's quality programme.

Pipelines and offshore

The natural gas transmission line that crosses Nova Scotia into New Brunswick and New England is regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator, with CSA Z662 as the core standard. Offshore activity is regulated by the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Energy Regulator, formerly the Canada-Nova Scotia Offshore Petroleum Board, whose mandate now includes offshore renewable energy. Offshore installations also involve third-party certifying authorities, and operators set their own personnel certification requirements, generally ISO 9712-based.

Marine, defence and other requirements

Classification societies and flag administrations set their own rules for ship repair NDT, and defence contracts carry DND and security requirements. Industrial sites typically require safety prequalification and orientation. Structural steel is fabricated by CWB-certified companies to CSA W59. None of these are replaced by our training; it fits alongside them for the work where SNT-TC-1A applies.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Nova Scotia

Direct answer: Atlantis trains Nova Scotia students through live online classes, private live-virtual cohorts and onsite delivery at the employer's facility, led by an ASNT Level III. Theory runs online, and practical sessions use real specimens at your site.

Nova Scotia's employers are mostly small and mid-sized, apart from the shipyard and the utility, and many can spare one or two people at a time. Live online seats let a technician in Sydney or Bridgewater join a class without a three-hour drive to Halifax. Larger crews get a private cohort and an onsite practical block. We schedule around local realities: power plant outages, shipyard production milestones, port and terminal maintenance windows, and winter storms that close the highways.

  • Live online seats for individuals anywhere in the province.
  • Private live-virtual cohorts for one company, built around its procedures and codes.
  • Onsite delivery at your Dartmouth shop, Cape Breton plant or South Shore factory, using your equipment and specimens.
  • Blended programmes with online theory, simulator practice and a short onsite practical.

We have no classroom in Nova Scotia. Ask about onsite training for your Nova Scotia crew, or read about online NDT training and corporate NDT training.

For Nova Scotia employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: a Nova Scotia employer that needs SNT-TC-1A certification for US-code or US-client work needs a written practice, a Level III to administer examinations, and records an auditor can follow. Atlantis provides these remotely or onsite, including for companies that keep CGSB-certified staff for their Canadian work.

The usual Nova Scotia request is a programme for a specific customer: a Dartmouth fabricator whose first US pressure-equipment order calls for SNT-TC-1A-certified examiners, a marine contractor bidding on US-owned vessel work, or an inspection company that wants a second certification track for staff who travel to US outages. We can:

  • write or update your SNT-TC-1A written practice (written practice development);
  • act as your outside Level III for examinations, procedure review and technique approval;
  • document which jobs use SNT-TC-1A personnel and which use CGSB personnel;
  • prepare your NDT programme for customer audits;
  • track certifications, training, vision tests and calibration in our NDT ERP, which handles CGSB and ASNT records together (see NDT ERP in Halifax).

Read SNT-TC-1A training and certification for employers or NDT consulting in Canada. Book a Level III consultation for your Nova Scotia programme.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator lets Nova Scotia trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments in a browser. It is practice only and does not replace the hands-on practical exam required by your written practice or by a CGSB scheme.

The welding workshop and storage tank environments suit Nova Scotia's fabrication, marine and terminal work, and the aircraft hangar environment gives aerospace trainees a feel for how methods are applied to airframes. Trainees can practise probe handling, scan planning and indication recognition from home before booking practical exam time. See Practical NDT or Practical NDT in Halifax, and try the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop writes the course material, the examinations and the employer written practices, and he is the Level III you speak with when you want an honest view of whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or both are right for your Nova Scotia work.

NDT training in Nova Scotia: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Nova Scotia?

Most Nova Scotia work, including shipbuilding and Canadian code work, needs CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification from an accredited certification body; confirm the current certification body, since arrangements changed in 2026. Work for US customers or US employers uses SNT-TC-1A employer certification, which is the route Atlantis trains for.

Is there NDT training online in Nova Scotia?

Yes. Live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes are open to technicians across the province. Practical training and exams happen on real specimens, usually at the employer's site. See NDT training online.

Can Atlantis training get me a job at the Halifax shipyard?

Not on its own. Naval shipbuilding and repair generally require CGSB-certified NDT personnel. Our training does not lead to CGSB certification, and we would rather tell you that now.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB or ISO 9712 training in Halifax?

No. We teach SNT-TC-1A only and claim no CGSB recognition.

Do I need a licence to do radiography in Nova Scotia?

For gamma radiography, yes. You must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator or a trainee under direct supervision, and your employer needs a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment is regulated provincially.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in Nova Scotia?

The Technical Safety Division of the Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration, under the Technical Safety Act and the Boiler and Pressure Equipment Regulations.

How much does NDT training cost in Nova Scotia?

It is quoted on request, based on method, level, number of trainees, delivery mode and any written practice or Level III work. Cohort and onsite quotes usually come back within one business day. Get a Nova Scotia training quote.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in Nova Scotia?

UT, MT and VT dominate shipbuilding, ship repair and fabrication. ET and PT matter in aerospace and power plants, and RT appears on piping and pressure-equipment welds.

Can you train our crew onsite in Dartmouth or Cape Breton?

Yes, subject to your site's safety and access rules. The instructor uses your equipment and specimens and supports practical exams under your written practice.

How long does UT Level II take?

Your written practice sets classroom and experience hours, using SNT-TC-1A recommendations as a baseline; see the training requirements matrix.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Nova Scotia?

Yes. Our Level III preparation for the Basic and method exams runs online.

What do NDT technicians earn in Nova Scotia?

Pay depends on sector, method, level and scheme. We do not publish our own figures; see the NDT salary guide.

Get a quote for NDT training in Nova Scotia

If you are a Dartmouth fabricator with a first US order, a marine contractor with a US client, a Cape Breton outage contractor building a cross-border crew, or a technician planning a move to US work, Atlantis NDT will build the programme around your work and schedule, and we will tell you straight away if CGSB is what you need instead. Request your Nova Scotia training quote, read about Atlantis NDT training, or see NDT training across Canada. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

NDT Training and Certification in Ohio

Short answer: an Ohio technician or employer gets ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual sessions, or onsite delivery at the employer's own plant, shop or turnaround site anywhere in the state. Courses cover Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, and every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Certification itself is issued by your employer under its written practice, and we help you build or tighten that written practice too.

Ohio is one of the busiest NDT states in the Midwest because it combines heavy steel, refining, nuclear power, aerospace engines, automotive assembly, shale gas and some of the most traffic-heavy river bridges in the country. That mix means Ohio employers ask for a wider spread of methods than most states: a Toledo refinery contractor wants UT thickness, PAUT and RT; a Cincinnati aerospace supplier wants PT, MT and ET under a tightly controlled written practice; a Youngstown pipe mill wants automated UT and MT; an eastern Ohio gathering-line contractor wants radiographers who understand API 1104. This page explains how training and certification work for each of those groups, what Ohio regulators expect, and how to get a quote for an individual seat or a whole crew. Request an Ohio NDT training quote and we reply with options within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Ohio

Direct answer: Ohio NDT work clusters in five areas: the Lake Erie industrial belt (Toledo refineries, Cleveland steel, the Davis-Besse and Perry nuclear stations), the Mahoning and Stark valleys (pipe mills and specialty steel), southwest Ohio (aerospace engines and Wright-Patterson Air Force Base), central Ohio (automotive, logistics and new advanced manufacturing) and the eastern Utica shale counties (gas gathering and processing).

Northwest Ohio and the Toledo refining corridor

Toledo and the neighbouring city of Oregon host two large refineries on the Maumee River and Lake Erie shoreline, along with terminals, a busy lake port and a dense ring of fabrication and mechanical contractors that support them. Refinery turnarounds here are the single largest seasonal draw for UT thickness, PAUT weld inspection, RT of new piping welds, PT and MT on repairs, and visual inspection of pressure equipment. Further south, Lima has its own refinery and the Joint Systems Manufacturing Center, a government-owned plant that builds armoured vehicles and depends on weld inspection. Contractors serving these sites usually work to ASME Section V for methods, ASME Section VIII for vessels and ASME B31.3 for process piping, with owner-specific procedures layered on top.

Northeast Ohio: Cleveland, Akron, Lorain and the nuclear stations

Cleveland remains a steel city, with integrated steelmaking on the Cuyahoga River, forge and casting shops across the region, and a large base of machine builders and valve, pump and fastener manufacturers. MT and PT of forgings and castings, UT of plate and bar, and ET of tubing are everyday work. NASA Glenn Research Center adds research-grade aerospace testing, and Akron's polymer and tyre industry supports its own maintenance and equipment inspection. Along the lake shore, the Davis-Besse station near Oak Harbor and the Perry station east of Cleveland are the state's two nuclear plants; outage work there is planned around ASME Section XI in-service inspection and draws qualified UT, ET and VT personnel from across the region.

Mahoning Valley and Stark County

Youngstown, Warren and Canton built their economies on steel, and seamless and welded pipe production, specialty bar and bearing steel, and heavy fabrication still employ NDT inspectors today. Pipe mills depend on automated UT and ET lines plus MT and visual end-inspection, and the people who calibrate, verify and sign off that automated equipment need solid Level II and Level III grounding. Canton also has a refinery, so the valley mixes mill inspection with downstream refinery work.

Southwest Ohio: Cincinnati and Dayton

The Cincinnati area is one of the largest jet-engine manufacturing and overhaul centres in the world, anchored by a major aircraft-engine maker in Evendale and surrounded by machine shops, forging houses and special-process suppliers. Those suppliers live on PT, MT, ET and UT performed under tightly controlled written practices, and their customers' quality systems often reference NAS 410 alongside SNT-TC-1A. Dayton is home to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base and the Air Force Research Laboratory, which pull in aerospace research, materials testing and defence-contractor work. Both cities also have power generation, chemical plants and Ohio River infrastructure.

Central Ohio: Columbus and the manufacturing ring

Columbus and its surrounding counties combine automotive assembly and powertrain plants northwest of the city, a large logistics and air-cargo base at Rickenbacker, research institutions, and large new advanced-manufacturing construction east of the city. Construction phases bring structural steel welding to AWS D1.1, pipe welding to ASME B31.3 and B31.9, and a steady demand for VT and UT inspectors who can work on fast-moving projects.

Eastern and southeastern Ohio: the Utica shale and the Ohio River

Counties such as Carroll, Harrison, Belmont, Monroe and Guernsey sit on the Utica and Point Pleasant shale. Gathering lines, compressor stations and gas processing plants there are built and maintained to API 1104 and ASME B31.8, which keeps radiographers, UT shear-wave inspectors and VT inspectors busy. The Ohio River corridor adds coal and gas-fired power plants, chemical plants, barge terminals and long-span bridges, including the major crossings at Cincinnati, Portsmouth and the eastern panhandle border with West Virginia.

Bridges, rail and transportation

Ohio has one of the largest bridge inventories in the country, and the Ohio Department of Transportation and county engineers commission fabrication inspection and in-service inspection of steel bridges. Fabrication work is typically done to the AASHTO/AWS D1.5 Bridge Welding Code, which leans heavily on UT and MT. Rail yards and car shops in Columbus, Toledo and Cleveland add axle, wheel and weld inspection work.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Ohio, step by step

Direct answer: under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, certification in Ohio is employer-based. Your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. There is no separate Ohio state NDT licence, except radiation safety rules for RT.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. This document, based on SNT-TC-1A, sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks, vision requirements, and recertification intervals for each method and level. If your company does not have one, we write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Take Level I and then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Training hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours per method and level.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience. Log supervised experience hours in the method at your Ohio workplace. Hours must be documented and verified by your employer.
  4. Pass the general exam. A closed-book written exam on the principles of the method.
  5. Pass the specific exam. Covers the procedures, codes, specifications and equipment you will actually use, for example ASME Section V, AWS D1.1 or API 1104.
  6. Pass the practical exam. Hands-on demonstration on real specimens with real flaws, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Pass the vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast checks, repeated at the interval in the written practice.
  8. Get certified by your employer. Your employer issues the certification based on documented training, experience and exams. Certification is tied to that employer.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Recertify at the interval set in your written practice, keep your vision test current, and add methods or levels as your career develops.

For more detail on how the employer-based system works, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Ohio requirements

Direct answer: Ohio is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the Ohio Department of Health's Bureau of Environmental Health and Radiation Protection under the Ohio Administrative Code, not directly by the NRC. Boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Ohio Department of Commerce; intrastate gas pipeline safety under the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio.

Industrial radiography

Ohio became an Agreement State in 1999, which means the state, rather than the NRC, licenses most uses of radioactive material inside Ohio. Companies performing gamma radiography with sources such as iridium-192 or cobalt-60 need an Ohio radioactive materials licence, and their radiographers and radiographer's assistants must meet the training, examination and supervision requirements in the state's industrial radiography rules, which mirror the federal requirements in 10 CFR Part 34. That includes radiation safety training, a radiation safety exam, a period as a radiographer's assistant under supervision, and recognised radiographer certification. X-ray equipment used for industrial radiography is also registered and inspected by the state. Out-of-state companies working in Ohio generally use reciprocity. RT method training under SNT-TC-1A, which is what Atlantis provides, covers film and digital technique, exposure calculation and interpretation; it sits alongside, not instead of, the radiation safety training Ohio requires. Always confirm current requirements with the Ohio Department of Health before deploying a crew.

Boilers and pressure vessels

Ohio's boiler and pressure vessel programme is run by the Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Industrial Compliance. Ohio adopts the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board inspection rules, so repair and alteration work on boilers and vessels needs NDT performed to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme. That is one reason Ohio R-stamp and fabrication shops care so much about a clean, auditable written practice.

Pipelines

Interstate pipelines are regulated by PHMSA. Intrastate gas pipeline safety in Ohio is overseen by the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio, which enforces federal pipeline safety rules for intrastate operators. Pipeline welding inspection commonly follows API 1104, with ASME B31.8 for gas transmission and gathering, and operators expect radiographers and UT technicians qualified to their procedures.

Codes Ohio employers commonly use

  • ASME Section V (NDT methods), Section VIII (pressure vessels) and B31.3 (process piping) in refining and chemicals
  • ASME Section XI for in-service inspection at the Davis-Besse and Perry nuclear stations
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for bridge fabrication
  • API 1104 and ASME B31.8 for pipelines in the shale counties
  • NAS 410 as context for aerospace suppliers in the Cincinnati and Dayton supply chain (Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A; your employer documents any additional aerospace requirements)

Some Ohio employers also ask for API inspector or CWI credentials for specific roles. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train; our programmes focus on ASNT SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Ohio

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Ohio. Instead, theory is delivered through live online or live-virtual classes, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility, using your equipment and specimens under ASNT Level III oversight. That model lets Ohio crews train without travelling and without losing shifts.

For individual technicians, online NDT training covers the classroom portion of Level I and Level II. You attend live sessions with a Level III instructor, ask questions in real time, and work through method principles, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation. Practical hours and the practical exam are then completed with your employer or at an employer-arranged facility.

For Ohio employers training a group, onsite delivery is usually the most efficient option. We schedule classroom and practical sessions at your plant, shop or project site, use your own instruments, reference standards and part samples, and build the course around the procedures your crew actually follows. A Cleveland forge shop gets MT and PT on its own parts; a Toledo contractor gets UT and PAUT on piping mock-ups; a Youngstown mill gets UT and ET sessions built around its inspection lines.

Ohio's industrial calendar shapes scheduling. Refinery turnarounds in Toledo, Lima and Canton cluster in spring and fall; nuclear outages follow each plant's refuelling cycle; bridge and construction work peaks in the warmer months; aerospace and manufacturing plants often have holiday or summer shutdowns. We plan cohorts to finish before the busy window, so certified technicians are ready when the work starts. Larger programmes run through corporate NDT training. For Ohio employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A puts responsibility for certification on the employer, so every Ohio NDT employer needs a written practice and access to a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams, and provides Level III services for companies that do not have one in-house.

Many Ohio NDT employers are small: a fabrication shop in Canton, a foundry in the Mahoning Valley, a machine shop in the Cincinnati aerospace chain, a mechanical contractor in Toledo. They need certified technicians but cannot justify a full-time Level III. That gap is where most audit findings come from: training records without hour counts, practical exams with no graded checklist, vision tests out of date, or a written practice copied from another company that does not match how work is actually done.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT simulator lets Ohio trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before their practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique, scanning patterns and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank environment. That spread matches Ohio work closely: the welding workshop for fabrication and bridge steel, the hangar for the Cincinnati and Dayton aerospace chain, the oil and gas site for Toledo and Lima refinery work and shale gathering lines, and the tank for terminal inspection. Trainees can repeat scans, explore indication types and get comfortable with the workflow before handling real equipment in front of an examiner.

NDT training in Ohio: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Ohio?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. Complete Level I and Level II classroom training in a method, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then issues certification under its written practice. If you are not yet employed, online classroom training prepares you, but certification follows once an employer documents your experience.

Is there NDT training online in Ohio?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online and live-virtual Level I and Level II classes that Ohio technicians can join from anywhere in the state. Practical training and practical exams are completed onsite with your employer, since they need real equipment and real specimens.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Ohio?

Ohio is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the Ohio Department of Health. The company holds the licence, and individual radiographers and assistants must meet state training, exam, supervision and certification requirements equivalent to 10 CFR Part 34. Confirm current requirements with the department before starting work.

How much does NDT training cost in Ohio?

Cost is quoted on request. It depends on the method and level, the number of trainees, whether classroom sessions are live online or onsite, and whether you need exam administration or written practice support. Send your requirements and we return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Ohio?

UT is the broadest, used in refining, steel, bridges and pipe mills. PAUT is growing fast in refinery and construction inspection. MT and PT are essential in Cleveland, Canton and Cincinnati manufacturing and aerospace, and RT stays in demand on shale-area pipelines and refinery piping.

Can you train our crew onsite in Toledo, Cleveland or Cincinnati?

Yes. We deliver classroom and practical sessions at your facility anywhere in Ohio, using your equipment and specimens, and schedule around turnarounds, outages and production shutdowns.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Ohio employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer certification in US industry, including refining, power, fabrication and many aerospace suppliers. Some customers add their own requirements, which your written practice can document.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums; see the training requirements matrix. Experience hours usually take much longer than classroom training.

Can I become a Level III in Ohio?

Yes. Level III candidates typically hold Level II experience and prepare for the ASNT Level III basic and method exams. See ASNT Level III training for exam preparation options.

Do you offer API 510 or CWI training in Ohio?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some Ohio employers ask for API or CWI credentials for specific roles, but those are separate programmes.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Ohio?

No. We deliver training live online and onsite at your facility, which avoids travel and lets crews train on their own equipment.

Can a small Ohio shop get help with its written practice?

Yes. We write or revise written practices, administer exams and provide Level III services for shops without an in-house Level III. See written practice development.

NDT Training and Certification in Oklahoma

Short answer: Oklahoma technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual sessions, or onsite delivery at their own fabrication shop, refinery, pipeline yard or hangar. We offer Level I and II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation, all led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Your employer certifies you under its written practice, and we help build or tighten that written practice.

Oklahoma is an energy and aviation state. Cushing, in Payne County, is one of the most important crude-oil storage and pipeline hubs in the world; five refineries operate in Tulsa, Ponca City, Ardmore and Wynnewood; gathering lines, gas processing plants and compressor stations cover the Anadarko and Arkoma basins; and Tulsa has a long tradition of heat exchanger, pressure vessel and process equipment fabrication. On the aviation side, Tinker Air Force Base in Midwest City runs one of the largest military aircraft depots in the country, Tulsa hosts one of the world's largest airline maintenance bases, and Oklahoma City is home to the FAA's Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center. Each of those sectors needs certified NDT people. This page explains how training and certification work in Oklahoma, what state regulators require, where the work is and how to get a quote. Request an Oklahoma NDT training quote and we reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Oklahoma

Direct answer: Oklahoma NDT work clusters in the Tulsa fabrication, refining and airline-maintenance corridor; the Oklahoma City military and civil aviation complex; the Cushing crude hub; the refinery towns of Ponca City, Ardmore and Wynnewood; the oil and gas basins of western and southern Oklahoma; and the military installations at Lawton, Altus and Enid.

Tulsa and Green Country

Tulsa grew up as the "Oil Capital of the World" and still carries that industrial base. The Tulsa area is one of the country's best-known centres for heat exchanger, air-cooled exchanger, pressure vessel, skid and process equipment fabrication, much of it built to ASME Section VIII and shipped to refineries and gas plants worldwide. Those shops need RT, UT, PAUT, MT, PT and VT technicians certified under written practices that satisfy ASME code customers and authorised inspectors. Tulsa's refinery complex adds turnaround work, and the airline maintenance base at Tulsa International Airport, together with aerospace suppliers in the area, brings ET, PT, MT and UT under aviation quality systems. The Port of Catoosa on the McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System supports heavy fabrication that ships out by barge.

Oklahoma City and Midwest City

Tinker Air Force Base is home to a major Air Force air logistics complex that overhauls tanker, bomber, airborne-surveillance and engine fleets. Depot maintenance work involves ET, PT, MT, UT and RT on aircraft structures and engine components, much of it to military technical orders, and the defence contractors around the base need certified personnel. Oklahoma City also hosts the FAA's Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center, a broad aerospace supplier base, and energy company headquarters with field operations across the state. Construction, power generation and transportation projects add VT, UT and MT demand.

Cushing and the crude-oil pipeline crossroads

Cushing is a delivery point for US crude futures and holds a vast concentration of crude storage tanks and pipeline interconnects. Tank construction and repair, tank bottom and shell inspection, pipeline construction and integrity digs keep UT thickness, VT, MT and RT technicians busy. Pipelines radiate from Cushing in all directions, so construction and maintenance contractors throughout central Oklahoma need radiographers and UT technicians qualified to API 1104.

The refinery towns: Ponca City, Ardmore and Wynnewood

Ponca City in the north, and Ardmore and Wynnewood in southern Oklahoma, each host a refinery, along with the mechanical contractors and inspection companies that support them. Turnarounds bring heavy seasonal demand for UT thickness and corrosion mapping, PAUT and RT of piping welds, ET of exchanger tubing, VT of pressure equipment and MT/PT on repairs, generally to ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3.

Western and southern Oklahoma oil and gas

The Anadarko Basin, the SCOOP and STACK plays and older fields across the state support gathering lines, compressor stations, gas processing plants and saltwater disposal systems. Midstream construction and maintenance follows API 1104 and ASME B31.4 and B31.8, with RT, UT and VT on pipeline welds and UT thickness on facilities. Oilfield equipment makers and repair shops in towns such as Oklahoma City, Elk City, Enid and Duncan use MT, UT and PT on drill pipe, pressure-control equipment and pumping units.

Military installations: Lawton, Altus and Enid

Fort Sill near Lawton is a major Army installation, Altus Air Force Base trains aircrews on heavy transport and tanker aircraft, and Vance Air Force Base in Enid trains pilots. Aircraft maintenance contractors at the air bases need ET, PT and UT technicians, and Lawton's manufacturing base adds MT and UT work.

Power, wind and infrastructure

Oklahoma has a large fleet of gas-fired power plants, hydroelectric dams on the Grand River and Arkansas River systems, and one of the largest installed wind generation capacities in the country. Power plant outages bring UT, PAUT, ET and VT work, wind towers need weld and bolt inspection, and the Oklahoma Department of Transportation's bridge programme adds AWS D1.5 fabrication inspection.

Enid and AltusAir bases, oilfield services, agriculture equipmentOnline and onsite (no city page)

Oklahoma City. Military depot maintenance at Tinker and the contractors and suppliers around it make Oklahoma City the state's aerospace NDT centre. Employers need ET, PT, MT and UT technicians with clean, auditable records. Energy companies and construction projects add pipeline, facility and structural work. See the Oklahoma City NDT training page.

Tulsa. Tulsa's fabrication shops build heat exchangers, pressure vessels and process skids to ASME Section VIII, so RT, UT, PAUT, MT, PT and VT are all in daily use, and authorised inspectors expect solid written practices. The airline maintenance base adds a large aviation NDT workforce, and Tulsa refineries add turnaround work. See the Tulsa NDT training page.

Lawton. Fort Sill and the manufacturing base in Lawton generate steady VT, MT and UT work, and southwest Oklahoma oil and gas operations add pipeline inspection.

Ponca City. The refinery and associated pipelines in Ponca City drive turnaround demand for UT, PAUT, RT, ET and VT, with contractors often training cohorts just before the season.

Cushing. Tank and pipeline work dominates: UT thickness surveys, VT and MT on tank repairs, RT and UT on new pipeline welds. Contractors typically train crews onsite at their yards.

Ardmore and Wynnewood. Southern Oklahoma's refineries and surrounding oil and gas operations need refinery inspection and pipeline NDT, generally served by contractors who also work in north Texas.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Oklahoma, step by step

Direct answer: NDT certification in Oklahoma is employer-based under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. Radiography adds Oklahoma DEQ radiation safety requirements.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A. We can write it: written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Level I, then Level II, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; see the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. On-the-job experience. Documented, supervised hours in the method.
  4. General exam on method principles.
  5. Specific exam on your procedures, codes and equipment, such as ASME Section V and VIII, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or aviation procedures.
  6. Practical exam on flawed specimens, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision exam for near-vision acuity and colour contrast.
  8. Employer certification based on documented training, experience and exams.
  9. Recertification at the interval in your written practice.

Read more on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Oklahoma requirements

Direct answer: Oklahoma is an NRC Agreement State; its agreement took effect in September 2000. The Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality's Radiation Management section licenses radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, and regulates industrial X-ray equipment. Boilers fall under the Oklahoma Department of Labor; intrastate pipelines under the Oklahoma Corporation Commission.

Industrial radiography

Because Oklahoma is an Agreement State, radiography companies working with sources such as iridium-192 hold an Oklahoma DEQ licence rather than an NRC licence, and industrial X-ray machines are registered with DEQ. Oklahoma's rules follow the federal model in 10 CFR Part 34: radiographers and radiographer's assistants must complete radiation safety training and exams, work under supervision as assistants, hold recognised radiographer certification, wear dosimetry and use calibrated survey meters. Companies licensed by the NRC or another Agreement State can work in Oklahoma under reciprocity when their licence allows. Atlantis RT training under SNT-TC-1A covers technique, exposure and film and digital interpretation; it complements but does not replace the radiation safety training and radiographer certification required by Oklahoma rules. Confirm current requirements with DEQ before a crew mobilises.

Boilers and pressure vessels

The Oklahoma Department of Labor's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Division administers the state's boiler and pressure vessel programme, applying ASME and National Board rules. For Tulsa's many ASME Section VIII fabricators and repair organisations, NDT must be performed to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the shop's quality programme, which makes a clear written practice essential.

Pipelines

Interstate pipelines are regulated by PHMSA. The Oklahoma Corporation Commission's pipeline safety programme oversees intrastate gas and hazardous liquid pipelines. Pipeline construction and repair welds are inspected to API 1104, with ASME B31.4 and B31.8 for design, so radiographers and UT technicians qualified to operator procedures are in steady demand.

Aviation and military

Depot, airline and FAA repair station work sets its own NDT personnel requirements, often referencing NAS 410 or military technical orders. Atlantis provides SNT-TC-1A method training as a foundation; employers manage any additional programme qualifications.

Codes Oklahoma employers commonly use

  • ASME Section V and Section VIII for pressure vessels and heat exchangers
  • ASME B31.3 in refineries and gas plants
  • API 1104 and ASME B31.4/B31.8 for pipelines
  • AWS D1.1 for structural welds and AWS D1.5 for bridges
  • NAS 410 and military technical orders as aviation context

Some Oklahoma employers also ask for API inspector or CWI credentials; those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Oklahoma

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Oklahoma. Classroom training is delivered live online or live-virtual, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility, using your equipment and specimens, under ASNT Level III oversight.

Individual technicians use online NDT training for Level I and II classroom hours, with live sessions led by a Level III covering principles, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation. Practical hours and exams happen with your employer.

Employers with a group usually prefer onsite delivery. We run classroom and practical sessions at your shop, yard, plant or hangar and use your instruments, reference blocks and parts. A Tulsa exchanger shop trains RT and PAUT on its own nozzle and tube-sheet welds; a Cushing contractor trains UT thickness and VT on tank components; an Oklahoma City aerospace supplier trains ET and PT on its own parts.

Oklahoma scheduling follows refinery turnarounds in spring and fall, pipeline construction seasons, tornado season in spring, and depot and airline maintenance schedules. We plan cohorts to finish before each busy window and can switch sessions to live online if weather intervenes. Multi-site programmes run through corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Oklahoma crew.

For Oklahoma employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: every Oklahoma employer certifying NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and Level III oversight. Atlantis NDT writes and revises written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams and provides Level III services for companies without an in-house Level III.

Many Oklahoma fabricators, pipeline contractors and oilfield equipment shops employ certified technicians without a full-time Level III. Authorised inspectors, operators and aviation customers regularly find the same gaps: training hours not documented, practical exams without graded checklists, expired vision tests, and written practices that do not match how work is actually done.

  • Written practice development to the current SNT-TC-1A edition and your customers' requirements: written practice development.
  • Exam administration under Level III oversight with traceable records.
  • Procedure review against ASME, API and AWS.
  • Audit preparation for ASME, National Board, operator and ISO 9001 audits.
  • Corporate programmes via corporate NDT training.

See also NDT consulting in Oklahoma and SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Oklahoma company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Practical NDT simulator lets Oklahoma trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before their practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace a practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. Those map closely to Oklahoma work: the welding workshop to Tulsa fabrication, the oil and gas site to refineries and pipelines, the storage tank to Cushing, and the hangar to Tinker and Tulsa aviation maintenance. See Practical NDT in Oklahoma and the city pages for Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Lawton and Ponca City. For written-exam practice, use UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Direct answer: Oklahoma programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop designs the courses, leads instruction and oversees exams and records so certification holds up under SNT-TC-1A and customer audits. He connects method theory to the codes, procedures and parts your Oklahoma crew uses. Ask about scheduling an Oklahoma programme.

NDT training in Oklahoma: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Oklahoma?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after classroom training, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and a vision test. Online training covers the classroom portion; practical work and exams happen with your employer.

Is there NDT training online in Oklahoma?

Yes. Atlantis runs live online and live-virtual Level I and II classes that Oklahoma technicians can join from anywhere in the state.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Oklahoma?

Oklahoma is an Agreement State. The radiography company needs an Oklahoma DEQ licence (or X-ray registration), and radiographers and assistants must meet state training, exam, supervision and certification requirements. Confirm current rules with DEQ's Radiation Management section.

How much does NDT training cost in Oklahoma?

Quoted on request. Cost depends on method and level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery and any written practice or exam support. We return a quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Oklahoma?

UT and RT lead because of pipelines, refineries and pressure vessel fabrication, and PAUT is growing in Tulsa shops. ET and PT are essential in Oklahoma City and Tulsa aviation maintenance.

Can you train our crew onsite in Tulsa, Oklahoma City or Cushing?

Yes. We deliver onsite anywhere in Oklahoma, on your equipment and parts, scheduled around turnarounds, pipeline projects and maintenance schedules.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Oklahoma employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most common basis for employer certification in Oklahoma fabrication, refining and pipeline work. Aviation employers may add NAS 410 or military requirements.

How long does Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and the method. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.

Can I work at Tinker AFB with SNT-TC-1A certification?

Military depot and contractor programmes set their own requirements, often referencing NAS 410 and technical orders. SNT-TC-1A method training is a common foundation; check the specific employer's requirements.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Oklahoma?

No. Training is delivered live online and onsite at your facility.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in Oklahoma?

Yes. See ASNT Level III training for online exam preparation.

Do you offer API 653 or CWI training in Oklahoma?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only, although many Cushing tank contractors also employ API-certified inspectors.
