NDT Training and Certification in Ontario

Short answer: Ontario employers and technicians can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, private live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at their own plant, shop or yard. We teach Level I and II in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every course, and your employer certifies you under its written practice.

Here is the honest part first. Canada's national NDT certification scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian version of ISO 9712, and most Canadian code work in Ontario is written around it. Ontario's nuclear sector, CWB-certified structural fabricators and many provincial and municipal owners ask for it. Atlantis NDT does not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712, and we do not claim any CGSB recognition. Our training follows the American employer-based scheme, SNT-TC-1A. Ontario sits right on the border with Michigan, Ohio and New York, and many Ontario companies sell across it. That creates a real group of people for whom SNT-TC-1A is the right choice: fabricators building ASME- or API-code equipment for US plants, suppliers to US automotive, aerospace and energy customers, US-owned operators with sites on both sides of the border, inspection companies sending crews to Detroit, Toledo or Buffalo, and technicians who plan to work in the US. This page explains where that fit is real, maps Ontario's NDT economy region by region, and shows how to request an Ontario NDT training quote. We usually reply within one business day.

SNT-TC-1A or CAN/CGSB-48.9712: what Ontario employers actually ask for

Direct answer: for Canadian-code work in Ontario, including nuclear, CSA W59 structural steel, and much provincially regulated pressure equipment, expect CAN/CGSB-48.9712 to be required or preferred. SNT-TC-1A is what US clients, ASME-stamped work for US sites, API 1104 cross-border pipeline projects and US employers expect. Many Ontario technicians end up holding both.

Ontario situationScheme usually expectedDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
Nuclear plant inspections and nuclear component manufacturing to CSA N285 standardsCAN/CGSB-48.9712, plus the licensee's own qualification rulesNo. Use a CGSB route; our training can add background only
Structural steel and bridges under CSA W59 / CSA S6 through CWB-certified companiesCAN/CGSB-48.9712 through CSA W178.1 inspection organisationsNo, not on its own
Sarnia or Nanticoke refinery work for an owner that accepts SNT-TC-1A in its specificationOwner specification (CGSB or SNT)Yes, where the owner accepts it
ASME Section VIII vessels, B31.3 spools or heat exchangers built in Ontario for US sitesSNT-TC-1A through ASME Section V and the clientYes. This is the core case
Automotive and aerospace suppliers shipping to US OEMsCustomer specification, often SNT-TC-1A, sometimes NAS 410 for aerospaceSNT-TC-1A yes; NAS 410 programmes need their own route, which we do not offer
Ontario crews working Michigan, Ohio or New York turnaroundsThe US employer's SNT-TC-1A written practiceYes

The Canadian scheme is also in transition. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Published guidance says the standard stays valid through its current cycle and that existing certificates are unaffected. Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body has said its certification services continue without interruption, and the CWB Group remains accredited to certify NDT personnel to the same standard. Before you build a CGSB plan, confirm the current certification body. Our part is SNT-TC-1A. If a job needs a CGSB certificate, we will tell you so before you spend money on the wrong course.

Where NDT technicians work in Ontario

Direct answer: Ontario NDT work is spread across seven clusters. They are Sarnia-Lambton's Chemical Valley, the nuclear stations on Lake Huron and Lake Ontario, Hamilton's steel and fabrication base, the Nanticoke industrial park, the Greater Toronto Area's aerospace, transit and manufacturing economy, the automotive belt from Windsor to Oshawa, and the mining and smelting districts of Sudbury and the north.

Sarnia-Lambton: Chemical Valley and the border crossing

Sarnia and the surrounding townships of St. Clair and Moore form Ontario's largest refining and petrochemical cluster. Three refineries operate there, alongside polymer, rubber, chemical and specialty plants, a deep-water port and pipeline terminals tied to the US Midwest. Enbridge Gas's Dawn storage hub sits just to the east, near Dawn-Euphemia. Turnarounds bring heavy demand for UT thickness and PAUT corrosion mapping, TOFD on heavy-wall vessels, RT of piping repairs, ET of exchanger bundles, and MT and PT on rotating equipment. Sarnia is connected to Port Huron, Michigan by the Blue Water Bridge, and contractors cross in both directions. That is exactly where SNT-TC-1A certification earns its keep. See NDT training in Sarnia and Sarnia Level III consulting.

Ontario's nuclear fleet: Bruce, Darlington and Pickering

Ontario runs a large share of Canada's nuclear generation. Bruce Power's site at Tiverton on Lake Huron, OPG's Darlington station in Clarington, and the Pickering station east of Toronto support refurbishment and major component replacement projects, outage inspection programmes, and a supply chain of fabricators and component makers across Durham Region, Peterborough, Cambridge and the GTA. OPG's small modular reactor project at the Darlington site adds new-build work. Nuclear inspection work is done to the CSA N285 series, under CNSC licensing and the operator's own qualification programmes, and it normally requires CGSB-certified personnel. Atlantis does not position SNT-TC-1A training as a route into Canadian nuclear inspection. Nuclear suppliers who also build for US utilities, where ASME Section III and Section XI apply, are a different case. They often run an SNT-TC-1A programme for that US work. For background, see power generation NDT training for the Toronto area.

Hamilton, Niagara and the Golden Horseshoe

Hamilton's integrated steel mills, structural and plate fabricators, and port industries make it one of the most NDT-intensive cities in Canada. Steel mill maintenance means UT on rolls, shafts and crane girders, MT on structural welds, and thickness surveys on furnace and gas systems. The Niagara Peninsula adds hydroelectric stations at Queenston, with penstocks, gates and turbine parts needing periodic UT, MT and VT, as well as Welland Canal infrastructure and shipyard work at Port Weller. Many Hamilton and Niagara shops ship pressure equipment and fabrications to US buyers across the Peace Bridge and the Queenston-Lewiston crossing. Related pages: Hamilton NDT consulting and Hamilton simulator practice.

Nanticoke and Haldimand County

The Nanticoke industrial area on Lake Erie has a refinery and a large steel works. Both rely on outage and turnaround inspection: UT and PAUT on piping and vessels, RT on repair welds, and MT and VT on structures and lifting equipment. Contractors from Hamilton, Brantford and Simcoe staff much of this work.

Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area

The GTA is Ontario's largest market for manufacturing and maintenance inspection, though not for heavy process plant. Aerospace companies in Mississauga, Brampton, Ajax and around Pearson airport build landing gear, structures and systems and maintain aircraft, so PT, MT, ET and UT are routine. Many of these customers follow NAS 410 or prime-specific rules, which Atlantis can discuss but does not train toward. Transit construction and maintenance, bridges and highway structures, data centres, and commercial building steel add structural UT and MT under CSA W59. Food, pharmaceutical and chemical plants across Peel, York and Durham have pressure vessels and piping inspected under TSSA rules. See Practical NDT in Toronto and Toronto Level III consulting.

The automotive belt: Windsor to Oshawa

Vehicle assembly plants in Windsor, Oakville, Alliston, Cambridge, Woodstock, Ingersoll and Oshawa, together with hundreds of parts suppliers and the new battery and EV supply chain, use NDT on castings, forgings, welds and bonded joints. ET and UT check heat treatment, weld quality and wall thickness, and PT and MT check castings and forgings. Windsor faces Detroit across the river, and many suppliers work under US customer quality systems that reference SNT-TC-1A.

Sudbury, Timmins and northern Ontario

Greater Sudbury is one of the world's major nickel and copper mining and smelting centres. The Timmins, Red Lake and Hemlo gold camps, the pulp and paper towns, and Thunder Bay's rail-car manufacturing and grain port add more work. Mining and processing equipment, hoists, headframes, crushers, haul trucks and smelter vessels need MT and UT on welds, shafts and structures, plus thickness surveys on process piping. Employers here are usually far from any classroom, so online theory plus onsite practicals makes sense. See Practical NDT in Sudbury.

Ottawa and eastern Ontario

Ottawa has defence, aerospace, electronics and research laboratories. Eastern Ontario adds chemical and manufacturing plants along the St. Lawrence corridor. Typical work includes PT and ET on precision components and UT and MT on structural and pressure equipment. See Practical NDT in Ottawa.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Ontario employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table maps each method to typical Ontario work. Your employer's written practice sets the exact training and experience hours.

MethodLevelsWhat Ontario employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepSarnia and Nanticoke thickness surveys, steel mill shafts and rolls, weld inspection on US-bound vessels and spoolsLevel I: employer requirements only. Level II: Level I training plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepRefinery corrosion mapping, encoded weld scans on pressure equipment for US clientsUT Level II recommended first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepHeavy-wall vessels and reactors in Chemical Valley, thick fabrication weldsUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPiping repair welds, pipeline tie-ins, shop RT of ASME weldsGamma work requires CNSC exposure device operator certification or direct supervision by a certified EDO
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepSteel mill and mining equipment, forgings, castings, crane and structural weldsEmployer requirements only
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepAerospace and automotive parts, stainless piping, valves, castingsEmployer requirements only
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual on US-code fabrication, in-service pressure equipment and tanksEmployer requirements only
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepRefinery exchanger tubing, aircraft maintenance, heat-treatment and conductivity checks on automotive and aerospace partsEmployer requirements only

Level III candidates can prepare for the ASNT Basic and method examinations online with our ASNT Level III training. A CGSB Level 3 follows the certification body's requirements and is outside our scope.

NDT training by city in Ontario

Direct answer: Atlantis has a dedicated NDT training page for Sarnia, a power-generation training page for the Toronto area, and Practical NDT simulator pages for Toronto, Hamilton, Ottawa, Sudbury and Sarnia. Every Ontario city is served the same way, with live online classes and onsite delivery at the employer's site. We have no Ontario classroom.

City or regionMain NDT sectorsPages
Sarnia-LambtonRefining, petrochemicals, pipelines, cross-border contractingSarnia NDT training; Sarnia simulator
Toronto / GTAAerospace, power generation, transit, manufacturing, building steelToronto power-sector NDT training; Toronto simulator
Hamilton and NiagaraSteel, fabrication, hydro, shipyardsHamilton simulator practice; Hamilton consulting
Sudbury and the northMining, smelting, mining equipment fabricationSudbury simulator
OttawaAerospace, defence, research, manufacturingOttawa simulator
Windsor, London, Kitchener-Waterloo, OshawaAutomotive, EV supply chain, nuclear components, general fabricationOnline and onsite; ask about a cohort

Sarnia. Contractors here run turnaround-driven programmes and often hold work on both sides of the St. Clair River. A typical Sarnia request is UT and PAUT Level II for a turnaround crew, plus a written practice that a US owner's auditor will accept.

Toronto. GTA requests are more varied: PT and ET for aerospace and automotive suppliers, NDT awareness and Level II theory for quality engineers, and Level III preparation for people who sign off procedures. Expect your customer's specification to decide the scheme.

Hamilton. Fabricators building pressure equipment and structures for US buyers are the main audience. Training usually runs onsite in the shop, around production, with practical specimens from the shop's own weld procedures.

Sudbury and northern Ontario. Mining employers usually want MT and UT Level II for maintenance staff. Distance makes live online theory and a short onsite practical block the sensible model.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Ontario, step by step

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A, an Ontario employer certifies its own technicians. You complete the classroom hours and documented experience set by the employer's written practice, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. The certification belongs to that employer's programme. It is not a national Canadian certificate.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A written practice that sets hours, exams and recertification. We can write or update it: written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete the formal hours your written practice requires, live online or onsite. The training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommendations by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience. Log supervised experience in the method on real work, with records your employer keeps.
  4. General, specific and practical exams. Theory, your employer's procedures and codes, and hands-on specimens, all administered under a Level III.
  5. Vision test. Near-vision and colour contrast, normally annual.
  6. Certification by the employer. The employer certifies you for the method and level. A new employer must recertify you under its own practice.
  7. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets.

If you are also pursuing CGSB certification, keep one clean experience log that can serve both schemes, and check the certification body's evidence rules early.

Radiography licensing and other Ontario requirements

Direct answer: gamma radiography in Ontario is federally regulated by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. Operators must be CNSC-certified exposure device operators or be directly supervised by one. Industrial X-ray equipment falls under Ontario's X-ray safety rules under the Occupational Health and Safety Act. Boilers, pressure vessels and many pipelines are administered by TSSA.

Industrial radiography

Canada has no Agreement State system, so the CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices across Ontario. Operating an exposure device requires CNSC exposure device operator (EDO) certification or direct supervision by a certified EDO. CNSC guidance describes formal EDO vocational training and a supervised on-the-job programme before the written exam, with CSA PCP-09 as the certification guide. Atlantis RT training covers technique, image quality, interpretation and code acceptance. It does not replace EDO certification. X-ray generators are registered and controlled provincially, and your radiation safety officer will know the current Ontario requirements.

Boilers and pressure vessels: TSSA

The Technical Standards and Safety Authority administers the Technical Standards and Safety Act for the Province, including its boilers and pressure vessels regulation and its oil and gas pipeline systems regulation. TSSA rules cover design registration, construction, repairs, alterations and in-service inspection, with CSA B51 and the ASME code sections as the main technical references. Inspection companies working in Ontario should read our TSSA compliance guide. Check with TSSA and the owner which NDE personnel certification they accept for each job.

Nuclear

Nuclear power plants are licensed by the CNSC, and periodic and in-service inspection follows the CSA N285 series. The licensee's qualification programme governs NDT personnel, and CGSB certification is the normal baseline. This work is outside the scope of Atlantis training.

Pipelines and codes used in Ontario

Interprovincial and international pipelines, including lines crossing at Sarnia and Windsor, fall under the Canada Energy Regulator. Intra-provincial oil and gas pipelines are covered by TSSA's regulation, with CSA Z662 as the core standard. API 1104 still appears on projects with US owners or contractors. Other codes common in Ontario include ASME Section V, VIII and IX, ASME B31.1 and B31.3, CSA W59 and CSA S6 for structures and bridges, and AWS D1.1 for US-bound structural work.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Ontario

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers Ontario training as live online seats for individuals, private live-virtual cohorts for one employer, or onsite training at your plant or shop led by a Level III. Practical sessions use real specimens, usually your own, at your site.

Ontario is large. The trip from Windsor to Sudbury is longer than many cross-border hops, and the province's NDT employers range from a Sarnia contractor with a big turnaround crew to a Thunder Bay shop with two inspectors. Online theory removes the travel. Onsite practicals keep training tied to the procedures and parts your technicians actually inspect. We schedule around spring and fall turnaround seasons in Chemical Valley and Nanticoke, steel mill and smelter outages, automotive model-year changeovers and summer shutdowns.

  • Live online seats for individuals anywhere in Ontario.
  • Private live-virtual cohorts built around your codes and procedures.
  • Onsite at your facility with your equipment and specimens, including practical exam support under your written practice.
  • Blended online theory, simulator practice and a short onsite practical block.

We have no Ontario classroom and do not suggest otherwise. Ask about onsite training for your Ontario crew, or read about online NDT training and corporate programmes.

For Ontario employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Ontario employers that need SNT-TC-1A certification for US customers or US-code work need a written practice, a Level III for examinations and procedure approval, and audit-ready records. Atlantis provides these remotely or onsite. That includes companies that keep CGSB-certified staff for Canadian work.

The cross-border position of Ontario industry means many companies run two certification systems. A Hamilton fabricator might use CGSB-certified technicians on a CSA W59 bridge job and SNT-TC-1A-certified technicians on an ASME vessel for an Ohio refinery. A Windsor parts supplier might have a US customer whose quality manual requires an SNT-TC-1A written practice and an identified Level III. We help with:

  • writing or updating an SNT-TC-1A written practice that fits your customers' requirements (written practice development);
  • outside Level III services: exam preparation and grading, procedure review and technique sheets;
  • making clear on every job which scheme each technician is certified under;
  • preparing for customer and third-party audits of your NDT programme;
  • certification, training and vision records. The NDT ERP for Ontario inspection companies tracks ASNT and CGSB certificates together.

See SNT-TC-1A training and certification for employers and NDT consulting in Canada. Book a Level III consultation for your Ontario company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator lets Ontario trainees practise 12 methods in 5 virtual environments in a browser before their hands-on exam. It is practice, not certification. It does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that your written practice, or a CGSB scheme, requires.

The NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank environments cover most of what Ontario technicians see, from Chemical Valley piping to aerospace parts in the GTA. Trainees use the simulator to rehearse scan coverage, calibration steps and indication recognition. Supervisors use it to check readiness before booking exam time. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT in Ontario. For written practice questions, try the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He prepares the course material, the examinations and the employer written practices, and he is the person to talk to when you need a straight answer about whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or both fit your Ontario work.

NDT training in Ontario: frequently asked questions

How do I get NDT certified in Ontario?

For most Canadian-code work, get CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712) certification through an accredited certification body. Confirm the current certification body, as arrangements changed in 2026. For US clients, US-code work or US employers, you are certified by your employer under SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis trains for the SNT-TC-1A route only.

Can I take NDT training online in Ontario?

Yes. Atlantis runs live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes for Ontario technicians. Practical training and exams happen on real specimens, normally at your employer's site. See online NDT training.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised in Ontario?

It is recognised by US customers and by owners whose specifications accept it, and it is the norm for ASME work going to the US. It is not the national Canadian scheme. Nuclear work and much CSA-code work expect CGSB certification.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB training in Ontario?

No. We do not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or ISO 9712 and claim no CGSB recognition. If you need a CGSB certificate, choose a CGSB-route provider.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Ontario?

For gamma radiography, yes. You need CNSC exposure device operator certification or direct supervision by a certified EDO, and your employer needs a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment falls under Ontario's X-ray safety rules.

How much does NDT training cost in Ontario?

It is quoted on request. The price depends on the method, level, group size, online or onsite delivery, and whether you also need a written practice or Level III services. Cohort and onsite quotes usually come back within one business day. Request an Ontario quote.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in Ontario?

UT and PAUT lead in refining, steel and power. MT and PT are everywhere in fabrication, mining and automotive, ET matters for exchangers and aerospace, and RT is used for piping and pipeline welds.

Can you train our crew onsite in Sarnia, Hamilton or Sudbury?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your plant, shop or mine site is a standard option. The instructor uses your equipment and specimens and supports practical exams under your written practice.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours, listed in the training requirements matrix, and the experience usually takes much longer than the classroom part.

Can Ontario technicians use SNT-TC-1A certification in Michigan or New York?

SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer that issues it. A US employer will review your training and experience records and certify you under its own written practice. Well-documented Atlantis training records make that review easier.

Can I become a Level III in Ontario?

Yes. For ASNT Level III, prepare for the Basic and method exams with our online Level III preparation. A CGSB Level 3 follows the certification body's own path.

What do NDT technicians earn in Ontario?

It varies by method, level, sector and overtime, and we do not publish our own salary numbers. See the NDT salary guide for context.

Atlantis NDT can help whether you need a Sarnia turnaround crew trained to UT Level II, a Hamilton fabricator ready for its first US ASME order, a written practice for a Windsor supplier, or Level III exam preparation for a GTA quality lead. We build the programme around your work and we are candid when CGSB is the answer instead. NDT Training and Certification in Oregon

Oregon technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite courses at their own foundry, shipyard, mill, dam or plant. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every programme and builds it around the employer's written practice, so training counts toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

Oregon's NDT economy is unusual. It has no oil refineries and no operating nuclear power plant, yet it is home to some of the most inspection-intensive metal manufacturing in the country. Portland's investment-casting and forging plants supply jet-engine and airframe parts worldwide, specialty-metals producers in the Willamette Valley make titanium, zirconium and nickel alloys, and heavy-truck, railcar, barge and ship work fills the Portland harbour. Federal dams on the Columbia, fuel terminals along the Willamette, gas transmission pipelines and hundreds of bridges add field work. Oregon also runs its own industrial radiographer rules. This page is organised around that map. If you already know what you need, request an Oregon training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Oregon

Oregon NDT work clusters in four areas: metals, aerospace castings, trucks and marine fabrication in the Portland metro; specialty metals and manufacturing in the Willamette Valley from Salem to Eugene; hydropower, pipelines and energy infrastructure along the Columbia River and in eastern Oregon; and aviation, ports and wood-products industry in southern Oregon and on the coast. Each favours different methods and specifications.

Portland metro: castings, trucks, ships and steel

Precision Castparts, owned by Berkshire Hathaway, has its roots and major investment-casting operations in Portland, producing large structural castings and engine components for the aerospace industry. Castings like these are among the most heavily inspected parts in manufacturing: RT for internal soundness, fluorescent PT for surface flaws, and UT and VT throughout, all under aerospace customer specifications. On Swan Island, Vigor operates a large shipyard and drydock complex that repairs and builds vessels for commercial operators, ferries and government customers, while Gunderson, part of Greenbrier, builds railcars and marine barges on the Willamette. Daimler Truck North America is headquartered in Portland and builds trucks there, and the city has a steel plate mill and metal recyclers in its industrial districts. Boeing operates a parts plant in Gresham. Methods in demand: RT, PT, UT, MT and VT on castings, forgings and welds, VT and MT on hull and railcar welds, and UT and PAUT on thick plate.

The Northwest Portland fuel hub and the harbour

Along the Willamette in Northwest Portland, a strip of fuel terminals and tank farms known as the Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub receives and stores most of the petroleum products used in Oregon, delivered by pipeline, barge, ship and rail. Because the hub sits on soils vulnerable to earthquake liquefaction, tank and piping integrity has had close attention from the state and the city. That means UT thickness surveys on tank shells, floors and piping, VT and MT on welds, and RT on pressure piping. The Port of Portland's marine terminals and Portland International Airport, which hosts the Oregon Air National Guard's fighter wing, add structural and aircraft work.

Willamette Valley: Albany, Salem and Eugene

Albany and nearby Millersburg are a centre of specialty metals, with ATI's operations producing titanium, zirconium, hafnium and nickel-based alloys for aerospace, nuclear, chemical and medical markets. Bar, plate and mill products from these plants need UT, ET and PT, and process equipment such as reactors and vessels needs UT and VT. Salem's manufacturers and Eugene and Springfield's wood-products mills, manufactured-housing and recreational-vehicle plants, and machinery makers add MT, PT, UT and VT on welded fabrications and boilers. Pulp, paper and lumber mills across the valley run boilers, digesters and pressure vessels that are inspected during annual shutdowns.

Columbia River: dams, power and pipelines

The US Army Corps of Engineers operates Bonneville, The Dalles, John Day and McNary dams on the Columbia, and the Bonneville Power Administration, headquartered in Portland, markets the federal hydropower and runs much of the region's transmission system. Turbines, penstocks, gates, cranes and structural steel at hydro plants need UT, MT and VT, with PT and ET on components. Interstate natural gas transmission pipelines cross Oregon from Canada and the Rocky Mountains, with compressor stations in eastern and central Oregon, and gas-fired plants at sites such as Hermiston and Boardman need outage inspection. The Interstate 5 bridge replacement project between Portland and Vancouver, Washington, and the Oregon Department of Transportation's large inventory of steel and concrete bridges add structural NDT work.

Southern Oregon and the coast

Kingsley Field in Klamath Falls trains Air National Guard fighter pilots and maintains their aircraft, which brings ET, UT and PT on aircraft structure. Medford and Grants Pass have wood-products, manufacturing and aviation businesses, and the Port of Coos Bay, the state's largest deep-draft coastal port, handles forest products and has marine and rail infrastructure. Coastal and southern Oregon employers are spread thin, which makes online theory especially useful.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Oregon employers

Atlantis NDT runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based courses in eight methods at Level I and Level II, plus Level III preparation. Oregon employers most often need RT, PT, UT and VT for aerospace castings and specialty metals, VT, MT and UT for shipyard, railcar and truck fabrication, and UT thickness, MT and VT for terminals, dams and mills.

Atlantis NDT has a dedicated training page and a Practical NDT simulator page for Portland, Oregon, and a simulator page for Eugene. Every other Oregon city is served through live online classes or onsite delivery at the employer's facility. There is no Atlantis training centre in Oregon; the course comes to your crew or your screen.

Portland. The centre of Oregon NDT. Casting and forging plants need large numbers of RT, PT and UT technicians who can work to aerospace specifications, and Swan Island and the Willamette industrial waterfront need VT, MT and UT on ship, barge and railcar welds. Portland employers often run onsite cohorts on their own parts, with theory delivered live online between shifts.

Albany and Millersburg. Specialty metals bring UT, ET and PT on bar, plate, tube and mill products, with customer specifications from aerospace, chemical and nuclear buyers. Accuracy of acceptance criteria and documentation is everything here.

Eugene and Springfield. Fabrication of RVs, manufactured homes, machinery and mill equipment needs VT, MT and UT on welds, and mill boilers need UT thickness and VT during shutdowns. Many employers here have small NDT teams and benefit from an outside Level III.

Columbia Gorge and eastern Oregon. Hydro, gas-fired power and pipeline compressor stations need UT, MT, VT and PT during outages, and remote locations make live online theory the practical choice.

Klamath Falls, Medford and Coos Bay. Aircraft maintenance, wood-products plants and port infrastructure each need a small number of qualified technicians, and online theory with onsite practicals avoids long drives to Portland.

Neighbouring hubs: NDT training across the Pacific Northwest, Seattle for Puget Sound employers with Oregon sites, Practical NDT for Washington State, and Idaho for crews working across the eastern border.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Oregon, step by step

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you, not the State of Oregon and not a training school. You complete method training, log documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you to its written practice. Radiographers also need Oregon's radiation safety qualification.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer needs a written practice that defines levels, training, experience, exams and recertification, and in aerospace casting and specialty-metals plants it must also satisfy customer audits. If one does not exist, we can write it.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete the method training the written practice requires, online, live-virtual or onsite. The training requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience on real work, whether castings in Portland, bar and plate in Albany or hull welds on Swan Island. Records are signed and kept.
  4. General exam. A written test on method principles.
  5. Specific exam. A written test on the specifications, procedures and equipment your employer uses, such as an aerospace customer's casting specification, AWS D1.1 or ASME Section V.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on inspection of specimens with known discontinuities, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast checks, annually.
  8. Certification. Issued by your employer and valid for that employer. A new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice, though your documented training and experience carry forward.
  9. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets, by evidence of continued satisfactory work or re-examination.

More detail is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Radiography licensing and other Oregon requirements

Oregon is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is regulated by Radiation Protection Services in the Oregon Health Authority's Public Health Division, under Oregon Administrative Rules chapter 333, with Division 105 covering industrial radiographic operations. Radiographers must complete specified radiation safety training, supervised hands-on experience and certification through a radiographer certification programme, separately from SNT-TC-1A method certification.

The Oregon rules set out the subjects radiographers must be trained in and a defined period of supervised on-the-job radiography experience, with separate segments for work with radioactive sources and with radiation machines, and they require radiographers to be certified through a recognised radiographer certification programme and instructed in the licensee's operating procedures. The employing company needs a radioactive materials licence or X-ray device registration from Radiation Protection Services, and out-of-state companies working in Oregon must follow the reciprocity rules. Our RT Level I and II courses cover the method side: exposure technique, image quality and film or digital interpretation. Check the current OAR 333 Division 105 requirements with the Oregon Health Authority before a crew starts field work, and check federal site requirements before working at a federal dam or military installation.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Building Codes Division of the Oregon Department of Consumer and Business Services runs the boiler and pressure vessel programme. It adopts and interprets the Oregon Boiler and Pressure Vessel Specialty Code, whose current edition took effect on 1 October 2024, and provides permits and inspections for installation, alteration, repair and operation of boilers and pressure vessels. Repair work generally follows the National Board Inspection Code, with NDT drawn from ASME Section V and the construction code.

Pipelines. The Oregon Public Utility Commission's pipeline safety programme is certified by the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) to inspect and enforce federal pipeline safety code for gas operators in the state; PHMSA itself oversees interstate lines. Pipeline weld inspection commonly follows API 1104.

Codes you will meet in Oregon. As local context only: aerospace customer casting and forging specifications, NAS 410 and ASTM practices for RT, PT, UT and ET in Portland's casting plants and Albany's mills, AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for bridges, ASME Section V and VIII for pressure vessels, ASME B31.1 and B31.3 for power and process piping, API 1104 for pipelines, Association of American Railroads requirements for railcar work, and US Coast Guard and classification-society rules at shipyards. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials; those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train for. Our training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Oregon

Oregon crews can take theory live online, join a live-virtual cohort, or have an Atlantis Level III-led programme delivered onsite at their facility. Practical training and practical exams use real specimens, at the employer's site or through a partner arrangement agreed beforehand.

Distance is the main reason Oregon employers choose online theory. Klamath Falls, Coos Bay and Hermiston are each several hours from Portland, and a technician in eastern Oregon loses most of a week driving to a classroom. Live online sessions are interactive, with the instructor present, and cover the general and specific knowledge the written exams test. See NDT training online for details.

Onsite delivery suits foundries, mills, yards and plants that want a group trained on their own parts and procedures. We schedule around Oregon's real calendar: annual mill shutdowns in the Willamette Valley, spring and fall outages at gas-fired plants, hydro maintenance that the Columbia's high spring flows usually push into lower-flow months, shipyard availabilities on Swan Island, and production ramps at casting plants. Winter rain and snow in the Cascades can affect field practicals, so we plan around them.

Practical skill is built on hardware. Practical sessions use real specimens, your production parts where appropriate, and the instruments your team uses. For employers with sites in Oregon and Washington or further afield, our corporate NDT training programme keeps training records consistent. Ask about onsite training for your Oregon crew.

For Oregon employers: written practice and Level III services

Every Oregon company certifying NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, administers and grades exams, reviews procedures and acts as an outside Level III for companies that do not have one in-house.

Common Oregon triggers are a customer audit or a new contract. A machine shop in Tualatin approved as a supplier for aerospace parts, a Eugene fabricator taking on pressure-vessel work, a Portland railcar or barge builder adding UT, or a mill whose long-serving Level III has retired cannot certify anyone until the written practice and Level III oversight are in place. Our written practice development service builds a document that fits your methods, specifications and audits, and our SNT-TC-1A guidance explains what auditors look for.

Level III support includes procedure and technique writing, exam administration and grading, review of training and experience files, and preparation for customer and registrar audits. For broader programme work, see our NDT consulting services. Book a Level III consultation for your Oregon company.

Practise before your practical exam

Practical NDT is Atlantis NDT's 3D simulator. Trainees practise 12 inspection methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It builds familiarity and confidence but is practice only; it does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

For Oregon trainees, the NDT lab mirrors the inspection rooms of Portland casting plants and Albany mills, the welding workshop matches shipyard, barge and railcar fabrication on the Willamette, the aircraft hangar reflects maintenance at Kingsley Field and Portland's air base, and the storage tank scene matches the Northwest Portland fuel terminals. Trainees can rehearse set-ups and scan patterns between classes and arrive at the practical exam knowing what to expect.

Simulator time does not count as on-the-job experience and is not a practical exam. See the Practical NDT simulator overview, or the city pages for Portland and Eugene.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As Level III he oversees course content, written practices, exams and practical assessment criteria, so the training an Oregon technician receives is tied to how that technician will be examined and certified. Questions about methods, written practices or an Oregon requirement can go to him through the contact form.

NDT training in Oregon: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Oregon?

Most Oregon NDT technicians are certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A: method training, documented on-the-job experience, general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and a vision test. Radiographers also need state radiation safety training and radiographer certification under Oregon's rules.

Is there NDT training online in Oregon?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online theory classes that technicians can join from Portland, Salem, Eugene, Albany, Klamath Falls, Hermiston or anywhere else in the state. Practical training and the practical exam still need real specimens, arranged onsite at your employer or through an agreed partner.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Oregon?

Yes. The company needs a licence or registration from the Oregon Health Authority's Radiation Protection Services, and individual radiographers must complete the training, supervised experience and certification required by OAR 333 Division 105. This is in addition to SNT-TC-1A RT method certification. Confirm current rules with the state.

How much does NDT training cost in Oregon?

Quote on request. It depends on the method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and whether you also need a written practice or exam administration. Send your crew size and methods and we will reply with a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in Oregon?

RT, PT, UT and VT are in constant demand at Portland's aerospace casting plants and the specialty-metals mills, while VT, MT and UT dominate in shipyards, railcar and truck plants and fabrication shops. UT thickness and MT are common in terminal, mill and hydro work.

Can you train our crew onsite in Portland or Albany?

Yes. Onsite delivery is available at your facility anywhere in Oregon, scheduled around production, shutdowns and outages. Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in the state; onsite means at your site.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Oregon employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used employer-based certification framework in US industry and is referenced by ASME, AWS and many customer specifications. Aerospace buyers sometimes require NAS 410 qualification as well, which your written practice and customer contract should address.

Are there NDT jobs in Oregon without a refinery or nuclear plant?

Yes. Oregon's NDT demand comes mostly from manufacturing rather than refining: aerospace castings and forgings, specialty metals, shipyards, railcars, trucks and fabrication, with field work at fuel terminals, dams, pipelines, mills and bridges.

How long does UT Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom training and experience for each level. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums are on our training requirements matrix. Experience usually takes longer than classroom time.

Can I prepare for the ASNT Level III exams from Oregon?

Yes. Our ASNT Level III training runs live online and covers the Basic and method exams. Level II candidates can also use the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Does my certification transfer to another Oregon employer?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the issuing employer. A new employer reviews your records and re-certifies you under its own written practice, which may require new specific and practical exams.

What do NDT technicians earn in Oregon?

Earnings vary by method, level, sector, shift and travel. For published ranges, see the NDT Level 2 salary and NDT Level 3 salary guides.

Start NDT training in Oregon

Whether you are a technician in Salem preparing for UT Level II, a Portland casting supplier that needs RT and PT qualified people, a Swan Island contractor preparing a VT and MT cohort, or a mill that needs a written practice and an outside Level III, Atlantis NDT will build the programme around your work. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable. Request your Oregon NDT training quote, tell us about your crew and methods, or browse the full training catalogue and the national NDT training in the USA hub.

NDT Training and Certification in Pennsylvania

Short answer: Pennsylvania technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, a private live-virtual cohort, or onsite delivery at the employer's mill, plant, depot, shipyard or shop anywhere in the Commonwealth. An ASNT NDT Level III leads each programme, practical exams are held on real specimens at your facility, and the employer certifies you under its own written practice.

Pennsylvania's NDT market is built on heavy industry rather than refining. It has four operating nuclear stations and a major nuclear supply chain, the Marcellus and Utica shale gas fields with the pipelines and processing that serve them, steelmaking in the Mon Valley, a large petrochemical plant on the Ohio River, defence depots and rotorcraft manufacturing, locomotive building in Erie, a Philadelphia shipyard and Navy engineering centre, and one of the largest and oldest bridge inventories in the country. This hub maps where Pennsylvania NDT technicians work, which methods each sector uses, what the Department of Environmental Protection expects from radiography crews, and how we train crews without anyone travelling to a training centre. To price your group now, request a Pennsylvania training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in Pennsylvania

Direct answer: Pennsylvania NDT work concentrates in Pittsburgh and the southwest (steel, petrochemicals, Marcellus gas, nuclear supply chain), the northeast and north-central gas fields, the Philadelphia and Delaware River region (shipbuilding, Navy engineering, refining, rotorcraft), central Pennsylvania (defence depots, manufacturing, nuclear plants), and Erie (locomotives and fabrication). Nuclear and steel shape demand more here than in most states.

Pittsburgh and southwestern Pennsylvania

The Pittsburgh region still makes steel: the Mon Valley Works, including the Clairton coke plant and the Edgar Thomson works in Braddock, keeps maintenance and fabrication NDT busy. Downriver in Beaver County, the Shell Polymers Monaca ethane cracker is one of the largest petrochemical plants built in the Northeast in decades, and Beaver Valley nuclear station sits nearby at Shippingport. Westinghouse, headquartered in Cranberry Township, anchors a nuclear engineering and component supply chain across the region. Washington and Greene counties are core Marcellus gas country, with gathering pipelines, compressor stations and processing plants. That mix creates demand for UT on heavy sections and welds, MT on structural and rotating equipment, RT on pipelines and process piping, ET for heat exchangers and condensers, and VT throughout. Pittsburgh's many river bridges add steel-bridge inspection; the 2022 collapse of the Fern Hollow Bridge in the city focused statewide attention on bridge condition.

Northeast and north-central Pennsylvania: the Marcellus gas fields

Susquehanna, Bradford, Tioga and Lycoming counties are among the most productive natural-gas areas in the country. Gathering systems, compressor stations, metering facilities and transmission pipelines generate steady pipeline weld radiography to API 1104, UT on station piping, and VT and MT on fabricated skids. Williamsport and the Wyoming Valley host service companies and fabrication shops supporting the field. Susquehanna nuclear station near Berwick adds outage work.

Philadelphia, the Delaware River and southeastern Pennsylvania

Philadelphia's shipyard builds commercial ships, and the Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division at the former Navy Yard is a centre for ship machinery engineering and testing. Boeing's Ridley Park site builds military rotorcraft. Along the river, the Trainer refinery and the Marcus Hook industrial complex (an export terminal for natural gas liquids carried across the state by pipeline) need refinery-style mechanical integrity inspection. Limerick and Peach Bottom nuclear stations lie within reach of the city. Demand here combines aerospace methods (PT, ET, UT, MT), Navy and shipbuilding inspection, and refinery UT, RT and PAUT.

Central Pennsylvania: Harrisburg, York, Lancaster and the depots

Central Pennsylvania mixes defence and manufacturing. Letterkenny Army Depot near Chambersburg and Tobyhanna Army Depot in the Poconos maintain military equipment, BAE Systems builds combat vehicles in York, and manufacturing plants across Lancaster, York and Cumberland counties produce heavy equipment, vehicles and components. The former Three Mile Island Unit 1, renamed the Crane Clean Energy Center, is the subject of a restart effort, which would bring significant nuclear inspection work if it proceeds. Weld inspection on armour and structures (UT, MT, VT), castings and forgings (RT, UT, MT) and in-service inspection at the nuclear plants dominate.

Lehigh Valley, Scranton and Erie

The Lehigh Valley around Allentown and Bethlehem has heavy-truck manufacturing, fabrication shops and a large logistics sector, and Scranton has an Army ammunition plant and metalworking. In the northwest, Erie is home to Wabtec's locomotive manufacturing, plus foundries and fabrication shops. Rail and heavy manufacturing need UT, MT and PT on castings, forgings, welded frames and axles, while United Refining in Warren adds a small refinery.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Pennsylvania employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT delivers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Pennsylvania employers, plus Level III exam preparation. Steel, rail and manufacturing lean on UT and MT; gas pipelines on RT; nuclear supply chain and plants on UT, PAUT, ET and PT; aerospace on PT and ET.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Pennsylvania, step by step

Direct answer: Pennsylvania NDT certification under ASNT SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. The written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and supervised experience; a Level III administers general, specific and practical exams; you pass a vision test; and the employer certifies you. No state agency issues a general NDT licence, but radiographers face DEP rules.

  1. Employer written practice. Based on SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. If you do not have one, see written practice development.
  2. Formal training. Complete the classroom hours the written practice requires, documented with course records.
  3. Supervised experience. Log on-the-job hours; the training requirements matrix shows typical figures by method and level.
  4. General and specific exams. Theory and your employer's procedures and codes (ASME V, VIII, B31.1 or B31.3, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or D1.5).
  5. Practical exam. Hands-on testing on flawed specimens, graded by a Level III at your facility.
  6. Vision test. Near-vision and colour-contrast checks at the written-practice interval.
  7. Certification and recertification. The employer certifies and later recertifies you; see Level II recertification.

Pennsylvania's nuclear and defence employers often layer additional requirements on top of SNT-TC-1A, so technicians moving from a fabrication shop into the nuclear supply chain should expect extra training, procedure-specific qualification and closer documentation. Keep a complete file of your training, experience and exam records. More detail: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Pennsylvania requirements

Direct answer: Pennsylvania became an NRC Agreement State in 2008. Industrial radiography is regulated by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Bureau of Radiation Protection. X-ray industrial radiography falls under 25 Pa. Code Chapter 225, and radioactive-material radiography follows state rules aligned with the NRC's 10 CFR Part 34.

Pennsylvania's industrial radiography rules require a programme for training personnel, written operating and emergency procedures, personnel monitoring, internal reviews and a defined organisational structure for radiographic operations. Registrants and licensees may not let anyone act as a radiographer or radiographer's assistant unless that person meets the training and testing requirements in the rules. Because Pennsylvania's Agreement State status is more recent than most, some older documents still refer to NRC licensing for sealed sources; today DEP is the licensing authority. Confirm current requirements with DEP before planning a programme.

Atlantis NDT's RT courses teach radiographic technique, exposure, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance criteria for SNT-TC-1A Level I and II. The state radiation-safety training and qualification of radiographers and assistants are separate requirements managed by your radiation safety officer. We help employers plan both so they run in parallel.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry's boiler division administers the state boiler and unfired pressure vessel law within the National Board framework. NDT on repairs and alterations follows the National Board Inspection Code and ASME Sections I and VIII.

Pipelines. The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission's pipeline safety programme oversees intrastate gas and certain hazardous-liquid pipelines, with PHMSA covering interstate lines. Gathering lines in the shale fields have their own reporting regime. API 1104 governs most pipeline weld inspection.

Bridges. PennDOT and local owners manage a very large inventory of bridges, many of them older steel structures. Bridge fabrication and repair welds follow AWS D1.5, and fracture-critical members need careful UT and MT.

Codes commonly used in Pennsylvania. ASME Section XI at Beaver Valley, Limerick, Peach Bottom and Susquehanna; ASME Sections III and V and nuclear quality programmes in the supply chain; ASME VIII and B31.1 or B31.3 in plants; API 1104 on pipelines; AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structures and bridges; NAVSEA requirements for Navy work; and NAS 410 for aerospace. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials for particular roles. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only; we mention these only as local context.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Pennsylvania

Direct answer: Pennsylvania technicians can take theory live online, join a private live-virtual cohort for their employer, or have an Atlantis Level III deliver the programme onsite at their mill, plant, depot or shop. Atlantis has no training centre in Pennsylvania; practical exams happen at the client's facility on real specimens.

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory with attendance records, useful across a state where gas-field crews in Bradford County and fabricators in Erie are hours apart. See online NDT training.
  • Private live-virtual cohort. A group from one employer, scheduled around shift rotations, with content mapped to that employer's written practice and procedures.
  • Onsite. A Level III teaches the hands-on portion and runs practical exams at your facility. See corporate NDT training.

Pennsylvania scheduling follows nuclear refuelling outages, which are planned well in advance, steel-mill maintenance shutdowns, and the construction season. Winter weather limits outdoor pipeline work in the northern tier, which often makes winter the best time for theory and spring for onsite practicals. Ask about onsite training for your Pennsylvania crew.

For Pennsylvania employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Pennsylvania fabricators, manufacturers, inspection contractors and gas-field service companies use Atlantis NDT to write or update SNT-TC-1A written practices, provide outside Level III services, administer exams and train whole teams. Customer audits from nuclear, defence and energy clients look closely at these records.

We often meet Pennsylvania manufacturers that built NDT capability gradually, with one or two technicians trained by a previous employer and no written practice of their own. When a nuclear, defence or energy customer asks for certification records, that gap becomes urgent. Other common issues include written practices that do not cover PAUT, unclear rules for crediting previous experience, missing vision records and practical exams without documented grading. We can review your documents, write or revise the written practice, prepare exam banks and act as your examining Level III.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Atlantis Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is a practice tool only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens set by your Level III.

Pennsylvania fabrication, rail and steel trainees get most from the welding workshop and NDT lab, gas-field trainees from the oil and gas site, and rotorcraft trainees from the aircraft hangar. See Practical NDT, Practical NDT in Pennsylvania, and city pages for Philadelphia and Pittsburgh. For written exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He designs the course content, maps it to each employer's written practice and oversees exams. On onsite programmes in Pennsylvania he works with your Level III or serves as examining Level III where you do not have one.

NDT training in Pennsylvania: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Pennsylvania?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its classroom training and supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, pass a vision test, and the employer certifies you.

Is there NDT training online in Pennsylvania?

Yes. Atlantis NDT delivers SNT-TC-1A theory live online across Pennsylvania. Practical training and exams are done onsite at your employer's facility.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Pennsylvania?

Your employer needs a DEP licence or registration, and you must meet the training and testing requirements for radiographers or radiographer's assistants under Pennsylvania's radiation rules, in addition to your SNT-TC-1A level. Check current details with DEP's Bureau of Radiation Protection.

How much does NDT training cost in Pennsylvania?

We quote on request. The cost depends on methods and levels, group size, delivery model and any exam administration or written-practice work. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Pennsylvania?

UT and MT are the broadest, thanks to steel, rail, defence and heavy fabrication. RT is strong in the gas fields, and ET, UT and PAUT are important for power and nuclear work.

Can you train our crew onsite in Pittsburgh or Philadelphia?

Yes. Onsite training and practical exams at your facility are available anywhere in Pennsylvania, scheduled around outages and shutdowns.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Pennsylvania employers?

Yes. It is widely used across manufacturing, fabrication, pipelines and power. Nuclear plants and suppliers add further requirements, Navy work may follow NAVSEA documents, and aerospace work may require NAS 410.

How long does UT Level II take in Pennsylvania?

It depends on the employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures; supervised experience is usually the longer part.

Can I work at a nuclear plant with SNT-TC-1A Level II?

Nuclear employers usually require qualification under their own programme, aligned with ASME Section XI and related standards, and some UT applications require performance demonstration. SNT-TC-1A training is a common foundation but not always sufficient on its own.

Does Atlantis NDT have a training centre in Pittsburgh or Philadelphia?

No. Atlantis NDT does not operate a physical training centre in Pennsylvania. Training is online, live-virtual, or onsite at your employer's facility.

Do you offer CWI or API inspector courses in Pennsylvania?

No. Atlantis NDT provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training only. Those separate credentials need a specialist provider.

Can you help our shop set up its first NDT programme?

Yes. We write the written practice, train your technicians, administer exams and can serve as your outside Level III. See NDT consulting in Pennsylvania.

NDT Training and Certification in Phoenix, AZ

Short answer: Phoenix-area technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, in private live-virtual cohorts, or onsite at the employer's own hangar, fab site, plant or shop anywhere in the Valley of the Sun. We cover Level I and II in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, with Level III exam preparation. Every course is led by an ASNT NDT Level III, and certification is issued by your employer under its written practice.

Phoenix has quietly become one of the most interesting NDT labour markets in the country. Aerospace and defence manufacturing has been here for decades, from aircraft engines and auxiliary power units near Sky Harbor to attack helicopters in Mesa and launch vehicles and satellites in Chandler. On top of that came a wave of semiconductor fab construction in north Phoenix and Chandler, battery and EV plants in Pinal County, data-centre campuses in Mesa and Goodyear, and steady work at the country's largest nuclear power station west of the city. Each of those employers needs a different method mix and different paperwork. Atlantis NDT does not operate a Phoenix campus; we bring the training to your crew or teach it live online, and the practical exam takes place on real specimens under a Level III. Request a Phoenix NDT training quote and we send options within one business day.

Quick factsPhoenix answer
SchemeASNT SNT-TC-1A, employer-based certification under your written practice
Training hoursSet by method and level in the written practice; see the training requirements matrix
ExperienceLogged with your employer and verified by its Level III
ExamsGeneral, specific and practical, administered by a Level III; annual vision test
WhereLive online, or onsite at your facility in Phoenix, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Glendale, Goodyear or anywhere in Maricopa and Pinal counties
RadiographyArizona is an NRC Agreement State; the Arizona Department of Health Services Bureau of Radiation Control regulates industrial radiography
PriceQuote on request; cohort and onsite quotes within one business day

NDT training in Phoenix: how it works for Phoenix employers and technicians

Direct answer: NDT certification in Phoenix is employer-based. You complete formal training, gain supervised experience, and pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III; your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and, when needed, the Level III services, written practice and exam administration behind it.

Two kinds of people search for NDT training in Phoenix. The first is the employer: an aerospace supplier in Tempe that has just added a penetrant line, a fabrication contractor bidding structural steel on a fab project, a utility contractor that needs radiographers for gas-line welds, or a data-centre builder whose owner wants Level II VT on every structural connection. For them, the course is one piece of a bigger requirement: an auditable certification programme that satisfies a prime contractor, a general contractor or a regulator. The second is the individual: someone moving into NDT from welding, aviation maintenance or the military who wants to be employable at Level II. For that person, the most important thing to understand is that a training certificate on its own is a training record. Certification happens when an employer's Level III examines you and the employer signs off under its written practice. We explain that on day one, and we document every training hour so a new employer's Level III can accept it.

Atlantis works with both. Employers can buy training alone, or training plus SNT-TC-1A certification support, which covers the written practice, exams and records. Individuals can join live online classes and use the documented hours when they join or move employers.

Where NDT technicians work in Phoenix

Direct answer: Phoenix NDT demand centres on aerospace and defence manufacturing and MRO, semiconductor and battery plant construction, the Palo Verde nuclear station and other power assets, gas and products pipelines, structural steel for data centres and high-rise work, and mining equipment serving the copper districts east and south of the metro.

Aerospace, defence and aviation maintenance

Phoenix is a major aerospace manufacturing centre. Aircraft engines, auxiliary power units, avionics and mechanical systems are designed and built near Sky Harbor International Airport and in Tempe. Boeing builds AH-64 Apache helicopters in Mesa, and Northrop Grumman manufactures launch vehicles and satellites in Chandler. Luke Air Force Base in Glendale trains F-35 pilots, and Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport hosts aircraft maintenance and modification work. Hundreds of machine shops, special-process houses and repair stations in Tempe, Chandler, Mesa and Deer Valley support these programmes. Their NDT work is dominated by PT, MT, ET and UT on machined, forged and cast parts, with RT and increasingly digital radiography on castings. Many of these employers also need NAS 410 qualification for aerospace customers; that is a separate scheme from SNT-TC-1A that Atlantis does not train for, but we help employers understand how the two relate.

Semiconductor fabs, batteries and data centres

North Phoenix is home to a multi-fab semiconductor campus under construction, and Chandler's Ocotillo campus has been expanded with new fabs. Battery and EV manufacturers have built plants in Queen Creek, Casa Grande and the wider Pinal County area, and data-centre campuses continue to grow in Mesa, Chandler, Goodyear and the West Valley. These projects need enormous amounts of structural steel, process piping, ultra-pure water and gas systems, and mechanical equipment. That creates demand for VT on structural welds, UT and PAUT on full-penetration welds, RT on piping, and PT on stainless process lines, usually to AWS D1.1 and ASME B31.3.

Palo Verde and power generation

The Palo Verde Generating Station near Wintersburg, west of Phoenix, is the largest nuclear power plant in the United States by generation. Its refuelling outages bring in-service inspection to ASME Section XI, with UT, ET on steam-generator tubes, VT and PT. Gas-fired and solar-plus-storage plants operated by the state's utilities, along with substations and transmission structures across the metro, add steady weld and corrosion inspection work.

Pipelines and fuel terminals

Phoenix receives its gasoline and diesel through refined-products pipelines from Texas and California that terminate at tank farms in west Phoenix and Tucson, and natural gas arrives through interstate transmission lines from the San Juan and Permian basins. New gas distribution, line replacements and terminal work keep radiographers and UT technicians busy on API 1104 welds, with tank inspection to API 653 as code context.

Mining equipment and the copper districts

Arizona produces most of the country's copper. Mines at Morenci, Bagdad, Miami-Globe, Ray and Safford, and the smelters and mills that serve them, rely on Phoenix-based fabricators and rebuild shops for shafts, gears, crusher components, haul-truck frames and structural steel. MT, UT and PT are the core methods for that work.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Phoenix

Direct answer: Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation, live online or onsite in the Phoenix metro. The table maps each method to typical Phoenix work and shows what a trainee needs first.

MethodLevelsWhat Phoenix employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepForgings and machined aerospace parts, structural welds on fab and data-centre steel, Palo Verde in-service inspection, thickness surveys on piping and tanksLevel I per employer; Level II needs Level I training plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepFull-penetration structural welds, process piping on fab projects, power plant weldsUT Level II recommended first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-section welds on pressure equipment and power plant componentsUT Level II recommended first
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepAerospace castings, pipeline and gas distribution welds, process piping, digital radiography in labsArizona radiation safety rules apply before working with sources
