Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepAircraft structure and wheel inspection, bolt holes, heat-exchanger and steam-generator tubingPer employer

For Level III candidates, see ASNT Level III training. Method guides for the Valley include ultrasonic testing in Phoenix, radiographic testing in Phoenix, penetrant testing in Phoenix and visual testing in Phoenix.

Method spotlight: VT and PT for fab and data-centre construction QA

The construction boom around Phoenix's fabs and data centres has created a specific shortage: qualified visual inspectors who can accept structural welds against AWS D1.1, and penetrant inspectors for stainless process systems. General contractors and owners increasingly ask subcontractors to show certification records for every inspector on site. A focused VT and PT Level II programme, combined with a written practice your company owns, is often the quickest way for a steel erector or mechanical contractor to meet that requirement. Ask about a VT and PT programme for your Phoenix construction crew.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Phoenix, step by step

Direct answer: written practice, formal training, supervised experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, a vision test, and employer certification. Hours vary by method and level, so use the training requirements matrix and your written practice, not a single quoted number.

  1. Get or confirm the written practice. It is the rulebook for your employer's programme. Atlantis can write one: see NDT written practice development.
  2. Complete formal training in the method and level, live online or onsite in Phoenix, with attendance and topics recorded.
  3. Build supervised experience on real work at your employer.
  4. Pass the general exam on method theory.
  5. Pass the specific exam on your employer's procedures, codes and customer specifications.
  6. Pass the practical exam on specimens with known discontinuities, under a Level III.
  7. Pass the vision test: near-vision acuity and colour contrast, annually.
  8. Receive employer certification in writing.
  9. Recertify at the interval your written practice sets.

How the practical works when you train online

Direct answer: theory can be online; the practical cannot. It is performed on real specimens under a Level III, usually onsite at your Phoenix facility with your own equipment and procedures, or at a location agreed with your employer before training starts. The simulator is rehearsal only.

For an aerospace shop with a penetrant line and reference panels, the onsite practical is straightforward: the Level III visits, verifies the process, and examines each trainee on the procedure they use every day. For a construction contractor without specimens, we agree a plan in advance, for example using welded specimens with documented discontinuities supplied for the exam, so the practical reflects the real work. Either way, your file ends up with graded exam records, training records and the vision test, ready for an auditor or a general contractor's QA manager.

Local NDT training options in Phoenix and Arizona

Direct answer: Arizona options include a public community-college aviation NDT certificate in Tucson, private Level III training and consulting providers, national schools with campuses in other states, and live online or onsite programmes such as Atlantis. The right choice depends on whether you need a career-entry programme or targeted employer qualification.

  • Pima Community College (Tucson) offers an aviation Nondestructive Testing certificate that covers the academic requirements for Level II in six methods (ET, PT, MT, RT, UT and VT). It is listed on Arizona's eligible training provider list, which matters if you are seeking WIOA funding.
  • Private Level III providers in the Phoenix and Tucson areas offer consulting, procedure writing and some training, often focused on aerospace.
  • The ASNT Arizona Section, based in the Greater Phoenix area, runs meetings and events where local technicians and Level IIIs meet.
  • National schools and test labs with campuses in other states run scheduled classroom courses that require travel.
  • Atlantis NDT trains employer crews onsite or live online, aligned to their written practice, with Level III services available. We have no Phoenix campus.

Radiography licensing and other Arizona requirements

Direct answer: Arizona is an NRC Agreement State. The Arizona Department of Health Services Bureau of Radiation Control licenses industrial radiography under Title 9, Chapter 7 of the Arizona Administrative Code, including sealed-source radiography and industrial X-ray. Boilers fall under the Industrial Commission of Arizona, and intrastate pipelines under the Arizona Corporation Commission Office of Pipeline Safety. Confirm current requirements with each agency.

Industrial radiography

Employers that perform radiography in Arizona hold a licence or registration from the Bureau of Radiation Control, and individual radiographers and radiographer's assistants must meet the state's training, certification and supervision rules. RT method training covers image quality and interpretation; radiation safety is a separate legal requirement that your employer's radiation safety officer manages. Crews that also work in California, New Mexico or Nevada need to follow each state's rules or reciprocity process.

Nuclear

Although Arizona is an Agreement State, commercial nuclear power reactors such as Palo Verde remain under direct NRC regulation. In-service inspection there follows ASME Section XI, and personnel qualification follows the plant's programme, which is stricter than general industrial practice.

Boilers, pipelines and structures

Boiler and pressure vessel inspection is administered through the Industrial Commission of Arizona, with the National Board Inspection Code for repairs and alterations. The Arizona Corporation Commission Office of Pipeline Safety oversees intrastate gas pipelines, and PHMSA regulates interstate lines. Phoenix-area building departments run special inspection programmes for structural welding and high-strength bolting on large projects. TWIC credentials are not usually needed for Phoenix work, since there are no maritime-regulated port facilities in the metro.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Phoenix crews

Direct answer: choose live online classes for one or two people, a private live-virtual cohort for a company team, or onsite delivery at your Phoenix facility. Every format is Level III-led, and scheduling works around production, outages and the summer heat.

Phoenix employers have scheduling constraints that are easy to underestimate. Outdoor construction and field crews often shift to early-morning work during the summer months, so afternoon or evening live online sessions work well. Palo Verde outages and utility shutdown windows pull qualified technicians away for weeks at a time, so we plan cohorts around them. Aerospace suppliers running multiple shifts usually prefer theory in short live sessions with the practical delivered onsite over a few days. See NDT training online and corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Phoenix crew.

Level III services and written practices for Phoenix NDT companies

Direct answer: many Phoenix employers need a Level III of record, a compliant written practice and procedures as much as they need training. Atlantis provides those services remotely and onsite so training, exams and documentation line up when an auditor reviews your programme.

Our consulting team already works with Arizona companies: see NDT consulting in Phoenix, steel NDT Level III consulting in Phoenix and NDT consulting in Tucson. Typical work includes a new SNT-TC-1A written practice for a fabrication contractor entering fab or data-centre work, technique sheets and procedures for an aerospace supplier, an outside Level III to administer and grade exams, and audit preparation before a prime contractor visit. Start with written practice development or book a Level III consultation for your Phoenix company.

Practise before the practical exam

Direct answer: the Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five environments, including an aircraft hangar, a welding workshop and an oil and gas site. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The hangar environment is especially relevant to Phoenix's aerospace workforce, and the welding workshop suits construction and fabrication trainees. Phoenix users can also see Practical NDT in Phoenix and Practical NDT in Tucson.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He teaches the classroom content, oversees practical examinations and supports employers with written practices and Level III services.

NDT training in Phoenix, Arizona and the Southwest: related pages

The statewide page is NDT training in Arizona. Southern Arizona aerospace employers can see aerospace NDT training in Tucson. Neighbouring cities include NDT training in Las Vegas, NDT training in Albuquerque and NDT training in Denver, and the regional overview is NDT training in the Rockies and Plains.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Phoenix

How do I get NDT certified in Phoenix?

Complete the formal training your employer's written practice requires, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training live online or onsite in Phoenix, and the Level III services if your employer needs them.

Can I do an NDT course online in Arizona?

Yes, the classroom portion. Atlantis teaches live online classes led by an ASNT Level III. The practical exam must still be done on real specimens under a Level III, usually at your employer's facility.

How much does an NDT course cost in Phoenix?

We quote on request. Cost depends on method, level, group size and whether training is online or onsite. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day. Request a Phoenix course quote.

How much does NDT school cost compared with targeted training?

A college certificate or campus programme covering several methods over months is a larger commitment than targeted employer training in one or two methods. If you are entering the field with no employer, a full programme may suit you; if your employer needs specific qualifications quickly, targeted training is usually more efficient.

How long is the NDT training course?

It depends on the method, the level and the written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends hours and experience for each; see the training requirements matrix. Live online classes can be spread out to suit shift work.

Which NDT course is best in Phoenix?

For aerospace manufacturing and MRO, PT, MT and ET are the most common starting methods. For fab, data-centre and pipeline construction, VT, UT and RT are in higher demand. Pick the method your current or target employer uses.

Do I need a license for radiography in Arizona?

Yes. Arizona is an Agreement State and the ADHS Bureau of Radiation Control licenses industrial radiography. Your employer holds the licence, and individual radiographers must meet the state's training and certification rules before working with sources.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Phoenix employers?

Yes. It is the most widely used employer certification guideline in US industry. Some aerospace customers additionally require NAS 410, and Palo Verde has its own nuclear qualification programme.

Can you train our crew onsite in Phoenix, Tempe, Mesa or Chandler?

Yes. A Level III can deliver training and practical exams at your facility anywhere in the Phoenix metro, including Glendale, Goodyear, Scottsdale and Pinal County sites.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Phoenix?

No. Atlantis delivers training live online and onsite at your facility. We do not have a physical campus in Arizona.

Can I use WIOA or the GI Bill for NDT training in Arizona?

Those programmes require an approved school or an eligible training provider listing, such as the Pima Community College certificate on Arizona's list. Atlantis does not claim those approvals. Employer-paid training is the common alternative.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in Phoenix?

Yes, through live online Level III exam preparation covering the Basic examination and method exams. See ASNT Level III training.

Do you offer CWI, API or NAS 410 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some Phoenix employers also ask for those credentials, but they are separate programmes.

NDT Training and Certification in Quebec

Short answer: Quebec employers and technicians can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and II, plus Level III exam preparation. You can join live online classes or a private live-virtual cohort, or we can train onsite at your plant, shop, smelter or yard. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every course, and your employer certifies you under its written practice.

Quebec needs more candour than most markets, so here it is up front. Canada's national NDT certification scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712. Quebec's large aerospace sector mostly works under NAS 410 or EN 4179 programmes required by aircraft and engine makers. Atlantis NDT does not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ISO 9712 or NAS 410, and we claim no CGSB recognition. What we teach is the American employer-based scheme, SNT-TC-1A. In Quebec it suits a narrower but real group: heavy fabricators and equipment makers building ASME- or API-code products for US customers, plants owned by US-headquartered companies whose corporate standards reference SNT-TC-1A, suppliers to US industrial buyers, inspection companies that send crews to New York, Vermont, New England or Ontario jobs with US clients, and technicians who intend to work in the US. This page explains where that fit is real and where it is not, maps Quebec's NDT economy from Montreal to the Côte-Nord, and shows how to request a Quebec NDT training quote. We usually reply within one business day.

SNT-TC-1A, CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or NAS 410: what Quebec work requires

Direct answer: Canadian-code work in Quebec, including structures, bridges, many pressure-equipment jobs and federal projects, usually requires CAN/CGSB-48.9712. Aerospace production mostly requires NAS 410 or EN 4179 programmes. SNT-TC-1A is the right fit for US-code fabrication, US customers and US-owned plants that specify it, and for technicians who plan to work in the US.

Quebec situationScheme usually expectedDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
Aircraft, engine and landing gear production in Greater MontrealNAS 410 / EN 4179, plus the prime's own requirementsNo. NAS 410 programmes need their own route, which we do not offer
Structural steel and bridges under CSA W59 / CSA S6CAN/CGSB-48.9712 through CSA W178.1 inspection organisationsNo, not on its own
Hydroelectric, federal shipbuilding and public infrastructure contractsContract specification, typically CGSB or ISO 9712 basedUsually no. Check the contract
ASME vessels, heat exchangers, B31.3 piping and turbine or penstock components built in Quebec for US buyersSNT-TC-1A through ASME Section V and the clientYes. This is the core case
US-owned refinery, smelter or chemical plant whose corporate standard accepts SNT-TC-1AOwner specificationYes, where the owner accepts it
Quebec technicians heading to New York, Vermont or other US workThe US employer's SNT-TC-1A written practiceYes

The Canadian scheme is in transition. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Published guidance says the standard remains valid through its current cycle and that existing certificates are unaffected. Natural Resources Canada's NDT Certification Body has said its certification services continue without interruption, and the CWB Group remains accredited to certify NDT personnel to the same standard. Confirm the current certification body before you build a CGSB plan. If what you need is a CGSB or NAS 410 certificate, we will tell you on the first call.

Where NDT technicians work in Quebec

Direct answer: Quebec NDT work concentrates in Greater Montreal's aerospace, refining, rail and fabrication base, the Quebec City and Lévis refining and shipbuilding area, the aluminium smelters of Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, the Côte-Nord and the St. Lawrence, Hydro-Québec's dams and generating stations, the Bécancour and Trois-Rivières industrial parks, and the mining regions of Abitibi-Témiscamingue and the Côte-Nord.

Greater Montreal: aerospace, refining and manufacturing

Montreal is one of the world's main aerospace centres. Business jets, the A220 line at Mirabel, gas-turbine engines in Longueuil, helicopters, landing gear, flight simulators and a large airline and MRO base all sit in the metropolitan area. Production NDT in these plants is mostly PT, MT, ET, UT and RT done under NAS 410 or EN 4179 programmes, and Atlantis does not position itself as a route into them. Montreal East also has a refinery, petrochemical plants, pipeline terminals and port facilities. The wider region has rail-car and transit manufacturing, metal fabrication, foundries and heavy equipment builders, many of which export to US buyers. That is where SNT-TC-1A training is relevant: UT and MT on ASME and AWS fabrication, PT on stainless equipment, RT on piping welds. See NDT training in Montreal, Practical NDT in Montreal and the NDT ERP for Montreal inspection companies.

Quebec City and Lévis

Lévis, across the river from Quebec City, has the province's other large refinery and the Chantier Davie shipyard, which builds and refits federal and commercial vessels. The Quebec City region adds pulp and paper, food processing, manufacturing and the port. Refinery turnarounds bring UT and PAUT corrosion work, RT on repair welds, ET on exchangers, and MT and PT on rotating equipment. Shipyard work is heavy on UT thickness, MT and VT, often under federal or class-society specifications. See Practical NDT in Quebec City.

Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean and the aluminium belt

Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean is one of the largest aluminium-producing regions in the world. Smelters there, and others at Bécancour, Deschambault, Baie-Comeau and Sept-Îles, run pot lines, anode plants, casting centres, gas-treatment systems, cranes and heavy structures that need MT and UT on welds and lifting equipment, thickness surveys on ducts and piping, and VT throughout. Port Alfred, hydro stations and paper mills add more. See Practical NDT in Saguenay.

Hydro-Québec's generating system

Quebec runs on hydroelectricity: the La Grande complex in James Bay, the Manicouagan and Outardes stations on the Côte-Nord, the Romaine complex and dozens of smaller stations. Penstocks, gates, spiral cases, turbine runners, shafts and generator components get periodic UT, MT, PT and VT, and new-build and refurbishment projects add fabrication NDT. Most of this work follows Canadian contract specifications. Turbine and penstock component makers in Quebec that also sell to US utilities are the ones that most often need an SNT-TC-1A programme.

Bécancour, Trois-Rivières and the St. Lawrence corridor

The Bécancour industrial park on the south shore holds chemical, metals and, more recently, battery-materials plants. Trois-Rivières and Shawinigan add pulp and paper, metal processing and manufacturing. Process plants mean pressure vessels and piping inspected under Quebec's pressure installation rules, with UT, PT, RT and ET as the core methods.

Mining regions: Abitibi-Témiscamingue and the Côte-Nord

Abitibi-Témiscamingue holds major gold mines around Malartic, Val-d'Or and Rouyn-Noranda, along with a copper smelter. The Côte-Nord has iron-ore mines around Fermont, pellet plants, rail lines to the coast and port terminals at Port-Cartier and Sept-Îles. Mining equipment, crushers, mills, conveyors, haul trucks and ore cars need MT and UT on welds, shafts and structures. These sites are remote, so online theory plus onsite practicals is the only sensible model.

Rail, bridges and public infrastructure

Quebec has major rail-car and transit manufacturing, the Montreal metro and REM networks, and a large provincial bridge and overpass inventory. Infrastructure owners in Canada generally specify CSA W59, CSA S6 and CGSB-certified personnel. That is a common reason SNT-TC-1A certification alone will not satisfy a Quebec contract. Rail equipment built for US transit agencies or freight railways may follow US specifications instead.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Quebec employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table maps each method to typical Quebec work where SNT-TC-1A applies. Your employer's written practice sets the exact hours.

Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepEncoded weld scans on heavy fabrication, corrosion mapping in refineries and chemical plantsUT Level II recommended first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepHeavy-wall vessels and thick fabrication weldsUT Level II recommended

For ASNT Level III, the Level III training programme prepares candidates for the Basic and method examinations online. A CGSB Level 3 or a NAS 410 Level 3 role follows different requirements and is outside our scope.

NDT training by city in Quebec

Direct answer: Atlantis has a dedicated NDT training page for Montreal and Practical NDT simulator pages for Montreal, Quebec City and Saguenay. Every Quebec region is served the same way, with live online classes and onsite delivery at the employer's site. We have no classroom in Quebec.

Quebec City and LévisRefining, shipbuilding, pulp and paper, manufacturingQuebec City simulator practice

Montreal. In Montreal the first question is which scheme your customer requires. For aerospace production, it is almost always NAS 410 or EN 4179. For heavy fabrication, pumps, valves and pressure equipment sold to US industry, it is usually SNT-TC-1A. We work with the second group, and with technicians planning US careers.

Quebec City and Lévis. Refinery and industrial maintenance contractors here schedule training before turnaround seasons. Shipyard work generally follows federal or class specifications.

Saguenay. Smelter maintenance teams and their contractors usually need MT and UT Level II on cranes, structures and pressure equipment. If the plant owner's corporate standard references SNT-TC-1A, we can train in-house staff and support their certification under the employer's written practice.

Côte-Nord and Abitibi. Remote mining and smelting employers need training that comes to them. Online theory and a short onsite practical block avoid sending staff on a long trip south.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Quebec, step by step

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A, a Quebec employer certifies its own technicians. That happens after classroom training, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and a vision test, all as the employer's written practice requires. The certification belongs to that employer's programme. It is not a Canadian national certificate and not an aerospace NAS 410 certification.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts an SNT-TC-1A written practice that sets hours, exams and recertification. We can prepare one with you: written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete the required formal hours, live online or onsite. The training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method and level.
  3. Experience. Log supervised on-the-job hours in the method on real work, with records kept by your employer.
  4. Exams. General, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III.
  5. Vision test. Near-vision and colour contrast, normally annual.
  6. Employer certification. The employer certifies you for the method and level. A new employer recertifies you under its own practice.
  7. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets.

If you are also working toward CGSB certification, keep one experience log that can support both schemes, and check the certification body's evidence rules early.

Radiography licensing and other Quebec requirements

Direct answer: gamma radiography in Quebec is federally regulated by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. Operators must be CNSC-certified exposure device operators or work under the direct supervision of one. Pressure installations are regulated by the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ), and owners must have their equipment inspected by organisations the RBQ recognises.

Industrial radiography

The CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices in Quebec as in every province. There is no Agreement State model. Operating a gamma exposure device requires CNSC exposure device operator (EDO) certification or direct supervision by a certified EDO. CNSC guidance describes formal EDO vocational training and a supervised on-the-job programme before the written exam, and CSA PCP-09 is the certification guide. Atlantis RT training covers technique, image quality and interpretation to code acceptance criteria. It does not replace EDO certification. X-ray equipment falls under provincial rules, so confirm current requirements with your radiation safety officer.

Pressure installations: RBQ

The RBQ administers Quebec's rules on boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping. Under them, the owner-user of a pressure installation must have it inspected by an organisation the RBQ recognises. Quebec references CSA B51, the ASME code sections and the BNQ 3650-900 installation code, among others. Manufacturers outside Canada register equipment through ASME and the National Board as well. Ask the RBQ, your recognised inspection organisation and the owner which NDE personnel certification they accept for each job.

Pipelines

Interprovincial pipelines serving Montreal and the St. Lawrence corridor fall under the Canada Energy Regulator. CSA Z662 is the core pipeline standard, and API 1104 appears on projects with US owners or contractors. Gas distribution within Quebec follows provincial rules.

Language

Quebec employers have French-language obligations under the Charter of the French Language, including for many workplace documents. When you ask for a quote, tell us the language needs of your crew and your documentation, and we will tell you honestly what we can provide.

Codes common in Quebec work

ASME Section V, VIII and IX, ASME B31.1 and B31.3, CSA B51, CSA Z662, CSA W59 and CSA S6, AWS D1.1 for US-bound structural steel, API 650 and 653 for tanks, and NAS 410 / EN 4179 in aerospace. Quebec companies that sell into the US often work to both Canadian and US codes on the same shop floor.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Quebec

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers Quebec training as live online seats, private live-virtual cohorts, or onsite training at your plant, shop, smelter or mine site with a Level III instructor. Theory can be done from anywhere in the province. Practical sessions use real specimens at your site.

Quebec covers vast distances. Sept-Îles, Fermont, Chibougamau or Rouyn-Noranda are a long way from any training room in Montreal or Quebec City. Online theory keeps people at work, and onsite practicals keep training tied to the welds, castings and procedures your technicians actually inspect. We schedule around smelter and mill shutdowns, refinery turnarounds in Montreal East and Lévis, hydro maintenance outages and the construction-holiday period many Quebec employers observe in summer.

  • Live online seats for individuals anywhere in Quebec.
  • Private live-virtual cohorts built around your codes and procedures.
  • Onsite at your facility with your equipment and specimens, including practical exam support under your written practice.
  • Blended online theory, simulator practice and a short onsite practical block.

We have no classroom in Quebec. Ask about onsite training for your Quebec team, or see online NDT training and corporate NDT training.

For Quebec employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Quebec employers that need SNT-TC-1A certification for US customers or US-code products need a written practice, a Level III for exams and procedure approval, and records an auditor can follow. Atlantis provides these remotely or onsite. That includes employers that keep CGSB-certified staff for Canadian contracts.

Typical Quebec cases include a pressure-vessel or heat-exchanger shop on the South Shore that wins a US order calling for SNT-TC-1A personnel, a turbine or penstock component maker supplying a US utility, a plant whose US parent's corporate inspection standard references SNT-TC-1A, and an inspection company sending crews to US jobs across the border. We help with:

  • SNT-TC-1A written practice development and revision (written practice development);
  • outside Level III services: exam preparation and grading, procedure and technique review;
  • clear records of which technicians hold SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or customer-specific qualifications for each job;
  • preparation for customer and third-party audits of your NDT programme;
  • certification, training and vision records in software that tracks ASNT and CGSB certificates together (Atlantis NDT ERP).

See SNT-TC-1A training and certification for employers and NDT consulting in Canada. Book a Level III consultation for your Quebec company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator gives Quebec trainees browser-based practice in 12 methods across 5 virtual environments before their hands-on exam. It is a practice tool only. It does not replace the practical examination on real specimens that your written practice, a CGSB scheme or a NAS 410 programme requires.

The NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank environments cover fabrication welds, process piping, tanks and aircraft structures. Trainees at remote smelters and mines can practise between shifts, and supervisors can use the simulator to check readiness before booking practical exam time. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT in Quebec. For written questions, try the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He prepares the course content, the examinations and the employer written practices. He will give you a straight answer on whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or an aerospace scheme is what your Quebec work actually needs.

NDT training in Quebec: frequently asked questions

How do I get NDT certified in Quebec?

For most Canadian-code work, get CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712) certification through an accredited certification body. Confirm the current certification body, as arrangements changed in 2026. Aerospace production uses NAS 410 or EN 4179 programmes run by employers. For US customers and US-code work, your employer certifies you under SNT-TC-1A, which is the only route Atlantis trains for.

Is there online NDT training in Quebec?

Yes. Atlantis runs live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes that Quebec technicians can join from anywhere in the province, with practicals on real specimens at the employer's site. See online NDT training.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB, ISO 9712 or NAS 410 training in Quebec?

No. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only. We claim no CGSB recognition and do not run NAS 410 or EN 4179 programmes. If those are what your job needs, choose a provider on that route.

Is SNT-TC-1A useful for Montreal aerospace jobs?

For most aerospace production roles, no. Those employers certify under NAS 410 or EN 4179. SNT-TC-1A is more useful in Montreal's heavy fabrication, pressure equipment, refining and industrial sectors that serve US customers.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Quebec?

For gamma radiography, yes. You need CNSC exposure device operator certification, or direct supervision by a certified EDO, and your employer needs a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment follows provincial rules.

How much does NDT training cost in Quebec?

It is quoted on request. The price depends on the method and level, group size, online or onsite delivery, travel to remote regions, and whether you also need a written practice or Level III services. Cohort and onsite quotes usually come back within one business day. Request a Quebec quote.

Which NDT methods are most in demand in Quebec?

UT and MT dominate in heavy industry, smelting, mining and hydro. PT and ET are central in aerospace and process plants, RT in fabrication and piping, and PAUT and TOFD on heavy-wall fabrication and refinery work.

Can you train our team onsite in Saguenay, Lévis or Sept-Îles?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your plant, shop or mine site is a standard option. The instructor uses your equipment and specimens and supports practical exams under your written practice.

Is training available in French?

Tell us your crew's language needs when you ask for a quote and we will tell you honestly what we can provide. Quebec employers also have French-language obligations for workplace documents under the Charter of the French Language.

How long does UT Level II training take?

Your employer's written practice decides. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours, listed in the training requirements matrix, and the experience usually takes the longest.

Can I use SNT-TC-1A to work in New York or Vermont?

SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer that issues it. A US employer will review your documented training and experience and certify you under its own written practice. Well-kept training records make that review straightforward.

Can I become an ASNT Level III in Quebec?

Yes. Prepare for the ASNT Basic and method examinations online with our Level III preparation. For context on pay across levels, see the NDT salary guide.

Get a quote for NDT training in Quebec

Atlantis NDT can help whether you need a South Shore fabricator's UT and MT technicians trained for a US ASME order, an SNT-TC-1A written practice for a plant whose US parent requires one, Level II training for a smelter maintenance team, or ASNT Level III preparation for a quality manager. We will be clear when CGSB or an aerospace scheme is the right answer instead. Request your Quebec training quote, read about Atlantis NDT training, or see NDT training across Canada. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

NDT Training and Certification in San Francisco, CA

San Francisco Bay Area technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, private live-virtual cohorts, or onsite courses at their own refinery, hangar, shop or jobsite anywhere from Richmond and Martinez to Oakland, SFO and Silicon Valley. An ASNT NDT Level III leads each course, and the hours are recorded against the employer's written practice so they count toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

The Bay Area's NDT market looks nothing like a typical industrial city. Refining is concentrated along the northern shore of San Pablo Bay and the Carquinez Strait, where Chevron Richmond and the Martinez refinery still process crude while Rodeo and Martinez have neighbours that converted to renewable fuels and Benicia has stopped refining. Around the bay sit airline maintenance at SFO, Travis Air Force Base, NASA Ames and Lockheed Martin Space, ship repair yards, the Port of Oakland, toll bridges and BART, and the strictest seismic building rules in the country, which make structural weld inspection a steady source of work. Silicon Valley's precision and semiconductor-equipment manufacturers add another layer. This page is built around that map. If you already know what you need, request a Bay Area training quote and we reply within one business day.

Quick facts for San Francisco and the Bay AreaAnswer
Certification schemeASNT SNT-TC-1A, employer-based: your written practice governs
Training hours and experienceSet per method and level by your written practice; see the NDT training requirements matrix for the recommended minimums
DeliveryLive online, live-virtual cohort, or onsite at your Bay Area facility. No physical Atlantis centre in San Francisco
ExamsGeneral, specific and practical, administered under a Level III, plus an annual vision test
Radiography licensingCalifornia is an NRC Agreement State; RT is licensed by the CDPH Radiologic Health Branch, which also issues radiographer identification
PriceQuote on request, usually within one business day

NDT training in San Francisco: how it works for Bay Area employers and technicians

In the Bay Area, NDT certification under SNT-TC-1A is granted by your employer. You complete classroom training per method and level, build supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Atlantis NDT delivers the training, Level III oversight and records, online or onsite at your facility.

There are few classroom NDT schools in the Bay Area, and searchers for "NDT training San Francisco" mostly find independent Level III consultants, directory listings and national companies whose nearest classrooms are in Southern California or out of state. Travelling for a week of classroom training is costly here, both in time and in the price of hotels and lost shifts. That is why the Atlantis model, live online theory with practical training and exams at the employer's own site, fits the Bay Area especially well.

What matters is that the training is accepted by your employer's Level III. Under SNT-TC-1A, the employer's written practice decides the training hours, experience, exam content and pass marks, and the Level III signs off. A training provider supplies documented hours and preparation; it cannot issue a "licence" every employer must accept. Atlantis records show method, level, topics, contact hours, instructor and exam results, laid out to be filed against your written practice and shown to a refinery owner's or customer's auditor. Employers can also have us write or revise the written practice, act as outside Level III and administer exams.

Two hypothetical Bay Area examples. Suppose a mechanical contractor working turnarounds in Contra Costa County needs four technicians moved from UT Level I to Level II before the next shutdown season: live-online theory in evening blocks, then onsite practical days on their own piping specimens, then exams under their written practice. Or suppose a testing agency in Oakland needs VT and UT Level II inspectors for steel moment-frame welds on a hospital project: a private cohort focused on AWS D1.1 and D1.8 work, with practical sessions on welded mock-ups.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in San Francisco

Atlantis NDT runs SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. Bay Area employers most often ask for UT, PAUT and RT for refinery and pipeline work, VT and UT for seismic structural welds, ET and PT for aircraft maintenance, and PT and VT for precision and semiconductor-equipment manufacturing.

MethodLevelsWhat Bay Area employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepRefinery piping and vessel thickness, structural steel welds on seismic frames, bridge and tank inspectionNone for Level I; Level I hours and experience for Level II per written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, IIRefinery and pipeline welds, corrosion mapping, encoded weld records that replace RT on some jobsUsually UT Level II first
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, IISizing flaws in thick pressure-vessel and heavy structural weldsUsually UT Level II first
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, IIProcess piping, pipeline tie-ins, castings and pressure parts; film, CR and DRRadiation safety training plus California radiographer rules
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, IIStructural steel, bridge members, lifting gear, ship repairNone for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, IIAircraft parts, stainless welds, vacuum and process components in precision manufacturingNone for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, IIStructural weld inspection, refinery in-service visual checks, fabrication receiving inspectionNone for Level I
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, IIAircraft structure and engine inspection, heat-exchanger tubing in refineries and power plantsNone for Level I

Course detail: UT Level 1, UT Level 2, PAUT Level 2, TOFD, RT Level 2, MT Level 2, PT Level 1, PT Level 2, VT Level 2, ET Level 1, ET Level 2. Level III candidates: ASNT Level III training. Aerospace-focused technicians can also see aerospace NDT training.

Method spotlight for the Bay Area: UT for seismic structural welds. After the 1994 Northridge earthquake exposed brittle fractures in welded steel moment-frame connections, California's building rules and the AWS D1.8 seismic supplement put much more weight on inspection of demand-critical welds. In San Francisco, Oakland and San Jose, special inspection under Chapter 17 of the California Building Code means testing agencies need UT technicians who can scan complete-joint-penetration welds, size indications and report to the engineer of record. Combine that with VT and MT and you have one of the most reliable sources of NDT work in the region, independent of refinery cycles.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in San Francisco, step by step

The path is written practice, formal training, experience, general, specific and practical exams, vision test, employer certification and recertification. Your employer's written practice sets hours, exam content and pass marks; in the Bay Area the codes behind the specific exam vary widely by sector.

  1. Identify the written practice that covers your method and level. No written practice? See written practice development.
  2. Complete formal training, live online or onsite. Recommended minimums are in the training requirements matrix; your employer may require more.
  3. Log supervised experience in the method. Refinery turnarounds and construction projects are common ways to build hours.
  4. Pass the general exam on method principles.
  5. Pass the specific exam on your employer's procedures and codes, such as ASME Section V, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or D1.8, or aircraft maintenance manuals.
  6. Pass the practical exam on real specimens under a Level III. This part is never online-only.
  7. Pass the vision test: near-vision acuity and colour contrast as required.
  8. Receive employer certification, signed by the Level III and valid while you work for that employer.
  9. Recertify on the interval in your written practice.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Bay Area crews

Atlantis NDT has no training centre in San Francisco. Theory runs live online or as a private live-virtual cohort; practical training and exams take place onsite at your Bay Area facility or an arranged site under Level III supervision. That avoids Bay Area travel and lets you schedule around turnarounds and project milestones.

Bay Area traffic and costs make a strong case for bringing training to the crew. Refinery contractors in Richmond, Martinez and Benicia work to turnaround calendars; testing agencies follow construction schedules; airline maintenance runs around the clock. Live online theory can be split into shorter blocks, including evenings, so technicians keep working, and onsite practical sessions can be fitted into quieter weeks. Training on your own specimens, equipment and acceptance criteria also makes the specific and practical exams far more relevant.

  • Live online: scheduled instructor-led classes with a Level III, open to individual technicians.
  • Live-virtual cohort: a private online class for your team.
  • Onsite: theory and practical at your plant, hangar, shop or jobsite in San Francisco, Alameda, Contra Costa, Solano, San Mateo or Santa Clara counties.
  • Blended: theory online, followed by a short onsite block for practical training and exams.

More on online NDT training and corporate NDT training. To plan a cohort, ask about onsite NDT training for your Bay Area crew.

Where NDT technicians work in the San Francisco Bay Area

Bay Area NDT work clusters in refining and renewable fuels along San Pablo Bay and the Carquinez Strait, aviation and aerospace (SFO, Travis AFB, NASA Ames, Lockheed Martin Space), seismic structural construction, bridges and transit, ports and ship repair, gas and electric utilities, and precision manufacturing in Silicon Valley.

Refining and renewable fuels: Richmond, Martinez, Rodeo, Benicia

Chevron's Richmond refinery and the Martinez refinery are the region's main crude-oil refineries. Phillips 66 converted its Rodeo refinery to renewable fuels, and the former Marathon refinery in Martinez now produces renewable diesel. Valero ended refining at Benicia in 2026, with the site continuing as a fuel import and storage terminal. Even with fewer crude units, these sites run tanks, piping, heat exchangers and pressure vessels that need UT thickness, PAUT, RT, ET tubing inspection, MT and PT during turnarounds. Atlantis teaches the NDT methods used on this work; API inspector programmes are separate and not part of our training. Nearby city pages: NDT training in Martinez.

Aviation and aerospace

United Airlines runs a large maintenance operation at San Francisco International Airport, Travis Air Force Base near Fairfield hosts airlift and refuelling aircraft, and NASA Ames Research Center and Lockheed Martin Space sit at Moffett Field and Sunnyvale. Aircraft work relies on ET, PT, UT and visual inspection to manufacturer and maintenance manual procedures. Many aerospace employers certify NDT personnel to NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A, so check your employer's requirement before choosing training.

Seismic construction, bridges and transit

High-rise, hospital, school and data-centre construction around the bay requires special inspection of structural steel welds. San Francisco's Department of Building Inspection oversees special inspections in the city, the Division of the State Architect oversees public school projects, and the state's health-facility agency oversees hospitals. Caltrans operates the state-owned toll bridges, including the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge, while the Golden Gate Bridge has its own district; BART and Caltrain maintain rail structures. All of this means VT, MT and UT to AWS D1.1, D1.5 and D1.8.

Ports, ship repair and marine terminals

The Port of Oakland is one of the busiest container ports on the West Coast, and ship repair yards operate in Alameda and Vallejo. Hull, crane and terminal-structure inspection uses UT thickness, MT and VT. Work inside secure port and refinery areas typically requires a TWIC card.

Utilities, pipelines and precision manufacturing

PG&E's gas transmission system has been under intense integrity scrutiny since the 2010 San Bruno pipeline explosion, and pipeline welds are inspected to API 1104 with RT and PAUT. Gas-fired power plants in the Delta add boiler and piping work. In Fremont and across Silicon Valley, automotive, semiconductor-equipment and precision manufacturers use PT, VT, ET and UT on welded vacuum, gas and structural components.

Radiography licensing and other California requirements

California is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is licensed by the California Department of Public Health, Radiologic Health Branch, and radiographers must hold California-recognised radiographer certification and a CDPH-issued identification card before doing industrial radiography in the state.

California's rules (Title 17 of the California Code of Regulations, which incorporates the federal radiography rules in 10 CFR Part 34) are stricter than many states'. Radiographers who are certified in another Agreement State or through ASNT's Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel programme may be able to obtain a provisional California identification card; otherwise the state's own certification route applies. For a Bay Area RT technician, this means two separate qualifications: the SNT-TC-1A RT Level II certificate from your employer, and California radiation-safety certification and identification. Atlantis RT courses teach the NDT method; radiation-safety qualification follows your employer's licence and CDPH rules. Confirm current requirements with CDPH before starting RT work.

Other authorities: boilers and pressure vessels fall under Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit; gas pipelines are regulated by the California Public Utilities Commission and hazardous-liquid pipelines by the Office of the State Fire Marshal, with interstate lines under PHMSA. Refineries also operate under Cal/OSHA's process safety management rules for petroleum refineries. Codes commonly met in the Bay Area: ASME Section V and VIII, ASME B31.3, API 1104, AWS D1.1, D1.5 and D1.8, and the California Building Code.

Local options compared: Bay Area NDT training and Atlantis

The Bay Area has the ASNT Golden Gate Section, independent Level III consultants, and community colleges with welding programmes, but few classroom NDT schools. National training companies teach mainly in Southern California or out of state. Atlantis NDT brings SNT-TC-1A training to you, online or onsite, with Level III support.

These options can be combined. A welding graduate still needs employer NDT certification; a company with an independent Level III can still use Atlantis for crew training or additional methods.

Level III services and written practices for Bay Area NDT companies

Bay Area testing agencies, refinery contractors and manufacturers can use Atlantis NDT for a written practice, an outside Level III, exam administration and audit preparation, so training becomes certifications that stand up to owners, building officials and customer auditors.

Refinery owners audit contractor NDT qualifications closely, and building departments and state agencies expect special inspectors to show proper certification records. Smaller firms often lack a Level III on staff or rely on a written practice that no longer matches their procedures. Atlantis can write or revise the written practice (written practice development), act as Level III, set and grade exams, and organise the records auditors look for. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification and the employer certification programme.

For Level III consulting in the city, see NDT consulting in San Francisco; for refinery-corridor work, refining NDT consulting in Richmond, NDT consulting in Martinez, Rodeo and Benicia; statewide, NDT consulting in California. To talk it through, book a Level III consultation for your Bay Area company.

Practise before the practical exam

The practical exam is done on real specimens under a Level III, onsite at your employer or an arranged site. Before that, Bay Area trainees can practise 12 methods in five environments on the Practical NDT 3D simulator. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam.

Environments include an NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank, which line up well with Bay Area refinery, hangar and structural work. Start at Practical NDT for the Bay Area refinery corridor, Practical NDT in California or the main Practical NDT page.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He designs course content, reviews written practices and oversees exams so training records hold up to employer, owner and customer audits.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in San Francisco

How do I get NDT certified in San Francisco?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete formal training, log the required experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and, for employers, Level III services and exams.

How much does an NDT course cost in the Bay Area?

It depends on methods, levels, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery and the practical specimens required. Atlantis quotes on request, usually within one business day. Request a San Francisco NDT course quote.

How much does NDT school cost?

College programmes and short certification courses are different products. Colleges publish tuition; short-course pricing depends on scope. In the Bay Area, also count travel and time off work, which onsite or online delivery avoids.

How long is the NDT training course?

Each method and level has recommended training and experience hours, and your employer's written practice may require more. See the training requirements matrix. Online theory can be split into shorter sessions.

Which NDT certification is best?

The one your employer and its customers require. For most US industrial and construction work that is SNT-TC-1A employer certification; many aerospace employers use NAS 410; Level III candidates often add ASNT's own Level III certificate. In California, RT also needs state radiographer certification.

Which NDT course is best to start with in the Bay Area?

VT and UT, because structural special inspection and refinery work both need them. Add MT for steel, ET and PT for aviation, and PAUT after UT Level II.

Can I take NDT training online in California?

Yes, for theory. The practical training and exam need real specimens and a Level III, completed onsite at your employer or an arranged site. See NDT training online.

Do I need a license for radiography in California?

Yes. Your employer needs a CDPH radioactive materials licence, and you need California-recognised radiographer certification and a CDPH identification card. An SNT-TC-1A RT certificate alone is not enough.

Can you train our crew onsite in Richmond, Oakland or San Jose?

Yes. Onsite delivery is how Atlantis trains most crews, with theory and practical at your site, scheduled around turnarounds or project milestones. Plan onsite NDT training in the Bay Area.

Do I need a TWIC card for NDT work in the Bay Area?

For unescorted access to secure areas of the Port of Oakland and many marine and refinery terminals, yes. Your employer or site will tell you; it is separate from NDT certification.

Is SNT-TC-1A certification recognised by Bay Area employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer certification in US industry and construction inspection. Recognition always runs through the employer's written practice, so training records must match it.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA for NDT training?

Those programmes generally require an approved school or provider, and Atlantis does not claim those approvals. Check with the programme administrator; many Bay Area technicians are trained through employer-paid programmes.

Where else in California does Atlantis offer NDT training?

See the California NDT training hub, Southern California, Los Angeles, Martinez, the West Coast hub and the US training locations.

Get started

Tell us your methods, levels, headcount and timing, and we reply with a plan and quote within one business day. Request your Bay Area NDT training quote, or start with the training overview.

NDT Training and Certification in San Jose, CA

Short answer: San Jose and Silicon Valley technicians and employers can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training with Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at the employer's own lab, fab, machine shop or plant. Courses cover Level I and Level II in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every programme, and your employer certifies you under its written practice.

Silicon Valley is not the first place most people associate with nondestructive testing, and that is exactly why so many searches for "NDT training San Jose" end in frustration. The valley's inspection demand is real but scattered: semiconductor equipment makers in Santa Clara, Fremont and Milpitas, space and defence hardware in Sunnyvale, electric-vehicle and battery manufacturing in Fremont, precision machine shops and welding contractors across San Jose's industrial districts, data-centre and fab construction, utility gas and power assets, and the refinery corridor an hour north in Contra Costa County. Few of these employers can spare a technician for weeks of classroom time out of state, and many need training that follows their own written practice rather than a generic syllabus. Atlantis NDT does not run a training centre in San Jose. Instead, theory is delivered live online or onsite at your facility, and the practical work happens on real specimens under a Level III. Request a San Jose NDT training quote and we reply with options within one business day.

At a glanceWhat it means for San Jose trainees
Certification schemeASNT SNT-TC-1A (employer-based); your employer's written practice sets the rules
Formal training hoursSet per method and level in your written practice; see the SNT-TC-1A training requirements matrix
On-the-job experienceLogged at your employer and verified by its Level III; also listed in the matrix
ExamsGeneral, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, plus an annual vision test
DeliveryLive online, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite at your San Jose or Bay Area facility
CommercialsQuote on request; cohort and onsite quotes within one business day

NDT training in San Jose: how it works for Silicon Valley employers and technicians

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A you are certified by your employer, not by a school. Training gives you the classroom hours your written practice requires; your employer then logs on-the-job experience, a Level III gives you general, specific and practical exams, and you pass a vision test. Atlantis delivers the training and can provide the Level III services that make the rest of the process work.

That model suits Silicon Valley well. Most local NDT work is done in-house by manufacturers and their suppliers rather than by large field-service contractors, so the person searching for training is often a quality manager who needs two or three technicians qualified in PT or VT for a specific product line, or a machine shop that has just won aerospace or semiconductor-equipment work and must show a customer auditor a compliant certification file. For those employers, the important thing is not just a course certificate but an auditable chain: a written practice, training records, experience logs, exam papers and grading, vision test records, and a Level III who signs off. Atlantis can supply the training portion alone, or the whole chain through our SNT-TC-1A training and certification support.

For individual technicians, the path is the same with one difference: you need an employer, or a prospective employer, whose written practice will recognise the training. Many Bay Area job postings for NDT technicians ask for Level II in one or two methods, and the classroom hours you complete with Atlantis are documented so that a new employer's Level III can review and accept them. We tell trainees honestly that a training certificate on its own is a training record; certification happens when an employer qualifies you under its written practice.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in San Jose

Direct answer: Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation, delivered live online or onsite anywhere in Santa Clara County and the wider Bay Area. The table shows how San Jose employers typically use each method and what a trainee needs before starting.

MethodLevelsWhat San Jose employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepBond and weld inspection on vacuum chambers and frames for semiconductor tools, thickness checks on utility and process piping, aerospace forgings and machined partsLevel I: per employer. Level II: Level I training plus documented experience
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepWeld inspection on fab and data-centre construction, pressure equipment, composite and bonded structures for space hardwareUT Level II recommended first
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-wall welds on pressure vessels and power equipment; refinery work in the East BayUT Level II recommended first
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepCastings and welds for aerospace and defence suppliers, pipeline and plant piping welds, digital and computed radiography in labsRadiation safety training and California radiographer requirements apply before working with sources
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepStructural steel welds, ferrous machined parts, rail and transit components, heavy equipmentPer employer
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepNon-ferrous machined parts, aluminium and stainless chambers, aerospace and medical-device components, weld surfacesPer employer
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld and fabrication acceptance, borescope inspection, construction QA on fabs and data centres, incoming inspectionPer employer; vision test always required
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepSurface crack detection on aerospace parts, conductivity and coating checks, tubing inspectionPer employer

Level III preparation covers the ASNT Basic examination topics and method examinations for candidates who want to become the Level III of record for a San Jose company. See ASNT Level III training for the structure of that programme.

Method spotlight: PT, VT and ET for precision manufacturing

In most US cities the busiest NDT methods are UT and RT on welds. In Silicon Valley the mix tilts toward surface methods. Semiconductor-equipment makers and their machine-shop supply chain work with aluminium, stainless steel, titanium and specialty alloys, and the defects that matter are often surface-breaking: cracks from machining or heat treatment, porosity in welds on vacuum chambers, and laps or seams in bar stock. Liquid penetrant and visual testing are the workhorses here, with eddy current used for conductivity checks and fast crack screening on aerospace parts. If you are setting up an in-house programme for a precision shop, starting with PT and VT Level II for two or three people and a Level III of record is often the most practical first step. Ask about a PT and VT starter programme for your San Jose shop.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in San Jose, step by step

Direct answer: the path runs from your employer's written practice, through formal training and on-the-job experience, to Level III-administered exams, a vision test and employer certification. Hours and experience vary by method and level, so check the training requirements matrix and your employer's written practice rather than relying on a single number.

  1. Written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A that sets training hours, experience, exam rules and recertification. If you do not have one, Atlantis can write it: see NDT written practice development.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete the method and level hours the written practice requires, live online or onsite in San Jose. Attendance and topics are documented.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience in the method at your employer, on real parts, welds or components.
  4. General exam. A written exam on method principles, administered under the Level III's control.
  5. Specific exam. A written exam on your employer's procedures, codes and specifications, for example ASME Section V, AWS D1.1 or customer specifications.
  6. Practical exam. You inspect real specimens with known flaws using the employer's equipment and procedures, and write up the results.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated annually.
  8. Certification. The employer certifies you in writing, at the level and in the method you qualified for.
  9. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets, by evidence of continuing work and/or re-examination.

How the practical exam works when theory is online

Direct answer: the theory can be taught online, but the practical exam cannot. It always happens on real specimens under a Level III, either onsite at your San Jose facility with your own equipment and procedures, or at a location arranged with your employer. The Practical NDT simulator is for rehearsal only.

This is the part of online NDT training that is most often explained badly, so here is exactly how Atlantis handles it for Bay Area employers. The classroom portion is taught live by a Level III instructor in scheduled sessions, with questions answered in real time, quizzes, and worked examples on the codes your company uses. When the trainee has completed the required hours and logged experience, the practical examination is arranged. For a company with its own equipment and parts, the simplest route is an onsite visit: the Level III comes to your facility, uses specimens with documented discontinuities, and examines the trainee on the procedure they will actually use at work. For a smaller shop without suitable specimens, we agree a practical plan with you before training starts, so nobody is surprised at the end. Either way, the result is a set of graded exam records your auditor can review.

Local NDT training options in San Jose and the Bay Area

Direct answer: San Jose trainees can choose between a public college apprenticeship, established private Level III training providers in the Bay Area, national schools with fixed campuses elsewhere, and online or onsite programmes like Atlantis. Each fits a different situation, and many employers use more than one.

  • Foothill College (Los Altos Hills) runs a Non-Destructive Testing Technician apprenticeship certificate that prepares students for Level I and II certification. It suits people starting a career who want a structured college pathway.
  • Private Level III training providers in the Bay Area, including a long-established Santa Clara school, run scheduled classroom courses for individuals and corporate groups.
  • The Golden Gate Section of ASNT brings Bay Area NDT professionals together through meetings and events. It is a good place to meet local Level IIIs and employers.
  • National schools in Southern California, Texas and the Midwest offer campus-based programmes that require travel.
  • Atlantis NDT fits employers who want training delivered to their crew at their own facility or live online, aligned to their written practice, with Level III services available alongside. We do not have a San Jose campus, and we say so plainly.

If you are an individual looking for a full career programme with funding support, a public college is often the better fit. If you are an employer who needs specific people qualified in specific methods on a specific schedule, onsite or live online delivery usually works better.

Where NDT technicians work in San Jose and Silicon Valley

Direct answer: San Jose-area NDT demand comes from semiconductor equipment and fab construction, space and defence hardware in Sunnyvale and Mountain View, EV and battery manufacturing in Fremont, precision machine shops, utility gas and power assets, transit and bridge work, and the East Bay refinery corridor within driving distance.

Semiconductor equipment and fab construction

Santa Clara, Fremont, Milpitas and San Jose host some of the world's largest makers of wafer-processing equipment and their supplier networks. Those suppliers machine and weld vacuum chambers, frames, gas-delivery hardware and precision assemblies in aluminium and stainless steel, which creates steady demand for PT, VT and leak-related inspection, plus UT for bonded and welded structures. New fab, data-centre and lab construction across the valley adds structural steel and process-piping weld inspection.

Space, aerospace and defence

Sunnyvale has long been a centre for space and defence work, including satellite and missile systems manufacturing and marine propulsion and launch systems. NASA Ames Research Center and Moffett Federal Airfield sit next door in Mountain View. Suppliers to these programmes need technicians certified under tightly controlled written practices, often with prime-contractor specifications layered on top, and some ask for NAS 410 qualification as well, which is a separate scheme from SNT-TC-1A.

Electric vehicles, batteries and advanced manufacturing

Fremont's large electric-vehicle assembly plant and the battery, robotics and hardware start-ups around it use VT, UT, ET and radiography or CT for welds, castings, joins and battery components. Many of these companies run in-house quality labs that need a written practice and a Level III of record.

Utilities, power and pipelines

Gas transmission and distribution lines, compressor and regulator stations, gas-fired power plants such as the Metcalf Energy Center in south San Jose, and the regional water system's large pipelines all generate weld and corrosion inspection work. Pipeline construction in California commonly follows API 1104 for welding and inspection.

Transit, bridges and the East Bay refineries

Light rail, Caltrain, the BART Silicon Valley extension and highway structures bring structural weld inspection, often to AWS D1.1 or AWS D1.5. North of the valley, the Contra Costa County refining and renewable-fuels corridor at Richmond, Martinez, Rodeo and Benicia draws UT, PAUT, RT and PT crews for turnarounds, inspected to ASME and API codes. Many San Jose technicians commute to that work during shutdown season.

Radiography licensing, TWIC and other California requirements

Direct answer: California is an NRC Agreement State, and the California Department of Public Health Radiologic Health Branch licenses industrial radiography and issues the state's industrial radiographer certification. Pressure vessels fall under Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit, and gas pipelines under the CPUC and PHMSA. Confirm current requirements with each agency before starting work.

Industrial radiography

Anyone handling radioactive sources or industrial X-ray equipment in California works under a licence or registration held by their employer, and individual radiographers must meet the state's certification, training and experience rules. Trainees work under the direct supervision of a qualified radiographer. NDT training in RT covers the method; the state radiation safety requirements are a separate obligation. Ask your employer's radiation safety officer which state requirements apply before you handle a source.

Pressure vessels, pipelines and structures

Boilers and pressure vessels are regulated by the Cal/OSHA Pressure Vessel Unit, and in-service inspection follows the National Board Inspection Code alongside ASME construction codes. Intrastate gas pipelines are overseen by the California Public Utilities Commission, interstate pipelines by PHMSA, and hazardous liquid pipelines by the Office of the State Fire Marshal. In San Jose, structural welding on buildings is checked under the city's special inspection programme, which recognises approved testing agencies.

TWIC

Most San Jose work does not require a Transportation Worker Identification Credential. Technicians who travel to the Port of Oakland or to East Bay refineries with marine terminals may need one to enter secure areas, so check with the site before mobilising.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for San Jose crews

Direct answer: Atlantis runs live online classes, private live-virtual cohorts for a single company, and onsite training at your San Jose or Bay Area facility. Scheduling is built around production, shutdowns and shift patterns, and every format is led by an ASNT Level III.

Live online is the fastest route for one or two people. Private cohorts suit a quality team that wants to train together using its own procedures and parts as examples. Onsite delivery suits larger crews or companies with equipment and specimens that make the training directly relevant. Bay Area employers often prefer a blend: theory live online in short sessions so production is not disrupted, followed by a few days onsite for hands-on work and the practical exam. If your crew also supports refinery turnarounds in the East Bay, we schedule training before or after shutdown season rather than during it. See NDT training online and corporate NDT training for how each format works. Ask about onsite training for your San Jose crew.

Level III services and written practices for San Jose NDT companies

Direct answer: many Silicon Valley manufacturers need a Level III of record, a written practice and procedures more than they need a course. Atlantis provides those services remotely and onsite, so training, exams and documentation all line up when a customer or auditor reviews your programme.

Our consulting team already supports Bay Area companies: see NDT consulting in Santa Clara, NDT consulting in San Francisco, NDT consulting in Fremont and steel NDT Level III consulting in Santa Clara, plus our California NDT Level III consulting page. Typical San Jose work includes writing an SNT-TC-1A written practice for a new in-house lab, drafting PT and VT procedures to a customer specification, reviewing technique sheets, preparing for a prime-contractor audit, and acting as the outside Level III who administers and grades exams. Start with written practice development or book a Level III consultation for your San Jose company.

Practise before the practical exam

Direct answer: the Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

Simulator practice helps trainees get used to scanning patterns, probe angles, indication evaluation and report wording before they sit in front of a real specimen with a Level III watching. It is useful between online theory sessions and the onsite practical, when trainees might otherwise go weeks without touching equipment. California users can also see Practical NDT in California.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He teaches the classroom content, oversees practical examinations and supports employers with written practices and Level III services.

NDT training in San Jose, California and the West: related pages

For statewide information see NDT training in California, which covers regulators, industries and cities across the state. Other California city pages include NDT training in Los Angeles, NDT training in San Diego and NDT training in Southern California. The regional overview is NDT training on the West Coast, and method guides for the Bay Area include ultrasonic testing in San Francisco.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in San Jose

How do I get NDT certified in San Jose?

Under SNT-TC-1A, you are certified by your employer. Complete the formal training your employer's written practice requires, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass a vision test. Atlantis provides the training online or onsite in San Jose and can supply the Level III services.

Can I take NDT training online in California?

Yes, for the classroom portion. Atlantis teaches live online classes led by an ASNT Level III, and many California employers accept documented online training hours. The practical exam must still be done on real specimens under a Level III.

How much does an NDT course cost in San Jose?

We quote on request because cost depends on the method, the level, how many people you train, and whether delivery is online or onsite. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Request a San Jose course quote.

How much does NDT school cost compared with employer-based training?

A full career programme at a college or campus school is a larger commitment, covering several methods over months. Employer-based training targets the specific methods and levels your job needs. Which one is better value depends on whether you need a broad entry programme or a targeted qualification.

How long is the NDT training course?

It depends on the method, the level, and your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends formal training hours and experience for each method and level; see the training requirements matrix. Online classes can be spread over weeks to fit around work.

Which NDT course is best to start with in Silicon Valley?

For precision manufacturing and semiconductor suppliers, PT and VT are the most common first methods, with UT and ET next. For construction, pipeline or refinery work, UT and RT are in higher demand. Choose the method your current or target employer actually uses.

Do I need a license to do radiography in California?

Yes. California is an Agreement State and the CDPH Radiologic Health Branch licenses industrial radiography and certifies radiographers. Your employer holds the licence, and you must meet the state's training and certification rules before working with sources.

Is ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification recognised by San Jose employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used employer certification guideline in US industry, and most San Jose employers' written practices are based on it. Some aerospace customers also require NAS 410, which is a separate scheme Atlantis does not train for.

Can you train our crew onsite in San Jose or elsewhere in the Bay Area?

Yes. A Level III can deliver training and practical exams at your facility in San Jose, Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Fremont, Milpitas or anywhere in the Bay Area, using your own equipment and procedures where possible.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in San Jose?

No. Atlantis delivers training live online and onsite at the employer's facility. We do not have a physical campus in San Jose or anywhere else in California.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training?

Those programmes generally require an approved school or an eligible training provider listing. Atlantis does not claim those approvals. Check with the VA or your local workforce board; the common alternative is employer-paid training.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in San Jose?

Yes. Atlantis runs Level III exam preparation live online covering the Basic examination and method exams. See ASNT Level III training.

Do you offer CWI, API or ISO 9712 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some local employers also ask for CWI or API inspector credentials, but those are separate programmes we do not offer.

Start NDT training in San Jose

Tell us which methods and levels you need, how many people, and whether you prefer live online, live-virtual or onsite delivery. We reply within one business day. Get a quote for your San Jose crew, or browse all NDT training programmes.
