NDT Training and Certification in Saskatchewan

Short answer: Saskatchewan technicians and employers can take ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, plus preparation for the ASNT Level III exams. Classes run live online, as a private live-virtual cohort for one company, or onsite at your shop, mine site or plant. An ASNT NDT Level III leads every course, and your employer certifies you under its own written practice.

Saskatchewan is a province where the honest answer matters more than the sales pitch. Canada's national NDT personnel certification scheme is CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712. It is a third-party scheme: an accredited certification body issues the certificate, not your employer. Atlantis NDT does not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712 and claims no CGSB recognition. What we teach is the American employer-based system, SNT-TC-1A. In Saskatchewan that is the right fit for a specific set of people: pipe and fabrication shops building to US codes for US buyers, pipeline contractors who also work the Bakken and the US Midwest, US-owned operators in the potash and fertiliser business that run one programme on both sides of the border, and technicians who want to work in North Dakota, Montana or further south. This page explains when SNT-TC-1A works in Saskatchewan and when it does not, maps where the inspection work is from Estevan to the uranium mines of the north, and shows how to get a quote. Request a Saskatchewan NDT training quote and we reply with options within one business day.

SNT-TC-1A or CAN/CGSB-48.9712: which one do Saskatchewan employers ask for?

Direct answer: most Saskatchewan code work, inspection-company contracts and owner specifications ask for CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712) certification. SNT-TC-1A suits work built to US codes, work for US clients and US-owned operators, cross-border pipeline and oilfield crews, and technicians heading to US jobs. It does not replace a CGSB certificate where the contract, the owner or the regulator requires one.

The province's economy is tied tightly to US markets. Most of its potash, crude, pipe, canola products and farm machinery is sold south of the border, and a fair share of its plants are owned by American companies. That creates real demand for technicians who understand ASME, API and AWS work and can be certified under an employer's SNT-TC-1A programme. But the inspection companies that serve Regina, Saskatoon and the oilpatch are generally built around CGSB-certified staff, and many owner specifications for Canadian work name CGSB. The table below is how we think about it when a Saskatchewan employer or technician calls us.

Your situation in SaskatchewanScheme usually expectedDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
Construction or in-service NDE on Saskatchewan-registered boilers and pressure vessels under a Canadian inspection-company contractCAN/CGSB-48.9712, often through a CSA W178.1-certified inspection organisationUsually no. Check the owner specification and TSASK requirements. Our training can add knowledge but does not lead to a CGSB certificate
Fabricating ASME-stamped vessels, skids or pipe spools for a US buyerSNT-TC-1A, as referenced by ASME Section V and the client specificationYes. This is the core use case
US-owned potash, fertiliser or agri-processing operator running one written practice across Saskatchewan and US plantsSNT-TC-1A employer programme, sometimes alongside CGSB-certified contractorsYes, for the employer's own programme and Level III support
Pipeline or oilfield crew that works both the Saskatchewan Bakken and North Dakota or MontanaSNT-TC-1A on the US side; CGSB or the project specification on the Canadian sideYes for the US work. Confirm the Canadian project specification separately
Uranium mine and mill maintenance or other CNSC-licensed workWhatever the licensee's program and specification require, typically CGSBRarely. Ask the licensee first
Technician from Regina or Saskatoon planning to move to US turnaround, pipeline or fabrication workSNT-TC-1A or CP-189 through the US employerYes. Your training record moves with you

A word on the CGSB side. The Canadian General Standards Board, which published the CAN/CGSB-48.9712 standard, ceased operations on 1 April 2026. Public notices from Natural Resources Canada and the CWB Group say the standard stays valid for its current cycle and existing certifications are unaffected. NRCan's NDT Certification Body has said its programmes continue without interruption, and the CWB Group also certifies NDT personnel to the standard. Because these arrangements are still settling, confirm the current certification body before you plan a CGSB route. Plenty of Saskatchewan technicians hold a CGSB certificate and an employer SNT-TC-1A certification at the same time, and the two can be planned together.

Where NDT technicians work in Saskatchewan

Direct answer: Saskatchewan NDT work clusters in five places: the Regina refining and steel corridor, the Saskatoon potash and manufacturing hub, the Lloydminster heavy-oil region on the Alberta border, the Bakken and coal-power country around Estevan in the south-east, and the uranium mines of the Athabasca Basin in the north. Pipelines, rail and power generation run between them.

Regina and Moose Jaw: refining, steel and pipe

Regina holds the Co-op Refinery Complex, a large refinery on the city's north-east side owned by Federated Co-operatives. Refinery maintenance and turnarounds create steady demand for UT thickness surveys, PAUT corrosion mapping on piping and vessels, RT and UT on repair welds, ET on heat exchanger bundles, and MT and PT on rotating equipment. Regina is also home to a large steel mill and pipe-making operation that produces line pipe and tubular products for North American energy customers, much of it shipped south. Pipe mills use automated UT, radiography, MT and visual inspection on seam welds and pipe body, and those programmes are often written to API and ASTM specifications that reference SNT-TC-1A. Moose Jaw, forty minutes west, adds an asphalt refinery and agri-processing. See Practical NDT simulator practice in Regina and the NDT ERP for Regina inspection companies.

Saskatoon and the potash belt

Saskatchewan produces a large share of the world's potash, and almost all of it comes from mines within a few hours of Saskatoon and Regina. Nutrien runs several potash mines around Saskatoon and in the east of the province, Mosaic operates major mines at Esterhazy, Belle Plaine and Colonsay, K+S runs the Bethune mine, and BHP's Jansen project east of Saskatoon is nearing first production. Potash mines and mills are heavy users of NDT: hoist and headframe inspection, shaft steel, crushers, dryers, conveyors and the pressure equipment in processing plants all need MT, PT, UT and VT, and solution mines add brine and steam piping. Saskatoon itself has a manufacturing base in mining equipment, agricultural machinery, fabrication and engineering services, and it is the logistics centre for the northern mines. See Saskatoon NDT simulator practice and NDT ERP for Saskatoon.

Lloydminster and the west-central heavy-oil region

Lloydminster straddles the Alberta border. The heavy oil upgrader on the Saskatchewan side, operated by Cenovus, and the asphalt refinery on the Alberta side anchor a large cluster of heavy-oil production, thermal projects, oilfield service companies and fabrication shops reaching north to the Battlefords and south to Kindersley. Thermal and conventional heavy-oil facilities mean steam lines, separators, treaters and tanks that need UT thickness surveys, RT of welds, and MT and PT on fabrication. Many Lloydminster contractors work on both sides of the border every week, so they deal with ABSA rules in Alberta and TSASK rules in Saskatchewan. See NDT ERP for Lloydminster.

Estevan and the south-east: Bakken oil and coal-fired power

The south-east corner of the province sits on the Canadian side of the Bakken formation. Oil batteries, gathering pipelines, gas plants and the service companies around Estevan, Weyburn and Carlyle create pipeline radiography, UT and VT work. SaskPower's Boundary Dam and Shand generating stations near Estevan, including the carbon capture unit at Boundary Dam, add boiler tube, header and high-energy piping inspection during outages. Crews here often cross into North Dakota for work, which is exactly where an SNT-TC-1A certification earns its keep.

The north: uranium and forestry

The Athabasca Basin in northern Saskatchewan hosts some of the world's highest-grade uranium mines and mills, operated by Cameco and Orano. These sites are licensed by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission and run strict maintenance, inspection and quality programmes. Prince Albert and the forest belt add pulp, sawmill and power-plant work. Northern sites are fly-in, rotation-based operations, so short onsite training blocks and online theory between rotations are the only practical model.

Pipelines, rail and power across the province

Major interprovincial and international pipelines cross Saskatchewan carrying Alberta crude to US markets, with pump stations, terminals and tank farms along the way, including the large tank and terminal complex at Kerrobert and terminals near Regina. Two Class I railways cross the province, with rail-car, wheel and coupler work for MT and UT. SaskPower's gas, coal and hydro stations, and the fertiliser and ethanol plants, need boiler and pressure-equipment inspection on regular cycles.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Saskatchewan employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus ASNT Level III exam preparation. The table shows what each method is used for in Saskatchewan and what a trainee needs first. Your employer's written practice sets the exact classroom and experience hours.

Regina. Regina employers tend to need two kinds of training. Refinery contractors need UT, PAUT, RT and ET technicians ready before a turnaround, usually in a short window. Pipe-making and fabrication operations need people who understand API and ASTM inspection requirements and can be certified under an SNT-TC-1A written practice for product sold into the US. Both work well with online theory followed by an onsite practical block at the plant.

Saskatoon. Saskatoon's demand comes from the potash mines and the shops that support them. Mine maintenance departments often want MT and UT Level II for in-house mechanical and electrical teams, plus a written practice that a US parent company can audit. Engineering firms and QA leads often take Level II theory or Level III preparation so they can specify NDT and review reports with confidence.

Estevan and the south-east. Crews here work the Canadian and US Bakken. An SNT-TC-1A certification under the employer's written practice is what North Dakota operators expect, while Saskatchewan work follows the project specification. We help employers keep both sets of records straight.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Saskatchewan, step by step

Direct answer: under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you. You complete classroom training and documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you to its written practice. It is an employer certification, not a Canadian national certificate.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice based on SNT-TC-1A. It sets training hours, experience hours, exam rules and recertification intervals. If your Saskatchewan company does not have one, we can write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Complete the formal training hours your written practice requires for the method and level, live online or onsite. The training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience. Log supervised hours on real work, whether that is refinery piping, pipe-mill inspection, mine equipment or pipeline welds. Your employer keeps the records.
  4. Examinations. Sit the general (theory), specific (your employer's procedures, codes and equipment) and practical (real specimens) examinations, administered under a Level III.
  5. Vision examination. Pass near-vision and colour contrast checks, repeated annually under most written practices.
  6. Certification. The employer certifies you for the method and level on the Level III's recommendation. A new employer must review and recertify you under its own written practice.
  7. Recertification. Recertify at the interval in your written practice, by examination or documented continued work, with vision checks continuing each year.

If you also want CGSB certification, keep your experience logs detailed enough to satisfy both schemes. The certification body sets its own evidence rules, so confirm them early rather than reconstructing records later.

Radiography licensing and other Saskatchewan requirements

Direct answer: industrial gamma radiography in Saskatchewan is regulated federally by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. Operators must be CNSC-certified exposure device operators or work under the direct supervision and continuous observation of one. Boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan (TSASK). Pipelines inside the province are regulated provincially; interprovincial and international lines by the Canada Energy Regulator.

Industrial radiography and the CNSC

Canada has no US-style Agreement State system. The CNSC licenses nuclear substances and exposure devices in every province. Under the Nuclear Substances and Radiation Devices Regulations, only a certified exposure device operator (EDO), or a trainee under the direct supervision and continuous observation of a certified EDO, may operate an exposure device. CNSC guidance (REGDOC-2.2.3 and the CSA PCP-09 certification guide) requires candidates to complete formal EDO vocational training, a supervised on-the-job training programme and CNSC examinations. Atlantis RT training covers radiographic theory, technique, film and digital interpretation, and code acceptance criteria. It does not replace EDO certification and we do not run CNSC examinations. X-ray equipment is not a nuclear substance and falls under provincial radiation health and safety rules, so your radiation safety officer should confirm the current registration and worker requirements with the province. The CNSC also licenses the uranium mines and mills in the north, which brings its own layer of program requirements for contractors working there.

Boilers and pressure vessels: TSASK

The Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan administers boiler and pressure vessel safety under The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act, 1999 and its regulations. TSASK handles design registration, inspection, and the licensing of companies and personnel, and it examines and certifies power engineers. Owners and contractors performing repairs and alterations work under TSASK-accepted quality programmes. Construction codes commonly referenced in Saskatchewan include CSA B51, ASME Section VIII for vessels, ASME Section I for boilers, ASME B31.1 and B31.3 for piping, and ASME Section V for NDE methods. Whether SNT-TC-1A personnel are acceptable on a given job depends on the code, the owner and the quality programme, so check before you rely on it.

Pipelines

Pipelines that stay inside Saskatchewan are regulated by the province under The Pipelines Act, 1998, through the ministry responsible for energy and resources. Interprovincial and international pipelines, including the big crude export lines that cross the province, fall under the Canada Energy Regulator. CSA Z662 is the core Canadian standard for design, construction and integrity, and it sets its own NDT personnel requirements. API 1104 still appears on projects with US owners and cross-border systems. Read the project specification before assuming SNT-TC-1A alone will do.

Other things Saskatchewan employers ask for

Site access at refineries, upgraders and mines usually involves safety prequalification through networks such as ISNetworld, Avetta or ComplyWorks, industry safety tickets, and a Certificate of Recognition for the employer. Structural steel fabrication to CSA W59 is done by CWB-certified companies whose NDT personnel are normally CGSB-certified. Atlantis training does not replace any of these. It sits beside them for the work where SNT-TC-1A applies.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Saskatchewan

Direct answer: Atlantis delivers Saskatchewan training three ways: live online classes for individuals, private live-virtual cohorts for one company's crew, and onsite delivery at your shop, mine or plant with a Level III instructor. Theory is online; practical sessions are held on real specimens at your site.

Saskatchewan is a big province with a small population spread across long distances. A technician in Estevan, a mine maintenance planner near Esterhazy and a fabricator in Lloydminster are all several hours from each other, and none of them should need to drive to a classroom. Online theory removes the travel, and onsite practical blocks mean nobody loses a shift. We schedule around the provincial calendar: refinery and upgrader turnarounds, potash mine maintenance shutdowns, winter pipeline construction, spring road bans that slow field work, and harvest season for the agricultural equipment makers.

  • Live online seats: individuals join a scheduled class from anywhere in the province with live instruction and questions answered in real time.
  • Private live-virtual cohort: your crew only, built around your procedures, codes and equipment.
  • Onsite at your facility: the instructor comes to your Regina plant, Saskatoon shop or mine site, uses your equipment and specimens, and supports practical examinations under your written practice.
  • Blended: online theory, simulator practice and a short onsite practical block, which suits rotational and fly-in crews.

We do not have a classroom in Saskatchewan and never claim one. Ask about onsite training for your Saskatchewan crew, or read about online NDT training and corporate NDT training.

For Saskatchewan employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: a Saskatchewan employer that needs SNT-TC-1A certification for US-code or US-client work needs a written practice, a Level III to administer examinations, and training and experience records an auditor can follow. Atlantis provides all three, remotely or onsite, including for companies that keep CGSB-certified staff for their Canadian work.

Typical Saskatchewan requests are programmes rather than single courses: a Regina fabricator taking its first ASME-stamped order for a US customer, a Saskatoon mine-services company whose US parent wants one written practice across all sites, or an Estevan pipeline contractor bidding work in North Dakota. We can:

  • write or rewrite your SNT-TC-1A written practice to match your ASME, API, AWS or client requirements (written practice development);
  • act as your outside Level III: prepare and grade general, specific and practical exams, review procedures and sign technique sheets;
  • map how your SNT-TC-1A programme and CGSB-certified staff fit together so certification records are clear on every job;
  • prepare you for client, quality-programme and third-party audits of your NDT programme;
  • keep certification, training, vision and equipment records in order with our NDT ERP, which tracks CGSB and ASNT certifications side by side (see the Saskatoon and Regina ERP pages).

More on SNT-TC-1A training and certification for employers and NDT consulting in Canada. Book a Level III consultation for your Saskatchewan programme.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: the Atlantis Practical NDT simulator lets Saskatchewan trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments from a browser before they handle real specimens. It is practice only. It does not replace the hands-on practical examination your written practice requires, or the practical examination in a CGSB scheme.

The five environments are an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. They map well onto Saskatchewan work: pipe and vessel welds, tank floors and shells at terminals, and plant equipment at refineries and upgraders. Trainees on rotation at a northern mine or a heavy-oil site can practise probe handling, scan planning and indication recognition between shifts, and supervisors can use it to judge readiness before booking practical exam time. See Practical NDT, or the city pages for Regina and Saskatoon. For written practice, try the UT Level II practice questions.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop designs the course content, the examinations and the written practices we prepare for employers. He is also the person you talk to when you are deciding whether SNT-TC-1A, CGSB or both make sense for your Saskatchewan work.

NDT training in Saskatchewan: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Saskatchewan?

There are two routes. For most Canadian work you need CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712) certification from an accredited certification body; confirm the current certification body, because arrangements changed in 2026. For US-code work, US clients or US employers, you are certified by your employer under SNT-TC-1A after training, experience, examinations and a vision test. Atlantis trains for the SNT-TC-1A route only.

Is there NDT training online in Saskatchewan?

Yes. Atlantis runs live online and live-virtual SNT-TC-1A classes that technicians can join from Regina, Saskatoon, Lloydminster, Estevan or a mine camp. Practical training and exams happen on real specimens, usually at your employer's site. See NDT training online.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB or ISO 9712 training in Saskatchewan?

No. We do not train toward CAN/CGSB-48.9712 or any ISO 9712 scheme and do not claim CGSB recognition. If your job needs a CGSB certificate, use a CGSB-route provider. We will say so on the first call.

Do I need a licence to do radiography in Saskatchewan?

For gamma radiography, yes. You must be a CNSC-certified exposure device operator or work under the direct supervision and continuous observation of one, and your employer must hold a CNSC licence. X-ray equipment is regulated provincially. RT training alone does not let you operate a source.

Who regulates boilers and pressure vessels in Saskatchewan?

The Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan (TSASK), under The Boiler and Pressure Vessel Act, 1999. TSASK handles design registration, inspections and licensing. Whether a given job accepts SNT-TC-1A personnel depends on the code, the owner and the quality programme.

How much does NDT training cost in Saskatchewan?

It is quoted on request. The price depends on the method and level, the number of trainees, online versus onsite delivery, and whether you also need a written practice or Level III exam administration. Cohort and onsite quotes usually come back within one business day. Request a Saskatchewan quote.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Saskatchewan?

UT is the workhorse across refining, heavy oil, pipe making and potash. MT is heavily used on mine hoists, crushers and structural steel. RT stays important for pipeline and piping welds, and ET matters for heat exchangers at the refinery, upgrader and power plants.

Can you train our crew onsite in Regina, Saskatoon or at a mine site?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your shop, plant or mine is a standard option for Saskatchewan employers. The instructor works with your equipment and specimens and supports practical examinations under your written practice, subject to your site's access and safety rules.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums, listed in our training requirements matrix. Experience hours usually take far longer than classroom hours. CGSB has separate requirements.

Can a Saskatchewan crew use SNT-TC-1A certification in North Dakota?

US operators and contractors generally work to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 employer certification, so a crew certified under its employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice is set up for that work. The certification belongs to the employer, so the employer's programme must cover the US jobs.

Can I become a Level III in Saskatchewan?

Yes, by either route. ASNT Level III candidates prepare for the Basic and method exams; our Level III preparation runs online. A CGSB Level 3 follows the certification body's own requirements.

What do NDT technicians earn in Saskatchewan?

Pay depends on method, level, certification scheme, rotation and overtime. We do not publish our own salary figures. For context, read the NDT salary guide.

Get a quote for NDT training in Saskatchewan

You might need two Regina technicians trained to UT Level II for a US pipe order, a potash mine maintenance team qualified in MT before the next shutdown, or a written practice and outside Level III for an Estevan contractor working both sides of the border. Atlantis NDT will build the programme around your work, your codes and your rotation, and we will tell you plainly when CGSB is what you actually need. Request your Saskatchewan training quote, learn more about Atlantis NDT training, or see NDT training across Canada. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

NDT Training and Certification in South Carolina

Short answer: South Carolina technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT in three ways: live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite sessions at your own plant, hangar, fabrication shop or outage site. An ASNT NDT Level III leads and oversees the training. Certification is employer-based. Your written practice sets the training, experience and exam rules, and a Level III gives the exams. Atlantis has no South Carolina training centre. We teach online or come to your facility.

Over the last thirty years South Carolina has become one of the country's busiest manufacturing states, and its NDT demand looks different from the oil-and-gas states. The Upstate builds cars, gas turbines and fighter aircraft. The Lowcountry builds wide-body airliners, cars and vans, and moves cargo through one of the East Coast's busiest ports. The Midlands and the Savannah River corridor are home to a Department of Energy site, a commercial nuclear fuel plant and nuclear power stations. Steel mills, tyre plants and a large automotive supplier base sit in between. Each of these sectors asks for something different from an NDT technician: aerospace wants surface and composite inspection to prime specifications, automotive wants fast production inspection, and nuclear wants rigorous documentation. This page covers where the work is, what each sector expects, which state agencies regulate radiography, boilers and pipelines, and how to request a South Carolina training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in South Carolina

Direct answer: South Carolina NDT work clusters in the Upstate (automotive, gas turbines, aerospace, tyres), the Lowcountry around Charleston (aircraft manufacturing, automotive, port, steel, defence), the Midlands around Columbia (nuclear fuel, nuclear power, manufacturing, military), the Savannah River corridor around Aiken (DOE nuclear site) and the Pee Dee and coast (steel, power, paper, fabrication).

The Upstate: Greenville, Spartanburg, Greer and Anderson

The I-85 corridor is South Carolina's manufacturing core. BMW's Plant Spartanburg near Greer is the company's largest plant in the world, and hundreds of automotive suppliers surround it. They need weld inspection on body and chassis parts, ultrasonic checks of spot welds and joints, eddy current sorting and crack detection, and magnetic particle and penetrant inspection of forged, cast and machined components. GE Vernova builds heavy-duty gas turbines in Greenville, where large forgings, castings, rotors and welded casings need ultrasonic, magnetic particle, penetrant and radiographic inspection. Lockheed Martin builds F-16 fighters in Greenville, and the aerospace MRO and supplier base around the Greenville-Spartanburg area adds eddy current, penetrant and ultrasonic work to aerospace specifications. Michelin's North American operations, other tyre makers, and a wide base of metal fabricators add plant and equipment inspection. Duke Energy's Oconee Nuclear Station near Seneca brings ASME Section XI outage work to the western Upstate.

The Lowcountry: North Charleston, Charleston, Summerville and Berkeley County

Boeing South Carolina in North Charleston builds 787 Dreamliners. That means composite structures inspected by ultrasonic methods, metallic parts inspected by penetrant and eddy current, and a supplier base working to Boeing and aerospace specifications. Mercedes-Benz Vans in Ladson and Volvo Cars in Ridgeville bring automotive inspection. Nucor's steel mill in Berkeley County and other heavy fabricators need UT of plate and welds, MT and VT. The Port of Charleston's terminals and cranes, Joint Base Charleston's air and naval operations, and the Naval Weapons Station add structural, aircraft and equipment inspection. Bridges such as the Arthur Ravenel Jr. Bridge and SCDOT's highway programme need bridge-weld and structural inspectors.

The Midlands: Columbia, Lexington County, Sumter and Fairfield County

Westinghouse's Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility makes nuclear fuel assemblies. The V.C. Summer Nuclear Station in Fairfield County operates one unit. Fort Jackson and Shaw Air Force Base near Sumter, a growing automotive cluster including the new Scout Motors plant at Blythewood, and manufacturers along I-26 and I-77 add production, aircraft and structural NDT demand.

The Savannah River corridor: Aiken, North Augusta and Barnwell

The Department of Energy's Savannah River Site near Aiken is one of the largest employers in the state. Its nuclear materials, waste-processing and construction projects need welding inspection, radiography, ultrasonic testing and visual inspection under strict quality-assurance programmes. Contractors and fabricators in Aiken County and across the river in Augusta serve it.

The Pee Dee, Rock Hill and the coast

Duke Energy's Catawba Nuclear Station in York County, near Rock Hill, and H.B. Robinson near Hartsville add more outage work. Steel mills, paper mills, fabricators and power plants across Florence, Darlington and Georgetown need plant and weld inspection. Gas transmission pipelines crossing the state bring API 1104 construction and integrity work.

Wherever your company works in South Carolina, you can ask about onsite training for your South Carolina crew. We schedule around production, model changeovers and outages.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for South Carolina employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT teaches UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, plus Level III exam preparation. Every course is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and your company's written practice. The table maps each method to South Carolina work.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in South Carolina, step by step

Direct answer: South Carolina does not issue general NDT technician licences. Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you based on its written practice. The practice sets training hours, experience, exams and vision tests, a Level III administers the exams, and the employer issues the certification.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. It defines methods, levels, training and experience hours, exam content, passing grades, vision tests and recertification. If your company needs one, see written practice development.
  2. You complete formal training. Classroom hours per method and level come from the practice, based on SNT-TC-1A recommendations. See the training requirements matrix for the guideline figures.
  3. You build documented experience. On-the-job hours in the method, under qualified supervision, on the kind of parts or welds you will inspect.
  4. You pass the general, specific and practical exams. The general exam covers theory, the specific exam covers your employer's procedures and specifications, and the practical exam is done on real specimens, all administered by a Level III.
  5. You pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity is checked annually, and colour contrast as the practice requires.
  6. Your employer certifies you. The certification belongs to that employer. If you move from an Upstate supplier to a Lowcountry plant, your new employer decides how to recertify you.
  7. You recertify on schedule. The interval and the evidence required are in the written practice.

The ASNT NDT Level III certificate is different. ASNT issues it centrally by examination, and employers then certify their Level III under their own practice. More detail is on the SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Radiography licensing and other South Carolina requirements

Direct answer: South Carolina is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive material licences for industrial radiography are issued by the state under Regulation 61-63 (Radioactive Materials, Title A). On 1 July 2024 the former SC DHEC was split into two agencies, and radioactive materials licensing now sits with the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (SCDES). Confirm the current licensing office and forms with SCDES before applying.

For a South Carolina radiography company, the state licence covers radiation-safety training, radiographer and assistant qualification, personnel dosimetry, survey instruments, source storage and transport, and field-crew rules, which follow the model of 10 CFR Part 34. X-ray equipment is registered with the state separately. Radiation-safety training is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT method training, which covers exposure technique, film and digital processing and interpretation. A field radiographer needs both. Work inside the Savannah River Site falls under DOE requirements as well, so check the site's rules before a crew mobilises. Because the 2024 reorganisation moved programmes between agencies, confirm current requirements before a new crew starts work.

Boilers and pressure vessels. South Carolina's boiler safety programme is administered by the Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation (LLR) under the state Boiler Safety Act. New boilers must be built to code and registered with the National Board, and the regulations can adopt sections of the National Board Inspection Code. ASME Section V NDT methods and Section I or VIII acceptance criteria therefore apply in shop and field work.

Pipelines. Intrastate gas pipeline safety in South Carolina is overseen by the state's pipeline safety programme under the Office of Regulatory Staff. PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines. Pipeline welding and NDT follow API 1104, and operators layer their own operator-qualification programmes on top of SNT-TC-1A certification.

Codes and specifications common in South Carolina. Aerospace prime-contractor specifications and NAS 410 in the Charleston and Greenville aerospace supply chains, mentioned as context only. Automotive OEM and supplier quality standards. ASME Section III and Section XI in nuclear work, plus DOE quality-assurance requirements at the Savannah River Site. ASME Section V, VIII and B31.1 in power and turbines. AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AASHTO/AWS D1.5 for bridges. API 1104 for pipelines.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across South Carolina

Direct answer: South Carolina crews can take theory online, join a live-virtual cohort with a Level III instructor, or bring the training onsite to their plant, hangar or site. Practical exams always use real specimens under Level III oversight. Video and simulation never replace them.

South Carolina's manufacturing calendar shapes when training works. Automotive plants have summer shutdown weeks and model-year changeovers, which are good windows for production inspectors. Aircraft and turbine plants run to delivery schedules, so short, focused onsite sessions work better than week-long absences. Nuclear stations at Oconee, Catawba, Robinson and V.C. Summer refuel on fixed cycles, and contract technicians are booked months ahead. Online theory lets them study between outages. Hurricane season on the coast can disrupt schedules from summer into autumn, so Lowcountry companies often prefer live-virtual theory they can reschedule easily.

Onsite delivery means the instructor comes to your South Carolina facility, uses your equipment and procedures, and, where possible, uses your own parts and welds as practice specimens. The specific exam can then reflect your real work. Onsite suits companies with several technicians in a method, or companies that want training tied tightly to their written practice. Live online theory suits mixed groups and individuals. See online NDT training and corporate NDT training. When you're ready, request a cohort or onsite quote for South Carolina. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

For South Carolina employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: A South Carolina company that certifies its own NDT people needs a compliant written practice, a responsible Level III, and auditable training and exam records. Atlantis NDT writes and reviews written practices, provides Level III services, and runs corporate training for South Carolina employers.

The state's supplier base is full of companies with a few NDT inspectors inside a quality department and no in-house Level III. Customer audits by aircraft, automotive and turbine OEMs are where gaps show up: training records that don't match the practice, exams not administered by a qualified Level III, out-of-date vision tests, or a practice that doesn't reflect what the shop actually does.   • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A, aligned with your customers' flow-down requirements.

The environments are an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. NDT training in South Carolina: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in South Carolina?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Complete the classroom training it requires, build documented experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass the vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and helps employers with the rest.

Is there NDT training online in South Carolina?

Yes. Theory for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET can be taken live online from anywhere in the state. Practical exams still use real specimens under Level III oversight.

Do I need a license to do radiography in South Carolina?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence from the state, because South Carolina is an NRC Agreement State. Since the 2024 split of DHEC, that licensing sits with the Department of Environmental Services. Radiographers and assistants must meet the licence's training and qualification rules.

How much does NDT training cost in South Carolina?

Training is quoted on request. The quote depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and any written-practice or exam support. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in South Carolina?

UT is in demand across aerospace, turbines, automotive and nuclear. PT and ET are central to aerospace. MT and PT are heavily used on automotive and turbine parts, and RT is used in nuclear, DOE-site and pipeline work.

Can you train our crew onsite in Greenville or Charleston?

Yes. Onsite training is available anywhere in South Carolina, using your equipment and procedures where possible.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted by aerospace companies in South Carolina?

Many aerospace customers reference NAS 410, which has its own requirements. SNT-TC-1A-based training can support NAS 410 programmes when your Level III maps it properly. Check your customer's specification.

How long does Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, the method and your experience. Classroom and experience hours are both set by the practice. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline figures.

Can I take NDT training without an employer in South Carolina?

Yes, you can take classroom training as an individual, and it counts toward the formal training requirement. Certification still needs an employer and its written practice.

Do you train technicians for Savannah River Site contractors?

We provide SNT-TC-1A method training that contractors can build into their qualification programmes. Site and DOE quality requirements are applied by the contractor's Level III and QA organisation. See nuclear NDT training in Aiken.

Do you prepare candidates for the ASNT Level III exams?

Yes. We offer preparation for the Basic and method examinations. See ASNT Level III training.

Pay varies by method, level, sector and overtime. See the NDT salary guide for published ranges.

NDT Training and Certification in Tennessee

Tennessee technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, in live-virtual cohorts, or onsite at their own plant, shop or site. Every course is led by an ASNT NDT Level III and mapped to the employer's written practice, so training counts toward certification. Methods: UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation.

Tennessee has one of the most nuclear-heavy NDT markets in the country. The Tennessee Valley Authority is headquartered in Knoxville and runs nuclear, hydro and fossil plants across the state; Oak Ridge has been a centre of nuclear work since the 1940s; and new advanced-reactor projects are under way there now. Add a refinery and a global air-cargo hub in Memphis, a large chemical complex in Kingsport, aerospace test facilities in Middle Tennessee, a fast-growing automotive and battery industry, and major river, rail and Interstate bridges, and the result is steady demand for qualified technicians in almost every method. This page maps that work by region and explains how certification and Tennessee's regulators fit together. Request a Tennessee training quote if you already know what you need.

Where NDT technicians work in Tennessee

Tennessee NDT work falls into four regions: East Tennessee's nuclear, federal-research and chemical complex (Knoxville, Oak Ridge, Chattanooga, Kingsport); Middle Tennessee's automotive, aerospace-test and construction economy (Nashville, Smyrna, Spring Hill, Tullahoma, Clarksville); West Tennessee's refinery, logistics and new automotive work (Memphis, Stanton); and TVA power and river infrastructure statewide.

East Tennessee: Oak Ridge and Knoxville

Oak Ridge is home to Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Y-12 National Security Complex and the former K-25 site, now the East Tennessee Technology Park. It is also becoming a centre for advanced nuclear: Kairos Power is building its Hermes demonstration reactor in Oak Ridge, and TVA has pursued a small modular reactor at its Clinch River site. That work involves high-integrity fabrication, nuclear-grade quality programmes and inspection under ASME Section III and related requirements, with heavy use of UT, RT, PT and VT. Knoxville hosts TVA's headquarters and a regional base of engineering and inspection contractors. See NDT training in Oak Ridge and nuclear NDT training in Oak Ridge.

Chattanooga and the southeast corner

TVA's Sequoyah nuclear plant at Soddy-Daisy and Watts Bar nuclear plant near Spring City both sit within an hour of Chattanooga, and Watts Bar Unit 2 was the first new US commercial reactor to enter service in the 21st century. Their refuelling outages draw ASME Section XI in-service inspection crews for UT, PAUT, ET and VT. Chattanooga also has a long heavy-manufacturing history, including boiler and pressure-vessel fabrication and foundries, plus the Volkswagen assembly plant and its suppliers.

Northeast Tennessee: Kingsport and the Tri-Cities

Eastman Chemical Company's Kingsport site is one of the largest chemical manufacturing complexes in the eastern United States, with miles of process piping, pressure vessels, heat exchangers and boilers. Plant inspection there involves UT thickness and corrosion monitoring, RT and PAUT on piping welds, ET on exchanger tubing and VT and PT across maintenance work. In Erwin, Nuclear Fuel Services manufactures nuclear fuel for the US Navy.

Middle Tennessee: Nashville, Smyrna, Spring Hill, Tullahoma and Clarksville

Nashville's construction boom keeps structural steel fabricators busy with VT, MT and UT under AWS D1.1. Nissan's Smyrna plant, General Motors at Spring Hill and their suppliers bring automotive weld, casting and battery-manufacturing inspection. In Tullahoma, Arnold Air Force Base hosts the Arnold Engineering Development Complex, whose wind tunnels and engine test cells involve large pressure systems and precision aerospace hardware. Clarksville, next to Fort Campbell, adds Army aviation maintenance and growing manufacturing. See NDT training in Nashville.

West Tennessee: Memphis and the Mississippi

Memphis has the Valero Memphis refinery, petroleum terminals on Presidents Island, the FedEx World Hub with its large aircraft maintenance operation, and river-port industry along the Mississippi. Refinery turnarounds drive UT, RT, PAUT and VT demand, and aircraft maintenance drives ET, PT and UT. Ford's BlueOval City at Stanton, northeast of Memphis, is a major new automotive and battery manufacturing site. The 2021 discovery of a fractured tie girder on the Interstate 40 Hernando de Soto Bridge over the Mississippi is a well-known example of why bridge inspection matters, and it is still taught as a lesson in fracture-critical inspection.

TVA power, dams and pipelines statewide

Beyond nuclear, TVA operates gas, coal and hydroelectric generation across Tennessee, with boiler-tube, penstock, turbine and generator inspection on every outage. Interstate natural gas transmission lines and product pipelines cross the state, and gas distribution utilities run constant replacement programmes, all needing weld and integrity inspection.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Tennessee employers

Atlantis NDT runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and II courses in eight methods plus Level III preparation. Tennessee nuclear and power employers rely on UT, PAUT, ET, RT and VT; chemical and refinery plants on UT, RT and PAUT; aircraft maintenance on ET and PT; fabrication, automotive and bridges on MT, UT and VT.

Nashville. A booming construction market means steady demand for VT, MT and UT on structural steel and bridges, plus automotive supplier work in the surrounding counties. The Nashville page and Practical NDT Nashville page go deeper.

Oak Ridge. Nuclear-grade quality expectations, traceability and strict procedure control. UT, RT, PT and VT at Level II are common, and Level III oversight is often a customer requirement.

Memphis. Refinery turnarounds and aircraft maintenance are the two big engines. Technicians with UT and RT on one side, or ET and PT on the other, are in steady demand.

Knoxville. TVA's home base supports a network of engineering and inspection contractors who staff outages across the Valley, which favours UT, ET and VT.

Neighbouring hubs: NDT training across the Southeast, Appalachia, Huntsville for North Alabama crews, and Lexington for Kentucky.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Tennessee, step by step

Tennessee does not license NDT technicians. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after you complete method training, gain documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test.

  1. Written practice. The employer's written practice sets levels, training, experience, exams and recertification for each method.
  2. Classroom training in the method, online, live-virtual or onsite. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums.
  3. On-the-job experience, supervised and documented: piping UT in Kingsport, structural MT in Nashville, ET at a Memphis hangar.
  4. General exam on method principles.
  5. Specific exam on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, such as ASME Section V, ASME Section XI or AWS D1.1.
  6. Practical exam on real specimens, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision test, near-vision and colour contrast, annually.
  8. Certification issued and documented by the employer.
  9. Recertification at the interval the written practice sets.

Nuclear owners and federal-site contractors may add site-specific qualification, and some nuclear UT exams also require performance demonstration under ASME Section XI Appendix VIII. Those are layers on top of a solid SNT-TC-1A foundation. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Tennessee requirements

Tennessee is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive materials is licensed and inspected by the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC) Division of Radiological Health, under state rules that follow the federal industrial radiography model in 10 CFR Part 34. Industrial x-ray equipment is registered with the same division.

For RT technicians, that means two qualifications: SNT-TC-1A method certification under the employer's written practice, and radiation safety qualification as a radiographer or radiographer's assistant under the company's state licence, including radiation safety training, certification and supervision rules. Out-of-state licensees need reciprocity before working in Tennessee. Note that work at federal Department of Energy sites in Oak Ridge can fall under DOE radiation protection rules rather than the state licence, so confirm the applicable authority for each job and confirm current requirements with TDEC before work starts.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development's Boiler Unit, within its workplace regulations and compliance division, has jurisdiction over high-pressure and low-pressure boilers and unfired pressure vessels in commercial and industrial use. State and insurance inspectors hold National Board commissions, and repairs follow the National Board Inspection Code with NDT drawn from ASME Section V and the construction code. Chemical plants, power plants and manufacturers generate most of this work.

Pipelines. The Tennessee Public Utility Commission's Gas Pipeline Safety Division inspects intrastate gas transmission and all natural gas distribution systems in the state, including municipal systems and utility districts, under a PHMSA grant. PHMSA itself regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid pipelines. API 1104 governs most pipeline weld inspection.

Codes in local use (context only). ASME Section III and NQA-1 quality programmes on nuclear fabrication, ASME Section XI at Sequoyah and Watts Bar, ASME Section I, V and VIII and B31.1 and B31.3 at power and chemical plants, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structures and bridges, API 1104 for pipelines, and NAS 410 or customer-specific aerospace requirements for aviation work. Some Tennessee employers also ask for API inspector or AWS CWI credentials, which are separate schemes; Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Tennessee

Tennessee crews can take NDT theory live online, join a live-virtual cohort, or have a Level III-led course delivered onsite at their facility. Practical training and practical exams are performed on real specimens at the employer's site or another arrangement agreed in advance.

Tennessee stretches roughly 440 miles from Memphis to Bristol, across two time zones. Online theory lets a technician in Memphis and one in Kingsport attend the same live class without losing days to travel. Sessions are interactive, led by a Level III, and cover what the general and specific exams test. See NDT training online.

Onsite training suits plants, shops and hangars that want a group trained on their own parts, procedures and equipment. We schedule around Tennessee's work calendar: spring and fall refuelling outages at Sequoyah and Watts Bar, TVA fossil and hydro maintenance seasons, refinery turnarounds in Memphis, planned unit shutdowns in Kingsport, and automotive model-year changeovers. Multi-state employers can use corporate NDT training to keep records consistent. Ask about onsite training for your Tennessee crew.

For Tennessee employers: written practice and Level III services

Every Tennessee company that certifies NDT personnel under SNT-TC-1A needs a written practice and Level III oversight. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, administers and grades exams, reviews procedures and acts as an outside Level III for companies without one in-house.

Tennessee's new manufacturing and nuclear projects are bringing in suppliers who must certify inspectors quickly: a fabricator qualifying for advanced-reactor work in Oak Ridge, a battery-plant supplier in West Tennessee adding NDT to its quality plan, or a Nashville steel erector whose customer now requires certified UT. Each needs a written practice that matches its methods, codes and customers. Our written practice development service builds it, and our SNT-TC-1A guide explains what auditors check.

Level III services include procedures and technique sheets, exam administration and grading, records review and audit preparation. For wider programme work see NDT consulting in Tennessee. Book a Level III consultation for your Tennessee company.

Practise before your practical exam

Practical NDT, Atlantis NDT's 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

Tennessee trainees will find the environments familiar. The aircraft hangar mirrors aircraft maintenance at Memphis and Clarksville. The welding workshop mirrors Nashville's and Chattanooga's fabricators. The oil and gas site and storage tank match the Memphis refinery and terminals. Simulator time is not on-the-job experience and is not graded as a practical exam. Explore the Practical NDT simulator and the state page, Practical NDT for Tennessee.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As Level III he sets course content, written practices, exam questions and practical grading criteria, so what a Tennessee technician learns lines up with how that technician is examined and certified. Questions about methods, codes or your written practice can go through the contact form.

NDT training in Tennessee: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Tennessee?

Most Tennessee NDT technicians are certified by their employer under ASNT SNT-TC-1A: classroom training in a method, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and a vision test. The employer then certifies you. Atlantis NDT provides training, exam support and the written practice if needed.

Is there NDT training online in Tennessee?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online NDT theory that technicians can join from Memphis, Nashville, Knoxville, Chattanooga or anywhere in the state. Practical training and the practical exam need real specimens, arranged onsite at your employer or through an agreed arrangement.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Tennessee?

Your company needs a radioactive materials licence or x-ray registration from TDEC's Division of Radiological Health, and radiographers must meet state radiation safety training and certification rules. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Work at federal sites may follow DOE rules instead. Confirm current requirements before starting.

How much does NDT training cost in Tennessee?

Quote on request. Cost depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and whether you need written-practice or exam services. Send your details for a quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Tennessee?

UT leads, driven by nuclear, power, chemical and refinery work. ET is in demand for tubing and aircraft maintenance, RT and PAUT for piping and nuclear fabrication, and MT and VT for structural steel and automotive.

Can you train our crew onsite in Memphis, Nashville or Knoxville?

Yes. Onsite delivery is available at your facility anywhere in Tennessee, scheduled around outages, turnarounds and production. Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in Tennessee; onsite means at your site.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Tennessee employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the main employer-based NDT certification framework in the United States and is referenced by ASME and AWS codes. Nuclear and aerospace customers may add requirements that your written practice should cover.

How long does UT Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimum hours and experience are on the training requirements matrix. Logging experience usually takes longer than the classroom part.

How do I get into nuclear NDT work in Tennessee?

Start with a solid SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT, ET or VT with an outage contractor, then add site-specific training and, for some UT tasks, performance demonstration qualification. See nuclear NDT training in Oak Ridge.

Can I start NDT training with no experience?

Yes. Level I has no experience prerequisite. Many Tennessee technicians start as helpers or trainees and build documented experience toward Level II.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Tennessee?

Yes. ASNT Level III training runs live online. Level II candidates can also use the UT Level 2 practice questions.

What do NDT technicians earn in Tennessee?

Pay varies by method, level, sector and outage travel. See the NDT Level 2 salary and NDT Level 3 salary guides for published ranges.

Start NDT training in Tennessee

Whether you are a Memphis technician working toward UT Level II, a Chattanooga contractor preparing a crew for the next Sequoyah outage, an Oak Ridge fabricator tightening its written practice, or a Nashville steel erector that needs certified inspectors, Atlantis NDT builds training around your work. NDT Training and Certification in Texas

Short answer: A Texas technician or employer gets ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II or III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at the employer's own plant, shop or yard anywhere in Texas. Every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Classroom hours feed into your employer's written practice, and practical exams are given on real specimens at your facility, so certification stays with the employer that actually signs it.

Texas is the largest single market for non-destructive testing in the United States. The Houston Ship Channel, the Golden Triangle around Beaumont and Port Arthur, the Coastal Bend at Corpus Christi, the Permian Basin and the aerospace corridor of Dallas-Fort Worth each hire inspectors for different reasons, against different codes, on different calendars. This page is the Texas hub: it maps where NDT work actually happens across the state, which methods and levels each region asks for, which state agencies matter (especially for radiography crews), and how to get a crew trained without pulling people off a turnaround. If you already know what you need, you can request a Texas training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Texas

Direct answer: Most Texas NDT jobs sit in five clusters: the Houston Ship Channel and Galveston Bay refining and petrochemical belt, the Beaumont-Port Arthur refinery and LNG corridor, the Corpus Christi refining and export port, the Permian Basin pipeline and tank network around Midland and Odessa, and the aerospace and manufacturing base of Dallas-Fort Worth and San Antonio. Each cluster leans on different methods.

Houston, the Ship Channel and Galveston Bay

The stretch from downtown Houston east through Pasadena, Deer Park and Baytown to Texas City is one of the densest concentrations of refining and petrochemical capacity in the world. ExxonMobil's Baytown complex, the Deer Park refinery, the Marathon Galveston Bay refinery and Valero's Texas City plant sit alongside dozens of olefins, polymer and specialty chemical units, plus Dow's large Freeport operation to the south. Work here is driven by OSHA process safety management (29 CFR 1910.119) mechanical integrity programmes, so the daily diet is ultrasonic thickness surveys on piping circuits, shear-wave and phased array weld inspection on repairs and new tie-ins, radiography of small-bore welds, magnetic particle and penetrant on rotating-equipment and nozzle welds, and visual inspection at every stage. Spring and autumn turnarounds swell crews quickly, which is why many contractors in the Houston area want people certified before the season starts rather than during it.

The Golden Triangle: Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange

Jefferson and Orange counties host some of the largest refineries in North America, including Motiva's Port Arthur refinery, ExxonMobil Beaumont and Valero Port Arthur, together with chemical plants along the Neches River and new LNG export construction around Sabine Pass and Port Arthur. LNG construction brings a heavy load of weld inspection on cryogenic stainless and nickel-alloy piping, which means penetrant testing, radiography and increasingly PAUT and TOFD in place of film where the code and the owner allow it. Fabrication shops in the area build pressure vessels, exchangers and pipe spools to ASME Section VIII and B31.3, and each of them needs certified UT, RT, MT and PT people.

Corpus Christi and the Coastal Bend

Corpus Christi combines refining (Flint Hills Resources, Valero and Citgo all run plants there), the Cheniere Corpus Christi LNG terminal, and a port that has become one of the country's largest crude export gateways. Across the bay, Ingleside hosts offshore and modular fabrication yards. That mix creates demand for corrosion mapping and thickness work on tanks and terminals, weld inspection on new construction, and visual inspection of marine structures.

The Permian Basin and West Texas

Midland and Odessa sit at the centre of the most productive oil field in the United States. NDT work in the Permian is dominated by gathering and transmission pipelines (API 1104 weld inspection and radiography on new spreads), aboveground storage tanks at terminals and tank batteries, gas processing plants, and drill-pipe and tubular inspection for the oilfield-service sector. Crews are spread over long distances, so live online theory followed by a short onsite practical block is often the only workable way to train them. El Paso adds a refinery, Fort Bliss and cross-border manufacturing, while the Panhandle around Amarillo adds the Pantex plant and agricultural and energy equipment fabrication.

Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio and Central Texas

North Texas is an aerospace and defence hub. Lockheed Martin builds the F-35 in Fort Worth, Bell builds rotorcraft in the area, and the airline and MRO presence around DFW and Alliance supports large maintenance operations. San Antonio's Port San Antonio (the former Kelly Air Force Base) hosts aircraft MRO and engine shops, alongside Joint Base San Antonio. Aerospace employers here use eddy current, penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic inspection on structures, engines and components, and many certify their people to NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A, which we explain below. Central Texas, from Austin to Taylor, adds semiconductor and battery manufacturing, while Waco and Temple carry heavy fabrication and rail. The two nuclear stations, Comanche Peak near Glen Rose and the South Texas Project near Bay City, create outage work under ASME Section XI, and TxDOT's bridge programme keeps steel-bridge weld inspection (AWS D1.5) busy statewide.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Texas employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation. In Texas the highest volume is UT (thickness and shear wave), RT and PAUT for refinery and pipeline work, with ET, PT and MT for aerospace employers in DFW and San Antonio.
