Houston. Houston is the head office for a large share of the US inspection-contractor industry, so demand here is for volume: Level I and II UT, RT, MT and PT technicians for turnarounds, plus Level III support for companies writing or revising their written practice. Many Houston employers want a mixed cohort, with new hires starting at Level I and experienced hands upgrading to PAUT, so we often run two tracks on the same onsite schedule.

Beaumont and Port Arthur. The Golden Triangle runs on refinery maintenance and large construction. The questions we hear most are about PAUT and TOFD for heavy-wall welds, penetrant on stainless for LNG, and how to get radiography trainees through the state's trainee requirements quickly. Training is usually scheduled around the big refinery outages rather than the calendar.

Corpus Christi. Coastal Bend employers combine refinery work with terminal and tank inspection, so UT thickness, corrosion mapping and VT dominate, along with weld inspection for the fabrication yards in Ingleside and Port of Corpus Christi projects.

Midland and Odessa. Permian employers need radiographers and UT technicians for pipeline construction and tank work, and they need them spread across a huge area. Live online theory plus a compact onsite practical week at the employer's yard is the model that works best here.

Dallas-Fort Worth and San Antonio. Aerospace and MRO employers need ET, PT, MT and UT, often under NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A. Our classroom content covers the method theory either way, but the certification itself must follow whichever standard the employer's customer requires, so we ask about that at the start.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Texas, step by step

Direct answer: In Texas, as everywhere in the US, SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based. Your employer's written practice sets the rules, you complete formal training and supervised experience, a Level III gives the general, specific and practical exams, you pass a vision test, and the employer certifies you. No state agency issues a general NDT licence.

  1. Employer written practice. The employer adopts a written practice based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A (or the stricter CP-189). It defines levels, training hours, experience hours, exam content and recertification intervals. If your company does not have one, see written practice development.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete the classroom hours required by the written practice for the method and level. Our live online and onsite courses provide documented hours with a course record your employer can file.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience in the method. Minimums are set in the written practice; the training requirements matrix summarises typical figures by method and level so you can plan.
  4. General and specific exams. Written exams on method theory and on the specific procedures, codes and equipment your employer uses (for example ASME V, B31.3 or API 1104).
  5. Practical exam. A hands-on exam on real specimens with real flaws, administered by a Level III. For Texas clients we hold this at your facility using your equipment.
  6. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated at the interval the written practice sets.
  7. Certification and recertification. The employer signs and files the certification. Recertification follows the written practice, usually by evidence of continued work plus re-examination where required. For a refresher see Level II recertification.

A practical Texas wrinkle: technicians often move between Houston contractors several times in a few seasons. Because certification belongs to the employer, a new employer must review your records and recertify you under its own written practice. Keeping a clean file of course records, experience logs and exam results makes that move fast. More background is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Radiography licensing and other Texas requirements

Direct answer: Texas is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography is regulated by the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program under 25 TAC §289.255, not directly by the NRC. Radiographers and trainees need DSHS-recognised certification or trainee status in addition to their employer's SNT-TC-1A level.

Texas has been an Agreement State since 1963. The DSHS radiation control rules for industrial radiography set out how licensees and registrants use sealed sources and X-ray equipment in the field and in fixed vaults. For individuals, the important points are that a trainee must complete a radiation-safety course that meets the state rule (published DSHS guidance describes a 40-hour course) and hold trainee status before working under a radiographer trainer, and must document supervised on-the-job training before applying for radiographer certification. Field crews must carry their credentials on the job. Rules and forms change, so confirm the current requirements directly with DSHS before you plan a programme.

It is important to be clear about what Atlantis NDT does and does not cover here. Our RT courses teach radiographic technique, exposure calculation, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance criteria for SNT-TC-1A Level I and II. The state radiation-safety course and the state certification process are separate requirements that your employer's radiation safety officer manages with DSHS. We help employers line the two up so that a trainee's SNT-TC-1A hours and state trainee status run in parallel instead of one after the other.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR) runs the state boiler programme and works within the National Board inspection framework. NDT technicians meet this mainly through repair and alteration work on boilers and pressure vessels, where the National Board Inspection Code and ASME Sections I and VIII govern examination.

Pipelines. The Railroad Commission of Texas (RRC) Pipeline Safety Department oversees intrastate pipeline safety, with PHMSA covering interstate lines. Weld inspection on pipelines usually follows API 1104, and operator qualification rules apply to covered tasks.

Codes commonly used in Texas. ASME Section V (NDE methods), Section VIII (pressure vessels), B31.3 (process piping), B31.4 and B31.8 (pipelines), API 1104 (pipeline welding), API 650 and 653 context for tanks, AWS D1.1 and D1.5 for structural and bridge steel, ASME Section XI at Comanche Peak and the South Texas Project, and NAS 410 for aerospace employers. Some Texas owners also ask for API 510, 570 or 653 inspectors or AWS CWI for specific roles. Those are separate schemes; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only, and we mention them only so you know what local job postings may also request.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Texas

Direct answer: Texas technicians can take the theory portion live online from anywhere in the state, join a live-virtual cohort with other trainees, or have an Atlantis Level III deliver the whole programme onsite at their employer's facility. Atlantis has no training centre in Texas; practical exams happen at the client's site on real specimens.

Texas is too large for one-location training to suit everyone. A crew in Odessa, a fabrication shop in Orange and an MRO in San Antonio have very different constraints, so we offer three models:

  • Live online. Scheduled instructor-led classes on method theory, codes and interpretation, with recorded attendance for your training file. Good for individuals and for employers with technicians spread across the Permian or the Gulf Coast. See online NDT training.
  • Live-virtual cohort. A private online cohort for one employer, timed around shift patterns, with content mapped to your written practice and your procedures.
  • Onsite at your facility. A Level III comes to your plant, shop or yard, teaches the hands-on portion with your equipment and specimens, and administers practical exams. See corporate NDT training.

Scheduling around the Texas calendar matters. Gulf Coast refineries concentrate turnarounds in the spring and autumn, hurricane season from June to November can disrupt coastal plans, and Permian crews follow drilling and construction activity. We usually recommend running theory in the quieter months and saving the onsite practical block for a window your operations team can protect. You can ask about onsite training for your Texas crew and we will propose dates around your outage plan.

For Texas employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Texas NDT contractors, fabricators and plant owners use Atlantis NDT for written-practice development, outsourced Level III services, exam administration and corporate training programmes. Because SNT-TC-1A is employer-based, the quality of your written practice and your Level III oversight is what an auditor or client actually checks.

Smaller Houston and Permian contractors often grow faster than their quality system. A typical gap list includes a written practice that has not been revised since the company had five technicians, no clear rule on how experience from a previous employer is accepted, missing vision-test records, and practical exams that were never graded against a documented checklist. Client audits by refinery owners and EPCs tend to find exactly these gaps. We can review your current documents, write or revise the written practice, prepare exam banks and practical specimens lists, and act as your outside Level III where you do not have one in house.

  • Written practice development to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189
  • SNT-TC-1A training and certification guidance
  • Corporate NDT training programmes for whole crews
  • NDT consulting in Texas for procedure review and audit preparation

If you are an inspection company preparing for a client audit, or a fabricator who has just won work that requires certified NDT personnel, book a Level III consultation for your Texas operation.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: Trainees can rehearse inspection technique in the Atlantis Practical NDT 3D simulator, which covers 12 methods across five environments including an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is a practice tool only. It does not replace the practical exam on real specimens that your Level III administers.

For Texas technicians, the oil and gas site and storage tank environments are the closest match to daily work on the Ship Channel or in the Permian, and the aircraft hangar environment suits DFW and San Antonio aerospace trainees. The welding workshop helps new hires in Beaumont and Houston fabrication shops get used to scanning patterns and indication sizing before they touch a real weld. Details are on Practical NDT and the Texas page Practical NDT in Texas. If you are preparing for a written exam, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He designs the course content, maps it to employer written practices, and oversees the exams. For onsite programmes in Texas he works with your own Level III or acts as the examining Level III where you do not have one.

NDT training in Texas: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Texas?

Get hired or sponsored by an employer that has an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the classroom training and supervised experience it requires, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you. If you are not yet employed, completing Level I theory first makes you a stronger candidate for Houston-area contractors.

Is there NDT training online in Texas?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online SNT-TC-1A theory courses that Texas technicians can join from anywhere in the state. The practical portion and practical exam still need real equipment and specimens, which we deliver onsite at your employer's facility.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Texas?

Yes, in addition to your SNT-TC-1A level. Texas DSHS regulates industrial radiography under 25 TAC §289.255. You need a qualifying radiation-safety course and trainee status to work under a radiographer trainer, then radiographer certification after documented on-the-job training. Your employer must also hold the relevant DSHS licence or registration.

How much does NDT training cost in Texas?

We quote on request. The figure depends on the method and level, the number of trainees, whether it is online, a private cohort or onsite, and whether you need exam administration and written-practice work. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Texas?

Ultrasonic testing, including thickness surveys, shear-wave and phased array, is the broadest demand across refining, petrochemical and pipeline work. Radiography is close behind for pipelines and construction. In DFW and San Antonio, eddy current and penetrant dominate for aerospace.

Can you train our crew onsite in Houston, Beaumont or Midland?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your facility is a standard option anywhere in Texas. A Level III comes to your plant, shop or yard, uses your equipment and specimens, and runs the practical exams there.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Texas employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for NDT personnel certification across Texas refining, petrochemical, pipeline and fabrication work. Aerospace employers may require NAS 410 instead, and some owners require additional inspector schemes for certain roles.

How long does Level II training take?

It depends on the method and on your employer's written practice, which sets the classroom and experience hours. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures. Classroom time is the short part; supervised experience usually takes longer.

Can I train for PAUT in Texas without UT Level II?

Most written practices expect UT Level II or substantial UT experience before PAUT Level II, because PAUT builds directly on conventional UT theory. We can assess your background and recommend whether to start with UT.

Does Atlantis NDT have a training centre in Houston?

No. We do not operate a physical training centre in Houston or elsewhere in Texas. Training is delivered live online, as a live-virtual cohort, or onsite at your employer's facility.

Do you offer API 510, API 653 or CWI courses in Texas?

No. Atlantis NDT training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training only. Some Texas employers also ask for those separate credentials for specific inspector roles, and you would need a provider that specialises in them.

Can you help us prepare for a client NDT audit?

Yes. We review written practices, certification files, exam records and procedures, close the gaps, and can act as your outside Level III. See NDT consulting in Texas.

Start NDT training in Texas

Whether you are a single technician in Odessa, a contractor staffing a Ship Channel turnaround, or an aerospace shop in Fort Worth, the route is the same: tell us the methods, levels and number of people, and whether you want online, live-virtual or onsite delivery. Request a Texas training quote, ask about a private cohort for your Texas crew, or browse all NDT training courses. Affordable. Accessible. Fully customizable.

NDT Training and Certification in Utah

Short answer: a Utah technician or employer gets ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual sessions, or onsite delivery at the employer's refinery, depot contract site, mine, mill or fabrication shop anywhere in Utah. Courses cover Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III, and certification is issued by your employer under its written practice.

Utah's inspection market is concentrated but intense. Almost all of the state's refining capacity sits in a few miles of the Wasatch Front north of Salt Lake City. Hill Air Force Base near Ogden is one of the Air Force's main depot maintenance centres, and northern Utah builds solid rocket motors and composite aerostructures. West of the capital, one of the deepest open-pit copper mines in the world runs a concentrator and smelter. The Uinta Basin produces waxy crude that travels to those Wasatch Front refineries. Each sector asks for a different mix of methods, and many of them run on tight schedules that make sending technicians out of state for training expensive. This page explains how training and certification work for Utah employers and technicians, what Utah regulators require, and how to get a quote. Request a Utah NDT training quote and we reply with options within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Utah

Direct answer: Utah NDT work clusters in five areas: the Salt Lake refining corridor (North Salt Lake, Woods Cross and Salt Lake City), northern Utah aerospace and defence (Hill Air Force Base, Ogden and the rocket-motor sites), the Salt Lake Valley's mining, metals and manufacturing base, the Uinta Basin oil field, and central and southern Utah power, rail and mining.

The Salt Lake refining corridor

Five petroleum refineries operate in Salt Lake City, North Salt Lake and Woods Cross, packed into a narrow strip between the mountains and the Great Salt Lake wetlands. Together they supply most of the fuel used in Utah and much of the surrounding Intermountain West, and they process both Rocky Mountain crude and the waxy crude from the Uinta Basin. Turnarounds, mechanical integrity programmes and routine repairs at these plants create the state's largest concentrated demand for UT thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD weld inspection, RT of new piping welds, PT and MT on repairs, ET on heat-exchanger tubing, and VT of pressure equipment. Because the refineries sit so close together, contractors serving them often move the same crew from one site to the next during a busy turnaround season, which rewards technicians who are certified in several methods.

Northern Utah: Hill Air Force Base, Ogden and the rocket-motor sites

Hill Air Force Base, between Layton and Ogden, hosts the Ogden Air Logistics Complex, which performs depot maintenance and modification on fighter aircraft, landing gear, components and strategic missile systems. Depot work and the contractors who support it use ET, PT, MT, UT and RT extensively on airframes, wheels, landing gear and structural components, under written practices that must satisfy military and prime-contractor requirements. In Box Elder County and on the west side of the Salt Lake Valley, large solid rocket motor plants build propulsion systems for space launch and defence programmes, using RT, CT and UT to inspect motor cases, propellant, bonds and insulation. Ogden, Clearfield and the surrounding industrial parks add aerospace machining, composite fabrication and defence electronics suppliers.

Salt Lake Valley: mining, metals and manufacturing

West of Salt Lake City, the Bingham Canyon copper mine and its concentrator, smelter and refinery in the Magna area run haul trucks, shovels, crushers, mills, conveyors and pressure equipment that need regular UT, MT, PT and VT on shafts, welds, gear teeth and structural steel. A magnesium plant on the shore of the Great Salt Lake, steel and metals processors, and a large inland port and distribution network add more inspection work. The valley is also a composites centre: carbon fibre production and commercial aerostructure plants in Salt Lake City and West Valley City make composite and bonded parts for airliners, which drives demand for UT, including PAUT, and for technicians who understand composite flaw types.

The Uinta Basin

Around Vernal and Roosevelt, the Uinta Basin produces waxy crude and natural gas from thousands of wells. Gathering lines, gas processing plants, compressor stations, heated tank batteries and truck and rail loading terminals keep radiographers, UT technicians and VT inspectors busy, working to API 1104 for pipeline welds and ASME B31.3 or B31.8 for plant and gas piping. Because the basin is several hours from the Wasatch Front over mountain passes, local contractors value training they can take without leaving the field.

Central and southern Utah: power, rail, steel and mining

Emery County and Millard County host large coal-fired and converting power stations, including a major generating complex near Delta that is transitioning to gas and hydrogen-ready units. Boiler tube, header and piping inspection during outages calls for UT, RT, ET and VT. Box Elder County in the far north has a steel mini-mill near Plymouth, Iron County has iron ore mining near Cedar City, and the Union Pacific main lines through the state add rail and car-shop inspection. In the southeast, uranium processing and potash and vanadium operations bring specialised inspection, and St. George has growing construction and manufacturing. Utah's military depots in Tooele County and the test ranges in the west desert add more defence inspection work.

Bridges, highways and water

The Utah Department of Transportation commissions fabrication and in-service inspection of steel bridges on I-15, I-80, I-84 and I-70, which typically follow AASHTO/AWS D1.5 with heavy use of UT and MT. Large water projects, aqueducts, penstocks and dams operated by federal and local water agencies add weld and structural inspection.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Utah employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods, plus Level III exam preparation. The table shows each method, the levels available, how Utah employers typically use it, and what a trainee needs before starting. Your employer's written practice sets the exact hours and experience required.

MethodLevelsWhat Utah employers use it forPrerequisite

Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepRefinery weld and corrosion mapping, composite panel inspection, thick structural weldsUT Level II recommended before PAUT

Utah employers often build multi-method pathways. A refinery contractor may train new hires in VT and UT Level I, then move them to UT Level II and PAUT once they have turnaround hours. An aerospace or depot contractor may certify technicians in PT and MT Level II, then add ET for wheel and bolt-hole inspection. A mine maintenance team may need MT and UT so it can check critical components between contractor visits. We plan those pathways around your written practice so classroom hours, exams and on-the-job experience line up. Level III candidates can see the ASNT Level III training and exam preparation page.

NDT training by city in Utah

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT serves every Utah city through online and onsite delivery. Salt Lake City has a dedicated training page and a Practical NDT simulator page; Ogden, Provo, Vernal, St. George and the other industrial centres are covered by this hub. The table links each existing local page, and the paragraphs below explain which NDT work dominates in each city.

CityMain NDT sectorsPage
Salt Lake CityRefining, mining and smelting, composites and aerostructures, railNDT training in Salt Lake City / Salt Lake City practice

Salt Lake City. The capital is Utah's main NDT labour market. Refinery contractors need UT, PAUT, RT and VT technicians ready for turnaround windows; the mining and smelting complex needs MT, UT and PT on heavy equipment; and composite aerostructure plants need UT technicians who understand bonded and laminated parts. Inspection companies based in the valley also send crews to Wyoming, Idaho and Nevada. See the Salt Lake City NDT training page and the radiographic testing in Salt Lake City service page for local detail.

North Salt Lake and Woods Cross. These small cities host most of the refinery capacity in the state. Contractors here need multi-method technicians who can move between sites during the same season, and refinery owners expect certification records that will pass their own contractor audits.

Ogden, Layton and Clearfield. Depot maintenance at Hill Air Force Base and its contractor community make this the most PT-, ET- and MT-intensive part of Utah. Employers need technicians whose certifications are backed by a written practice that satisfies military and prime-contractor audits, and many also need Level III oversight for procedure approval.

Magna and West Valley City. The copper smelter and refinery, rocket-motor production and composite plants sit close together here. RT and UT on motor cases and composites, and MT and UT on heavy smelter equipment, are the main skills.

Provo and Orem. Utah County's manufacturing, construction and fabrication shops need VT, MT and UT to AWS D1.1, and fast-growing construction programmes need inspectors trained quickly.

Vernal and Roosevelt. Uinta Basin contractors need RT, UT and VT for gathering lines, plants and terminals, and value online theory because the drive to the Wasatch Front is long and weather-dependent in winter.

Delta, Price and Cedar City. Power plant outages, coal operations and iron ore mining create demand for boiler-tube UT, ET and RT, and MT on heavy equipment.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Utah, step by step

Direct answer: under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, certification in Utah is employer-based. Your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete classroom training and on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, pass a vision test, and your employer certifies you. Utah has no separate state NDT licence, but radiography is regulated by the state.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. Based on SNT-TC-1A, it sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks, vision requirements and recertification intervals for each method and level. If your company has none, we write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Take Level I and then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours per method and level.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience in the method at your Utah workplace, logged and verified by your employer.
  4. Pass the general exam on the principles of the method.
  5. Pass the specific exam on the procedures, codes and equipment you actually use, for example ASME Section V, API 1104 or your customer's aerospace specifications.
  6. Pass the practical exam on real specimens with real flaws, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Pass the vision exam for near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated at the interval in your written practice.
  8. Get certified by your employer. Certification is tied to that employer and based on documented training, experience and exams.
  9. Maintain and recertify at the interval in your written practice, and add methods or levels as your career develops.

For more detail on the employer-based system, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Utah requirements

Direct answer: Utah is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the Utah Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control, under the Utah radiation control rules. Boilers and pressure vessels fall under the Utah Labor Commission; intrastate natural gas pipeline safety under the Utah Division of Public Utilities.

Industrial radiography

As an Agreement State, Utah licenses most radioactive material used in the state through the Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control. A company doing gamma radiography with iridium-192 or similar sources needs a Utah radioactive materials licence, or reciprocity recognition if it holds an NRC or other Agreement State licence and is working temporarily in Utah. Industrial X-ray equipment is registered with the state as well. Radiographers and radiographer's assistants must meet the state's training, examination, supervision and certification requirements, which parallel the federal rules in 10 CFR Part 34. Federal sites in Utah can have their own arrangements, so confirm with the site owner. RT method training under SNT-TC-1A, which is what Atlantis provides, covers technique, exposure, film and digital imaging and interpretation; it sits alongside, not instead of, the radiation safety training and radiographer certification Utah requires. Always confirm current requirements with the Division before you deploy a crew.

Boilers and pressure vessels

The Utah Labor Commission's boiler and elevator safety programme inspects boilers and pressure vessels in the state. Utah follows the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board inspection practice, so repairs and alterations need NDT performed to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme. Refinery owners, power plants and repair shops therefore expect clear, auditable certification records.

Pipelines

The Pipeline Safety programme of the Utah Division of Public Utilities, within the Department of Commerce, inspects and enforces federal pipeline safety rules for intrastate natural gas transmission and distribution operators under certification from PHMSA. PHMSA oversees interstate pipelines directly. Pipeline welding inspection usually follows API 1104, with ASME B31.8 for gas and B31.4 for liquids, which drives demand for radiographers and UT technicians in the Uinta Basin and along transmission routes.

Codes Utah employers commonly use

  • ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3 at the Wasatch Front refineries
  • API 1104 and ASME B31.8 on Uinta Basin and transmission pipelines
  • ASME Section I and B31.1 for power plant boilers and piping
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AWS D1.5 for UDOT bridge fabrication
  • Military technical orders and NAS 410 as context for depot and aerospace work (Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A; your employer documents any additional aerospace requirements)

Some Utah employers also ask for API inspector or CWI credentials for specific roles. Those are separate schemes that Atlantis does not train; our programmes cover ASNT SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Utah

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Utah. Theory is delivered through live online or live-virtual classes, and practical training and exams are delivered onsite at your facility, using your equipment and specimens under ASNT Level III oversight. Utah crews train without losing turnaround or production days.

For individual technicians, online NDT training covers the classroom portion of Level I and Level II. You attend live sessions with a Level III instructor, ask questions in real time, and work through method principles, equipment, technique, codes and interpretation. Practical hours and the practical exam are then completed with your employer, on the equipment and parts you will actually inspect.

For employers training a group, onsite delivery is usually most efficient. We schedule classroom and practical sessions at your refinery contractor yard, depot contract facility, mine shop or fabrication plant, use your instruments, reference standards and specimens, and build the course around your procedures. A Woods Cross contractor gets UT and PAUT on piping mock-ups; an Ogden aerospace supplier gets PT, MT and ET on its own parts; a Vernal pipeline contractor gets RT and UT on weld coupons that match its procedures.

Utah's calendar shapes scheduling. Refinery turnarounds on the Wasatch Front cluster in spring and autumn, pipeline construction in the Uinta Basin slows in deep winter, power plant outages follow each owner's cycle, and depot contractors often train between aircraft inductions. We plan cohorts to finish before your busy window. Larger programmes run through corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Utah crew.

For Utah employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: SNT-TC-1A makes the employer responsible for certification, so every Utah NDT employer needs a written practice and access to a Level III. Atlantis NDT writes and updates written practices, reviews procedures, administers exams, and provides Level III services for companies without a Level III on staff.

Many Utah NDT employers are small or mid-sized: a radiography contractor in Roosevelt, an aerospace machine shop in Clearfield, a fabrication shop in Orem, a mine maintenance department near Magna. They need certified technicians but cannot justify a full-time Level III. That gap is where most audit findings come from: training records without hour counts, practical exams with no graded checklist, vision tests out of date, or a written practice copied from another company that does not match how work is actually done.

  • Written practice development and revision aligned with the current edition of SNT-TC-1A and your customers' requirements. See written practice development.
  • Exam administration: general, specific and practical exams prepared and graded under Level III oversight, with records your auditors can follow.
  • Procedure review for UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET procedures against ASME, AWS, API and customer requirements.
  • Audit preparation for refinery contractor audits, prime-contractor reviews, National Board or ASME reviews and ISO 9001 surveillance.
  • Corporate programmes for multi-site companies through corporate NDT training.

For broader Level III consulting, see our NDT consulting services and our guide to SNT-TC-1A certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Utah company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT simulator lets Utah trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments before their practical exam. It builds familiarity with technique, scan patterns and indications, but it is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The Practical NDT simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. That spread maps neatly onto Utah: the aircraft hangar for Hill Air Force Base contractors and aerostructure suppliers, the oil and gas site and storage tank for the Wasatch Front refineries and Uinta Basin facilities, and the welding workshop for fabrication, mining and bridge steel. Trainees can repeat scans and explore indication types before handling real equipment in front of an examiner.

Salt Lake City trainees can also use the Practical NDT Salt Lake City page. For written-exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Direct answer: Utah programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT.

Anoop leads course design, delivers Level III-led instruction, and oversees the exams and records that make certification defensible under SNT-TC-1A. His focus is practical: connecting method theory to the procedures, codes and parts your Utah crew actually inspects, and helping employers build written practices that hold up in audits. Ask about his availability when you contact us about Utah training.

NDT training in Utah: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Utah?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. Complete Level I and Level II classroom training in a method, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then issues certification under its written practice. If you are not yet employed, online classroom training prepares you, and certification follows once an employer documents your experience.

Is there NDT training online in Utah?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online and live-virtual Level I and Level II classes that Utah technicians can join from Salt Lake City, Ogden, Vernal, St. George or anywhere else. Practical training and practical exams are completed with your employer because they need real equipment and specimens.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Utah?

Utah is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the Utah Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control. The company holds the licence, and individual radiographers and assistants must meet state training, exam, supervision and certification requirements equivalent to 10 CFR Part 34. Confirm current requirements with the Division before starting work.

How much does NDT training cost in Utah?

Cost is quoted on request. It depends on the method and level, the number of trainees, whether sessions are live online or onsite, and whether you need exam administration or written practice support. Send your requirements and we return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Utah?

UT and PAUT lead at the Wasatch Front refineries and in composite aerostructures. PT, MT and ET are essential for depot and aerospace work around Ogden. RT and UT dominate Uinta Basin pipeline work, and MT and UT matter for mining, smelting and steel.

Can you train our crew onsite in Ogden, Salt Lake City or Vernal?

Yes. We deliver classroom and practical sessions at your facility anywhere in Utah, using your equipment and specimens, and schedule around turnarounds, outages, depot workloads and winter access.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Utah employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used basis for employer certification in US industry, including refining, pipelines, mining, fabrication and many aerospace suppliers. Customer-specific requirements can be added to your written practice.

How long does UT Level II training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, which sets classroom and experience hours. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums; see the training requirements matrix. Experience hours usually take much longer than the classroom portion.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III in Utah?

Yes. Level III candidates normally have substantial Level II experience and prepare for the ASNT Level III basic and method exams. See ASNT Level III training for exam preparation options.

Do you offer API 510 or CWI training in Utah?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some Utah refinery and fabrication employers also ask for API or CWI credentials for particular roles, but those are separate programmes.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Utah?

No. We deliver training live online and onsite at your facility. There is no Atlantis classroom building in Salt Lake City or elsewhere in Utah.

What do NDT technicians earn in Utah?

Pay varies with method, level, sector and travel. For published ranges by level, read our NDT salary guide.

Start NDT training in Utah

Whether you are one technician in Ogden, a refinery contractor in Woods Cross, a mine maintenance team in the Salt Lake Valley or a pipeline contractor in the Uinta Basin, Atlantis NDT can build an ASNT SNT-TC-1A programme that fits your work and your written practice. Training is quoted on request, and programmes are affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Request your Utah training quote, explore all NDT training courses, or talk to us about certifying your Utah crew.

NDT Training and Certification in Virginia

Short answer: Virginia technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training from Atlantis NDT in three ways: live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite sessions at your own shipyard, plant, fabrication shop or outage site. An ASNT NDT Level III leads and oversees the training. Certification under SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. Your company's written practice sets the rules, and a Level III gives the exams. Atlantis has no training centre in Virginia. We teach online or come to your facility.

Virginia's NDT market is shaped by ships more than any other state's. Hampton Roads has the country's only builder of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers, one of the Navy's four public shipyards, the largest naval base in the world and a ring of private ship-repair yards. All of that work runs on weld inspection, much of it to naval specifications. Away from the water, Virginia also has two nuclear power stations, a naval nuclear components industry in Lynchburg, aerospace research and launch sites, heavy-truck and defence manufacturing in the southwest, gas transmission pipelines across the Piedmont and the mountains, and a construction boom in Northern Virginia. This page covers where Virginia NDT work is, what each sector asks of technicians, which state agencies regulate radiography, boilers and pipelines, and how to request a Virginia NDT training quote for your crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Virginia

Direct answer: Virginia NDT work clusters in Hampton Roads (shipbuilding, ship repair, naval bases, offshore wind staging), the Peninsula and Middle Peninsula (aerospace research, nuclear), Central Virginia and Richmond (power, chemicals, manufacturing, aero-engine parts), Lynchburg (naval nuclear and commercial nuclear components), Southwest Virginia and the New River Valley (trucks, munitions, coal, pipelines) and Northern Virginia (data-centre and infrastructure construction, space and defence).

Hampton Roads: Newport News, Norfolk, Portsmouth, Chesapeake and Virginia Beach

Newport News Shipbuilding, a division of HII, builds the Navy's nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and, with a partner yard, its nuclear submarines. Across the harbour, Norfolk Naval Shipyard in Portsmouth overhauls and repairs carriers, submarines and surface ships. Private yards in Norfolk and Portsmouth handle surface-ship maintenance and repair under Navy contracts. Naval Station Norfolk, NAS Oceana and the other Hampton Roads installations add facility and equipment work. For NDT people this means a steady load of visual testing of welds, magnetic particle and penetrant testing of hull, piping and machinery welds, radiography of piping and structural joints, and ultrasonic testing of thick plate and castings. Much of it is done to naval technical publications and specifications rather than to ASME or AWS, and Navy and prime-contractor qualification rules sit on top of a company's own written practice. The Port of Virginia's marine terminals, the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel expansion, and the staging of Dominion Energy's Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind project at Portsmouth add structural steel, monopile and heavy-weld inspection.

The Peninsula and the Eastern Shore

NASA Langley Research Center in Hampton and Joint Base Langley-Eustis bring aerospace structures, wind-tunnel hardware and aircraft-maintenance work. On the Eastern Shore, NASA's Wallops Flight Facility supports rocket launches and research flights. These sites, and the contractors that support them, use eddy current, ultrasonic testing of composites and bonded structures, penetrant testing of aerospace parts and radiography of assemblies.

Central Virginia: Richmond, Petersburg, Hopewell and Chesterfield

The Richmond area combines power generation, chemical and fibre plants along the James River at Hopewell, tobacco and food processing, and precision manufacturing. Rolls-Royce's Crosspointe site in Prince George County machines aero-engine components, where surface and volumetric inspection to aerospace customer requirements is routine. Utility generating stations, gas compressor stations and steam systems around Richmond generate boiler, piping and pressure-vessel inspection during outages.

Lynchburg and the nuclear supply chain

Lynchburg is one of the country's centres of nuclear manufacturing and services. BWX Technologies builds naval nuclear reactor components there, and Framatome's US operations have a large presence in the city. Work for naval nuclear and commercial nuclear customers involves some of the strictest NDT in any industry: radiography, ultrasonic and surface methods applied under quality programmes that customers audit closely. Dominion Energy's North Anna Power Station in Louisa County and Surry Power Station on the James River add ASME Section XI in-service inspection during refuelling outages.

Southwest Virginia, the New River Valley and Roanoke

Volvo's New River Valley truck plant in Dublin, the Radford Army Ammunition Plant, rail shops in Roanoke, and metal fabricators across the I-81 corridor need weld and casting inspection. Gas transmission pipelines, including the Mountain Valley Pipeline and the older interstate systems that cross the state, create construction and integrity work in API 1104 territory. The coalfields in the far southwest still need mining-equipment and structural inspection.

Northern Virginia

Northern Virginia's data-centre construction boom needs structural steel and welding inspection, plus inspection of generator, fuel and cooling systems. The area also hosts space and defence contractors and Washington Dulles International Airport, where aircraft maintenance relies on eddy current and ultrasonic methods.

Wherever your company works in the Commonwealth, you can ask about onsite training for your Virginia crew. We plan the schedule around your production, availability or outage window.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Virginia employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT teaches UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and Level II, plus Level III exam preparation. Every course is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and on your company's written practice. The table shows how each method maps to Virginia work.

Our training teaches the method and supports your SNT-TC-1A written practice. Your Level III decides how it maps to any additional naval qualification rules your contract carries. Level III candidates usually prepare for the ASNT Basic examination and a method examination, often UT or RT in Virginia. See ASNT Level III training. UT Level II candidates can test themselves with the UT Level 2 practice questions.

NDT training by city in Virginia

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT serves every Virginia city online or onsite at the employer's facility. Newport News and Norfolk have dedicated training pages, including maritime and nuclear pages, and Richmond, Norfolk and Newport News have Practical NDT simulator pages. The table shows the main sectors in each city.

Newport News. The shipyard dominates the city's NDT market, and its suppliers and subcontractors carry the same quality expectations into smaller shops. Technicians here need sound weld-inspection skills across VT, MT, PT, UT and RT, plus an understanding of how naval specifications define acceptance. Nuclear work adds documentation discipline. See the Newport News training page and the nuclear NDT training page for the city detail.

Norfolk and Portsmouth. Ship repair runs on availability schedules, so private yards and subcontractors need technicians who can be qualified quickly and then deployed onto tight schedules. Short onsite courses timed between availabilities work well. See the Norfolk training page and maritime NDT training in Norfolk.

Richmond. Richmond-area crews tend to split between plant work (power stations, chemical plants and steam systems on the James) and production work (aero-engine and precision parts). Plant crews need UT thickness, PAUT and RT. Production inspectors need deep skill in one or two surface or volumetric methods. The Practical NDT Richmond page covers simulator practice.

Lynchburg. Nuclear manufacturers run tightly audited quality programmes. Training here is often for a specific method and a specific component family, and the specific exam must reflect the employer's procedures. Onsite training on the employer's own specimens is the strongest fit.

Roanoke, the New River Valley and Northern Virginia. Truck, rail and munitions plants need MT, PT and UT on welds, castings and forgings. Pipeline contractors need RT and PAUT to API 1104. Northern Virginia construction work leans on VT and UT to AWS D1.1. All are served online and onsite.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Virginia, step by step

Direct answer: Virginia does not issue general NDT technician licences. Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. Its written practice sets training hours, experience, exams and vision requirements. A Level III administers the exams, and the employer issues the certification once you meet every requirement.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. It defines methods, levels, training and experience hours, exam content, passing grades, vision tests and recertification. If your company needs one, see written practice development.
  2. You complete formal training. Classroom hours per method and level come from the written practice, based on SNT-TC-1A recommendations. See the training requirements matrix for the guideline figures.
  3. You build documented experience. On-the-job hours in the method, under qualified supervision, on the kind of work you will be certified for, whether that is ship welds, plant piping or production parts.
  4. You pass the general, specific and practical exams. The general exam covers theory, the specific exam covers your employer's procedures, codes and equipment, and the practical exam is done on real specimens. A Level III prepares and administers them.
  5. You pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity is checked annually, and colour contrast as the practice requires.
  6. Your employer certifies you. The certification belongs to that employer. If you move from one Hampton Roads yard to another, the new employer decides how to recertify you.
  7. You recertify on schedule. The written practice sets the interval and the evidence needed.

The ASNT NDT Level III certificate works differently. ASNT issues it centrally by examination, and employers then certify their Level III under their own practice. For more, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Virginia requirements

Direct answer: Virginia is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials used in industrial radiography, such as Ir-192 and Co-60 sources, are licensed by the Virginia Department of Health's Office of Radiological Health through its Radioactive Materials Program under the Virginia Radiation Protection Regulations (12VAC5-481). Work at federal facilities, such as Navy installations, may fall under NRC jurisdiction or other federal programmes instead.

For a Virginia radiography company, this means the state licence sets radiation-safety training, radiographer and radiographer's-assistant qualification, personnel monitoring, survey-meter and source-handling rules, and field-crew requirements, which follow the model of 10 CFR Part 34. VDH also regulates X-ray equipment. Radiation-safety training is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT method training, which covers technique, exposure, film and digital processing and interpretation. A field radiographer needs both. Exclusive federal jurisdiction areas and military sites have their own rules, so confirm the licensing route with VDH and with the facility before mobilising a crew. Rules change, so check the current requirements before a new crew starts work.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Virginia's boiler and pressure vessel programme is run by the Department of Labor and Industry (DOLI). The state adopts ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code construction rules and National Board Inspection Code repair rules. ASME Section V NDT methods with Section I or Section VIII acceptance criteria therefore show up in Virginia shop and field work, and repair organisations work to National Board requirements.

Pipelines. The Virginia State Corporation Commission's Division of Utility and Railroad Safety oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety. PHMSA regulates interstate gas and hazardous-liquid lines. Pipeline welding and NDT generally follow API 1104, and operators run their own operator-qualification programmes on top of SNT-TC-1A certification.

Codes and specifications common in Virginia. Naval technical publications and Navy fabrication and inspection standards in shipbuilding and repair. ASME Section III and Section XI in nuclear manufacturing and at North Anna and Surry. AWS D1.1 for structural steel and AASHTO/AWS D1.5 for bridges. API 1104 for pipelines. ASME B31.1 and B31.3 for power and process piping. Aerospace customer specifications and NAS 410 in aero-engine and aerospace supply chains, mentioned here as context only, because Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Virginia

Direct answer: Virginia crews can take theory online, join a live-virtual cohort with a Level III instructor, or bring the training onsite to their yard, plant or shop. Practical exams always use real specimens under Level III oversight. Video and simulation never replace them.

Training works best when it follows the state's work rhythm. Shipyards and ship-repair contractors run to availability and delivery schedules, and their busiest weeks leave no room for a classroom week, so we run theory in the gaps and keep onsite sessions short and focused. Nuclear stations refuel on fixed cycles, and contract technicians are booked months ahead for outages. Online theory lets them study between outages. Pipeline construction in the mountains slows in winter, which suits training. Data-centre construction in Northern Virginia runs year-round, so evening live-virtual sessions often work better than daytime blocks. Technicians in Southwest Virginia and on the Eastern Shore benefit most from online theory, because a classroom week in Hampton Roads or Richmond costs them days of travel.

Onsite delivery means the instructor works at your Virginia facility, with your equipment, your procedures and, where possible, your own welds and parts as practice specimens. The specific exam can then reflect your real work. Onsite delivery suits companies with several technicians in a method, or companies that want training tied closely to their written practice. Live online theory suits mixed groups and individual technicians. See online NDT training and corporate NDT training. When you are ready, request a cohort or onsite quote for Virginia. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

For Virginia employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: A Virginia company that certifies its own NDT personnel needs a compliant written practice, a responsible Level III, and training, experience and exam records that survive an audit. Atlantis NDT writes and reviews written practices, provides Level III services and runs corporate training for Virginia employers.

Many shipyard subcontractors, fabrication shops and manufacturers in Virginia have a few certified technicians and no in-house Level III. Prime-contractor audits, Navy source inspections and nuclear supplier audits are where the gaps show: training records that don't match the practice, exams not given by a qualified Level III, expired vision tests, or a practice that doesn't cover a method the shop now uses. We help close those gaps through:

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A, mapped to what your customers require.
  • Level III services: procedure and technique-sheet review, exam preparation and administration, and audit support. See NDT consulting in Virginia.
  • Corporate training programmes for multi-site employers, so crews in Newport News, Richmond and Roanoke train to one standard.
  • Plain guidance on SNT-TC-1A certification for companies writing their first practice.

If a customer audit is coming, book a Level III consultation. We start by reviewing your current documents.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets Virginia trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments before their hands-on exam. It builds familiarity with set-up and technique, but it is practice only. It does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The simulator includes an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Virginia users, the welding workshop matches shipyard and fabrication weld inspection, the aircraft hangar matches Hampton, Oceana and Dulles maintenance work, and the oil and gas site and storage tank match pipeline, terminal and power-station work. See Practical NDT and the Practical NDT Virginia page.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, written practices and Level III services, and the live-virtual and onsite training delivered to Virginia employers.

NDT training in Virginia: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Virginia?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice. Complete the classroom training it requires, log the on-the-job experience, and pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, plus the vision test. Your employer then certifies you. Atlantis provides the training and can help your employer with the practice and exams.

Is there NDT training online in Virginia?

Yes. Theory for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET can be taken live online from anywhere in the state, from Virginia Beach to the coalfields. Practical exams still use real specimens under Level III oversight.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Virginia?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence from the Virginia Department of Health, because Virginia is an NRC Agreement State. Radiographers and assistants must meet the licence's training and qualification rules. Work on federal sites can fall under federal jurisdiction, so confirm the route before you mobilise.

How much does NDT training cost in Virginia?

Training is quoted on request. The quote depends on method, level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, and whether you also need written-practice or exam support. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Virginia?

Weld inspection drives demand. VT, MT, PT, UT and RT are all heavily used in shipbuilding and ship repair, and UT and RT in nuclear manufacturing and pipelines. ET matters for aircraft maintenance and heat-exchanger tubing.

Can you train our crew onsite in Newport News or Norfolk?

Yes. Onsite training is available anywhere in Virginia, using your equipment and procedures where possible, and scheduled around availabilities and outages.

Is SNT-TC-1A accepted for shipyard work in Virginia?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used as the basis for employer certification. Naval and prime-contractor work often adds requirements of its own. Check your contract's NDT qualification clauses and have your Level III map training to them.

How long does Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice, the method and your prior experience. Both classroom and experience hours are set by the practice. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline figures.

Can I take NDT training without an employer in Virginia?

Yes, you can take classroom training as an individual, and it counts toward the formal training requirement. Certification still needs an employer and its written practice.

Do you train technicians for nuclear work in Virginia?

We provide SNT-TC-1A method training that nuclear employers can build into their qualification programmes. Nuclear owners and suppliers set their own additional requirements, which your Level III applies. See the nuclear NDT training page.

Do you prepare candidates for the ASNT Level III exams?

Yes. We offer preparation for the Basic and method examinations. See ASNT Level III training.

What does an NDT technician earn in Virginia?

Pay varies by method, level, sector and overtime. For published ranges, see the NDT salary guide.

NDT Training and Certification in Washington

Short answer: Washington State technicians and employers can get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III NDT training from Atlantis NDT live online, in live-virtual cohorts, or onsite at their own plant, shipyard, refinery or project site, led and overseen by an ASNT NDT Level III. Certification is employer-based under your written practice. Atlantis has no training centre in Washington; delivery is online or at your facility. (This page covers Washington State. For the capital region, see NDT training in Washington, DC.)

Washington State combines some of the most demanding NDT customers in the country. Commercial aircraft are built around Puget Sound, five refineries sit on the northern Puget Sound and Tacoma shorelines, the Navy maintains submarines and aircraft carriers at Bremerton, the Hanford Site and the state's only commercial nuclear plant sit near Richland, the Columbia River hydropower system runs through the centre of the state, and ports, bridges and ferries need constant structural inspection. Each of these sectors works to different codes and customer requirements, and the combination makes Washington one of the most varied NDT markets in the West. This page explains how Atlantis NDT training works in Washington, the regulators that matter, and how to request a Washington training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in Washington

Direct answer: Washington NDT demand clusters in the Puget Sound aerospace corridor (Everett, Renton, Auburn, Kent), the northern Puget Sound refinery belt (Anacortes, Ferndale, Blaine), Kitsap County and the shipyards (Bremerton, Bangor, Seattle, Everett, Tacoma), the Tri-Cities (Hanford and nuclear power), Spokane and Eastern Washington (aluminium, aerospace parts, air base, mining), and the Columbia River and port cities (Longview, Vancouver).

Puget Sound aerospace: Everett, Renton, Auburn and Kent

Boeing builds commercial aircraft in Everett and Renton and makes parts and assemblies in Auburn and at its composites operations in the region, and hundreds of Washington suppliers machine, form, bond and assemble aerospace parts. Aerospace manufacturing is NDT-intensive: ultrasonic inspection of composite structures, eddy current on fastener holes and aluminium structure, penetrant and magnetic particle on machined and forged parts, and radiography of castings and assemblies. Blue Origin in Kent and other space companies add further demand. Aerospace employers usually qualify technicians to their customer's system, often NAS 410; our SNT-TC-1A training is the method foundation, and your Level III maps it into the customer's requirements.

Northern Puget Sound refineries: Anacortes, Ferndale and Blaine

Washington's refining capacity is concentrated in Skagit and Whatcom counties: two refineries at March Point near Anacortes, one near Ferndale and BP's Cherry Point refinery near Blaine, with a fifth, smaller refinery at the Port of Tacoma. Refinery turnarounds bring in contract technicians for UT thickness surveys, PAUT and TOFD on pressure-vessel welds, radiography of piping welds, and tank inspection. The Olympic Pipeline carries refined products south from these refineries through Seattle and Tacoma to Portland, adding pipeline integrity and repair work.

Shipyards and naval bases: Bremerton, Bangor, Everett, Seattle and Tacoma

Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility in Bremerton is one of the Navy's four public shipyards and maintains aircraft carriers and submarines; Naval Base Kitsap at Bangor and Naval Station Everett add more naval work. Naval NDT runs under NAVSEA requirements, with VT, MT, PT, UT and RT on hull, piping and structural welds. Commercial shipyards in Seattle and Tacoma build and repair ferries, fishing vessels, tugs and barges, and Washington State Ferries operates the largest ferry system in the US.

Tri-Cities: Richland, Kennewick and Pasco

The Hanford Site near Richland is the largest environmental clean-up project in the US, including tank waste storage and treatment facilities, and Energy Northwest's Columbia Generating Station is Washington's only commercial nuclear power plant. Nuclear and waste-treatment work brings ASME Section XI in-service inspection, quality programmes under NQA-1, and UT, VT, PT and RT of welds and components. See NDT training in Richland and nuclear NDT training in Richland.

Spokane and Eastern Washington

Spokane has aluminium rolling at Kaiser Aluminum's Trentwood works, aerospace parts manufacturers, Fairchild Air Force Base's tanker fleet, and mining and heavy-equipment suppliers serving the Inland Northwest. Central Washington's Columbia River dams, including Grand Coulee, the largest power station in the US by capacity, need inspection of penstocks, turbines, gates and structural steel.

Ports, bridges and the Columbia River

The Northwest Seaport Alliance ports of Seattle and Tacoma, the Port of Vancouver and the Port of Longview have cranes, terminals and bulk-handling structures that need regular inspection. WSDOT's bridge network includes floating bridges such as SR 520 and long-span crossings such as the Tacoma Narrows bridges, and the Interstate Bridge replacement programme between Vancouver and Portland is one of the largest planned infrastructure projects in the region. Pulp and paper mills in Longview and elsewhere add boiler and pressure-vessel work.

Wherever your crew is, you can ask about onsite training for your Washington crew.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Washington employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT teaches UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and II, plus Level III exam preparation, to ASNT SNT-TC-1A and your company written practice. The table maps each method to Washington work.

Seattle. Seattle's NDT market mixes aerospace suppliers, shipyards and the container port with a large construction sector. Technicians commonly hold UT and ET for aerospace or UT, MT and VT for marine and structural work. See the Seattle training page.

Richland and the Tri-Cities. Hanford and Columbia Generating Station make this the state's nuclear and quality-programme hub. Training here often needs to fit NQA-1 quality systems and ASME Section XI work; we teach the NDT methods and help employers document qualification under their written practice.

Tacoma. The Port of Tacoma, its refinery, shipyards and Joint Base Lewis-McChord nearby create varied demand from structural and crane inspection to piping and aircraft work.

Spokane. Aluminium rolling, aerospace parts and heavy equipment give Spokane demand for UT, ET and PT, and Eastern Washington employers benefit most from online theory because of travel distances.

Everett, Renton and the refinery belt. Aerospace manufacturing in Everett and Renton and turnaround work in Anacortes and Ferndale are the two biggest contract-technician magnets in Western Washington.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Washington, step by step

Direct answer: Washington State does not certify NDT technicians. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you when you meet its written practice: training, experience, general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and vision tests.

  1. Written practice. The employer's document sets methods, levels, training and experience requirements, exam content and recertification. If you need one, see written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. Hours per method and level per the practice; see the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline figures.
  3. On-the-job experience. Documented time in the method on the work you will do, under qualified supervision.
  4. Exams. General, specific and practical, administered by a Level III, with practicals on real specimens.
  5. Vision tests. Annual near-vision and colour contrast as the practice requires.
  6. Employer certification. Valid with that employer under its practice.
  7. Recertification. At the interval the practice defines.

The ASNT NDT Level III certificate is issued by ASNT through examination; the employer then certifies its Level III. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Washington requirements

Direct answer: Washington is an NRC Agreement State. The Washington State Department of Health, Office of Radiation Protection, licenses and inspects radioactive-materials users, including industrial radiography companies, and also registers and inspects X-ray equipment. Its rules are kept compatible with the NRC's industrial radiography requirements in 10 CFR Part 34.

A Washington radiography company therefore deals with the state, not the NRC, for its licence, inspections, reporting and reciprocity for out-of-state crews. Radiographers and radiographer trainees need radiation-safety training, an accepted radiographer certification route, personnel dosimetry, calibrated survey instruments and compliant crew arrangements. Federal facilities such as the Hanford Site and the naval shipyard operate under their own federal programmes, and contractors working there follow site-specific radiation-protection rules in addition to their own licence. Radiation-safety training is separate from the SNT-TC-1A RT method course, which teaches technique and interpretation; your crew needs both. Confirm current requirements with the Office of Radiation Protection before new field work.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Washington's boiler and pressure-vessel programme is run by the Department of Labor and Industries (L&I). Washington adopts ASME and National Board codes, so ASME Section V NDT and Section I or VIII acceptance criteria apply to new construction, and National Board Inspection Code rules apply to repairs and alterations.

Pipelines. The Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission runs the state's pipeline safety programme for intrastate lines and acts as an agent of PHMSA for some interstate inspections; PHMSA regulates interstate pipelines such as the Olympic Pipeline. Pipeline welding and NDT generally follow API 1104 and operator qualification programmes.

Codes common in Washington. Aerospace customer specifications and NAS 410 (context only); ASME V, VIII and B31.3 at refineries; ASME Section XI and NQA-1 in nuclear; NAVSEA technical publications in naval shipyards; AWS D1.1 and AASHTO/AWS D1.5 for structural steel and WSDOT bridges; API 1104 for pipelines; API 650 and 653 for tanks as owner programmes (we train the NDT technicians, not API inspectors).

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Washington

Direct answer: Washington crews can take Atlantis NDT theory live online or in live-virtual cohorts on Pacific time, or have Level III-led training delivered onsite at their facility. Practical exams always use real specimens under Level III oversight.

Scheduling in Washington follows the industries. Aerospace manufacturing runs on production rates and shifts, so evening online sessions suit many technicians. Refinery turnarounds in Anacortes, Ferndale, Blaine and Tacoma concentrate demand into a few weeks, so we push theory into the months before. Naval shipyard availabilities and nuclear refuelling outages at Columbia Generating Station are scheduled long in advance. Eastern Washington and the Tri-Cities are a long way from Puget Sound, and crossing the Cascades in winter is unreliable, so online theory with onsite practicals is often the best combination there. Construction and bridge work slows in the wet season, which is a good time for structural inspectors to study. Onsite training uses your equipment, procedures and parts, and suits aerospace suppliers and fabrication shops that need several technicians at once. See online NDT training and corporate NDT training, then request a cohort or onsite quote for Washington; quotes come back within one business day.

For Washington employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Washington employers that certify their own NDT personnel need an SNT-TC-1A written practice, a qualified Level III and auditable records. Atlantis NDT writes and reviews written practices, provides Level III services and runs corporate training programmes for Washington companies.

Aerospace suppliers in particular face frequent customer audits, and nuclear and naval contractors face strict quality-programme reviews. Typical findings are written practices that do not match current procedures, training records without hours or instructor details, exams not administered by a Level III, and lapsed vision tests. We help with:

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A, aligned with customer requirements.
  • Level III services: procedures, technique sheets, exam administration and audit support; see NDT consulting in Washington.
  • Corporate training programmes for employers with sites on both sides of the Cascades.
  • Guidance on SNT-TC-1A certification.

Facing a customer or quality audit? Book a Level III consultation for your Washington company.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets Washington trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments before their hands-on exam. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

The aircraft hangar environment suits Puget Sound aerospace and base maintenance; the oil and gas site and storage tank match refinery and pipeline work in the northern Puget Sound and Tacoma; the welding workshop matches shipyard, structural and fabrication work; and the NDT lab covers fundamentals for every method. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT Washington.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, written practices, exams and Level III services for Washington clients.

NDT training in Washington: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Washington State?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete the required training and experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass the vision test. The employer then certifies you.

Is there NDT training online in Washington?

Yes. Theory for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET is available live online across Washington, from Bellingham to Spokane. Practical exams use real specimens under Level III oversight.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Washington State?

Washington is an Agreement State, so radiography companies are licensed by the Department of Health's Office of Radiation Protection, and radiographers must meet its training and certification requirements. Confirm current rules with the Office of Radiation Protection.

Can you train our crew onsite in Everett, Tacoma or Spokane?

Yes. Onsite training is available at your facility anywhere in Washington, subject to your site access and safety requirements.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Washington employers?

Yes, across refining, power, construction, shipbuilding and much of manufacturing. Aerospace employers often also reference NAS 410, and naval work references NAVSEA requirements, so check your customer's standard.

How long does UT Level II take?

It depends on the written practice and your experience. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A guideline hours.

Can I take NDT training without an employer?
