NDT Training and Certification in Wisconsin

Short answer: A Wisconsin technician or employer gets ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II or III training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, a private live-virtual cohort, or onsite delivery at the employer's own foundry, shipyard, fabrication shop or plant. Every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III. Classroom hours are mapped to your employer's written practice, and practical exams are given on real specimens at your facility, so the certification stays with the employer that signs it.

Wisconsin is a manufacturing state before it is anything else. Heavy equipment, castings and forgings, engines, pressure vessels, cranes, military vehicles, marine propulsion and ships are built here, and almost every one of those products passes through a magnetic particle bench, an ultrasonic station or a radiography vault before it ships. Add a lakeshore nuclear station, the Superior refinery and crude terminal at the head of Lake Superior, a dense paper-mill belt along the Fox and Wisconsin rivers, and a large bridge inventory managed by the state DOT, and you have steady NDT demand that looks very different from the Gulf Coast. This hub explains where that demand sits, which methods and levels Wisconsin employers ask for, which state agencies matter for radiography crews, and how to get people trained without shutting down a production line. If you already know what you need, request a Wisconsin training quote and we will reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Wisconsin

Direct answer: Wisconsin NDT work clusters in five areas: the Milwaukee, Waukesha and Racine-Kenosha manufacturing corridor; the Fox Valley and Green Bay paper, vehicle and machinery belt; the lakeshore shipbuilding and nuclear coast from Manitowoc to Marinette; the Twin Ports energy hub at Superior; and the western and central cities of La Crosse, Eau Claire and Wausau. Manufacturing quality control drives most of it.

Milwaukee, Waukesha, Racine and Kenosha

The southeast corner of the state carries the largest share of Wisconsin's industrial employment. Milwaukee's industrial valley and the suburbs around it are home to foundries, forge shops, gear and power-transmission manufacturers, mining-equipment builders (the large-shovel and mining-machinery works in South Milwaukee and Milwaukee) and engine and motorcycle production. Waukesha County adds engine, generator and medical-equipment manufacturing, and Racine and Kenosha add agricultural equipment, consumer-goods plants and a growing band of distribution and light-manufacturing sites along the I-94 corridor. For NDT this means a lot of in-house quality labs: magnetic particle inspection of castings, forgings and welded frames; penetrant testing of non-ferrous parts; ultrasonic testing of heavy sections, shafts and weldments; and film or digital radiography of castings in fixed vaults. Many of these employers certify their own Level I and II staff under an SNT-TC-1A written practice and bring in an outside Level III to write procedures and give exams, which is exactly the model Atlantis supports.

Fox Valley, Oshkosh and Green Bay

From Fond du Lac north through Oshkosh, Neenah, Appleton and Kaukauna to Green Bay, the Fox River valley combines one of the country's densest concentrations of paper and tissue mills with heavy vehicle and machinery manufacturing. Oshkosh builds military and specialty trucks, Fond du Lac builds marine engines, and the region has a long tail of fabrication shops that supply the mills with pressure vessels, digesters, dryers, piping and structural steel. Paper mills are steam-heavy plants: Yankee dryers, recovery boilers, digesters and pressure piping all need ultrasonic thickness surveys, shear-wave weld inspection and visual inspection during scheduled mill outages, and a dryer or recovery boiler inspection programme often calls for UT, MT, PT and sometimes eddy current. Green Bay adds a commercial port, food-processing plants with stainless pressure systems, and the fabrication and machining shops that serve them.

Manitowoc, Sturgeon Bay, Marinette and the lakeshore

Wisconsin's Lake Michigan shore is a shipbuilding coast. Marinette builds naval and commercial vessels, Sturgeon Bay builds and repairs Great Lakes freighters, tugs and barges, and Manitowoc has a long shipbuilding and crane-manufacturing history with marine fabrication still active today. Shipyard work is weld-inspection work: visual testing of every weld, magnetic particle on fillet and structural welds, ultrasonic and radiographic testing of butt welds, and increasingly phased array, all to naval or classification-society requirements. Navy programmes typically reference NAVSEA technical publications for NDT personnel and acceptance standards, which some yards apply alongside SNT-TC-1A, so a yard's written practice needs to be explicit about which requirement governs. On the same shore, near Two Rivers, the Point Beach nuclear plant runs refuelling outages that bring in inspection crews working to ASME Section XI.

Superior and the Twin Ports

At the western tip of Lake Superior, the city of Superior hosts a refinery, a major crude-oil pipeline terminal where Canadian crude enters the US Great Lakes system, grain and ore docks, and shipyard repair work. The refinery and terminal run mechanical integrity programmes with ultrasonic thickness surveys on piping and tanks, weld inspection on repairs, and radiography of small-bore piping, while pipeline construction and maintenance in the region call for API 1104 weld inspection. Superior shares a labour market with Duluth, Minnesota, so many technicians work both sides of the bridge; our Duluth NDT training page covers the Minnesota side.

La Crosse, Eau Claire, Wausau and central Wisconsin

Western and central Wisconsin carry HVAC and refrigeration equipment manufacturing in La Crosse, food and dairy processing with stainless pressure systems across the dairy counties, paper mills along the Wisconsin River at Wisconsin Rapids, Stevens Point and Rhinelander, window and door manufacturing, and fabrication shops that serve agriculture and energy. Coal and gas-fired power stations, plus wind and solar projects, add boiler, piping and structural inspection. Statewide, the Wisconsin Department of Transportation's steel bridge inventory keeps bridge weld inspection to AWS D1.5 in demand, and rail freight lines and car shops add wheel, axle and weld inspection work.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses for Wisconsin employers

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, plus Level III exam preparation. In Wisconsin the heaviest demand is MT, PT and UT for castings, forgings and weldments, RT for foundry and shipyard work, and UT, VT and ET for paper mills, power plants and the lakeshore nuclear outage market.

MethodLevelsWhat Wisconsin employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic testing (UT)I, II, III prepShaft, forging and heavy-section inspection in Milwaukee plants, thickness surveys on paper-mill dryers and digesters, shear-wave weld inspection in shipyards and fabrication shopsLevel I: none beyond employer requirements. Level II: Level I plus experience per written practice

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Wisconsin, step by step

Direct answer: Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you, not the state or a school. You complete the training and experience your employer's written practice requires, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, pass a vision test, and the employer issues certification. The same path applies in every Wisconsin industry that uses SNT-TC-1A.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer (or the company sponsoring you) must have a written practice that sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and recertification rules for each method and level. If your company does not have one, we can write it.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the formal training hours required for your method and level. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures; your written practice is what governs.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience in the method, documented by your employer. In a Wisconsin foundry or shipyard this is usually the longest part of the process.
  4. General and specific written exams. A Level III administers the general (theory) and specific (procedures, codes and equipment) exams.
  5. Practical exam. You perform the method on real specimens and write up results, graded by a Level III against a documented checklist.
  6. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, typically repeated every year.
  7. Certification. The employer certifies you to Level I or II in that method. Certification is tied to that employer.
  8. Recertification. At the interval set in the written practice, by exam or by evidence of continued satisfactory work, depending on the employer's rules.

For a fuller explanation, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiography licensing and other Wisconsin requirements

Direct answer: Wisconsin has been an NRC Agreement State since August 2003, so industrial radiography with sealed sources is licensed by the Wisconsin Department of Health Services (DHS) Radiation Protection Section under chapter DHS 157 of the Wisconsin Administrative Code, not directly by the NRC. Radiographers and trainees must meet those state rules in addition to their employer's SNT-TC-1A certification.

Wisconsin's industrial radiography rules follow the same structure as the federal rules in 10 CFR Part 34: a licensee must have a radiation safety officer and operating and emergency procedures; individuals must complete radiation-safety training and work as trainees under a qualified radiographer trainer before acting as radiographers; radiographers must be certified through a recognised certifying programme; and personnel must wear dosimetry and carry survey meters in the field. X-ray equipment used in fixed vaults, common in Wisconsin foundries, is also regulated by DHS. Details change, so confirm the current requirements with the DHS Radiation Protection Section before you plan an RT programme.

What Atlantis NDT covers: our RT courses teach radiographic technique, exposure calculation, film and digital interpretation, and code acceptance criteria for SNT-TC-1A Level I and II. The state radiation-safety requirements and radiographer certification are separate obligations that your radiation safety officer manages. We help employers line the two up so a trainee's SNT-TC-1A hours and state trainee status run in parallel.

Boilers and pressure vessels. The Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS) runs the state boiler and pressure vessel programme, working within the National Board inspection framework. NDT technicians meet this mainly in repair and alteration work on boilers and vessels at mills, power plants and food plants, where the National Board Inspection Code and ASME Sections I and VIII govern examination.

Pipelines. The Public Service Commission of Wisconsin oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety in partnership with PHMSA, which regulates interstate gas and hazardous liquid lines such as the crude system serving Superior. Pipeline weld inspection usually follows API 1104, and operator qualification rules apply to covered tasks.

Codes commonly used in Wisconsin. ASME Section V (NDE methods), Sections I and VIII (boilers and pressure vessels), B31.1 and B31.3 (power and process piping), ASTM casting and forging standards, AWS D1.1 for structural steel and D1.5 for bridges, NAVSEA publications in naval shipbuilding, ASME Section XI at Point Beach, and API 1104 for pipelines. Some Wisconsin employers also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials for particular roles. Those are separate schemes; Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only, and we mention them only so you know what local job postings may request.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Wisconsin

Direct answer: Wisconsin technicians can take theory live online, join a private live-virtual cohort for their employer, or have an Atlantis Level III deliver the programme onsite at their plant, shop or yard. Atlantis has no training centre in Wisconsin; practical exams are held at the client's facility on real specimens.

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory classes with attendance records, suited to individuals and to plants running three shifts. See online NDT training.

  • Onsite. A Level III teaches the hands-on portion and runs practical exams at your facility, whether that is a foundry in Milwaukee, a mill in the Fox Valley or a yard on the lakeshore. See corporate NDT training.

The Wisconsin calendar matters. Paper mills schedule outages months in advance, the Point Beach plant runs refuelling outages on its own cycle, Great Lakes shipyards do much of their repair work during the winter lay-up when the Soo Locks are closed and freighters come in, and outdoor bridge and pipeline work slows in deep winter. We usually suggest online theory in the quiet weeks and a protected onsite practical block. Ask about onsite training for your Wisconsin crew.

For Wisconsin employers: written practice and Level III services

Direct answer: Wisconsin manufacturers, foundries, shipyards and inspection labs use Atlantis NDT to write or update SNT-TC-1A written practices, provide outside Level III services, administer exams and train whole teams. Customer audits from OEMs, the Navy supply chain and plant owners check exactly these records.

Common gaps in Wisconsin manufacturers' NDT programmes include a written practice that was written for one method and never extended when the plant added UT or PAUT, procedures that cite an outdated edition of a code, missing documentation of practical exams, and vision-test records that lapsed when a supervisor retired. Shipyards add the complication of reconciling NAVSEA and SNT-TC-1A requirements. We review your documents, write or revise the written practice and procedures, build exam banks, and can act as your examining Level III.

Practise before your practical exam

Direct answer: The Atlantis Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens given by your Level III.

Wisconsin foundry and machine-shop trainees get most from the NDT lab scene, shipyard and fabrication trainees from the welding workshop, and Superior refinery and terminal trainees from the oil and gas site and storage tank scenes. See Practical NDT and Practical NDT in Wisconsin. For written exam practice, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He builds the course content, maps it to each employer's written practice and oversees examinations. On onsite programmes in Wisconsin he works alongside your Level III or serves as the examining Level III if you do not have one.

NDT training in Wisconsin: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Wisconsin?

Work for or be sponsored by an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete its required classroom training and supervised experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you. Starting Level I theory before you are hired can make you a stronger candidate for Wisconsin manufacturers and labs.

Is there NDT training online in Wisconsin?

Yes. Atlantis NDT delivers the theory portion live online to Wisconsin technicians. Practical training and practical exams are completed on real specimens, either at your employer's facility or through an arranged practical session.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Wisconsin?

Industrial radiography in Wisconsin is licensed by the Department of Health Services, because Wisconsin is an NRC Agreement State. Your employer holds the licence; individuals need state-compliant radiation-safety training, trainee status and radiographer certification. SNT-TC-1A certification is a separate, additional requirement.

How much does NDT training cost in Wisconsin?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on the method, the level, the number of people, and whether you choose online, a private cohort or onsite delivery. Request a quote and we reply within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Wisconsin?

Magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing are the most widely used in Wisconsin because of the volume of castings, forgings and heavy weldments built here. Radiography is strong in foundries and shipyards, and visual testing is required almost everywhere.

Can you train our crew onsite in Milwaukee or Green Bay?

Yes. A Level III can deliver the hands-on portion at your plant in Milwaukee, Green Bay or anywhere else in Wisconsin, using your equipment and parts, and run the practical exams there.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Wisconsin employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the most common basis for NDT certification in Wisconsin manufacturing, fabrication and power generation. Naval shipyards may apply NAVSEA requirements in addition, and some aerospace suppliers use NAS 410.

How long does Level II training take?

It depends on the method and your employer's written practice, which sets the classroom and experience hours. The training requirements matrix shows typical figures. Supervised experience usually takes longer than the classroom part.

Does Atlantis NDT have a training centre in Milwaukee?

No. We do not operate a physical training centre in Milwaukee or anywhere else in Wisconsin. Training is delivered live online, as a live-virtual cohort, or onsite at your employer's facility.

Can a Wisconsin foundry certify its own MT and PT inspectors?

Yes, if it has an SNT-TC-1A written practice and access to a Level III to administer exams. Many foundries use an outside Level III for this; Atlantis can fill that role.

Do you offer CWI or API inspector courses in Wisconsin?

No. Atlantis NDT training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training only. Some Wisconsin employers also ask for those separate credentials for particular roles, and you would need a provider that specialises in them.

NDT Training and Certification in Wyoming

Short answer: Wyoming technicians and employers get ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training from Atlantis NDT through live online classes, live-virtual cohorts, or onsite delivery at their own refinery, gas plant, mine, power station or fabrication shop. Courses cover Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, every programme is led by an ASNT NDT Level III, and your employer certifies you under its written practice, which we can help you write.

Wyoming is an energy state from end to end. It produces more coal than any other state from the Powder River Basin around Gillette, it has large natural gas fields and processing plants in the southwest, oil fields across the central basins, refineries at Sinclair, Casper, Cheyenne and Newcastle, the world's largest known trona deposits around Green River, coal-fired power plants, some of the biggest wind projects in the West, and now a first-of-a-kind advanced nuclear plant under construction near Kemmerer. All of that sits in the least populous state in the country, where crews are small and distances are long. NDT training here has to work around those realities: technicians who cannot leave site for weeks, small employers without an in-house Level III, and a seasonal calendar where outdoor work slows sharply in winter. This page sets out where the work is, which methods each sector needs, how radiography is regulated in Wyoming, and how to get a programme built for your crew. Request a Wyoming NDT training quote and we reply within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Wyoming

Direct answer: Wyoming NDT work clusters in five regions: the Powder River Basin around Gillette (coal mining, oil and gas), central Wyoming around Casper (refining, oil field service and fabrication), the southwest around Rock Springs, Green River, Kemmerer and Pinedale (gas processing, trona, power and nuclear construction), the south-central I-80 corridor around Rawlins and Sinclair (refining and wind), and southeast Wyoming around Cheyenne and Laramie (refining and renewable diesel, an Air Force base, rail and data centres).

The Powder River Basin: Gillette, Wright and Douglas

Campbell and Converse counties host the giant surface coal mines of the Powder River Basin and a large share of Wyoming's oil and gas drilling. Mines run fleets of haul trucks, shovels, draglines, crushers and long conveyor systems, all of which need regular MT and UT inspection of welded frames, booms, pins and shafts, plus VT and PT on repairs. Mine-mouth power plants near Gillette add boiler tube, high-energy piping and pressure-part inspection during outages. The oil and gas side brings gathering lines, compressor stations and tank batteries inspected with RT, UT and VT to API 1104 and ASME B31 codes. Gillette is also home to many of the fabrication and repair shops that keep this equipment running.

Central Wyoming: Casper and Glenrock

Casper is the state's oil town. The HF Sinclair refinery in Casper, a long list of oil field service, pipeline and fabrication companies, and the regional offices of producers and midstream operators make it the natural base for inspection companies serving the central basins. Refinery turnarounds bring UT thickness, PAUT, TOFD, RT, ET and VT work; pipeline and terminal operators need integrity digs and weld inspection; and fabrication shops building skids, vessels and tanks need certified inspectors to ASME Section VIII and AWS D1.1. The Dave Johnston power plant at Glenrock east of Casper is another outage-driven NDT customer.

Southwest Wyoming: Rock Springs, Green River, Kemmerer and Pinedale

Sweetwater County's trona mines and soda ash refineries around Green River are heavy industrial plants with kilns, calciners, crystallisers, pressure vessels and process piping that need regular UT, MT, PT and VT inspection. Further north, the Jonah and Pinedale Anticline gas fields and the large gas processing complex at Shute Creek near LaBarge drive pipeline and plant inspection. The Jim Bridger power plant east of Rock Springs and the Naughton plant near Kemmerer add power plant outage work. Kemmerer is also the site of TerraPower's Natrium plant: the NRC approved its construction permit in March 2026 and nuclear construction began in April 2026, which brings nuclear-quality fabrication and construction inspection into the region, including documented NDT on welds and components built to nuclear codes.

South-central Wyoming: Rawlins, Sinclair and the wind corridor

The Sinclair refinery, one of the oldest in the Rocky Mountains, sits just east of Rawlins on Interstate 80. Its turnarounds draw UT, PAUT, RT, ET and VT technicians from across the region. Carbon County is also home to some of the largest wind energy developments in the West; turbine towers, foundations and transmission structures involve UT and MT of structural welds during fabrication and erection, plus VT and UT of bolted and welded connections during maintenance.

Southeast Wyoming: Cheyenne and Laramie

Cheyenne has an HF Sinclair renewable diesel unit on the site of its former crude refinery, F.E. Warren Air Force Base with its missile wing, a major rail yard and a growing cluster of large data centres. Base construction and maintenance, rail car and track work, and data-centre construction with their large structural steel frames and backup power systems all generate VT, UT and MT work. Laramie adds the University of Wyoming's engineering and research activity and regional construction.

Northeast Wyoming: Newcastle and Sheridan

Newcastle has its own small refinery, and Sheridan has fabrication, construction and coal-related activity near the Montana border. Both are typical of Wyoming's small, dispersed NDT employers that need a few multi-method technicians rather than large crews.

Pipelines, rail and highways

Wyoming is a crossroads for crude, natural gas, natural gas liquids and carbon dioxide pipelines heading to markets in every direction, and a major east-west rail corridor runs along Interstate 80. Pipeline construction, integrity digs, compressor and pump stations, rail shops and the Wyoming Department of Transportation's bridge inventory all need RT, UT, MT and VT inspectors.

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I and Level II courses in eight methods plus Level III exam preparation. Because Wyoming crews are small, multi-method technicians are especially valuable. A Casper inspection company may want its people certified in UT, MT, VT and RT; a Gillette mine wants MT and UT Level II for its maintenance planners; a Green River soda ash plant wants UT thickness and PT for its reliability team. We sequence those certifications around your written practice so the classroom, exam and experience requirements fit together. Method-specific pages include UT Level 2 training, MT Level 2 training, RT Level 2 training and oil and gas NDT training; Level III candidates can start with ASNT Level III training.

NDT training by city in Wyoming

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT serves every Wyoming city through online and onsite delivery. Casper and Cheyenne have Practical NDT simulator pages; other cities are covered by the state programme on this page. The table summarises the main NDT sectors by city, followed by a short note on what employers in each city need.

Casper. The centre of Wyoming's inspection industry. Refinery turnarounds, pipeline integrity work and fabrication for the oil field keep UT, RT, MT, PT and VT technicians busy, and many statewide inspection companies are based here. A cohort trained before a turnaround window is the most common request.

Cheyenne. Renewable diesel operations, base construction and maintenance at F.E. Warren, rail work and data-centre construction create a mix of plant inspection and construction VT, UT and MT. Federal and data-centre customers expect clean, auditable certification records.

Gillette. Mining equipment inspection dominates: MT and UT on welded structures, pins and shafts, with VT and PT on repairs, alongside power plant and oil field work. Mine maintenance departments often certify their own people rather than rely solely on contractors.

Rock Springs and Green River. Soda ash plants, gas processing and the Jim Bridger plant generate steady UT, PT, ET and VT work, with RT on pipeline and piping welds.

Kemmerer. Nuclear construction and the existing Naughton plant make Kemmerer a place where documented, auditable NDT matters more than almost anywhere else in the state. Contractors supporting nuclear-quality work need written practices and records that satisfy demanding quality assurance programmes.

Rawlins and Sinclair. Refinery turnarounds and wind farm construction and maintenance call for UT, PAUT, MT and VT, with RT on refinery piping.

Laramie, Sheridan and Newcastle. Smaller markets where a fabrication shop, construction contractor or the Newcastle refinery may need just one or two certified inspectors and a written practice that fits their size.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Wyoming, step by step

Direct answer: Wyoming has no state licence for NDT technicians. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you once you have completed classroom training and documented experience and passed general, specific, practical and vision exams administered under a Level III. Radiography also requires federal radiation safety qualification.

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. This SNT-TC-1A-based document sets training hours, experience hours, exam content and pass marks, vision rules and recertification intervals. If your company does not have one, we write it with you; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Level I and then Level II training in your method, live online or onsite. Hours follow your written practice; the training requirements matrix lists SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. Build documented on-the-job experience. Log supervised experience at your refinery, mine, gas plant or pipeline spread, documented and verified by your employer.
  4. Pass the general exam. A written exam on method principles.
  5. Pass the specific exam. On your employer's procedures, the applicable codes (ASME Section V, B31.3, API 1104, AWS D1.1) and your equipment.
  6. Pass the practical exam. A hands-on test on real flawed specimens, graded by a Level III against a checklist.
  7. Pass the vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated on schedule.
  8. Get certified by your employer. Certification is issued by, and tied to, your employer.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Keep your vision test current, recertify on schedule and add methods or levels.

For the full background, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification. New entrants can start with NDT Level 1 training.

Radiography licensing and other Wyoming requirements

Direct answer: Wyoming is an NRC Agreement State only for a limited scope: uranium and thorium milling (since 2018) and certain source material from mineral processing (added in 2026). Industrial radiography with sources such as iridium-192 remains licensed by the NRC, Region IV, under 10 CFR Part 34. Intrastate gas pipeline safety is overseen by the Wyoming Public Service Commission, and interstate lines by PHMSA.

Industrial radiography

Wyoming's agreement with the NRC is narrower than most. When Wyoming became the 38th Agreement State in 2018, it took over regulation of uranium and thorium milling and the associated byproduct material, and in 2026 it added certain source material produced during other mineral processing, administered by the Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality. The NRC kept jurisdiction over other radioactive materials, which includes the sealed sources used for gamma radiography. In practice that means a radiography company working in Wyoming needs an NRC licence, or files for NRC reciprocity if it is licensed in an Agreement State, and its radiographers and assistants must meet 10 CFR Part 34: radiation safety training, a radiation safety exam, a supervised assistant period, recognised radiographer certification, dosimetry and the two-person rule in the field. For industrial X-ray equipment, confirm current state requirements with the Wyoming Department of Health. Because this split is unusual, always confirm the current licensing authority with the NRC and the state before deploying a crew. Atlantis RT training covers SNT-TC-1A method knowledge, technique, exposure and interpretation; it complements, but does not replace, the radiation safety training the licence holder must provide.

Boilers and pressure vessels

Wyoming has historically not run a general statewide boiler and pressure vessel inspection programme of the kind found in most states, so inspection of boilers and vessels is usually driven by insurers, owners' mechanical integrity programmes, federal requirements and local codes. Confirm current requirements with the state and your insurer. Regardless of who inspects, repairs and alterations are normally performed to the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code and National Board rules, with NDT to ASME Section V by personnel certified under the repair organisation's quality programme. Refineries and gas plants also apply process safety management rules, which make documented inspection and certified personnel part of mechanical integrity.

Pipelines

The Wyoming Public Service Commission is authorised by PHMSA to inspect intrastate natural gas transmission and distribution systems, regulated gas gathering, propane distribution and new construction. Interstate gas and liquids lines are regulated by PHMSA directly. Weld inspection on these lines follows API 1104, with ASME B31.4 and B31.8, and operators expect RT and UT technicians qualified to their procedures and operator qualification programmes.

Codes Wyoming employers commonly use

  • ASME Section V, Section VIII and B31.3 at the Sinclair, Casper and Newcastle refineries, the Cheyenne renewable diesel unit, gas plants and soda ash plants
  • API 1104 with ASME B31.4 and B31.8 for gathering, transmission and products pipelines
  • ASME Section I and B31.1 for boilers and power piping at the coal-fired plants
  • Nuclear quality and ASME Section III context for the Kemmerer construction project (Atlantis trains SNT-TC-1A method certification; nuclear owners and their contractors set any additional requirements)
  • AWS D1.1 for structural steel, data centres, wind towers and mining equipment repair

Some Wyoming employers also look for API inspector or CWI credentials for certain roles. Atlantis does not train those schemes; our focus is ASNT SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Online, live-virtual and onsite training across Wyoming

Direct answer: Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Wyoming. Classroom theory is delivered live online or in live-virtual cohorts, and practical training and exams happen onsite at your facility with your equipment and specimens under ASNT Level III oversight. In a state where the nearest training specimens may be a day's drive away, that saves travel, lodging and lost shifts.

Individual technicians can join online NDT training from Casper, Gillette, Rock Springs or any site with a reliable connection. Sessions are live, with a Level III instructor answering questions in real time. Many Wyoming technicians work rotations at mines, gas fields or remote plants, so classroom blocks can be planned around time off. Practical hours and the practical exam are completed with your employer.

For employers, onsite delivery is usually the most efficient approach. We run classroom and practical sessions in your mine training building, refinery training room or shop, using your instruments, reference standards and part samples, and teach to your procedures. A Gillette mine gets MT and UT on the components its maintenance team actually repairs; a Casper inspection company gets RT and UT built around API 1104; a Green River plant gets UT thickness and PT tied to its reliability programme.

Wyoming's seasons shape the calendar. Pipeline and construction work peaks between late spring and autumn; deep winter cold and wind slow field work, which makes it the natural classroom season; refinery turnarounds, gas plant shutdowns and power plant outages run on their own schedules, commonly in spring and fall. We plan cohorts so certifications are complete before the work starts. Multi-site employers can use corporate NDT training. Ask about onsite training for your Wyoming crew.

For Wyoming employers: written practice and Level III services

NDT training in Wyoming: frequently asked questions

How do I become NDT certified in Wyoming?

Your employer certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice after you complete Level I and Level II classroom training, log documented experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Online classroom training can start before you are hired, with certification following once an employer documents your experience.

Is there NDT training online in Wyoming?

Yes. Atlantis NDT runs live online and live-virtual Level I and Level II classes that Wyoming technicians can join from anywhere in the state. Practical training and the practical exam are completed onsite with your employer.

Do I need a license to do radiography in Wyoming?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence for gamma radiography. Because Wyoming's Agreement State authority is limited to uranium recovery and certain source material, radiography sources are licensed by the NRC, and radiographers must meet 10 CFR Part 34. Confirm current requirements with the NRC and the state before starting work.

How much does NDT training cost in Wyoming?

Training is quoted on request. The quote depends on method and level, number of trainees, online or onsite delivery, travel for practical sessions, and whether you need exam administration or a written practice. We return a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

Which NDT method is most in demand in Wyoming?

UT and VT are needed almost everywhere. RT leads on pipelines, MT is essential in Powder River Basin mining, and PAUT and ET are central to refinery, gas plant and power plant inspection.

Can you train our crew onsite in Casper, Gillette or Rock Springs?

Yes. We deliver classroom and practical sessions at your facility anywhere in Wyoming and schedule around turnarounds, outages, rotations and the construction season.

Is SNT-TC-1A recognised by Wyoming employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard basis for employer certification across US refining, pipelines, mining and power. Owners and operators may add their own requirements, which your written practice can document.

How long does UT Level II take?

It depends on your employer's written practice. See the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums. Experience hours usually take longer than classroom training.

Will the Kemmerer nuclear project need NDT technicians?

Large nuclear construction projects typically require extensive weld and component inspection with demanding documentation. Requirements are set by the owner and its contractors, so check their published requirements; a solid SNT-TC-1A certification and clean records are the usual starting point.

Is there an NDT school in Wyoming I can attend in person?

Atlantis NDT does not operate a physical school or campus in Wyoming. Training is live online or onsite at your employer's facility.

Can I become a Level III in Wyoming?

Yes. Candidates with Level II experience can prepare for the ASNT Level III examinations through our online Level III training.

What do NDT technicians earn in Wyoming?

Pay depends on method, level, location and rotation. For general context, see the NDT salary guide.
